**THE GOSPEL ACCORDING TO LUKE BEGINS.**

*[Note: Col. 0583]*

**[Inscription: “anastodeiþ”]** See the note on the inscription to Mark.

[Note: [Col. 0583] Since indeed many have begun to write an account of the events fulfilled among us,] [Note: [Col. 0583] raihtis] St. adds *rahtis*.] [Note: [Col. 0583] just as those who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and ministers of the word delivered them to us:] Therefore, since many have begun to write an account among us of the events that have been fully accomplished, just as [they] handed them down to us who from the beginning were eyewitnesses and ministers of the word, it seemed good also to me and to the Holy Spirit, having carefully followed everything from the beginning, to write it out for you in orderly sequence, excellent Theophilus,, [Note: [Col. 0583] and to the Holy Spirit,] and to the Holy Spirit, o Greek manuscripts generally; the Gothic and Latin versions agree.] [Note: [Col. 0583] afarlaistjandin] Greek manuscripts generally place this before “from the beginning.”] so that you may recognize the certainty of the words about which you have been instructed. [Note: [Col. 0583] So that you may recognize the truth of the words in which you have been instructed.]

[Note: [Col. 0583] Now it happened in the days of Herod, king of Judea, that there was a priest named Zechariah, from the division of Abijah, and his wife was from the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.] It happened in the days of Herod, king of Judea: a priest named Zechariah, from the division of Abijah, and his wife from the daughters of Aaron, whose name was Elizabeth. [Note: [Col. 0583] þiudanis] J. and St. add *þiudans*.—[Note: [Col. 0583] gudja] The Codex Argenteus and the editions add *gudji*; otherwise Wulfila has ὁ τὶς. *afar* properly means “after”; here, used substantivally, it signifies “descendants,” but the Gothic departs considerably from the Greek, which has ἐφημερία. He understood the meaning of that word neither here nor in verse 8, where he translates it by *kuni* (“kind, race”); for ἐφημερία is one of the twenty-four classes of priests who served in the Temple each week.] So that you may know the certainty of the words concerning which you have been instructed.. It was in the days of Herod, king of Judea: a priest named Zechariah, from the division of Abijah, and his wife was from the daughters of Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.

They were both righteous before God, walking blamelessly in all the commandments and ordinances of the Lord. They were both righteous in God’s presence, walking in all the commandments and righteous requirements of the Lord. [Note: [Col. 0583] But they had no children, because Elizabeth was barren, and both were advanced in their days.] But she was barren, and they were both advanced in age. [Note: [Col. 0583] *vas*] The Greek has this after *aileisabaiþ*.]

Now it happened, while he was serving as priest in the order of his division before God, according to the custom of the priesthood, that the lot fell to him to offer incense, and he entered the Temple of the Lord; and the whole multitude was outside, praying at the hour of incense. [Note: [Col. 0583] *kunjis*] “Of the division”; see the note on verse 5.] [Note: [Col. 0583] According to the custom of the priesthood, the lot came out for him to offer sacrifice, as he entered the Temple of the Lord.] The lot came out for him to go and offer sacrifice, entering the Temple of the Lord. And the whole multitude was outside, waiting. [Note: [Col. 0584] *manageins*] B. adds *managens*.—[Note: [Col. 0584] *beidandans*] “Waiting”; Greek προσευχόμενον. Gr. IV, 192 prefers *bidjandans* (“praying”), but some manuscripts have προσδεχόμενον (“expecting”).]

Now there appeared to him, in a vision, an angel of the Lord, standing at the right side of the altar of incense. It happened to him in a vision: an angel of the Lord was standing at the right side of the altar of incense. [Note: [Col. 0584] *siunai*] J. and St. add *siuna*.] [Note: [Col. 0583] And Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear fell upon him.] Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear seized him. [Note: [Col. 0583] The angel said to him: Do not fear, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.] The angel said to him: “Do not fear, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard, and your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you shall call his name John.”

And you shall have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth. [Note: [Col. 0584] *þus faheds*] “Joy for you”; according to the Greek manuscripts generally.] And you will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth. For he will be great before the Lord, and he will drink neither wine nor strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even from his mother’s womb. [Note: [Col. 0584] *nauhþan*] St. adds *naukþan*.—[Note: [Col. 0584] *ïn*] According to *in*; Greek ἐκ.] For he will be great in the presence of the Lord; he will drink neither wine nor strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit even in his mother’s womb. [Note: [Col. 0583] and he will turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God;] And he will turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God. [Note: [Col. 0583] and he himself will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers to children and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous, to prepare for the Lord a perfected people.] And he himself will go before him in the presence of God, in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers toward children and the disobedient toward the wisdom of the righteous, to prepare for the Lord a prepared multitude. [Note: [Col. 0584] *ïn*] Third person; J. and St. omit *du* (“to”).]

And Zechariah said to the angel: “By what shall we know this? For I am old, and my wife is advanced in her days.” [Note: [Col. 0584] *kunnum*] “We know”; Greek generally has γνώσομαι, “I shall know.”] Zechariah said to the angel: “How shall we know this? For I am indeed old, and my wife is advanced in age.”

And the angel answered and said to him: “I am Gabriel, who stand in the presence of God, and I have been sent to speak to you and to announce this good news to you.” And the angel answered him: “I am Gabriel, who stand in the presence of God, and I have been sent to speak to you and to proclaim this to you.”

“And behold, you shall be silent and unable to speak until the day when this happens, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their time.” [Note: [Col. 0584] *jah*] An addition; Wulfila has Greek ἰδού (“behold”).—[Note: [Col. 0584] *dag ei*] St. adds *jct.* The use of the relative particle in place of a pronoun should be noted: thus XVII, 30, *vairþiþ þamma daga ei* (“it will happen on the day when”); Nehemiah V, 14, *fram þamma daga ei* (“from the day when”); see also the passages noted at Timothy II, III, 8. Elsewhere *ei* is attached to a demonstrative pronoun, thereby producing a relative pronoun; thus Corinthians I, II, 23, *ïesus ïn þizaiei naht galeviþs vas, nam hlaif* (“Jesus, on the night in which he was betrayed, took bread”).] I have been sent to speak to you and to proclaim this to you. You shall be silent and unable to speak until the day when this happens (see the following page), because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled in their appointed time.

The people were waiting for Zechariah, and they were astonished that he was delayed in the Temple. [Note: [Col. 0585] And when he came out, he could not speak to them, and they understood that he had seen a vision in the Temple; and he was signaling to them and remained mute.] The people were waiting for Zechariah and were astonished at how long he remained in the Temple. When he came out, he could not speak to them; and they understood that he had seen a vision in the Temple. He himself was signaling to them and remained mute.

And when the days of his service were completed, he went to his house. [Note: [Col. 0585] *dagos*] The Codex Argenteus adds *dagis*. Z. ventured to defend the reading of the Codex and translated it, “when the duties of the day had been completed,” forgetting that the priests’ service lasted not merely one day but seven days.—[Note: [Col. 0585] *andbahteis*] B. and Z. omit *andbahtheins*. *andbahteis* is the form of the genitive of nouns ending in *-i* (*-eis* for *-jis*), a form which Grimm I, 606 still desired; compare *gavairþeis* in Corinthians II, XIII, 11; Ephesians IV, 3; *trausteis* in Ephesians II, 12; *valdufneis* in *Skeireins* 49, 2. As for *waiteis* in John XII, 24, it is uncertain whether it is masculine (*waiteis*, compare German *der Weizen*) or neuter (*waiti*, compare Icelandic *hveiti*).]

After those days, Elizabeth his wife conceived, and she kept herself hidden for five months, saying: “Thus the Lord has dealt with me in the days in which he looked upon me, to take away my reproach among people.” [Note: [Col. 0585] *afniman*] Z. adds *afnimam*.—[Note: [Col. 0585] *ïdveit*] St. adds *ïdveiþ*.] He was mute. When the days of his service had been completed, he went to his house. After those days Elizabeth his wife conceived and hid herself for five months, saying: “Thus the Lord has dealt with me in the days when he looked upon me, to remove my reproach among people.”

Now in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent by God to a city of Galilee called Nazareth, to a virgin betrothed to a man whose name was Joseph, from the house of David; and the virgin’s name was Mary. [Note: [Col. 0585] “Then in the sixth month the angel Gabriel was sent by God into a city of Galilee called Nazareth, to a virgin betrothed to a husband whose name was Joseph, from the house of David, and the name of the virgin was Mary.”] The angel Gabriel was sent by God to a city of Galilee called Nazareth, to a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin’s name was Mary..

And the angel entered and said to her: “Rejoice, richly favored one; the Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women.” [Note: [Col. 0585] *anstai audahafta*] J. and St. add *jct.*] And the angel entered and said to her: “Rejoice, richly favored one; the Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women.”

But when she saw him, she was troubled at his entrance and considered what kind of greeting this was, by which he had blessed her. [Note: [Col. 0585] *gasaiwandei*] “Seeing,” according to the Greek manuscripts generally.—[Note: [Col. 0585] *gaþlahsnoda*] The Greek has this after it.—[Note: [Col. 0585] *ïnnagahtai*] That is, not “in speech,” as B. interprets it, but “at his entrance,” as Gord. rightly recognized in *Appendix Ulfilana*, p. 57. Greek manuscripts generally have λόγῳ; Wulfila and the Latin versions agree. J. and St. add *ïnnsagahtai*.—[Note: [Col. 0585] *ïs*] “His,” according to the Greek manuscripts generally.—[Note: [Col. 0585] *þatei—ïzai*] “By which he thus blessed her,” according to the Greek manuscripts generally.] When she saw him, she was troubled at his entrance and considered within herself what sort of greeting this might be, by which he had thus blessed her.

And the angel said to her: “Do not fear, Mary, for you have found favor with God. And behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus.” The angel said to her: “Do not fear, Mary; for you have found favor with God. And behold, you will conceive in your womb and bear a son, and you shall call his name Jesus.”

“He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High, and the Lord God will give him the throne of David his father.” [Note: [Col. 0586] *hauhistins*] J. and St. add *hauhistons*.—[Note: [Col. 0586] *gibid*] J. and St. omit *gibiþ*.] He will be great and will be called Son of the Most High, and the Lord God will give him the throne of David his father.

“And he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and there will be no end to his kingdom.” [Note: [Col. 0586] *ïn ajukduþ*] J., St., and B. omit this in favor of *ïn aivins* (“forever”).—[Note: [Col. 0586] *jah*] In the second position, J., St., and B. omit it in favor of *ïþ*.—[Note: [Col. 0586] *andeis*] J. and B. add *andei*. That *andeis* is truly the nominative form has now been learned from Corinthians I, XV, 24, and Corinthians II, XI, 15. Its authority should not be doubted with Z.; nor should anyone, with J. and others, continue to take *andeis* as a genitive.] The Lord God will give him the throne of David his father, and he will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and there will be no end to his kingdom.

Then Mary said to the angel: “How shall this be, since I do not know a husband?” Mary said to the angel: “How can this be, since I do not know a husband?”

And the angel answered and said to her: “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you; therefore the one who is born will be holy and will be called the Son of God.” [Note: [Col. 0586] *ïzai*] J., St., and B. add *ïzaize*.—[Note: [Col. 0586] *duþe ei*] J., St., and B. add *duþeh*; otherwise Wulfila has Greek καί.] And the angel answered and said to her: “The Holy Spirit will come upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore the holy one who is born will be called the Son of God.”

“And behold, Elizabeth your kinswoman has also conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her who is called barren.” [Note: [Col. 0586] *aileisabaiþ*] St. adds *aileizabaiþ*.—[Note: [Col. 0586] *ïnkilþo*] See the note on verse 24.—[Note: [Col. 0586] *sunau—seinamma*] J. and B. add *suna* (B. adds *sunu*), then *ganam ... nin seinam*; thereafter a lacuna continues until verse 38, *jah galaiþ*.] And behold, Elizabeth your kinswoman has conceived a son in her old age, and this is the sixth month for her who is called barren. For nothing is impossible with God. [Note: [Col. 0586] *guþa*] “With God,” Greek παρὰ θεῷ.] For nothing is impossible with God.

And Mary said: “Behold, the Lord’s servant; let it happen to me according to your word.” And the angel departed from her. Mary said: “Behold, the Lord’s servant; let it happen to me according to your word.” And the angel departed from her.

Now Mary arose in those days and went hurriedly into the hill country, to a city of Judah. She arose in those days and went into the hill country in haste, to a city of Judah.

And she entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth. She entered the house of Zechariah and greeted Elizabeth.

And it happened, when Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, that the infant leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit. She exclaimed with a loud voice and said: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb.” [Note: [Col. 0586] *ufvopida*] St. adds *usvopida*.] Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting; the child leaped in her womb, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.

She cried out with a loud voice and said: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb. And from where is this granted to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?” She cried out with a loud voice and said: “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb. And why is this granted to me, that the mother of my Lord should come to me?”

“For behold, as soon as the voice of your greeting came into my ears, the infant leaped in joy in my womb.” [Note: [Col. 0587] “For behold, when the voice of your greeting first came into my ears, this infant leaped in joy in my womb.”] “For behold, as soon as the voice of your greeting came into my ears, the child leaped in joy in my womb.”

“And blessed is she who believed, because there will be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.” [Note: [Col. 0587] And blessed is she who believed that there would be a fulfillment of what was spoken to her by the Lord.] Mary said: “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior.” Mary said: “My soul magnifies the Lord, and my spirit rejoices in God my Savior.”

“For he has looked upon the humility of his servant; for behold, from now on all generations will call me blessed.” For he has looked upon the lowliness of his servant; for behold, from now on all generations will call me blessed.

“For the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name. And his mercy is from generation to generation upon those who fear him.” For the Mighty One has done great things for me, and holy is his name. His mercy is from generation to generation upon those who fear him.

“He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thought of their heart.” He has shown strength with his arm; he has scattered the proud in the thought of their heart.

“He has brought down the mighty from their thrones and exalted the lowly.” He has brought down the mighty from their thrones and exalted the lowly.

“He has filled the hungry with good things, and has sent the rich away empty.” He has filled the hungry with good things and has sent the rich away empty.

“He has helped Israel his servant, remembering his mercy, as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed forever.” [Note: [Col. 0587] *þiumagu*] A more unusual form of the dative than *þiumagau*; compare VII, 26 *praufetu*, IX, 26 *vulþu*, verse 38 *sunu*, instead of *praufetau*, *vulþau*, *sunau*. Compare I, 79 *dauþus*; Romans IX, 23 *vulþus*; Corinthians I, I, 12 *pavlus* (if Cast. edited it correctly), instead of *dauþaus*, *vulþaus*, *pavlaus*; see also the note on Mark VII, 32.—[Note: [Col. 0587] *gamunands*] “Remembering”; Greek manuscripts generally have μνησθῆναι; Wulfila agrees with the Latin versions.] He has helped Israel his servant, remembering his mercy, as he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed forever. [Note: [Col. 0587] *fraiv*] This reading of the Codex Argenteus and the editions is entirely false; the dative *fraiva* is required. To take *fraiv* as the complete reading, as though it were an accusative—which could also be *abrahama*, see verse 73—is not permitted by the sense.] As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and to his seed forever, remembering his mercy.

Mary remained with her about three months and returned to her home. [Note: [Col. 0587] Elizabeth’s time was fulfilled for giving birth, and she bore a son.] Mary remained with her about three months, then returned to her home. Elizabeth’s time was fulfilled for giving birth, and she bore a son.

And her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had magnified his mercy toward her, and they rejoiced with her. Elizabeth’s neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had magnified his mercy toward her, and they rejoiced with her.

And it happened on the eighth day that they came to circumcise the child, and they called him by the name of his father, Zechariah. [Note: [Col. 0587] *aileisabaiþ*] Wulfila has Greek δέ (“and”).] On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they called him after the name of his father, Zechariah.

But his mother answered and said: “No; rather, he shall be called John.” His mother answered: “No; he shall be called John.”

And they said to her: “There is no one among your kindred who is called by this name.” They said to her: “No one in your family is called by this name.”

Then they motioned to his father, asking what he wanted him to be called. They gestured to his father, asking what he wished to call him.

He asked for a tablet and wrote, saying: “John is his name”; and they all marveled. [Note: [Col. 0587] *ïs*] The Greek manuscripts generally have *is* earlier.—[Note: [Col. 0587] *nam jah*] “Took and,” according to the Greek manuscripts generally.] He asked for a writing tablet and wrote: “John is his name.” And they all marveled.

Immediately his mouth and tongue were opened, and he spoke, blessing God. [Note: [Col. 0587] *tuggo*] St. adds *tungo*.] His mouth was opened at once, and his tongue, and he spoke, saying: “John is his name,” blessing God.

And fear came upon all who dwelt around them, and throughout all the hill country of Judea all these words were spoken. His mouth and tongue were opened, and he spoke, blessing God. Fear came upon all who dwelt around him, and throughout all the hill country of Judea all these words were reported. [Note: [Col. 0587] *ïna*] “Him”; Greek αὐτούς, “them.”—[Note: [Col. 0587] *bisitandam*] The Codex Argenteus adds *bisitantandam*; the following *tan* begins the next line.]

And all who heard them laid them up in their hearts, saying: “What then will this child be?” For the hand of the Lord was with him. All who heard them laid them up in their hearts, saying: “What will this child become?” For the hand of the Lord was with him. [Note: [Col. 0588] *wa*] Wulfila has Greek ἄρα (“then”).—[Note: [Col. 0588] *jah þan*] “And indeed”; Greek καί, and Wulfila with some manuscripts perhaps read καὶ γάρ; compare Corinthians II, II, 10.]

And Zechariah, his father, was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying: “Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, for he has visited and wrought redemption for his people.” His father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit, prophesied, and said: “Blessed is the Lord God of Israel, for he has visited and made redemption for his people.”

“And he has raised up for us a horn of salvation in the house of David his servant.” [Note: [Col. 0588] *daveidis þiumagaus*] St. adds *deveidis þiumagans*.] He has raised up for us a horn of salvation in the house of David his servant.

“As he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from the beginning of the age.” [Note: [Col. 0588] *fram anastodeinai aivis*] “From the beginning of the age”; Greek ἀπ᾽ αἰῶνος, which in John IX, 32 is simply rendered *fram aiva* (“from of old”).] As he spoke through the mouth of his holy prophets from the beginning of the age.

“To grant us salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all those who hate us.” [Note: [Col. 0588] *giban*] “To grant”; according to the Greek manuscripts generally.—[Note: [Col. 0588] *handau*] J. and St. add *handam*.] To grant us salvation from our enemies and from the hand of all those who hate us.

“To show mercy to our fathers and to remember his holy covenant.” To show mercy to our fathers and to remember his holy covenant.

“The oath which he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant us.” [Note: [Col. 0588] *aiþis*] A genitive dependent on *gamunan* (“to remember”); Greek ὅρκον. The same construction is found in Theophylact, in the Roman, Paris, and Venetian editions.—[Note: [Col. 0588] *abrahama*] An unusual form instead of *abraham* (Luke III, 8; John VIII, 57); compare verse 55.] The oath which he swore to Abraham our father, that he would grant us—

“To serve him without fear, delivered from the hand of our enemies, in truth and righteousness before him all our days.” To serve him without fear, delivered from the hand of our enemies, in truth and righteousness before him all our days. [Note: [Col. 0588] *garaihtein*] J., St., B., and Hz. omit *garaihteim*.]*.]

“And you, little child, will be called prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways.” [Note: [Col. 0589] *fauragaggis*] St. adds *fauragangis*.] “And you, child, will be called prophet of the Most High; for you will go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways.”

“To give knowledge of salvation to his people in the forgiveness of their sins.” To give knowledge of salvation to his people in the forgiveness of their sins.

“Through the compassionate mercy of our God, by which the rising from on high will visit us.” [Note: [Col. 0589] *ïn þammei*] “In which”; Greek manuscripts generally have ἐν οἷς, understood as “in the inward parts.” Strictly, *ïn þizaiei* would be more correct, since it should refer to *armahairtei* (“mercy”).] Through the compassionate mercy of our God, by which the rising from on high will visit us.

“To shine upon those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death, to direct our feet into the way of peace.” [Note: [Col. 0589] *dauþus*] See the note on verse 54.] The rising from on high will shine upon those sitting in darkness and the shadow of death, to direct our feet into the way of peace.

But the child grew and became strong in spirit, and was in the deserts until the day of his manifestation to Israel. [Note: [Col. 0589] *dag ustaikneinais*] J. and St. add *dagus taikneinais*.] The child grew, became strong in spirit, and was in the desert until the day of his manifestation to Israel.

Now it happened in those days that a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole world should be registered. [Note: [Col. 0589] *agustau*] Z. adds *augustau*. The statements of Grimm I, 46 and Bopp, *Vergleichende Grammatik* I, p. 68, that Wulfila regularly renders the Greek diphthong αυ in proper names by *au*, are mistaken; for the example they offer, *Augustus*, is false, as we have seen. Moreover, Παῦλος is not Gothic *paulus*, but *pavlus* (Corinthians II, I, 1; Titus I, 1; Philemon 19), just as Ἡσαῦ is *esav* (Romans IX, 13), and the Latin *cautio* is *kavtsjo* in the Neapolitan Monument. Similarly, the Greek diphthong ευ is rendered by the Goths not as *aiu* but as *aiv*, compare *aivaggeljo*, *aivxaristia*, and *aivlaugia* (εὐαγγέλιον, εὐχαριστία, εὐλογία).] It happened in those days that a decree went out from Caesar Augustus that the whole world should be registered.

This registration was the first, when Quirinius was governor of Syria. [Note: [Col. 0589] *þan*] “Now”; according to the Greek manuscripts generally.—[Note: [Col. 0589] *at visandin*] J., St., and Z. add *jct.*—[Note: [Col. 0589] *syriais*] Thus the Codex Argenteus and Z.; J., St., and B. omit the final *s*. Compare Corinthians I, XVI, 1 (*galatiais* in codex B); XVI, 19 (*asiais*); Corinthians II, VIII, 1 (*makidonais*); Luke IV, 26 (*seidonais*); VIII, 41 (*synagogais*). Moreover, *visandin kindina syriais* is a gloss on *raginondin saurim*, first written in the margin and later inserted into the text by an inexperienced scribe.] The first registration took place when Quirinius was governing Syria.

And all went to be registered, each to his own city. [Note: [Col. 0590] *seinai*] “His own”; Greek ἰδίαν. Since this is usually rendered in Gothic by *sves*, one might suspect that Wulfila here read ἑαυτοῦ, but compare John VII, 18; VIII, 44; Romans XIV, 4; Corinthians I, II, 21, where *seins* likewise corresponds to ἴδιος.] All went to be registered, each to his own city.

Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, into Judea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem, because he was from the house and family of David. [Note: [Col. 0589] Joseph went up from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, into Judea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem, because he was from the house and family of David.] [Note: [Col. 0590] *þan*] B. adds *þanei*.—[Note: [Col. 0590] *galeilaia*] J. and St. add *galilaia*; B. adds *o us galeilaia*, and J. adds *o us baurg nazaraiþ*.—[Note: [Col. 0590] *baurg*] In the second occurrence J. adds *baurh*.—[Note: [Col. 0590] *beþlahaim*] J., St., and B. omit *beþlaihaim*, though that form occurs at John VII, 42; in Luke, *beþlahaim* is found, see verse 15.—[Note: [Col. 0590] *garda fadreinais*] “House of family”; Greek manuscripts generally have οἴκου καὶ πατριᾶς.] Joseph went up from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth, into Judea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem, because he was from the house and family of David.

He went to be registered with Mary, who was betrothed to him as wife and was pregnant. [Note: [Col. 0589] “To be registered with Mary, who was betrothed to him as wife, being pregnant.”] He went to be registered with Mary, who was betrothed to him as wife and was pregnant.

And while they were there, the days for her to give birth were completed. [Note: [Col. 0590] *ïnkilþon*] See the note on I, 24.] While they were there, her days for giving birth were completed.

And she bore her firstborn son, wrapped him, and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the lodging. [Note: [Col. 0590] *þo vesun*] According to the Greek manuscripts generally.] She bore her firstborn son, wrapped him, and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in that place. [Note: [Col. 0590] *seinana—frumabaur*] J. and St. add *seinama—frumabauri*.—[Note: [Col. 0590] *ïm*] St. adds *ïn*.—[Note: [Col. 0590] *þamma*] “This,” according to the Greek manuscripts generally.]

And there were shepherds in that same region, keeping watch and guarding the watches of the night over their flock. [Note: [Col. 0590] *þamma samin*] Greek manuscripts generally place this after *landa*.] Shepherds were in that same land, keeping watch through the night over their flock.

And behold, an angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they feared with great fear. [Note: [Col. 0590] *ïþ*] Wulfila, some manuscripts, and the Latin versions have Greek ἰδού (“behold”).] They were keeping watch over the night watches of their flock. Then an angel of the Lord came upon them, and the glory of the Lord shone around them, and they were greatly afraid.

And the angel said to them: “Do not fear; for behold, I announce to you great joy, which will be for all the people: for today a Savior has been born for you, who is Christ the Lord, in the city of David.” [Note: [Col. 0589] *gabaurans*] Z. adds *gabauran*.] The angel said to them: “Do not fear. Behold, I proclaim to you great joy, which will be for all the people: today a Savior has been born for you, who is Christ the Lord, in the city of David.

“And this will be a sign for you: you will find an infant wrapped and lying in a manger.” [Note: [Col. 0590] *jah*] In the second position, “and,” according to the Greek.] “This will be a sign for you: you will find a child wrapped and lying in a manger.”

And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host, praising God and saying: “Glory to God in the highest, and on earth peace among people of good will.” [Note: [Col. 0590] *aggilau*] J. adds *aggilu*, as also in verse 21.] Suddenly there was with that angel a multitude of the heavenly host, praising God and saying: “Glory in the highest to God, and on earth peace among people of good will.” [Note: [Col. 0590] *godis viljins*] “Of good will”; Greek εὐδοκία.]

And it happened, when the angels had gone away from them into heaven, that those men, the shepherds, said to one another: “Let us go now as far as Bethlehem and see this event that has happened, which the Lord has shown us.” [Note: [Col. 0591] *vaurþano*] St. adds *vaurþand*.—[Note: [Col. 0591] *ju*] “Already”; Greek manuscripts generally have δή, though Wulfila seems to have read ἤδη; see the *Prolegomena*, p. [lacuna].] The glory was in the highest to God, and on earth peace among people of good will. When the angels had gone away from them into heaven, the shepherds said to one another: “Let us go now as far as Bethlehem and see this event that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”

And they came in haste and found Mary and Joseph and the infant lying in a manger. [Note: [Col. 0591] *sniumjandans*] St. adds *snumjandans*.—[Note: [Col. 0591] *bigetun*] Wulfila has Greek τέ (“and”); this particle is rendered by *ïþ* in John VI, 18 and is often omitted in the Epistles; see Romans VII, 7; X, 12; Corinthians I, I, 24; Ephesians III, 19.] They came in haste and found Mary, Joseph, and the child lying in the manger.

When they saw it, they made known the word that had been spoken to them about this child. [Note: [Col. 0591] *gakannidedun*] J. and St. add *gakannadedun*.] When they saw it, they made known what had been spoken to them concerning this child.

And all who heard it marveled at what had been told them by the shepherds. [Note: [Col. 0591] *hairdjam*] J., St., and B. add *hairdjan*.] All who heard it marveled at the word that had been spoken to them concerning the child.

But Mary kept all these words, pondering them in her heart. Mary preserved all these words, pondering them in her heart.

And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all that they had heard and seen, just as it had been told them. [Note: [Col. 0591] *sis*] After Grimm, having proposed changing it to *sik* in *Grammatik* IV, 30, later argued on p. 943 that the dative could be defended. That is correct, but Titus I, 14 should not be compared; there *afvandjandana sis sunja* means “those who turn truth away from themselves,” rather than “truth away from them.” Here, however, Wulfila, together with the great majority of the manuscripts, seems to have read ἐπέστρεψαν, so that *sis* means “to themselves,” that is, to their flocks; compare Luke XVIII, 11, *standands sis*, σταθεὶς πρὸς ἑαυτῶν.—[Note: [Col. 0591] *hairdjos*] J., St., and B. add *hairdjonds*.—[Note: [Col. 0591] *þizeei*] J., St., and B. add *þoeei*. To establish the Codex Argenteus reading, J. does not correctly cite the passages from John in which *hausjan* means our “to hear” an address, words, or doctrine; here the genitive *þizeei* does not depend on *hausjan*, but is placed according to the figure of attraction, as comparison with the Greek will show.] And the shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for all that they had heard and seen, just as it had been told them.

And when the eight days were completed for circumcising him, his name was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived in the womb. [Note: [Col. 0591] *usfulnodedun*] J. and Z. have *usfullnodedun*, which is more correct, but the second liquid is omitted in this verb not only in the Codex Argenteus, where it occurs several times—see verses 22; IX, 51; XIV, 23, where Z., inconsistently, admitted *usfulnai* into the text—but also in Ephesians III, 19, codex A.—[Note: [Col. 0592] *aggilau*] J. and St. add *aggilu*.] When eight days had been completed for circumcising him, his name was called Jesus, as it had been spoken by the angel before he was conceived in the womb.

And when the days of their purification were completed according to the law of Moses, they brought him to Jerusalem to present him before the Lord. [Note: [Col. 0592] *usfulnodedun*] See the note on verse 21.—[Note: [Col. 0592] *hraineinais*] J. adds *hraineimais*.] When the days of their purification were completed according to the law of Moses, they brought him to Jerusalem to present him before the Lord.

As it is written in the law of the Lord: “Every male that opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord.” As it is written in the law of the Lord: “Every male who opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord.”

And to offer a sacrifice concerning him, as it is said in the law of the Lord: “A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.” [Note: [Col. 0592] *fram ïmma*] “Concerning him,” or “for him,” according to the Greek manuscripts generally. The use of *fram* in this sense, “for, concerning,” which Junius in his *Glossarium* p. 53 entirely overlooked, is not very frequent; apart from this passage, it is scarcely found except at Mark I, 44; Luke V, 14; VI, 28; John XVII, 19; Ephesians V, 20; compare Romans XIV, 12.—[Note: [Col. 0592] *hraivadubono*] St. adds *hraivadubona*.] And to offer a sacrifice concerning him, as it is said in the law of the Lord: “A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”

Now there was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon, and this man was righteous and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him. [Note: [Col. 0592] *þaruh*] It may be questioned whether Wulfila omitted Greek ἰδού (“behold”). The same particle is used for Greek καὶ ἰδού at Matthew IX, 3, and also for ἰδού at Matthew IX, 18, and for καί in many passages.—[Note: [Col. 0592] *vas*] In the second occurrence, “was,” according to the Greek manuscripts generally.—[Note: [Col. 0592] *veihs vas*] According to the Greek manuscripts generally.] Now there was a man in Jerusalem, whose name was Simeon. This man was righteous and devout, waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was upon him.

].

And he [was] righteous and God-fearing, awaiting the consolation of Israel; and the Holy Spirit was upon him. And it had been revealed to him by the Holy Spirit that he would not see death before he had seen the Lord’s Christ. And he came in the Spirit into the temple; and, while the parents were bringing in the child Jesus in order to do for him according to the custom of the law, he took him into his arms, blessed God, and said:

“Now dismiss your servant, Master, Lord, according to your word, in peace; for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you prepared before the face of all peoples: a light for revelation to the nations, and glory for your people Israel.”

And Joseph and his mother were marveling at the things spoken concerning him. And Simeon blessed them and said to Mary, his mother:

“Behold, this one is appointed for the fall and rising of many in Israel, and for a sign opposed—and a sword shall pierce through your own soul also—so that thoughts out of many hearts may be revealed.”

[Col. 0593] “And there was Anna, a prophetess, daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was very advanced in days, having lived with her husband seven years from her virginity.”

And she was a widow of eighty-four years. She did not depart from the temple, serving the Lord with fastings and prayers night and day. And at that very hour she stood by, gave thanks to the Lord, and spoke concerning him among all who were awaiting the consolation of Jerusalem.

And when they had completed all things according to the law of the Lord, they returned into Galilee, to their own city Nazareth. But the child grew and became strong, filled with Spirit and wisdom; and the grace of God was upon him.

And his parents went every year to Jerusalem for the feast of the Passover. And when he was twelve years old, as they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast, and had completed the days, when they returned again Jesus the child remained in Jerusalem; and Joseph and his mother did not know it. Supposing him to be among the traveling company, they came a day’s journey and sought him among their relatives and acquaintances. And when they did not find him, they returned to Jerusalem seeking him. And after three days they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and questioning them. And all who heard him were astonished at his understanding and his answers. And when they saw him, they were astonished. And his mother said to him:

“Child, why have you treated us so? Behold, your father and I, grieving, have been seeking you.”

And he said to them:

“Why were you seeking me? Did you not know that I must be in the things of my Father?”

But they did not understand the word that he spoke to them. And he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and he was obedient to them. And his mother kept all these words in her heart.

And Jesus advanced in wisdom, stature, and grace with God and men.

[Col. 0593–0595] In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governing Judaea, and Herod was tetrarch of Galilee, while Philip, his brother, was tetrarch of the region of Ituraea and Trachonitis, and Lysanias was tetrarch of Abilene, under the high priests Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John, son of Zachariah, in the wilderness.

And he came through all the region around the Jordan, proclaiming a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins, as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet:

“The voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight. Every valley shall be filled, and every mountain and hill shall be brought low; the crooked shall become straight, and the rough ways smooth; and all flesh shall see the salvation of God.”

Then he said to the crowds who came out to be baptized by him:

“Brood of vipers, who warned you to flee from the coming wrath? Therefore produce fruit worthy of repentance, and do not begin to say among yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that God can raise up children for Abraham from these stones. But already the axe lies at the roots of the trees. Therefore every tree that does not produce good fruit is cut down and thrown into the fire.”

And the crowds asked him, saying:

“What, then, shall we do?”

And he answered and said to them:

“Let the one who has two tunics give to the one who has none; and let the one who has food do likewise.”

Tax collectors also came to be baptized and said to him:

“Teacher, what shall we do?”

And he said to them:

“Exact nothing beyond what has been appointed for you.”

Soldiers also asked him, saying:

“And what shall we do?”

And he said to them:

“Rob no one, extort no one, and be content with your wages.”

Now, while all the people were expecting, and all were thinking in their hearts about John, whether he might perhaps be the Christ, John answered everyone, saying:

“I indeed baptize you with water, but one stronger than I is coming, whose sandal strap I am not worthy to loosen. He will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire. His winnowing shovel is in his hand, and he will cleanse his threshing floor and gather the grain into his granary; but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire.”

And with many other exhortations he proclaimed the good news to the people.

But Herod the tetrarch, reproved by him concerning Herodias, the wife of his brother, and concerning all the evil things that Herod had done, added this also to everything: he shut John up in prison.

And it happened, when he was baptizing all the multitude, and Jesus had been baptized and was praying, that heaven was opened, and the Holy Spirit descended upon him in bodily form, like a dove; and a voice came from heaven, saying:

“You are my beloved Son; in you I have been well pleased.”

And Jesus himself was about thirty years old, under public manifestation, being regarded as the son of Joseph: son of Heli, son of Matthat, son of Levi, son of Melchi, son of Janna, son of Joseph, son of Mattathias, son of Ammon, son of Naum, son of Esli, son of Nagge, son of Maath, son of Mattathias, son of Semein, son of Joseph, son of Joda, son of Joannan, son of Rhesa, son of Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, son of Neri, son of Melchi, son of Addi, son of Cosam, son of Elmodam, son of Her, son of Joses, son of Eliezer, son of Jorim, son of Mattathan, son of Levi, son of Symeon, son of Judah, son of Joseph, son of Joannan, son of Eliakim, son of Melea, son of Mainan, son of Mattathan, son of Nathan, son of David, son of Jesse, son of Obed, son of Boaz, son of Salmon, son of Nahasson, son of Amminadab, son of Aram, son of Esrom, son of Phares, son of Judah, son of Jacob, son of Isaac, son of Abraham, son of Terah, son of Nahor, son of Serug, son of Ragau, son of Phaleg, son of Eber, son of Salah, son of Cainan, son of Arphaxad, son of Shem, son of Noel, son of Lamech, son of Methuselah, son of Enoch, son of Jared, son of Mahalaleel, son of Cainan, son of Enos, son of Seth, son of Adam, son of God.

But Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, turned back from the Jordan and was led by the Spirit in the wilderness for forty days, being tempted by the devil. And he ate nothing during those days, and when they were completed he was hungry.

And the devil said to him:

“If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread.”

And Jesus answered him, saying:

“It is written: ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.’”

And the devil led him up onto a high mountain and showed him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said to him:

“To you I will give all this authority and their glory, because it has been delivered to me, and I give it to whomever I wish. Therefore, if you worship me in my presence, all of it will be yours.”

And Jesus answered him and said:

“It is written: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God, and him alone you shall serve.’”

Then he led him to Jerusalem and set him on the pinnacle of the temple and said to him:

“If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here. For it is written: ‘He will command his angels concerning you, to preserve you’; and: ‘They will hold you up in their hands, lest you strike your foot against a stone.’”

And Jesus answered and said to him:

“It is said: ‘You shall not tempt the Lord your God.’”

And when the devil had completed every temptation, he departed from him until the appointed time.

And Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, and news about him went out through all the surrounding region. And he taught in their assemblies, being glorified by all.

And he came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up, and entered the synagogue according to his custom on the Sabbath day. And he stood up to read. And the book of the prophet Isaiah was handed to him. And when he had opened the book, he found the place where it was written:

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to proclaim good news to the poor; he has sent me to heal the brokenhearted, to proclaim release to captives and sight to the blind, to release those who have been crushed into consolation, to proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord.”

And he folded up the book, gave it back to the attendant, and sat down. And the eyes of everyone in the synagogue were fixed upon him. And he began to say to them:

“Today this Scripture has been fulfilled in your ears.”

And all bore witness to him and were amazed at the words of grace that came from his mouth, and they said:

“Is this not Joseph’s son?”

And he said to them:

“Surely you will say to me this proverb: ‘Physician, heal yourself. Whatever we have heard was done in Capernaum, do also here in your homeland.’”

And he said:

“Amen, I tell you: no prophet is accepted in his homeland.”
