[Note: [Col. 0617] You did not kiss me, but she, from the time I entered, has not stopped kissing my feet.]

[Note: [Col. 0617] *fotuns meinans*: corresponds to all the Greek manuscripts.]

You did not anoint my head with oil; but she has anointed my feet with perfume.

[Note: [Col. 0617] You did not anoint my head with oil, but she has anointed my feet with perfume.]

[Note: [Col. 0617] *fotuns meinans*: corresponds to the Greek.]

Therefore I tell you: her many sins have been forgiven, because she loved much; but the one to whom little is forgiven loves little.”

[Note: [Col. 0617] Therefore I tell you: her many sins have been forgiven, because she loved much; but the one to whom little is forgiven loves little.]

And he said to her, “Your sins have been forgiven.”

[Note: [Col. 0617] And he said to her, “Your sins have been forgiven.”]

[Note: [Col. 0617] *qaþuh þan*: so the Argenteus manuscript; St and Z add *gaþ uþþan*. *þus*: “to you,” as in all Greek manuscripts; the Greek has σοῦ, which Ulfila renders by *þeinos*.]

But those reclining with him began to say among themselves, “Who is this, who even forgives sins?”

[Note: [Col. 0617] Those reclining with him began to say among themselves, “Who is this, who even forgives sins?”]

[Note: [Col. 0617] *sis silbam*: St adds *sissilban*. *saei*: Ulfila has the Greek καί.]

But he said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”

[Note: [Col. 0617] But he said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you; go in peace.”]

[Note: [Col. 0617] *ïs*: “he,” as in all Greek manuscripts. *gavairþi*: J, St, and B add *gavairþa*.]

After this, he went through towns and villages, proclaiming and announcing the good news of the kingdom of God; and the Twelve were with him.

[Note: [Col. 0617] And it happened afterward that he went through towns and villages, proclaiming and announcing the good news of the kingdom of God; and the Twelve were with him.]

[Note: [Col. 0617] *biþe afar þata*: “afterward,” that is, ἐν τῷ καθεξῆς; the neuter is superfluous, as B. and Ih. think. *þata ei*: J, B, and Z add an abbreviation; St has *þatei*. *ei*: “so that,” as in the Greek; see the note on VI, 12. Thus after *varþ* (ἐγένετο, “it happened”), *ei* frequently occurs, and often *jah* also follows; hence we suspect that neither *ei* nor *jah* arose from a gloss. *vratoda [Col. 0618] and baurgs*: St has a lacuna; J has only traces; B prints *vratoda ...*. *haimos*: J adds *haimo*; St has *haimo ...*, omitting everything through *londs*. *þiuþspillonds*: We have printed this form with J and B, based on III, 18. In the Argenteus manuscript nothing beyond *---llonds* can be read. We do not accept the reading *vailaspillonds* printed by Ih. and Z., since that compound is found nowhere.]

And it happened afterward that he went through towns and villages, proclaiming and announcing the good news of the kingdom of God.

[Note: [Col. 0617] And women who had been healed of evil spirits and diseases were with him: Mary, who was called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out.]

[Note: [Col. 0618] *qinons*: Ulfila and the versions have τινές. *galeikinodos*: J has *galeikinode*; St has *galeik...*. *sauhte jah*: J and St add *sauhtaim*. *jah*: the third hand adds “and,” as in all Greek manuscripts. *usïddjedun*: all Greek manuscripts add this after *sibun*.]

And the Twelve were with him, and certain women who had been healed of evil spirits and diseases: Mary, who was called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had gone out; and Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod’s steward; and Susanna; and many others, who ministered to them from their own possessions.

[Note: [Col. 0617] And Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod’s steward, and Susanna, and many others, who ministered to them from their own possessions.]

[Note: [Col. 0618] *fauragagjins*: so the Argenteus manuscript and J, St, and B; the marginal hand and Z omit *fauragaggjins*; see the note on XVI, 1. *herodes*: St adds *heordes*. *andbahtededun*: the Argenteus manuscript has this instead of *andbahtidedun*; J, St, and B add *andbatheidedun*. *ïm*: “to them,” Greek αὐτῷ. *seinaim*: J and St add *seinain*.]

When a large crowd had gathered, including those who came to him from the towns, he spoke by a parable:

[Note: [Col. 0617] When large crowds had gathered, and those who came to him from the towns, he spoke by a parable.]

[Note: [Col. 0618] *hiumam*: see the note on VI, 17; J adds *hiuman*. *þaiei us*: St and an abbreviated witness add this. *us baurgim*: “from the towns,” Greek κατὰ πόλιν, that is, “those living in the town and setting out from the town.”]

“A sower went out to sow his seed. And as he sowed, some fell beside the road, was trampled, and the birds of heaven devoured it.

[Note: [Col. 0617] He went out to sow his own seed; and as he sowed, some fell beside the road, was trampled, and the birds of heaven devoured it.]

[Note: [Col. 0618] *saiands*: J, St, and B add the article, as in Mark IV, 3 and 14; the Argenteus manuscript does not recognize it here. *saiso*: St adds an abbreviation. *gatrudon*: Since this form can be neither an infinitive, on account of the construction (for *varþ* normally takes a participle), nor a participle, on account of its ending, we fear that it was written by scribal error for *gatrudan*, if Grimm I, 844, is correct.]

And some fell on rock; when it had grown up, it withered because it had no moisture.

[Note: [Col. 0617] And another fell on rock; when it had sprouted, it withered because it had no moisture.]

[Note: [Col. 0618] *uskijanata*: Grimm I, 841 suspects this to be false for *uskinanata*. We think it is rather a past participle belonging to the verb *keian* (Grimm I, 854, 7). *qrammiþa*: J and St add *qarmmiþa*.]

And some fell among thorns, and the thorns growing up with it choked it.

[Note: [Col. 0619] And some fell among thorns, and the thorns growing up with it choked it.]

[Note: [Col. 0619] *afwapidedun*: see the note on Mark IV, 7.]

And some fell on good soil, grew up, and produced a hundredfold. As he said this, he called out, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”

[Note: [Col. 0619] And some fell on good soil, grew up, and produced a hundredfold. As he said this, he called out, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”]

[Note: [Col. 0619] *taihuntaihundfalþ*: St adds *taihuntaihundfalt*. *þan*: “then,” as in the Greek.]

His disciples asked him, “What does this parable mean?”

[Note: [Col. 0619] His disciples asked him, saying, “What is this parable?”]

[Note: [Col. 0619] *gajuko*: St adds *tajuko*.]

He said, “To you it has been granted to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God; but to the others they are given in parables, so that, seeing, they may not see, and hearing, they may not understand.

[Note: [Col. 0619] Jesus said: “To you it has been granted to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God; but to the others they are given in parables, so that, seeing, they may not see, and hearing, they may not understand.”]

[Note: [Col. 0619] *ïesus*: see the note on Mark I, 42. *þiudinassaus*: J and St add *þiudanassaus*.]

Now this is the parable: the seed is the word of God.

[Note: [Col. 0619] Now this is the parable: the seed is the word of God.]

[Note: [Col. 0619] *þata ïst*: corresponds to all the Greek manuscripts.]

Those beside the road are those who hear.

[Note: [Col. 0619] But they
[Note: [Col. 0619] In this rock are those who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; but they have no roots. They believe for a time, and at the time of temptation they fall away.]

[Note: [Col. 0619] *ïze* for *ïzei*, as in Mark 9:1 and *sa ïze* in Matthew 5:32; see also the note on 10:5.—*vaurtins*: see the note on Mark 4:6.]

Then the devil comes and takes the word away from their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.

But those upon the rock are the ones who, when they hear, receive the word with joy; yet they have no roots. They believe for a time, and in the time of testing they fall away.

[Note: [Col. 0619] But that which fell among the thorns: these are those who hear, but, going away amid the cares, possessions, and pleasures of this life, are choked and bear no fruit.]

[Note: [Col. 0619] *þaiei*: thus the Argenteus manuscript; the editions add *þatei*. Otherwise the Greek manuscripts all have οἱ. See the Prolegomena, column 485.—*saurgom*: clearly so in the Argenteus manuscript; the editions add *saurjom*.—*afwapnand*: see the note on Mark 4:7.]

Those who believe for a while and, in a time of testing, fall away. But those among the thorns are those who hear and, going their way amid cares, riches, and pleasures of life, are choked and bear no fruit.

But that which is in the good soil: these are those who, hearing the word in a good and noble heart, hold fast to it and bear fruit with endurance.

[Note: [Col. 0619] *þulainai*: J. St. B. add *þuldinai*.]

They bear fruit and do not wither. But that in the good earth: these are those who, in a good heart, having heard the word, hold it fast and bear fruit with endurance.

[Note: [Col. 0619] No one lights a lamp and covers it with a vessel, or puts it under a bed; rather, he puts it on a lampstand, so that those entering may see the light.]

No one, after lighting a lamp, covers it with a vessel, or puts it under a bed; rather, he puts it on a lampstand, so that those entering may see the light.

[Note: [Col. 0619] For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, nor concealed that will not be known and come into the open.]

For nothing is secret that will not become manifest, nor hidden that will not be known and come into the open.

[Note: [Col. 0619] *ni auk*: J. St. add *niuh þan*.—*nih*: J. St. add *ni*.—*svekunþamma*: thus the Argenteus manuscript; J. St. B. add *svesunþamma*. Maresh, p. 456, and Lye read *svikunþamma*, correctly; the Goth used *i* and *e* interchangeably, as in *wileiks* and *weleiks*, *azitizo* and *azetizo*, *aggeljus* and *aggiljus*, and so forth.]

[Note: [Col. 0619] Consider, therefore, how you hear; for whoever has, to him it will be given, and whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him.]

[Note: [Col. 0620] *andqiþan ïmma*: J. St. add *duatgaggan*.]

So see how you hear. For whoever has, to him it will be given; and whoever does not have, even what he thinks he has will be taken away from him.

[Note: [Col. 0619] His mother and brothers came to him, but they could not approach him because of the crowd.]

[Note: [Col. 0619] And it was reported to him that your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wishing to see you.]

His mother and brothers came to him, but they could not get near him because of the crowd.

[Note: [Col. 0620] *ïmma*: Ulfila, the manuscripts, and the versions have the equivalent of the Greek λεγόντων, “saying.”—*þatei*: “that,” corresponding to the Greek ὅτι.—*gasaiwan*: B. adds *gasaivan*.—*gairnjandona*: J. omits *viljandans*, but places it before *þuk gasaiwan*, “wishing to see you”; St. has a lacuna before *þuk gasaiwan*.]

And it was reported to him: “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wishing to see you.”

[Note: [Col. 0619] But he answered and said to them: “My mother and my brothers are these: those who hear the word of God and do it.”]

[Note: [Col. 0620] *sind*: J. St. B. add *sindon*.]

But he answered and said to them: “My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it.”

Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wishing to see you. But he answered and said to them: “My mother and my brothers are these: those who hear the word of God and do it.”

[Note: [Col. 0619] It happened on one of those days that he entered a boat with his disciples and said to them: “Let us cross over this lake.” And they went.]

[Note: [Col. 0620] *þan*: “then,” corresponding to the Greek καί.—*þize*: J. St. add *þizai*.—*marisaiv*: J. St. B. add *marein*.]

It happened on one of those days that he entered a boat with his disciples and said to them: “Let us cross over this lake.” And they went.

[Note: [Col. 0619] Then, while they were sailing, he fell asleep, and a windstorm came down upon the lake; they were filled with water and endangered.]

[Note: [Col. 0620] *sve*: J. St. omit *o*.—*anasaisleiþ*: thus the Argenteus manuscript, though the *i* appears to have been erased; J. St. divide it twice; B. and Z. read *anasaislep*. See the note on 3:5.]

As they were sailing, a windstorm came down upon the lake, and they were being swamped and endangered.

[Note: [Col. 0619] They came to him and woke him, saying: “Teacher, we are perishing!”]

[Note: [Col. 0621] But he arose and rebuked the wind and the water; they ceased, and there was a calm.]

[Note: [Col. 0620] *duatgaggandans*: J. St. B. omit *at*.—*urraisidedun*: the editions have *usraisidedun*. In the Argenteus manuscript it is difficult to determine whether *urr-* or *usr-* is written; nevertheless, the form printed here is required by Gothic usage: *urrinnan*, *urrannjan*, *urruns*, *urreisan*, *urrists*. There is only one other passage, 2 Corinthians 6:11, where one manuscript correctly has *urrumnoda*, while another incorrectly reads *usrumnoda*.—*talzjand*: St. has a lacuna in place of this word; J., following certain Greek witnesses, includes it twice, but in the Argenteus manuscript no trace of the second occurrence can be found.]

They came to him and woke him, saying: “Teacher, we are perishing!” He arose, rebuked the wind and the water, and they ceased; and there was a calm.

[Note: [Col. 0621] Then he said to them: “Where is your faith?” But they were afraid and amazed, saying to one another: “Who then is this, that he commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him?”]

[Note: [Col. 0621] *siai sa*: found in all Greek manuscripts; Ulfila likewise has the equivalent of ἄρα, “then.”—*vatnam*: “to the waters,” corresponding in all Greek manuscripts to ὕδατι.]

He arose, rebuked the wind and the waves of the water; they ceased, and there was a calm. Then he said to them: “Where is your faith?” And they, afraid, were amazed and said to one another: “Who is this, that he commands even the winds and the water, and they obey him?”

[Note: [Col. 0621] And they sailed to the region of the Gadarenes, which lies opposite Galilee.]

[Note: [Col. 0621] *galeilaia*: J. adds *galilaia*.]

They sailed to the region of the Gadarenes, which lies opposite Galilee.

[Note: [Col. 0621] When he came ashore, a certain man from the town met him; he had demons for a long time, wore no clothing, and did not live in a house but in the tombs.]

[Note: [Col. 0621] *unhulþons*: J. substitutes *skohsla*, a marginal gloss, for the textual reading; B. combines *skohsla*, the gloss, with *unhulþons* in the text.]

When he had gone out onto the land, a certain man from the town met him. He had been possessed by demons for a long time; he wore no clothing, lived neither in a house nor elsewhere, but in the tombs.

[Note: [Col. 0621] When he saw Jesus, he cried out, fell before him, and said in a loud voice: “What have I to do with you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me.”]

[Note: [Col. 0621] *balvjais mis*: corresponding to the reading in all the Greek manuscripts.]

When he saw Jesus, he cried out, fell before him, and said in a loud voice: “What have I to do with you, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me.”

[Note: [Col. 0621] For he had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. It had seized him for a long time; he had been bound with iron chains and kept in fetters, but, breaking the chains, he was driven by the demon into the wilderness.]

[Note: [Col. 0621] *eisarnabandjom*: J. St. B. divide the word.—*vas*: “was,” the secondary form, as in all the Greek manuscripts.]

For he had commanded the unclean spirit to come out of the man. For it had seized him for a long time, and he had been bound with iron chains and fetters; but, breaking the bonds, he was driven by the demon into deserted places.

Jesus asked him, saying: “What is your name?” He said: “Legion,” because many demons had entered him.

[Note: [Col. 0621] *qiþands*: J. omits it.—*þein*: all the Greek manuscripts have σοί, “to you,” before *ïst*.—*harjis*: Ulfila renders the Greek-Latin *legio* with a Gothic word here, although in Mark 5:9 and 5:15 he writes *laigaion*. See *Skeireins* 49.2, where the author of that work renders the name of the apostle Peter with *stains*, “stone.”]

There was a legion, and he was breaking the chains; he was driven by the demon into deserted places.

Jesus asked him: “What is your name?” He said: “Legion,” because many demons had entered him.

[Note: [Col. 0621] And he begged him not to command them to go into the abyss.]

He asked him, saying: “What is your name?” He said: “Legion,” because many demons had entered him. And he begged him not to command them to go into the abyss.

[Note: [Col. 0621] There was there a large herd of pigs feeding on the mountain; and they begged him to allow them to enter into them, and he allowed them.]

[Note: [Col. 0621] *ïm*: the secondary form; J. St. add *ïn*, “into.”]

There was there a large herd of pigs feeding on the mountain. They begged him to allow them to enter into the pigs, and he allowed them.

[Note: [Col. 0621] The demons came out of the man and entered the pigs, and the herd ran down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.]

[Note: [Col. 0621] *suns*: “immediately,” as in all the Greek manuscripts.—*mann*: J. St. B. add *manna*, “the man.”—*galiþun*: J. omit *ïddjedun*, “went.”—*rann*: J. omit it and read *draus*, “fell,” leaving out the remainder up to *saiv*.—*so vriþus*: B. proposes the conjectural restoration *so hairda*, “the herd.”]

Immediately the demons came out of the man and entered the pigs; and the herd ran down the steep bank into the lake and was drowned.

[Note: [Col. 0621] When those tending them saw what had happened, they fled and reported it in the town and in the villages.]

[Note: [Col. 0622] *gaþlauhun*: J. St. add *gaplaujun*.—*baurg*: J. St. add *baurgi*.—*veihsa*: J. omit it and read *haiþjos*; St. has a lacuna.]

When those tending the pigs saw what had happened, they fled and reported it in the town and in the countryside.

[Note: [Col. 0621] They went out to see what had happened and came to Jesus; they found the man from whom the demons had gone out sitting, clothed, and in his right mind at the feet of Jesus, and they were afraid.]

[Note: [Col. 0622] *at ïesua*: St. has a lacuna.—*gavasidana*: J. St. add *gavasidona*.—*ïesuis*: J. St. B. omit *ïesua*.]

They went out to see what had happened and came to Jesus. They found the man from whom the demons had gone out sitting, clothed, and in his right mind at the feet of Jesus, and they were afraid.

[Note: [Col. 0621] Those who had seen it also told them how the demoniac had been healed.]

[Note: [Col. 0622] *þan ïm jah*: St. has a lacuna.—*ïm*: J. adds *du ïm*, “to them.”—*waiva ganas*: J. St. add *wai vas haileda*, “how he was healed.”]

Those who had seen it also told them how the demoniac had been healed.

[Note: [Col. 0621] All the inhabitants of the region of the Gadarenes begged him to depart from them, because they had been seized by great fear; but he entered the boat and turned back.]

[Note: [Col. 0622] *bedun ïna*: J. St. add *badun ïm*, “they begged him.”—*gaujans*: St. adds *manjans*.—*gaddarene*: thus the Argenteus manuscript; J. St. Ih. Z. read *gadarene*. See also Mark 5:1 and Luke 8:26.—*fairra sis*: J. St. add *us fram*, “away from them,” and then have a lacuna to the end of the verse.]

All the inhabitants of the region of the Gadarenes begged him to depart from them, because they had been seized by great fear. But he entered the boat and turned back.

[Note: [Col. 0621] The man from whom the demons had gone out begged him to let him remain with him; but Jesus dismissed him, saying:]

[Note: [Col. 0622] *baþ þan ïna*: St. has a lacuna.—*usïddjedun*: the Greek places *þos* before it.]

The man from whom the demons had gone out begged him to let him remain with him. But Jesus dismissed him, saying:

[Note: [Col. 0621] “Return to your house and tell how much God has done for you.” And he went through the whole town, proclaiming how much Jesus had done for him.]

[Note: [Col. 0622] *usspillo*: J. St. add *uspillo*.—*galaiþ and*: J. St. add *galaiþands*.—*baurg alla*: corresponds to all the Greek manuscripts.]

“Return to your house and tell how much God has done for you.” And he went through the whole town, proclaiming how much Jesus had done for him.

[Note: [Col. 0621] When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed him, for they were all waiting for him.]

[Note: [Col. 0622] *þizei*: J. St. omit *þize*.—*sah*: “and he”; Ulfila does not omit the Greek καί, as Sch. notes. Compare *sah* for καὶ αὐτός in 17:16 and 19:2; see also the note on John 18:26.—*gard*: St. adds *garda*.]

When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed him, for they were all waiting for him.

And behold, a man came whose name was Jairus. He was the ruler of the synagogue. He fell at the feet of Jesus and begged him to go into his house.

[Note: [Col. 0623] His only daughter was about twelve years old, and she died. As he went, the crowds pressed around him.]

[Note: [Col. 0623] *vintrive*: J. St. B. add *vintraive*.—*miþþanei—ïs*: J. adds *galeiþanti þanei þan ïna*; St. adds *begaiþ þanei þan ïna*.—*manageins*: St. has a lacuna.]

His only daughter was about twelve years old, and she died. As Jesus went, the crowds pressed around him.

There was a woman who had suffered from an issue of blood for twelve years. She had spent all her possessions on physicians, but no one had been able to heal her.

[Note: [Col. 0623] *lekjans*: J. St. omit *lei* and read *leikjans*.—*aigina*: J. St. B. add *aihna*.—*seinamma*: the Greek has “her own.”]

A woman who had suffered from an issue of blood for twelve years had spent all her possessions on physicians, but no one had been able to heal her.

[Note: [Col. 0623] Coming up behind him, she touched the fringe of his garment, and immediately the flow of her blood stopped.]

[Note: [Col. 0623] *du*: see the note on Mark 10:13.]

She came up behind him and touched the fringe of his garment, and immediately the flow of her blood stopped.

[Note: [Col. 0623] Jesus said: “Who touched me?” When all denied it, Peter and those with him said: “Teacher, the crowds surround you and press upon you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”]

Jesus said: “Who touched me?” When all denied it, Peter and those with him said: “Teacher, the crowds surround you and press upon you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”

[Note: [Col. 0623] Then Jesus said: “Someone touched me, for I knew that power had gone out from me.”]

Jesus said: “Someone touched me, for I knew that power had gone out from me.”

[Note: [Col. 0623] When the woman saw that she had not escaped notice, she came trembling and fell before him. Because she had touched him, she confessed before all the people how she had been healed immediately.]

[Note: [Col. 0623] *reirandei*: J. St. omit it; some Greek witnesses add “she came.”]

When the woman saw that she had not escaped notice, she came trembling and fell before him. In the presence of all the people, she told him why she had touched him and how she had been healed immediately.

[Note: [Col. 0623] Jesus said to her: “Daughter, take courage; your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”]

[Note: [Col. 0623] *ïesus*: the Greek has the article, “the Jesus.”]

He said to her: “Daughter, take courage; your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”

[Note: [Col. 0623] While he was still speaking, someone from the ruler of the synagogue’s household came and said to him: “Your daughter has died. Do not trouble the teacher.”]

[Note: [Col. 0623] *nauhþan*: the editions add *div*.—*gaggiþ*: St. omits the final *þ* and reads *gaggid*.—*manne*: “of a man,” as in all the Greek manuscripts.—*þis fauramaþleis*: this genitive does not depend on the preposition *fram*, “from,” but on an implied noun *mannam*, “the man”; compare the notes on 19:7, Matthew 27:57, and John 16:32.—*synagogeis*: it appears that *synagogais* should be read, as in verse 41 and John 9:22.—*þeina*: J. adds *þein*.]

While he was still speaking, someone from the household of the ruler of the synagogue came and said to him: “Your daughter has died. Do not trouble the teacher.”

[Note: [Col. 0623] But Jesus, hearing this, answered him: “Do not fear; only believe, and she will be healed.”]

[Note: [Col. 0623] When he entered the house, he did not allow anyone to enter except Peter, James, John, the girl’s father, and her mother.]

[Note: [Col. 0623] *aino hun ïnngaggan*: corresponds to the reading in all the Greek manuscripts; for *ainohun*, see also the note on Mark 9:8.—*ïakobu—ïohannen*: corresponds to the Greek; compare 9:28.]

Jesus, hearing this, answered him: “Do not fear; only believe, and she will be healed.”

When he entered the house, he did not allow anyone to enter except Peter, James, John, the girl’s father, and her mother.

[Note: [Col. 0623] They were all weeping and mourning for her. Then he said: “Do not weep, for she has not died but is sleeping.”]

[Note: [Col. 0624] *unte*: “for,” corresponding to the Greek γάρ.]

They were all weeping and mourning for her. Then he said: “Do not weep, for she has not died but is sleeping.”

[Note: [Col. 0623] They mocked him, knowing that she had died.]

[Note: [Col. 0624] *gasaiwandans*: “seeing,” corresponding in all the Greek manuscripts to εἰδότες, “knowing.”]

They laughed at him, knowing that she had died.

[Note: [Col. 0623] Then he put them all outside, took her by the hand, and called out, saying: “Girl, arise!”]

[Note: [Col. 0624] *allans ut*: corresponds to all the Greek manuscripts.]

He put them all outside, took her by the hand, and called out, saying: “Girl, arise!”

[Note: [Col. 0623] Her spirit returned, and she arose immediately; and he commanded that food be given to her.]

[Note: [Col. 0624] *ustoþ*: J. St. read *usstoþ*, which is indeed more correct, but contrary here to the authority of the Argenteus manuscript; see the note on Mark 3:13.]

Her spirit returned, and she arose immediately. He commanded that food be given to her.

[Note: [Col. 0623] Her parents were astonished; but he commanded them to tell no one what had happened.]

[Note: [Col. 0624] *qiþeina*: for *qeþeina*. The same form occurs in 9:21 and 17:6, *qiþeiþ*. Compare *usdribeina* in 9:40, *qimi* in 7:3, *galagidideina* in 5:18, *tavidideina* in 6:11, and *ufkunþidun* in Nehemiah 6:16; see Grimm I.36.]

Her parents were astonished, but he commanded them to tell no one what had happened.

[Note: [Col. 0623] Calling the twelve apostles together, he gave them power and authority over all demons and to heal diseases.]

[Note: [Col. 0624] *apaustauluns*: “apostles,” corresponding to the Greek.]

Calling the twelve apostles together, he gave them power and authority over all demons and to heal diseases.

[Note: [Col. 0623] He sent them to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.]

[Note: [Col. 0624] *allans*: “all,” corresponding to the Greek.]

He sent them to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.

[Note: [Col. 0623] And he said to them: “Take nothing for the journey: neither staff, nor bag, nor bread, nor money; do not have two tunics.”]

[Note: [Col. 0624] *nih*: Z. adds *ni*.—*valuns*: “staff,” corresponding to the Greek ῥάβδον.—*nih hlaib*: J. omits the second *nih*; Z. adds *ni*.—*nihþan*: Z. adds *ni þan*.]

He said to them: “Take nothing for the journey: neither staff, nor bag, nor bread, nor money; do not have two tunics.”

[Note: [Col. 0623] Whatever house you enter, remain there and depart from there.]

[Note: [Col. 0624] *þanei*: St. adds *þainei*.]

“Whatever house you enter, remain there and depart from there.”

[Note: [Col. 0623] And wherever they do not receive you, when you leave that town, shake the dust from your feet as a testimony against them.]

[Note: [Col. 0624] *and all*: J. St. B. add an uncertain form, apparently *jct*.]

“Wherever they do not receive you, when you leave that town, shake the dust from your feet as a testimony against them.”

They went through the villages, proclaiming the good news and healing everywhere.

[Note: [Col. 0623] Herod the tetrarch heard of all that was happening through him and was perplexed, because some were saying that John had risen from the dead.]

[Note: [Col. 0624] *taitrarkes*: the Argenteus manuscript has *Hz.*; the editions add *taitarkes*. See 3:19.]

Herod the tetrarch heard of everything that was happening through him and was perplexed, because some were saying that John had risen from the dead.

[Note: [Col. 0625] Some said that Elijah had appeared; others that one of the ancient prophets had risen.]

[Note: [Col. 0625] *sumai—qeþun*: “some—said,” corresponding in all the Greek manuscripts to ὑπό τινων λέγεσθαι, “to be said by some.” At verse 7 the Goth rendered διὰ τὸ λέγεσθαι ὑπό τινων as *unte qeþun sumai*, “because some said”; here he repeats *qeþun* for clarity. Conversely, he omits the following ὅτι, “that,” which all the Greek manuscripts read.—*sumaiþ-þan*: thus the Argenteus manuscript; the editions add *sumai uþþan*.]

Some said that Elijah had appeared; others that one of the ancient prophets had risen.

[Note: [Col. 0625] Herod said: “John I beheaded; but who is this about whom I hear such things?” And he sought to see him.]

[Note: [Col. 0625] *ïohannau*: Z. adds *johannau*. The unusual ending *-au* is noteworthy; it belongs only to nouns ending in *-us*. Elsewhere the forms are *ïohanne* or *ïohannen*.—*ïst*: Z. adds *ïs*.—*ïna gasaiwan*: corresponds to the Greek.]

Herod said: “John I beheaded; but who is this about whom I hear such things?” And he sought to see him.

[Note: [Col. 0625] The apostles returned and reported to him all that they had done. Taking them with him, he withdrew privately to a deserted place belonging to a town called Bethsaida.]

[Note: [Col. 0625] *namnidaizos*: J. adds *namndaizos*, St. *mamndaizos*.—*baidsaiïdan*: an obvious error for *baidsaïdan* or *baidsaeidan*; see 10:13. As for *baidsaïdan* instead of *bedsaïdan*, see the note on Matthew 8:28.]

The apostles returned and reported to him all that they had done. Taking them with him, he withdrew privately to a deserted place belonging to a town called Bethsaida.

[Note: [Col. 0625] The crowds, learning this, followed him. Taking them with him, he spoke to them about the kingdom of God and healed those who needed healing.]

[Note: [Col. 0625] *þo*: “these things,” corresponding to the Greek.—*þarbans*: St. adds *þarbands*.]

The crowds, learning this, followed him. Taking them with him, he spoke to them about the kingdom of God and healed those who needed healing.

[Note: [Col. 0625] The day began to decline. The twelve came to him and said: “Send the crowd away, so that they may go to the surrounding villages and farms, find lodging, and buy food for themselves, for we are here in a deserted place.”]

[Note: [Col. 0625] *juþan*: “already,” corresponding to the Greek; the Goth uses *jah* for both δέ and ἤδη, as Mill also observed.—*du ïmma*: “to him,” found in all the Greek manuscripts.—*jah bugjaina sis matins*: “and buy food for themselves,” corresponding to the Greek καὶ εὕρωσιν ἐπισιτισμόν; Ulfila agrees with Brix.]

The day had already begun to decline. The twelve came to him and said: “Send the crowd away, so that they may go to the surrounding villages and farms, find lodging, and buy food for themselves, for we are here in a deserted place.”

[Note: [Col. 0625] He said to them: “You give them something to eat.” But they said to him: “We have no more than five loaves and two fish—unless perhaps we should go and buy food for all these people.”]

[Note: [Col. 0626] *du ïmma*: “to him,” as in all the Greek manuscripts.—*fiskos*: St. adds *siskos*.—*niba þau þatei*: “unless perhaps,” as in all the Greek manuscripts, εἰ μή τι. If the Goth had read εἰ μή τι, he would have written either only *niba þau*, as in 1 Corinthians 7:5, or *nibai aufto*, as in manuscript A of 2 Corinthians 13:5. It therefore appears that he read εἰ μή τι or εἰ μὴ ὅτι; compare *niba þatei* in 2 Corinthians 12:13 and Ephesians 4:9.—*veis gaggandans*: corresponds to the Greek.—*manaseidai*: the Argenteus manuscript has *managein* in the margin, a synonymous word, which J. St. incorporated into the text.]

He said to them: “You give them something to eat.” But they said: “We have no more than five loaves and two fish—unless perhaps we should go and buy food for all these people.”

[Note: [Col. 0625] For there were about five thousand men. He said to his disciples: “Make them recline in groups of about fifty.”]

[Note: [Col. 0626] *vaire*: all the Greek manuscripts place this before *fimf*, “five.”—*kubituns*: thus the Argenteus manuscript; B. Ih. Z. add *kumbituns*.—*warjanoh*: thus clearly the Argenteus manuscript; the editions add *warjamoh*.—*fimftiguns*: J. St. add *fimftijuns*.]

There were about five thousand men. He said to his disciples: “Make them recline in groups of about fifty.”

And they did so, and made them all recline.

[Note: [Col. 0625] He took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up toward heaven, blessed them, broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the crowd.]

They made them recline in groups of about fifty. He took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up toward heaven, blessed them, broke them, and gave them to the disciples to set before the crowd.

[Note: [Col. 0625] They ate and were all satisfied, and what remained of the fragments was gathered up: twelve baskets.]

They ate and were all satisfied. What remained of the fragments was gathered up: twelve baskets.

[Note: [Col. 0625] While he was praying privately, his disciples came to him, and he asked them, saying: “Who do the crowds say that I am?”]

[Note: [Col. 0626] *gamotitedun*: “they came to meet,” corresponding to the Greek συνῆσαν; B. perceptively suspects that Ulfila read συνήντησαν.—*ïs*: “his,” corresponding to the Greek.—*frah*: J. St. B. add *froh*.—*visan*: all the Greek manuscripts place it after *manageins*.]

It happened that, while he was praying privately, his disciples came to him, and he asked them: “Who do the crowds say that I am?”

[Note: [Col. 0625] They answered: “John the Baptist; others say Elijah; others that one of the ancient prophets has risen.”]

[Note: [Col. 0626] *heleian*: J. St. omit the first *e* and read *helian*, as also in verse 54.]

They answered: “John the Baptist; others say Elijah; others that one of the ancient prophets has risen.”

[Note: [Col. 0625] He said to them: “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered: “The Christ of God.”]

[Note: [Col. 0626] *þu—guþs*: “you—the Christ of God,” corresponding to the Greek τὸν Χριστὸν τοῦ θεοῦ; Ulfila agrees with the Latin versions.]

He said to them: “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered: “The Christ of God.”

[Note: [Col. 0625] But he rebuked them and commanded them to tell this to no one.]

[Note: [Col. 0626] *qiþeina*: see the note on 8:56.]

But he rebuked them and commanded them to tell this to no one.

[Note: [Col. 0625] He said: “The Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and rise on the third day.”]

[Note: [Col. 0626] *uskusans*: J. St. B. add *uskesans*.—*usqiman*: see Grimm, *Grammatik* IV.943.]

He said: “The Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, chief priests, and scribes, be killed, and rise on the third day.”

[Note: [Col. 0625] He said to all: “If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross each day, and follow me.”]

[Note: [Col. 0627] *dag wanoh*: J. St. B. add an uncertain form, apparently *jct*.]

He said to all: “If anyone wishes to come after me, let him deny himself, take up his cross each day, and follow me.”

[Note: [Col. 0627] For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it; but whoever loses his life for my sake will save it.]

For whoever wishes to save his life will lose it; but whoever loses his life for my sake will save it.

[Note: [Col. 0627] What profit is it for a man to gain the whole world, yet lose or harm himself?]

What profit is it for a man to gain the whole world, yet lose or harm himself?

[Note: [Col. 0627] For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when he comes in his glory, and in the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.]

[Note: [Col. 0627] *aiþþau*: “or,” corresponding in all the Greek manuscripts to καί, “and.”—*sik biþe*: J. St. add *urriþe*. The same editors, contrary to Z., do not read *skammaid* but correctly *skamaid*.—*vulþu*: for *vulþau* (which B. printed in the text), see the note on 1:54.—*veihane*: J. St. add *veihame*.—*aggele*: thus the Argenteus manuscript and J. St.; B. Ih. Z. add *aggile*. See 15:10.]

For whoever is ashamed of me and of my words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when he comes in his glory, and in the glory of the Father and of the holy angels.

[Note: [Col. 0627] But I tell you truly: there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God.]

[Note: [Col. 0627] *sunja*: “truly,” corresponding in all the Greek manuscripts to ἀληθῶς.—*dauþau*: and soon afterward *þiudinassau*; see the note on Mark 7:32.]

But I tell you truly: there are some standing here who will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God.

[Note: [Col. 0627] About eight days after these words, he took Peter, James, and John and went up the mountain to pray.]

[Note: [Col. 0627] *vaurþun*: “they came to pass,” corresponding to all the Greek manuscripts except one manuscript cited by Mill, which agrees with the Gothic.—*ahtau*: Ulfila and the manuscripts have the equivalent of καί.—*ïakobu—ïohannen*: see the note on 8:51.]

About eight days after these words, he took Peter, James, and John and went up the mountain to pray.

[Note: [Col. 0627] And it happened that, while he prayed, the appearance of his face became different and his clothing white and shining.]

[Note: [Col. 0627] *baþ*: J. St. omit *bad*.]

While he prayed, the appearance of his face became different and his clothing white and shining.

[Note: [Col. 0627] And behold, two men were speaking with him; they were Moses and Elijah.]

And behold, two men were speaking with him; they were Moses and Elijah.

[Note: [Col. 0627] They appeared in glory and spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish in Jerusalem.]

[Note: [Col. 0627] *urruns*: J. St. B. add *urrune*.—*þai*: “they,” corresponding to οἱ in all the Greek manuscripts; see the Prolegomena, column 485.]

They appeared in glory and spoke of his departure, which he was about to accomplish in Jerusalem.

[Note: [Col. 0627] Peter and those with him were weighed down by sleep. When they awoke, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.]

Peter and those with him were weighed down by sleep. When they awoke, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.

[Note: [Col. 0627] When the men were separating from him, Peter said to Jesus: “Teacher, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah”—not knowing what he was saying.]

[Note: [Col. 0627] *afskaiskaidun*: J. St. Hz. Z. add *afskaidun*. Since that form cannot be derived from *afskaidan*, the reading of the Argenteus manuscript must be defended with Benzelius, who correctly compares *maimait* and *lailaik*; add *haihait* and *aiaik*. See Grimm I.840.—*gavaurkjaima*: J. St. add *gavaurkjaim*.—*jah*: Z. adds *jai*.]

When the men were separating from him, Peter said to Jesus: “Teacher, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three tents: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah”—not knowing what he was saying.

[Note: [Col. 0627] As he was saying this, a cloud came and overshadowed them; and they were afraid when they entered the cloud.]

[Note: [Col. 0627] *qemun—milhmin*: the Argenteus manuscript has in the margin *jah at ïm ïn milhmam atgaggandam*, “and as they entered into the clouds.” J. incorrectly placed this in the text as *qemun. jah at ïm ïn milhmin atgaggandun*, and B. as *qemun. jah at ïm ïn þamma milhmin atgaggandam*. No Greek manuscript follows the order of the marginal gloss; especially objectionable is *jah* at the beginning, unless the glossator intended to write *jah faurhtidedun at ïm*, “and they were afraid when they entered.”]

As he was saying this, a cloud came and overshadowed them; and they were afraid when they entered the cloud.

[Note: [Col. 0627] A voice came from the cloud, saying: “This is my Son, my beloved one; listen to him.”]

[Note: [Col. 0627] The words should be arranged as indicated here: *varþ miþþanei* belongs later, as Z. correctly observed. The unusual word order may be compared with 14:28, *ïzvara was raihtis*, and see also the notes on 14:28 and 17:17.—*gasewum*: St. adds *gaseiwun*.]

A voice came from the cloud, saying: “This is my Son, my beloved one; listen to him.”

[Note: [Col. 0627] When the voice came, Jesus was found alone. They kept silent and told no one in those days anything of what they had seen.]

[Note: [Col. 0628] *varþ miþþanei*: these words must be transposed, as Z. already correctly noted; compare the note above.]

When the voice came, Jesus was found alone. They kept silent and told no one in those days anything of what they had seen.

[Note: [Col. 0627] The next day, when they had come down from the mountain, a large crowd met him.]

[Note: [Col. 0628] *ïn þamma daga*: “on that day,” corresponding to the Greek ἐν τῇ ἑξῆς ἡμέρᾳ, “on the following day”; J. St. accordingly omit *ïn þamma daga* and print *ïn þamma afar daga*, as in 7:11.—*atgaggandam*: J. St. add *afgaggandam*.—*fairgunja*: J. St. omit the article *þamma*.]

The next day, when they came down from the mountain, a large crowd met him.

[Note: [Col. 0627] And behold, a man from the crowd cried out, saying: “Teacher, I beg you to look at my son, for he is my only child.”]

[Note: [Col. 0628] *manna*: J. St. omit *vair*, “man,” and then have a lacuna to the end of the verse.—*ïnsaiwan*: B. adds *ïnsaivan*; Ulfila and the manuscripts read the Greek ἐπιβλέψαι, “to look upon.”—*sunu*: B. omits *sunau*; see the note on 1:54.—*meinamma*: B. adds *minamma*.—*mis ïst*: corresponds to all the Greek manuscripts.]

And behold, a man from the crowd cried out, saying: “Teacher, I beg you to look at my son, for he is my only child.”

[Note: [Col. 0627] And behold, an unclean spirit seizes him; suddenly he cries out and convulses him with foaming, and it scarcely departs from him, bruising him.]

[Note: [Col. 0628] *unhrains*: “unclean,” J. St. omit it, although it is found in the Greek manuscripts.—*anaks hropjiþ*: J. omits it and reads *sunsaiv ufhropjiþ*; St. adds *sunfaiv ufhropjiþ*. As for *hropjiþ* (for *hropeiþ*), Grimm—[reference incomplete in the supplied text].]

I. 847 appears suspect. — *tahjiþ*] J. St. have a lacuna up to *ïmma*. — *waþon*] B. *waþ..*. — *aflinniþ*] B. *afleiþiþ*. Although this whole page of Codex Argenteus can scarcely be read, and the verb *aflinnan* occurs nowhere else, while *afleiþan* is used in the same sense at M. VII, 23, Benzelius’s reading should nevertheless not be admitted into the text. The translator frequently uses so-called *ἅπαξ εἰρημένα* (“words occurring only once”) in this Gospel, and close inspection of the manuscript reveals certain traces of *aflinnan*, first discovered by lh.

“My son; for he is my only one. And behold, an unclean spirit takes him, and suddenly he cries out, and it convulses him with foam; it scarcely departs from him, bruising him.”

[Col. 0629] “And I asked your disciples to cast it out, and they could not.” — *siponjans þeinans*] J. St. add *siponjam þeinaim*. — *usdribeina*] J. St. add *usvairpana*; B. *usdreibeina*, correctly indeed, but see VIII, 56. — *ïmma*] J. St. add *ïna*. — *mahtedun*] J. adds *mahtidedun*, St. *mahtidun*; in Codex Argenteus it cannot be determined whether *mahtidedun* or *mahtededun* was written, but both are wrong. The same error was present at 2 Cor. III, 7, where *mahtededeina* was read.

“And it convulses him with foam, and the unclean spirit scarcely departs from him, bruising him. And I asked your disciples to cast it out, and they could not.”

[Col. 0629] “But Jesus answered and said: O unbelieving and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you and endure you? Bring your son here.” — *qaþ*] J. St. add *du ïm*. — *kuni*] J. St. add *kunni*, as at v. 43. — *ïnvindo*] J. St. have a lacuna up to *gabrak ïna* in the following verse. — *attiuh*] Z. adds *atþiuh*; B. *at . . .* — *hidrei*] B. omits; Greek has *πρὸς* before *þana*.

But Jesus answered and said, “O unbelieving and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you and endure you? Bring your son here.”

[Col. 0629] “While he was still coming, the demon dashed him down and convulsed him; but Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him to his father.” — *þaruh*] B. omits; adds *nauh þanuh*, “still,” and reads: “as he was still coming, it convulsed him.” — *ahmin*] J. St. add *ahman*.

And while he was still coming, the demon dashed him down and convulsed him. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him to his father.

[Col. 0629] “And all were astonished at this greatness of God. But while all marvelled at everything which Jesus did, Peter said: Lord, why could we not cast this out? But Jesus said: This kind does not go out except by prayer and fasting. And he said to his disciples:” — *qaþ paitrus—fastubnja*] “Peter said—fasting”; omitted by all Greek manuscripts. Ulfilas agrees with the Latin versions from the parallel passages Mt. XVII, 19–21 and Mk. IX, 28 ff. — *kuni*] See v. 41. — *þan*] The final *autem* (“but”) is omitted by all Greek manuscripts.

And all were astonished at the greatness of God. But while all marvelled at everything Jesus did, Peter said, “Lord, why could we not cast this out?” But Jesus said, “This kind does not go out except through prayers and fasting.” Then he said to his disciples:

[Col. 0629] “Put these words into your ears, for the Son of Man is to be delivered into the hands of men.”

“Put these words into your ears: for the Son of Man is to be delivered into the hands of men.”

[Col. 0629] “But they did not understand this saying; and it was hidden from them, so that they might not understand it, and they were afraid to ask him concerning this saying.”

But they did not understand this saying; it was hidden from them so that they might not understand it, and they were afraid to ask him about it.

[Col. 0629] “Then a thought entered into them: which of them might be greatest?” — [Col. 0630] *ïze—vesi*] According to all Greek manuscripts.

Then a thought entered them: which of them might be greatest?

[Col. 0629] “But Jesus, seeing the thought of their heart, took a child and set him before himself.” — [Col. 0630] *gasatida*] Ulfilas omits *αὐτό*.

But Jesus, seeing the thought of their heart, took a child and set it before himself.

[Col. 0629] “And he said to them: Whoever receives this child in my name receives me; and whoever receives me receives him who sent me. For he who is least among all of you, he becomes great.” — [Col. 0630] *sandjandan*] J. St. add *sandjandin*. — *visands*] Greek places it after *ïzvis*. — *allaim*] J. St. add *allan*.

And he said to them, “Whoever receives this child in my name receives me; and whoever receives me receives him who sent me. For he who is least among all of you, he becomes great.”

[Col. 0629] “And John answered and said: Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we forbade him, because he does not follow with us.” — [Col. 0630] *ana*] J. St. omit *ïn*. — *þeinamma namin*] According to all Greek manuscripts.

Then John answered, “Teacher, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we forbade him, because he does not follow with us.”

[Col. 0629] “And Jesus said to them: Do not forbid him; for he who is not against you is for you. For there is no one among men who does not perform a mighty work in my name.” — [Col. 0630] *ïm*] “to them”; Greek has *αὐτόν*, “him.” — *ni ainshun—meinamma*] “There is no one—my”; J. St. omit it, together with all Greek manuscripts. Ulfilas agrees with the Latin versions from the parallel passage Mk. IX, 39.

And Jesus said to them, “Do not forbid him; for he who is not against you is for you. For there is no one among men who does not perform a mighty work in my name.”

[Col. 0629] “And it came to pass, when the days of his assumption were fulfilled, that he fixed his face to go to Jerusalem.” — [Col. 0630] *usfulnodedun*] Hz. Z. *usfullnodedun*; see II, 21. — *andanumtais*] Thus Codex Argenteus, B., H., Z.; J. St. add *andanumftais*; see Rom. XI, 15.

And it came to pass, when the days of his assumption were fulfilled, that he fixed his face to go to Jerusalem.

[Col. 0629] “And he sent messengers before himself; and they went and entered a village of Samaritans, to prepare for him.”

And he sent messengers before himself; and they went and entered a Samaritan village in order to prepare for him.

[Col. 0629] “And they did not receive him, because his face was going toward Jerusalem.”

And they did not receive him, because his face was directed toward Jerusalem.

[Col. 0629] “And when his disciples James and John saw this, they said: Lord, do you wish that we should say, Let fire come down from heaven and consume them, as Elijah also did?” — [Col. 0630] *gasaiwandans*] St. adds *gasaiwands*. — *ïakubos*] J. St. add *ïakobos*. — *heleias*] See v. 19.

When his disciples James and John saw this, they said, “Lord, do you wish that we should say, ‘Let fire come down from heaven and consume them,’ as Elijah also did?”

[Col. 0629] “But he turned and rebuked them and said to them: Do you not know whose spirit you are?” — [Col. 0630] *du ïm*] “to them,” omitted in Greek. — *niu*] J. adds *niu*. — *sijuþ*] Ulfilas, with the manuscripts, omits “you.”

But he turned, rebuked them, and said to them, “Do you not know whose spirit you are?”

[Col. 0629] “For the Son of Man did not come to destroy lives but to save them. And they went into another village.” — [Col. 0630] *unte—nasjan*] “for—to save,” omitted in Greek. — *saivalom*] Ulfilas, with the versions, omits *ἀνθρώπων*, “of men.”

“For the Son of Man did not come to destroy lives, but to save them.” And they went into another village.

[Col. 0629] “And it came to pass, as they were going on the road, that someone said to him: I will follow you wherever you go, Lord.” — [Col. 0630] *þiswaduh*] J. St. add *þuswaduh*.

As they went along the road, someone said to him, “I will follow you wherever you go, Lord.”

[Col. 0629–0631] “And Jesus said to him: Foxes have dens, and birds of heaven have resting-places; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”

Jesus said to him, “Foxes have dens, and birds of heaven have resting-places; but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”

[Col. 0631] “But he said to another: Follow me. But he said: Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father.”

Then he said to another, “Follow me.” But he said, “Lord, permit me first to go and bury my father.”

[Col. 0631] “Jesus said to him: Let the dead bury their own dead; but go and proclaim the kingdom of God.”

Jesus said to him, “Let the dead bury their own dead; but go and proclaim the kingdom of God.”

[Col. 0631] “And another also said: I will follow you, Lord; but first permit me to bid farewell to those who are in my house.” — *þaim þaiei sind*] Thus Codex Argenteus; J. adds *þammei vesind*, St. *þaimmei vesind*, B. *þaimei veisind*.

Another said, “I will follow you, Lord; but first permit me to bid farewell to those who are in my house.”

[Col. 0631] “But Jesus said to him: No one who puts his hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.” — *ana—guþs*] J. St. have a lacuna. — *saiwands*] B. adds *saivands*. — *gatils*] B. has a lacuna and conjectured *ni fagrs*. Ih. has correctly restored this extremely difficult passage of Codex Argenteus; compare Mk. VI, 21.

Jesus said to him, “No one who puts his hand to the plough and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”

[Col. 0631] “After this the Lord appointed seventy others also and sent them two by two before his face into every city and place where he intended to go.” — *ustaiknida*] J. St. B. add *usmarkoda*. — *anþarans sibuntehund*] J. St. add *anþarana sibuntiguns*; B. *anþarans sibuntiguns*. — *ïns*, to the end of the verse] J. St. B. have a lacuna.

After this the Lord appointed seventy others also and sent them two by two before himself into every city and place where he intended to go.

[Col. 0631] “And he said to them: The harvest is great, but the labourers few. Pray therefore the Lord of the harvest that he may send labourers into his harvest.” — *ïm*] J. St. add *ïmma*. — *asans*] J. St. add *sa asa*. — *ei*] St. omits. — *ussatjai*] B. *ussandjai*, as in the parallel passage Mt. IX, 38; compare Mk. I, 43. Yet the reading of Codex Argenteus should not be rejected in favour of that excellent conjecture; compare Mk. XII, 19, where *ussatjan* = *ἐξαναστῆσαι*, “to raise up.” — *vaurstvjans*] The final form in Codex Argenteus is *vaurstvjands*; a similar scribal error occurs at 2 Cor. IX, 4; X, 18. — *þo*] J. St. B. omit. — *seina*] J. St. add *seinamma*.

And he said to them, “The harvest is great, but the labourers are few. Pray therefore the Lord of the harvest to send labourers into his harvest.”

[Col. 0631] “Go; behold, I send you as lambs in the midst of wolves.”

“Go; behold, I send you as lambs in the midst of wolves.”

[Col. 0631] “Carry neither purse nor bag nor shoes; greet no one on the road.” — *pugg*] J. St. B. omit *gairda*. — *nih*] St. adds *ni*. — *gaskohe*] This appears to be how the word is written in Codex Argenteus, but its final letters have faded so completely that they can no longer be read. The accepted reading (J. St. B. omit *skohe*) does not seem correct. Although variation of case causes no difficulty (see VII, 21), it is highly doubtful whether a plural of *gaskoh* (“shoe,” French *chaussure*) can be accepted. At XV, 22 Ulfilas renders Greek *ὑποδήματα* by singular *gaskoh*; especially for that reason, *gaskoh* should be preferred here also. — *ni*] [Col. 0632] Ulfilas omits Greek *καί*, “and”; from here to the end of the verse J. St. B. have a lacuna.

Carry neither purse nor bag nor shoes, and greet no one on the road.

[Col. 0631] “Into whatever house you enter, first say: Peace to this house.” — [Col. 0632] *ïn þane gardei*] “into whatever house,” thus Codex Argenteus; Ih. Z. add *ïn þana gard ei*, J. St. B. *ïn þane gard ei*. Ih.’s reading may indeed be defended from Neh. V, 14, *þamma daga ei*, “on the day in which,” where *ei* is used for the relative pronoun *þammei*, or rather is detached from the demonstrative pronoun, so that it stands for *þammei daga*. But because Codex Argenteus clearly reads *þane*, not *þana*, this passage must be explained according to Gothic usage (see vv. 8 and 10, *ïn þoei baurge*; compare 1 Cor. XII, 22): *þane* is written for *þanei*, as elsewhere *miþþane*, *blotande*, *þoze*, *þize*, and *þataine* occur for *miþþanei*, *blotandei*, *þozei*, *þizei*, and *þatainei* (Lk. II, 43; II, 37; XIX, 37; 1 Cor. VIII, 11; 2 Cor. XII, 13; Skeir. 37, 16). See also 2 Thess. III, 17 and Lk. VIII, 13. Likewise *gardei* is written for *garde*; see III, 5. Thus the phrase must be translated “into whatever house.” Ulfilas omits Greek *δέ*; perhaps the scribe omitted *þan* because of the preceding *þane*. Compare Mt. IX, 16; Mk. X, 39, 42; Rom. IX, 15. — *ïnngaggaiþ*] J. St. B. add *ïngaggiþ*; thence to *gavairþjis* in the following verse they have a lacuna.

Into whatever house you enter, first say, “Peace to this house.”

[Col. 0631] “And if a son of peace is there, your peace shall rest upon him; but if not, it shall return to you.”

And if a son of peace is there, your peace shall rest upon him; but if not, it shall return to you.

[Col. 0631] “Remain in that house, eating and drinking what is with them; for the labourer is worthy of his wage. Do not go from house to house.” — [Col. 0632] *ïst*] Greek places it after *seinaizos*.

Remain in that house, eating and drinking what is with them, for the labourer is worthy of his wage. Do not go from house to house.

[Col. 0631] “And into whatever city you enter and they receive you, eat what is set before you.” — [Col. 0632] *faurlagido*] J. St. add *fauralagido*.

Into whatever city you enter, if they receive you, eat what is set before you.

[Col. 0631] “And heal the sick in it, and say to them: The kingdom of God has come near to you.” — [Col. 0632] *ïnngaggaiþ*] St. adds *ïngaggaiþ*.

Heal those sick in it, and say to them, “The kingdom of God has come near to you.”

[Col. 0631] “But into whatever city you enter and they do not receive you, go out into its streets and say:”

But into whatever city you enter, if they do not receive you, go out into its streets and say:

[Col. 0631] “Even the dust that clings to us from your city we wipe from our feet against you; nevertheless know this, that the kingdom of God has come near to you.” — [Col. 0632] *ana fotuns unsarans*] “from our feet,” omitted in Greek. — *sveþauh*] J. St. add various readings, as J. does also at vv. 14 and 20. — *ana ïzvis*] “against you,” omitted in Greek. — *þiudangardi*] St. adds *þiudangardja*.

“Even the dust that clings to us from your city we wipe from our feet against you; nevertheless know this, that the kingdom of God has come near to you.”

[Col. 0631] “I tell you: for Sodom it shall be more tolerable on that day than for that city.”

I tell you that it shall be more tolerable for Sodom on that day than for that city.

[Col. 0631–0633] “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! He said to him, “You have answered correctly; do this and you shall live.”

But he, wishing to justify himself, said to Jesus, “And who is my neighbour?”

[Col. 0633] “Jesus answered and said: A man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers, who stripped him and inflicted wounds . . .” — [Col. 0634] *manna*] Ulfilas omits Greek *τις*, “a certain.” — *ïaireikon*] Thus Codex Argenteus; editions add *ïaireikom*. — *þaiei*] J. St. add *þaei*. — *biraubodedun*] “stripped,” Greek *ἐκδύσαντες*. — *analag.*] Thus far Codex Argenteus; J. St. Z. restore the complete *analagjandans*.

Jesus answered and said, “A man went down from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell among robbers, who stripped him and inflicted wounds . . .”

“But when you are invited, go and recline in the lowest place, so that, when the one who invited you comes, he may say to you: Friend, go up higher. Then you shall have honour before those reclining with you.” — [Col. 0634] *hauhis*] “higher”; scholars who took it as a genitive, “of the high,” were mistaken. Grimm, having made the same determination at III, 88, p. 591, correctly recognized it as a comparative adverb.

But when you are invited, go and recline in the lowest place, so that, when the one who invited you comes, he may say to you, “Friend, go up higher.” Then you shall have honour before those reclining with you.

[Col. 0635] “For everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled, and he who humbles himself shall be exalted.” — *silban*] J. St. add *silba*. They ought not to have criticized lh. because the construction would require the accusative; rather, Gothic usage—departing from the rules of Latin grammar (see Ramshorn, *Latin Grammar*, p. 523)—requires it. For many similar passages see 2 Cor. V, 12.

For everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled, and he who humbles himself shall be exalted.

St. add *gabeijans*. — *aftra haitaina*] J. B. Z. add a conjunction; see Mk. VIII, 25. — *þuk*] Greek places it before *aftra*.

And you shall be blessed, because they have nothing with which to repay you; for you shall be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.

VII, 3, where *gasviltan* = *συναποθανεῖν*, while another manuscript has *miþgasviltan*.

When one of those reclining heard this, he said to him, “Blessed is he who eats bread in the kingdom of God.”

Then the Lord said to him, “A certain man made a great supper and invited many.”

The servant came and reported these things to his master. Then the master of the house became angry and said to his servant, “Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in here the poor, disabled, blind, and lame.”

[Col. 0635] “And the servant said: Lord, it has been done as you commanded, and there is still room.” — *stads ïst*] St. omits it.

The servant said, “Lord, it has been done as you commanded, and there is still room.”

For I tell you that none of those men who were invited before shall taste my supper.

[Col. 0635] “Now great crowds were going with him; and he turned and said to them:” — [Col. 0636] *þan*] Ulfilas omits Greek *καί*. We do not think that it is expressed by the particle *uh* joined to *nauh*, because here *καί* means “also,” and, so far as we know, Gothic never renders that meaning by *uh*. See, however, Jn. XVIII, 26.

Great crowds were going with him; and he turned and said to them:

[Col. 0635] “If anyone comes to me and does not hate his father, mother, wife, children, brothers, sisters, and even his own life, he cannot be my disciple.”

“If anyone comes to me and does not hate his father, mother, wife, children, brothers, sisters, and even his own life, he cannot be my disciple.”

[Col. 0635–0636] “And whoever does not carry his cross and come after me cannot be my disciple.” — *visan meins*] According to Greek; see v. 33.

And whoever does not carry his cross and come after me cannot be my disciple.

[Col. 0635–0637] “For which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate whether he has the means to complete it?” — [Col. 0636] *ïzvara*] Greek manuscripts place it after *raihtis*; see IX, 36. — *manvi—ustiuhan*] “means—to complete.” Scholars have judged this passage differently. B. preferred *habaiþ* to *habaiu* and translated “the equipment which he has for finishing”; this is wrong, since *þo* is not a relative but a demonstrative pronoun. L., retaining the reading of Codex Argenteus, translates “whether he has provision sufficient for completion,” but wrongly refers *þo* to *manvi*. Lh., *Ulfilas Illustratus*, p. 234, considers the word order to be *habaiu manvi du ustiuhan þo*; Z., who says that lh. would be right if Ulfilas had read Greek *τὰ πρός* with the manuscripts, thereby shows that he does not understand the Greek. Z.’s conjecture *manviþo*, taken as a participle, is impossible: participles in this form end in *-ido*, never *-iþo*. Nor can *manviþa* be a plural genitive of any verb. Though the reading is defective, the only conclusion is that Ulfilas, with the manuscripts, read either *τὰ εἰς* or *τὰ πρός*, omitting their authority only by transposing *þo habaiu* from *habaiu þo*, “whether he has these things.” The transposition nevertheless appears scribal; words are sometimes transposed, as noted at IX, 36. — *ustiuhan*] St. adds *usstiuhan*.

For which of you, wishing to build a tower, does not first sit down and calculate whether he has the means to complete it?

[Col. 0637] “Lest, after he has laid the foundation and is unable to finish, all who see begin to mock him,” — *mahtedi*] Codex Argenteus, Hz., J., St., and B. have *mahtide*; compare Jn. XVIII, 36.

Lest, after he has laid the foundation and is unable to finish, all who see begin to mock him,

[Col. 0637] “saying: This man began to build and was not able to finish.” — *timbrjan*] J. St. omit *timrjan*.

saying, “This man began to build and was not able to finish.”

[Col. 0637] “Or what king, going to make war against another king, does not first sit down and consider whether, with ten thousand, he is able to meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand?” — *viganna*] Thus the editions; Codex Argenteus has *viga || na*, doubtless a false division for *vigana*, the dative of *vigans*, “war.” Grimm, *Grammar* IV, 105, explains it likewise. Repetition of *n* may be compared with Gal. V, 15; scribes often repeated letters or syllables written at the end of one line at the beginning of the next. Compare Jn. IX, 41. Lh. wrongly took *viganna* as a gerund (*Ulfilas Illustratus*, p. 154), or as an infinitive with added *na* (p. 245); Z., with lh., wrongly conjectured *vigan ïna*, for the infinitive is *veihan*, not *vigan*. Moreover, this verb takes *du* (see 1 Cor. XV, 32), not an accusative. What F. meant by *vigamma* is unknown. — *pankeiþ*] Thus Codex Argenteus for the usual *pagkeiþ*, as at XV, 22 *bringiþ*, XVII, 9 *pank*, XIX, 31 *inqis*. — *siaiu*] J. St. B. add *siau*; Greek places it after *mahteigs*. — *pusundjo*] J. St. B. add *pusundjom*.

Or what king, going to make war against another king, does not first sit down and consider whether, with ten thousand, he is able to meet the one coming against him with twenty thousand?

[Col. 0637–0638] “Otherwise, while he is still far away, he sends an embassy and asks for peace.” — *eiþau*] Found only here, equivalent to *aiþþau* = Greek *εἰ δὲ μήγε*, “or else, if not.” The following *jabai nist mahteigs*, “if he is not able,” undoubtedly arose from a marginal gloss explaining the less common particle; there is no trace of it in Greek. — *fairra ïmma*] According to Greek. — *ïnsandjands airu*] According to all Greek manuscripts.

Otherwise, while he is still far away, he sends an embassy and asks for peace.

[Col. 0637–0638] “Thus, then, every one of you who does not renounce all his possessions cannot be my disciple.” — *aigina seinamma*] According to Greek. — *visan meins*] See v. 27.

Thus, then, every one of you who does not renounce all his possessions cannot be my disciple.

[Col. 0637] “Salt is good; but if salt becomes tasteless, with what shall it be seasoned?” — [Col. 0638] *jabai*] St. adds *jadai*.

Salt is good; but if salt becomes tasteless, with what shall it be seasoned?

[Col. 0637] “It is fit neither for land nor for manure; they throw it out. He who has ears to hear, let him hear.” — [Col. 0638] *ni*] St. has *nih*.
which is better.] my disciples. Good salt. But if the salt becomes tasteless, with what shall it be seasoned? It is useless either for the earth or for the manure heap; they throw it out. Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.

[Note: [Col. 0637] Now all the tax collectors and sinners were drawing near to him to hear him.]

[Note: [Col. 0638] “Approaching him”: corresponding to the Greek.]

It is beautiful. So that he may throw it out. Whoever has hearing ears, let him hear. Yet they were all approaching him, the tax collectors and sinners, to hear him. And the Pharisees and scribes were murmuring, saying:

[Note: [Col. 0637] “And the Pharisees and scribes murmured, saying that this man receives sinners and eats with them.”]

[Note: [Col. 0637] “He said to them this parable, saying:”]

They were saying that this man receives sinners and eats with them. Then he spoke this parable to them, saying::

[Note: [Col. 0637] “What man among you, possessing a hundred sheep and losing one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the lost one until he finds it?”]

[Note: [Col. 0638] ““Hundred”: *taihuntehund* for the usual *taihuntaihund* (VIII, 8; XVI, 6f.); otherwise J. adds *taihunte hund*, as shortly afterward *niunte hund*.*.—“Lost”: J. and St. add *fralausanin*; likewise at verse 6.]

What man among you, having a hundred sheep and losing one of them, would not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go after the lost one until he finds it?? And when he finds it, he lays it upon his shoulders, rejoicing,

[Note: [Col. 0637] “and, finding it, he places it on his shoulders, rejoicing.”]

[Note: [Col. 0638] “He lays it”: B. adds *uslaujiþ*.]

and, going home, he calls together his friends and neighbors, saying to them:

[Note: [Col. 0637] “And coming home, he summons his friends and neighbors, saying to them: Rejoice with me, because I have found this sheep of mine that was lost.”]

[Note: [Col. 0638] “He found”: St. adds *bigaþ*.—“Lost”: see the note at verse 4.]

“Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that was lost.” I tell you that thus there is joy in heaven over one sinner who repents, more than over ninety-nine righteous persons who have no need of repentance.

[Note: [Col. 0637] “I tell you that thus joy arises in heaven over one repentant sinner more than over ninety-nine righteous persons who do not need repentance.”]

[Note: [Col. 0638] “But”: J. and St. add *pan*.—“Of the ninety-nine”: J. and St. add *niutehundas*.—“Who”: St. adds *þaei*.]

.

[Note: [Col. 0637] “Or what woman, having ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp, sweep the house, and search carefully until she finds it?”]

[Note: [Col. 0638] “A certain”: “a certain woman,” Greek τίς (*tis*, “who”), for which Ulfilas mistakenly read τις (*tis*).—“Ten, if”: J. and St. add *taihunja sai*.—“Searches”: J. and B. add *usbaugeiþ*. “Carefully”: thus the Argenteus manuscript; Hz. and Z. add *glaggvuba*.]

““Or what woman, having ten drachmas, if she loses one drachma, does not light a lamp, sweep the house, and search carefully until she finds it?? And when she finds it, she calls together her friends and neighbors, saying:

[Note: [Col. 0637] “And finding it, she summons her friends and neighbors, saying: Rejoice with me, because I have found the drachma that I lost.”]

[Note: [Col. 0638] “Drachma”: J., St., and B. add *drakmin*, for this is the third case of the form *drakma* (see verse 8). In this place Ulfilas uses the Greek form, as often—*ein* for *-ην*, see M. XXVII, 62 *paraskaivein* (παρασκευήν), L. VII, 5 *synagogein* (συναγωγήν), Rom. XVI, 22 *aipistaulein* (ἐπιστολήν); Z. therefore improperly attempted to alter that form.—“Lost”: J., St., and B. add *fralausda*.]

“Rejoice with me, because I have found the drachma that I lost.” [Col. 0639]

And he said: “A certain man had two sons.”

[Note: [Col. 0639] “And he said: A certain man had two sons.”]

“Joy arises in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner who repents.” Then he said:

[Note: [Col. 0639] “And this younger one of them said to his father: Father, give me the share of the property that falls to me.”]
