Martha said to him, “I know that he will rise in the resurrection, on the last day.” [Note: [Col. 0685] “Martha said to him, ‘I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day.’”] [Note: [Col. 0685] *spedistin*] The Argenteus codex, Hertz, J., St., and B. add *spedistan*.

Jesus said, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me, even if he dies, will live.” [Note: [Col. 0685] “Jesus said, ‘I am this resurrection and life: whoever believes in me, even if he dies, lives.’”] [Note: [Col. 0685] *þan*] “but”; the Greek has αὐτῇ, “to her,” contrary to Ulfilas. [Note: [Col. 0685] *jah*] St. adds *jak*. [Note: [Col. 0685] *þauhjaba*] The Argenteus codex, Hertz, and Z. add *þauhgaba*; the more usual form is *þauhjabai*, see 1 Corinthians VII, 21; 2 Corinthians IV, 16; Skeireins 44, 15.]

“And everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?” [Note: [Col. 0685] “And whoever lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”]

She said to him, “Yes, Lord; I have believed that you are the Christ, the Son of God, the one coming into the world.” [Note: [Col. 0685] “She said to him, ‘Yes, Lord, I have believed that you are the Christ, the Son of God, the one coming into the world.’”]

And after saying this she went and secretly called Mary, her sister, saying, “The Teacher is here and is calling you.” [Note: [Col. 0685] “And after saying this she went and secretly called Mary, her sister, saying, ‘The Teacher has come and is calling you.’”] [Note: [Col. 0685] *qam*] “has come”; all the Greek manuscripts have πάρειστι, “is present.”

But when she heard it, she rose quickly and went to him. [Note: [Col. 0685] “But she, as soon as she heard it, rose immediately and went to him.”] [Note: [Col. 0685] *ïþ*] “but”; so the Greek.

Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Martha had met him. [Note: [Col. 0685] “For Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was still in the place where Martha had met him.”] [Note: [Col. 0685] *nauhþanuh*] “still”; a secondary reading, corresponding to the Greek ἔτι, “still.”

The Jews who were with her in the house and consoling her, seeing Mary—that she had risen quickly and gone out—followed her, saying that she was going to the tomb to weep there. [Note: [Col. 0685] “The Jews who were with her in the house, consoling her, seeing Mary suddenly rise and go out, went after her, saying that she was going to the tomb to weep there.”] [Note: [Col. 0685] *garda*] Ulfilas and the other codices have καί, “and.” [Note: [Col. 0686] *greitai*] Hertz omits it.

But Mary, when she came where Jesus was, saw him and fell at his feet, saying to him, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.” [Note: [Col. 0685] “But Mary, as soon as she came where Jesus was, seeing him, fell at his feet, saying to him, ‘Lord, if you had been here, my brother would not have died.’”] [Note: [Col. 0686] *veiseis*] Z. omits *veseis*; see Nehemiah V, 15, 17; VI, 17, 18, *veisun*; V, 14, *veisjau*.

Then Jesus, when he saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her weeping, groaned in spirit and troubled himself. [Note: [Col. 0685] “Then Jesus, as soon as he saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her weeping, groaned in spirit and stirred himself.”] [Note: [Col. 0686] *ïudaiuns*] The Greek places it after *ïzai*; Gothic does not agree with the manuscripts cited by Sch. [Note: [Col. 0686] *gretandans*] J., St., and B. omit *greitandans*.

And he said, “Where have you laid him?” They said to him, “Lord, come and see.” [Note: [Col. 0685] “And he said, ‘Where have you laid him?’ They said to him, ‘Lord, come here and see.’”] [Note: [Col. 0686] *lagidedun*] “they laid”; all the Greek manuscripts have τεθείκατε, “you have laid.”

And Jesus wept. [Note: [Col. 0685] “And Jesus wept.”] [Note: [Col. 0686] *jah*] “and”; so the Greek.

Then the Jews said, “See how he loved him.” [Note: [Col. 0685] “Then the Jews said, ‘Behold, how he loved him.’”]

But some of them said, “Could not this man, who opened the eyes of to the blind man., have caused even this man not to die?” [Note: [Col. 0685] “But some of them said, ‘Could not this man, who opened the eyes of the blind man, have caused even this man not to die?’”]

Then Jesus, again groaning within himself, went to the tomb. It was a cave, and a stone had been placed over it. [Note: [Col. 0685] “Then Jesus, groaning again within himself, went to this tomb. It was a cave, and it was covered above with a stone.”] [Note: [Col. 0686] *staina*] Interpreters wrongly take this as a nominative form. Z. erred especially, declaring its nominative gender masculine, since the form *ufarlagida* cannot be masculine but is feminine. Anyone familiar with the Gothic language and considering the Greek text, where Ulfilas renders ἐπ’ αὐτῷ by the adverb *ufaro*, “above,” will not doubt that *staina* must be taken as a dative and *ufarlagida* as the feminine form referring to *hulundi*: “the cave was covered above with a stone.” Compare Lye in Benzelius’ preface, p. LXVII; also Matthew VI, 6, *galukands haurdai* (“closing the door”), corresponding to κλείσας τὴν θύραν.]

The blind man.
to do so, and that he might not die. Then Jesus, again becoming inwardly agitated, goes to the tomb. [Col. 0687] [Note: [Col. 0687] Jesus said: “Remove this stone.” Martha, the sister of the dead man, said to him: “Lord, he already smells, for he has been four days [in the tomb].”] Now it was a cave, and a stone had been laid over it above. Jesus said: “Take away the stone.” His sister, Martha, of the dead man, said to him: ““Lord, he already smells; for he has been dead four days.”.” Jesus said to her: “Did I not tell you that, if you believe, you will see the glory of God?” They then took away the stone where it was. [Note: *þarei vas*: “where it was,” absent from the Greek. *uzuhhof*: see the note on Mark XIV, 44. *ïup*: Z. adds *jup*.] But Jesus raised his eyes upward and said: “Father, I give thanks to you because you have heard me; and I knew that you always hear me, but because of this crowd standing around I said it, so that they might believe that you sent me.” And when he had said this, he cried out in a loud voice: “Lazarus, come out here!” And the dead man came out, bound hand and foot with bandages, and his face was bound with a cloth. [Note: *handuns jah fotuns*: according to the Greek; accusatives used in the Greek manner (Matthiae, *Greek Grammar*, p. 782, 4). For other examples see Mark XII, 4, *haubiþ vundan* (“wounded in the head”); Ephesians VI, 14, *ufgaurdanai hupins* (“girded about the loins”). *bibundans*: “bound,” all Greek manuscripts *περιεδέδετο*.] Jesus said to them: “Unbind him and let him go.”.”

[Note: [Col. 0687] Then many of these Jews, who came to Mary and saw what he had done, believed in him.]

Then many of the Jews who came to Mary and saw what he had done believed in him. [Note: “Jews”: thus the Argenteus manuscript; see the note at L. III, 5. St. omits *ïudaie*, as do J. B. and Z.]

[Note: [Col. 0687] But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.]

But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done. [Note: *sumaiþ*: J. and St. omit the final *þ*, referring to the note at M. V, 37.]

[Note: [Col. 0687] Then the chief priests and the Pharisees assembled …]

Then the chief priests and the Phari… [lacuna] [Note: *farei …*: thus far is read in the Argenteus manuscript; J. and St. conjecturally complete it as *fareisaieis*.]

[Note: [Col. 0687] In Bethany, where Lazarus was, the dead man whom Jesus raised from the dead.].]

In Bethany, where Lazarus was, the dead man whom he had raised from the dead. [Note: In the word *ïn* the Argenteus manuscript continues; J. and St. conjecturally add *qam* (“came”). “Jesus”: supplied from the Greek.]

Then they made him a supper there, and Martha served; but Lazarus was one of those reclining with him. Mary took a pound of costly nard perfume (*nardaus pistikeinis filugalaubis*), anointed Jesus’ feet, and wiped his feet with her hair. The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.

[Note: [Col. 0687] One of his disciples, Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon, who was about to betray him, said:]

One of his disciples, Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon, who was about to betray him, said: “Why was this perfume not sold for three hundred denarii and the proceeds given to the poor?”

[Note: [Col. 0687] He said this, not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief, and, having the money-box, he used to take what was put into it.]

He said this, not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief and had the money-box, and he used to take what was put into it.

[Note: *nardaus*: J. and St. add *nardans*; J. also adds *pistikeinis*.]

[Note: *filugalaubis*: St., B. and Z. defend this reading. Ih. and Ulfilas Illustrated, Preface p. 6, and Grimm II, 176, regard it as a gloss, whose author, having misunderstood Greek *πιστικῆς*, derived it from *πίστις* (“faith”) and interpreted it as *filugalaubs*. Others show that this is not correct from passages where *galaubs* has the meaning “precious”; see Romans IX, 21: “to make from the same lump one [vessel] for a precious use” (*us þamma samin daiga taujan sum du galaubamma kasa* = Greek *εἰς τιμὴν σκεῦος*), and another for a dishonorable use (*sumuþ-þan du ungalaubamma* = *εἰς ἀτιμίαν*), that is, to make from the same material one vessel for an honorable use and another for a non-honorable use. First Corinthians VII, 23: “you were bought at a precious price” (*vairþa galaubamma usbauhtai sijuþ*, Greek *τιμῇ*). It is therefore apparent that *filugalaubs* correctly corresponds to Greek *πολύτιμος* (“very precious”).]

[Note: *skufta seinamma*: all Greek manuscripts place this before *fotuns* (“feet”).]

One of those reclining with him was present. Mary took a pound of costly nard perfume and anointed Jesus’ feet, wiping his feet with her hair. The house was filled with the fragrance of the perfume.

[Note: [Col. 0687] But one of his disciples, Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon, who was about to betray him, said:]

But one of his disciples, Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon, who was about to betray him, said: “Why was this perfume not sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?”

[Note: *sa*: “this”; all Greek manuscripts have this reading.]

[Note: [Col. 0687] Why was this perfume not sold for three hundred denarii and distributed to the poor?]

Why was this perfume not sold for three hundred denarii and distributed to the poor?

[Note: [Col. 0687] He said this, not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief and, having the money-box, he took what was put into it.]

But he said this, not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief and had the money-box, and he took what was put into it.

[Note: *qaþ*: the Greek text places this before *þatuh*.]

[Note: *ïna*: all Greek manuscripts place this after *vesi*.]

Jesus said: “Leave her; she has kept this for the day of my burial. For you always have the poor with you, but you do not always have me.”.”

[Note: [Col. 0687] The great crowd of Jews learned that Jesus was there, and they came, not because of Jesus alone, but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.]

A great crowd of Jews learned that Jesus was there, and they came, not because of Jesus alone, but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead.

[Note: *ïesus*: supplied from the Greek. *urraisida*: J. and St. add *urreisida*.]

The chief priests then planned also to kill Lazarus, because many of the Jews were going there on his account and were believing in Jesus.

[Note: *þan auk*: “but” or “for”; Greek *δέ*. Compare Romans VIII, 10 and First Corinthians X, 20.]

[Note: *lazarau*: Hz. adds *lazaru*.]

The chief priests planned to kill Lazarus also, because many of the Jews were going there on his account and believed in Jesus.

[Note: *ïudaiei*: B. omits *ïudaie*; see the note at L. III, 5.]

The next day the great crowd that had come to the festival, hearing that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem, took palm branches and went out to meet him, crying: “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!”

[Note: *ïftumin daga*: J. adds *jct.*; otherwise all Greek manuscripts have *o daga* (“the day”).]

On the following day the great crowd that had come to the festival, hearing that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem, took branches of palm trees and went out to meet him, crying: “Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, the King of Israel!”

Jesus found a young donkey and sat upon it, as it is written:

“Do not fear, daughter of Zion; behold, your king is coming, sitting on a donkey’s colt.”

[Note: *qimanda*: J. and St. add *qimands*.]

Jesus found a donkey and sat upon it, as it is written: “Do not fear, daughter of Zion; behold, your king is coming, sitting on a donkey’s colt.”

[Note: [Col. 0689] But his disciples did not understand this at first; but when Jesus had been glorified, then they remembered that this had been written about him, and that they had done this to him.]

His disciples did not understand these things at first; but when Jesus had been glorified, then they remembered that this had been written about him, and that they had done this to him.

[Note: [Col. 0689] The crowd that had been with him testified that he had called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him from the dead.]

The crowd that had been with him testified that he had called Lazarus from the tomb and raised him from the dead.

[Note: *þan*: “when”; Greek *ὅτι*.]

For this reason the crowd went out to meet him, because they had heard that he had performed this sign..

[Note: *duþþe*: Ulfila, with the manuscripts, has *kai* (“and”). *ïddjedun gamotjan*: see the note at First Corinthians IX, 25. *þo*: “this”; all Greek manuscripts place it before *gatavida*.]

For this reason they went out to meet him, because they had heard that he had performed this sign.

Then the Pharisees said to one another: “You see that you are accomplishing nothing. Behold, the world has gone after him.”

[Note: [Col. 0689] Some gentiles among those who went out came to worship at this festival.]

Some gentiles among those who went out were there in order to worship at this festival.

[Note: *þiudo þize urrinnandane*: Grimm, Grammar IV, 586, interprets this incorrectly. *þize urrinnandane* does not belong to *þiudo*, but is what is called a partitive genitive: “there were some gentiles among those who went out.”]

There were some gentiles among those who went out..”

[Note: [Col. 0689] These approached Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying: Lord, we wish to see Jesus.]

Some of the gentiles among those who went out came to Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying: “Lord, we wish to see Jesus.”

[Note: *þai*: Ulfila, with the manuscripts, has Greek *οὖν* (“therefore”).]

Philip went and told Andrew; Andrew and Philip again told Jesus. But Jesus answered them, saying: “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.”

[Note: [Col. 0689] Philip went and said to Andrew, and again Andrew and Philip said to Jesus.]

Philip went and told Andrew; then Andrew and Philip told Jesus..”

Jesus answered them, saying: “The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.”

“Amen, amen, I say to you: unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.”

[Note: *waiteis*: see the note at L. I, 23.]

Whoever loves his life loses it, and whoever hates his life in this world will preserve it for eternal life. If anyone serves me, let him follow me; and where I am, there my servant must also be. If anyone serves me, the Father will honor him.

[Note: *was andbahtjai*: according to the Greek. *þaruh*: Ulfila has Greek *καί* (“and”); unless perhaps *jah* should be read instead of *sa*. *visan habaiþ*: “must be,” that is, “will be”; see the note at L. VI, 25. *jah*: “and,” according to the Greek. *mis*: J. and St. add *mik* (“me”).]

Whoever loves his life loses it, and whoever hates his life in this world will preserve it for eternal life.. If anyone serves me, let him follow me; and where I am, there my servant must be. If anyone serves me, the Father will honor him.

Now my soul is troubled, and what shall I say? “Father, save me from this hour”? But for this reason I came to this hour.

[Note: [Col. 0689] Now my soul is troubled, and what shall I say: Father, save me from this hour? But for this reason I came to this hour.]

Now my soul has become troubled. And what shall I say? “Father, save me from this hour!” But it was for this reason that I came to this hour.

“Father, glorify your name.” Then a voice came from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.”

[Note: *namo þeinata*: according to all Greek manuscripts.]

“Father, glorify your name.” Then a voice came from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.”

[Note: [Col. 0689] The crowd standing and hearing said that thunder had occurred; others said: An angel has spoken to him.]

The crowd that stood by and heard it said that thunder had occurred. Others said: “An angel has spoken to him.”

[Note: *stoþ*: Ulfila and the manuscript have Greek *καί* (“and”).]

Jesus answered and said: “This voice did not come for my sake, but for yours. Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast out. And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw everyone to myself.”

[Note: *fairwaus*: St. adds *faurwaus*. Sch.’s note that Ulfila omits Greek *τούτου* (“of this”) is mistaken.]

[Note: *alla*: “everyone”; Greek *πάντας*.]

Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast out. And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw everyone to myself.

He said this to indicate by what kind of death he was going to die.

[Note: [Col. 0689] The crowd answered him: We have heard from the law that the Christ remains forever; and how do you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?]

The crowd answered him: “We have heard from the law that the Christ remains forever. How then do you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?”

[Note: *was*: J. and St. add *wa* (“what”).]

Jesus therefore said to them: “The light is with you for a little while longer. Walk while you have the light, so that darkness does not overtake you; and whoever walks in darkness does not know where he is going. While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may become sons of light.”

Jesus said these things, then went away and hid himself from them.

[Note: *galaiþ*: B. adds *galiþ*.]

Jesus spoke these things, then went away and hid himself from them.

Although he had performed so many signs before them, they did not believe in him, so that the word of the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled, which he said:

“Lord, who has believed our report, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”

[Note: *esaeiïns*: St. and Hz. add *esaejins*.]

Although he had performed so many signs before them, they did not believe in him, so that the word of the prophet Isaiah might be fulfilled, which he said: “Lord, who has believed our report, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”

For this reason they could not believe, because Isaiah again said:

“He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, so that they would not see with their eyes, understand with their heart, turn, and I would heal them.”

“You did not choose me, but I chose you, that you may go and bear fruit, and that your fruit may remain for ever; that whatever you ask the Father in my name, he may give you.”

[Note: [Col. 0697] You did not choose me, but I chose you, that you may go and bear fruit, and that your fruit may remain for ever, that whatever you ask the Father in my name he may give you.]

[Note: [Col. 0698] *ïzvis*: second hand; Ulfilas, with the manuscripts, omits Greek *καὶ ἔθηκα ὑμᾶς* (“and I appointed you”).—*du aiva*: “for ever,” omitted by all Greek witnesses.—*þatawah þei*: see verse 7.—*bidjaiþ*: St. adds *bidjaþ*.]

“I made [it] known to you. You did not choose me, but I chose you, that you may go and bear fruit, and that your fruit may remain for ever, that whatever you ask the Father in my name he may give you. This I command you: that you love one another.”

“If the world hates you, know that it hated me before you.”

[Note: [Col. 0697] If this world hates you, know that it hated me before you.]

[Note: [Col. 0698] *fruman ïzvis*: “before you,” Greek *πρῶτον ὑμῶν*. It should further be noted that *fruman* is comparative in meaning, though not in form; likewise *auhuma* (= *ὑπερέχων*, “surpassing”) at Philippians II.3.]

“This I command you: that you love one another. If the world hates you, know that it hated me before you.”

[Note: [Col. 0697] If you were of this world, the world would love its own; but because you are not of this world, and I chose you out of this world, therefore the world hates you.]

[Note: [Col. 0698] *svesans*: “its own,” Greek *τὸ ἴδιον*.]

“… therefore the world hates you. Remember the word which I said to you: a servant is not greater than his master. If they persecuted me, they will persecute you also; if they kept my word, they will keep yours also.”

[Col. 0699]

“But they do all these things to you because of my name, because they do not know him who sent me.”

[Note: [Col. 0699] *sandjandan*: J. and St. add *sandjandin*.]

“If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.”

“If I had not done among them the works which no one else did, they would not have sin; but now they have both seen and hated both me and my Father.”

[Note: [Col. 0699] *anþar ainshun*: “any other,” omitted by all Greek witnesses.—*mik*: first hand, “me,” omitted by Greek.]

[Note: [Col. 0699] *þata*: St. adds *þaþa*.—*gamelido*: J. adds *melido*.—*arvjo*: J., St., and B. add *arujo*.]

“They hated me without cause.”

[Note: [Col. 0699] *þan jus*: omitted by all Greek witnesses.]

[Note: [Col. 0699] They shall expel you from the assemblies; but an hour is coming when everyone who kills you will think that he offers sacrifice to God.]

“But these things I have spoken to you, that, when their hour comes, you may remember them—that I told you. But I did not tell you these things from the beginning, because I was with you.”

[Note: [Col. 0699] *ïze*: “their,” omitted by all Greek witnesses except manuscript 11 according to Mi. Since that manuscript omits the following *αὐτῶν*, rendered in our text by *þize*, we fear that one or the other may have entered the text from the margin; cf. XIII.29 and Luke V.35.]

“But I tell you the truth: it is better for you that I go; for if I do not go, the Paraclete will not come to you; but if I go, I shall send him to you.”

[Note: [Col. 0699] *ïzvis qiþa*: omitted by Greek.—*parakletus*: St. adds *paracletus*.—*jabai*: second hand; J. adds *gabai*.]

“And when he comes, he shall convict the world concerning sin, concerning righteousness, and concerning judgment.”

“Concerning sin indeed: that they do not believe in me.”

[Note: [Col. 0699] *þata*: “this,” omitted by Greek, and especially objectionable in Gothic. Unless it has been said by analogy with Mark IX.23, Luke I.62, and IX.46—which we doubt—it must be deleted as a scribal error caused by the following *þatei*. In those passages *þata* always has an antecedent; here it has none, nor is there any trace of it in Greek. Cf. 2 Corinthians X.12.]

“Concerning righteousness: that I go to my Father, and you no longer see me.”

“Concerning judgment: that the ruler of this world has been judged.”

“I still have much to say to you, but you cannot bear it now.”

“But when that one comes, the Spirit of truth, he will lead you into all truth; for he will not speak from himself, but whatever he hears he will speak, and he will announce to you the things to come.”

[Note: [Col. 0700] *anavairþo*: Z. adds *anavairhto*.]

“He will glorify me, because he will take from what is mine and announce it to you.”

“All that the Father has is mine; therefore I said that he will take from what is mine and announce it to you.”

“A little while longer, and you do not see me; and again a little while, and you see me, because I go to the Father.”

[Note: [Col. 0699] A little while longer and you do not see me, and again a little while and you see me, because I go to the Father.]

[Note: [Col. 0700] *nauh*: “still,” omitted by Greek.—*ïk*: “I,” omitted by Greek.]

Then some of his disciples said to one another: “What is this that he says to us: ‘A little while, and you do not see me; and again a little while, and you see me’; and, ‘Because I go to the Father’?”

[Note: [Col. 0699] Then some of his disciples said to one another: “What is this that he says to us: ‘A little while, and you do not see me; and again a little while, and you see me’; and, ‘Because I go to the Father’?”]

[Note: [Col. 0700] *siponjam*: Ulfilas, with manuscripts 7 and x according to Mi., omits *αὐτοῦ* (“his”).—*ei*: “that”; Greek has *καί* (“and”). Ulfilas, however, varies his expression in his customary manner; cf. Luke VI.37, where, unless he read *ἵνα* for *καὶ οὐ* with the manuscripts, he used *ei* in place of *jah* for the same reason indicated above.]

They said: “What is this that he says: ‘A little while’? We do not know what he says.”

[Note: [Col. 0699] They said, “What is it that he says, ‘A little while’? We do not know what he says.”]

[Note: [Col. 0700] *qeþunuh*: see X.20.]

But Jesus knew that they wished to ask him, and said to them: “Do you inquire among yourselves concerning this, because I said: ‘A little while, and you do not see me; and again a little while, and you see me’?”

[Note: [Col. 0699] But Jesus knew that they wished to ask him, and said to them: “Do you inquire among yourselves concerning this, because I said, ‘A little while, and you do not see me, and again a little while, and you see me’?”]

[Note: [Col. 0700] *ïþ*: “but,” omitted by Greek.—*ïesus vissuh*: omitted by Greek.]

[Col. 0701]

“Amen, amen, I say to you: you shall weep and lament, but the world shall rejoice; you shall become sorrowful, but your sorrow shall become joy.”

[Note: [Col. 0701] *jus*: second hand; Ulfilas, with the manuscripts, omits *δέ* (“but”).]

“A woman, when she gives birth, has sorrow, because her hour has come; but when the child has been born, she no longer remembers the distress because of the joy, because a human being has been born into the world.”

[Note: [Col. 0701] *gabauran ïst*: “the child has been born”; Greek has *γεννήσῃ*, “the woman gives birth [to a child].”—*ni þanaseiþs ni*: see VIII.42.]

“Because a human being has been born into the world. And now you indeed have sorrow; but I shall see you again, and your heart shall rejoice, and no one shall take your joy from you.”

[Note: [Col. 0701] *þan*: Greek places it after *jus*.—*saurga*: Greek places it before *auk* (“indeed”). Sch. erred in classing Gothic among those reading *νῦν μέν* rather than *μέν νῦν*.]

[Note: [Col. 0701] *þiswah þei*: thus Codex Argenteus; St. and Z. add *þiswaþei*.]

“Until now you have asked nothing in my name. Ask, and receive, that your joy may be fulfilled.”

[Note: [Col. 0701] *faheþs*: see XV.11.]

“These things I have spoken to you in parables; but an hour is coming when I shall no longer speak to you in parables, but shall openly announce the Father to you.”

[Note: [Col. 0701] *akei*: “but,” omitted by Greek.—*panuh*: “then”; Greek has *ὅτε* (“when”).—*ïzvis*: second hand; Greek places it after *rodja*.]

“On that day you shall ask in my name; and I do not say to you that I shall ask the Father for you.”

“But the Father himself loves you, because you loved me and believed that I came forth from God.”

[Note: [Col. 0701] *ak*: “but”; Greek has *γάρ* (“for”), although Gothic also renders Greek *γάρ* by *ak* at Ephesians II.10.]

“I came forth from the Father and entered the world; again I leave the world and go to the Father.”

[Note: [Col. 0701] *uzuhïddja*: see Mark XIV.44.—*atïddja*: St. adds *attiddja*.]

Then his disciples said: “Behold, now you speak openly and say no parable.”

[Note: [Col. 0701] *þaruh*: “then,” omitted by Greek.—*qeþun*: Ulfilas, with the manuscripts, omits *αὐτῷ* (“to him”).—*gajukono*: J. and St. add *gajukno*.]

“Now we know that you know all things and have no need that anyone should question you. By this we believe that you came forth from God.”

[Note: [Col. 0701] *þu*: “you,” in either instance, omitted by Greek.—*þuk was*: omitted by Greek.—*fraihnai*: Z. adds *frahnai*.]

Jesus answered them: “Do you now believe?”

[Note: [Col. 0702] *ïm*: J. and B. add *him*.]

“Behold, an hour is coming, and has now come, when each of you shall be scattered to his own, and you shall leave me alone; and I am not alone, because the Father is with me.”

[Note: [Col. 0702] *distahjada*: “be scattered”; Greek has *σκορπισθῆτε*.—*seina*: this form, which Z. preferred to alter to *seinaim*, seems to us to be a genitive of the reflexive pronoun, as at Luke VII.32. *Du seina* is elliptic, as at Luke XIX.7, *du fravaurhtis mans*, “to a sinful man”; see Luke VIII.49.]

“These things I have spoken to you, that you may have peace in me. In the world you have affliction; but take courage: I have overcome the world.”

[Note: [Col. 0702] *fairwu*: J. and St. add *fairwau*.]

“These things Jesus spoke, and lifted his eyes toward heaven, and said: ‘Father, the hour has come. Glorify your Son, that your Son may glorify you.’”

[Note: [Col. 0702] *uzuhhof*: “lifted”; see XVIII.26 and Mark XIV.44.—*ei*: Ulfilas, with the manuscripts, omits Greek *καί* (“and”).]

“As you gave him authority over all flesh, that he may give eternal life to all that which you gave him.”

“And this is eternal life: that they may know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom you sent.”

[Note: [Col. 0702] *sunja*: “truly.” Z. rightly observed that *sunja* is an adverb; cf. *alja*. Likewise at Luke IX.27, *sunja*, corresponding to Greek *ἀληθῶς*, may be taken as an adverb.]

“I glorified you on earth. I completed the work which you gave me to do.”

“And now glorify me, Father, with yourself, with the glory which I had with you before the world existed.”

[Note: [Col. 0702] *at þus*: Greek places it after *vesi*; Ulfilas agrees with the versions.]

“I manifested your name to the people whom you gave me out of the world. They were yours, and you gave them to me, and they kept your word.”

[Col. 0703]

[Note: [Col. 0703] *atgaft ïns*: omitted by Greek.]

“Now I have known that all things which you gave me are with you.”

“For the words which you gave me I gave to them, and they received them in truth, and believed that I came forth from you, and that you sent me.”

[Note: [Col. 0703] *nemun*: Ulfilas, with the manuscripts, omits *καὶ ἔγνωσαν* (“and they knew”).]

“I pray for them. I do not pray for the world, but for those whom you gave me, because they are yours.”

“And all mine are yours, and yours are mine, and I have been glorified in them.”

“I am no longer in the world; but they are in the world, and I go to you. Holy Father, keep them in your name, whom you gave me, that they may be one, as we are.”

[Note: [Col. 0703] Beginning: Ulfilas omits *καί* (“and”).—*panzei*: “whom”; Greek has singular *ᾧ*.]

“While I was with them in the world, I kept them in your name. Those whom you gave me I preserved; and none of them perished except the son of perdition, that the Scripture might be fulfilled.”

“But now I go to you, and I speak these things in the world, that they may have my joy fulfilled in themselves.”

“I gave them your word, and the world hated them, because they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.”

[Note: [Col. 0703] *so*: St. adds *sa*.—*ni ïm*: Greek places it before *us*.]

“I do not pray that you take them out of the world, but that you protect them from the evil.”

“They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.”

“Sanctify them in truth. Your word is truth.”

[Note: [Col. 0703] *sunjai*: Ulfilas, with the manuscripts, omits Greek *σοῦ* (“your”).]

“As you sent me into the world, so I sent them into the world.”

[Note: [Col. 0703] *svah*: see XV.9.—*manased*: J. and St. omit *manaseþ*.]

“And for them I sanctify myself, that they too may be sanctified in truth.”

[Note: [Col. 0703] *sijaina*: Greek places it after *eis* (“they”).]

“But I pray not for these alone, but for those believing in me through their word.”

[Note: [Col. 0703] *ak*: Ulfilas omits *καί* (“also”).—*vaurda*: “words”; Greek has singular *λόγου* (“word”).]

“That they all may be one, as you, Father, are in me and I in you; that they too may be one in us, that the world may believe that you sent me.”

“And the glory which you gave me I gave them, that they may be one as we are one.”

[Note: [Col. 0703] *siju*: the editions omit *sijum*; see X.30 and Mark X.39.]

“I in them, and you in me, that they may be made perfect into one, and that the world may know that you sent me and loved them as you loved me.”

[Note: [Col. 0703] *jah*: second hand; Ulfilas omits *ἵνα* (“that”).]

“Father, those whom you gave me, I desire that, where I am, they also may be with me, that they may see my glory which you gave me, because you loved me before the creation of the world.”

[Note: [Col. 0703] *þatei*: “that which”; Greek has *οὕς* (“those whom”).—*ïm ïk*: thus Codex Argenteus; Z. omits *ïk ïm*.]

“Righteous Father, the world did not know you; but I knew you, and these knew that you sent me.”

“These things Jesus said, and went out with his disciples across the torrent, the Cedron, where there was a garden, into which Jesus and his disciples went.”

[Note: [Col. 0704] *ïesus*: the second occurrence; thus Codex Argenteus; see Mark I.42.]

“Judas also, who was betraying him, knew the place, because Jesus often met there with his disciples.”

[Note: [Col. 0704] *galevjands*: J., St., and B. omit *levjands*; in Codex Argenteus *ga* is written above the line.]

“But Judas took a cohort and servants of the chief priests and Pharisees, and went there with lanterns, torches, and weapons.”

[Note: [Col. 0704] *miþ*: Z. adds *mit*.—*skeimam*: thus Codex Argenteus. Zahnii’s conjecture *skeinam* seems probable: *skeina* would then be formed from *skeinan*, “to shine” (Luke IX.29; XVII.24; 2 Corinthians IV.6).]

“But Jesus, knowing all things that were coming upon him, went out and said to them: ‘Whom do you seek?’”

[Note: [Col. 0704] *andafjandans—qeþun*: “answering—they said”; Greek *ἀπεκρίθησαν*, “they answered.”—*þaruh*: “then,” omitted by Greek.]

[Col. 0705]

“Then, when he said to them, ‘I am,’ they went backward and fell down.”

“Then he asked them again: ‘Whom do you seek?’ But they said: ‘Jesus the Nazarene.’”

[Note: [Col. 0705] *aftra*: Greek places it before *þaþroh*.]

Jesus answered: “I told you that I am. If you seek me, let these go.”

[Note: [Col. 0705] *gaggan*: St. adds *gaggam*.]

[Note: [Col. 0705] That the word might be fulfilled,]
that he said that of those whom he gave me, I lost none of them.] [Note: [Col. 0705] *atgaf*: thus the Arg. manuscript; Hz. and the editors have *atgaft* (“you gave”), in agreement with all the Greek manuscripts (*δέδωκας*).] Jesus answered: “I told you that I am he. If you are looking for me, let these men go, so that the word which he said might be fulfilled: ‘Of those whom he gave me, I did not lose a single one.’”

But Simon Peter, having a sword, drew it and struck the servant of the high priest, cutting off his right ear; the man’s name was Malchus.] [Note: [Col. 0705] *sah—namin*: “this man—by name”; Greek: “and the servant’s name was …”; otherwise Z. omits *sa*.] [Note: [Col. 0705] *þan haitans vas namin malkus*: “then he was called by the name Malchus.”]

Then Jesus said to Peter: “Put the sword into its sheath. Shall I not drink the cup which the Father has given me?”] [Note: [Col. 0705] “Then the cohort, the commander, and the Jewish attendants seized Jesus and bound him.”] [Note: [Col. 0705] *þanei gaf mis atta*: “which the Father gave me.”] [Note: [Col. 0705] *ni drigkau þana*: “shall I not drink it?”]

Then the cohort, the commander, and the attendants of the Jews seized Jesus and bound him, and led him first to Annas. For he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.] [Note: [Col. 0705] *sa*: “this man”; Greek …] [Note: [Col. 0705] *kajafin*: Massmann conjectures that this was written by a copyist in error instead of *kajafins*, but the learned man is himself mistaken, since the Goths regularly use the dative for the genitive.] [Note: [Col. 0705] *þis ataþnjis*: J. St. adds *þiza taþnjis*; Maresh. p. 408 had already defended the genuine reading.]

The Jews seized Jesus, bound him, and led him to Annas first. Now Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jews that it was better for one man to perish for the people. He was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was the high priest that year.

Then Simon Peter and another disciple followed Jesus. That disciple was known to the high priest, and he entered with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest.] [Note: [Col. 0705] *paitrus*: the Arg. manuscript has *prus*; this name is never written by abbreviation, and even if it were, the abbreviation mark ought not to be absent; compare 2 Cor. 11:5.] [Note: [Col. 0705] *miþïnngalaiþ*: St. adds *miþïggalaiþ*.] [Note: [Col. 0705] *þatei batizo ïst*: “that it is better.”] [Note: [Col. 0705] *ainana mannan fraqistjan faur managein*: “to cause one man to perish for the people.”]

But Peter stood outside at the door. Then the other disciple—the one known to the high priest—went out, spoke to the doorkeeper, and brought Peter in.] [Note: [Col. 0705] *paitru*: J. St. adds *paitrus*.]

Then that maidservant, the doorkeeper, said to Peter: “Are you not also one of this man’s disciples?” But he said: “I am not.”] [Note: [Col. 0706] *ïþ*: “but,” omitted in all Greek manuscripts.] [Note: [Col. 0706] *ïs qaþ*: “he said,” according to all Greek manuscripts.]

The servants and attendants were standing there, having made a charcoal fire, because it was cold, and they were warming themselves; Peter too was with them, standing and warming himself.] [Note: [Col. 0706] *standands*: St. adds *standans*, as in verse 22.] [Note: [Col. 0706] *jah*: at the end, Z. omits it.]

Then the high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and about his teaching. Jesus answered him: “I have spoken openly to the world. I have always taught in the assembly and in the temple, where all the Jews gather, and I have said nothing secretly. Why do you question me? Question those who have heard what I said to them. Look, they know what I said.”] [Note: [Col. 0705] *sinteino*: “always,” Greek *πάντες* (“all”).]

When he had said this, one of the attendants standing there struck Jesus with the palm of his hand and said: “Is that how you answer the high priest?”] [Note: [Col. 0706] *þata*: J. St. adds *þana*.] [Note: [Col. 0706] *qiþandin ïmma*: according to the Greek.] [Note: [Col. 0706] *standands*: see the note on verse 18.] [Note: [Col. 0706] *slah lofin*: J. St. adds *jct.*] [Note: [Col. 0706] *svau*: J. St. B. adds *svah*.]

Jesus answered him: “If I have spoken wrongly, testify concerning the wrong; but if I have spoken rightly, why do you strike me?”] [Note: [Col. 0706] *andhof*: Ulfila omits *αὐτῷ* (“to him”).]

Then Annas sent him bound to Caiaphas, the high priest.] [Note: [Col. 0706] *þanuh*: “then,” omitted in the Greek.] [Note: [Col. 0706] *gabundanana*: J. St. adds *gabundana*.]

Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. Then they said to him: “Are you not also one of this man’s disciples?” But he denied it and said: “No, I am not.”] [Note: [Col. 0706] *paitrus*: J. St. B. adds *paitraus*.] [Note: [Col. 0706] *vas*: all Greek manuscripts place it before *seimon*.] [Note: [Col. 0706] the second *ïþ*: “but,” omitted in the Greek.] [Note: [Col. 0706] *ïs afaiaik*: according to the Greek.] [Note: [Col. 0706] *ne*: “no,” omitted in all Greek manuscripts.]

One of the servants of the high priest, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said: “Did I not see you in the garden with him?”] [Note: [Col. 0707] *sah*: “and this man,” used instead of *saei* (“who”). Grim. III, pp. 23–24, and we ourselves (on Mark 2:11 and 1 Corinthians 16:13) have observed that the enclitic particle *uh*, meaning the same as *jah* (“and”), joins individual concepts and statements. We now learn that, added to a demonstrative pronoun, it makes a relative expression, as in Luke 2:37; 16:20; 17:12; 1 Corinthians 15:1; Philemon 2. Compare Matthew 27:57. Moreover, *sah* is also used for “and he himself” or “and this man” (Luke 2:37 and following; 8:44; 17:16; 19:2), and in place of other coordinating particles; compare Matthew 27:44 (*δέ*), John 10:20; 16:18 (*οὖν*). When *καί* means “also,” it seems to be forbidden by the nature of the particle itself to render it by *uh*, except in *svah* = “thus also,” 1 Corinthians 15:22; 2 Corinthians 8:6; Ephesians 5:24, for which *sva jah* is also found in 2 Corinthians 1:5; 8:11; 10:7; Colossians 3:13; 1 Thessalonians 4:14.] [Note: [Col. 0707] *ïk*: all Greek manuscripts place it before *þuk*; St. omits it.]

Again Peter denied it, and immediately the rooster crowed.] [Note: [Col. 0707] *sums þise skalke þis maistins gudjins*: “one of these servants of the high priest.”]

They then led Jesus from Caiaphas into the praetorium. It was morning, but they themselves did not enter the praetorium, so that they would not be defiled, but might eat the Passover.] [Note: [Col. 0707] *eis*: “they”; all Greek manuscripts omit it.] [Note: [Col. 0707] *ak*: Ulfila and the manuscripts omit *ἵνα* (“so that”).]

Then Pilate went out to them and said: “What accusation are you bringing against this man?”] [Note: [Col. 0707] *wo vrohe bairiþ ana þana mannan*: “what charge do you bring against this man?”]

They answered and said to him: “If he were not a criminal, we would not have handed him over to you.”] [Note: [Col. 0707] *veis*: “we,” omitted in all Greek manuscripts.] [Note: [Col. 0707] *atgebeima þus*: according to all Greek manuscripts.]

Pilate then said to them: “Take him yourselves and judge him according to your law.” The Jews said to him: “It is not lawful for us to kill anyone.”] [Note: [Col. 0707] *jah*: Z. omits it.] [Note: [Col. 0707] *eis*: “they”; the sense appears to require this. Perhaps it was introduced from a manuscript in which *ἐκεῖνοι* stood instead of *Ἰουδαῖοι*; one or the other is therefore superfluous. Compare Luke 5:35; John 13:29; 16:4; 1 Corinthians 15:19. Compare, however, Mark 1:16, where Ulfila and the manuscripts read *broþar ïs* (“his brother”).]

This was so that the word of the Lord might be fulfilled, which he had spoken, signifying by what death he was to die.] [Note: [Col. 0708] *fraujins*: “of the Lord,” Greek *Ἰησοῦ* (“of Jesus”).]

Pilate went into the praetorium again, called Jesus, and said to him: “Are you the king of the Jews?”] [Note: [Col. 0708] *galaiþ*: Ulfila omits *οὖν* (“then”).]

Jesus answered: “Do you say this of your own accord, or did others tell you about me?”] [Note: [Col. 0708] *andhof*: Ulfila and the manuscripts have *αὐτῷ* (“to him”).] [Note: [Col. 0708] *abu*: that is, “[lacuna]f-u,” *abne*.]

Pilate answered: “Am I a Jew? Your nation and the chief priests handed you over to me. What have you done?”] [Note: [Col. 0708] *vaitei*: St. adds *vaite*.]

Jesus answered: “My kingdom is not from this world. If my kingdom were from this world, my attendants would fight so that I would not be handed over to the Jews. But now my kingdom is not from here.”] [Note: [Col. 0708] *meina þiudangardi*: according to the Greek.] [Note: [Col. 0708] *usdaudidedeina*: the Arg. manuscript and the editors have *usdaudedideina*, with the syllables *de* and *di* transposed by a copyist’s error; compare Galatians 4:11, *arbaidedidjau* instead of *arbaididedjau*, and Luke 14:29.]

Pilate therefore said to him: “So you are a king?” Jesus answered: “You say that I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I came into the world: to testify to the truth. Everyone who belongs to the truth hears my voice.”] [Note: [Col. 0708] *an nuh*: J. St. adds *jct.*] [Note: [Col. 0708] *andhafjands*: “answering”; all Greek manuscripts have *ἀπεκρίθη*.] [Note: [Col. 0708] *veitvodjau*: Z. adds *veidvodjau*.] [Note: [Col. 0708] *stibnos meinaizos*: according to all Greek manuscripts.]

Then Pilate said to him: “What is truth?” Having said this, he went out again to the Jews and said to them: “I find no fault in him.”] [Note: [Col. 0708] *þanuh*: “then,” omitted in all Greek manuscripts.] [Note: [Col. 0708] *so*: “this,” omitted in the Greek.] [Note: [Col. 0708] *qiþands*: Ulfila omits *πάλιν* (“again”).] [Note: [Col. 0708] *ïm*: J. St. omits *du ïm* (“to them”).]

“It is your custom that I release one man to you at the Passover. Do you therefore wish me to release to you the king of the Jews?”] [Note: [Col. 0708] *ei*: “so that,” omitted by all Greek manuscripts except the apostolic codex and Mi.] [Note: [Col. 0708] *fraletau ïzvis*: according to the Greek.]

Then they all cried out again, saying: “Not this man, but Barabbas!” Now Barabbas was a criminal.] [Note: [Col. 0708] *eis*: “they,” omitted in all Greek manuscripts.] [Note: [Col. 0708] *sah*: “this man,” omitted by all Greek manuscripts; otherwise J. St. omits *sa*.]

Then Pilate took Jesus and scourged him.] [Note: [Col. 0707] *panuh þan nam peilatus ïesu jah usblaggv*: “Then Pilate took Jesus and scourged him.”]

The soldiers twisted a crown of thorns, placed it on his head, and dressed him in a purple garment.] [Note: [Col. 0707] *slahins lofin*: St. adds *jct.*]

They said: “Hail, King of the Jews!” And they struck him with the palm of the hand.] [Note: [Col. 0708] *slahins lofin*: St. adds *jct.*]

Pilate went out again and said to them: “Look, I am bringing him out to you, so that you may know that I find no fault in him.”] [Note: [Col. 0708] *bigat*: “I found,” Greek *εὑρίσκω*.]

Then Jesus came out, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple garment. Pilate said to them: “Here is the man.”] [Note: [Col. 0708] *ut ïesus*: according to the Greek.] [Note: [Col. 0708] *sa ïst*: “this is he,” all Greek manuscripts having *ἴδε* (“behold”).]

When the chief priests and the attendants saw him, they cried out, saying: “Crucify him, crucify him!” Pilate said to them: “Take him yourselves and crucify him; for I find no fault in him.”] [Note: [Col. 0708] *fairina—bigita*: according to all Greek manuscripts; otherwise J. St. B. omits *fairino*.]

The Jews answered him: “We have a law, and according to our law he ought to die, because he made himself the Son of God.”] [Note: [Col. 0709] *vitoþ*: St. adds *viþoþ*.] [Note: [Col. 0709] *guþs sunu*: according to the Greek.]

When Pilate heard this word, he was even more afraid.] [Note: [Col. 0709] *biþe*: Ulfila omits *οὖν* (“then”).]

He went into the praetorium again and said to Jesus: “Where are you from?” But Jesus gave him no answer.] [Note: [Col. 0709] *andavaurdi*: We do not know why F. and Z. are offended by this form; compare Luke 2:47 and *gavaurdi* in 1 Corinthians 15:33.] [Note: [Col. 0709] *þanuh*: “then,” omitted in the Greek.] [Note: [Col. 0710] *þuk*: the second occurrence; St. adds *þu*.]

Pilate therefore said to him: “Do you not speak to me? Do you not know that I have authority to crucify you, and authority to release you?”]

Jesus answered: “You would have no authority over me at all, unless it had been given to you from above. Therefore the one who handed me over to you has the greater sin.”] [Note: [Col. 0710] *ïupaþro*: Z. adds *jupaþro*.] [Note: [Col. 0710] *habaid*: J. St. B. omit *habaiþ*.]

From this point Pilate sought to release him, but the Jews cried out, saying: “If you release this man, you are not Caesar’s friend. Everyone who makes himself a king opposes Caesar.”] [Note: [Col. 0710] *sawazuh*: thus the Arg. manuscript; St. and Z. add *sahwazuh*.]

When Pilate heard these words—] [Note: [Col. 0710] *þize*: “these things” or “these words,” Greek *τοῦτον* (*τὸν λόγον*).]

Then Pilate, hearing this, [continued …]

# EPISTLES

## TO THE ROMANS
[Note: [Col. 0709] For the wages of sin are death, but the grace of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus, our Lord.]

[Note: [Col. 0709] These words are read in Codex Ambrosianus A.]

[Note: [Col. 0709] *auk launa*: This is our conjecture, which Castiglione, who himself had printed *mikiluna*, admits is confirmed by the authority of Codex A after re-examining it. The unusual use of the article is not objectionable here; see XIII, 3 *þai auk reiks*; X, 1 *sa raihtis vilja*.]

*þo auk launa fravaurhtais dauþus. ïþ ansts guþs libains aiveino ïn xristau ïesu fraujin unsa*

““For the wages of sin are death, but the grace of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus, our Lord.”.”

[Note: [Col. 0709] Or do you not know, brothers—for I speak to those who know the law—that the law rules over a person for as long as he lives?]

[Note: [Col. 0709] *mann sva*: Codex A and Castiglione add *manns*. First, *mann* must be the dative required by the construction of the verb *fraujinon*; secondly, although Castiglione says that no trace of *sva* can be recognized in Codex A, the scribe has omitted only part of it, for *s* is written; compare verse 25, where, having omitted *k* in place of *ïk*, the scribe wrote only *ï*. Alternatively, the letters *va* may have disappeared through erasure in the margin.]

*ramma. þau niu vituþ. broþrjus. kunnandam auk vitoþ rodja. þatei vitoþ fraujinoþ mann sva lagga*

“Do you not know, brothers—for I speak to those who know the law—that the law rules over a person for as long as he lives?”

[Note: [Col. 0709] For the woman is bound by law to her living husband; but if the husband dies, she is released from the law of the husband.]

[Note: [Col. 0709] *jah auk*: “for,” corresponding throughout to Greek γάρ; compare I Corinthians XV, 16, *jah jabai auk* = εἰ γάρ.]

[Note: [Col. 0710] *uf va ra*: We reluctantly miss the article *so*, which the Goths usually add in this construction; see X, 6 *so us galaubeinai garaihtei*; XI, 21 *þans us gabaurþai astans*. See, however, IX, 11, where, with the article omitted in the same way, *bi gavaleinai muns* is written; compare the note on II Corinthians VII, 10.]

[Note: [Col. 0710] *at libandin abin*: Ulfilas appears to have read ζῶντος τοῦ ἀνδρός; see verse 3.]

*weila sve libaiþ. jah auk uf vaira qens at libandin abin gabundana ïst vitoda. aþþan jabai gasviltiþ*

“For as long as he lives. And indeed, while the husband lives, the woman is bound by the law. But if he dies—”

[Note: [Col. 0709] Therefore, while the husband lives, she will be called an adulteress if she belongs to another man; but if the husband dies, she is free from this law, so that she is not an adulteress if she belongs to another man.]

[Note: [Col. 0710] *þannu*: So Codex A; Castiglione adds *þanuh*. Instead of the printed *þanuh*, we believe *þannu* should be read also in I Corinthians XV, 18, for *þannu* = ἄρα; see Romans X, 17; XIV, 12, 19; II Corinthians V, 15, throughout, where the Greek has the corresponding particle.]

[Note: [Col. 0709] *haituda harinondei*: Corresponds to the Greek throughout.]

[Note: [Col. 0709] *jabai*: According to the Gothic manuscripts, corresponding to Greek δέ.]

*aba. galausjada af þamma vitoda abins. þannu þan at libandin abin haitada horinondei. jabai vairþiþ vaira anþaramma. jabai gasviltiþ vair. frija ïst þis vitodis ei ni sijai horinondei vaurþana abin anþaramma.*

“So then, she will be released from the law of the husband. Therefore, while the husband lives, she will be called an adulteress if she belongs to another man. But if the husband dies, she is free from this law, so that she is not an adulteress if she belongs to another man.”

[Note: [Col. 0709] Therefore now you also, my brothers, were put to death to the law through the body of Christ, so that you might belong to another—to him who was raised from the dead—in order that we might bear fruit for God.]

[Note: [Col. 0710] *nu*: “now,” corresponding throughout to Greek νυνί.]

[Note: [Col. 0710] *jah jus*: The Greek has this after *meinai*.]

*svaei nu jah jus. broþrjus meinai. afdauþidai vaurþuþ vitoda þairh leik xristaus. ei vairþaiþ*

“Thus now you also, my brothers, were put to death to the law through the body of Christ, so that you might belong—”

[Col. 0711]

[Note: [Col. 0711] For while we were in the flesh, the passions of sins, which came through the law, worked in our members so as to bear fruit for death.]

[Note: [Col. 0711] *fravaurhti*: So Codex A, instead of *fravaurhte*, as in Titus I, 14 *spilli* instead of *spille*.]

*anþaramma þamma us dauþaim urreisandin. ei akran bairaima guþa. þan auk vesum ïn leika.*

“for another, who was raised from the dead, so that we might bear fruit for God. For when we were in the flesh—”

[Note: [Col. 0711] But now, behold, we have been released from the law, having died to that in which we were held, so that we may serve in newness of spirit and not in the oldness of the letter.]

[Note: [Col. 0711] *sai*: “behold.” This particle, joined with the adverb *nu*, almost always renders Greek νυνί in Gothic; see I Corinthians V, 11; II Corinthians VIII, 11, 22; Ephesians II, 13. It is also used for simple νῦν in Galatians IV, 9, while simple *nu* renders νυνί in Romans VII, 17; I Corinthians XII, 18, 20; XV, 20; Colossians I, 21; III, 8. Finally, *sai* renders νῦν in I Thessalonians III, 8.]

*vinnons fravaurhti þos þairh vitoþ vaurhtedun ïn liþum unsaraim du akran bairan dauþau. ïþ nu sai andbundanai vaurþum af vitoda gadauþnandans ïn þammei gahabaidai vesum svaei skalkinoma*

“The sinful passions worked through the law in our members to bear fruit for death. But now, behold, we have been released from the law, having died to that in which we were held, so that we may serve—”

[Note: [Col. 0711] What shall we say, then? Is the law sin? Certainly not. Yet I would not have known sin except through the law; for I would not have known covetousness unless the law had said, ‘You shall not covet.’]

[Note: [Col. 0711] *ïst*: “is,” corresponding to Greek.]

[Note: [Col. 0711] *ni sijai*: Note this spelling of the formula here and in verse 13; elsewhere it is usually written *nis sijai*; see Luke XX, 16; Romans IX, 14; XI, 1, 11; Galatians II, 17.]

[Note: [Col. 0711] *unte*: Gothic for Greek τε; see the note on Luke II, 16.]

[Note: [Col. 0711] *qeþi*: So Codex A; Castiglione adds *qeþ*.]

*ïn niujiþai ahmins jah ni fairniþai bokos. wa nu qiþam. vitoþ fravaurhts ïst. ni sijai. ak fravaurht*

“in newness of spirit and not in oldness of the letter. What shall we say, then? Is the law sin? Certainly not. But sin—”

[Note: [Col. 0711] Yet sin, taking an opportunity through the commandment, worked in me every kind of covetousness; for apart from the law sin was dead.]

[Note: [Col. 0711] *nimands*: Instead of *nimandei*; see the note on Nehemiah VI, 16.]

*ni ufkunþedjau. nih þairh vitoþ. unte lustu nih kunþedjau. nih vitoþ qeþi. ni gairnjais. ïþ lev nimands*

““I would not have known sin except through the law; for I would not have known covetousness unless the law had said, ‘You shall not covet.’ But sin, taking—”—”

[Note: [Col. 0711] But I was once alive apart from sin; when the commandment came, sin came to life again.]

[Note: [Col. 0711] *simle—libaida*: In all the Greek manuscripts these words occur in different positions.]

[Note: [Col. 0711] *qimandein*: Gothic for Greek δέ (*þan*). Castiglione perhaps could not read the word, for because the parchment was erased he admits that he conjectured *qimandein anabusnai* rather than actually read it.]

*fravaurhts þairh anabusn gavaurhta ïn mis allana lustu. unte ïnu vitoþ fravaurhts vas navis. ïþ ïk*

“sin through the commandment worked in me every kind of covetousness. For apart from the law sin was dead. But I—”

[Note: [Col. 0711] But I died, and the commandment that was intended for life was found by me to be for death.]

[Note: [Col. 0711] *gadauþnoda*: In Codex A nothing more than *gadauþ* could be read; Castiglione correctly completed it.]

[Note: [Col. 0711] *visan*: “to be,” corresponding throughout to Greek, which has αὕτη or αὐτή instead. The infinitive depends on *bigitana varþ*.]

*simle ïnu vitoþ libaida. at qimandein anabusnai fravaurhts gaqiunoda. ïþ ik gadauþnoda jah bigitana*

““But I formerly lived apart from the law. When the commandment came, sin came to life, but I died, and the commandment intended for life was found to be for death to me—”—”

[Note: [Col. 0711] Now sin, taking an opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me.]

*varþ mis anabusns. sei vas du libainai. visan du dauþau. unte fravaurhts lev nimands þairh anabusn*

“the commandment became death for me, although it was intended for life. For sin, taking—”

[Note: [Col. 0711] Therefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy and righteous and good.]

[Note: [Col. 0711] *aþþan nu*: “but now,” corresponding throughout to Greek ὥστε.]

*uslutoda mik jah þairh þo usqam. aþþan nu sveþauh vitoþ veihata jah anabusns veiha jah*

“sin, taking an opportunity through the commandment, deceived me and through it killed me. Therefore the law is indeed holy, and the commandment holy and—”

[Note: [Col. 0711] Did that which is good, then, become death to me? Certainly not; but sin did, so that sin might be shown to be sin through the good thing working death in me, so that through the commandment sin might become exceedingly sinful.]

[Note: [Col. 0711] *varþ mis*: Corresponds to the Greek throughout.]

[Note: [Col. 0711] *ni sijai*: See the note on verse 7.]

*garaihta jah þiuþeiga. þata nu þiuþeigo varþ mis dauþus. ni sijai. ak fravaurhts. ei uskunpa vaurþi fravaurhts þairh þata þiuþeigo mis gavaurkjandei dauþu. ei vaurþi ufarassau fravaurhta fravaurhts*

“righteous and good. Did that which is good become death to me? Certainly not, but sin did, so that sin might be recognized as sin through that which is good, working death in me, so that through the commandment sin might become exceedingly sinful.”

[Note: [Col. 0711] For we know that the law is spiritual, but I am fleshly, sold under sin.]

*þairh anabusn. vitum auk þatei vitoþ ahmein ïst. ïþ ïk leikeins ïm frabauhts uf fravaurht.*

“through the commandment. For we know that the law is spiritual, but I am fleshly, sold under sin.”

[Note: [Col. 0711] What I do, I do not understand; for I do not do what I want, but what I hate—that I do.]

[Note: [Col. 0712] *þatei*: Gothic for Greek γάρ.]

[Note: [Col. 0712] *viljau*: Gothic manuscripts correspond to Greek τοῦτο.]

[Note: [Col. 0711] But if I do what I do not want, I agree with the law that it is good.]

*þatei vaurkja. ni fraþja. unte ni þatei viljau tauja. ak þatei hatja þata tauja. ïþ jabai þatei in viljau*

“What I do, I do not understand. For I do not do what I want, but what I hate—that I do. But if I do what I do not want—”

[Note: [Col. 0711] But now it is no longer I who do it, but sin dwelling in me.]

*þata tauja. gaqiss ïm vitoda. þatei goþ. ïþ nu ju ni ïk vaurkja þata ak so bauandei ïn mis fravaurhts.*

“I do what I do not want. I agree with the law that it is good. But now it is no longer I who do it, but sin dwelling in me.”

[Note: [Col. 0711] For I know that good does not dwell in me—that is, in my flesh—for willing is present with me, but I do not find the ability to do good.]

[Note: [Col. 0712] *bauïþ*: So Codex A instead of *bauaiþ*, as though it derived from the form of the first conjugation. We have not altered it, because the same form occurs in verses 20 and 9, and in II Timothy I, 14.]

[Note: [Col. 0712] *atligiþ*: So Codex A; Castiglione adds *ataigiþ*.]

*vait auk þatei ni bauïþ ïn mis. þat-ïst ïn leika meinamma. þiuþ. unte viljan atligiþ mis. ïþ gavaurkjan*

“For I know that good does not dwell in me, that is, in my flesh. For willing is present with me, but doing good—”

[Note: [Col. 0711] For I do not do the good that I want, but I do the evil that I do not want.]

[Note: [Col. 0712] *ubil*: Gothic for Greek τοῦτο.]

[Note: [Col. 0711] Therefore, if I do what I do not want, it is no longer I who do it, but sin dwelling in me.]

[Note: [Col. 0712] *bauïþ*: See the note on verse 18.]

*goþ ni bigita. unte ni þatei viljau vaurkja goþ ak þatei ni viljau ubil tauja. jabai nu þatei ni viljau*

“I do not find the good. For I do not do the good that I want, but I do the evil that I do not want. Now if I do what I do not want—”

[Note: [Col. 0711] I find this law, then, when I want to do good: evil is present with me.]

[Note: [Col. 0712] *goþ taujan*: Corresponds throughout to the Greek.]

[Note: [Col. 0712] *atïst ubil*: Corresponds throughout to the Greek.]

*ïk. þata tauja. ju ni ïk vaurkja ïta ak sei bauïþ ïn mis fravaurhts. bigita nu vitoþ viljandin mis goþ*

“I do what I do not want. It is no longer I who do it, but sin dwelling in me. I find, then, the law for me who want to do good—”

[Note: [Col. 0711] For I delight in the law of God according to the inner person.]

[Note: [Col. 0712] *ïnnumin*: See the note on Colossians I, 29.]

* [Note: [Col. 0711] but I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind and taking me captive in the law of sin that is in my members.]

[Note: [Col. 0712] *andvaihando*: So Codex A and Castiglione; the reading is undoubtedly false. In its place one should write either *andvaihando* (compare I Corinthians XV, 32) or perhaps *andvaihjando*.]

*taujan. unte mis atïst ubil. gavizneigs ïm auk vitoda guþs bi þamma ïnnumin mann. aþþan gasaiwa anþar vitoþ ïn liþum meinaim andvaihando vitoda ahmins meinis jah frahinþando mik ïn vitoda*

“I find the law, when I want to do good, that evil is present with me. For I delight in the law of God according to the inner person, but I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind and taking me captive in the law—”

[Note: [Col. 0711] Wretched man that I am! Who will deliver me from this body of this death?]

[Note: [Col. 0712] *vainans*: Castiglione is mistaken in taking this as the passive participle of the verb *vainan*. Perhaps *vainahs* should be read. Grimm, Grammar IV, 78 and 763, emends it to *vainags*; but if the letter-forms are considered, *vainahs*, which we have not conjectured, is more probable.]

*fravaurhtais þamma visandin ïn liþum meinaim. vainans ïk manna. was mik lauseiþ us þamma leika*

“of sin that exists in my members. Wretched man that I am! Who will deliver me from this body—”

[Note: [Col. 0711] I give thanks to God through Jesus Christ—]

[Col. 0713]

[Note: [Col. 0711] our Lord. So then, I myself serve the law of God with my mind, but with my flesh the law of sin.]

[Note: [Col. 0712] *jau*: So Codex A, but this seems false to us, because the particle *jau*, which serves to form a question (see Luke VI, 7; John VII, 48), is not admitted by the sense here. Castiglione conjectured *jai*, not implausibly; compare below IX, 18 and 20. Unless we are being too bold, we propose *sai*, as *sai nu* renders Greek ἄρα οὖν in Ephesians II, 19.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] *ïk*: Castiglione adds *o*; Codex A has *ï*. See the note on verse 1.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] *skalkino gahugdai*: Corresponds throughout to the Greek; otherwise the Gothic manuscripts correspond to Greek μέν.]

*dauþaus þis. aviliudo guþa þairh ïesu xristu fraujan unsarana. jau nu silba ïk skalkino gahugdai*

“of this death. Thanks be to God through Jesus Christ our Lord. So then, I myself serve with my mind—”

[Col. 0713]

[Note: [Col. 0713] There is therefore now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus, who do not walk according to the flesh.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] *þannu nu*: Castiglione adds *jct.*, as this learned man consistently writes.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] *ni—leika*: “not—body,” corresponding to the Greek, which places *gaggandam* after *leika*.]

*vitoda guþs ïþ leika vitoda fravaurhtais. ni vaiht þannu nu vargiþos þaim ïn xristau ïesu ni gaggandam*

“of God, but the law of sin. There is therefore now no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus who do not walk—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set me free from the law of sin and death.]

*bi leika. unte vitoþ ahmins libainais ïn xristau ïesu frijana brahta mik vitodis fravaurhtais jah*

“according to the flesh. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus set me free from the law of sin and—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] For what was impossible for the law, weakened as it was through the flesh, God did, sending his own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and, on account of sin, condemned sin in the flesh.]

*dauþaus. unte þata unmahteigo vitodis. ïn þammei siuks vas þairh leik. guþ seinana sunu ïnsandjands*

“death. For what was impossible for the law, because it was weak through the flesh, God did, sending his own Son—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] so that the righteous requirement of the law might be fulfilled in us who do not walk according to the flesh.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] *gaggandam*: Gothic for Greek ἀλλὰ κατὰ πνεῦμα.]

*ïn galeikja leikis fravaurhtais ja bi fravaurht gavargida fravaurht ïn leika. ei garaihtei*

“in the likeness of sinful flesh, and on account of sin condemned sin in the flesh, so that the righteousness—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] For those who are according to the flesh think about the things of the flesh, but those who are according to the Spirit think about the things of the Spirit.]

*vitodis usfulljaidau ïn uns þaim ni bi leika gaggandam. unte þai bi leika visandans þo þoei leikis*

“of the law might be fulfilled in us who do not walk according to the flesh. For those who are according to the flesh think about the things of the flesh—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] But the mind of the flesh is death, whereas the mind of the Spirit is life and peace.]

*sind mitond. ïp þai bi ahmin þo þoei ahmins. aþþan fraþi leikis dauþus. ïp fraþi ahmins libains*

“They think about them. But those who are according to the Spirit think about the things of the Spirit. The mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] For the mind of the flesh is hostile to God; it does not submit to the law of God, nor indeed can it.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] *vitoda*: Gothic for Greek γάρ, while the sense is nevertheless preserved.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] And those who are in the flesh cannot please God.]

*jah gavairþi. unte fraþi leikis fijands du guþa vitoda guþs ni ufhauseiþ. ïþ nih mag. aþþan ïn*

““And peace. For the mind of the flesh is hostile to God; it does not submit to God’s law, nor indeed can it. But those who are in—”—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] But you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, that person does not belong to him.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] *þis—ïs*: These words have changed places in all the Greek manuscripts. It should also be noted that *ni ïst* is written here, whereas elsewhere it is written *nist* through synaloepha; see the note on VII, 7.]

*leika visandans guþa galeikan ni magun. ïþ jus ni sijuþ ïn leika ak ïn ahmin. sveþauh jabai ahma*

“being in the flesh, cannot please God. But you are not in the flesh, but in the Spirit—if indeed the Spirit—”

[[Note: [Col. 0713] If indeed Christ is in you, the flesh indeed—]—]

*guþs bauïþ ïn ïzvis. ïþ jabai was ahman xristaus ni habai. þis ni ïst ïs. jabai auk xristus ïn ïzvis.*

“the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, that person does not belong to him. But if Christ is in you—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] who is at the right hand of God and also intercedes for us.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] *saei*: Gothic manuscripts correspond to Greek καί.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] *bidjiþ*: So Codex A; Castiglione adds *bideiþ*.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] Who will separate us from the love of Christ? Tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword?]

*leiks raihtis------saei ïst ïn taihsvon guþs. saei jah bidjiþ faur uns. was uns afskaidai af friaþvai*

““the body indeed [lacuna]—he who is at the right hand of God, who also intercedes for us. Who will separate us from the love—”—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] As it is written: For your sake we are put to death all day long; we were counted as sheep for slaughter.]

*xristaus. aglo þau aggviþa þau vrakja þau huhrus þau naqadei þau sleiþei þau hairus. svasve*

“of Christ? Tribulation, or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or danger, or sword. As—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] But in all these things we conquer through him who loved us.]

*gameliþ ïst þatei ïn þuk gadauþjanda all dagis. rahnidai vesum sve lamba slauhtais. akei ïn þaim*

“It is written: For your sake we are put to death all day long; we were counted as sheep for slaughter. But in all these things—”

[[Note: [Col. 0713] For I confess that neither death, nor angels, nor rulers, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come—]—]

[Note: [Col. 0713] *dauþus*: Gothic for οὔτε ζωή.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] *reikja*: Castiglione supplied this word by conjecture, since he could not read it in the manuscript.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] *ni mahteis*: The Greek places this after *anavairþo*.]

*allaim jiukam þairh þana frijondan uns. gatraua auk þatei ni dauþus nih aggeljus ni reikja ni mahteis*

“we conquer through him who loved us. For I am convinced that neither death nor angels, nor rulers nor powers—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] nor things present nor things to come, nor heights nor depths, nor any other creature will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus, our Lord.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] *nih*: Third occurrence; the Gothic manuscripts correspond to Greek τίς.]

*nih andvairþo nih anavairþo. nih hauhiþa nih diupiþa nih gaskafts anþara mahteiga ïst uns*

“nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing is able to separate us—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] I speak the truth in Christ; I do not lie, my conscience bearing witness with me in the Holy Spirit.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] *qiþa*: Gothic for ἐν Χριστῷ.]

[Note: [Col. 0714] *vaiht*: “anything,” corresponding throughout to the Greek.]

*afskaidan af friaþvai guþs þizai ïn xristau ïesu fraujin unsaramma. sunja qiþa. ni vaiht liuga miþveitvodjandein*

“separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus, our Lord. I speak the truth: I do not lie, my conscience bearing witness—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] that I have great sorrow and continual pain in my heart.]

[Note: [Col. 0714] *unweilo*: Note the concrete form, as it is called, following the abstract one (*mikila*); compare *ni ïbna nih galeiks* in the Gothic Skeireins 37, 6, and *ni ïbnon ak galeika* in 46, 17.]

*mis miþvissein meinai ïn ahmin veihamma. þatei saurga mis ïst mikila jah unweilo*

““in the Holy Spirit; that I have great sorrow and continual pain—”—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] For I could wish that I myself were accursed and separated from Christ for the sake of my brothers, my kinsmen according to the flesh.]

[Note: [Col. 0714] *usbida*: “I pray,” corresponding to Greek ηὐχόμην. Here *usbida* occurs instead of *usbidja*, as *bidan* occurs for *bidjan* in I Corinthians VII, 5. Grimm, Grammar IV, 101, more boldly writes *usbidja*.]

[Note: [Col. 0714] *silba ïk*: So Codex A; Castiglione adds *silban*. The Greek has this after *auk*.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] *samakunjans*: The Gothic manuscripts correspond to Greek μοῦ.]

*aglo hairtin meinamma. usbida auk anaþaima visan silba ik af xristau faur broþruns meinans þans*

“in my heart. For I could wish that I myself were accursed, separated from Christ, for the sake of my brothers—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] who are Israelites, whose are adoption, glory, covenants, giving of the law, service, and promises.]

[Note: [Col. 0714] *ïst*: “is,” corresponding throughout to the Greek.]

[Note: [Col. 0714] *jah triggvos*: The Greek manuscripts place this before *jah vitodis*.]

*samakunjans bi leika. þaiei sind ïsraelitai. þizeei ïst frastisibja jah vulþus jah vitodis garaideins*

“my kinsmen according to the flesh, who are Israelites, whose are adoption, glory, the covenants, and the giving of the law—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] whose are the patriarchs, and from whom Christ is according to the flesh, who is God over all, blessed forever. Amen.]

*jah triggvos jah skalkinassus jah gahaita. þizeei attans jah us þaimei xristus bi leika. saei ïst*

“and the covenants, service, and promises; whose are the patriarchs, and from whom Christ is according to the flesh, who is—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] Yet it is not as though the word of God has failed; for not all who are from Israel are Israel.]

[Note: [Col. 0714] *sind*: “are,” corresponding throughout to the Greek.]

*ufar allaim guþ þiuþiþs ïn aivam amen. aþþan sveþauh ni usdraus vaurd guþs. ni auk allai þai us*

“over all, God, blessed forever. Amen. Yet it is not as though the word of God has failed. For not all those who are from—”

[Note: [Col. 0713] nor are all Abraham’s descendants his children; but, ‘In Isaac your offspring shall be called.’]

[Note: [Col. 0714] *þaiei*: “who”; Greek throughout has ὅτι, which might lead one to suspect that *þatei* should be read; see the note on Luke VIII, 14. Nevertheless, there are versions and Fathers that read ὅσοι and *qui*.]

*ïsrael þai sind ïsrael. niþ-þaiei sijaina fraiv abrahamis allai barna. ak ïn ïsaka. haitada þus fraiv.*

“Israel are Israel. Nor are all Abraham’s offspring children; but, ‘In Isaac your offspring shall be called.’”

[Note: [Col. 0713] That is, not the children of the flesh are children of God, but the children of the promise are counted as offspring.]

[Note: [Col. 0714] *þo*: “these”; Ulfilas joins the Gothic *þo* with the preceding Greek τὰ τέκνα τῆς σαρκός.]

[Note: [Col. 0713] For the word of promise is this: ‘At this time I will come, and Sarah shall have a son.’]

[Col. 0715]

[Note: [Col. 0714] *ïst*: “is,” corresponding throughout to the Greek.]

*þat-ïst ni þo barna leikis barna guþs. ak barna gahaitis rahnjanda du fraiva. gahaitis auk vaurd*

“That is, not the children of the flesh are children of God, but the children of the promise are counted as offspring. For the word of promise is—”

[Note: [Col. 0715] and not only this, but Rebecca also, when she had conceived by one act of intercourse with Isaac our father.]

*þat-ïst. bi þamma mela qima jah vairþiþ sarrin sunus. aþþan ni þat-ain ak jah raibaikka us*

“That is: ‘At this time I will come, and Sarah shall have a son.’ But not only this; Rebecca also, from—”

[Note: [Col. 0715] For while they had not yet been born and had done nothing good or bad, so that God’s purpose according to election might remain—not from works, but from the one who calls—]

[Note: [Col. 0715] *ni*: At the beginning; Castiglione adds it. Although it has been obliterated in Codex A, sufficient space remains for the word.]

[Note: [Col. 0715] *aiþþau*: At the beginning, “otherwise”; Greek μηδέ, although the translator renders the sense rather than the words.]

*ainamma galigrja habandei ïsakis attins unsaris. aþþan nauhþanuh ni gabauranai vesun. aiþþau tavidedeina wa þiuþis aiþþau unþiuþis ei bi gavaleinai muns guþs visai ni us vaurstvam ak us*

“having one act of intercourse with Isaac our father. But while they had not yet been born, nor had done anything good or bad, so that God’s purpose according to election might remain, not from works but from—”

[Note: [Col. 0715] It was said to her: ‘The elder shall serve the younger,’ as it is written:]

[Note: [Col. 0715] ‘Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated.’]

[Note: [Col. 0715] *fijaida*: A marginal variant reading has been completely erased. I suspect that *andvaih* (“I opposed”) should be read. Castiglione.]

*þamma laþondin. qiþan ïst ïzai þatei sa maiza skalkinoþ þamma minnizin. svasve gameliþ ïst. ïakob*

“to the one who calls. It was said to her: ‘The elder shall serve the younger,’ as it is written: ‘Jacob—’”

[Note: [Col. 0715] What shall we say, then? Is there injustice with God? Certainly not; for he says to Moses: ‘I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will show compassion to whom I show compassion.’]

[Note: [Col. 0715] *gableiþja*: Gothic for ὃν ἂν οἰκτίρω (*þanei gableiþja*). The omission was undoubtedly caused by the scribe’s error, for the words cannot be absent without damaging the sense. Such scribal omissions often occurred when the same words appeared twice in one verse and the eye slipped from one occurrence to the other; see Mark X, 39; John X, 18; II Corinthians III, 5; IV, 10; XIII, 11 (Codex B); Ephesians V, 4; compare Mark XI, 7; II Corinthians V, 18; Galatians IV, 7, and the note on Luke X, 5.]

*frijoda ïþ esav fijaida. wa nu qiþam. ïbai ïnvindiþa fram guþa. nis-sijai. du mose auk qiþiþ.*

“Jacob I loved, but Esau I hated. What shall we say, then? Is there injustice with God? Certainly not. For he says to Moses—”

[Note: [Col. 0715] Therefore it depends not on the one who wills or on the one who runs, but on God who shows mercy.]

[Note: [Col. 0715] *gaarma þanei arma jah gableiþja*: “I will have mercy on whom I have mercy, and I will show compassion on whom I show compassion.”]

*ga arma þanei arma jah gableiþja. þannu nu ni viljandins ni rinnandins ak armandins guþs.*

“Therefore it depends not on the one who wills or on the one who runs, but on God who shows mercy.”

[Note: [Col. 0715] For Scripture says to Pharaoh: ‘For this very purpose I raised you up, so that I might show my power in you and so that my name might be proclaimed throughout all the earth.’]

[Note: [Col. 0715] *jah*: First occurrence, “also,” corresponding throughout to the Greek.]

[Note: [Col. 0715] *jah*: Second occurrence, corresponding to Greek ὅπως.]

*giþiþ auk þata gamelido du faraoni. unte ïn þize jah raisida þuk ei gabairhtjau bi þus maht meina*

“For Scripture says to Pharaoh: ‘For this very purpose I raised you up, so that I might show my power in you—’”

[Note: [Col. 0715] Therefore he has mercy on whom he wills, but he hardens whom he wills.]

[Note: [Col. 0715] *jai*: “indeed,” corresponding throughout to the Greek.]

*jah gateihaidau namo mein and alla airþa. þannu nu jai þanei vili armaiþ ïþ þanei vili gahardeiþ.*

“and so that my name might be proclaimed throughout all the earth. Therefore he has mercy on whom he wills, but whom he wills he hardens.”

[Note: [Col. 0715] You will say to me, then: ‘Why does he still find fault? For who has resisted his will?’]

[Note: [Col. 0715] *mis nu*: Corresponds to the Greek.]

[Note: [Col. 0715] *aþþan*: “but,” corresponding throughout to the Greek.]

[Note: [Col. 0715] *andstand*: See the note on II Corinthians XIII, 3.]

*qiþis mis nu. aþþan wa nauh faianda. unte viljin ïs was andstandiþ. þannu nu jai manna. þu was*

“You will say to me, then: ‘Why does he still find fault? For who has resisted his will?’ Therefore, indeed, O man, who are you—”

[Note: [Col. 0715] Indeed, O man, who are you to answer back to God? Shall the molded thing say to the one who molded it, ‘Why did you make me thus?’]

*ïs ei andvaurdjais guþa. ïbai qiþiþ gadikis du þamma digandin. wa mik gatavides sva.*

“that you should answer God? Shall the molded thing say to the one who molded it, ‘Why did you make me thus?’”

[Note: [Col. 0715] Or does the potter not have authority over the clay, from the same lump, to make one vessel for honor and another for dishonor?]

[Note: [Col. 0715] *kasja valdufni*: Corresponds throughout to the Greek.]
