[Note: [Col. 0715] *kasa*: Castiglione, not knowing why he was led into this error, takes it as a plural, although it is a singular dative governed by *du*.]

*þau niu habaiþ kasja valdufni þahons us þamma samin daiga taujan sum du galaubamma kasa. sumuþ-þan*

“Do you not have authority over the clay, from the same lump, to make one vessel for honor and another—”

[Note: [Col. 0715] But if God, wishing to show his wrath and make known his power, endured with great patience vessels of wrath prepared for destruction—]

[Note: [Col. 0716] *mahteigo*: Gothic for Greek αὐτοῦ.]

[Note: [Col. 0716] *usbeidands*: “enduring,” corresponding throughout to Greek ἤνεγκεν.]

*du ungalaubamma. ïþ jabai viljands guþ ustaiknjan þvairhein jah uskannjan þata mahteigo*

“for dishonor. But if God, wishing to show his wrath and make known his power—”

[Note: [Col. 0715] in order to show the abundance of his glory upon vessels of mercy, which he prepared beforehand for glory—]

[Note: [Col. 0716] At the beginning, the Gothic manuscripts correspond to Greek καί.]

[Note: [Col. 0716] *vulþus*: Instead of *vulþaus*; see the note on Luke I, 54.]

*usbeidands ïn managai laggamodein bi kasam þvairheins gamanvidaim du fralustai. ei gakannidedi*

“enduring with much patience the vessels of wrath prepared for destruction, so that he might make known—”

[Note: [Col. 0715] the abundance of his glory upon vessels of mercy, which he prepared beforehand for glory, namely us, whom he also called, not only from the Jews but also from the nations.]

*gabein vulþus seinis bi kasam armaions. þoei fauragamanvida du vulþau. þanzei jah laþoda uns*

“the abundance of his glory upon vessels of mercy, which he prepared beforehand for glory, namely us, whom he also called—”

[Note: [Col. 0715] as he also says in Hosea: ‘I will call the one who was not my people my people, and the one who was not loved, loved.’]

*ni þatainei us ïudaium ak jah us þiudom. svasve jah ïn oseïn qiþiþ. haita þo ni managein meina*

“not only from the Jews but also from the nations. As he also says in Hosea: ‘I will call the one who was not my people—’”

[Note: [Col. 0715] And it shall be: in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not my people,’ there they will be called sons of the living God.]

[Note: [Col. 0716] *þai*: “these”; so Codex A. Greek has ἐκεῖ, which is also found in those who read αὐτοί.]

*managein meina jah þo unliubona liubona. jah vairþiþ. ïn þamma stada þarei qiþada ïm. ni managei*

“my people, and the one who was not loved, loved. And it shall be: in the place where it was said to them, ‘You are not my people—’”

[Note: [Col. 0715] But Esaias cries out concerning Israel: ‘Though the number of the sons of Israel were like the sand of the sea, the remnant will be saved.’]

*meina jus þai haitanda sunjus guþs libandins. ïþ esaïas greteiþ bi ïsrael. jabai vesi raþjo sunive*

“my people, you will be called sons of the living God. But Esaias cries out concerning Israel: ‘Though the number of the sons of Israel—’”

[Note: [Col. 0715] For he completes and cuts short the word in righteousness, because the Lord will execute a shortened word upon the earth.]

*ïsraelis svasve malma mareins. laibos ganisand. vaurd auk ustiuhands jah gamaurgjands ïn garaihtein.*

“of Israel were like the sand of the sea, the remnant will be saved. For the Lord, completing and cutting short the word in righteousness—”

[Note: [Col. 0715] And as Esaias foretold: ‘Unless the Lord Sabaoth had left us offspring, we would perhaps have become like Sodom and perhaps would have been made like Gomorrah.’]

[Note: [Col. 0716] *nih*: Codex A and Castiglione add *niu*. Greek εἰ μή corresponds to *nih*, which we printed; we are weary of producing examples to prove it. *niu* serves to form a question, which the sense here does not permit.]

[Note: [Col. 0716] *fraiva*: Castiglione thinks that *fraiv* was written, but the reading of Codex A is correct, for *bileiþan* also governs the third case; see Mark XII, 19; John VIII, 29.]

*unte vaurd gamaurgiþ taujiþ frauja ana airþai. jah svasve fauraqaþ esaïas. nih frauja sabaoþ biliþi*

“For the Lord will execute a shortened word upon the earth. And as Esaias foretold: ‘Unless the Lord Sabaoth had left us offspring—’”

[Note: [Col. 0715] What shall we say, then? That the nations, who were not pursuing righteousness, attained righteousness—]

[Col. 0717]

[Note: [Col. 0716] *wa*: Codex A and Castiglione add *wo*. Since that is feminine, it has no place here; and even if, considering only the form, we wished to allow *wo* as neuter plural, the sense and the Greek text would not permit it.]

[Note: [Col. 0716] *galaubeinai*: Castiglione adds *galaubein*; Codex A has only *galaubei*. The form we printed is required by the preposition *us*. The same error occurs in Codex B at Colossians II, 23, where *unfreidei* is written instead of *unfreideinai*, correctly written in Codex A; compare the note on Luke XVIII, 11.]

[[Note: [Col. 0717] namely, righteousness that comes from faith.]

“offspring for us; we would have become like Sodom and been made like Gomorrah. What then shall we say? That the Gentiles, who were not pursuing righteousness, attained righteousness, namely the righteousness that comes from faith.”.]

[Note: [Col. 0717] But Israel, pursuing a law of righteousness, did not attain the law of righteousness.]

[Note: [Col. 0717] Why? Because it was not from faith but from works of the law. They stumbled over the stone of stumbling—]

[Note: [Col. 0717] *ak*: Gothic manuscripts have *k* for Greek ὡς.]

[Note: [Col. 0717] *bistuggqun*: Gothic manuscripts correspond to Greek γάρ.]

*us vaurstvam vitodis. bistuggqun du staina bistuggqis. svasve gameliþ ïst. sai. galagja ïn sion*

“from works of the law. They stumbled over the stone of stumbling, as it is written: ‘Behold, I place in Zion—’”

[Note: [Col. 0717] a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, and whoever believes in him will not be put to shame.]

[Note: [Col. 0717] *sa raihtis*: So Codex A; Castiglione adds *garaihtis*. See the note on IX, 33.]

*stain bistuggqis jah hallu gamarzeinais jah sa laubjands du ïmma ni gaaiviskoda. broþrjus. sa*

“a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense, and whoever believes in him will not be put to shame. Brothers, the—”

[Note: [Col. 0717] Brothers, the desire of my heart and my prayer to God for them is for salvation.]

*raihtis vilja meinis hairtins jah bida du guþa bi ïns du naseinai.*

“indeed, desire of my heart and prayer to God for them is for salvation.”

[Note: [Col. 0717] For I bear them witness that they have zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.]

*veitvodja auk ïm þatei aljan guþs*

“For I bear them witness that they have zeal for God—”

[Note: [Col. 0717] For, being ignorant of God’s righteousness and seeking to establish their own righteousness, they did not submit to God’s righteousness.]

*haband akei ni bi kunþja. unkunnandans auk guþs garaihtein jah seina garaihtein sokjandans*

“but not according to knowledge. For, being ignorant of God’s righteousness and seeking their own righteousness—”

[Note: [Col. 0717] For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone who believes.]

*stiurjan garaihtein guþs ni ufhausidedun. ustauhts auk vitodis xristus du garaihtein allaim þaim*

“seeking to establish their own righteousness, they did not submit to God’s righteousness. For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to everyone—”

[Note: [Col. 0717] who believes.]

[galaubjandam.]

“who believes.”

[Note: [Col. 0717] For “Moses writes concerning the righteousness from the law: ‘The person who does these things will live in—’” them.’]

[Note: [Col. 0717] *ïzai*: “by them,” corresponding to Greek αὐτοῖς.]

*moses auk meleiþ þo garaihtein us vitoda þatei sa taujands þo manna libaiþ ïn*

“Moses writes concerning the righteousness from the law: ‘The person who does these things will live by—’”

[Note: [Col. 0717] But the righteousness from faith says this: ‘Do not say in your heart, “Who will ascend into heaven?”’—that is, to bring Christ down—]

*ïzai. ïþ so us galaubeinai garaihtei sva qiþiþ. ni qiþais ïn hairtin þeinamma. was ussteigiþ*

““it. But the righteousness from faith says this: ‘Do not say in your heart, “Who will ascend—”’”—”’”

[Note: [Col. 0717] ‘or, “Who will descend into the abyss?”’—that is, to bring Christ up from the dead.]

[Note: [Col. 0717] *ïup*: Codex A has in the margin the remains *…rjo*; we do not know what word these belong to. We do know that it cannot be the adverb *ufarjo*, as Castiglione supposes, because the form he wants is written *ufaro*.]

*ïn himin. þat-ïst xristu dalaþ attiuhan. aiþþau was gasteigiþ ïn afgrundiþa. þat-ïst xristu us*

“into heaven—that is, to bring Christ down—or, ‘Who will descend into the abyss?’—that is, to bring Christ up—”

[Note: [Col. 0717] from the dead. But what does it say? ‘The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart’—that is, the word of faith which we proclaim.]

[Note: [Col. 0718] *galaubeinais*: Castiglione adds *gllaubeinais*.]

*dauþaim ïup ustiuhan. akei wa qiþiþ. newa þus þata vaurd ïst ïn munþa þeinamma jah ïn hairtin*

“from the dead. But what does it say? ‘The word is near you, in your mouth and in your heart’—”

[Note: [Col. 0717] that is, the word of faith which we proclaim.]

[Note: [Col. 0717] And if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.]

[Note: [Col. 0718] *ïesu*: Codex A adds *ui* for *ïu*.]

[Note: [Col. 0718] *urraisida us*: So Codex A, with the syllables *us da* written above the line as *daus* (*urraisidauþain*). Since Castiglione did not initially notice this, he printed *urraisi*.]

[Note: [Col. 0718] *ganisis*: So Codex A; Castiglione adds *ganisi*.]

*þeinamma. þat-ïst vaurd galaubeinais. þatei merjam. þei jabai andhaitis ïn munþa þeinamma fraujan ïesu jah galaubeis ïn hairtin þeinamma þatei guþ ïna urraisida us dauþaim. ganisis.*

“in your heart. That is the word of faith which we proclaim: if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.”

[Note: [Col. 0717] For with the heart one believes unto righteousness, but with the mouth one confesses unto salvation.]

[Note: [Col. 0718] *hairto—galaubeiþ*: “heart—believes,” corresponding throughout to Greek καρδία—πιστεύεται.]

[Note: [Col. 0718] *garaihtiþai*: Codex A and Castiglione add *garaihtiþa*.]

[Note: [Col. 0717] For Scripture says: ‘Everyone who believes in him will not be put to shame.’]

*hairto auk galaubeiþ du garaihtiþai. ïþ munþa andhaitada du ganistai. qiþiþ auk þata gameliþ.*

“For with the heart one believes unto righteousness, but with the mouth one confesses unto salvation. For Scripture says—”

[Note: [Col. 0717] For there is no distinction between Jew and Greek; the same Lord is Lord of all, rich toward all who call upon him.]

[Note: [Col. 0718] *ïudaiaus*: Gothic for Greek τέ; see the note on Luke II, 16.]

[Note: [Col. 0718] *krekis*: So Codex A; Castiglione adds *krekos*.]

*wazuh sa galaubjands du ïmma ni gaaiviskoda. ni auk ïst gaskaideins ïudaiaus jah krekis. sama*

“for there is no distinction between Jew and Greek. The same—”

[Note: [Col. 0717] For everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord will be saved.]

[Note: [Col. 0718] *bidai*: “by prayer,” corresponding throughout to Greek.]

[Note: [Col. 0717] How, then, will they call upon him in whom they have not believed? Or how will they believe in him whom they have not heard? And how will they hear without someone proclaiming?]

[Note: [Col. 0718] *ïnu*: Castiglione, with Codex A, adds *ïna*.]

[Note: [Col. 0718] *aiþþau*: “or,” corresponding throughout to Greek δέ; perhaps *aþþan* should therefore be read.]

*auk frauja allaize gabigs ïn allans þans bidjandans sik. wazuh auk saei anahaitiþ bidai namo*

“For the Lord of all is rich toward all who call upon him. For everyone who calls upon the name—”

[Note: [Col. 0717] of the Lord will be saved. How, then, will they call upon him in whom they have not believed? Or how will they believe in him whom they have not heard? But how will they hear without someone proclaiming?]

*fraujins ganisiþ. waiva nu bidjand þammei ni galaubidedun. aiþþau waiva galaubjand þammei*

“of the Lord will be saved. How, then, will they call upon him in whom they have not believed? Or how will they believe in him whom—”

[Note: [Col. 0717] But how will they proclaim unless they are sent? As it is written: ‘How beautiful are the feet of those who proclaim peace, of those who proclaim good things?’]

*ni hausidedun. ïþ waiva hausjand ïnu merjandan. ïþ waiva merjand niba ïnsandjanda. svasve*

“they have not heard? But how will they hear without someone proclaiming? And how will they proclaim unless they are sent? As—”

[Note: [Col. 0717] But not all obeyed the gospel. For Esaias says: ‘Lord, who believed our report?’]

*gameliþ ïst. waiva skaunjai fotjus þize spillondane gavairþi þize spillondane þiuþ. akei ni allai*

“It is written: ‘How beautiful are the feet of those who proclaim peace, of those who proclaim good things?’ But not all—”

[Note: [Col. 0717] So faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ.]

[Note: [Col. 0718] *þannu*: Castiglione adds *þau nu* (“or now”); see the note on VII, 3.]

[Note: [Col. 0718] *xristaus*: “of Christ,” whereas the Greek has Θεοῦ.]

*uf hausidedun aivaggeljon. esaïas auk qiþiþ. frauja. was galaubida hauseinai unsarai. þannu*

“obeyed the gospel. For Esaias says: ‘Lord, who believed our report?’ Therefore—”

[Note: [Col. 0717] But I say: Did they not hear? Indeed, their sound went out through the whole earth, and their words to the ends of the world.]

[Note: [Col. 0718] *raihtis*: Note the unusual position of this particle. Concerning the particle *auk*, which sometimes undergoes the same treatment, see the note on John IX, 30.]

[Note: [Col. 0718] *andins*: Castiglione read this after re-examining Codex A; see Castiglione’s Addenda to II Thessalonians, p. 65. If *andins* is correctly read, it belongs to *ands*, a form not previously known.]

*galaubeins us gahauseinai. ïþ gahauseins þairh vaurd xristaus. akei qiþa. ïbai ni hausidedun.*

“faith comes from hearing, and hearing through the word of Christ. But I say: Did they not hear?”

[Note: [Col. 0717] But I say: Did Israel not know? Moses is the first to say: ‘I will provoke you to jealousy by those who are not a nation; by a foolish nation I will provoke you to anger.’]

[Note: [Col. 0718] *ïnuh*: “without.” This reading of Codex A is undoubtedly false, for not only should an accusative follow *ïnuh*, but even then the sense would remain intolerable. Following the traces of the Greek text, it appears that *ïn ni* was written and should be restored. Massmann plausibly conjectures *ïn unthiudom* for *ïnuh þiudom*.]

[Col. 0719]

*raihtis and alla airþa galaiþ drunjus ïze jah and andins midjungardis vaurda ïze. akei qiþa.*

“Indeed, their sound went out through the whole earth, and their words to the ends of the world. But I say—”

[Col. 0719]

[:]

[Note: [Col. 0719] ‘I was found by those who were not seeking me; I became known to those who were not asking for me.’]

*ïbai ïsrael ni fanþ. frumist moses qiþiþ. ïk ïn aljana ïzvis brigga. ïnuh þiudom ïn þiuda*

““Did Israel not know? First Moses says: ‘I will provoke you to jealousy by a non-nation; by a foolish nation I will provoke you to anger—’”

[Note: [Col. 0719] But Esaias is bold and says:].]

*unfraþjandein ïn þvairhein ïzvis brigga. ïþ esaïas anananþeiþ jah qiþiþ. bigitans varþ miþ þaim*

“I will provoke you to anger by a foolish nation. But Esaias is very bold and says: ‘I was found by those—’”

[Note: [Col. 0719] But to Israel he says: ‘All day long I stretched out my hands to a disobedient and contrary people.’]

*ni gasokjandam. svikunþs varþ þaim mik ni gafraihnandam. ïþ du ïsraela qiþiþ. allana dag*

“who did not obey. I became known to those who did not inquire of me. But to Israel he says: ‘All day—’”

[Note: [Col. 0719] *seinamma*: A solecism for *seinai*; see the note on Nehemiah VI, 16.]

[Note: [Col. 0719] I stretched out my hands to a people who did not believe and who resisted.]

*usbraidida handuns meinos du managein ungalaubjandein jah andstandandein. qiþa nu. ïbai*

“I stretched out my hands to a people who did not believe and who resisted. I say, then: ‘Surely—’”

[Note: [Col. 0719] Or did they stumble so as to fall? Certainly not. But through their transgression salvation has come to the nations, in order to provoke them to jealousy.]

[Note: [Col. 0719] *gadruseina*: So Codex A; Castiglione adds *gadruseinai*.]

[Note: [Col. 0719] *missadedai*: So, apparently correctly, Codex A; Castiglione adds *missadeda*.]

[Note: [Col. 0719] *varþ*: “has come to pass.” All the Greek manuscripts have the corresponding form.]

[Note: [Col. 0719] *du*: This must be joined with *brigga*. It is thus separated from its infinitive by other words belonging to its domain; compare Philippians IV, 10 *du faur mik fraþjan*. Skeireins.]

I was found by those who were not seeking me; I became known to those who were not asking about me.” [Note: [Col. 0719] *miþ*] “with”: Gothic agrees with those manuscripts that have ἐν; cf. J. XII, 35.]

““To provoke you to jealousy.” But Isaiah boldly prophesies and says: “I was found by those who were not seeking me; I became known to those who were not asking about me.” But to Israel he says:: “All day long I stretched out my hands to a people who do not believe in me and who oppose me.” [Note: [Col. 0719] “But he says to Israel: Has God rejected his people? By no means! For I myself am an Israelite—”] [Note: [Col. 0719] *seinamma*] an idiom for *seinai*; see the note on Neh. VI, 16.]

“I stretched out my hands to a people that does not believe and resists.” I ask, then: “Did they stumble so as to fall?” By no means! Rather, through their trespass salvation came to the gentiles, in order to provoke them to jealousy. [Note: [Col. 0719] *gadruseina*] so Codex A; Cast. adds *gadruseinai*.—*missadedai*] apparently correctly so in Codex A; Cast. adds *missadeda*.—*varþ*] “came to be.” Greek universally.—*du*] must be joined with *briggan*; thus *du* is separated from its infinitive by intervening words belonging to its construction, as in Philipp. IV, 10, *du faur mik fraþjan* (“to think of me beforehand”), and *Skeir.* XL, 14, *du garehsn daupeinais andniman* (“to undertake the arrangement of baptism”); cf. the note on L. XIX, 7.]

Has God rejected his people? By no means! For I too am an Israelite—[lacuna]—that they might fall? By no means! [Note: [Col. 0719] “But if their trespass is the world’s wealth, and their failure the wealth of the gentiles, how much more will their fullness be?”]

But through their trespass salvation came to the gentiles, in order to provoke them to jealousy.. [Note: [Col. 0719] “To you, gentiles, I say: inasmuch as I am the apostle of the gentiles, I glorify my ministry, if somehow I may provoke my flesh to jealousy and save some of them.”] [Note: [Col. 0719] *sve*] Gothic manuscripts agreeing with μέν.—*ïk ïm*] by interpolation, Greek.]

Their trespass is the world’s wealth, and their loss the wealth of the gentiles. How much more will their fullness be! For I speak to you gentiles: insofar as I am the apostle of the gentiles, I glorify my ministry, if somehow I may provoke my flesh to jealousy and save some of them. [Note: [Col. 0719] *leik mein*] “my flesh,” according to the Greek.]

For if their rejection is the world’s reconciliation, what will their acceptance be but life from the dead? [Note: [Col. 0719] *gabei*] “wealth”; Greek universally has καταλλαγή, which is *gafriþons*. Here *gabei fairwaus* perhaps arose through a scribal error from *gabei fairwau* in verse 12. Moreover, instead of *was andanumts*, it would more correctly have been *wo andanumts*.]

If the first portion is holy, so is the whole mass; and if the root is holy, so are the branches. [Note: [Col. 0719] *þandei*] see the note on verse 21.]

And if some of the branches were broken off, while you, although a wild olive tree, were grafted in among them and became a sharer in the root and richness of the olive tree— [Note: [Col. 0719] “and if some of these branches have been broken off; but you, being a wild olive tree, were grafted into them and became a partner in the root and richness of the olive tree.”] [Note: [Col. 0719] *vaurtsai*] Cast. adds *vaurtsa*; Codex A, as Cast. says after reexamining it, adds *vaurhtsa*. From this false reading in Codex A we at least gain the certainty that *s* is the root’s nominative letter; and Cast., who at verse 18 notes *vaurts* as an accusative incorrectly written for *vaurt*, is now shown to have been mistaken. The plural *vaurteis* (see the note on Mc. IV, 6) supplies that *s*.—*varst*] see Cast.’s Addenda to Thess. II, p. 65.]

—and if some of the branches were broken off. But do not boast against the branches; and if you boast, remember that you do not bear the root, but the root bears you. [Note: [Col. 0719] *“Do not boast against those branches; but if you boast, it is not you who bear the root, but the root that bears you.”*] [Note: [Col. 0720] *astans*] Codex A and Cast. add *anstans*.—*bairiþ*] thus Codex A; Cast. adds *bairaiþ*; otherwise Greek universally.]

You will say, then: “Branches were broken off so that I might be grafted in.” [Note: [Col. 0719] “Quite so: they were broken off because of unbelief, but you stand through faith. Do not think highly of yourself, but fear!”] [Note: [Col. 0720] *astos*] since all the letters have completely disappeared in Codex A, Cast. supplied this word by conjecture.]

For if God did not spare the natural branches, neither will he spare you. [Note: [Col. 0719] *gastost*] thus Codex A; Cast. adds *gastos*.]

See, then, God’s kindness and severity: severity toward those who fell, but kindness toward you, if you remain in kindness; otherwise you too will be cut off. [Note: [Col. 0719] *þandei*] = εἰ γάρ, used here for εἰ δέ above at verse 16; Gal. IV, 7 and perhaps J. VIII, 46.—*þuk*] correctly so in Codex A; Cast. adds *þus.] [Note: [Col. 0720] *garaihta*] “just,” Greek universally.—*aþþan*] the second recension has this, as do Codex A and Cast.; but this seems false, since it disturbs the sense. Here it is not used with the meaning found in L. VI, 24 and XIX, 17, where it means πλήν (“nevertheless”), simply introducing what follows. What is now required is the particle corresponding to Greek ἐπεί (“otherwise, if not”), namely *aiþþau*; see Cor. I, XV, 29, cf. VII, 14.]

But fear. For if God did not spare the natural branches, perhaps he will not spare you either. See, then, the goodness and severity of God: severity toward those who fell, but kindness toward you, if you remain in his kindness; otherwise you too will be cut off. [Note: [Col. 0719] “And they too, unless they remain in unbelief, will be grafted in, for God is able to graft them in again.”] [Note: [Col. 0720] *jainai*] Gothic for δέ.]

For if you were cut from the naturally wild olive tree and, contrary to nature, were grafted into a cultivated olive tree, how much more will these, according to nature, be grafted into their own olive tree? [Note: [Col. 0720] *us vistai—alevabagmis*] “from nature—olive tree,” Greek universally ἐκ τῆς κατὰ φύσιν—ἀγριελαίου. The unusual form *ïntrusgans*, a passive participle for *ïntrusgiþs*, is noteworthy; likewise, two forms of the verb *gaggan* occur, *gaggiþs* in M. III, 11 and *gaggans* in Mc. VII, 30. For *vilþeis*, Grimm, *Gramm.* IV, 326, proposes reading *vilþeins*, an otherwise unattested form.—*godana*] thus, we hope, Codex A, since Cast. could no longer distinguish it; he himself supplied *gudana*.]

And they will be grafted in. For God is able to graft them in again. For if you were cut from the natural wild olive tree and, being of another stock, were grafted into the good olive tree, how much more will these be grafted into their own olive tree according to nature?

For I do not want you, brothers, to be ignorant of this mystery, lest you become wise in your own estimation: blindness has come upon part of Israel until the fullness of the gentiles enters. [Note: [Col. 0721] *ïzvis*] the word translating Greek ἀγνοεῖν has been omitted through scribal error; Cast. correctly recognized *unveisans* from Cor. II, I, 8 and Thess. I, IV, 13.—*sumata*] = ἀπὸ μέρους; elsewhere this is usually rendered *bi sumata*, see Cor. II, I, 14; II, 5.]

And thus all Israel will be saved, as it is written: “The deliverer will arise from Zion; he will turn ungodliness away from Jacob.” [Note: [Col. 0721] *du afvandjan*] “to turn away,” Greek καὶ ἀποστρέψει.—*afgudein*] “ungodliness,” Greek universally ἀσεβείας, in the plural.]

“And this will be my covenant with them, when I take away their sins.” [Note: [Col. 0721] “And so all Israel is saved, as it is written: The one who delivers arises from Zion, to turn ungodliness away from Jacob.”]

According to the gospel, they are enemies for your sake; but according to election, they are beloved for the sake of the fathers. [Note: [Col. 0721] “And this covenant comes from me to them: when I take away their sins.”]

For the gifts and calling of God are irrevocable. [Note: [Col. 0721] *sind*] “are,” Greek universally.]

For just as you once did not believe God, but now have received mercy because of their unbelief, so they too have now disbelieved because of the mercy shown to you, so that they too may receive mercy. [Note: [Col. 0721] *raihtis*] Gothic manuscripts agree with καί.]

For God has confined all to unbelief so that he may have mercy on all. [Note: [Col. 0721] “So they too have now not believed because of your mercy, so that they too may receive mercy.”]

O the depth of the riches, wisdom, and knowledge of God! How inexpressible are his judgments and untraceable his ways!! [Note: [Col. 0721] At the beginning, Gothic has *o*, corresponding to ὦ; cf. the note on L. VI, 20.—*gabeins*] Gothic manuscripts agree with καί.—*handugeins*] after this word, where Codex Ambrosianus ends, the first fragment of Codex Carolinus begins and continues to XII, 5.—*unusspilloda*] Lh. in *Ulfilae illustr.* p. 105 conjectured *unusspillodos*. Since it is common for the adjective’s gender not to agree with its noun (see the note on Neh. VI, 16), this conjecture seems unnecessary. Another point deserves the attentive reader’s notice: since the verb *usspillon* corresponds to Greek κηρύσσειν or διηγεῖσθαι, and since *unusspilloþs* correctly translates ἀνεκδιήγητος in Cor. II, IX, 15, whereas here all Greek manuscripts have ἀνεξερεύνητος, the Gothic translator seems not to have properly understood the Greek word and to have confused it with a form derived from the root εἴρειν. Griesbach therefore notes that Gothic may have read ἄρρητα.—*sind*] “are,” Greek universally.]

All things are in unbelief, so that he may have mercy on all. O the depth of the riches, wisdom, and knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments and inscrutable his ways! Who has known the mind of the Lord, or who has been his counselor? [Note: [Col. 0721] *ïmma*] “of him,” Greek αὐτοῦ; all manuscripts after *ragineis*.]

Or who has first given to him, so that he might be repaid? [Note: [Col. 0721] *ïmma*] Greek universally after *gaf*.—*fruma gaf*] thus Codex Carolinus; the editions add *frumozo fragaf*. Clearly *fruma* is correct: an *f* can be read, and with close attention even the letters *ga* can be recognized.]

For from him and through him and in him are all things.. To him be glory forever. Amen. [Note: [Col. 0721] *unte*] thus Codex Carolinus; Kn. and Ih. add *uste*.]

Or who has been his counsellor? Or who first gave to him, and it will be repaid to him?? For from him, through him, and in him are all things; to him be glory forever. Amen.

I appeal to you now, brothers, through the mercy of God, to present your bodies as a living sacrifice, holy and pleasing to God, your rational worship. [Note: [Col. 0721] *blotinassu*] Ih. p. 102 adds *bloti-nassu*.]

And in him are all things; to him be glory forever. Amen. I appeal to you, brothers, through God’s mercies: present your bodies as a living, holy sacrifice, well pleasing to God—your rational worship. Do not conform yourselves to this age, but be transformed by the renewal of your mind, so that you may discern what the will of God is—what is good, pleasing, and perfect.. [Note: [Col. 0722] At the beginning, Gothic manuscripts have *ak*, corresponding to καί.—*ak ïnmaidjaiþ ananiujiþai*] In Codex Carolinus, because the upper part of the membrane is mutilated, one verse is missing containing the words by which Gothic rendered Greek ἀλλὰ μεταμορφοῦσθε. Nothing remains except *þ* at the beginning of the next verse; the editors, disregarding this, joined the *þ* to what follows and wrote “+ . . . þana niujiþai.” Lh. alone, p. 107, suspects that *þ* should be separated from *ana*. We hope that the form supplied here correctly fills the codex’s lacuna. Through *ïnmaidjan*, Ulfilas also renders μεταμορφοῦν in Mc. IX, 2; and for the Greek middle or passive he very often uses the Gothic active without *sik* (see many passages below, XII, 9, *haftjan*). The omission of this pronoun was especially easy here because *ïzvis* immediately precedes. Those who are dissatisfied with our reasoning may read, with Z. p. 127, *ïnmaididai vairþaiþ*. Moreover, *niujiþa* is καινότης or καίνωσις; but ἀνακαίνωσις should be rendered by *ananiujiþa*, cf. Cor. II, IV, 16; Col. III, 10; Eph. IV, 23, where *ananiujan* translates ἀνακαινοῦν and ἀνανεοῦν.—*fraþjis*] Codex Carolinus and the editions add *framaþjis*; Ih. p. 111 already found the correct reading.—*gakiusan*] Gothic manuscripts and Codex 18 in Mi. have *o ὑμᾶς*.—*sijai*] “may be,” Greek universally.—*þatei*] “which,” namely *ïst* (“is”); Gothic uses this to render Greek τό. This ellipsis of the substantive verb is often repeated in such Gothic renderings of the Greek article; see Eph. IV, 6, *ains atta allaize saei ïn allaim uns* (“one Father of all, who is in us all”), II, 17, and L. XVII, 31. We note this lest anyone, with Griesbach, suppose that Gothic, like the versions, adds *þatei* (“which?”).—*galeikaiþ*] see the note on Tim. I, VI, 6.]

Do not think more highly of yourselves than you ought to think, but think so as to think soberly, each according to the measure of faith God has allotted. [Note: [Col. 0721] “For I say, through the grace of God given to me, to everyone among you: not to think more highly than one ought to think, but to think toward sound judgment; to each as God has apportioned the measure of faith.”] [Note: [Col. 0722] *guþs*] “of God,” Greek.—*vaila fraþjan*] Lh., Z., and Cast. add *jet*.]

For just as in one body we have many members, but all the members do not have the same function, so we, many as we are, are one body in Christ; but each one [lacuna]. [Note: [Col. 0721] “For just as in one body we have many members, but all these members do not have the same function.”] [Note: [Col. 0722] *þaiþ-þan*] Kn. and Cast. add *jet*; Ih., rashly rejecting the codex reading, conjectures *þaih þan*; see the note on M. V, 37.—*tauï haband*] according to all Greek manuscripts.]

One who distributes, let him do so in simplicity; one who presides, with diligence; one who shows mercy, with cheerfulness.. [Note: [Col. 0723] “Here he gives in simplicity; here he presides with diligence; here he shows mercy with cheerfulness.”]

Let love be sincere. Hate what is evil; cling to what is good. [Note: [Col. 0723] *ubila*] “evil,” Greek universally τὸ πονηρόν.]

In brotherly love, be devoted to one another; in honor, anticipate one another. [Note: [Col. 0723] “Brotherly love toward you, showing affection to one another, anticipating one another in honor.”]

Do not be lazy in diligence; be fervent in spirit; serve the Lord; rejoice in hope; endure affliction; persist in prayer. [Note: [Col. 0723] *fraujin*] “the Lord,” Greek καιρῷ.]

Share in the needs of the saints; pursue hospitality. [Note: [Col. 0723] *andaviznim*] Cast. adds *andaviznam*; the passage is obliterated in Codex A.]

Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse. [Note: [Col. 0723] “Bless those who persecute you; bless and do not curse.”]

Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep. [Note: [Col. 0723] *faginondam*] Gothic manuscripts agree with καί.]

Have the same mind toward one another; do not set your mind on high things, but associate with the lowly; do not become wise in your own estimation. [Note: [Col. 0723] “Having the same attitude toward one another, not aspiring to high things, but associating with the humble; do not become wise in your own estimation.”] [Note: [Col. 0723] *hauhiþa*] “high things,” Greek universally τὰ ὑψηλά. Grimm, *Gramm.* IV, 695, proposes *hauhiþai* because a dative commonly follows *fraþjan*; but it also takes an accusative, see Phil. IV, 2.]

Repay no one evil for evil; take thought for what is good, not only in the sight of God but also in the sight of all people. [Note: [Col. 0723] *ni þatainei—ak jah*] “not only—but also,” Greek.—*ïn*] according to the first recension; here begins the second fragment of Codex Carolinus; see the note on verse 8.—*manne allaize*] according to all Greek manuscripts.]

If possible, insofar as it depends on you, live at peace with all people. [Note: [Col. 0723] *magi vairþan*] “it can happen,” Greek universally δυνατός.]

Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but give place to wrath; for it is written: “Vengeance is mine; I will repay,” says the Lord. [Note: [Col. 0723] *gavrikandans*] thus the manuscripts; Kn. adds *gavrisandans*, the correct reading found by Ih.; Z. and Cast. had already given it from Codex A.—*þravirhein*] thus the manuscripts, Z., and Cast.; Kn. reads *þvair…*, and Ih. adds *tvair…*. Kn. incorrectly supplied *þvairheinai*, since substantives are not formed from adjectives in *-eins*, but in *-ei*. Had Ih. and Z. known this, they would scarcely have noted that both *þvairhein* and *þvairheinai* are correct. Kn. was then misled by the stroke over the *i*, which marks the ending *-n* and which he took for a sign of the note *gþs* [Col. 0724], and added *guþs*. Ih. accepted this for reasons unknown to us, and Z. retained it.—*fraveit letaidau*] thus Codex A and Cast.; Codex Carolinus has *fraveit leitaidau*. On this difference among the codices, see the note on M. IX, 6. Kn., Ih., and Z. add *fraveito ei gildau*, relying on whose authority Griesbach notes that Gothic read ἵνα ἀποδίδω. We now note that *letaidau* (“let it be left”) is omitted by all Greek manuscripts.]

If your enemy is hungry, give him food; if he is thirsty, give him drink. For by doing this you will heap burning coals on his head. [Note: [Col. 0723] “If your enemy is hungry, give him food; but if he is thirsty, refresh him with drink; for by doing this you heap fiery coals upon his head.”] [Note: [Col. 0724] *jabai*] Gothic manuscripts agree with οὖν.—*mat*] thus Codex A and Cast.; Codex Carolinus, Kn., Ih., and Z. add *mad*.]

For it is written: “Vengeance is mine; I will repay,” says the Lord. If your enemy is hungry, give him food; but if he is thirsty, give him drink. For by doing this you will heap burning coals of fire upon his head. Do not be conquered by evil, but conquer evil with good. [Note: [Col. 0724] *gajiukaizau*] Cast. adds *gajiukizau*.—*fram*] the second recension has this; Greek universally ἐν.] [Note: [Col. 0723] “Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.”].”]

Let every soul be subject to the governing authorities, for there is no authority except from God; and those that exist have been established by God. Therefore the one who resists the authority resists God’s ordinance; and those who resist will bring condemnation upon themselves. [Note: [Col. 0723] “Let every soul be subject to the higher authorities, for there is no authority except from God; and those that exist have been established by God.”] [Note: [Col. 0724] *andstoþ*] “resisted”; Gothic, not understanding the perfect meaning of Greek ἀνθέστηκεν, incorrectly renders it by the preterite, where it should have written *andstandiþ*. The same thing happened to Ulfilas in Mc. III, 26, where he renders ἀνέστη by *usstoþ*.]

For rulers are not a terror to good work but to evil. Do you wish not to fear the authority? Do what is good, and you will receive praise from it. [Note: [Col. 0723] “For rulers are not a terror to good works, but to evil; and do you wish not to fear the authority? Do what is good, and you will have praise from it.”] [Note: [Col. 0724] *godamma—ubilamma*] “good—to evil,” Greek τῶν ἀγαθῶν ἔργων ἀλλὰ τῶν κακῶν.]

For it is God’s servant for your good. But if you do evil, fear; for it does not bear the sword in vain. It is God’s servant, an avenger for wrath against the one who does evil. [Note: [Col. 0723] “For he is God’s servant to you for good; but if you do evil, fear, for he does not bear the sword in vain, since he is God’s servant, avenging in wrath the one who does evil.”] [Note: [Col. 0724] *hairu*] Codex A and Cast. have *hairau*; on this variation see the note on Mc. VII, 32.]

Therefore you must submit, not only because of wrath but also because of conscience. [Note: [Col. 0723] “Therefore submit not only because of wrath, but also because of conscience.”] [Note: [Col. 0724] *ufhausjaiþ*] “submit,” Greek ἀνάγκη ὑποτάσσεσθαι. Here the second fragment of Codex Carolinus ends; see the note on XII, 8.]

For this reason you also pay taxes, for they are God’s ministers, serving precisely for this purpose. Therefore pay everyone what is owed: tax to whom tax is owed; revenue to whom revenue; fear to whom fear; honor to whom honor. [Note: [Col. 0723] “For this reason you also pay tribute, for they are God’s ministers, serving this very purpose.”] [Note: [Col. 0724] *þammei*] “to whom,” namely “you owe,” Greek universally τῷ.]

Owe no one anything except to love one another; for the one who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law. [Col. 0725] [Note: [Col. 0725] “Do not owe anyone anything, except that you love one another, for the one who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law.”] [Note: [Col. 0723] This material is found in Codex A, and from *ïn andvairþja guþs* XII, 17 through XIII, 5 also in Codex Carolinus, *duþþe ufhausjaiþ*.] [Note: [Col. 0725] *frijoþ*] the first recension has this; thus Codex A; Cast. adds *frijaiþ*.—*usfullida*] thus Codex A; Cast. adds *usfullide*.]

For this: “You shall not commit adultery; you shall not murder; you shall not steal; you shall not covet”; and if there is any other commandment, it is summed up in this word: “You shall love your neighbor as yourself.” [Note: [Col. 0725] “Do not commit adultery; do not kill; do not steal; do not covet; and if any other commandment is summed up in this word, you shall love your neighbor as yourself.”] [Note: [Col. 0723] This material is found in Codex A and, from *ïn andvairþja guþs* XII, 17 through XIII, 5, also in Codex Carolinus, *duþþe ufhausjaiþ*.] [Note: [Col. 0725] *anþaraizo*] thus Codex A, as we suspect; Cast. could not distinguish the final syllables and printed *anþaraize*.—*þauma*] the second recension has this; Greek universally ἐν τῷ.]

Love does no evil to one’s neighbor; therefore love is the fulfillment of the law. [Note: [Col. 0725] *newundjins*] “of the neighbor,” Greek universally τῷ πλησίον, dependent on ἐργάζεται, whereas Gothic has referred it to *friaþva*.—*ïst*] “is,” Greek universally.]

And do this because you know the time: it is already the hour for us to rise from sleep, for salvation is nearer to us now than when we believed. [Note: [Col. 0725] “And knowing this time, that it is the hour for us already to rise from sleep, for our salvation is nearer now than when we believed.”] [Note: [Col. 0725] *ïst*] both recensions have this, “is,” Greek universally.—*naseins unsara*] according to all Greek manuscripts, “our salvation.”]

The night has advanced, and the day has drawn near. Let us therefore cast off the works of darkness and put on the weapons of light. [Note: [Col. 0725] “The night has passed, but the day has drawn near; let us now cast off the works of darkness and put on the weapons of light.”]

Let us walk properly as in the day, not in reveling and drunkenness, not in sexual intercourse and debauchery, not in strife and jealousy. [Note: [Col. 0725] *dragkaneim*] see the note on Gal. V, 21.]

But put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and do not make provision for the flesh in its desires. [Note: [Col. 0725] *unsaramma*] “our,” Greek; Gothic manuscripts c and d and 8 in Mi.—*xristau ïesua*] according to all Greek manuscripts.]

And do not engage in reveling and drunkenness, in sexual intercourse and debauchery, in quarrels and jealousy. But put on our Lord Jesus Christ.

Receive the one who is weak in faith, not for disputes over opinions. [Note: [Col. 0725] “Receive the one who is weak in faith, not for disputes over thoughts.”]

One person believes that he may eat everything; but the one who is weak eats vegetables. [Note: [Col. 0725] “One person believes that he may eat everything; but the one who is weak eats vegetables.”] [Note: [Col. 0725] *frakunni*] Codex A and Cast. add *frakuni*.—*matjandan*] Codex A and Cast. add *matjandin*.]

The one who eats must not despise the one who does not eat; and the one who does not eat must not judge the one who eats, for God has accepted him. [Note: [Col. 0725] “Let the one who eats not despise the one who does not eat; and let the one who does not eat not judge the one who eats, for God has accepted him.”]

Who are you to judge another’s servant? He stands or falls before his own master. And he will stand, for the Lord is able to make him stand. [Note: [Col. 0725] *frauja*] “Lord,” Greek θεός.—*gastoþanan*] Cast. conjectured *gastoþan*, which seems plausible; nevertheless compare Thess. I, 2, 17, *gaainanaidai*.]

One person indeed judges one day above another—[lacuna]—and rules over the living and the dead. [Note: [Col. 0725] “One person judges one day above another—”] [Note: [Col. 0725] “He both rules the living and the dead.”] [Note: [Col. 0725] *13 leguntur in cod. Carol.*] “13” is read in Codex Carolinus.. [Note: [Col. 0725] *qivaim—dauþaim*] according to the Greek.]

But you: why do you judge your brother? Or you also: why do you despise your brother? For we will all stand before the judgment seat of Christ. [Note: [Col. 0725] “But you, why do you judge your brother? Or you, why do you despise your brother? For we all stand before the tribunal of Christ.”]

For it is written: “As I live,” says the Lord, “every knee will bow to me, and every tongue will confess to God.” [Note: [Col. 0726] *biugiþ*] Greek universally has this before *all*.—*andhaitiþ*] Greek after *razdo*.]

Therefore each of us will give an account of himself to God. [Note: [Col. 0725] “Therefore each of us will render an account of himself to God.”] [Note: [Col. 0726] *usgibiþ*] “gives back,” Greek δώσει; Ulfilas’ manuscripts have ἀποδώσει.]

So then, let us no longer judge one another; rather, judge this: not to place a stumbling block or an occasion for falling before a brother. [Note: [Col. 0725] “Therefore let us no longer judge one another, but judge this instead: not to place a stumbling block or an occasion for falling before a brother.”] [Note: [Col. 0726] *ni*] the first recension; Kn. adds *ui*.]

I know and am persuaded in the Lord Jesus that nothing is unclean in itself, except that to the one who considers something unclean, to that person it is unclean. [Note: [Col. 0725] *jag-gatraua*] thus Codex Carolinus; Kn. adds *jai tatraua*, while Lh., Z., and Cast. omit *jai gatraua*. This gave rise to Griesbach’s error, when he noted that Gothic had read ναί instead of καί.—*wa unhrain visan*] we supplied this from the lower portions of letters that were almost entirely cut away (see the note on XII, 2). Kn. and Z. and Cast. mark a lacuna; Lh. neglected to mark it.—*ïst*] “is,” Greek universally.]

But if, because of food, your brother is grieved, you are no longer walking according to love. Do not destroy by your food the one for whom Christ died. [Note: [Col. 0725] “But if your brother is grieved because of food, you are no longer walking according to love; therefore do not destroy by your food the one for whom Christ died.”] [Note: [Col. 0725] 13 …]
are read in Codex Carolinus.]

[Note: [Col. 0726] *nunu*] therefore, as in all Greek manuscripts; likewise in verse 20.]

What is unclean is unclean to that person. But if your brother is grieved because of food, you are no longer walking according to love. Therefore, do not destroy with your food the one for whom Christ died.

[Note: [Col. 0725] Let not our good be blasphemed.]

[Note: [Col. 0726] *vajamerjaidau*] “Let it be blasphemed,” according to the Gothic manuscripts; some Greek manuscripts read οὖν (“therefore”).]

Go, then. Do not destroy, on account of your food, that for which Christ died. Let not what is good for us be blasphemed.

For the kingdom of God is not food and drink, but righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

[Note: [Col. 0725] For whoever serves Christ in these things is pleasing to God and approved by human beings.]

[Note: [Col. 0726] *þiudangardi*] Thus Codex Carolinus; the editions add *þiudangard* (“kingdom”).]

[Note: [Col. 0726] *ïst*] “Is,” as in all Greek manuscripts; likewise above, instead of *vaila galeikaiþ*, all Greek manuscripts have εὐάρεστος (“pleasing”).]

For whoever serves Christ in these things is pleasing to God and approved by human beings.

Let us therefore pursue the things that make for peace and the things that build one another up.

[Note: [Col. 0725] Therefore, do not destroy the work of God on account of food.]

[Note: [Col. 0726] *sind*] The second edition; Lehmann adds *find*.]

[Note: [Col. 0727] *nunu*] See the note on verse 15.]

So then, let us pursue the things that make for peace and the things that build us up among one another. Do not, then, on account of food—

[Col. 0727]

[lacuna] The reproaches of those who reproach you fell upon me.

[Note: [Col. 0727] *þize*] Kn. adds *vize*.]

For whatever was written beforehand was written for our instruction, so that through the endurance and encouragement of the Scriptures we might have hope.

[Note: [Col. 0727] *gameliþ varþ*] “Was written,” as all Greek manuscripts have προεγράφη (“was written beforehand”); see the note on 1 Timothy VI, 6.]

[Note: [Col. 0727] *auk*] Ih. adds *ank*.]

[Note: [Col. 0727] *jah*] Gothic manuscripts; some Greek manuscripts have διά (“through”).]

But may the God of endurance and encouragement grant you to think the same thing among yourselves according to Christ Jesus, so that with one accord and one mouth you may glorify God and the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.

Therefore, accept one another, just as Christ also accepted you, for the glory of God.

[Note: [Col. 0727] *svasve*] Ih. adds *sva ve*.]

For I say that Christ Jesus became a servant of the circumcision for the truth of God, to confirm the promises made to the fathers, and that the nations might glorify God for his mercy, as it is written:

[Note: [Col. 0727] *auk*] “For,” whereas the Greek has δέ (“but” or “and”).]

[Note: [Col. 0727] *xristu ïesu*] In accordance with the Greek.]

[Note: [Col. 0727] *bimaitis*] “Of the circumcision”; we have supplied this from our own manuscripts; see the note on XII, 2. It should also be noted that the Gothic translator, unlike elsewhere, here places the participle *vaurþanana* (“having become”) after *qiþan* (“to say”); we think he did so because it would not have been permissible to add *visan* (“to be”). He likewise omits the infinitive of the substantive verb in the formula *viljau ïzvis unvitans* or *unveisans* (“I wish you not to be ignorant”), 1 Corinthians X, 1; 2 Corinthians I, 8; 1 Thessalonians IV, 13. In the following verse he correctly continues, “but the nations glorify God.”]

I will confirm the promise made to the fathers. But the nations, because of mercy, glorify God, as it is written:

“Therefore I will confess you among the nations, Lord, and sing to your name.”

And again it says:

“Rejoice, nations, with his people.”

And again it says:

“Praise the Lord, all nations, and let all peoples praise him.”

[Note: [Col. 0727] *qiþiþ*] “He says,” whereas the Greek has the corresponding form.]

[Note: [Col. 0727] *fraujan*] The Greek has the accusative before *allos*.]

[Note: [Col. 0727] *hazjaina*] “Let them praise,” corresponding to the Greek ἐπαινέσατε.]

It says: “Praise the Lord, all nations, and let all peoples praise him.”

And again Isaiah says:

“There shall be a root of Jesse, and he who rises shall rule the nations; in him the nations shall hope.”

[Note: [Col. 0727] *ïaissaizis*] Lehmann adds *jaisaizis*.]

[Note: [Col. 0728] *reikinoþ*] “He rules,” because all Greek manuscripts have ἄρχειν (“to rule”). Ih. p. 132 thinks that *reikinon* should be read instead of *reikinoþ*. He is correct, but the Gothic translation does not distort the meaning; therefore we have not ventured to emend the reading of the codex.]

Isaiah again says:

“There shall be a root of Jesse, and he who rises shall rule the nations; in him the nations shall hope.”

[Note: [Col. 0727] “But may the God of hope fill you with all joy—”]

[Note: [Col. 0727] “And Lucius and Jason and Sosipater, my kinsmen.”]

[Note: [Col. 0728] What is printed from this point to the end has been drawn from Codex A.]

The nations hope in him. But may the God of hope fill you with all joy [lacuna] and Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen.

[Note: [Col. 0727] “I, Tertius, writing this epistle in the Lord, greet you.”]

I, Tertius, who write this epistle, greet you in the Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0727] Gaius, my host and that of the whole church, greets you; Erastus, the city steward, greets you, and Quartus, the brother.]

Gaius, my host and that of the whole church, greets you. Erastus greets you—

[Note: [Col. 0728] *gaius*] Thus Cast., without any trace of the dots formerly placed above the *i*; H. says that it is written this way in Codex A, both here and at 1 Corinthians I, 14. But the Gothic form is less correct; this name is never disyllabic in such a way that *ai* forms a diphthong.]

[Note: [Col. 0728] *allaizos aikklesjons*] In accordance with the Greek.]

[Note: [Col. 0727] The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.]

[Note: [Col. 0728] “ahmin izvaramma”: “with your spirit”; all Greek manuscripts read “of all of you.” Subscription: ““du rumonim ustauh” (“the Epistle to the Romans ends”)”), according to the Gothic text only in manuscript G. “du rumonim meliþ—kaurinþon” (“written to the Romans—from Corinth”): the Greek manuscripts read variously or omit these words; the Gothic agrees with manuscripts B and D.]

“fauragaggja baurgs jah qartus sa broþar”: “the city’s steward and Quartus, the brother.” “The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.”

The letter to the Romans ends here. The letter to the Romans was written from Corinth.

[Note: [Col. 0728] “ahmin izvaramma”: “with your spirit”; all Greek manuscripts read “of all of you.” Subscription: “du rumonim ustauh” (“postscript to the Romans”), according to the Gothic text only in manuscript G. “du rumonim meliþ—kaurinþon” (“written to the Romans—from Corinth”): the Greek manuscripts read variously or omit these words; the Gothic agrees with manuscripts B and D.]

**To the Corinthians I**

[Col. 0727]

[Col. 0727] [Note: [Col. 0727] “I am Paul’s,” but “I am Apollos’s,” but “I am Cephas’s,” but “I am Christ’s.”] [Note: [Col. 0727] *pavlaus*: thus manuscript A; Cast. reads *pavlus* (see on L. I, 54).] [Note: [Col. 0727] “Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you, or were you baptized in Paul’s name?”] [Note: [Col. 0728] *ïst*: Gothic; Greek has ὁ Χριστός, “the Christ.”]—“I am Paul’s,” or “I am Apollos’s,” or “I am Cephas’s,” or “I am Christ’s.” Has Christ been divided? Was Paul crucified for you, or were you baptized in Paul’s name?

[Note: [Col. 0727] “I thank God [Col. 0729] that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius.”] [Note: [Col. 0728] *gaiu*: see on Rom. XVI, 23.] I thank God that I baptized none of you except Crispus and Gaius, [Note: [Col. 0729] “so that no one may say that you were baptized in my name.”] [Note: [Col. 0729] “For I baptized also the household of Stephanas; beyond that I do not know whether I baptized anyone else.”] [Note: [Col. 0729] *ïk*: “I”; Greek throughout.] [Note: [Col. 0729] *gadaukans*: Cast., comparing this word of doubtful origin and sense with *dauhts* (“meal”), translates it “table-companions”; Mssm. prefers *gadaurans*, “those who use the same door.” Greek throughout has οἶκον, “household.”] [Note: [Col. 0729] *þata*: “this”; Greek has τό. Gothic, with the manuscripts, reads τό here, as at II, XIII, 11; compare Eph. VI, 10 and Phil. III, 1.] [Note: [Col. 0729] *ainnohun*: Gothic, with the manuscripts, has ἄλλον, “another.”]—Gaius, so that no one might say that you had been baptized in my name. For I baptized also the household of Stephanas; beyond that I do not know whether I baptized anyone else.

[Col. 0729] [Note: [Col. 0729] “For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to preach; not in wisdom of speech, lest the cross of Christ should be made void.”] For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to proclaim the good news; not in wisdom of speech, lest the cross of Christ should be made void.

[Note: [Col. 0729] “For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to those who are being saved it is God’s power.”] [Note: [Col. 0729] *ganisandam*: Gothic; the manuscripts have ἡμῖν, “to us.”] For the word of the cross is foolishness to those who are perishing, but to those who are being saved it is the power of God. [Note: [Col. 0729] “For it is written: ‘I shall destroy the wisdom of the wise, and reject the understanding of the prudent.’”] For it is written: “I shall destroy the wisdom of the wise, and reject the understanding of the understanding ones.”

[Note: [Col. 0729] “Where is the wise man? Where the scribe? Where the disputant of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of this world?”] Where is the wise man? Where is the scribe? Where is the investigator of this age? Has not God made foolish the wisdom of this world?

[Note: [Col. 0729] “For since, in God’s wisdom, the world did not know God through wisdom, God was pleased through the foolishness of the proclamation to save those who believe.”] [Note: [Col. 0729] *ni*: manuscript A and Cast. add *niu ni*, “is it not?”] For since, in God’s wisdom, the world did not know God through wisdom, God was pleased through the foolishness of preaching to save those who believe.

[Note: [Col. 0729] “For Jews ask for signs, but Greeks seek wisdom.”] [Note: [Col. 0729] *unte*: Gothic omits καί, “also.”] For Jews ask for signs, while Greeks seek wisdom.

[Note: [Col. 0729] “But we proclaim Jesus crucified: to Jews an offence.”] [Note: [Col. 0729] *ïesu*: “Jesus”; Greek throughout has Χριστόν, “Christ.”] [Note: [Col. 0729] *ïudaium*: Gothic omits Greek μέν, “indeed/on the one hand.”] [Note: [Col. 0729] “But to the nations foolishness; but to those who are called, Jews and nations alike, Christ—God’s power and God’s wisdom.”] [Note: [Col. 0729] *ïudaie*: Greek has τε, “both”; see on L. II, 16.] But we proclaim Jesus crucified: to Jews an offence, and to the nations foolishness; but to those who are called, Jews and Gentiles alike, Christ is God’s power and God’s wisdom.

[Note: [Col. 0729] “For the foolishness of God is wiser than human beings—”] [Note: [Col. 0729] *handugozei*: this is the necessary reading; Cast. adds *handugo*. In manuscript A a space sufficient for the syllable *zei* remains, but no trace of letters.] For the foolishness of God is wiser than human beings—[lacuna]

[Note: [Col. 0729] “—that he may be found faithful.”] [Note: [Col. 0729] *was triggvs*: corresponding to Greek throughout; Cast. nevertheless adds *tkiggvs*.]—that he may be found faithful.

[Note: [Col. 0729] “But for me it is a very small thing that I should be examined by you or by a human day; indeed, I do not even examine myself.”] [Note: [Col. 0729] *ussokjaidau*: thus manuscript A; Cast. adds *ussokjaida*.] But for me it is a very small thing that I should be examined by you or by a human day; indeed, I do not even examine myself.

[Note: [Col. 0729] “For I am conscious of nothing against myself, yet I am not thereby justified; but he who examines me is the Lord.”] For I am conscious of nothing against myself; yet I am not thereby justified, but he who examines me is the Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0729] “Therefore do not judge before the time, until the Lord comes, who both brings to light the hidden things of darkness and reveals the counsels of hearts; then praise comes to each from God.”] [Note: [Col. 0729] *ei*: “that”; an idle particle, since μή here is not a conjunction, “that not,” but an adverb, “not,” corresponding to *ni*.] [Note: [Col. 0729] *ni*: Gothic, with the manuscripts, omits τί, “anything.”] [Note: [Col. 0729] *vairþiþ*: thus manuscript A; Cast. reads *vairþaiþ*.] [Note: [Col. 0729] *warrjammeh*: thus manuscript A; [Col. 0730] Cast. reads *wakjizummah*.] Therefore do not judge before the time, until the Lord comes, who will bring to light what is hidden in darkness and reveal the counsels of the heart; and then praise will come to each from God.

[Note: [Col. 0729] “But, brothers, I have transferred these things to myself and Apollos for your sakes, so that in us you may learn not to think beyond what is written, lest one for one be puffed up against another.”] [Note: [Col. 0730] *aþþan*: Gothic omits ταῦτα, “these things,” or perhaps *þo* has dropped out through a scribe’s negligence, as the plural *þairhgaleikonda* seems to show. This plural, having nothing to which it can refer, is highly objectionable. Perhaps *þo þan* should be read for *aþþan*, or *þairhgaleikoda* for *þairhgaleikonda*, as the Greek text, μετεσχημάτισα (“I transferred/applied”), seems to demand; yet even if this is accepted, *þo* ought not to be absent. Cast., after again examining the manuscript, says in Addenda, p. 66, that *þairgaleikonda* is indeed written in the codex, but that the *n* is less distinct than the other letters, so that the scribe himself seems to have erased it.] [Note: [Col. 0730] *ganimaiþ*: Ulfilas, with the manuscripts, has τό, “that which.”] [Note: [Col. 0730] *ufar*: Cast. adds *ufak*.] [Note: [Col. 0730] *ufblesans sijai*: “may be puffed up”; Greek throughout has φυσιοῦσθε.] [Note: [Col. 0730] *ana anþarana*: Greek throughout places these words after *sijai*.] But, brothers, I have applied these matters to myself and Apollos for your sakes, that in us you may learn not to think beyond what is written, lest one be puffed up for one person against another.

[Note: [Col. 0729] “For who distinguishes you? And what do you have which you did not receive? And if you received it, why do you boast as though you had not received it?”] [Note: [Col. 0730] *jabai*: Gothic, with codex d in Mill, has καί, “and.”] For who distinguishes you? And what do you have that you did not receive? And if you did receive it, why do you boast as though you had not received it?

[Note: [Col. 0729] “Already you are satisfied, already you have become rich; without us you have reigned; and would that you did reign, so that we too might reign with you.”] [Note: [Col. 0730] *vainei*: Gothic, with the manuscripts, has γε, “indeed.”] Already you are satisfied; already you have become rich; without us you have reigned—and would indeed that you had reigned, so that we also might reign with you.

[Note: [Col. 0729] “For I think that God displayed us apostles last, as men condemned to death; for we became a spectacle to the world, to angels, and to human beings.”] [Note: [Col. 0730] *apaustauluns*: thus manuscript A; Cast. reads *apaustaulans*.] For I think that God displayed us apostles last, as men sentenced to death; for we became a spectacle to the world, to angels, and to human beings.

[Note: [Col. 0729] “We are fools for Christ, but you are wise; we are weak, but you are strong; you are honoured, but we dishonoured.”] [Note: [Col. 0730] *frodai*: Gothic omits ἐν Χριστῷ, “in Christ,” unless Cast.’s reading is preferable; he could not recognize even the syllable *ai*, and the *ïn xristau*—that is, *ïn xau*—at the end of the line also escaped him.] [Note: [Col. 0730] *þan*: “indeed”; Greek throughout has μέν.] We are fools in Christ, but you are wise; we indeed are weak, but you strong; you indeed are honoured, but we dishonoured.

[Col. 0731] [Note: [Col. 0731] “Until this present hour both hungry and thirsty and naked and beaten and unsettled.”] [Note: [Col. 0731] *hugridai*: for *huggrïdai* (J. VI, 35); compare nevertheless the note on Mc. X, 37.] [Note: [Col. 0731] “and—”] Until the present hour we are hungry and thirsty and naked and beaten and without a settled dwelling; and—[lacuna]

[Note: [Col. 0731] “—I have now judged, as though present, him who has so done this thing.”] [Note: [Col. 0731] “in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when you and my spirit are assembled together with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ.”] [Note: [Col. 0731] *samaþ gagaggandam*: Cast. adds *jct.*; likewise at VII, 5 and XIV, 26. See on Mc. IX, 25; compare Cor. II, VII, 3.]—I have judged, as though present, the one who has done this thing, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when you and my spirit are assembled together with the power of our Lord Jesus Christ,

[Note: [Col. 0731] “to hand such a one over to the devil for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord Jesus.”] to hand such a one over to the devil for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord Jesus.

[Note: [Col. 0731] “Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump?”] Your boasting is not good. Do you not know that a little leaven leavens the whole lump?

[Note: [Col. 0731] “Purge out the old leaven, that you may be a new lump, as you are unleavened; for our Passover, Christ, has been sacrificed for us.”] [Note: [Col. 0731] *ushraineiþ*: thus manuscript A; Cast. reads *ushrainaiþ*.] [Note: [Col. 0731] *unbeistjodai*: one might expect *unbeistidai* (see v. 6); yet we do not judge our form corrupt, since *auhjon* too ends in *-jon*.] [Note: [Col. 0731] *ufsniþans ïst*: Greek throughout places this before *xristus*.] Purge out the old leaven, that you may be a new lump, as you are unleavened; for our Passover, Christ, has been sacrificed for us.

[Note: [Col. 0731] “Therefore let us celebrate the feast, not with old leaven, nor with leaven of wickedness and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.”] Therefore let us celebrate the feast, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of wickedness and evil, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.

[Note: [Col. 0731] “I wrote to you in the letter not to associate with fornicators.”] [Note: [Col. 0731] *blandaiþ*: “associate”; Greek throughout has συναναμίγνυσθαι.] I wrote to you in the letter: do not associate with fornicators—

[Note: [Col. 0731] “not with the fornicators of this world, or with the greedy and rapacious, or idolaters; for then you would have to leave this world.”] [Note: [Col. 0731] At the beginning Gothic, with the manuscripts, has καί, “also.”] [Note: [Col. 0731] *ni*: Gothic omits πάντως, “altogether.”] [Note: [Col. 0731] *jah*: “and”; Greek has ἤ, “or.”] [Note: [Col. 0731] *þan*: here, answering Greek ἄρα, it has been used for *þannu*; the same is to be restored below at XV, 14 for *þau*, falsely read in manuscript A.]—not with the fornicators of this world, or with the greedy and rapacious, or idolaters; for then you would have to leave the world.

[Note: [Col. 0731] “But now, behold, I wrote to you not to associate, if anyone called a brother is a fornicator, or greedy, or an idolater, or a reviler, or a drunkard, or rapacious; with such a person do not even eat together.”] [Note: [Col. 0731] *faihufriks*: the scribe, having omitted this word, added it above the line; hence *aiþþau*, “or,” is also absent once (Cast.). Compare J. XII, 42. We have placed *aiþþau* in the text because the sense requires it.] But now, behold, I have written to you not to associate with anyone called a brother if he is a fornicator, greedy, an idolater, a reviler, a drunkard, or a rapacious person; with such a one do not even eat together.

[Note: [Col. 0731] “For what have I to do with judging those outside? Do you not judge those within? But God judges those outside. Remove the evil man from among yourselves.”] [Note: [Col. 0731] *wa*: Gothic has γάρ, “for.”] [Note: [Col. 0731] *mik*: correctly so in manuscript A, for *kara* or *kar-ist*, “care,” must be supplied (M. XXVII, 4), with which the accusative is customarily joined; see J. X, 13; M. VIII, 29; Mc. I, 24 and elsewhere. In “what is there to us and to thee?” the construction is different.] For what concern is it of mine to judge those outside? Do you not judge those within? But God judges those outside. Remove the wicked man from among yourselves.

[Note: [Col. 0731] “Does any of you, having a lawsuit against another, dare to go to judgment before the unjust and not before—”] [Note: [Col. 0732] *staua habands*: Greek places this before *viþra*.] Does any of you, having a lawsuit against another, dare to go to judgment before the unjust and not before—[lacuna]

[Note: [Col. 0731] “—one another, except perhaps by agreement for a certain time, that you may be free to fast and pray, and then come together again, lest Satan tempt you because of your incontinence.”] [Note: [Col. 0732] *niba*: Gothic has τί; perhaps it read μήτι.] [Note: [Col. 0732] *fastan jah*: “to fast and”; Greek omits it.] [Note: [Col. 0732] *bidan*: see on Rom. IX, 3.] [Note: [Col. 0732] *samaþ gavandjaiþ*: see on V, 4; Cast. adds *samlþ*. For ἦτε, Gothic certainly read συνέρχεσθε.]—one another, except perhaps by agreement for a short time, that you may have leisure to fast and pray; then come together again, lest Satan tempt you because of your lack of self-control.

[Note: [Col. 0731] “But this I say by concession, not as a command.”] [Note: [Col. 0731] “Yet I wish all people to be as I myself am; but each has his own gift from God, one thus and another thus.”] [Note: [Col. 0732] *ïþ*: “but”; Greek γάρ, “for,” likewise at XI, 31.] [Note: [Col. 0732] *sve*: Gothic omits καί, “also.”] [Note: [Col. 0732] *giba habaiþ*: corresponding to the Greek.] This I say by concession, not as a command. Yet I wish all people to be as I myself am; but each has his own gift from God, one in this way and another in that.

[Note: [Col. 0731] “But I say to the unmarried and to widows: it is good for them if they remain as I.”] [Note: [Col. 0732] *ïst ïm*: corresponding to Greek throughout.] [Note: [Col. 0732] *ïk*: Gothic, with codex k in Mill, reads ἐγώ, “I,” for κἀγώ, “I also.”] But I say to the unmarried and to widows: it is good for them if they remain as I am.

[Note: [Col. 0731] “But if they cannot contain themselves, let them marry; for it is better to marry than to burn.”] [Note: [Col. 0732] *liugandau*: thus manuscript A. It is a middle form, such as Gothic uses here for γαμησάτωσαν, as *atsteigadau* at Mc. XV, 32 and M. XXVII, 42 for καταβάτω, although Greek uses active forms; see further on J. XIII, 35.] [Note: [Col. 0732] *ïst auk*: corresponding to Greek throughout.] But if they cannot contain themselves, let them marry; for it is better to marry than to burn.

[Note: [Col. 0731] “But to those joined in marriage I command—not I, but the Lord—that a wife not separate from her husband.”] [Note: [Col. 0732] *liugom haftam*: Cast. adds *jct.*] But to those joined in marriage I command—not I, but the Lord—that a wife not separate from her husband.

[Note: [Col. 0731] “But if she does separate, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled again to her husband; and let a husband not dismiss his wife.”] [Note: [Col. 0732] *jabai*: Gothic omits καί, “and.”] [Note: [Col. 0732] *visan—gagavairþjan*: “remain—be reconciled,” corresponding to μενέτω—καταλλαγήτω; compare M. V, 24. Moreover *aftra*, “again,” is omitted in Greek throughout.] [Note: [Col. 0732] *aban*: one would expect *abin* (see v. 10), for it depends on *anabiuda*, “I command.”] But if she does separate, let her remain unmarried or be reconciled again to her husband; and let a husband not dismiss his wife.

[Note: [Col. 0731] “But to the others I say, not the Lord: if any brother has an unbelieving wife and she is willing [Col. 0733] to live with him, let him not dismiss the wife.”] [Note: [Col. 0732] *þo qen*: “that wife”; Greek throughout has αὐτήν, “her.”] But to the others I say, not the Lord: if any brother has an unbelieving wife and she is willing to live with him, let him not dismiss the wife.

[Col. 0733] [Note: [Col. 0733] “And a wife who has an unbelieving husband, if he is willing to live with her, let her not dismiss that husband.”] [Note: [Col. 0733] *þana aban*: “that husband”; Greek has αὐτόν, “him.”] And a wife who has an unbelieving husband, if he is willing to live with her, let her not dismiss that husband.

[Note: [Col. 0733] “The unbelieving wife has been sanctified in the husband, and the unbelieving husband has been sanctified in the wife; otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.”] [Note: [Col. 0733] The clause in which the wife is said to be sanctified is placed by all Greek manuscripts after the other clause, in which the husband is said to be sanctified. Moreover, at the beginning Gothic omits γάρ, “for.”] [Note: [Col. 0733] *aiþþau*: Gothic seems to omit ἄρα, for *aiþþau* answers only to ἐπεί; see XV, 29 and on Rom. XI, 22.] For the unbelieving wife has been sanctified in the husband, and the unbelieving husband has been sanctified in the wife; otherwise your children would be unclean, but now they are holy.

[Note: [Col. 0733] “But if the unbelieving person separates, let him separate; a brother or sister is not enslaved in such cases; but God called us in peace.”] But if the unbelieving person separates, let him separate. A brother or sister is not enslaved in such cases; rather, God called us in peace.

[Note: [Col. 0733] “For what do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or what do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?”] [Note: [Col. 0733] *nuk-kannt*: do not, with Mssm., *Skeir.* p. 59, take this as an instance of consonant doubling, a form nowhere otherwise found; rather it is assimilation for *nuh kannt*, where *nuh* is interrogative. See Mc. XII, 9, *wa nuh*, and J. XVIII, 37, *an nuh*. The same must be concluded concerning *dul-leitilai*, Cor. II, VII, 8, written for *duh leitilai*; *uh* is enclitic and corresponds to Greek καί. Compare the note on J. XVIII, 26. For the other examples cited by Mssm., see our remarks on M. V, 37.] [Note: [Col. 0733] *þu qinon*: thus manuscript A; Cast. has *qenon*, omitting *þu*. Observe the unusual vocative for *qino*. On *þu*, which is often added to vocatives, see L. VI, 20.] [Note: [Col. 0733] *ganajsais*: manuscript A and Cast. first read *ganasjas*.] [Note: [Col. 0733] *kannt*: thus manuscript A and Cast., for the usual *kant*; we fear that the doubled *n* is due to scribal error.] [Note: [Col. 0733] *þeina*: “your”; Greek omits it throughout. Gothic frequently uses the possessive pronoun for the Greek article; see II, 12, 7; M. VIII, 20; Mc. I, 41; L. XXVIII, 13; J. XIV, 31; Gal. V, 24.] For what do you know, wife, whether you will save your husband? Or what do you know, husband, whether you will save your wife?

[Note: [Col. 0733] “Not as God apportioned to each, as the Lord called each, so let him walk. And thus I command in all the churches.”] [Note: [Col. 0733] *ni ei*: there is no doubt that Gothic did not understand the elliptical force of εἰ μή, “unless”; for what it wrote, “not as,” has no sense.] [Col. 0734] [Note: [Col. 0734] *warjammeh*: thus manuscript A; Cast. has *warjizummeh*.] [Note: [Col. 0734] *guþ*: “God”; Greek has κύριος, “Lord.”] [Note: [Col. 0734] *ainwarjizoh*: so Cast. printed it, but we do not doubt that he wrongly read it for *ainwarjanoh*. On a renewed inspection, Cast. says that *ainwarjatoh* seems to be written; if this is correct, Gothic had ἕκαστον as a neuter.] [Note: [Col. 0734] *allaim aikklesjom*: corresponding to Greek throughout except codex i in Mill.] Not as God apportioned to each, as God called each, so let him walk. Thus I command in all the churches.

[Note: [Col. 0733] “Was anyone called circumcised? Let him not undo circumcision. Was anyone called in foreskin? Let him not be circumcised.”] [Note: [Col. 0734] *bimaitai*: “let him circumcise,” for “let him be circumcised”; compare XV, 29.] Was anyone called circumcised? Let him not undo circumcision. Was anyone called uncircumcised? Let him not be circumcised.

[Note: [Col. 0733] “Circumcision is nothing, and foreskin is nothing, but the keeping of God’s commandments.”] [Note: [Col. 0734] *ni vaihts*: manuscript A and Cast. first have *ni vaihi ni vaihts*. Of these, *ni vaihts* seems to have entered the text from a gloss correcting the corrupt reading *ni vaiht*; see on Mc. VII, 15.] Circumcision is nothing, and uncircumcision is nothing, but keeping God’s commandments.

[Note: [Col. 0733] “Let each remain in the calling in which he was called.”] Let each remain in the calling in which he was called.

[Note: [Col. 0733] “Were you called as a slave? Do not be concerned; but even if you can become free, make use of it rather.”] Were you called as a slave? Do not be concerned; but even if you can become free, make use of it rather.

[Note: [Col. 0733] “For the slave called in the Lord is the Lord’s freedman; likewise the free man who is called is Christ’s slave.”] [Note: [Col. 0734] *samaleiko*: Gothic, with codex o, has καί, “also.”] For the slave called in the Lord is the Lord’s freedman; likewise the free person called is Christ’s slave.

[Note: [Col. 0733] “You were bought with a great price; do not become slaves of human beings.”] [Note: [Col. 0734] *galaubamma*: “great”; Greek omits it throughout; Gothic agrees with the Vulgate. See on J. XII, 3.] You were bought with a great price; do not become slaves of human beings.

[Note: [Col. 0733] “Let each one, brothers, remain with God in that in which he was called.”] Let each one, brothers, remain with God in that in which he was called.

[Note: [Col. 0733] “But concerning virgins I have no command of the Lord; I give counsel, as one who has received mercy from the Lord to be faithful.”] But concerning virgins I have no command of the Lord; I give counsel, as one who has received mercy from the Lord to be faithful.

[Note: [Col. 0733] “I think therefore that this is good because of the present necessity: that it is good for a man to be thus.”] [Note: [Col. 0734] *ïst*: “is”; Greek omits it throughout.] [Note: [Col. 0734] *mann*: Gothic omits τό, “the.”] I think therefore that this is good because of the present necessity: that it is good for a man to be thus.

[Note: [Col. 0733] “Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek release. Have you been released from a wife? Do not seek a wife.”] Are you bound to a wife? Do not seek release. Have you been released from a wife? Do not seek a wife.

[Note: [Col. 0733] “But if you take a wife, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned; but such persons have affliction of the flesh. Yet I spare you—”] [Note: [Col. 0734] *jabai*: Gothic omits καί, “and.”] [Note: [Col. 0734] *nimis qen*: Gothic, with the manuscripts, reads λαβῇς γυναῖκα, “take a wife,” for γήμῃς, “marry.”] [Note: [Col. 0734] *fravaurhta*: Cast. reads *fravahrhta*.] But if you take a wife, you have not sinned; and if a virgin marries, she has not sinned; but such persons will have affliction of the flesh. Yet I spare you—[lacuna]

[Note: [Col. 0733] “—let it be for the weak; for if someone sees you, who possess knowledge, reclining in an idol-temple, will not the conscience of one who is weak be built up to eat things sacrificed to idols?”] [Note: [Col. 0734] *galiuge stade*: Cast. adds *jct.*]—let it be for the weak; for if someone sees you, who have knowledge, reclining in an idol-temple, will not the conscience of the weak person be built up to eat food sacrificed to idols?

[Note: [Col. 0733] “For through your knowledge the weak person perishes, the brother for whom Christ died.”] [Note: [Col. 0734] *auk*: “for”; Greek has καί, “and.”] [Note: [Col. 0734] *broþar*: Greek places this before *ana*.] [Note: [Col. 0734] *þize*: see on L. X, 5.] For through your knowledge the weak person perishes, the brother for whom Christ died.

[Note: [Col. 0733] “But by sinning against the brothers, [Col. 0735] and striking their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.”] [Note: [Col. 0734] *aþþan*: Gothic omits οὕτω, “thus.”] [Note: [Col. 0734] *broþruns*: Gothic, with codex G, omits καί, “also.”] But by sinning against the brothers and striking their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.

[Col. 0735] [Note: [Col. 0735] “Therefore, if food makes my brother stumble, I shall never eat flesh, lest I make my brother stumble.”] [Note: [Col. 0735] *broþar*: Gothic, with the manuscripts, has μοῦ, “my,” before it.] [Note: [Col. 0735] *gamarzjau*: Greek throughout places this after *meinana*.] Therefore, if food makes my brother stumble, I shall never eat flesh, lest I make my brother stumble.

[Note: [Col. 0735] “Am I not an apostle? Am I not free? Have I not seen Jesus Christ our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?”] [Note: [Col. 0735] *niu*: thus manuscript A; Cast. adds *nih*.] [Note: [Col. 0735] *apaustaulus—freis*: corresponding to Greek.] [Note: [Col. 0735] *fraujan*: Gothic has ἡμῶν, “our.”] [Note: [Col. 0735] *vaurstv*: manuscript A and Cast. read *vausstv*.] Am I not an apostle? Am I not free? Have I not seen Jesus Christ, our Lord? Are you not my work in the Lord?

[Note: [Col. 0735] “If I am not an apostle to others, yet to you I am; for you are the seal of my apostleship.”] [Note: [Col. 0735] *aiþþau*: see on II, IV, 16.] [Note: [Col. 0735] *sijuþ*: Gothic, with the manuscripts, has ἐν κυρίῳ, “in the Lord.”] If I am not an apostle to others, yet to you I am; for you are the seal of my apostleship.

[Note: [Col. 0735] “My defence to those who examine me is this.”] [Note: [Col. 0735] *þat-ïst*: an instance of a construction peculiar to Germanic languages; another such instance is noted on Mc. VI, 3.] My defence to those who examine me is this:

[Note: [Col. 0735] “Do we not have authority to eat and drink?”] Do we not have authority to eat and drink?

[Note: [Col. 0735] “Do we not have authority to lead about a sister as a wife, as the other apostles and the brothers of the Lord and Cephas do?”] [Note: [Col. 0735] *svasve*: Gothic manuscripts have καί, “also.”] Do we not have authority to lead about a sister as a wife, as the other apostles, the brothers of the Lord, and Cephas do?

[Note: [Col. 0735] “Or do only I and Barnabas lack authority not to work?”] [Note: [Col. 0735] “Who ever serves as a soldier at his own expense? Who plants a vineyard and does not eat its fruit? Who tends a flock and does not eat milk from the flock?”] [Note: [Col. 0735] *satjiþ*: thus manuscript A; Cast. reads *sateiþ*.] [Note: [Col. 0735] *akran*: “fruit”; Greek has ἐκ τοῦ καρποῦ, “of the fruit.”] [Note: [Col. 0735] *matjai*: Gothic, with the manuscripts, has ἤ, “or,” before it.] [Note: [Col. 0735] *miluks*: those are mistaken who take *miluks* for a neuter accusative.
