[Col. 0811]

“Therefore, my beloved and longed-for brothers, my joy and crown, stand firm thus in the Lord.”

[Note: [Col. 0811] *nu*] “therefore,” omitted by all Greek witnesses. —*fraujin*] The Gothic omits Greek ἀγαπητοί (“beloved”).]

“I entreat Euodia and I entreat Syntyche to think the same thing in the Lord.”

[Note: [Col. 0811] *aiodian*] It should have been written *aivaudian* in order to render Greek Εὐοδίαν (“Euodia”); compare *aivxaristia*, *aivlaugia*, *paraskaive*, and others. Yet compare *agustus* for *avgustus*. Nor are there lacking words in which the Goth expresses even short *o*, where it usually answers Greek long ω, by *o*. Perhaps Greek Εὐωδίαν (“Euodia”) was written in his copy; we see that this has occurred elsewhere. —*jah*] Codex A has *jas*.]

“Yes, I also entreat you, chosen companion: help these women, who laboured with me in the gospel, together with Clement and my other fellow-workers, whose names are in the book of life.”

[Note: [Col. 0811] *bidja*] All Greek witnesses place it before *jah*. —*valiso … gajuko*] Absent from the Greek. —*miþarbaididedun mis*] All Greek witnesses place this after *aivaggeljon*. —*miþ*] The Gothic agrees with manuscripts omitting Greek καί (“and”). —*klemaintau*] Codex A has *klaimaintau*, without its customary way of rendering eta-vowels; see the note on Matthew VIII.28. Castiglione, however, has *klemaintaii* and *klaimaintaii*. —*sind*] “are,” omitted by all Greek witnesses.]

“Therefore now, rejoice always in the Lord; again I say, rejoice!”

[Note: [Col. 0811] *nunu nu*] “therefore now,” omitted by all Greek witnesses. Moreover, we suspect that one of these particles is superfluous through scribal carelessness.]

“Let your gentleness be known to all people; the Lord is near.”

[Note: [Col. 0812] *anavilje*] Thus the manuscripts for *anaviljei*; see the note on Luke X.5. —*siai*] Codex A, perhaps, has *sijai*. —*ïst*] “is,” omitted by all Greek witnesses.]

“Be anxious about nothing; but in every prayer and petition, with thanksgivings, let your requests be made known to God.”

[Note: [Col. 0812] *allai*] As though the Gothic read Greek πάσῃ (“every”); Greek ἐν παντί (“in everything”) should have been *ïn allamma*. —*aihtronai*] Castiglione has *aihtkonai*. —*aviliudam*] “thanksgivings,” Greek εὐχαριστίας (“thanksgiving”) in all witnesses, in the singular number.]

“And the peace of God, which surpasses all understanding, shall guard your hearts and bodies in Christ Jesus.”

[Note: [Col. 0812] *ufarïst*] Codex A ends here. —*hairtona*] The Gothic omits Greek ὑμῶν (“your”). —*leika*] “bodies,” Greek νοήματα (“thoughts,” “minds”).]

“Finally, brothers, whatever is true, whatever honourable, whatever just, whatever holy, whatever pleasing, whatever commendable—if there is any goodness, if there is any praise—think on these things.”

[Note: [Col. 0812] *veih*] “holy”; the Gothic, agreeing with Latin versions, appears to have read Greek ἅγια (“holy things”) rather than ἁγνά (“pure things”). —*godeino*] The Gothic agrees with versions omitting Greek καί (“and”).]

“What you also learned and received and heard and saw in me—do these things; and the God of peace shall be with you.”

[Note: [Col. 0812] *gavairþeis*] See the note on Luke I.23.]

“But I rejoiced greatly in the Lord, because at last you have revived your concern for me; indeed, you were concerned, but lacked opportunity.”

[Note: [Col. 0812] *du*] Belongs with *fraþjan* (“to think”); see the note on Romans XI.11.]

“Not that I say this from need; for I have learned, in whatever circumstances I am, to be content. I know also how to be humbled, and I know how to abound; in every circumstance and in all things I have been instructed, both to be filled and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer want.”

[Note: [Col. 0812] *ufarassau*] For *ufarassu*; see above and compare the note on Mark VII.32.]

“I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me. Yet you did well in sharing my affliction.”

[Note: [Col. 0812] *xristau*] “through Christ,” omitted by the Greek. —*gamainja briggandans*] Castiglione adds an uncertain correction.]

“But you yourselves know, Philippians, that at the beginning of the gospel, when I departed from Macedonia, no church shared with me in an account of giving and receiving, except you alone. For even in Thessalonica, once and twice, you sent assistance for my need.”

[Note: [Col. 0812] *ainnohun*] Thus codex B and Castiglione, incorrectly for *ainohun*; see the note on Galatians V.15. —*aikklesjono mis*] Absent from all Greek witnesses. —*tvaim*] The Gothic agrees with manuscripts reading Greek εἰς (“once,” literally “unto”).]

“Not that I seek the gift, but I seek fru—”

[Note: [Col. 0812] *ak …*] A fragment of the word *akran* (“fruit”), as Castiglione rightly restores.]

## TO THE COLOSSIANS

[Col. 0813]

[Note: [Col. 0813] in truth;] [Note: [Col. 0813] *ïn sunjai*] Codex B begins here.] [Note: [Col. 0813] as you received from Epaphras, our beloved fellow-servant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ Jesus;] [Note: [Col. 0813] *svasve*] Gothic with the manuscripts reads καί.---*ïesuis*] The Greek omits it; Gothic follows the Vulgate.]—in truth. As you received from Epaphras, our beloved fellow-servant, who is a faithful minister of Christ Jesus for you. [Note: [Col. 0813] who also made known to us your love in the Spirit;] [Note: [Col. 0813] therefore we also, from the day on which we heard, have not ceased praying and asking for you, that you may be filled with the knowledge of his will in all wisdom and spiritual understanding;] [Note: [Col. 0813] *þamma daga ei*] Thus for *þammei daga* (“from the day”), ἧς ἡμέρας, as he speaks at 1 Cor. 11:23 and Gal. 5:1; see, however, on Luke 1:20.] He also made known to us your love in the Spirit. [Note: [Col. 0813] who delivered you from the power of darkness and transferred you into the kingdom of the Son of his love;] [Note: [Col. 0813] *ïzvis*] “you”; the Greek has ἡμᾶς (“us”).] He delivered you from the power of darkness and transferred you into the kingdom of the Son of his love, [Note: [Col. 0813] in whom we have redemption, the forgiveness of sins;] [Note: [Col. 0813] *fravaurhte*] Codex B and Castiglione add *fravaurte*; cf. on Matt. 5:15. [Note: [Col. 0813] who is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn of all creation.] [Note: [Col. 0813] *ungasaiwanis*] Thus, instead of the more usual *ungasaiwanins*; see 2 Cor. 4:4. Castiglione.] [Note: [Col. 0813] For in him all things were created in heaven and upon earth, the visible and the invisible, whether thrones, or dominions, or kingdoms, or powers: all things were created through him and in him.] [Note: [Col. 0813] *himina*] “heaven,” Codex A with all Greek manuscripts except the present passage. [Note: [Col. 0813] And he is before all things, and all things have been constituted in him;] And he is before all things, and all things hold together in him. [Note: [Col. 0813] and he is the head of the body, the church; he is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, that in all things he might hold the pre-eminence.] And he is the head of the body, the church. He is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that in all things he may have the first place. [Note: [Col. 0813] For in him it pleased all fullness to dwell;] [Note: [Col. 0813] and through him to reconcile all things in him, making peace through the blood of his cross through him, whether things upon earth or things in heaven.] [Note: [Col. 0814] *ïmma*] “him”; Gothic, with the Latin versions, seems to have read αὐτόν (“him”) instead of ἑαυτόν (“himself”), as also in v. 22.---*ana*] The second “upon”: Gothic with the manuscripts reads ἐπί.] For it pleased that all fullness should dwell in him, and through him to reconcile all things in him, making peace through the blood of his cross through him, whether things on earth or things in heaven.

[Note: [Col. 0813] And you, who once were alienated and enemies in mind through evil works,] [Note: [Col. 0814] *nu*] See on Rom. 7:6.---*gafriþodai*] “reconciled”; the Greek has ἀποκατήλλαξεν (“he reconciled”).] And you, once alienated and hostile in mind through evil works, [Note: [Col. 0813] yet now reconciled in the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy, blameless, and irreproachable before him;] [Note: [Col. 0814] *mammons*] “flesh.” Castiglione appears to have found this written in Codex B; Codex A is so worn away here that he did not venture to confirm the other reading from it. Since at 1 Cor. 8:13 κρέας (“meat”), a word of related sense, is translated by *mimz*, we hope that a more exact inspection of the manuscripts, here or in the Corinthian passage, will recover a reading displaying words more similar in form.---*ïs*] See on v. 20.] but now reconciled in the body of his flesh through death, to present you holy, without blemish, and unreproveable before him, [Note: [Col. 0813] if indeed you continue in the faith, grounded and settled, and not moved away from the hope of the gospel which you heard, which has been preached in all creation under heaven, of which I, Paul, became a minister.] [Note: [Col. 0814] *ïn*] The first “in”; omitted by the Greek.---*gaþvastidai—gatulgidai*] Separated in Codex A.] if indeed you continue in the faith, grounded and steadfast, and are not moved away from the hope of the gospel which you heard, which has been preached in all creation under heaven, of which I, Paul, became a minister.

[Note: [Col. 0815] Whom we proclaim, admonishing every person and teaching every person in all wisdom, that we may present every person perfect in Christ Jesus;] [Note: [Col. 0815] *ïesu*] “Jesus”; omitted by the Greek.] Him we proclaim, admonishing every person and teaching every person in all wisdom, so that we may present every person complete in Christ Jesus, [Note: [Col. 0815] for which I labor, striving according to the working which works inwardly in me with power.] [Note: [Col. 0815] *þammei*] Gothic has καί (“and”).---*bi*] Codex B ends.---*vaurstv*] Gothic has αὐτοῦ (“his”).---*ïnnana usvaurkeiþ*] We have printed this on certain conjecture. Further, *ïnnuna*, which the surviving traces suggest and which Castiglione printed at Rom. 7:22, 2 Cor. 4:16, and Eph. 3:16, has not been put in the text because, as Grimm, *W. J.* LXX, p. 31, discovered by an inspired conjecture from the Ephesian passage, the manuscripts read not this but *ïnnuma* (“inner”). Therefore *ïnnuna* cannot be an adverbial form, but must be *ïnnana* or *ïnna*, omitted by Grimm, who approved *sa ïnnuna* at 2 Cor. 4:16 and believed it so spoken in the same fashion as the following *sa utana* (“the outward [one]”).---*mahtai*] Codex A ends.] for this I labor, striving according to the working which works inwardly in me with power. [Note: [Col. 0815] sins of the flesh in the circumcision of Christ.] [Note: [Col. 0815] *fravaurhte*] “sins”; omitted by the Greek. Codex B continues.] sins of the flesh in the circumcision of Christ. Unless transferred here from another place, this addition amplifies the notion; examples of this figure have been collected in the note on 1 Cor. 9:25. In all wisdom and spiritual understanding, teach and admonish one another with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord. [Note: [Col. 0817] Whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.] [Note: [Col. 0818] At the beginning and again after *guþa*, Gothic has καί (“and”) with the manuscripts.] Whatever you do, in word or deed, do everything in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through him.

[Note: [Col. 0817] Wives, submit yourselves to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord;] [Note: [Col. 0818] *jus*] “you”; see on Luke 6:20.---*ïzvaraim*] “your”; omitted by the Greek; cf. on 1 Cor. 7:16.] Wives, submit yourselves to your husbands, as is fitting in the Lord. [Note: [Col. 0817] Husbands, love [Col. 0819] your wives and do not be harsh toward them;] [Note: [Col. 0818] *ïzvaros*] “your”; omitted by the Greek.] Husbands, love your wives and do not be harsh toward them. [Note: [Col. 0819] Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is well pleasing in the Lord;] [Note: [Col. 0819] *ïst*] The Greek places it before *vaila* (“well”).] Children, obey your parents in everything, for this is pleasing in the Lord. [Note: [Col. 0819] Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, lest they become discouraged;] [Note: [Col. 0819] *du þvairhein*] Castiglione errs in saying that *du þvairhein* is superfluous because *gramjan* properly means ἐρεθίζειν (“to provoke”). For the addition of *du þvairhein* (“to anger”) to *gramjan* (“to provoke”) demonstrates that the Gothic translator read not ἐρεθίζετε but, with certain manuscripts, παροργίζετε (“provoke to anger”).] Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger, lest they become discouraged. [Note: [Col. 0819] Slaves, obey in everything your masters according to the flesh, not serving merely before their eyes as people-pleasers, but in singleness of heart, fearing God.] [Note: [Col. 0819] *leika fraujam*] Castiglione adds *jct.*, for *leika* corresponds to Greek κατὰ σάρκα (“according to the flesh”), which ought indeed to have been rendered with added *bi* (“according to”); we also greatly miss the article *þaim*: *þaim bi leika fraujam*.---*guþ*] “God”; the Greek has κύριον (“the Lord”).] Slaves, obey in everything your masters according to the flesh, not serving merely before their eyes as people-pleasers, but in singleness of heart, fearing God. [Note: [Col. 0819] Whatever you do, work from the soul, as for the Lord and not for people,] [Note: [Col. 0819] At the beginning Gothic has καὶ πᾶν (“and everything”) with the manuscripts.---*fraujin*] Gothic omits καί.] Whatever you do, work heartily, as for the Lord and not for people, [Note: [Col. 0819] knowing that from the Lord you will receive the recompense of the inheritance; for you serve the Lord Christ.] [Note: [Col. 0819] For the wrongdoer receives what he has done wrong, and there is no partiality with God.] [Note: [Col. 0819] *auk*] “for”; the Greek has δέ (“but”).---*viljahalþei*] Codex B and Castiglione add *viljahalþein*; see Eph. 6:9.---*at guþa*] “with God”; omitted by the Greek.] knowing that from the Lord you will receive the recompense of the inheritance; for you serve the Lord Christ. For the wrongdoer will receive what he has wrongfully done, and there is no partiality with God. [Note: [Col. 0819] Masters, render justice and equity to slaves, knowing that you too have a master in heaven.] [Note: [Col. 0819] *aihuþ*] The Greek has this after *jus* (“you”).] Masters, render justice and equity to your slaves, knowing that you too have a master in heaven.

[Note: [Col. 0819] Continue steadfastly in prayer, keeping watch in it with thanksgiving;] [Note: [Col. 0819] *haftjandans*] “continuing steadfastly”; the Greek has προσκαρτερεῖτε, except Codex Colbertinus 7 cited by Mill.---*aviliudam*] “thanksgivings”; the Greek has εὐχαριστίᾳ (“thanksgiving”).] Continue steadfastly in prayer, keeping watch in it with thanksgivings, [Note: [Col. 0819] praying at the same time also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I also am bound,] praying also at the same time for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I am also bound, [Note: [Col. 0819] that I may make it manifest, as I ought to speak;] [Note: [Col. 0819] *svasve*] Codex A continues.] that I may make it manifest as I ought to speak. [Note: [Col. 0819] Walk in wisdom toward those outside, redeeming the time.] [Note: [Col. 0819] *þata*] Omitted by Codex A.] Walk in wisdom toward those outside, redeeming the time. [Note: [Col. 0819] Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how you ought to answer each person.] [Note: [Col. 0819] *ïzvar*] Castiglione adds *ïzvak*.---*gasuqoþ*] Thus the manuscripts, not *gasukoþ* in Codex A as Castiglione noted; in Codex Argenteus it occurs twice, Mark 9:50 and Luke 14:34, in the same sense as *gasupon*.---*siai*] Codex A has *sijai*, which all Greek witnesses omit.---*ei viteiþ*] “that you may know”; the Greek has εἰδέναι (“to know”); Gothic agrees with the Vulgate.] Let your speech always be gracious, seasoned with salt, so that you may know how you ought to answer each person.

[Note: [Col. 0819] Tychicus, the beloved brother, faithful minister, and fellow-servant in the Lord, will make known to you everything concerning me;] [Note: [Col. 0820] *tykekus*] Codex A has *tykeikus*.] Tychicus, the beloved brother, faithful minister, and fellow-servant in the Lord, will make known to you everything concerning me. [Note: [Col. 0819] I have sent him to you for this purpose, that he may know your circumstances and comfort your hearts,] I sent him to you for this purpose, that he may learn how things stand with you and comfort your hearts, [Note: [Col. 0819] together with Onesimus, the beloved and faithful brother, who is one of you. They will make known to you everything here.] [Note: [Col. 0820] *liubin—triggvin*] Omitted by the Greek.---*þaiei*] “who”; omitted by the Greek. Gothic agrees with Codex D, οἵ.] together with Onesimus, the beloved and faithful brother, who is one of you. They will make known to you everything here.

[Note: [Col. 0819] Aristarchus, my fellow-prisoner, greets you, and Mark, Barnabas’s cousin, concerning whom you received instructions: if he comes to you, receive him;] [Note: [Col. 0820] *areistarkus*] Codex A adds *ariastarkus*.---*du*] A new use of this preposition with the accusative should be noted, occurring besides here also at v. 13. In both places it means the same as *bi* (“for”); consequently these passages cannot be cited to confirm the view that at John 16:32 *seina* is an accusative dependent on *du*, for that meaning is irrelevant there.] Aristarchus, my fellow-prisoner, greets you, and Mark, Barnabas’s cousin, concerning whom you received instructions: if he comes to you, receive him. [Note: [Col. 0819] And Jesus, who is called Justus, greets you. These are of the circumcision. These alone are fellow-workers for the kingdom of God, and they have been a comfort to me.] [Note: [Col. 0820] *sind*] “are”; omitted by the Greek.---*þiudangardjos*] “for the kingdom”; the Greek has εἰς τὴν βασιλείαν (“for the kingdom”).] Jesus, who is called Justus, also greets you. These are of the circumcision. These alone are fellow-workers for the kingdom of God, and they have been a comfort to me.

[Note: [Col. 0819] Epaphras, a servant of Christ Jesus and one of you, greets you. He always strives for you in prayers, that you may stand fully assured and complete in every will of God;] [Note: [Col. 0820] *sa*] The second “he”; omitted by the Greek.---*allavaurstvans—fullavitans*] Omitted by the Greek; Gothic, with certain manuscripts, seems to have read πεπληροφορημένοι (“fully assured”) instead of πεπληρωμένοι (“filled”).] Epaphras, one of you, a servant of Christ, greets you. He continually strives for you in prayers, that you may stand fully active and fully assured in all the will of God. [Note: [Col. 0819] For I bear him witness that he has much zeal for you and for those in Laodicea and Hierapolis.] [Note: [Col. 0820] *manag aljan*] “much zeal”; the Greek has πολὺν πόνον (“much labor”).---*du*] “for”; omitted by the Greek; otherwise see on v. 10.---*sind*] Codex A ends.---*jah*] The second “and”; Gothic omits τῶν ἐν (“those in”).] For I bear him witness that he has much zeal for you and for those in Laodicea and Hierapolis. [Note: [Col. 0819] Luke, the beloved physician, greets you;] [Note: [Col. 0820] *liuba*] Gothic omits καὶ Δημᾶς (“and Demas”).] Luke, the beloved physician, greets you. [Note: [Col. 0819] Greet the brothers in Laodicea, and Nympha, and the church in her house.] Greet the brothers in Laodicea, and Nympha, and the church in his house.

[Note: [Col. 0821] And when this letter has been read among you, arrange that it also be read in the church of Laodicea, and that you read the one from Laodicea.] [Note: [Col. 0821] *laudekaion*] It should thus be written rather than the erroneous reading of Codex B, *laudekaiom*.---*þoei*] Unless this has been written by scribal error for *soei* (equivalent to *sei*), *þo ei* (“the [letter] which”) should be read; see on Luke 1:20.---*laudeikaion*] The second occurrence: Gothic agrees with the Vulgate, omitting ἵνα καί (“that also”).---*ussiggvaid. jah*] Codex B and Castiglione add *ussiggvaidjau*.] And when the letter has been read among you, arrange that it also be read in the church of Laodicea, and that you read the one from Laodicea. [Note: [Col. 0821] And say to Archippus: See to the ministry which you received in the Lord, that you may fulfill it.] And say to Archippus: See to the ministry which you received in the Lord, that you may fulfill it. [Note: [Col. 0821] The greeting in my own hand—Paul’s.] [Note: [Col. 0821] Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.

The Epistle to the Colossians ends.

] [Note: [Col. 0822] *bandjos*] “bonds”; the Greek has δεσμῶν.---*amen*] “Amen”; omitted by the Greek. Subscription: no Greek manuscript has it as Gothic does; moreover, in the codex *kaulaussaim* is written in abbreviated form as *kaussaim*.] The greeting in my own hand: Paul’s. Remember my bonds. Grace be with you. Amen.

The Epistle to the Colossians ends.

## TO THE THESSALONIANS. A.

[Note: [Col. 0821]

Fragments of this epistle occur in Codex B; Codex A contains only the portion from 5:22 to the end.

We have supplied the title from Phil. 4:16, where *þaissalauneika*, the name of the city Thessalonica, occurs.]

[Col. 0821]

[Note: [Col. 0821] —and God, how holily, justly, and blamelessly we behaved toward you who believe,] [Note: [Col. 0821] *waiva*] “how” (πῶς); Greek ὡς. — [Note: [Col. 0821] *veihaba*] “holily”: perhaps Gothic, with codex F, reads ἁγίως rather than ὁσίως, since *veihs* corresponds to Greek ἅγιος; see, however, Titus 1:8, where it likewise stands for ὅσιος.] —and God, how holily, justly, and blamelessly we were toward you believers. [Note: [Col. 0821] As you know, exhorting and comforting each one of you, as a father his own children,] [Note: [Col. 0821] *vituþ*] Gothic omits ὡς (πῶς).] [Note: [Col. 0821] and testifying that you should walk worthily of God, who called you into his own kingdom and glory.] As you know, each one of you, as a father his children, exhorting you, comforting you, and testifying, that you should walk worthily of God, who called you to his own kingdom and glory.

[Note: [Col. 0821] Therefore we too give thanks to God unceasingly, because, when you received from us the word of God’s report, you accepted it not as the word of human beings, but, as it truly is, as the word of God, which also works in you who believe.] [Note: [Col. 0821] *unsveibandans*] Thus codex B; Cast. *Add.* p. 71. — [Note: [Col. 0821] *at unst*] All Greek witnesses place this after *hauseinais*; Gothic agrees with the Vulgate. — [Note: [Col. 0821] *svasve*] First occurrence omitted by all Greek witnesses; Gothic agrees with the versions. — [Note: [Col. 0821] *vaurkeiþ*] Thus [Col. 0822] it should be written instead of *vaurkei*, the reading of codex B and Castillion.] Therefore we too unceasingly give thanks to God, because, having received from us the word of God’s hearing, you accepted it not as a human word but, as it truly is, as God’s word, which also works in you who believe.

[Note: [Col. 0821] For you, brothers, became imitators of the churches of God which are in Judaea in Christ Jesus; for you too suffered the same things from your own countrymen as they did from the Jews,] [Note: [Col. 0822] *veis*] “we”; all Greek witnesses: αὐτοί, “they themselves.”] For you, brothers, became imitators of the churches of God existing in Judaea in Christ Jesus; for you too suffered the same things from your own countrymen as we did from the Jews, [Note: [Col. 0821] who also killed the Lord Jesus and their own prophets, persecuted us, do not please God, and are hostile to all people,] [Note: [Col. 0822] *svesaim*] “their own”; Greek τούς.] who also killed the Lord Jesus and their own prophets, persecuted us, do not please God, and are hostile to all people, [Note: [Col. 0821] forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles so that they might be saved, always to fill up their sins. But God’s wrath has come upon them to the end.] [Note: [Col. 0822] *guþs*] “God,” omitted in Greek.] forbidding us to speak to the Gentiles in order that they might be saved, always to fill up their sins. But God’s wrath has come upon them to the end.

[Note: [Col. 0821] But we, brothers, having been bereaved of you for a brief time—of face, not of heart—were exceedingly eager to see your face with much longing.] [Note: [Col. 0822] *ïzvara*] Used solelycistically for *andaugi*, “face”; the usage of the Gothic language prevents its being treated as a genitive plural.] But we, brothers, having been bereaved of you for a short time, in presence and not in heart, were all the more eager to see your face with great longing. [Note: [Col. 0821] For we wished to come to you—I, Paul, both once and twice—but Satan hindered us.] [Note: [Col. 0822] *unte*] “for”; Greek διό, “therefore.”] For we wished to come to you—I, Paul, once and twice—but Satan hindered us.

[Note: [Col. 0821] For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of boasting? Is it not [Col. 0823] you before our Lord Jesus Christ at his coming?] [Note: [Col. 0822] *ïst*] “is,” omitted by all Greek witnesses. — [Note: [Col. 0822] *niu*] “is it not?” Greek ἢ οὐχὶ καί; Gothic agrees with the Vulgate.] For what is our hope, or joy, or crown of boasting? Is it not you before our Lord Jesus Christ [Col. 0823] at his coming? [Note: [Col. 0823] For you are our glory and joy.] For you are our glory and joy.

[Note: [Col. 0823] Therefore, when we could endure it no longer, we resolved to be left alone at Athens;] [Note: [Col. 0822] *ju—þanamais*] On this fullness of expression see Luke 15:19; indeed, *ju ni* was sufficient to render Greek μηκέτι, “no longer”; see v. 5.] Therefore, when we could no longer endure it, we resolved to remain alone at Athens, [Note: [Col. 0823] and sent Timothy, our brother and God’s minister in Christ’s gospel, to strengthen and exhort you concerning your faith,] [Note: [Col. 0823] *andbaht*] “minister”; Greek συνεργόν, “fellow worker.” — [Note: [Col. 0823] *ïz is gatulgjai*] Omitted by all Greek witnesses. — [Note: [Col. 0823] *bidjai*] Gothic, with certain manuscripts, omits ὑμᾶς, “you.”] and sent Timothy, our brother and God’s minister in the gospel of Christ, to strengthen you and exhort you concerning your faith, [Note: [Col. 0823] that no one may be shaken by these afflictions; for you yourselves know that we are appointed for this.] [Note: [Col. 0823] *ratidai*] Castillion correctly conjectured *satidai* beyond all doubt; see Philippians 1:17, where Gothic likewise uses *gasatiþs im* for Greek κεῖμαι.] that no one may be shaken in these afflictions. For you yourselves know that we are appointed to this.

[Note: [Col. 0823] For even when we were with you, we told you beforehand that we were to suffer afflictions, as it also happened, and you know.] [Note: [Col. 0823] *vesum*] All Greek witnesses place it after *ïzvis*.] For even when we were with you, we told you beforehand that we were to suffer afflictions, as indeed happened, and you know. [Note: [Col. 0823] Therefore I also, being no longer able to endure it, sent to learn of your faith, lest perhaps the tempter had tempted you and our labour should prove vain.] [Note: [Col. 0823] *usþulands*] Codex B and Castillion read *usþulans*; see Mark 12:24.] Therefore I too, no longer able to endure it, sent to learn of your faith, lest perhaps the tempter should have tempted you and our labour become vain.

[Note: [Col. 0823] But now, when Timothy has come to us from you and has brought us news of your faith and love, and that you always have a good remembrance of us, longing to see us as we also long to see you,] [Note: [Col. 0823] *teimauþaiu*] For *teimauþaiau*; see Luke 1:54. — [Note: [Col. 0823] *galaubein*] Gothic omits καί, “and.” — [Note: [Col. 0823] *habaiþ*] All Greek witnesses place it before *gaminþi*.] But now, when Timothy has come to us from you and brought us news of your faith and love, and that you always have a good remembrance of us, longing to see us as we also long to see you, [Note: [Col. 0823] because of this, brothers, we have been comforted by you in all our distress and affliction through your faith.] [Note: [Col. 0823] *fram*] “from”; all Greek witnesses: ἐφ’ (“because of”). — [Note: [Col. 0823] *nauþai—aglon*] Omitted by Greek witnesses.] because of this we have been comforted, brothers, by you amid all our distress and affliction through your faith. [Note: [Col. 0823] For now we live, if you stand firm in the Lord.] For now we live, if you stand firm in the Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0823] For what thanks can we repay to the Lord God concerning you, for all the joy with which we rejoice because of you before our God?] [Note: [Col. 0823] *usgildan*] Omitted by Greek witnesses except codex I in Mill, after *guþa*. — [Note: [Col. 0823] *fraujin guþa*] “the Lord God”; Greek witnesses have either θεῷ, “God,” or κυρίῳ, “Lord,” as Mill notes.] For what thanks can we repay to the Lord God concerning you, for all the joy with which we rejoice because of you before our God, [Note: [Col. 0823] night and day praying most earnestly that we may see your faces and supply what is lacking in your faith?] [Note: [Col. 0823] *andvairþja ïzvara*] “your faces”; all Greek witnesses: ὑμῶν τὸ πρόσωπον, “your face.” The Vulgate, with Gothic, places the pronoun after the noun. — [Note: [Col. 0823] *ustiuhaima*] Thus codex B; Castillion: *usþiuhaima*. — [Note: [Col. 0823] *vaninassu*] Thus codex B; Castillion: *vanona þis*.] night and day praying most earnestly that we may see your faces and supply the deficiency of your faith.

[Note: [Col. 0823] Now may our God and Father himself, and our Lord Jesus Christ, direct our way to you.] Now may God himself and our Father, and our Lord Jesus Christ, direct our way to you. [Note: [Col. 0823] And may the Lord cause you to increase and abound in love toward one another and toward all, as we also do toward you,] [Note: [Col. 0823] *jah*] According to Gothic, εἰς, “toward,” is omitted.] And may the Lord make you increase and abound in love toward one another and toward all, as we also do toward you, [Note: [Col. 0823] to establish your hearts blameless in holiness before God and our Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints.] [Note: [Col. 0823] *hairtona ïzvara*] Omitted by all Greek witnesses; Gothic agrees with the Vulgate.] to establish your hearts blameless in holiness before God and our Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ with all his saints.

[Note: [Col. 0823] Accordingly then, brothers, we ask and exhort you in the Lord Jesus that, as you received from us how you ought to walk and please God—as indeed you do walk [Col. 0824]—you may abound still more.] [Note: [Col. 0823] *þannu*] “accordingly”; Greek omits (τὸ) λοιπόν, “finally.” — [Note: [Col. 0823] *ei*] “that”; omitted in Greek. — [Note: [Col. 0823] *svasve jah gaggiþ*] “as indeed you walk” [Col. 0824], omitted in Greek; Gothic agrees with manuscripts which read καθὼς καὶ περιπατεῖτε. Thus there is no need, with Castillion, to suppose *svasve* stands for *sva*. — [Note: [Col. 0823] *jah*] The fourth “and”: ἵνα, “that,” which Greek has here; Gothic, with certain manuscripts, placed it above after *ïesua*.] Accordingly then, brothers, we ask and exhort you in the Lord Jesus that, as you received from us how you ought to walk and please God—as indeed you walk—you may abound still more. [Note: [Col. 0823] For you know what commandments we gave you through the Lord Jesus Christ.] [Note: [Col. 0824] *xristu*] “Christ,” omitted by all Greek witnesses except manuscripts a and d in Mill.] For you know what commands we gave you through the Lord Jesus Christ.

[Note: [Col. 0823] For this is the will of God: your sanctification, that you abstain from fornication,] [Note: [Col. 0824] *ei gahabaiþ*] “that you abstain”; all Greek witnesses have ἀπέχεσθαι, “to abstain.” Gothic, with the Vulgate, similarly rendered Greek εἰδέναι, “to know,” in the following verse by *ei viti*. — [Note: [Col. 0824] *kalkinassau*] Codex B reads *kalkinassaus*, but *af* requires the accusative. The passages mentioned at Matthew 27:57 differ; we have already observed the same scribal error in codex B above at 2 Corinthians 3:18 (*af ahmins*), where A correctly has *af ahmin*.] For this is God’s will: your sanctification, that you abstain from fornication, [Note: [Col. 0823] that each one of you may know how to possess his own vessel in holiness and honour,] [Note: [Col. 0824] *gastaldan*] All Greek witnesses place it after *kas*.] that each of you may know how to possess his own vessel in holiness and honour, [Note: [Col. 0823] not in the passion of lust, as also the Gentiles who do not know God,] not in the passion of lust, as also the Gentiles who do not know God, [Note: [Col. 0823] that no one may transgress [Col. 0825] or defraud—his brother; for the Lord is the avenger in all these matters, as we also told you beforehand and testified.] [Note: [Col. 0824] *nih*] “nor”; all Greek witnesses: καί, “and.” — [Note: [Col. 0824] *bifaih . . .*] Castillion printed *bifaihodai ïn . . o . . s*, from whose latter letters he inferred *toïs*, said for *tojis*. We doubt whether anyone will approve this conjecture—for he himself admits that, apart from *bifaih*, which we print, almost nothing can be known with certainty—and perhaps he has now withdrawn his own defence of it. We read *bifaiho (ïn) wamma toje*, i.e. “may he defraud [in] some matter,” on the supposition that, with the Armenian version, with which Gothic often agrees, it read τῳ for τῷ. — [Note: [Col. 0825] *ïst*] “is,” omitted by all Greek witnesses. — [Note: [Col. 0825] *allaize*] “of all”; all Greek witnesses: περὶ πάντων τούτων, “concerning all these things.”] that no one may transgress or defraud [lacuna] his own brother—for the Lord is the avenger in all these matters, as we told you beforehand and testified.

[Note: [Col. 0825] For God did not call us to impurity, but to sanctification.] For God did not call us to impurity, but to sanctification. [Note: [Col. 0825] Therefore, whoever rejects this rejects not a human being but God, who gave his Holy Spirit to you.] [Note: [Col. 0825] *ïnuh*] Thus codex B; Castillion adds *ïþ*. — [Note: [Col. 0825] *saei*] The second occurrence: Gothic, with certain manuscripts, omits καί, “also.” — [Note: [Col. 0825] *ïzvis*] “to you”; Greek εἰς ἡμᾶς, “to us.”] Therefore whoever rejects this rejects not a human being but God, who gave his Holy Spirit to you.

[Note: [Col. 0825] But concerning brotherly love we have no need to write to you, for you yourselves have been taught by God to love one another;] [Note: [Col. 0825] *broþrulubon*] Thus codex B; Romans 12:10 reads *broþralubon*. — [Note: [Col. 0825] *þaurbum*] “we have need”; Greek χρείαν ἔχετε, “you have need”; cf. 5:1.] But concerning brotherly love we have no need to write to you, for you yourselves have been taught by God to love one another; [Note: [Col. 0825] and indeed you do this toward all the brothers throughout all Macedonia. But we exhort you, brothers, to increase more and more,] and indeed you do this toward all the brothers throughout all Macedonia. But we exhort you, brothers, to increase more and more, [Note: [Col. 0825] and to aspire to quietness, to attend to your own affairs, and to work with your hands, as we commanded you,] [Note: [Col. 0825] *vaurkjan*] Gothic agrees with manuscripts reading ἰδίαις, “your own.” — [Note: [Col. 0825] *jah*] The fourth “also,” omitted by Greek witnesses except codex f and α in Mill.] and to aspire to quietness, attend to your own affairs, and work with your hands, as we commanded you, [Note: [Col. 0825] so that you may walk honourably toward those outside and lack nothing from anyone.] [Note: [Col. 0825] *gafehaba*] Thus codex B upon reinspection; we formerly conjectured *garedaba* (see Romans 13:13). — [Note: [Col. 0825] *ni ainishun wis*] “lack nothing from anyone”; all Greek witnesses: μηδενός, “of no one.” Gothic agrees with the Vulgate.] so that you may walk honourably toward outsiders and lack nothing from anyone.

[Note: [Col. 0825] But, brothers, we do not wish you to be uninformed concerning those who are asleep, so that you may not grieve as the others do, who have no hope.] [Note: [Col. 0825] *unveisans*] Understand *visan*, “to be”; see Romans 15:8. — [Note: [Col. 0825] *broþrjus*] Castillion adds *broþrus*. — [Note: [Col. 0825] *sve*] Gothic omits καί, “also.”] But, brothers, we do not wish you to be uninformed concerning those who are asleep, so that you may not grieve like the others who have no hope. [Note: [Col. 0825] For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, so also God will bring with him, through Jesus, those who have fallen asleep.] [Note: [Col. 0825] *tiuhaiþ*] Since not only *þiuhaiþ* here but also Galatians 5:10 *bairaiþ* and Colossians 3:15 *svignjaiþ* occur, for which, if they are indicatives, *tiuhiþ, bairiþ, svigneiþ* should according to the rules of formation be written, and, if subjunctives, *tiuhai, bairai, svignjai*, it is now beyond doubt that this subjunctive form with added *þ*, foreign to the language of the Gospels, was introduced in a later period and used in place of a Greek future or imperative.] For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, so also God will bring with him, through Jesus, those who have fallen asleep.

[Note: [Col. 0825] For we say this to you by the word of the Lord: we who are alive, who remain until the coming of the Lord, shall not precede those who have fallen asleep.] For we say this to you by the word of the Lord: we who are alive, who remain until the coming of the Lord, shall not precede those who have fallen asleep. [Note: [Col. 0825] For the Lord himself, with a command, with the voice of an archangel, and with God’s trumpet, will descend from heaven; and the dead in Christ will rise first.] [Note: [Col. 0825] *haitjai*] Thus codex B; Castillion adds *hait jah*. — [Note: [Col. 0825] *þai*] [Col. 0826] “they,” omitted by all Greek witnesses.] For the Lord himself, with a command, with an archangel’s voice, and with God’s trumpet, will descend from heaven, and the dead in Christ will rise first. [Note: [Col. 0825] Then we who are alive, who remain, shall immediately be caught up with him in clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and so shall we be with the Lord forever.] [Note: [Col. 0826] *ïmma*] “with him”; all Greek witnesses: αὐτοῖς, “with them.” Gothic agrees with Slavonic 5. — [Note: [Col. 0826] *jah*] Gothic omits οὕτω, “thus.”] Then we who are alive, who remain, shall immediately be caught up with him in clouds to meet the Lord in the air, and henceforth we shall be with the Lord forever. [Note: [Col. 0825] Therefore now comfort one another with these words.] [Note: [Col. 0826] *nu*] “therefore,” omitted by all Greek witnesses.] Therefore comfort one another with these words.

[Note: [Col. 0825] But concerning times and seasons, brothers, we have no need to write to you;] [Note: [Col. 0826] *þaurbum—meljaima*] Greek χρείαν ἔχετε—γράφεσθαι, “you have need—to be written to”; Gothic agrees with the Vulgate.] But concerning times and seasons, brothers, we have no need to write to you, [Note: [Col. 0825] for you yourselves know exactly that the day of the Lord comes as a thief in the night.] for you yourselves know exactly that the day of the Lord comes as a thief in the night. [Note: [Col. 0825] When they say, “Peace and security,” then destruction suddenly comes upon them, like labour-pains upon a pregnant woman, and they do not escape.] [Note: [Col. 0826] *biqimith*] Thus codex Castillion, *Add.* p. 71. — [Note: [Col. 0826] *fralusts*] This word, entirely faded in codex B, was correctly restored by Castillion. — [Note: [Col. 0826] *sair qiþuhaftons*] Thus codex B; Castillion adds *qaisv þis hafteis*, although in his note he calls that reading certain. — [Note: [Col. 0826] *jah*] In the second occurrence *ni*, “not,” is absent through an obvious scribal error, unless in this difficult, erased place the manuscript read *ni gaþliuhand*. *Unþaþliuhand* is certainly a properly compounded word, and especially suitable for rendering Greek ἐκφεύγειν, “to escape” (see 2 Corinthians 2:33); but it usually takes with it the object escaped. Where this case is omitted, Gothic uses *gaþliuhan*, as we propose; see Matthew 8:33; Mark 5:14; 14:50; 16:8.] When they say, “Peace and security,” then destruction suddenly comes upon them, like labour-pains upon a pregnant woman, and they do not escape.

[Note: [Col. 0825] But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that the day should overtake you like a thief;] But you, brothers, are not in darkness, so that the day may overtake you like a thief. [Note: [Col. 0825] For you are all children of light and children of day; we are not of night nor of darkness.] [Note: [Col. 0826] *siuþ*] “you are”; Greek ἐσμέν, “we are.” — [Note: [Col. 0826] *nahts*] Codex B adds *nahs*.] For you are all children of light and children of day; you are not of night or darkness. [Note: [Col. 0825] Accordingly then, let us not sleep as the others do, but let us watch and be sober;] [Note: [Col. 0826] *sve*] Gothic, with manuscripts and versions, omits καί, “also.”] Accordingly then, let us not sleep as the others do, but let us watch and be sober. [Note: [Col. 0825] For those who sleep, sleep by night; and those who become drunk become drunk by night.] [Note: [Col. 0826] *nahts*] Castillion ought not to have conjectured *nahti*, for this is not an unusual—as he calls it—but an erroneous form; *nahts* is correct; see Luke 2:8.] For those who sleep sleep by night, and those who become drunk become drunk by night. [Note: [Col. 0825] But we, who belong to the day, [Col. 0827] should be sober, having put on the breastplate of faith and love, and as a helmet the hope of salvation;] [Note: [Col. 0826] *unskavai*] From 1 Corinthians 15:34 Castillion correctly observes that *usskavai*, or rather *usskavjai*, should be read; cf. [Col. 0827] v. 6. We have often observed interchange of *n* and *s*: Matthew 7:23; Mark 6:2. — [Note: [Col. 0827] *nasseinais*] Thus codex B for *naseinais*; see Galatians 5:15.] But we, being of the day, should be sober, clothed with the breastplate of faith and love and with the helmet of the hope of salvation.

[Note: [Col. 0827] For God did not appoint us for wrath, but for obtaining salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,] For God did not appoint us for wrath, but for obtaining salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ, [Note: [Col. 0827] who died for us, so that, whether we sleep or wake, we may live together with him.] [Note: [Col. 0827] *slepaima—vakaima*] Omitted by Greek witnesses.] who died for us, so that, whether we sleep or wake, we may live together with him. [Note: [Col. 0827] Therefore comfort one another and build up each one the other, as you also do.] Therefore comfort one another and build one another up, as you also do.

[Note: [Col. 0827] But we ask you, brothers, to recognize those who labour among you and preside over you in the Lord.] [Note: [Col. 0827] *fraujin*] Gothic omits καὶ νουθετοῦντας ὑμᾶς καί, “and admonish you, and.” — [Note: [Col. 0827] *sveraiþ*] “honour”; Greek ἡγεῖσθαι, governed by ἐρωτῶμεν, “we ask.” Since Gothic here employs the imperative, it rightly adds *jah* before *gavairþi habaiþ*, “have peace,” which is likewise rightly absent from Greek. — [Note: [Col. 0827] *ïzvis*] “among yourselves”; all Greek witnesses: ἑαυτοῖς, “yourselves”; cf. 2:14.] But we ask you, brothers, to recognize those who labour among you and preside over you in the Lord.

[Note: [Col. 0827] Honour them abundantly in love because of their work, and have peace among yourselves.] Honour them exceedingly in love because of their work, and have peace among yourselves. [Note: [Col. 0827] But we ask you, brothers, admonish the disorderly, comfort the faint-hearted, support the weak, be patient toward all;] [Note: [Col. 0827] *broþrjus*] Codex B adds *broþjus*. — [Note: [Col. 0827] *ungatassans*] Thus codex B; Castillion: *ungatlisans*. — [Note: [Col. 0827] *usþulaip*] “support”; all Greek witnesses: ἀντέχεσθε, “hold fast to” (cf. Titus 1:9, *andnimaiþ*). Gothic appears mistakenly to have read ἀνέχεσθε, “bear with,” an error likewise made by the scribe of codex 74.] But we ask you, brothers: admonish the disorderly, comfort the faint-hearted, support the weak, be patient toward all.

[Note: [Col. 0827] See that no one repays evil for evil to anyone; but always pursue what is good, both toward one another and toward all.] [Note: [Col. 0827] *ubil ana*] Castillion adds “jct.” Moreover, instead of *ana* (“upon”), all Greek witnesses have ἀντί (“for”). Since *ana* does not correspond to the sense of that preposition, we do not doubt that codex B wrote *und*, as in Romans 12:17 [Col. 0828] *ni ainummehun ubil und ubilamma usgibands*, “repaying evil for evil to no one”; cf. Matthew 5:38. — [Note: [Col. 0827] *laistjaiþ*] Gothic, with certain manuscripts, omits καί, “also.”] See that no one repays evil for evil to anyone; rather, always pursue what is good, both toward one another and toward all.

[Note: [Col. 0827] Always rejoice in the Lord;] [Note: [Col. 0828] *ïn fraujin*] “in the Lord,” omitted in Greek.] Always rejoice in the Lord. [Note: [Col. 0827] Pray without ceasing; in everything give thanks;] Pray without ceasing; in everything give thanks. [Note: [Col. 0827] For this is God’s will in Christ Jesus toward you.] [Note: [Col. 0828] *ïst*] “is,” omitted in Greek.] For this is God’s will in Christ Jesus toward you.

[Note: [Col. 0827] Do not quench the Spirit;] Do not quench the Spirit. [Note: [Col. 0827] Do not despise prophecies;] Do not despise prophecies. [Note: [Col. 0827] But test everything; hold fast what is good;] But test everything; hold fast what is good. [Note: [Col. 0827] Abstain from every kind of evil,] [Note: [Col. 0828] *ubilaizo*] Codex A begins here.] Abstain from every kind of evil.

[Note: [Col. 0827] May the God of peace himself sanctify you wholly; and may your entire spirit, soul, and body be preserved blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.] [Note: [Col. 0828] *jah—ahman*] Since Gothic here uses the accusative, nothing is more certain than that it understood καὶ ὁλόκληρον ὑμῶν τὸ πνεῦμα, “and may your whole spirit,” to depend on ἁγιάσαι, “sanctify,” whereas in all Greek witnesses and versions it belongs with ψυχή, “soul,” and σῶμα, “body,” under τηρηθείη, “may be preserved,” and ought to be in the nominative (*jah gahails ïzvar ahma*).] May the God of peace himself sanctify you wholly, and may your whole spirit, soul, and body be preserved blameless at the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ. [Note: [Col. 0827] Faithful is he who calls you; he will also do it.] Faithful is he who calls you, who will also do it. [Note: [Col. 0827] Brothers, pray also for us.] [Note: [Col. 0828] *þan jah*] “but also,” for Greek καί, as in Matthew 9:17.] Brothers, pray also for us.

[Note: [Col. 0827] Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss.] Greet all the brothers with a holy kiss. [Note: [Col. 0827] I charge you by the Lord that this letter be read to the holy brothers.] [Note: [Col. 0828] *aipistaule*] Codex B, with codex 17, omits πᾶσι, “all.” In codex A, although traces of that word (*allaim*) cannot be discerned because of an erasure in the parchment, the space is sufficient to contain it.] I charge you by the Lord that the letter be read to the holy brothers. [Note: [Col. 0827] The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.] [Note: [Col. 0828] *amen*] “Amen,” omitted in Greek.] The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you. Amen.

## The Second Epistle to the Thessalonians Begins

[Note: [Col. 0827]

Inscription: *du þaissalaunekaium anþara anastodeiþ*] Codex A: *du þaissalauneikaum* (thus!) *b anas[todeiþ]*. The final letters of the verb *anastodeiþ*, which we have supplied from codex A in the title, were so faded that Castiglione restored them by conjecture; cf. *Prolegomena*, col. 480, note 8. Moreover, in the title of the earlier epistle, instead of *þaissalauneikim*, as we wrote *rumonim, galatim*, and the like, we ought rather to have written *þaissalauneikaium* [Col. 0829] (for this is more correct than what the manuscripts offer, and it is likewise found in the subscription of this epistle); and *kaulaussaim* in the subscription to Colossians also appears to require correction to *kaulaussaium*.]

[Col. 0827]

[Col. 0827] Paul and Silvanus and Timothy to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ:

Paul and Silvanus and Timothy to the church of the Thessalonians in God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

[Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.]

Jesus Christ. Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

[We ought always to give thanks to God for you, brothers, as is fitting; because your faith grows exceedingly, and the love of every one of you all toward one another abounds.]

We ought always to thank God for you, brothers, as is fitting. For your faith increases greatly, and the love of each one of you all toward one another abounds.

[So that we ourselves glory in you in the churches of God, because of your steadfastness and faith in all your persecutions and afflictions which you endure.]

[ïn] The first *ïn* is omitted by codex B; we have added it from codex A.—[stivitjis] This is to be read thus in place of *stivitjons*, which Castiglione printed from a completely erased passage. This is required first by *izvaris*, a neuter form, and then because the Goths call ὑπομονή, “steadfastness,” not *stivitjon* but *stiviti*; see 2 Corinthians 1:6; 6:4.—[vrakjom] Thus the codices; Castiglione has added *vrakjam*.

So that we ourselves glory in you in the churches of God, for your steadfastness and faith in all your persecutions and afflictions which you endure.

[An indication of the righteous judgment of God, so that you may be made worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you also suffer.]

[ïn] Codex B ends here. What Castiglione printed from this point through *jabai* in the following verse he supplied wholly by conjecture, since the parchment had been entirely erased; “thus,” he says, “in this and the next two little pages many conjectures were necessary.”

An indication of the righteous judgment of God, that you may be deemed worthy of the kingdom of God, for which indeed you suffer.

[Yet it is righteous with God to repay affliction to those afflicting us,]

[jabai] All Greek witnesses: εἴπερ, “if indeed.” Since the Gothic normally renders this as *sveþauh jabai* (“yet if indeed”; see Romans 8:9; cf. 2 Corinthians 10:8), we have judged that it should be written here too in place of simple *jabai*. For although Castiglione, after again consulting the codex, could discern scarcely any letters, he nevertheless says that the space suffices for so many letters. In other places the enclitic περ is rendered in Gothic by *raihtis*; see on 2 Corinthians 8:7. Thus *jabai raihtis* might also be read. But because Castiglione expressly says that after *jabai* nothing is visible at this place, conjecturing *jabai raihtis* must be avoided.—[ïst] “is”; all Greek witnesses.—[uns] “us”; all Greek witnesses have ὑμᾶς, “you,” except codex B 2 in Mill.

Yet if indeed it is righteous with God to repay affliction to those who afflict us,

[but to you who are afflicted, rest with us, at the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ from heaven with the angels of his power,]

[ïþ] “but”; all Greek witnesses have καί, “and”; the Gothic agrees with the Latin Sabatier version.—[gapraihanaim] Massmann, *M. G. A.* 1840, p. 127, wrongly considers this false; see Matthew 7:14; 2 Corinthians 4:8. Nor does the immediately preceding verse read *gaþraihandam*, as he says, but correctly *gaþreihandam*.—[ïusila] Castiglione restored this entirely obliterated word with the help of 2 Corinthians 8:13.—[unsaris] “our”; the Greek lacks it; the Gothic agrees with the codices cited by Mill.—[xristaus] “Christ”; omitted by the Greek; the Gothic agrees with the codices cited by Mill and by Mai.—[himinam] “from heaven”: apparently Castiglione found *himinam* written on the erased parchment in place of *himina* (οὐρανοῦ, “of heaven”). This is surprising: although in the Gospels the singular οὐρανός is almost always rendered by the Goths as *himinōs*, plural, in the Epistles our translators not only follow the Greek forms, but even use a singular for a plural without Greek authority; see on Ephesians 3:15 and Colossians 1:16.

But to you who are afflicted, relief with us at the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ from heaven, with the angels of his power,

[in a flame of fire, giving vengeance to those who do not know God and do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ;]

[Col. 0830] [funins lauhmonai] “in a flame of fire,” Greek πυρὶ φλογός. The Gothic, together with the codices, reads φλογὶ πυρός, with the words transposed. Moreover, for *lauhmonai* we think, with Massmann at the cited place, p. 126, that *lauhmonjai* should be read; see Luke 10:18; 17:24.—[gibandins] Thus *gibandis* should be read in place of the form which Castiglione wrongly printed from a wholly erased passage.

In a flame of fire, giving vengeance to those who do not know God and do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ.

[Who shall pay the penalty, eternal destruction, away from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of his power;]

[þaiei] Since the two words following this, corresponding to the Greek δίκην τίσουσι, “they shall pay a penalty,” were wholly erased in the codex, Castiglione supplied *fraveit usgiband* by conjecture; Massmann wrongly praises this conjecture at the cited place, p. 134. For a word meaning ἐκδίκησις, “vengeance,” cannot also mean δίκη, “penalty.” Castiglione was more correct in using *usgiband* for τίσουσι; see Philemon 19. But what other Gothic word was written in place of *fraveit* is difficult to say, since δίκη occurs nowhere else in the New Testament from which a conjecture can be made.

Who shall [lacuna] eternal destruction, from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of his power,

[when he comes to be glorified in his saints and . . . . . . in all those who believed, because our testimony to you was believed on that day.]

[Col. 0830] [qimiþ] Castiglione restored *qemi* by conjecture. But the construction does not permit this, because where a Greek aorist subjunctive, used in place of the Latin future perfect, is to be expressed, the Goths normally use the present indicative, more rarely the present subjunctive; see Grimm, *Grammar*, IV, 147. Thus below, 2:3, *qimiþ* or *qimai* must again be read in place of *qemi*, as is also proved by the following *vairþai*.—[ushauhjan] Perhaps *ushauhnan* should be read, as Castiglione also printed in verse 12.—[. . . le . . . ba . . .] From these individual letters Castiglione made *mikilein atgiban guþa*, “to give great things to God,” and Massmann approves this reading at the cited place, p. 134. But if the translator had really written this, how far, one asks, would he have departed from the Greek author? And how can he who is said to be θαυμασθῆναι ἐν πᾶσι τοῖς πιστεύσασι, “admired among all who believed,” be said by the translator to “give great things to God among all believers”? It would be more probable if one read *mikilein haban ïn allaim þaim galaubjandam*, “to have glory among all believers.”—[ïzvis] “to you”; all Greek witnesses have ἐφ’ ὑμᾶς. Undoubtedly the preposition *du* or *ïn* has dropped out before *ïzvis*, which could easily happen because of the following ï. But do not supply *ana*, since it has an adversative force and has no place here.—[jainamma daga] “on that day”; all Greek witnesses.

When he comes to be glorified in his saints and [lacuna] among all believers; for our testimony to you was believed on that day.

[For this reason we also pray always for you, that our God may make you worthy of this calling and fulfill every good pleasure of his goodness and work of faith in power,]

[seinaizos] “his own”; omitted by all Greek witnesses; the Gothic agrees with the Vulgate and the Arabic and Ethiopic versions.

For this reason we also pray always for you, that our God may make you worthy of the calling and fulfill every good pleasure of his own goodness and the work of faith in power,

[that the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and of the Lord Jesus Christ.]

[Col. 0831] [ïesuis] The Gothic agrees with codices omitting χριστοῦ, “Christ.”—[unsaris] The second “our”; omitted by all Greek witnesses; the Gothic agrees with Sabatier.

That the name of our Lord Jesus may be glorified in you, and you in him, according to the grace of our God and our Lord Jesus Christ.

[But we ask you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and our gathering together to him,]

[broþruns] “brothers.” The Goth uses the accusative, dependent on *ïzvis* and *bidjam*, “we ask you,” in place of the Greek vocative ἀδελφοί. Massmann, at the cited place, p. 126, rightly denied that *broþruns* is a vocative form, as Castiglione had said here; but he should not therefore have thought that the Goth, misled by the Latin versions (*rogamus vos fratres*, “we ask you, brothers”), translated in this way. For, as he himself judges with Castiglione at p. 332, the Gothic translation was drawn from Greek books, not from Latin versions.—[qumis] This should be read in place of *quma*, which Castiglione printed in disregard of grammatical rules; for the final letter in the codex is erased.—[. . . gaqumþais unsaraizos] “our gathering together”; omitted by all Greek witnesses. Castiglione printed *miþgaqumþais*, but the reading is uncertain, and we do not think Gothic *miþ-* suitable in compounds for representing Greek ἐπί.

But we ask you, brothers, concerning the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ and [lacuna] our gathering together to him,

[not to be quickly shaken in mind, nor alarmed, neither by spirit nor by word nor by letter as though from us, as though the day of Christ were at hand.]

[ïzvis ahin—washun ïzvis] All this is so erased that it had to be guessed in large part; nevertheless, the letters which can be read agree with my reading. CASTIGLIONE.—[ïzvis] We have written this in place of the solecistic *jus*, since after *du* with an infinitive the subject of the clause is put in the accusative; see 1 Thessalonians 2:12, *veitvodjandans du gaggan ïzvis vairþaba guþs*, “testifying that you should walk worthily of God.” Cf. Mark 4:1, *galesun sik du ïmma manageins filu, svasve ïna galeiþan ïn skip*, “a great crowd gathered to him, so that he entered into a boat.”—[drobnan] Wherever the Goths use this verb, it is compounded, either *ïndrobnan* (John 13:21; 14:1, 27) or *gadrobnan* (Luke 1:12; John 12:27). When we asked Castiglione about this place, he replied that he could read absolutely nothing more; perhaps, therefore, one or the other of those compounds stood here in the codex.—[vaurda] “word(s)”; all Greek witnesses have λόγου, singular. Castiglione fabricated the printed reading from the final letter *a*, which alone can be read.—[ïnstandai] Only the final two letters of this word remain [Col. 0832]. Comparing 2 Timothy 4:2, Castiglione conjectured *ïnstandan*, which Massmann wrongly approves at the cited place, p. 134. For ἐνεστάναι, which had to be translated here, and ἐπιστῆναι, rendered by the Goth as *ïnstandan* in the passage in Timothy, signify altogether different things. Perhaps *atgaggai* should rather be written; see 2 Timothy 3:1.—[xristaus] “Christ”; the Greek has κυρίου, “Lord.”—[wamma haidau] This is how it should be read. Castiglione conjectured *wammeh*, of which he could identify only the first letter. *Wazuh*, meaning “all” or “each,” has no place in negative statements of this kind. Moreover, do not suppose with Castiglione that the Goth read differently from the Greek witnesses: the Goths do not everywhere imitate the Greek practice of doubling negatives.—[niba—faurþis] Traces of letters are scarcely visible here. CASTIGLIONE. He supplied the text correctly, except that he should have put *qimiþ* or *qimai* in place of *qemi*; see on 1:10.

Not to be quickly shaken in mind, nor alarmed, neither through spirit nor through word nor through a letter as though from us, that the day of Christ is at hand.

[Let no one deceive you in any way; for unless the apostasy comes first, and the man of sin is revealed, the son of perdition,]

The foregoing note applies here also: [ïzvis ahin—washun ïzvis] All this is so erased that it had to be guessed in large part; nevertheless, the readable letters agree with Castiglione’s reading.—[ïzvis] We write this instead of *jus*, because the subject after *du* with an infinitive stands in the accusative; cf. 1 Thessalonians 2:12 and Mark 4:1.—[drobnan] The Gothic usage otherwise requires a compound, *ïndrobnan* or *gadrobnan*; Castiglione could read no more at this point.—[vaurda] “word(s)”; Greek λόγου, singular; Castiglione made the printed reading from the sole visible final *a*.—[instandai] Only the last two letters remain [Col. 0832]. Castiglione conjectured *ïnstandan* by comparison with 2 Timothy 4:2, but ἐνεστάναι and ἐπιστῆναι differ entirely in sense; *atgaggai* may be preferable; see 2 Timothy 3:1.—[xristaus] “Christ”; Greek κυρίου, “Lord.”—[wamma haidau] This is the correct reading; Castiglione conjectured *wammeh*. *Wazuh*, “all” or “each,” does not fit such negative clauses. Nor should one infer a Greek reading different from the witnesses, for Gothic does not always reproduce doubled Greek negatives.—[niba—faurþis] The letter-traces are scarcely apparent. Castiglione supplied the text correctly except that *qimiþ* or *qimai*, rather than *qemi*, should have been used; see on 1:10.

Let no one deceive you in any way; for unless the apostasy comes first,

[who opposes and exalts himself above every so-called god or every object of worship, so that he sits in the temple of God—]

[Col. 0832] [ufar] “above”; all Greek witnesses have ἐπί; the Gothic agrees with the Old Latin.—[qiþana] This is incorrect. Either the Goth read with that Old Latin version which has *qui dicitur*, “which is called” (and then *qiþanana* should be written), or he referred it to *all* (and then *qiþan* or *qiþano* would be required). We prefer *qiþanana*; cf. Massmann at the cited place, p. 133.—[svaei ïn] I find no trace of these letters, but there is space for them. CASTIGLIONE. He should also have added *ïna*, because *svaei* normally has its subject, with its infinitive, in the accusative; see on verse 2. The Old Latin and Vulgate omit it, but that is another matter.—[al] Thus the codex for *alh*, as at Mark 15:38; see on Matthew 5:15.—[s . . . . . .] Castiglione printed *sik ustaiknjands*, “showing himself.” Since nothing remains except the first letter *s*, the reading is wholly uncertain; *sve guþ . . .*, “as God . . .,” could equally have been conjectured, since many Greek witnesses insert ὡς θεόν, “as God.” Codex A ends here.

And the man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition, who opposes and exalts himself above every so-called god or every object of worship, so that he sits in the temple of God, [lacuna].

[—ours.]

[Col. 0833] [unsaros] Codex B continues. Castiglione thinks that *þairh aipistauleins*, “through our letter,” preceded, and that the Goth used a plural for δι’ ἐπιστολῆς ἡμῶν and here declined it otherwise than at Nehemiah 6:17, where *aipistaulans* occurs. We think otherwise. There is no reason why the translator should have used a plural here, and ἐπιστολή is often rendered in the Pauline epistles by singular *aipistaule*. Since a plural substantive is required by the pronoun *unsaros*, what undoubtedly preceded was *þairh bokos*, “through our writings”; thus below, 3:14, διὰ τῆς ἐπιστολῆς is again rendered *þairh þos bokos*. Cf. 2 Corinthians 7:8; 3:1.

[But our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God, even our Father, who loved us and gave us eternal consolation and good hope through grace,]

But our Lord Jesus Christ himself, and God, our Father, who loved us and gave eternal consolation and good hope in grace,

[may comfort your hearts and establish you in every good work and word.]

[hairtona ïzvara] Omitted by all Greek witnesses except codex k in Mill; likewise below, 3:5, where no Greek witness agrees.—[gatulgjai] The Gothic agrees with codices reading ὑμᾶς, “you.”—[vaurstvam jah vaurdam] “works and words”; omitted by all Greek witnesses.

May comfort your hearts and establish you in every good work and word.

[Finally, brothers, pray also for us, that the word of the Lord may run and be glorified, as also among you,]

[ei bidjaiþ] “that you may pray”; all Greek witnesses have προσεύχεσθε. Thus Galatians 5:16, in place of λέγω δέ, πνεύματι περιπατεῖτε, “but I say, walk by the Spirit,” he says: *aþþan qiþa, ei ahmin gaggaiþ*, “but I say that you should walk in the Spirit”; cf. on Mark 15:36.—[jah bi unsis broþrjus] “also for us, brothers”; all Greek witnesses have ἀδελφοί περὶ ἡμῶν. This transposition of words is also found in Sabatier; codex B, however, adds *broþrous*.

Finally, pray also for us, brothers, that the word of the Lord may run and be glorified, as also among you,

[and that we may be delivered from unreasonable and evil people; for faith is not possessed by all.]

[Col. 0833] [af gastojanaim] Castiglione confirms, after inspecting the codex again, that this reading is certain; but many considerations show that it is false. First, what is this participial form from the verb *stojan*? It should certainly be *stauïþs* or *stojiþs*. Further, if this form is granted, how can one be called “judged” whom the Greeks call ἄτοπος, “out of place,” “unreasonable”? We think rather that *afgastoþanaim* should be read. As *ungastoþans visan* in 1 Corinthians 4:11 means ἀστατεῖν, “to have no fixed place,” so *afgastoþans* properly means one moved from his place, ἄτοπος. The Goths frequently render figurative expressions literally: thus, to cite one example out of many, in 1 Timothy 3:6 the Goth calls νεόφυτος, “a recent convert,” *niujana satidana*, “newly planted.” Such things, of course, are for Castiglione signs of the translator’s carelessness; cf. his note on verse 7. Those who approve this conjecture considered in itself may perhaps demand that the Gothic omit ἀπό after ῥύειν; but similarly the translator omits the preposition *af* after verbs of loosing or freeing in 1 Corinthians 7:27: *galausiþs ïs qenai*, “are you loosed from a wife?” for λέλυσαι ἀπὸ γυναικός. Castiglione, moreover, correctly restored the largely obliterated word *uslausjaindau*.—[ïst] “is”; omitted by all Greek witnesses.

And that we may be delivered from unreasonable and evil people; for faith is not for all.

[But the Lord is faithful, who shall establish you and deliver you from evil.]

[triggvs] The Gothic omits ἐστίν, “is.”

But faithful is the Lord, who will establish you and deliver you from evil.

[But we have confidence in the Lord concerning you, that you both do and will do what we command you.]

[Col. 0834] [anabudum] “we command”; all Greek witnesses and versions have παραγγέλλομεν.

But we have confidence in the Lord concerning you, that what we command you, you both do and will do.

[May the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God and into the steadfastness of Christ.]

[frauja] The Gothic omits δέ, “but.”—[hairtona ïzvara] See on 2:17.

May the Lord direct your hearts into the love of God and into the steadfastness of Christ.

[But we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you withdraw yourselves from every brother walking disorderly and not according to the tradition which you received from us.]

[wairbandane ungatassaba] “walking disorderly”; omitted by all Greek witnesses; the Gothic agrees with the Vulgate.—[anafilham] “tradition”; all Greek witnesses have παράδοσιν.—[andnemuþ] “you received”; Greek παρελάβοσαν.

But we command you, brothers, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you separate yourselves from every brother walking disorderly and not according to the tradition which you received from us.

[For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us;]

[ïst] Codex A continues.

For you yourselves know how it is fitting to imitate us.

[For we did not behave disorderly among you; nor did we eat anyone’s bread freely, but worked night and day with toil and hardship, so that we might not burden any of you.]

[ni] The second occurrence: codex A has *nih*, “nor.”—[vinnandans arbaidai] “working with toil”; all Greek witnesses have ἐν κόπῳ καὶ μόχθῳ, “in toil and hardship.” Moreover, Castiglione rightly observes that *ïn arbaidai*, rather than *arbaidai* alone, should have been written.

For we were not disorderly among you, nor did we eat bread from anyone without payment; but, working in labor by night and day, we worked so that we might not burden any of you.

[Not because we do not have authority, but in order that we might give ourselves to you as an example for you to imitate us.]

[gebeima] The Gothic omits ὑμῖν, “to you.”

Not because we did not have authority, but in order that we might give ourselves as an example for you to imitate us.

[Col. 0833] [For even when we were with you, we gave you this command: if anyone is unwilling to work, neither let him eat.]

[Col. 0834] [ïzvis anabudum] “we commanded you”; omitted by all Greek witnesses.—[ni] The second occurrence: in codex A there is room for one letter, so that *nih*, “nor,” could have been written; nevertheless, there is no trace of an *h*. CASTIGLIONE.

For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: if anyone is unwilling to work, neither let him eat.

[For we hear that some among you walk disorderly, doing no work at all, but meddling in trifles.]

For we hear that some among you walk disorderly, doing no work, but being busybodies.

[Now such persons we command and exhort in the Lord Jesus Christ that, working quietly, they eat their own bread.]

[þaimuh] “to such persons”; all Greek witnesses have τοῖς δέ. The Goth similarly puts the enclitic *-uh* for Greek δέ at Matthew 27:44; see on John 18:26.—[ïn fraujin] “in the Lord”; Greek διὰ τοῦ κυρίου, “through the Lord.” The Gothic agrees with the Vulgate, which omits ἡμῶν, “our.”

Now such persons we command and exhort in the Lord Jesus Christ that, working quietly, they eat their own bread.

[But you, brothers, do not grow weary in doing good.]

But you, brothers, do not become weary in doing good.

[But if anyone does not obey our word through this letter, take note of that person; do not associate with him, that he may be ashamed.]

[ni] The second occurrence: “not”; Greek καὶ μή, “and not.”

But if anyone does not obey our word through these writings, mark that person. Do not associate with him, that he may be ashamed.

[And do not regard him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.]

[ïna] “him”; omitted by all Greek witnesses.

And do not regard him as an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.

[Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace always in every way. The Lord be with all of you.]

[stadim] “places”; Greek τρόπῳ, “way” or “manner.”

Now may the Lord of peace himself give you peace always in every place. The Lord be with all of you.

[This greeting is in my own hand, Paul’s, which is the sign in every one of my letters: thus I write.]

[aipistaulem meinaim] “in my letters.” Codex B has *aipistaulemeinaim*, so that the scribe not only omitted *m* at the end of *aipistaulem* because of the same following letter—as at 2 Timothy 2:2, *þrighvaimannam* for *þriggvaim mannam*; cf. on John 12:42—but also put the mutilated *-em* in place of the full ending *-eim*; see on Luke 10:5, where the following should be added: *frume* in the subscription to 1 Corinthians; *anavilje*, Philippians 4:5; *ne*, *Skeireins* 38.7. Codex A is erased here, and all Greek witnesses omit *meinaim*, “my.”—Subscription: Greek witnesses vary.—[anþara] “second”; codex B, for codex A is erased, wrongly has *frumei*, “first.” Since the subscription of this second Epistle to the Thessalonians and the heading of the first to Timothy are written on the same little page, and the scribe ought to have written: *du þaissalauneikaium anþara ustauh*, “The Second to the Thessalonians ends”; then: *du teimauþaiu frumei dustodeiþ*, “The First to Timothy begins”: he mistakenly wrote *frumei* above for *anþara*, and below *ustauh* for *dustodeiþ*; cf. the heading of 1 Timothy.

The greeting in my own hand—Paul’s—which is the sign in all my letters: thus I write.

[Grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

The Second to the Thessalonians ends.]

Grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.

The Second to the Thessalonians ends.

## The First to Timothy Begins

[Col. 0835]

The heading is found only in codex B.—[þeimauþaiau] Codex B has *þaimaauþaiau*. Moreover, *þeimauþaius* is written for *teimauþaius*, likewise at 1:2; see on 2:10. But *teimauþaius* is correctly written below at 1:18; 2:1, 2.—[dustodeiþ] “begins”; codex B has *ustauh*, “ends”; see the subscription to 2 Thessalonians.

The beginning of this epistle is found in both codices.

[Col. 0835]

[Note: [Col. 0835] Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus according to the command of God our Savior and Christ Jesus, our hope.] [Note: [Col. 0835] *xristaus ïesuis*] omitted by nearly all Greek manuscripts except codex f according to Mill. — *anabusnim*: “command”; all Greek manuscripts have ἐπιταγήν.]

Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, according to the command of God our Savior and Christ Jesus, our hope, [Note: [Col. 0835] To Timothy, beloved son in faith: grace, mercy, peace from God the Father and Christ Jesus our Lord.] [Note: [Col. 0835] *þeimauþaiu*] thus codex B; codex A, more correctly, has *þeimauþaiau*; see on Luke I.54. — *attin*] Gothic, with codices, omits “our” (ἡμῶν).]

to Timothy, a chosen child in faith: grace, mercy, peace from God the Father and Christ [Note: [Col. 0835] As I urged you to remain at Ephesus when I was going into Macedonia, so that you might command certain persons not to teach otherwise,] [Note: [Col. 0835] *galeiþands*] thus correctly codex A; codex B has *galeiþans*. The scribe of codex B often made this error: below, verse 9, *vitans*; III.4, *fauragaggans*, whereas in both places codex A correctly has *vitands* and *fauragaggands*. The same error also occurs at II.II.6, where *arbaidjans* is written for *arbaidjands*; conversely, at I.II.13 *gadigans* must be read for *gadigands*; see on Mark XII.24. — *makidonais*] codex A has *makedonais*; compare the note on 2 Corinthians I.16. For the genitive used after verbs of departure, see Luke XV.15.]

Jesus our Lord. As I urged you, when departing for Macedonia, to remain at Ephesus, in order that you might prohibit certain persons [Note: [Col. 0835] nor to give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which produce disputes rather than the edification of God which is in faith.] [Note: [Col. 0835] *andilausaize*] codex A has *andalausaize*; see V.14. — *þau*] thus the codices; Castiglione adds *þan*. — *timreinai*] “edification”; Greek οἰκονομίαν. — *visandein*] “being/existing”; omitted by all Greek manuscripts. Moreover codex A has *visandin*, just as below, III.4, it has *anaviljin* for *anaviljein*. Undoubtedly *visandin* was likewise written at Skeireins, p. 49, line 17, for *visandein.]

not to teach differently, nor to pay attention to fables and interminable genealogies, which generate disputes rather than God’s edification, which exists in faith. But the end of the command is [Note: [Col. 0835] But the end of the command is love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and sincere faith.] [Note: [Col. 0835] *aþþanandeis*] codex B has *aþþandeis*: scribes omit not only individual letters that ought to be doubled, but also syllables; thus Matthew XXVI.73 has *standans* for *standandans*, and likewise below, III.13; IV.7; II.I.8, and elsewhere. Compare the note on I.17. — *ïst anabusnais*] “is of the command,” omitted by all Greek manuscripts. [Col. 0836] — *miþvissein*] in the margin of codex A, *gamundai*, “remembrance.”]

love from a pure heart, a good conscience, and unfeigned faith. From which [Note: [Col. 0835] From which certain persons, having wandered away, turned aside to empty talk,] certain persons, having gone astray, turned aside to empty speech, wishing to be teachers of the law, not understanding either [Note: [Col. 0835] wishing to be teachers of the law, not understanding either what they say or what they confidently affirm.] [Note: [Col. 0836] *ni*] codex A has *nih*, “nor.”]

what they say or what they affirm. But we know [Note: [Col. 0835] But we know that the law is good, if anyone uses it lawfully;] [Note: [Col. 0836] *vitum*] “we know”; codex A has *vituþ*, “you know.” — *vitodeigo*] “lawfully”; codex a has *vitoda*, “by the law, according to the law,” a dative of manner, as at Luke I.74 *unagein*, ἀφόβως, “without fear.” Thus Castiglione and Massmann err, in the cited passage, p. 212, by writing *vitodabrukeiþ* as one word, just as Castiglione erred at Colossians III.22 by writing *leika fraujam* (κατὰ σάρκα κυρίοις, “masters according to the flesh”) as one word; compare below on V.14. The words *vitodalaisarjos* and *svultavairþja*, which Castiglione objects to us, are altogether different.]

that the law is good if anyone uses the law lawfully, knowing [Note: [Col. 0835] knowing that law is not laid down for a righteous man, but for lawless and disobedient persons, ungodly and sinners, unholy and profane, those who strike fathers and those who strike mothers, murderers,] [Note: [Col. 0836] *vitands*] codex B has *vitans*; see on verse 3. Moreover Gothic omits τοῦτο, “this”; see on II.I.15. — *vitoþ nist*] omitted by codex A. — *ak*] “but”; all Greek manuscripts have δέ; see 1 Corinthians XIV.20. — *jah*] the second and fourth occurrences, “and,” are omitted by all Greek manuscripts. — *unsibjaim*] ἀνόμοις, “lawless”; the margin of codex A, with all Greek manuscripts, has *afgudaim*, ἀσεβέσι, “ungodly.” — *aipeins*] codex A ends. — *horam*] Gothic omits ἀρσενοκοίταις, “men who lie with males”; on this omission see Massmann, cited work, p. 220.]

that law is not appointed for the righteous, but for lawless and unruly persons, ungodly and sinful persons, unholy and profane persons, those who strike fathers, those who strike mothers, murderers, [Note: [Col. 0835] fornicators, enslavers of men, liars, perjurers, and whatever else is opposed to sound teaching,] [Note: [Col. 0836] *gaþivandam*] Castiglione supplied *gaþivjandam* from a wholly erased place, which Massmann, cited work, p. 134, ought not to have approved. Compare *anaþivan* (“to bring into bondage”) at 1 Corinthians IX.27, and *gaþivan* (“to enslave”) at 1 Corinthians VII.15 (καταδουλοῦν), 2 Corinthians II.20, Galatians II.4 (περιπείρειν), and 1 Timothy VI.10. But *þivjan* occurs nowhere. — *wa alja … andstandand*] provided that this reading is certain, and since *wo* is not written for *wa* in the manuscript, beware, with Castiglione, of taking *wa* as a plural: it would have to be *wo*.
