Rather, *wa* is an absolute accusative used adverbially and means “perhaps”; see 2 Corinthians XII.6, 18; John XIV.13; similarly *we* at 2 Corinthians XI.21. The Gothic translator seems to have read εἴ τι as the single word εἴτι.]

fornicators, enslavers of men, liars, perjurers, and if perhaps anything else opposes sound teaching, [Note: [Col. 0835] which accords with the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, entrusted to me;] [Note: [Col. 0836] *sei ïst*] “which is”; omitted by all Greek manuscripts. Gothic agrees with the versions.]

which is according to the gospel of the glory of the blessed God, with which I was entrusted. And I give thanks to Christ Jesus our Lord, who strengthens me, because he considered me faithful, appointing me [Note: [Col. 0835] And I give thanks to Christ Jesus our Lord, who strengthens me, because he considered me faithful, appointing me to ministry,] to ministry, though formerly I was a blasphemer, persecutor, and violent man; but I received mercy because I acted ignorantly in unbelief. [Note: [Col. 0835] Although formerly I was a blasphemer, a persecutor, and a violent man; yet I received mercy, because I acted ignorantly in unbelief.] But the grace of the Lord abounded exceedingly [Note: [Col. 0835] But the grace of the Lord abounded exceedingly with faith and love which are in Christ.] [Note: [Col. 0836] *ufarassiþ*] Castiglione believes this should be read in the erased place, and denies that *ufarasseiþ* can be read because the space lacks so many letters. Since nearly all Greek manuscripts have ὑπερεπλεόνασε, in the past tense, we conjectured *ufarassida*. It is also possible that the scribe wrote *ufaraseiþ* for *ufarasseiþ*; but *ufarassiþ* is wholly incorrect. [Col. 0837] — *fraujins*] Gothic omits ἡμῶν, “our.” — *xristau*] Gothic omits Ἰησοῦ, “Jesus.”]

with faith and love in Christ. Faithful is the saying, and worthy of every acceptance: Christ Jesus came into the world [Note: [Col. 0835] Faithful is this saying [Col. 0837] and worthy of every acceptance: Christ Jesus came into this world to save sinners, of whom I am the first.] to save sinners, of whom I am the foremost. But for this reason I received mercy: that in me, the foremost, Christ Jesus might display all patience as an example for those who were to believe in him for [Note: [Col. 0837] But for this reason I received mercy, that in me, the first, Christ Jesus might display all patience, as an example for those who would believe in him unto eternal life.] [Note: [Col. 0837] *xristaus ïesus*] omitted by all Greek manuscripts. Moreover, concerning *xristaus*: it is not, as Castiglione says, an erroneous form, but an unusual form for *xristus*; see Mark VII.32, and add Galatians IV.19, *xristaus*; Mark X.46, *barteimaiaus*; John VIII.52 and 2 Timothy I.10, *dauþau*, for *xristus*, *barteimaius*, *dauþu*. — *du galaubjan*] Castiglione adds *jct.* The construction *du* with an infinitive after *anavairþs* occurs again at 1 Thessalonians III.4: *anavairþ vas uns du vinnan agliþos*, “it was before us that we should suffer affliction.”]

eternal life. Now to the King of the ages, immortal, invisible, the only wise God, be honor and glory for ages of ages. Amen. [Note: [Col. 0837] *undivanjamma*] written thus for *undivanamma*, as it should have been; see 1 Corinthians XV.53–54; 2 Corinthians V.4. Castiglione states that, on examining the manuscript again, he read it thus. Whether the Gothic translator read ἀθανάτῳ, “immortal,” or ἀφθάρτῳ, “incorruptible,” cannot be determined with certainty; *divans* is also used at 1 Corinthians XV.54 for φθαρτός, “corruptible.” — *frodamma*] “wise,” omitted by the Greek; codex B has *fridamma*. — *aldins aive*] in the manuscript I read *ald . . . dins aive*; but the first *d* has faded, and still more so the letters standing between the two *d*s. It therefore appears that the scribe wrote the letters *dins* twice and then erased them once. CASTIGLIONE. Perhaps *allos aldins aive* was also written, as at Ephesians III.21; in this way the Gothic translator often expands one parallel passage from another.]

This command I entrust to you, child Timothy, in accordance with the earlier prophecies concerning you, that by them you may wage the good warfare, [Note: [Col. 0837] This command I entrust to you, child Timothy, according to the earlier prophecies concerning you, that by them you may wage the good warfare,] [Note: [Col. 0837] *faura*] “earlier,” superfluous and omitted by all Greek manuscripts. Codex A continues from here.]

holding faith and a good conscience. Certain persons, having rejected these, have suffered shipwreck concerning the faith. Among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I handed over to Satan so that they may learn not to blaspheme. [Note: [Col. 0837] holding faith and a good conscience, which certain persons have rejected and suffered shipwreck concerning the faith; among them are Hymenaeus and Alexander, whom I handed over to Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.]

I urge, then, first of all, that prayers, petitions, intercessions, thanksgivings be made for all people, [Note: [Col. 0837] I urge, then, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercessions, thanksgivings be made for all people;] [Note: [Col. 0837] *frumist*] Castiglione adds *fkumist.*]

for kings and all who are in high position, that we may live a quiet and tranquil life in all godliness and dignity. [Note: [Col. 0837] for kings and all those who are in high position, that we may lead a quiet and tranquil life in all godliness and chastity.] [Note: [Col. 0837] *fram*] the second occurrence, “for,” is omitted by all Greek manuscripts. — *jah sutjat*] codex A has *jas-sutja*. — *sutja los*] Castiglione says that it seems to be written thus, as two words, in both codices. Those who, with us, write them separately should neither treat *slavandein* as a substantive—without any authority for doing so—nor regard *sutjalos* as an unusual adverb and, moreover, a wholly superfluous comparative. [Col. 0838]]

For this is good and acceptable before God our Savior, [Note: [Col. 0837] For this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our Savior,] [Note: [Col. 0838] *ïst*] “is,” omitted by all Greek manuscripts.]

who wills all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of truth. [Note: [Col. 0837] who wills all people to be saved and to come to the knowledge of truth.] [Note: [Col. 0838] *ïn*] “to”; omitted by codex B; supplied from codex A.]

For there is one God, and one mediator between God and human beings, the human being Christ Jesus, [Note: [Col. 0837] For there is one God, and one mediator of God and human beings, the human being Christ Jesus,] who gave himself [Note: [Col. 0837] who gave himself as a ransom for all, the testimony at its proper times;] [Note: [Col. 0838] *andabaht*] thus in both codices, where one would expect *andabauht*, as Massmann already judged in the Skeireins Glossary, p. 125, and Castiglione agrees here. Compare *faurbauhts*, Ephesians I.7 and Colossians I.14. If *andbaht* had been written instead of *andabaht*, we would not hesitate to approve the reading of the codices; for Christ can also be said to have given himself as a minister for many.]

as a ransom for all, the testimony at the proper times. For this I was appointed herald and apostle—I speak the truth in Christ; I do not lie—a teacher of the nations in faith and truth. [Note: [Col. 0837] for which I was appointed a herald and apostle; I speak the truth in Christ, I do not lie; a teacher of the Gentiles in faith and truth.] [Note: [Col. 0838] *ïn xristau*] “in Christ,” omitted by the Greek.]

I therefore desire that men pray in every place, lifting up holy hands without anger and disputing. [Note: [Col. 0837] I therefore desire that men pray in every place, lifting up pure hands without anger and disputing;] [Note: [Col. 0838] *vairans bidjan*] “men to pray,” omitted by all Greek manuscripts; compare nevertheless codex d according to Mill.]

Likewise, women should adorn themselves in pure dress, with chastity and modesty, not with braided hair or gold [Note: [Col. 0837] likewise women also, adorning themselves in pure clothing with chastity and modesty, not with braids or gold or pearls or expensive clothing,] [Note: [Col. 0838] *mahein*] Massmann, *Monumenta Germaniae Antiqua*, p. 127, and Grimm, *Grammar* I, p. 40, 3rd ed., correctly observe that *ïnahein* should be read. The same word, which here signifies σωφροσύνη, “self-control,” is used below at II.I.7 for σωφρονισμός; and at Romans XII.16 the translator uses the adjective *ïnahs* for φρόνιμος, “prudent.” — *gulþa*] codex B and Castiglione have *gulþ*; evidently the second *a* dropped out because of the following *aiþþau*; compare John XII.42. Codex A is erased here. — *galubaim*] thus in both codices for the usual *galaubaim*; see Romans IX.21; 1 Corinthians V.23; *filugalaubs*, John XII.3; *ungalaubs*, Romans IX.21. Thus *u* is also inaccurately written for *au* in *diabulus*, and often in verbal endings; see Luke I.54.]

or pearls or costly clothing, but with what is fitting for women who profess to worship God: good works. [Note: [Col. 0837] but with what is fitting for women [Col. 0839] who profess to worship God, through good works.] [Note: [Col. 0838] *blotan*] codex B and Castiglione have *bloþan*; codex A is erased; see Galatians II.11. The same scribe erred in the same word at 2 Corinthians VIII.4; both manuscripts also wrote *þeimaþaius* above, I.2, for *teimauþaius*, and codex A at III.16 has *ïnsahþaba* for *ïnsahtaba.*]

Let a woman learn in silence, in all submission. [Note: [Col. 0839] Let a woman learn in silence, in all submission.] [Note: [Col. 0839] *hauïþa*] Castiglione affirms that this is written in both codices. Yet this unusual word troubled him, and he conjectures *hauniþa*—rather *hauniþai*—“in humility.” But neither codex bears an abbreviation mark, and *hauniþa* seems too far removed from the meaning of the Greek text for us to approve it. Perhaps *ïn hliuþa*, “in hearing,” should be read—that is, “while listening”; compare Gothic *hliuma*, Icelandic *hliodr, hlyda*; Graff IV, p. 1102.]

But I do not permit a woman to teach or to exercise authority over a man, but to be in silence. [Note: [Col. 0839] But I do not permit a woman to teach, nor to exercise authority before a man, but to be in silence.] [Note: [Col. 0839] *galaisjan qinon*] “to teach a woman,” omitted by the Greek. — *faura*] “before”; omitted by all Greek manuscripts. The Gothic translator therefore indicates by the phrase *ni fraujinon faura vaira* that women in assemblies should neither claim authority for themselves nor exercise dominion before men. — *þahainai*] Castiglione edited *þeigainai* from codex B—for codex A is entirely erased here—although he could not distinctly read the *e*. But since among the known Gothic words there is none from which it can properly derive (for who could believe that *þeigains* derives from *þeihan*, and that the translator, so careful where silence is being discussed, used it?), the same objection applies to *þageinai*, conjectured by Massmann, cited work, p. 127. We therefore did not hesitate to place our conjecture in the text; *þahains* derives from *þahan* (σιγᾶν, σιωπᾶν, φιμοῦσθαι: “to be silent, to keep silence, to be muzzled”).]

For Adam was formed first, then Eve. [Note: [Col. 0839] For Adam was formed first, then Eve.] [Note: [Col. 0839] *gadigans*] codex B has *gadigands*; codex A is obliterated; see I.3.]

And Adam was not deceived, but the woman, having been deceived, came to be in transgression. [Note: [Col. 0839] And Adam was not deceived, but the woman, deceived, came to be in transgression.]

Yet she will be saved through childbearing, if they continue in faith and love and holiness with self-control. [Note: [Col. 0839] Yet she will be saved through the bearing of children, if they remain in faith and love and holiness with modesty.]

Faithful is the saying: if anyone aspires to oversight, he desires a good work. [Note: [Col. 0839] Faithful is the saying: if anyone desires the office of bishop, he desires a good work.]

An overseer, then, must be irreproachable, the husband of one wife, sober, self-controlled, prudent, respectable, hospitable, able to teach, [Note: [Col. 0839] An overseer, then, must be blameless, husband of one wife, sober, chaste, prudent, respectable, hospitable, fit to teach,] [Note: [Col. 0839] *ungafairinonds*] thus the active form in both codices, though *ungafairinoþs* ought to stand, as correctly read at III.10; V.7; VI.14; Titus I.7; and *unfairinodaba* at 1 Thessalonians II.10. Gothic agrees with the Vulgate, which nevertheless places this after κόσμιον.]

not given to wine, not violent, but gentle, pious, not quarrelsome, not a lover of money; [Note: [Col. 0839] not a drunkard, not a striker, but gentle, pious, not contentious, not avaricious,] [Note: [Col. 0839] *airknis*] “pious”; omitted by all Greek manuscripts. To those who prefer *airkns* to *airknis*, Castiglione replies that the word as edited is doubtful in both codices, but seems to rest upon *is*. — *sakjis*] Castiglione edited *sakjas*; but after reexamining the manuscript he says that the place is indeed erased, yet *sakjis* can be read.]

managing his own household well, having children in all submission. [Note: [Col. 0839] managing his own house well, having children in obedience with all dignity.] [Note: [Col. 0839] *fauragaggands*] thus correctly codex A; *fauragaggans*, [Col. 0840] which codex B gives, is the same error noted above at I.3, and cannot be defended as Castiglione thinks, since the participle *gaggans* is quite different. — *ufhausjandona*] codex B ends here. — *anaviljein*] codex A has *anaviljin*; see I.4.]

But if someone does not know how to manage his own household, how will he care for the church of God? [Note: [Col. 0839] But if someone cannot manage his own house, how will he care for the church of God?]

He must not be newly planted, lest, becoming puffed up, he fall into the judgment of the devil. [Note: [Col. 0839] Nor newly planted, lest perhaps, lifted up, he fall into the judgment of Satan.] [Note: [Col. 0840] *niujan satidana*] since *skal visan* preceded, the Gothic translator should have written *niuja satiþs*, in the nominative case. But the translator often, following the authority of the Greek text, departed from correct construction. Thus also in verse 8 *diakaunjus* should have been written instead of *diakaununs*, and at V.1–2 datives stand for accusatives. Codex A has *satidina*. The translator rendered νεόφυτος more precisely as *niuja satiþs*, “newly planted,” since the Greek does not properly mean one recently planted but someone very recently admitted to the Christian congregation. — *staua*] this is what should be read. Castiglione, unable to read this word in the manuscript, wrongly edited *stauai*, which the order of words does not permit; see verse 7, *atdriusai ïn ïdveit.*]

Moreover, he must have a good testimony from those outside, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil. [Note: [Col. 0839] For he must have a good testimony from those outside, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of Satan.] [Note: [Col. 0840] *atdriusai ïn ïdveit*] “fall into reproach”; omitted by all Greek manuscripts.]

And likewise deacons must be chaste, not avaricious, not devoted to much wine, not greedy for shameful gain, [Note: [Col. 0839] And likewise deacons, chaste, not avaricious, not attached to much wine, not seeking shameful gain;] [Note: [Col. 0840] *jah*] “and,” omitted by the Greek. — *sva diakaununs*] “thus, deacons”; omitted by all Greek manuscripts. On *diakaununs* in the accusative, where the nominative was required, see verse 6. — *faihufrikans*] “avaricious”; all Greek manuscripts have διλόγους, “double-tongued.” — *veina filu*] it should be noted that the Gothic translator uses a different construction: *veina* does not depend on *filu*, as in the Greek, but on *haftjandans*. Similarly, below, V.23, he translates οἴνῳ ὀλίγῳ χρῷ, “use a little wine,” by *veinis leitil brukjais*; and 2 Timothy II.16, ἐπὶ πλεῖον προκόψουσιν ἀσεβείας, “they will advance further into ungodliness,” by *filu gaggand du afgudein*. For *filu* and *leitil* are adverbs, and consequently the substantives in these places depend on the verbs.]

holding the mystery of faith in a pure conscience. [Note: [Col. 0839] holding the mystery of faith in a pure conscience.] [Note: [Col. 0840] *hrainjai*] Castiglione adds *hrainjon*; see II.I.3; no trace of letters remains in the manuscript.]

These also must first be tested; then let them serve, being irreproachable. [Note: [Col. 0839] And let these first be tested, and then serve, being irreproachable.] [Note: [Col. 0840] *jas-sva*] “and then”; Greek εἶτα. — *visandans*] codex A has it written twice; see 2 Corinthians X.12.]

Women likewise must be dignified, not slanderers, sober, faithful in everything. [Note: [Col. 0839] Women likewise, chaste, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things.] [Note: [Col. 0840] *gafaurjos*] in the margin of codex A, *an..þ . . . . .*, undoubtedly *andaþahtos*. CASTIGLIONE. Correctly so; see verse 2.]

Let deacons be husbands of one wife, managing their children and their own households well. [Note: [Col. 0839] Let deacons be husbands of one wife, taking good care of children and their own houses.]

For those who serve well acquire a good standing [Note: [Col. 0841] and much confidence in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.] [Note: [Col. 0840] *grid*] Gothic omits ἑαυτοῖς, “for themselves.” — *galaubeinai*] “faith”; all Greek manuscripts have ἐν πίστει, “in faith,” which the Gothic translator omits. More probably, however, the scribe omitted *ïn*, whose letters are identical with those on which the preceding *balþein* rests. Massmann likewise judges this, cited work, p. 138; see I.5.]

and much confidence in the faith in Christ Jesus.

I write these things to you, hoping to come to you soon; [Note: [Col. 0841] I write these things to you, hoping to come to you soon;] but if I delay, so that you may know how one ought to conduct oneself in God’s household, which is the church of the living God, the pillar and foundation of the truth. [Note: [Col. 0841] but if I delay, that you may know how one ought to conduct oneself in the house of God, which is the church of the living God, pillar and foundation of the truth.] [Note: [Col. 0841] *usmitan*] thus codex A; Castiglione has *usmetan.*]

And undeniably great is the mystery of godliness: he who was manifested in flesh, vindicated in spirit, seen by angels, proclaimed among [Note: [Col. 0841] And undeniably great is the mystery of godliness: he was manifested in flesh, justified in spirit, seen by angels, proclaimed among the nations, believed in in the world, received up in glory.] [Note: [Col. 0841] *unsahtaba*] codex A has *unsahþaba*; see II.10. — *saei*] Castiglione, who in his critical discussion on Philippians, p. 63, had affirmed that *guþ*, “God,” was to be read here, after straining his eyes and repeatedly treating the parchment with acids and soap, eventually perceived faint strokes of *soei*; see his work on Timothy, p. 62 ff. But if the Gothic translator had truly written this, he would have had in his manuscript the reading μυστήριον ὃ ἐφανερώθη, “the mystery which was manifested.” Since, however, he says *gabairhtiþs varþ—garaihts gadomiþs varþ*, and so forth, he cannot have written *soei* referring to *runa*, “mystery,” but without doubt wrote *saei*, which suits both the preceding *mikils*, “great,” and the following participles. We were not overly bold in writing *saei*, since Castiglione himself later admits that the place is wholly erased.]

the nations, believed in in the world, received up in glory.

Grimm, *Grammar* I, p. 59, 3rd ed., considers the edited reading a scribal error for *speidistaim*. — *dagam*] “days”; all Greek manuscripts have καιροῖς, “times.” — *airziþos*] “of error”; Greek πλάνοις. who forbid marriage and require abstinence from foods that God created to be received with thanksgiving by believers and those who know the truth. [Note: [Col. 0841] By placing these things before the brothers, you will be a good minister of Christ Jesus, nourished by the words of faith and good teaching, which you have followed.] [Note: [Col. 0841] *xristaus ïesuis*] omitted by the Greek. — *alands*] thus codex B; codex A is erased. Castiglione believes that the Gothic translator used an active participle because he mistakenly took ἐντρεφόμενος for an active form. Massmann, cited work, p. 140, thinks the scribe wrote *alands* for *alans* through a frequent interchange; see I.I.3. Neither opinion pleases us. Rather, this is a form of *alan*, “to grow, be nourished” (Grimm, *Grammar* [Col. 0842] II, p. 8), whose participle is *alands*; from it is formed the transitive *aljan*, “to feed, nourish.”]

But reject profane, old-womanish fables; rather train yourself for godliness. Among the ancient Germans, similarly, *ar-* or *iralten* produces *ar-* or *iraltet*, “an old woman, aged person”; see Graff I, p. 200 ff. Compare *usvahsans* (ἡλικίαν ἔχων, “being of age”) at John IX.21. We are surprised that Castiglione, who writes *us alþanaizo* separately, did not see that this construction is solecistic. Massmann, cited work, p. 131, noticed it and, to avoid violating the rules of the language, attempts to connect *us*, as wrongly placed by the scribe, with *þroþei*. But those who accept this ingenious conjecture must prove that simple *alþana* can mean γραῦς, “old woman.” Grimm, *Grammar* I, p. 41, 3rd ed., likewise reads *usalþanaizo*. — *ïþ*] codex B omits it; or rather, the scribe wrote *bivandeiþroþei* for *bivandeiïþþroþei*, as at 1 Corinthians XIII.12. Since all Greek manuscripts have μετὰ ἐπιθέσεως, “with the laying on,” he should have translated *miþ analageinai*. — *praizbytaireis*] “of the presbyter”; all Greek manuscripts have πρεσβυτερίου, “of the presbyterate,” except the Leicester manuscript, which has πρεσβυτέρου, “of the presbyter,” with which Gothic agrees. Castiglione has *ïnuþþan*, and moreover thinks that *ïn* is compounded with *visan*, so that the verb *ïnvisan* governs the genitive *þize*. [Note: [Col. 0843] But if any widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to show piety toward their own household and to repay their parents; for this is good and acceptable before God.] [Note: [Col. 0843] *galaisjaina*] codex A continues. — *sik*] omitted by codex B; supplied from codex A, for μανθάνειν is *laisjan sik*, “to learn”; see II.11; V.13.]

II, III, 14; Phil. 4:9, 11. *Skeireins* 45:7.—*barusnian*] The meaning of this word, whose reading is beyond doubt in both codices, seems to have been wholly unknown to learned men. Castiglione says that here it is derived from *beruseis* and has the sense of governing; but what has the notion of governing in common with εἰσεβεῖν [“to act piously”], which the text has, and what does management of a household have to do with children? Massmann, to whom Castiglione’s interpretation rightly does not appeal, pp. 130 and 179, thinks that *barusnjan* is derived from *BARU*, to be referred to *paro* (“wood”), *parawari* (“priest”), and other such words, and means “to cultivate, to worship”; but this too does not suit the sense of our passage. Rather, it appears to us to be derived from the same root as *barn* (“child”) and to mean: “to care for in the manner of children, as children are accustomed to do,” which corresponds most aptly to the Greek εὐσεβεῖν, “to act piously.”—*god jah*] “good and,” omitted by codex A together with the Greek.

“If any widow has children or grandchildren, let them first learn to care piously for their own household and to render recompense to their parents; for this is good and acceptable in the sight of God.”

“But younger widows [lacuna]”

“[lacuna] they have made the faith void.”

[Note: Col. 0843] “And at the same time they learn also to be idle, going about from house to house; and not merely idle, but also—”

“—garrulous and meddlesome, speaking things which are not proper.”

[Note: Col. 0844] *fairveitjandeins*] After the first syllable of this word, quire XLI of codex A ends and quire XLIV begins, [Col. 0845] in which all writing has been erased. “But younger widows [lacuna] have made the faith void. But at the same time they also learn to be idle, going about the houses; and not merely idle, but also chatterers and busybodies, speaking improper things.”
