**GAIUS**, masculine proper name, Γάϊος, “Gaius”: Romans XVI.23; 1 Corinthians I.14.

**GAIRGAISAINUS**, masculine proper name, Γεργεσηνός, “Gergesene”: Matthew VIII.28.

**GAIRDAN** (Old Norse *girda, giörd*; Old Saxon *gurdian*; Anglo-Saxon *gyrdan*; Old High German *kurtil*; Old Frisian *gerdel*; English *girdle*; Swedish *gorael*; Danish *gjorde, gyrdel*; Dutch *gordel*; Modern High German *Gürtel*; Gr. II, 38; III, 449; Gf. IV, 248 ff.; Rchth. 774), first conjugation, *gard, gaurdun, gaurdans*, to gird.

**BI-GAIRDAN**, to gird about, περιζωννύναι: Luke XVII.8.

**UF-GAIRDAN**, the same: Ephesians VI.14.

**GAIRDA**, feminine, belt, girdle, ζωνή: Matthew I.6; VI.8.

**GAIRNEI**, see under **Geiran**.

**GAIRNJAN**, see under **Geiran**.

**GAIRU** (Castilian Glossary on Corinthians, at this word; Gr. III, 442), neuter, goad (French *une discipline*), σκόλοψ, “thorn”: 2 Corinthians XII.7, in this place.

**GAISJAN**, see under **Geisan**.

**GAITEI** (Old Norse *geit*; Anglo-Saxon *gat*; Old High German *keiz*; English *goat*; Danish *geed*; Dutch *geyt*; Modern High German *Geiss*; compare Latin *hoedus*; Gr. III, 327, 338; Gf. IV, 286), feminine, she-goat, ἔριφος: Luke XV.29.

**GAITSA**, feminine, goat, kid, χίμαρος: Nehemiah V.18, in this place.

**GALATIA**, proper name, Γαλατία, “Galatia”: 1 Corinthians XVI.1; Galatians I.2; 2 Timothy IV.10.

**GALATIUS**, masculine, Γαλάτης, “Galatian”: 1 Corinthians XVI.1, in this place.

**GALATUS**, the same: superscription of Galatians and III.1.

**GALGA** (Old Norse *galgi*; Old High German, Old Saxon *galgo*; Anglo-Saxon; Old Frisian *galga*; English *gallows*; Swedish, Danish, Dutch *galge*; Modern High German *Galgen*; Gf. IV, 185; Rchth. 772), masculine, cross, σταυρός: Matthew X.38; XXVII.42; Mark VIII.34; X.21; XV.21, 30, 32; Luke IX.23; XIV.27; 1 Corinthians I.17, 18; Galatians V.11; VI.12, 14; Ephesians II.16; Philippians III.18; Colossians I.20; II.14.

**GALEILAIA**, proper name, Γαλιλαία, “Galilee”: Matthew XXVII.55; Mark I.9, 14, 28, 39; III.7; VI.21; IX.30; XV.41; Luke II.39; III.1; IV.14, 31, 44; V.17; VIII.26; XVII.11; John VII.1, 41.

**GALEILAIUS**, masculine, Γαλιλαῖος, “Galilean”: Matthew XXVI.69; Mark VII.31; John VI.1.

**GANSJAN** (Castilian [Glossary] on Galatians VI.17; Old High German *ganzen*; Gf. IV, 222), second conjugation, to provide, furnish, παρέχειν: Galatians VI.17.

**GAU** (that is, *ga-u*), a particle formed from *ga* and the interrogative *u*, which is inserted between it and the compounded word; see under *u* and at Matthew IX.28.

**GAULGAUþA**, proper name, Γολγοθᾶ, “Golgotha”: Mark XV.22.

**GAUMAURRA**, proper name, Γόμορρα, “Gomorrah”: Romans IX.29.

**GAUMAURUS**, masculine, Γόμορρος, “Gomorrah”: Mark VI.11.

**GAUMJAN** (Old Norse *gaumr*; Old Saxon *gomian*; Anglo-Saxon *gyman*; English *gaum*; Gr. II, 47; Gf. IV, 201, 205), second conjugation, to see, perceive, ὁρᾶν: Matthew IX.11; Mark IV.12; Luke V.8; XVII.14, 15; John IX.1; βλέπειν, “to see”: Luke VI.41, 42; διαβλέπειν, “to see clearly”: Luke VI.42; θεᾶσθαι, “to behold”: John VI.5; θεωρεῖν, “to observe”: Mark XVI.4; κατανοεῖν, “to notice”: Luke VI.41; προσέχειν, “to attend to”: 1 Timothy IV.13; Skeir. VII.d; in the passive, “to be seen, appear,” φαίνεσθαι: Matthew VI.5.

**GAUNON** (Anglo-Saxon *geong*; compare Greek γοᾷν, “to lament”; second conjugation), to lament, mourn, πενθεῖν: Luke VI.25; θρηνεῖν: Luke VII.32; John XVI.20.

**GAUNOþA**, feminine, lamentation, mourning, ὀδυρμός: 2 Corinthians VII.7.

**GAUJA**, see under **Gavi**.

**GAURS** (Old Saxon *gornon*; Old High German *gor*; compare Greek γοργός, “fierce”; Gr. II, 57; Gf. IV, 237), adjective, sad, sorrowful, σκυθρωπός: Matthew VI.16; λυπούμενος, “grieved”: Mark X.22; συλλυπούμενος, “grieved with”: Mark III.5; περίλυπος, “deeply grieved”: Mark VI.26; Luke XVIII.23, 24.

[Col. 1286] **GAURIþA**, feminine, grief, mourning, sorrow, λύπη: John XVI.6.

**GAUREI**, feminine, the same: Philippians II.27.

**GAURJAN**, second conjugation, to grieve, make sorrowful, λυπεῖν: Romans XIV.15; 2 Corinthians II.2, 5; VII.8, 9; Ephesians IV.30.

**GARDS** (Old Norse *garðr*; Old Saxon *gard*; Anglo-Saxon *geard*; Old High German *gart*; Old Frisian *garda*; English *yard*; Swedish *garder, gärda, gård*; Danish *gaard*; compare **Gairdan**; compare Old High German *karto*, English *garden*, Modern High German *Garten*, Latin *hortus*; Gr. II, 39; III, 426; Gf. IV, 249; Rchth. 773), masculine (plural *gardeis*), house, household, family, race, οἶκος: Matthew IX.6, 7; XI.8; Mark II.1, 11, 26; III.20; V.19, 38; VII.17, 30; VIII.3, 26; IX.28; Luke I.23, 27, 33, 40, 56, 69; II.4; V.24, 25; VI.4; VII.10; VIII.39, 41; IX.61; X.5; XIV.23; XV.6; XVI.4; XVIII.14; XIX.5, 7, 9, 46; John XI.20; 1 Timothy III.4, 12, 15; V.4; 2 Timothy I.6; Titus I.11; οἰκία, “house”: Matthew VIII.6, 14; IX.10, 23; Mark I.29; II.15; III.25, 27; VI.4, 10; VII.24; IX.33; X.10, 29, 30; Luke IV.38; V.29; VII.6, 36, 44; VIII.27, 51; IX.4; X.5, 7; XVIII.29; John VIII.35; XI.31; XII.3; XIV.2; 1 Corinthians XI.22; XVI.15; 2 Corinthians V.1; 1 Timothy III.4, 5, 12, 15; V.4, 13; 2 Timothy II.20; III.6; αὐλή, “court”: Mark XIV.54; XV.16; *faur gard*, “into the forecourt,” εἰς προαύλιον: Mark XIV.68. *Garda valdands*, see under **Valdan**.

**AURTI-GARDS**, garden, κῆπος: John XVIII.1, 26.

**MIDJUN-GARDS** (Gr. III, 393; DM. 458), inhabited world, οἰκουμένη: Luke II.1; IV.5; Romans X.18; Skeir. IV.b.

**VEINA-GARDS**, vineyard, ἀμπελών: Mark XII.1, 8, 9; Luke XX.9, 10, 13, 15, 16.

**ÏN-GARDIS**, adjective, resident, domestic, “at home,” ὁ κατ’ οἶκον: 1 Corinthians XVI.19; Colossians IV.15.

**ÏN-GARDJA**, masculine, member of the household, οἰκεῖος: Ephesians II.19; 1 Timothy V.8.

**þIUDAN-GARDI**, feminine, 1) royal palace, royal residence, βασιλεῖον: Luke VII.25; 2) kingdom, βασιλεία: Matthew V.19, 20; VI.13; VII.21; VIII.11, 12; IX.35; XI.11, 12; Mark I.14, 15; III.24; IV.11; VI.23; X.14, 15, 23, 24, 25; XI.10; XII.34; XV.43; Luke IV.43; VI.20; VII.28; VIII.1; IX.2, 11, 27, 60, 62; X.9; XIV.15; XVI.16; XVII.20, 21; XVIII.16, 17, 24, 25, 29; XIX.11, 12, 15; John III.3, 5; XVIII.36; Romans XIV.17; Galatians V.21; Ephesians V.5; Colossians I.13; IV.11; 1 Thessalonians II.12; 2 Thessalonians I.5; Skeir. II.a; III.c.

**GARDA**, masculine, court, αὐλή: John X.1.

**MIþ-GARDA-VADDJUS**, see under **Vaddjus**.

**GASTS** (Old Norse *gestr*; Anglo-Saxon *gest*; English *guest, host*; Swedish *gäst*; Danish *gjæst*; Old Saxon, Dutch, Modern High German *Gast*; Latin *hostis*; DRA. 396; Gf. IV, 268), masculine (plural *gasteis*), stranger, guest, ξένος: Matthew XXV.38, 43; XXVII.7; Ephesians II.12, 19. *Gastins andniman*, “to receive a stranger,” to practise hospitality, ξενοδοχεῖν: 1 Timothy V.10.

**GASTI-GODS**, see under **Gods**.

**GATVO** (Old Norse and Swedish *gata*; Old Saxon, Old Frisian *gat*; Anglo-Saxon *geat*; Old High German *gaza*; English *gate*; Danish *gade*; Dutch *gatte*; Modern High German *Gasse*; Bopp 122; Gr. II, 25; III, 396; Gf. IV, 105; Rchth. 847, under *Iet*; compare **Gaggan**), feminine, street, πλατεῖα: Luke XIV.21.

**GAVI** (Old High German *kouwi*; Old Saxon *ga*; Old Frisian *go*; Modern High German *Gau*; Gr. III, 395; DRA. 496; Gf. IV, 274; Rchth. 771), neuter, land, region, χώρα: Matthew VIII.28; Luke VIII.26; XV.14, 15; περίχωρος, “surrounding region”: Mark VI.55; *gavi bisitande*, the same: Luke IV.14.

**GAUJA**, masculine, country-dweller; plural *gaujans*, equivalent to *gavi*, περίχωρος, “district around”: Luke III.3; πλῆθος τῆς περιχώρου, “the multitude of the surrounding district”: Luke VIII.37.

**GEIGAN** (*geiggan*, 1 Corinthians IX.20 ff.) (Old Norse *gagn*; Swedish *gagna, gina, gagn*; Danish *gavne*; compare Modern High German *Gauner*), second conjugation, to benefit, bring advantage.

**GA-GEIGAN**, to gain, κερδαίνειν: Mark VIII.36; Luke IX.25; 1 Corinthians IX.19, 20, 21, 22.

**GEIRAN** (Old Norse *giarn, giarnan, girna*; Old Saxon *geron, gernian*; Anglo-Saxon *geornian*; Old High German *giri, geron*; Old Frisian *ieria, girich, ierne*; English *yearn*; Swedish *gerna, gjarna, begära*; Danish *gjerne, gjerrig*; Modern High German *Gier, gern, begehren*; Gr. II, 57; Gf. IV, 225; Rchth. 846), first conjugation, *gair, gairun, gairans*, to seek, desire.

[Col. 1287] **GEIRO**, feminine, desire.

**FAIHU-GEIRO**, feminine, love of possessions, avarice, greed, πλεονεξία: Colossians III.5, in this place; φιλαργυρία, “love of money”: 1 Timothy VI.10.

**FAIHU-GEIRONJAN**, second conjugation, to be covetous or greedy, ἐπιθυμεῖν: Romans XIII.9.

**GAIRUNI**, neuter, passion, πάθος: 1 Thessalonians IV.5.

**GAIRNS**, adjective, desirous, greedy.

**SEINAI-GAIRNS**, self-love, φίλαυτος: 2 Timothy III.2, in this place.

**FAIHU-GAIRNS**, fond of money, φιλάργυρος: 2 Timothy III.2.

**GAIRNEI**, feminine, longing, desire, ἐπιπόθησις: 2 Corinthians VII.7, 11; προθυμία, “readiness, eagerness”: 2 Corinthians VIII.19; XIX.2.

**FAIHU-GAIRNEI**, shameful gain, αἰσχρὸν κέρδος: Titus I.11.

**GAIRNJAN**, second conjugation, to desire, with the genitive or infinitive, ἐπιποθεῖν, “to long for”: 2 Corinthians V.2; IX.14; Philippians II.26; 1 Thessalonians III.6; 2 Timothy I.4; ἐπιθυμεῖν, “to desire”: Luke XV.16; XVI.21; XVII.22; Romans VII.7; Galatians V.17; 1 Timothy III.1; ὀρέγεσθαι, “to aspire”: 1 Timothy III.1; VI.10; θέλειν, “to wish”: Luke VIII.20; χρείαν ἔχειν, “to have need”: Mark XI.3; Luke XIX.31.

**GEISAN** (English *gaster, gast, gastly*; Gr. II, 46; IV, 26; Gf. IV, 266), first conjugation, *gais, gisun, gisans*.

**US-GEISNAN**, third conjugation, to be astonished, amazed, ἐξίστασθαι: Mark II.12; V.42; Luke II.47; VIII.56; 2 Corinthians V.13; ἐκπλήττεσθαι, “to be astounded”: Mark X.26; ἐκθαμβεῖσθαι, “to be alarmed”: Mark IX.15; XVI.5.

**US-GAISJAN**, to cause astonishment, drive out of one’s mind, ἐξιστάναι: Mark III.21.

**GEPANTA**, sluggish, slow, indolent. Jordanes, p. 98, Lindenbrog: “At the beginning the Goths went forth from the womb of the island of Scanzia with their king Berich, carried in only three ships to the shore of the nearer Ocean. One of these three ships, being conveyed more slowly, as often happens, is said to have given its name to the people, namely the Gepids; for in their language *gepanta* means ‘sluggish.’”

**GIBAN** (Old Norse *gefa, giöf, giöft*; Old Saxon *geban*; Anglo-Saxon *gifan*; Old High German *geban*; Old Frisian *iéva*; English *give*; Swedish *gifva, gift*; Danish *give, gave*; Dutch *geven*; Modern High German *geben, Gabe*—English *gift*; Gr. II, 24; Gf. IV, 108; Rchth. 847), first conjugation, *gaf, gebun, gibans*: to give, διδόναι: Matthew V.31, 42; VI.11; IX.8; XXV.42; Mark II.26; IV.7, 8, 25; V.43; VI.2, 22, 23, 25; VIII.37; X.21, 40, 45; XII.9, 14; XIII.22, 24; XIV.5, 11; XV.23; Luke I.32, 71, 73, 77; II.24; IV.6; VI.4, 30, 38; VII.44; VIII.18, 55; IX.13, 16; XV.12, 16, 22; XVI.12; XVII.18; XVIII.43; XIX.24, 26; XX.2, 10, 16, 22; John VI.27, 31, 32, 33, 34, 37, 51, 52; VII.19; IX.24; X.28; XI.22; XIII.29, 34; XIV.16, 27; XV.16; XVII.2, 22, 24; XVIII.11, 22; XIX.9; Romans XII.3, 19; XV.5; 1 Corinthians VII.25; XV.57; 2 Corinthians I.22; V.5, 12, 18; VI.3; VIII.1, 10, 16; IX.9; Galatians I.4; II.9; Ephesians I.17; III.2, 7, 16; IV.11, 27, 29; VI.19; Colossians I.25; 1 Thessalonians IV.8; 2 Thessalonians I.8; III.9, 16; 1 Timothy II.6; IV.14; 2 Timothy I.7, 9, 16, 18; II.6, 25; ἐπιδιδόναι, “to give over”: John XIII.26; ἀποδιδόναι, “to render”: Matthew XXVII.58; Luke XX.25; μεταδιδόναι, “to share”: Luke III.11. *Fruma giban*, “to give beforehand, betray,” προδιδόναι: XI.35.

**GIBANDS**, participle used substantivally, giver, δότης: 2 Corinthians IX.7.

**AT-GIBAN**, to give, deliver, διδόναι: Matthew XXVII.10; Mark IV.10; VI.28; VIII.6; XI.28; XIV.44; Luke VII.15; VIII.10; IX.1, 42; X.19; XV.29; XIX.13, 15; John V.22, 36; VI.65; VII.22; XIII.15; XVII.2, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 14, 24; XVIII.9; XIX.11; 2 Corinthians VIII.5; X.8; XII.7; Galatians II.9; IV.15; Ephesians I.22; III.8; IV.7, 8; 1 Thessalonians IV.2; 2 Thessalonians II.16; ἐπιδιδόναι, “to give over”: Luke IV.7; παραδιδόναι, “to hand over”: Matthew V.25; XXVI.2; XXVII.18; Mark I.14; IV.29; IX.31; X.33; XV.

[Col. 1288] 10, 15; Luke IV.6; IX.44; X.22; XVIII.32; XX.20; John XVIII.30; XIX.11; 1 Corinthians V.5; XIII.3; XV.3; 2 Corinthians IV.11; Galatians II.20; Ephesians IV.19; V.2, 25 (1 Thessalonians IV.2); Skeir. VI.a.

**AF-GIBAN**, to withdraw; *afgiban sik*, to remove oneself, withdraw, χωρίζεσθαι: Philemon 15.

**US-GIBAN**, to give, furnish, render, ἀποδιδόναι: Matthew V.26, 33; VI.4, 18; Mark XII.17; Luke IV.20; VII.42; XVI.2; XX.25; Romans XII.17; XIV.12; 1 Timothy V.4; 2 Timothy IV.8; Philemon 19 (for the Gothic writer here probably read ἀποδώσω, “I shall repay,” with the manuscripts, instead of ἀποτίσω, “I shall pay”); Skeir. V.d; παριστάναι, “to present”: Romans XII.1; 2 Corinthians XI.2, in this place; 2 Timothy II.15.

**FRA-GIBAN**, 1) to give, grant, bestow, χαρίζεσθαι: Luke VII.21; Philippians I.29; Philemon 22; δωρεῖσθαι, “to grant”: Mark XV.45; διδόναι: Mark X.37; John X.29; 2 Corinthians XIII.10; παρέχεσθαι, “to provide”: Luke VII.4; Skeir. III.c; V.c; VII.b; 2) to forgive, spare, χαρίζεσθαι: Luke VII.42; 2 Corinthians II.7, 10; XII.13; Ephesians IV.32; Colossians II.13; III.13.

**GIBA**, feminine, gift, endowment, δόσις: Philippians IV.15; δόμα: Ephesians IV.8; Philippians IV.17; δῶρον: Matthew V.24; VIII.4; Ephesians II.8; δωρεά: 2 Corinthians IX.15; Ephesians III.7; IV.7; χάρισμα: Romans XI.29; 1 Corinthians VII.7; 2 Corinthians I.11.

**FRA-GIFTS** (*fragibts*, Luke I.27), feminine, gift, grant, betrothal; Skeir. III.c. *ïn fragiftim* (namely, *visandei*), “in betrothal,” “betrothed,” μεμνηστευμένη: Luke I.27; II.5.

**GABEI**, feminine, riches, πλοῦτος: Mark IV.19; Luke VIII.14; Romans IX.25; XI.12, 15, 33; 2 Corinthians VIII.2; Ephesians I.7, 18; II.7; III.8, 16; Colossians I.27. But if at Romans XI.15 it is used for καταλλαγή, “reconciliation,” this is merely an error, and indeed one to be attributed to scribal negligence.

**GABIGS** (*gabeigs*, Luke VI.24; XIV.12; XVI.1, 21, 22; XVIII.23; Ephesians II.4), adjective, rich, πλούσιος: Matthew XXVII.57; Mark X.25; Luke VI.24; XIV.12; XVI.1, 19, 21, 22; XVIII.23, 25; XIX.2; 2 Corinthians VIII.9; Ephesians II.4; πλουτῶν, “being rich”: Romans X.12. *Gabigs vairþan*, “to become rich,” πλουτεῖν: 1 Corinthians IV.8; 2 Corinthians VIII.9; 1 Timothy VI.9.

**GABIGABA**, adverb, richly, πλουσίως: Colossians III.16.

**GABIGJAN**, second conjugation, to enrich, πλουτίζειν: 2 Corinthians VI.10.

**GABIGNAN**, third conjugation, to be rich, πλουτεῖν: Luke I.53; πλουτίζεσθαι, “to be enriched”: 2 Corinthians IX.11.

**GIBLA** (Old Norse *gafl*; Old High German *gibil*; Middle High German *gebel*; English *gable*; Danish *gavl*; Dutch *gevel*; Modern High German *Giebel, Gipfel*; Gr. III, 399; Gf. IV, 128), masculine, pinnacle, highest point of a roof, πτερύγιον: Luke IV.9.

**GILDAN** (Old Norse *gilda, giald, gialda*; Old Saxon and Anglo-Saxon *gyldan*; Old High German *geltan*; Old Frisian *ielda, gelda*; English *yield*; Swedish *giald, gild, gälla*; Danish *gjæld, gjælde*; Modern High German *gelten, Geld*; Gr. II, 33; DM. 24; Gf. IV, 185; Rchth. 842), first conjugation, *gald, guldun, guldans*, to be worth.

**US-GILDAN**, to repay, ἀποδιδόναι: 1 Thessalonians V.15; 2 Timothy IV.14; ἀνταποδιδόναι, “to repay in return”: Luke XIV.12, 14; 1 Thessalonians III.9; 2 Thessalonians I.6.

**FRA-GILDAN**, the same, ἀποδιδόναι: Luke XIX.8; ἀνταποδιδόναι: Romans XI.35; XII.19.

**GILD**, neuter, tax, tribute, φόρος: Luke XX.22.

**KAISARA-GILD**, Caesar’s tax, κῆνσος: Mark XII.14.

**GILSTR** (Old High German *gelstar*; Gf. IV, 194; DRA. 358; hence Wachter is not to be heeded, who in *Gloss.* V, *Gilde*, p. 587, proposes that *gildameleins* should be read for *gilstrameleins*), neuter, tax, tribute, φόρος: Romans XIII.6.

**GILSTRA-MELEINS**, see under **Mel**.

**GILþA** (Old Norse *gelda*; Anglo-Saxon *gylte*; English *geld*; Swedish *gälda*; Danish *gilde*; compare Modern High German *gelden*; Gr. III, 416), feminine, sickle, δρέπανον: Mark IV.29.

**GILSTR**, see under **Gildan**.

[Col. 1289] **GINNAN** (Old High German *ïn-* and *biginnan*; Old Saxon *biginnan*; Anglo-Saxon *beginnan*; Old
Old Frisian *biienna*, English *begin*, Swedish *begynna*, Danish *begynde*, Modern High German *beginnen*; Gr. II, 34; Gf. IV, 208; Rchth. 638), conjugation I, *gann, gunnun, gunnans*; to begin. **DU-GINNAN**, to begin, commence, **ἄρχεσθαι** (“to begin”): Matt. 11:7, 20; 26:74; Mark 1:45; 2:23; 4:1; 5:20; 6:2, 7, 55; 8:11, 31, 32; 10:28, 32, 41, 47; 11:15; 12:1; 14:65, 69, 71, 72; 15:8, 18; Luke 3:8; 4:21; 5:21; 7:15, 24, 38, 49; 9:12; 14:18, 29; 15:14, 24; 19:37, 45; 20:9; 2 Cor. 3:1; **προενάρχεσθαι** (“to begin beforehand”): 2 Cor. 13:10; **ἐπιχειρεῖν** (“to undertake”): Luke 1:1. It is also used to circumscribe the future: Luke 6:25; Phil. 1:18.

**GIUTAN** (Old Norse *giota*, Old Saxon *giotan*, Anglo-Saxon *geotan*, Old High German *giuzan*, Old French *giata*, English *gush*, Swedish *gjuta*, Danish *gyde*, Modern High German *giessen*, Latin *gutta*, Greek **χέω, χεύσω**, “pour”; Gr. II, 19; Gf. IV, 281; Rchth. 776), conjugation I, *gaut, gutun, gutans*; to pour, **βάλλειν** (“to cast”): Matt. 9:17; Mark 2:22; Luke 5:37–38. **UFAR-GIUTAN**, to pour over, **ὑπερεκχύνειν**: Luke 6:38. **US-GUTNAN**, conjugation III, to flow out, be poured out, **ἐκχεῖσθαι**: Matt. 9:17; Mark 2:22; Luke 5:37.

**GISTRA** (Old Norse *gär*, Anglo-Saxon *gistran, gyrstan daeg*, English *yesterday*, Old High German *gestar*, Modern High German *gestern*; cf. Swedish *i går, gårdag*, Danish *i gaar*; Greek **χθές**, Latin *heri, hesternus*; Bopp 81; Gf. IV, 273), adverb: yesterday. **GISTRA-DAGIS**, see under **Dags**.

**GITAN** (Old Norse *geta*, Old French *gata*, Anglo-Saxon *getan*, Old Saxon *bigetan*, Old High German *gezan*, English *get*, Modern High German *gattern*; Gr. II, 25; Gf. IV, 276; Rchth. 775), conjugation I, *gat, getun, gitans*; to receive, obtain, attain. **BI-GITAN**, to find, **εὑρίσκειν**: Matt. 7:14; 8:10; 10:39; Mark 1:37; 7:30; 11:2, 4, 13; 14:55; Luke 1:30; 2:12, 45–46; 4:17; 5:19; 6:7; 7:9–10; 8:35; 9:36; 15:4–6, 8–9, 24, 32; 17:18; 18:8; 19:48; John 6:25; 7:34–35; 9:35; 10:9; 11:17; 12:14; 14:30; 18:38; 19:4, 30, 32; Rom. 7:10, 18, 21; 10:20; 1 Cor. 4:2; 15:15 (*bi---gitan*); 2 Cor. 2:12; 5:3; 9:4; 11:12; 12:20; Gal. 2:17; Phil. 2:7; 3:9; 2 Tim. 1:17–18; *Skeir.* VII, c; **ἀνευρίσκειν** (“find after searching”): Luke 2:16.

**GLAGGVUS** (Old Norse *glöggr*, Old Saxon *glau*, Anglo-Saxon *gleav*, Old High German *glaw*, Modern High German *glau*; Gf. IV, 294), adjective: circumspect, prudent, attentive. **GLAGGVUBA** (*glaggvaba*, Luke 15:8), adverb: prudently, **ἀκριβῶς** (“exactly”): Luke 1:3; accurately, diligently, **ἐπιμελῶς**: Luke 15:8. **GLAGGVO**, adverb: prudently, **ἀκριβῶς**: 1 Thess. 5:2 (thus, probably, and more suitably to the sense, it must be read in place of *gaaggvo*, read and published by Castillon).

**GLITMUNJAN** (Old Norse *glita*, Old Saxon *glitan*, Anglo-Saxon *glisian, glitnian*, Old High German *glizan*, Old French *glisa*, English *glitter*, Danish *glindse, glise, glitte*, Modern High German *gleissen, glizzern*; Gr. II, 175; III, 391; Gf. IV, 289; Rchth. 776), conjugation II: to shine, gleam, **στίλβειν**: Mark 9:3.

**GUÞ** (Old Norse, Swedish, Danish *gud*, Old High German *got*, Old Saxon, Anglo-Saxon, Old French, English, Dutch *god*, Modern High German *Gott*; Gr. III, 348; Gf. IV, 146; Rchth. 776), plural *guda* (*guþa*, Gal. 4:8; cf. Gr. I, 605): God; a god; an idol, **θεός**: Matt. 5:8, 34; 8:29; 27:46; Mark 2:7; 4:11, 26, 30; 7:8–9, 12; 10:6, 9, 14, 23–25, 27; 11:22; 12:14, 17, 26–27, 30, 34; 13:19; 15:34, 39, 43; Luke 1:6, 8, 16, 19, 26, 30, 32, 35, 37, 47, 64, 68, 78; 2:13, 20, 28, 40, 52; 3:2, 6, 8, 38; 4:3–4, 8–9, 12, 34, 41, 43; 5:1, 21, 25–26; 6:4, 12; 7:16, 28–30; 8:1, 10–11, 21, 28, 39; 9:2, 11, 20, 27, 43, 60, 62; 10:9, 11, 27; 14:15; 15:10; 16:13, 15–16; 17:15, 18, 20–21; 18:2, 43; 20:21, 25, 37–38; John 6:27, 29, 33; 7:17; 8:47, 54; 9:3, 16, 24, 29, 31, 33, 35; 10:34–35; 11:4, 22, 27, 40; 12:43; 13:31–32; 14:1; 16:2, 30; 17:5; 19:7; Rom. 6:23; 7:4; 8:3, 7, 9, 34; 9:5–6; 10:1; 11:21–23, 29, 33; 12:1–3, 17, 19; 13:1–2, 4, 6; 14:3, 11–12, 17–18, 20; 15:5–9, 13; 1 Cor. 1:14, 20–21, 25; 4:5, 9; 5:13; 7:7, 17, 19; 9:21; 10:20, 31–32; 11:3, 22; 12:18; 13:25; 15:9–10, 15, 24–25, 28, 50, 57; 2 Cor. 1:1–3, 9, 12, 19; 2:15, 17; 3:4; 4:2, 4, 6–7, 15; 5:1, 5, 11, 18–21; 6:1, 4, 7, 16; 7:1, 6, 9–12; 8:1, 5, 16, 21; 9:7–8, 11–15; 10:5, 13; 11:2, 7, 11, 31; 12:2–3; 13:4, 7, 11, 13; Gal. 1:1, 3–4, 20, 24; 2:6, 19, 21; 4:4, 6–9, 14; 6:7, 16; Eph. 1:2–3, 11, 17; 2:4, 8, 10, 16, 19, 22; 3:2, 7, 9–10, 19; 4:6, 13, 18, 30, 32; 5:1–2, 5–6, 20; 6:13, 17, 23; Phil. 1:14, 28; 2:6, 27; 3:9, 14–15, 19; 4:6–7, 9; Col. 1:10, 25; 2:12, 19; 3:1, 17, 22; 1 Thess. 2:18, 12–13; 3:2, 11; 4:1, 5, 7, 14; 5:9, 23; 2 Thess. 1:1–2, 4–6, 8, 11–12; 2:4, 16; 3:5; 1 Tim. 1:1–2, 4, 11, 17; 2:3, 5, 10; 3:5, 15; 4:3–5, 10; 5:4–5, 21; 6:11, 13; 2 Tim. 1:1–2, 6–8; 2:2, 9, 15, 19, 25; 3:4; Titus 1:1, 4, 7, 16; Neh. 5:45; Ps. 53:2; *Skeir.* I, a, c; III, b; V, d; VIII, c.

**GALIUGA-GUÞ**, false god, idol, **εἴδωλον**: 1 Cor. 8:10; 10:19–20; Eph. 5:5. *Galingagude skalkinassus*, idolatry, **εἰδωλολατρεία**: Gal. 5:20; Eph. 5:5; Col. 3:5. **GUD-HUS**, see under **Hus**. **GUDA-LAUS**, see under **Liusan**. **GUDI-LUB**, proper name; see under **Lubs**. **GUÞA-SKAUNEI**, see under **Skauns**. **GUDA-FAURHTS**, see under **Faurhts**.

**GUDISKS**, adjective: divine, *Skeir.* I, b, c. *Gudiska ahmateins*, divine inspiration, divine inbreathing; hence *boka gudiskaizos ahmateinais*, Scripture divinely inspired, handed down and dictated by God, **γραφὴ θεόπνευστος** (“God-breathed Scripture”): 2 Tim. 3:16.

**AF-GUDS**, adjective: impious, godless, **ἀσεβής**: 1 Tim. 1:9, at this passage; *Skeir.* IV, d. **GA-GUDS**, pious, honourable, **εὐσχήμων**: Mark 15:43. **GA-GUDABA**, adverb: piously, **εὐσεβῶς**: 2 Tim. 3:12. **AF-GUDEI**, feminine: impiety, **ἀσέβεια**: Rom. 11:26; 2 Tim. 2:16. **GA-GUDEI**, piety, **εὐσέβεια**: 1 Tim. 2:2; 3:16; 4:7–8; 6:3, 5–6, 11; 2 Tim. 3:5; Titus 1:1; *Skeir.* I, c.

**GUDJA** (Old Norse *godi*; cf. Old High German *coting*; DRA. 751; DM. 58; Gf. IV, 153), masculine: priest, **ἱερεύς**: Matt. 8:4; Mark 1:44; Luke 1:5; 5:14; 6:4; 17:14; Ezra 2:36; high priest, **ἀρχιερεύς**: Matt. 27:1, 3, 6, 12; Mark 2:16; 14:10; Luke 9:22; 20:1; John 18:15–16. For **ἀρχιερεύς**, *auhumists gudja*, *maists gudja*, and *reikists gudja* are also used; see under **Auhuma**, **Mais**, and **Reiks**. **UFAR-GUDJA**, high priest, **ἀρχιερεύς**: Mark 10:33. **GUDJINON**, conjugation II: to perform priestly service, **ἱερατεύειν**: Luke 1:8. **GUDJINASSUS**, masculine: priesthood; priestly office, **ἱερατεία**: Luke 1:9; **λειτουργία** (“ministry, service”): 2 Cor. 9:12.

**GULÞ** (Old Norse *gull, gullinn*, Old Saxon *gold, guldin*, Anglo-Saxon *gold, gyldin*, Old French *gold, gelden*, Old High German *gold, guldin*, Swedish and Danish *guld, gylden*, English and Modern High German *gold, golden*; Gr. II, 55, 456; III, 453; Gf. IV, 194; Rchth. 774, 780), neuter: gold, **χρυσός**: 1 Tim. 2:9. **FIGGRA-GULÞ**, ring, golden ring, **δακτύλιος**: Luke 15:22. **GULÞEINS**, adjective: golden, **χρύσεος**: 2 Tim. 2:20.

**GUMA** (Old Norse *gumi*, Old Saxon *gomo, gumo, —guma*, Anglo-Saxon *guma*, Old High German *gomo*, Old French *goma*, English *gom*, Swedish and Danish *—gom*, Modern High German *—gam*; cf. Latin *homo*; Gr. II, 47, 456; DRA. 418; Gf. IV, 198; Rchth. 781), masculine: man, **ἀνήρ**: Luke 19:2; Neh. 5:17. **GUMA-KUNDS**, see under **Kuni**. **GUMEINS**, adjective: male, masculine, **ἄρρην**: Mark 10:6.

**GUND** (Old High German *gunt*, Anglo-Saxon *gund*; Gr. II, 457; Gf. IV, 219): pus, ichor, putrefaction, **γάγγραινα** (“gangrene”): 2 Tim. 2:17, at this passage.

**GUT** (Anglo-Saxon *geatas*, Old High German *guti, gudi*; Gf. IV, 173): Goths. **GUT-ÞIUDA**, see under **þiuda**. **GUTNAN**, see under **Giutan**.

**GRABAN** (Old Norse *grafa*, Old Saxon *bigraþan*, Anglo-Saxon *grafan*, Old French *greva*, Old High German *graban*, English *grave*, Swedish *gräfva, graf*, Danish *grave*, Modern High German *graben*; Greek **γράφειν**; Gr. II, 9; Gf. IV, 301; Rchth. 784), conjugation I, *grof, grobun, grabans*: to dig, **σκάπτειν**: Luke 6:48; 16:3. **BI-GRABAN**: 1. to dig around; *bigraban grabai*, to surround, **περιβάλλειν χάρακα** (“to cast up a palisade around”): Luke 19:43. **US-GRABAN**, to dig out, **ὀρύττειν**: Mark 12:1; 2. to pluck out, **ἐξορύττειν**: Mark 2:4; Gal. 4:15. **UF-GRABAN**, to dig through, **διορύττειν**: Matt. 6:19–20. **GRABA**, feminine: ditch, trench, **χάραξ**: Luke 19:43. **GROBA**, feminine: den, hole, **φωλεός**: Matt. 8:20; Luke 9:58.

**GRAMJAN** (Old Norse *gremian, gramr, grimmr*, Old Saxon *gram*, Old French *grim*, Anglo-Saxon *grimman, gramian*, Old High German *gram, gramjan, grim*, Swedish *gram, grämja*, Modern High German *gram, grämlich, grimmig*; Gr. II, 33; Gf. IV, 320; Rchth. 787): to provoke; *gramjan du þvairhein*, **παροργίζειν** (“provoke to anger”): Col. 3:21, at this passage. **IN-GRAMJAN**, the same, **παροξύνειν** (“provoke”): 1 Cor. 13:5. **GRAMSTS**, masculine: mote, **κάρφος**: Luke 6:41–42.

**GRAS** (Old Norse and Old Saxon *gras*, Anglo-Saxon *graes, gaers*, Old High German *gras*, Old French *gers, gres*, English *grass*, Swedish *gräs*, Danish and Modern High German *gras*; Latin *gramen*; Gr. II, 44; III, 371; Gf. IV, 333; Rchth. 774), neuter: grass, herb, vegetable, **χόρτος**: Mark 4:28; **λάχανον** (“vegetable”): Mark 4:32; Rom. 14:2.

**GREDUS** (Old Norse *gradugr*, Old Saxon *gradag*, Anglo-Saxon *graedig*, Old High German *gratag*, English *greed*, Swedish *gradig*, Danish *graadig*; Gf. IV, 311), masculine: hunger, **λιμός**: 2 Cor. 11:27. **GREDAGS**, adjective: hungry; *gredags visan* and *gredags vairþan*, to hunger, **πεινῆν**: Matt. 25:42; Mark 2:25; 11:12; Luke 1:53; 4:2; 6:3, 21, 25; 1 Cor. 11:21; Phil. 4:12. **GREDON**, conjugation II: to hunger, **πεινῆν**; impersonally, *gredoþ mik* (“I am hungry”), **πεινῶ**: Rom. 12:20.

**GREIPAN** (Old Norse, Old French, Swedish *gripa*, Old Saxon and Anglo-Saxon *gripan*, Old High German *grifan*, English *gripe*, Danish *gribe*, Modern High German *greifen*; Bopp 88, 127; Gr. II, 13; Gf. IV, 314; Rchth. 787), conjugation I, *graip, gripun, gripans*: to seize, apprehend, **κρατεῖν**: Mark 14:44, 49, 51; **συλλαμβάνειν**: Mark 14:48. **UND-GREIPAN**, the same: **κρατεῖν**: Mark 1:31; 9:27; 12:12; 14:46; **λαμβάνειν**: Mark 12:8; **συλλαμβάνειν**: John 18:12; **ἐπιλαμβάνεσθαι**: 1 Tim. 6:12; **ἀγγαρεύειν** (“press into service”): Mark 15:21. **FAIR-GREIPAN**, the same: **κρατεῖν**: Mark 5:41; Luke 8:54; **ἐπιλαμβάνεσθαι**: Mark 8:23; Luke 9:47.

**GRETAN** (*greitan*, Mark 14:72; Luke 7:38; John 11:31, 35; Old Norse *grata*, Old Saxon *griotan*, Anglo-Saxon *graetan*, Swedish *gråta*, Danish *graede*; cf. Modern High German *grinsen*; Gf. IV, 328), conjugation I, *gaigrot, gretans*: to weep, **κλαίειν**: Matt. 26:75; Mark 5:38–39; 14:72; 16:10; Luke 6:21, 25; 7:13, 32, 38; 8:52; 19:41; John 11:31, 33; 16:20; Rom. 12:15; Phil. 3:18; **κράζειν** (“cry aloud”): Rom. 9:27.

**GRETS**, masculine: weeping, lamentation, **κλαυθμός**: Matt. 8:12.

**GREFTS** (cf. *greipan*; Old High German *grift*; Gf. IV, 319). **GA-GREFTS** (but not *gagreifts*), feminine: ordinance, decree, dogma, **δόγμα**: Luke 2:1; *in gagreftai visan*, to be ready, to be at hand, **προκεῖσθαι**: 2 Cor. 8:12, at this passage.

**GRIDS** (Old Norse *grada*, Old French, Anglo-Saxon, Old High German *grad*, Middle High German *grede* or *critmali, gritmali*, Gr. Gr. I, 59 [3rd edition]; Latin *gradi*, Modern High German *grätschen*; Gf. IV, 311; Rchth. 781), feminine: step, rank, position, **βαθμός**: 1 Tim. 3:13.

**GRIND** (Anglo-Saxon *grindan*, English *grind*, Old High German *grint*, Modern High German *grand*; Gf. IV, 330), small, minute. **GRINDA-FRAÞJIS**, see under **Fraþjan**.

**GRUDS** (English *grudge*), adjective: sluggish, indolent. **US-GRUDS**, the same; *vairþan usgrudja* (always in this construction), to grow weary or lose heart, **ἐκκακεῖν**: Luke 18:1; 2 Cor. 4:1, 16; Gal. 6:9; Eph. 3:13; 2 Thess. 3:13.

**GRUNDUS** (Old Norse *grunnr*, Old High German *grunt*, Old Saxon, Anglo-Saxon, Old French, Swedish, Danish, and Modern High German *grund*, English *ground*; Gr. II, 456; III, 394; DRA. 492), masculine: foundation. **GRUNDU-VADDJUS**, see under **Vaddjus**. **AF-GRUNDIÞA**, feminine: abyss, **ἄβυσσος**: Luke 8:31; Rom. 10:7. **GROBA**, see under **Graban**.

**GODS** (also *goþ* in the neuter; Old Norse *godr*, Old Saxon, Old French, Anglo-Saxon *god*, Old High German *got*, English *good*, Swedish and Danish *god*, Dutch *goed*, Modern High German *gut*; cf. Greek **ἀγαθός**; Gr. II, 43; III, 602; Gf. IV, 154; Rchth. 777), adjective: good, beautiful, **ἀγαθός**: Matt. 5:45; 7:17; Luke 8:8; 19:17; Rom. 7:19; 12:2, 9; 13:3–4; 2 Cor. 9:8; Eph. 2:10; 4:29; 1 Thess. 3:6; 2 Thess. 2:16–17; 1 Tim. 1:5, 19; 2:10; 5:10; 2 Tim. 2:21; 3:17; Titus 1:16; **καλός** (“good, fine”): Matt. 5:16; 7:19; Mark 4:8, 20; 7:27; 9:5, 42–43, 45, 47, 50; 14:6; Luke 3:9; 6:38, 43; 8:15; 9:33; 14:34; John 10:11, 14, 32–33; Rom. 7:16, 18, 21; 11:24; 12:17; 1 Cor. 5:6; 7:8, 26; 2 Cor. 8:21; 13:7; 1 Thess. 5:21; Col. 1:10; Gal. 4:18; 6:6, 9; 1 Tim. 1:8, 18; 2:3; 3:1, 7, 13; 4:4, 6; 5:4, 10, 25; 6:12–13; 2 Tim. 1:14; 2:3; 4:7; **χρηστός** (“kind”): Luke 6:35; 1 Cor. 15:33. *Gods alevabagms*, see under **Bagms**; *gods vilja*, see under **Viljan**. **GASTI-GODS**, hospitable, **φιλόξενος**: 1 Tim. 3:2; Titus 1:8. **GODEI**, feminine: goodness, virtue, **ἀρετή**: Phil. 4:8. **GASTI-GODEI**, hospitality, **φιλοξενία**: Rom. 12:13. **GODA-KUNDS**, see under **Kuni**.

**GOLJAN** (cf. *gailjan*; cf. Old High German *guol*; Gr. II, 9; Gf. IV, 183), conjugation II: to greet, **ἀσπάζεσθαι**: Matt. 5:47; Luke 1:40; 10:4; Rom. 16:22–23; 1 Cor. 16:19–20; 2 Cor. 13:12; 1 Thess. 5:26; Col. 4:10, 12, 14–15; Philem. 23; **χαίρειν** (“hail”): Mark 15:18.

**GOLEINS**, feminine: greeting, salutation, **ἀσπασμός**: Luke 1:29, 41, 44; 1 Cor. 16:21; Col. 4:18; 2 Thess. 3:17.

[Col. 1291] D
[Col. 1291] **DABAN** (Old Saxon *thau*, Anglo-Saxon *gedafan, getheavod*, Old High German *dau, daulih*; Gr. II, 42; Gf. V, 87), conjugation I, *dob*: to be fitting, to be suitable.

[Col. 1292] **GA-DABAN**, 1) to accommodate oneself, to adapt oneself—(with accusative), *Skeir.* III, c; 2) to occur, to happen (French *se passer*), συμβαίνειν: Mc. X, 32.

[Col. 1293] **GA-DOBS** (*gadofs* Tit. II, 1), adjective: fitting, seemly, becoming, πρέπων: Eph. V, 3; Tim. I, II, 10; Tit. II, 1; *Skeir.* I, c (twice); II, c.

**DAGS** (Old Norse *dagr*, Anglo-Saxon *daeg*, Old and Modern High German *tag*, Old French *di, dei, dach*, English *day*, Old Saxon, Swedish, Danish *dag*; Gr. II, 44, 451; III, 351, 488; Gf. V, 353; Rchth. 685), masculine: day, ἡμέρα: Mth. VII, 22; IX, 15; XI, 24; XXVII, 63, 64; Mc. I, 9, 13; II, 1, 20; IV, 27; V, 5; VI, 11, 21; VIII, 1, 2; IX, 2, 31; X, 34; XI, 12; XIII, 17, 19, 20, 24; XIV, 12, 49; XV, 29; Luc. I, 5, 7, 18, 20, 23, 24, 25, 39, 59, 75, 80; II, 1, 6, 21, 22, 36, 37, 43, 44, 46; IV, 2, 16, 25, 42; V, 17, 35; VI, 12, 13, 23; VIII, 22; IX, 12, 22, 23, 28, 36, 37, 51; X, 12, 14; XV, 13; XVI, 19; XVII, 4, 22, 24, 26, 27, 28, 29, 30, 31; XVIII, 7, 33; XIX, 42, 43, 47; XX, 1; Joan. VI, 40, 54; VII, 37; VIII, 56; IX, 4; XI, 6, 9, 17, 24; XII, 7, 12, 48; XIV, 20; XVI, 23; Rom. VIII, 36; X, 21; XIII, 12, 13; XIV, 5; Cor. I, IV, 3; V, 5; XV, 4, 31; Cor. II, I, 14; III, 14, 15; IV, 16; VI, 2; Gal. IV, 10; Eph. IV, 30; VI, 13; Col. II, 16; Thess. I, III, 10; V, 2, 5, 8; Thess. II, I, 10; III, 8; Tim. I, V, 5; Tim. II, I, 3, 12, 18; III, 1; IV, 8; Neh. V, 18; καιρός, “season, appointed time”: Tim. I, IV, 1; *naht jah dag*, “night and day,” an entire (civil) day, νυχθήμερον: Cor. II, XI, 25.

For *himma daga* (“on this day”) and *hina dag* (“this day”), see under **His**; for *Sabbato dags* (“Sabbath day”), see under **Sabbatus**.

**AFAR-DAGS** (for this is probably to be read instead of *afar dags*, just as *afarsabbatus*, “the following day”): the next day, ἡ ἐξῆς, Luc. VII, 11.

**GISTRA-DAGIS**: yesterday. In Mth. VI, 30 it is used for “tomorrow morning” (αὔριον); see, however, the note on that passage.

**\* . . . . DOGS**, adjective: —days old.

**AHTAU-DOGS**: eight days old, born eight days previously, ὀκταήμερος: Phlpp. III, 5.

**FIDUR-DOGS**: four days old, having existed for four days, τεταρταῖος: Joan. XI, 39.

**DADDJAN** (Swedish *dia*, Old High German *taan, tutta, tuzjan*, Greek ΘΛΩ, τιθήνη; Gf. V, 284, 381, 463), conjugation II: to suckle, θηλάζειν: Mc. XIII, 17.

**DAIGS**, see under **Deigan**.

**DAIKAPAULIS**, proper name: Decapolis, Δεκάπολις: Mc. V, 20; VII, 31.

**DAILS** (Old Norse *deila*, Old Saxon *del, delian*, Anglo-Saxon *dael, daelan*, Old High German *tail, teil, tailjan*, Old French and Swedish *del, dela*, Danish *deel, dele*, English *deal*, Dutch *deylen*, Modern High German *Theil, theilen*; Gr. II, 44, 490; Gf. V, 402; Rchth. 682), feminine: part, portion, μέρος: Luc. XV, 12; XVIII, 12; Cor. I, XIII, 10, 12; Col. II, 16; μερίς, “share”: Cor. II, VI, 15; Col. I, 12.

**DAILA**, feminine: 1) participation, sharing, μετοχή: Cor. II, VI, 14; 2) mina, μνᾶ: Luc. XIX, 13, 24, 25.

**DAILJAN**, conjugation II: to divide, distribute, share; διαιρεῖν, “to apportion”: Cor. I, XII, 11; μεταδιδόναι, “to impart”: Rom. XII, 8; Eph. IV, 28.

**AF-DAILJAN**: to divide; *afdailjan taihundon dail*, to exact a tenth part, to tithe, ἀποδεκατοῦν: Luc. XVIII, 12.

**GA-DAILJAN**: to divide, apportion, distribute; μερίζειν: Mc. III, 24, 25, 26; Rom. XII, 3; Cor. I, VII, 17; διδόναι, “to give”: Luc. XIX, 8; διαδιδόναι, “to distribute”: Luc. XVIII, 22; Joan. VI, 11.

**DIS-DAILJAN**: to divide, apportion; μερίζειν: Cor. I, I, 13; διαμερίζειν, “to distribute”: Mc. XV, 24; διαιρεῖν: Luc. XV, 12.

**FRA-DAILJAN**: to distribute, διδόναι: Joan. XII, 5.

**GA-DAILA**, masculine: participant, companion, κοινωνός: Luc. V, 10; Cor. I, X, 20; Cor. II, I, 7; συγκοινωνός, “fellow participant”: Cor. I, IX, 23; συμμέτοχος, “joint participant”: Eph. III, 6; V, 7; ἀντιλαμβανόμενος, “one who shares in support”: Tim. I, VI, 2.

**DAIMONAREIS** (Greek vocable), masculine: demoniac, one possessed by a demon, δαιμονιζόμενος: Mth. VIII, 16, 28, 33; IX, 32; δαιμονισθείς, “one who had been demon-possessed”: Luc. VIII, 36.

**DAL** (Old Norse *dalr, dala*, Old High German *tal*, English *dale, dell*, Old Saxon, Swedish, Danish, Dutch *dal*, Modern High German *Thal, telle*; Gr. II, 41; III, 395; Gf. V, 396), neuter, or masculine *dals*: valley, ravine, pit; φάραγξ: Luc. III, 5; βόθυνος, “pit”: Luc. VI, 39; *dal uf mesa*,

[Col. 1294] a vessel placed beneath a winepress, ὑπολήνιον: Mc. XII, 1; see the note on this passage.

**ÏD-DALJO**, feminine: descent, κατὰβασις: Luc. XIX, 37.

**DALAþ**, adverb: below, downward, from above, upon the ground; κάτω, “down”: Luc. IV, 9; χαμαί, “on the ground”: Joan. IX, 6; XVIII, 6; *dalaþ atgaggan*, to go down, καταβαίνειν: Mth. VIII, 1, 7, 25, 27; Mc. IX, 9; Luc. VI, 17; κατέρχεσθαι: Luc. IX, 37; *atsteigan dalaþ*, to descend, καταβαίνειν: Luc. XVII, 31; XIX, 5; Thess. I, IV, 16; *dalaþ attiuhan*, to draw down, κατὰγειν: Rom. X, 6; *und dalaþ*, as far as below, ἕως κάτω: Mth. XXVII, 51; Mc. XV, 38.

**DALAþA**, adverb: below, κάτω: Mc. XIV, 66.

**DALAþRO**, adverb: below, downward, κάτω: Joan. VIII, 23.

**DALMATIA**, feminine proper name: Dalmatia, Δαλματία: Tim. II, IV, 10.

**DAMASKO**, feminine proper name: Damascus, Δαμασκός: Cor. II, XI, 23.

**DAMASKS**, adjective: Damascene, δαμασκηνός: Cor. II, XI, 32.

VII, 4; X, 7, 9; XI, 15; XIV, 9; Cor. I, XV, 12, 13, 16, 20, 21, 29, 35; Cor. II, I, 9, 10; Gal. I, 1; Eph. I, 20; II, 1, 5; Phlpp. I, 20; III, 11; Col. I, 18; II, 12, 13; Thess. I, IV, 16; Tim. **DEIGAN** (*digan*, Rom. IX, 20; Old Norse *deig*, Old High German *teig*, Swedish *deg*, Danish *deig*, Dutch *deeg*, Modern High German *teig, gediegen*; Gr. II, 47; III, 461; Gf. **\* DIGRS** (Old Norse *digr, digurd, þykr*, Old Saxon *thicci*, Anglo-Saxon *ðik*, Old French *thikke*, Old High German *dik*, English *thick, tight*, Swedish *tjok*, Danish *tyk*, Modern High German *dick, dicht*; Gf. V, 111; Rchth. 1072), adjective: firm, thick, abundant.

**\* DIUPAN** (Old Norse *diupr*, Old Saxon *diop, dopian*, Anglo-Saxon *diop, dyppan*, Old High German *tiuf, taufjan*, Old French *depa*, English *dip, deep*, Swedish *djup*, Danish *dyb*, Modern High German *tief, taufen*; Gr. I, I, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17; X, 2; XII, 13; XV, 29; Gal. III, 27; *Skeir.* III, a; IV, b; 2) to be baptized, βαπτίζεσθαι: Mc. VII, 4.

**DAUPJANDS**, participle and substantive (Mc. VIII, 28): Baptist, βαπτιστής: Mth. XI, 11, 12; Mc. VI, 24, 25; VIII, 28; Luc. VII, 20, 28, 33.
