**ESAV**, masculine proper name, Ἠσαῦ, Esau: Rom. 9:13.

**ETA**, see under *Ita*.

[Col. 1305] Q

[Col. 1305] **QAINON** (Old Norse *qveina, veina*; Anglo-Saxon *evanian, vanian*; Old High German *weinon*; English *whine*; Swedish *hvina*; Dutch *kwynen*; Modern High German *queulen, weinen*; Latin *queri*; *Gr.* II, 13; *Gf.* I, 888), conjugation II, to weep, mourn, πενθεῖν: Matt. 9:15; Mark 16:10; 2 Cor. 11:21; to beat the breast, κόπτεσθαι: Matt. 12:17.

[Col. 1306]

**\*QAIRNUS** (Old Norse *qvörn*; Anglo-Saxon *cvyrn*; Old Saxon, Old Frisian, English *quern*; Old High German *quirn*; Swedish *qvarn*; Danish *quaern*; *Gf.* IV, 680; *Rchth.* 882), masculine, millstone, mill.

**ASILU-QAIRNUS**, properly an ass-mill, that is, one moved by an ass; generally, a millstone, μύλος ὀνικός: Mark 9:42.

**QAIRRUS** (Old Norse *kyrr*; Danish *qver*; Modern High German *kirr*; compare Latin *cicur*), adjective, gentle, mild, quiet, ἤπιος: 2 Tim. 2:24.

**QAIRREI**, feminine, gentleness, πραότης: 2 Cor. 10:1; Gal. 5:23; 6:1; Eph. 4:2; Col. 3:12; 1 Tim. 6:11; 2 Tim. 2:25.

**cQAL** (Old Norse *qvölld*; Anglo-Saxon *cvyld*; English *quell*; Swedish *quäll*; *Gr.* II, 29), neuter, security.

**ANA-QAL**, rest, τὸ ἡσυχάζειν, “to be quiet”: 1 Thess. 4:11.

[Col. 1307] **QARTUS**, masculine proper name, Κούαρτος, Quartus: Rom. 16:23.

**QENS** (*qeïns*, Luke 1:5; 2:5; Old Norse *kona, qvan, qven*; Anglo-Saxon *cven*; Old Saxon *quena*; Old High German *cheona, qvena*; English *queen, quean*; Swedish *kåna, qvinna*; Danish *kone, qvinde*; Greek γυνή; *Gr.* II, 56; III, 322; *Gf.* IV, 677), feminine, woman, wife, especially a woman joined in marriage, γυνή: Matt. 5:31, 32; 27:19; Mark 6:17, 18; 10:2, 11, 29; 12:19, 20, 22, 23; Luke 1:5, 13, 18, 24; 2:5; 3:19; 8:3; 14:20, 26; 16:18; 17:32; 18:29; 20:28–30, 32, 33; Rom. 7:2; 1 Cor. 7:10–14, 27, 28; Eph. 5:22, 25, 28; Col. 3:19; 1 Tim. 3:2, 12; 5:9; Titus 1:6; Neh. 6:18. *Qen niman*, “to take a woman,” to marry, γαμεῖν: 1 Cor. 7:28.

**\*QENJAN**, conjugation II, to enter into marriage.

**UN-QENIþS**, past participle, unmarried, ἄγαμος: 1 Cor. 7:8.

**QINO**, feminine, equivalent to *qens*, taken commonly and generically, woman, γυνή: Matt. 5:28; 11:11; 27:55; Mark 5:25, 33; 7:25, 26; 10:12; 15:40; Luke 1:28, 42; 4:26; 7:28, 37, 39, 44, 50; 8:2, 43, 47; 15:8; John 16:21; 1 Cor. 7:16; 9:5; 11:3, 5, 6; Gal. 4:4; Col. 3:18; 1 Tim. 2:9–12, 14; 3:2, 11.

**QINEINS**, adjective, female, feminine, θῆλυς: Mark 10:6. Neuter *qinein*, woman, female, γυναικάριον: 2 Tim. 3:6.

**QINA-KUNDS**, see under *Kuni*.

**QIþAN** (Old Norse *qveda*; Old Saxon *quethan*; Anglo-Saxon *cvaeðan*; Old High German *quedan*; Old Frisian *quetha*; Swedish *qväda*; Danish *qvaede*; English *quoth, quote*; compare Dutch *kouten*, Modern High German *kosen*; Latin *inquit*; Greek κωτίλλειν; Bopp 117; *Gr.* II, 26; *Gf.* IV, 636; *Rchth.* 882), conjugation I, *qaþ, qeþun, qiþans*:

1. To speak, say, εἰπεῖν and ἐρεῖν: Matt. 5:21, 22; 7:22; 8:4, 8, 10, 13, 19; 9:3, 4, 22; 10:27; 11:3, 4; 25:40, 41; 27:4, 6, 9, 63, 64; Mark 1:17, 42; 2:8, 9; 3:9, 32; 4:39, 40; 5:7, 33, 34; 6:16, 22, 24; 7:6, 10, 11, 27, 29, 36; 8:26; 9:12, 17, 18, 21, 23, 29, 36, 39; 10:3, 4, 14, 18, 20, 21, 36–39; 11:3, 23, 31; 12:32, 36; 13:21; 14:14, 62; 15:12; 16:7; Luke 1:61; 2:49; 3:12; 4:3; 5:14; 7:7, 40, 42; 8:56; 9:20, 54; 14:10, 17–20; 15:11, 17, 18; 17:5–7, 21, 23; 18:26; 19:15, 31; 20:2, 3, 5, 6, 25, 39; John 6:25; 8:55; 10:6, 34; 11:13, 28; 12:29; 14:2, 29; 18:8, 22, 34; Rom. 7:7; 9:12, 14, 19, 30; 10:6; 11:19; 1 Cor. 1:15; 7:15, 21; 10:28; 11:22, 24; 14:23; 15:27, 35; 2 Cor. 4:6; 12:6, 9; Gal. 2:14; Phil. 4:4, 11; Col. 4:17; Titus 1:12; Neh. 5:13; 7:3.

   To say, λέγειν: Matt. 5:18, 20, 22; 6:25, 29, 31; 7:21; 8:2, 4, 11; 9:21, 27, 30; 10:27; 11:9; 25:44, 45; 27:11, 65; Mark 1:7, 24, 25, 37–41; 2:5, 10, 18; 3:3–5, 11, 21–23, 28, 30, 33, 34; 4:2, 9, 11, 21, 24, 26, 30, 35, 38, 41; 5:8, 9, 19, 23, 28, 30, 31, 35, 36, 39, 41; 6:2, 4, 10, 14, 15, 18, 25; 7:9, 11, 14, 18, 20, 28, 34, 37; 8:1, 12, 15–17, 19, 26, 27; 9:1, 5, 11, 13, 19, 24, 25, 31, 35, 38, 41; 10:11, 15, 18, 23, 24, 26–28, 32, 35, 42, 47; 11:9, 23, 31; 12:18, 36, 37; 14:14, 57, 58, 68–71; 15:28, 29, 31, 34; Luke 1:67; 2:13; 5:24; 7:39, 47; 8:24; 9:18, 20, 27, 31, 33, 34; 10:5; 14:12, 24; 15:9, 10; 16:6; 17:4, 10; 18:1–3, 19, 34; 19:7, 26, 41; 20:37, 41; John 6:5; 8:54; 9:17, 41; 13:13, 22; 16:7, 26, 29; 18:37; Rom. 7:7; 9:1, 15, 17, 25; 10:6, 8, 11, 16, 18, 21; 11:1, 13; 12:3, 19; 14:11; 15:8; 1 Cor. 7:6, 8, 12; 9:8; 10:15, 29; 11:25; 14:21; 15:12, 51; 2 Cor. 6:2, 13, 17; 7:3; 8:8; 9:3, 4; 11:16; Gal. 4:1, 21, 30; 5:2, 16; Eph. 4:8, 17; Phil. 4:11; 1 Thess. 4:15; 2 Thess. 2:4; 1 Tim. 2:7; 4:1; 5:18; 2 Tim. 2:7, 18; Philem. 21; *Skeir.* I.b; II.a, b, c; III.a; IV.[Col. 1308]a, b; V.b, d; VI.a, c, d; VIII.b, c, d.

   To contradict, ἀντιλέγειν: Luke 20:27. To declare, φάναι: Matt. 8:8; 27:11; Luke 7:41, 44; John 9:38; 1 Cor. 10:15, 19; 15:50; 2 Cor. 10:10. To speak, λαλεῖν: 2 Cor. 11:23.

2. To speak of, mention, name, λέγειν: Mark 14:71; 12:37; 15:12; Luke 18:19; John 6:71; 8:27, 54; 15:15; Phil. 3:18. To say, εἰπεῖν and ἐρεῖν: John 10:35; 15:15. To call, καλεῖν: Luke 2:21; *Skeir.* II.b; IV.d. Hence *garaihtana sik qiþan*, see under *Raihts*; *ubil qiþan*, with the dative, to revile, κακολογεῖν: Mark 7:10; *vaila qiþan*, to praise, bless, καλῶς εἰπεῖν: Luke 6:26.

**ANA-QIþAN**, to blaspheme, revile, βλασφημεῖν: 1 Cor. 10:30.

**AND-QIþAN**, 1. to take leave, bid farewell, with the dative, ἀποτάσσεσθαι: Luke 9:61; 2. to converse with, with the dative, συντυγχάνειν: Luke 8:19.

**AF-QIþAN**, to take leave of, renounce, with the dative, ἀποτάσσεσθαι: Luke 14:33.

**GA-QIþAN**, to remonstrate; *gaqiþan sis*, to say to oneself; to agree, συντίθεσθαι: John 9:22.

**MIþ-QIþAN**, to interpose in speech, dispute: *Skeir.* V.a.

**US-QIþAN**, to spread abroad, publish widely, διαφημίζειν: Mark 1:45.

**FAUR-QIþAN**, to excuse oneself, decline, παραιτεῖσθαι: Luke 14:18, 19; to annul, reject, ἀθετεῖν: Gal. 2:21; 5:21; see the note on this passage.

**FAURA-QIþAN**, to foretell, προειπεῖν: Rom. 9:29; 2 Cor. 7:3; 13:2; Gal. 5:21; 1 Thess. 4:6; to say beforehand, προλέγειν: Gal. 5:21, at this passage; 1 Thess. 3:4; to prophesy, προφητεύειν: Matt. 11:43 [apparently uncertain or erroneous citation].

**FRA-QIþAN**, 1. to promise, vow, curse, or execrate, καταρᾶσθαι: Matt. 25:41; Mark 11:21; Luke 6:28. Past participle *fraqiþans*, accursed, ἐπικατάρατος: John 7:49; *Skeir.* VIII.d. 2. To dishonour, discredit, ἀθετεῖν: Luke 7:30; see the note on this passage.

**UN-QEþIS**, adjective, unutterable, ἄρρητος: 2 Cor. 12:4.

**QIþLO**, neuter, word, speech: *Skeir.* V.d.

**\*QISS**, feminine, speech, discourse, word.

**ANA-QISS**, blasphemy, βλασφημία: Col. 3:8; 1 Tim. 6:4.

**GA-QISS**, agreement, τὸ σύμφωνον: 1 Cor. 7:5.

**þIUþI-QISS**, blessing, praise, εὐλογία: 1 Cor. 10:16.

**MISSA-QISS**, dissension, division, σχίσμα: John 7:43; 9:16; 10:19.

**US-QISS**, charge, accusation, κατηγορία: Titus 1:6.

**SAMA-QISS**, agreement, concord, συμφώνησις: 2 Cor. 6:15; συγκατάθεσις: 2 Cor. 6:16.

**VAILA-QISS**, praise, blessing, εὐλογία: 2 Cor. 9:5.

**GA-QISS**, adjective, fitting, suitable: *Skeir.* at the cited place; *gaqiss visan*, to be consistent, to agree, συμφάναι: Rom. 7:16.

**QIþUS** (Old Norse *qvidr*; Anglo-Saxon *cvið*; Old High German *quiti*; Swedish *qvider, qved*; compare Modern High German *kutteln*; *Gr.* III, 466; *Gf.* IV, 650), masculine: 1. belly, κοιλία: Luke 1:41, 42; 2. womb, μήτηρ: Luke 2:23; 3. stomach, στόμαχος: 1 Tim. 5:23.

**QIþU-HAFTS**, see under *Haban*.

**LAUS-QIþRS**, adjective, fasting, with an empty stomach, νῆστις: Mark 8:3.

**DAUS-QIþREI**, feminine, fasting, νηστεία: 2 Cor. 6:5; 11:27.

**QIMAN** (Old Norse *koma*; Old Saxon and Anglo-Saxon *cuman*; Old High German *queman*; Old Frisian *kuma*; English *come*; Swedish *komma*; Danish *komme*; Dutch *komen*; Modern High German *kommen*; *Gr.* II, 30; *Gf.* IV, 655; *Rchth.* 880), conjugation I, *qam, qemun, qumans*, to come, arrive, construed with the dative and with *ïn, ana, at,* and *hindar*, ἔρχεσθαι: Matt. 5:17; 6:10; 7:15, 25, 27; 8:9, 11, 28, 29; 9:1; 10:23, 34, 35; 11:3, 14; 27:49, 64; Mark 1:7, 29, 38, 40; 2:2, 17; 3:8, 31; 4:4, 15, 21; 5:1, 14, 22, 23, 33, 35; 6:1, 29; 7:1, 31; 8:3, 10, 22, 38; 9:1, 11–14, 33; 10:1, 45, 46, 50; 11:9, 10, 13; 12:9, 14; 13:26; 14:45, 62; 15:21, 36; Luke 1:43, 59; 2:16, 27, 44, 51; 3:3; 4:34, 42; 5:7, 35; 6:17; 7:3, 7, 8, 19, 20; 8:12, 17, 35, 41; 9:26, 56; 14:10, [Col. 1309] 20, 21; 15:6, 7, 20, 25, 30; 17:20, 22, 27; 18:5, 8, 30; 19:5, 10, 13, 18, 24, 38; 20:16; John 3:31; 6:14, 23, 24, 44, 65; 7:28, 31, 34, 41, 42; 8:14, 20, 42; 9:4, 7, 39; 10:7, 10, 12, 41; 11:17, 20, 27; 12:9, 12, 13, 46; 14:3, 6; 15:22; 18:4, 37; Rom. 7:9; 9:9; 1 Cor. 4:5; 11:26; 13:10; 16:2, 5, 10–12; 2 Cor. 1:15, 23; 2:1, 3, 12; 7:5; 9:4; 11:4, 9; 12:1, 14, 20, 21; 13:1, 2; Gal. 1:21; 2:11, 12; 4:4; Eph. 2:17; 5:6; Phil. 1:27; 2:24; Col. 3:6; 4:10; 1 Thess. 2:18; 3:6; 5:2; 1 Tim. 1:15; 2:4; 3:14; 4:13; 2 Tim. 3:7; 4:9, 13; Neh. 5:17; *Skeir.* I.a, c; IV.c, d; VIII.c.

To enter, εἰσέρχεσθαι: Matt. 5:20; Mark 10:15; Luke 8:51; 9:34; 18:17. To come down, καταβαίνειν: Mark 3:22; John 6:51. To come, ἥκειν: Matt. 8:11; Mark 8:3; Luke 15:27; 19:43; John 6:37; 8:42. To occur, come to pass, γίγνεσθαι: Mark 1:11; 4:17; 9:33; John 6:19, 25; 2 Tim. 1:17. To come near or arrive, παραγίγνεσθαι: Luke 7:4, 20; 14:21; 19:16; John 3:23; 1 Cor. 16:3. In the preterite, to be present, πάρειναι: John 11:28; Gal. 4:20. *Ïn sis qiman*, to come to oneself (French *rentrer en soi-même*), ἔρχεσθαι εἰς ἑαυτόν: Luke 15:17.

**ANA-QIMAN**, to come upon, with accusative, ἐφίστασθαι: Luke 2:9.

**BI-QIMAN**, to come upon, ἐφίστασθαι: 1 Thess. 5:3.

**GA-QIMAN**, to come together: ἔρχεσθαι, John 11:19, at this passage; to attain, καταντᾶν: Phil. 3:11; to assemble, συνέρχεσθαι: Luke 5:17; John 18:20; 1 Cor. 14:23; συνιέναι (?) “to understand”: Luke 8:4; to gather, συνάγεσθαι: Matt. 27:17, 62; Mark 2:2. *Gaqiman sik*, to gather together, συνάγεσθαι: Mark 5:21; 7:1; to go together, συμπορεύεσθαι: Mark 10:1. Impersonally, “it is fitting, proper,” ἀνήκει: Col. 3:18.

**MIþ-QIMAN**, to come together, συνεισέρχεσθαι: John 6:22; *qiman miþ*, the same: John 11:33.

**US-QIMAN**, to kill, slay, κατασφάττειν: Luke 19:27; ἀποκτείνειν: Mark 8:31; Luke 9:22; 20:15; Rom. 7:11; 2 Cor. 3:6. Commonly with the dative: Matt. 10:28; Mark 6:19; 8:31; 9:31; 10:34; 12:7, 8; Luke 18:33; John 7:25; 8:22, 37; 12:10; 16:2; 18:31; 1 Thess. 2:15. To destroy, ἀπολλύναι: Mark 3:6. Also with accusative, ἀποκτείνειν: Mark 12:5; compare John 7:1, 19, 20; 8:40.

**FAURA-QIMAM**, to go before, precede, προέρχεσθαι: Luke 1:17.

**FRA-QIMAN**, 1. to consume, destroy, with dative, ἀναλίσκειν: Luke 9:54; Gal. 5:15. 2. To expend, spend, προσαναλίσκειν: Luke 8:43; δαπανᾷν: Mark 5:26; 2 Cor. 12:15; Neh. 5:18.

**QUMS**, masculine, coming, advent, παρουσία: 1 Cor. 15:23; [Col. 1310] 16:17; 2 Cor. 7:6, 7; 10:10; Phil. 1:26; 1 Thess. 2:19; 3:13; 4:15; 2 Thess. 2:1; appearing, ἐπιφάνεια: 1 Tim. 6:14; 2 Tim. 4:1, 8.

**GA-QUMþS**, feminine: 1. assembly, gathering, ἐπισυναγωγή: 2 Thess. 2:2; 2. council, συνέδριον: Matt. 5:22; 3. school, synagogue, συναγωγή: Matt. 6:2, 5; 9:35; Luke 4:15; John 16:2; 18:20.

**QINO**, see under *Qens*.

**QIUS** (Old Norse *qvikr*; Old Saxon *quic*; Anglo-Saxon *quic*; Old High German *quek*; Old Frisian *quik*; English, Swedish, Dutch *kwick*; Modern High German *queck* …; Latin *vivus*; Bopp 128; *Gr.* II, 52; *Gf.* IV, 632; *Rchth.* 883), adjective, living, alive, ζῶν: Mark 12:27; Luke 20:38; Rom. 12:1; 14:9; Col. 2:20; 2 Tim. 4:1.

**ANA-QIUJAN**, conjugation II, to revive, restore to life, rekindle, ἀναζωπυρεῖν: 2 Tim. 1:6.

**GA-QIUJAN**, to make alive, ζωοποιεῖν: 2 Cor. 3:6; 1 Tim. 6:13; *Skeir.* V.b.

**MIþGA-QIUJAN**, to make alive together with, συζωοποιεῖν: Eph. 2:5; Col. 2:13.

**GA-QIUNAN**, conjugation III, to be restored to life, be made alive, ζωοποιεῖσθαι: 1 Cor. 15:22; to live again, ἀναζῆν: Luke 15:24, 32; Rom. 7:9.

**QISS**, see under *Qiþan*.

**QISTJAN** (Old High German *quistjan*; Anglo-Saxon *cvysan*; Dutch *quisten*; compare English *quench*; *Gr.* II, 44; III, 411; *Gf.* IV, 680), conjugation II, to destroy, with dative, ἀπολλύναι: Luke 9:56.

**US-QISTJAN**, the same, with dative, ἀπολλύναι: Mark 9:22; 11:18; Luke 20:16; with accusative: Mark 12:9; Luke 19:47; to kill, ἀποκτείνειν: Mark 3:4; 9:31; Luke 6:9.

**FRA-QISTJAN**, the same, with dative (only Luke 17:27 with accusative), ἀπολλύναι: Matt. 10:39, 42; Mark 1:24; 8:35; 9:41; Luke 4:34; 9:24, 25; 17:29, 33; John 10:10; 12:25; 18:9, 14; Rom. 14:15; 1 Cor. 1:19; 2 Cor. 4:9; to kill, ἀποκτείνειν: Matt. 10:28.

**FRA-QISTNAN**, conjugation III, to perish, ἀπόλλυσθαι: Matt. 5:29; 8:25; 9:17; Mark 4:38; Luke 5:37; 8:24; 15:17; John 6:12; 10:28; 17:12; 1 Cor. 8:11; 15:18; 2 Cor. 2:15.

**QISTEINS**, feminine, corruption, ruin, ὄλεθρος: 1 Cor. 5:5.

**FRA-QISTEINS**, destruction, perdition, ἀπώλεια: Mark 14:4, at this passage.

**QUMS** and **QUMþS**, see under *Qiman*.

**\*QRAMMS** (Swedish *kram*; Danish *klam*), adjective, moist.

**QRAMMIþA**, feminine, moisture, dampness, ἰκμάς: Luke 8:6.

[Col. 1309] Z

[Col. 1309] **ZAIBAIDAIUS**, masculine proper name, Ζεβεδαῖος, Zebedee: Matt. 27:56; Mark 1:19, 20; 3:17; 10:35; Luke 5:10.

**ZAKARIAS** (*zaxarias*, Luke 3:2), masculine proper name, Ζαχαρίας, Zechariah: Luke 1:5, 13, 21, 40, 59; 3:2.

**ZAKKAIUS**, masculine proper name, Ζακχαῖος, Zacchaeus: Luke [Col. 1310] 19:2, 5.

**ZAURAUBABIL**, masculine proper name, Ζοροβάβελ, Zerubbabel: Luke 3:27.

**ZAXXAIUS**, masculine proper name, Ζακχού, Zaccai: Ezra 2:9.

**ZELOTES** (Greek vocable), Ζηλωτής, Zealot: Luke 6:15.

[Col. 1309] H
[Col. 1309] . . . . H, see under . . .uh. **HABAN** (Old Norse *hafa*, Old Saxon *hebbian*, Anglo-Saxon *habban*, Old Lithuanian, Old High German *haben*, Old French *hebba*, Dutch *hebben*, English *have*, Swedish *hafva*, Danish *have*, Latin *habere*; Gr. II, 9 ff.; Gf. IV, 711; Rchth. 801), conjugation II:

1) to have, possess, ἔχειν (“to have”): Mth. V, 23, 46; VI, 1; VII, 29; VIII, 20; IX, 36; XXVII, 16, 65; Mc. I, 22; II, 19; III, 1, 3, 10, 15, 22, 26, 29; IV, 5, 6, 9, 17, 21, 25, 40; V, 3, 15, 23; VI, 18; VII, 16, 25; VIII, 1, 7, 14, 16, 17, 18; IX, 17, 43, 45, 47, 50; X, 21, 22; XI, 13, 22, 25; XIV, 7, 8; Luc. III, 11, 17; IV, 33, 40; V, 24; VI, 8; VII, 8, 33, 42; VIII, 6, 8, 13, 18, 27; IX, 3, 58; XIV, 14, 18, 19, 28, 35; XV, 8; XVII, 6; XVIII, 22, 24; XIX, 17, 20, 24, 25, 26; XX, [Col. 1310] 24; Joan. V, 36, 38; VI, 9, 53, 68; VII, 20; VIII, 12, 48, 49; IX, 41; X, 18, 20, 21; XII, 6, 8, 35, 48; XIII, 29, 35; XIV, 21; XV, 13, 22; XVI, 21, 33; XVII, 5, 13; XVIII, 10; XIX, 11; Rom. VIII, 9; IX, 10, 21; X, 2; XII, 4; XIII, 3; XV, 4; Cor. I, IV, 7; VI, 1; VII, 7, 25; VIII, 10; IX, 4; XI, 22; XII, 12; XIII, 2; XIV, 26; XV, 31, 34; Cor. II, I, 9, 15; II, 3, 4, 12; III, 4, 12; IV, 1, 7, 13; V, 1, 12; VII, 1, 5, 12; VIII, 11, 12; IX, 8; X, 6, 15; Gal. VI, 4; Eph. I, 7; II, 12, 18; III, 12; IV, 28; V, 5, 27; Phlpp. I, 23, 30; II, 2, 27, 29; III, 4, 9, 17; Col. I, 14; II, 23; III, 13; IV, 13; Thess. I, III, 6; IV, 13; Thess. II, III, 9; Tim. I, I, 19; III, 4, 7, 9; IV, 8; V, 4, 20; VI, 2; Tim. II, I, 13; II, 19; III, 5; Tit. I, 6; Philem. 17; κατέχειν (“to hold fast”): Luc. XIV, 9.

Formulas: *gavairþi haban*, “to have peace”; *frumadein haban*, “to have first place”; *ufarassu haban*, “to have superiority”; *du gavaurkja haban*, “to have for accomplishing,” etc.; see under *Vairþi*, *Fruma*, *Ufar*, *Vaurkjan*, etc.

2) *ju haban*, to have already, ἀπέχειν (“to receive in full”): Mth. VI, 5; Luc. VI, 24.

3) to have a definite duration, whether of existence or of age, ἔχειν (“to have”): Joan. VIII, 57; XI, 17.

4) to be situated, to be: *ubil* and *ubilaba haban*, “to be ill,” κακῶς ἔχειν: Mth. VIII, 16; Mc. I, 32, 34; II, 17; VI, 55; *mais vairs haban*, “to become worse,” μᾶλλον εἰς τὸ χεῖρον ἔρχεσθαι: Mc. V, 36; *aftumist haban*, “to be at the point of death,” ἐσχάτως ἔχειν: Mc. V, 22; *manvuba haban*, “to have in readiness,” ἐν ἑτοίμῳ ἔχειν: Cor. II, X, 6.

5) to have, hold, κρατεῖν (“to hold”): Mth. IX, 25; Mc. VII, 3, 4, 8; IX, 10; Col. II, 19; hence *sa fairwu habands*, “the possessor, ruler of this world,” κοσμοκράτωρ: Eph. VI, 12; *gafahana haban*, “to hold a captive,” ζωγρεῖν: Tim. II, II, 26; *habaiþ visan*, “to be ready” (French *se tenir prêt*), προσκαρτερεῖν: Mc. III, 9; *fairra sik haban*, “to keep oneself away,” ἀπέχειν: Mc. VII, 6; *aljaleikos sik haban*, “to be otherwise disposed,” ἄλλως ἔχειν: Tim. I, V, 25.

6) to have, suppose, ἔχειν: Mc. XI, 32.

7) to be able, ἔχειν: Mc. XIV, 8; Luc. XIV, 14; Eph. IV, 28.

8) to wish, be about to, μέλλειν: Mc. X, 32; Joan. VI, 6, 71; hence it is also used to express the future periphrastically: Joan. XII, 26, *visan habaiþ* (“will be,” ἔσται); Cor. II, XI, 12, *taujan haba* (“I shall do,” ποιήσω); Thess. II, III, 4, *taujan habaiþ* (“you will do,” ποιήσετε); Skeir. I, a, b, *ustauhana habaida vairþan garehsns*, “the purpose had to be fulfilled”; II, c, *þeihan habaida*, “he was about to depart.”

**UN-HABANDS**, participle: not having, μὴ ἔχων: Luc. III, 11; XIX, 26; Cor. I, XI, 22.

**ANA-HABAN**, to hold fast; past participle *anahabaiþs*, held fast, afflicted, συνέχομενος: Luc. IV, 38; troubled, ὀχλούμενος: Luc. VI, 18.

**AT-HABAN**, to hold fast; *athaban sik*, to draw near, προσεγγίζειν [printed προςπορεύεσθαι]: Mc. X, 35.

**AF-HABAN**, to hold back; *afhaban sik*, to abstain, ἀπέχεσθαι: Thess. I, V, 22.

**GA-HABAN**:

1) to have, hold, retain, ἔχειν: Mc. X, 23; κατέχειν (“to hold fast”): Luc. IV, 42; VIII, 15; Rom. VII, 6; Thess. I, V, 21; Philem. 13.

2) to seize, κρατεῖν: Mc. III, 21; VI, 17; Skeir. VII, a.

3) *gahaban sik*, to restrain oneself, ἐγκρατεύεσθαι: Cor. I, VII, 9; ἀπέχεσθαι (“to abstain”): Thess. I, IV, 3.

**UNGA-HABANDS**, participle: not holding; *ungahabands sik*, incontinent, ἀκρατής: Tim. II, III, 3.

**DIS-HABAN**, to restrain, constrain, seize, συνέχειν: Luc. VIII, 37; Cor. II, V, 14; Phlpp. I, 23; περιέχειν (“to surround”): Luc. V, 9.

**UF-HABAN**, to hold up, raise, αἴρειν: Luc. IV, 11.

**HAFTS**, adjective: joined; *liugom hafts*, joined in marriage, married, γεγαμηκώς: Cor. I, VII, 10.

**AUDA-HAFTS**, blessed; *anstai audahafts*, full of grace, κεχαριτωμένος: Luc. I, 28.

**QIþU-HAFTA**, pregnant, ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα (“having in the womb”): Mc. XIII, 17; Thess. I, V, 3.

**HAFTJAN** (Old Saxon *heftian*, Old High German *haftjan*), conjugation II: to bind, cling to, κολλᾶσθαι: Rom. XII, 9; to attend to, προσέχειν: Tim. I, III, 8; to persist in, προσκαρτερεῖν: Rom. XII, 12; *sik haftjan*, the same: Col. IV, 2.

**GA-HAFTJAN**, the same; *gahaftjan sik*, to cleave to, κολλᾶσθαι: Luc. XV, 15.

**GAGA-HAFTJAN**, to be joined together, συμβιβάζειν: Eph. IV, 16, in this passage.

**GA-HAFTNAN**, conjugation III: to cleave to, κολλᾶσθαι: Luc. X, 11.

**GAHOBAN**, to restrain oneself.

**GA-HOBAINS**, feminine: self-control, ἐγκράτεια: Gal. V, 23.

**UNGA-HOBAINS**, lack of self-control, ἀκρασία: Cor. I, VII, 5.

**HAZJAN** (Anglo-Saxon *herian*, Old High German *heren*, Old Saxon *heron*; compare English *hery*, Danish *haeder*; Gf. IV, 998), conjugation II: to praise, αἰνεῖν: Luc. II, 13, 20; XIX, 37; Rom. XV, 11; Neh. V, 13; ἐπαινεῖν (“to commend”): Luc. XVI, 8; Rom. XV, 11; Cor. I, XI, 2, 22.

**HAZEINS**, feminine:

1) praise, αἶνος: Luc. XVIII, 43; commendation, ἔπαινος: Rom. XIII, 3; Cor. I, IV, 5; Cor. II, VIII, [Col. 1312] 18; Eph. I, 6, 12, 14; Phlpp. IV, 8.

2) hymn of praise, ὕμνος: Eph. V, 19; Col. III, 16.

**HAHAN** (Old Norse *hanga*, Old Saxon *hangon*, Anglo-Saxon *hon, hangian*, Old French *hua, hangia, hingia*, Old High German *hahan, hengan*, English *hang*, Danish *haenge*, Swedish *hänga*, Dutch and Modern High German *hangen*; DRA. 682; Gf. IV, 764; Rchth. 829), conjugation I, *haihah, haihahun, hahans*: to remove; leave in doubt, αἴρειν: Joan. X, 24.

**AT-HAHAN**, to let down, lower, χαλᾷν: Luc. V, 4; Cor. II, XI, 33.

**US-HAHAN**, to hang up; *ushahan sik*, to hang oneself, ἀπάγγεσθαι: Mth. XXVII, 5.

**HAHAN**, conjugation II: to hang, ἐκκρέμασθαι: Luc. XIX, 48.

**FAUR-HAH** (*faurahah*, Mc. XV, 38), neuter: veil, curtain, καταπέτασμα: Mth. XXVII, 51; Mc. XV, 38.

**GA-HAHJO**, adverb: consecutively, in order, καθεξῆς: Luc. I, 3.

**HAIBRAIUS**, masculine proper name: Hebrew, Ἑβραῖος: Cor. II, XI, 12; Phlpp. III, 5, 11.

**HAIDUS** (Old Saxon *hed*, Anglo-Saxon *had*, Old High German *hait, heiti*, Old French . . . *hede, heid*; Gr. II, 497, 642; Gf. IV, 802; Rchth. 802), masculine: manner, mode, τρόπος: Phlpp. I, 18; Thess. II, II, 3; Tim. II, III, 8.

**HAIHS** (compare Latin *caecus*), adjective: one-eyed, μονόφθαλμος: Mc. IX, 47.

**HAIþI** (Old Norse *heidi*, Anglo-Saxon *haeð*, Old High German *haida*, Old French *heidena*, English *heath*, Swedish *hed*, Danish *hede*, Dutch *heyde*, Modern High German *haide*; Gr. III, 395; DRA. 499; Gf. IV, 809; Rchth. 813), feminine: field, ἀγρός: Mth. VI, 28, 30; Luc. XV, 15; XVII, 7, 31.

**HAIþIVISKS**, adjective: wild, ἄγριος: Mc. I, 6.

**HAIþNO** (Old Norse *heidinn*, Old Saxon *hethin*, Anglo-Saxon *haeðen*, Old High German *heidan*, Old French *hethan*; Gf. IV, 810; Rchth. 812), feminine: a Gentile woman, Greek woman, Ἑλληνίς: Mc. VII, 26.

**HAILEIAS**, see *Helias*.

**HAILEISAIUS**, masculine proper name: Elisha, Ἑλισσαῖος: Luc. IV, 27.

**HAILS** (Old Norse *heill*, Anglo-Saxon *hal*, Old High German *heil*, English *hail, heal*, Old Saxon and Old French, Swedish *hel*, Danish *heel*, Dutch and Modern High German *heil*; Gf. IV, 861; Rchth. 803), adjective: healthy, healed, ὑγιής: Mc. V, 34; Joan. VII, 23; healthy, ὑγιαίνων: Luc. V, 31; VII, 10; XV, 27; Tim. I, I, 10; VI, 3; Tim. II, I, 13; IV, 3; Tit. I, 9; II, 1; vigorous, ἰσχύων: Mth. IX, 12; *hails visan*, “to be healthy,” ὑγιαίνειν: Tit. I, 13; *hails vairþan*, “to recover,” σώζεσθαι: Joan. XI, 12; at the beginning of an address, “Hail!,” χαῖρε: Mc. XV, 18; Joan. XIX, 3.

**GA-HAILS**, whole, complete, ὁλόκληρος: Thess. I, V, 23.

**UN-HAILS**, sick, infirm, ἄρρωστος: Cor. I, XI, 30; weak, ἀσθενῶν: Luc. IX, 2; ill, κακῶς ἔχων: Luc. V, 31.

**UN-HAILI**, neuter: sickness, disease, μαλακία: Mth. IX, 35; *unhaili haban*, “to be ill,” κακῶς ἔχειν: Mth. IX, 12.

**HAILJAN**, conjugation II: to heal, θεραπεύειν: Mth. IX, 35; Mc. III, 2, 15; Luc. IV, 23; ἰᾶσθαι: Luc. V, 17; *hailjan sik*, passive, “to be healed,” ἰαθῆναι: Luc. VI, 18.

**GA-HAILJAN**, the same: θεραπεύειν: Mth. VIII, 7, 16; Mc. I, 34; III, 10; VI, 5, 13; Luc. IV, 40; VI, 18; VII, 21; IX, 1; ἰᾶσθαι: Luc. IX, 2, 11, 42.

**GA-HAILNAN**, conjugation III: to be healed, ἰαθῆναι: Mth. VIII, 8, 13; Mc. V, 29; Luc. VII, 7; VIII, 47.

**HAIMS** (Old Norse *heimn*, Old Saxon *hem*, Anglo-Saxon *ham*, Old High German *heime, haim*, Old French *hem, him*, English *home*, Swedish *hem*, Danish *hjem*, Modern High German *heim*; compare κώμη; Gr. II, 496; III, 136, 393; Gf. IV, 946; Rchth. 794), feminine, plural *haimos*: village, town, κώμη: Mth. IX, 35; Mc. VI, 56; XI, 2; Luc. V, 17; VIII, 1; IX, 6; XII, 52, 56; XVII, 12; XIX, 30; Joan. XI, 1; field, ἀγρός: Mc. V, 14; *haimos jah baurgs*, “villages and towns,” κωμοπόλεις: Mc. I, 38.

**HAIMOþLI**, neuter: field, open country, ἀγρός: Mc. X, 29, 30.

**ANA-HAIMS**, adjective: at home, ἐνδημῶν: Cor. II, V, 9; *anahaims visan*, “to be at home,” ἐνδημεῖν: Cor. II, V, 8.

[Col. 1313] **AF-HAIMS**, away from home, a sojourner, ἐκδημῶν: Cor. II, V, 6, 9.

**HAIRAISIS** (Greek word): heresy, αἵρεσις: Gal. V, 20.

**HAIRDA** (Old Norse *hiörd*, Anglo-Saxon *heord*, Old Saxon and Old High German *herta*, English *herd*, Swedish *hiord*, Danish *hjord*, Dutch *herde*, Modern High German *heerde*; compare Latin *cohors*; Gr. II, 62; III, 475; Gf. IV, 1028), feminine: flock, ποίμνη: Luc. II, 8; herd, ἀγέλη: Mth. VIII, 30; Mc. V, 11, 13; Luc. VIII, 32.

**HAIRDEIS**, masculine: shepherd, ποιμήν: Mth. IX, 36; Luc. II, 8, 15, 18, 20; Joan. X, 2, 11, 12, 14, 16; Eph. IV, 11.

**HAIRþRA** (Old High German *herdar*, Swedish *härþar*, “shoulders,” Anglo-Saxon *haerðan*, “testicles”; Gr. III, 407; Gf. IV, 1030), neuter plural only: inward parts, affections, heart, σπλάγχνα: Cor. II, VI, 12; Philem. 12; see on this passage.

**HAIRUS** (Old Norse *hiör*, Anglo-Saxon *heor*, Old Saxon *heru*; Gr. I, 45; II, 460; III, 440; Schm. Hel. Gloss., p. 55), masculine: sword, μάχαιρα: Mth. X, 34; Mc. XIV, 43; Joan. XVIII, 10, 11; Rom. VIII, 35; XIII, 4; ῥομφαία: Luc. II, 35.

**HAIRTO** (Old Norse *hiarta*, Old Saxon *herta*, Anglo-Saxon *heorte*, Old High German *herza*, Old French *herte, hirte*, English *heart*, Swedish *hiarta, hjerta*, Danish *hjerte*, Dutch *hart*, Modern High German *herz*; Greek καρδία, Latin *cor, cordis*; Bopp 23, 81; Gr. III, 399; Gf. IV, 1043; Rchth. 817), neuter: heart, καρδία: Mth. V, 28; VI, 21; IX, 4; Mc. II, 6, 8; III, 5; IV, 15; VII, 6, 19, 21; VIII, 17; XI, 23; XII, 30, 33; Luc. I, 17, 51, 66; II, 19, 35, 51; III, 15; IV, 18; V, 22; VI, 45; VIII, 12, 15; IX, 47; X, 27; XVI, 15; Joan. XII, 40; XIV, 1, 27; XVI, 6, 22; Rom. IX, 2; X, 1, 6, 8, 9, 10; Cor. I, IV, 5; XIV, 25; Cor. II, I, 22; II, 4; III, 2, 3, 15; IV, 6; V, 12; VI, 11; VII, 3; VIII, 16; IX, 7; Gal. IV, 6; Eph. I, 18; III, 17; IV, 18; V, 19; VI, 22; Phlpp. IV, 7; Col. II, 23, in this passage; Thess. I, II, 17; III, 13; Thess. II, II, 17; III, 5; Tim. I, I, 5; Tim. II, II, 22; Skeir. VI, d.

**ARMA-HAIRTS**, adjective: compassionate, tender-hearted, εὔσπλαγχνος: Eph. IV, 32.

**HAUH-HAIRTS**, proud, self-willed, αὐθάδης: Tit. I, 7; arrogant, ὑπερήφανος: Tim. II, III, 2.

**HRAINJA-HAIRTS**, pure in heart, καθαρὸς τῇ καρδίᾳ: Mth. V, 8.

**ARMA-HAIRTEI**, feminine: mercy, ἔλεος: Luc. I, 50, 54, 58; Rom. XV, 9; Eph. II, 4; Col. III, 12; Tim. II, I, 18.

**HAUH-HAIRTEI**, pride, ὑπερηφανία: Mc. VII, 22.

**HARDU-HAIRTEI**, hardness of heart, σκληροκαρδία: Mc. X, 5.

**ARMA-HAIRTIþA**, feminine: compassion, mercy, ἔλεος: Mth. IX, 13; Luc. I, 72; almsgiving, ἐλεημοσύνη: Mth. VI, 4.

**HAIRODIAS**, i.e. Herodias; see under *Herodes*.

**HAIS**, neuter: torch, λαμπάς: Joan. XVIII, 3.

\***HAISTS** (is it to be referred to *Haitan*? Wellmann, *Goth. Adject.*, p. 12), adjective. **US-HAISTS**, needy, poor, ὑστερηθείς: Cor. II, XI, 8.

**HAITAN** (Old Norse *heita*, Old Saxon *hetan*, Anglo-Saxon *hatan*, Old High German *haizan*, Old French, Swedish *heta*, Danish *hede*, Dutch *heeten*, Modern High German *heissen*; Gr. II, 498; Gf. IV, 1077; Rchth. 812), conjugation I, *haihait, haihaitun, haitans*:

1) to call, name, καλεῖν: Mth. V, 19; X, 25; XXVII, 8; Mc. XI, 17; Luc. I, 13, 31, 32, 35, 36, 59, 60, 61, 62, 76; II, 4, 21, 23; VI, 15, 46; VIII, 2; XV, 19, 21; XVI, 20; XIX, 2, 29; XX, 44; Rom. IX, 7, 25, 26; Cor. I, XV, 9; λέγειν (“to say”): Mth. IX, 9; XXVII, 17; Mc. XV, 7; Joan. IX, 11; XVIII, 10; Col. IV, 11. In the passive, “to be called, named,” also λέγεσθαι: Joan. XI, 16; χρηματίζειν (“to bear the name”): Rom. VII, 3; ὄνομά ἐστί τινι (“someone’s name is”): Luc. I, 26. Also *haitans ïm namin*: Joan. XVIII, 10; *haitans namin*, “by name,” ὀνόματι: Luc. XVI, 20.

2) to summon, call, καλεῖν: Mc. I, 20; Luc. VII, 39; XIV, 10, 12, 13, 16, 17, 24; Joan. X, 3; Cor. I, VII, 22; φωνεῖν (“to call aloud”): Mc. III, 31; Luc. XIV, 12; Joan. XI, 28; *aftra haitan*, to invite in return, ἀντικαλεῖν: Luc. XIV, 12; *faura haitans*, invited, κεκλημένος: Luc. XIV, 24.

[Col. 1314] 3) to command, order, κελεύειν: Mth. VIII, 18; XXVII, 64; Luc. XVIII, 40; εἰπεῖν (“to tell”): Mc. V, 43; X, 49; Luc. XIX, 15; ἐρωτᾶν (“to ask”): Luc. V, 3; διαστέλλεσθαι (“to give strict orders”): Mc. V, 43.

**ANA-HAITAN**, to invoke, with dative and accusative, ἐπικαλεῖσθαι: Cor. II, I, 23; Skeir. VIII, b; *bidai anahaitan*, the same: Rom. X, 13; Tim. II, II, 22; ἐρωτᾶν (“to request”): Thess. I, IV, 1.

**AND-HAITAN**:

1) to confess, acknowledge, ὁμολογεῖν: Mth. VII, 23; X, 32; Joan. IX, 22; XII, 42; Rom. X, 9, 10; Tim. I, VI, 12; Tit. I, 16; ἐξομολογεῖσθαι: Mc. I, 5; Rom. XIV, 11; XV, 9; Skeir. V, a.

2) to give thanks, ἐξομολογεῖσθαι: Luc. X, 21; ἀνθομολογεῖσθαι: Luc. II, 38.

**AT-HAITAN**, to call to oneself, καλεῖν: Luc. XIX, 13; προσκαλεῖσθαι: Mth. X, 1; Mc. III, 13, 23; VI, 7; VII, 14; VIII, 1, 34; X, 42; XV, 44; Luc. VII, 19; XV, 26; XVI, 5; XVIII, 16.

**GA-HAITAN**:

1) to call together, συγκαλεῖν: Mc. XV, 16; Luc. IX, 1; XV, 9.

2) to promise, ἐπαγγέλλεσθαι: Mc. XIV, 11; Tim. I, II, 10; Tit. I, 2; Skeir. III, c; V, b.

**FAURAGA-HAITAN**, to prepare, προκαταγγέλλειν (“to announce beforehand”): Cor. II, IX, 5.

**US-HAITAN**, to provoke, προκαλεῖν: Gal. V, 26.

**FAIR-HAITAN**, to confess; *þagk fairhaitan*, to promise thanks, χἀριν ἔχειν (“to be thankful”): Luc. XVII, 9.

**ANDA-HAIT**, neuter: confession, ὁμολογία: Cor. II, IX, 13; Tim. I, VI, 12, 13.

**BI-HAIT**, contention, ἐριθεία: Cor. II, XII, 20.

**GA-HAIT**, promise, ἐπαγγελία: Rom. IX, 4, 8, 9; XV, 8; Cor. II, I, 20; VII, 1; Gal. III, 29; IV, 23, 28; Eph. I, 13; II, 12; III, 6; Tim. I, IV, 8; Tim. II, I, 1.

**HAITI**, feminine: command, κέλευσμα: Thess. I, IV, 16; injunction, ἐπιταγή: Cor. I, VII, 6.

**BI-HAITJA**, masculine: boaster, ἀλαζών: Tim. II, III, 2; Tit. I, 7; see on this passage.

**DULGA-HAITJA**, creditor, lender, δανειστής: Luc. VII, 41.

**HAIFSTS**, feminine: contention, strife, ἔρις: Rom. XIII, 13; Gal. V, 20; Phlpp. I, 15; Tim. I, VI, 4; selfish rivalry, ἐριθεία: Phlpp. I, 16; II, 3; Skeir. IV, d; contest, ἀγών: Phlpp. I, 30; Tim. I, VI, 12; Tim. II, IV, 7; whispering (?) ψιθυρισμός: Cor. II, XII, 20.

**HAIFTSJAN**, conjugation II: to contend, struggle, ἀγωνίζεσθαι: Cor. I, IX, 25; Tim. I, VI, 12; Tim. II, IV, 7; to compete, ἀθλεῖν: Tim. II, II, 5.

**HAKUL** (Old Norse *hökull, hekla*, Anglo-Saxon *hacela*, Old High German *hachul*, Old French *hekil*; Gf. IV, 797; Rchth. 813), neuter: cloak, φαιλόνης: Tim. II, IV, 13.

**HALBS** (Old Norse *halfr*, Old Saxon *halba*, Anglo-Saxon *healf*, Old French and English, Swedish *half*, Danish *halv*, Old and Modern High German *halb*; Bopp 432; Gf. IV, 882; Rchth. 792), adjective: half, ἥμισυς: Mc. VI, 23; Luc. XIX, 8.

**HALBA**, feminine: half, part, μέρος: Cor. II, III, 10; IX, 3, in the expression *ïn þizai halbai* (ἐν τούτῳ τῷ μέρει), “in this respect.”

**HALDAN** (Old Norse *hallda*, Old Saxon and Anglo-Saxon *healdan*, Old High German *haltan*, English *hold*, Danish *holde*, Swedish *halda, hålla*, Dutch *houden*, Modern High German *halten*; compare Greek ἄλδειν; Gf. IV, 896), conjugation I, *haihald, haihaldun, haldans*: to feed, βόσκειν: Mth. VIII, 30, 33; Mc. V, 11, 14; Luc. VIII, 32, 34; XV, 15; to shepherd, ποιμαίνειν: Luc. XVII, 7; Cor. I, IX, 7.

**HALDIS**, see under *Hilþan*.

**HALþEI**, see under *Hilþan*.

**HALISAIV** (compare Gr. III, 218, 590), see under *Aivs*.

**HALKS**, adjective: poor, needy, wretched, πτωχός: Cor. I, XV, 10; Gal. IV, 9.

**HALLUS** (Old High German *hall*), masculine: rock, cliff, πέτρα: Rom. IX, 33.

**HALJA** (Old Norse *halr, hel*, Old Saxon *hellia*, Anglo-Saxon *hell*, Old High German *hella*, Old French *hille, helle*, English *hell*, Danish *helvede*, Swedish *helfvete*, Dutch *helle*, Modern High German *hölle*; Gr. II, 29; III, 354, 458; DM. 195, 461, 486; Gf. IV, 860; Rchth. 814), feminine: Hades, the underworld, ᾅδης: Mth. XI, 23; Luc. X, 15; XVI, 23; Cor. I, XV, 55.

**HALS** (Old Norse, Anglo-Saxon, Old High German, Old [Col. 1315] Saxon, etc., *hals*; Gr. III, 402, 458, 496; Gf. IV, 927), masculine: neck, throat, τράχηλος: Luc. XV, 20.

**HALS-AGGA**, see under *Agga*.

**SLA-HALS** (compare Old Norse *hals*, “a strong man”), quarrelsome, a striker, πλήκτης: Tim. I, III, 3; Tit. I, 7.

**FREI-HALS** (*freijhals*, Cor. II, III, 17, in this passage; Gal. II, 4, in this passage; Old Norse *frials*, Anglo-Saxon *freols*, Old High German *frihals*, Swedish *fräls*; Gr. II, 630; DRA. 282), free person; freedom, ἐλευθερία: Cor. II, III, 17; Gal. II, 4; V, 1, 13; Eph. III, 12.

**HALTS** (Old Norse *halltr*, Anglo-Saxon *healt*, Old High German *halz*, Old Saxon, Old French, English, Swedish, Danish *halt*; compare Latin *claudus*, Greek χωλός; Gf. IV, 929; Rchth. 794), adjective: lame, χωλός: Mth. XI, 5; Mc. IX, 45; Luc. VII, 22; XIV, 13, 21.

\***HAM** (Old Norse *hamr*, Old Saxon . . . *hamo*, Anglo-Saxon *hama*, Old French *homa, hama*, Old High German *hamo, hemidi*, Danish *ham*, Old High German *hemde*; Gr. II, 55; III, 447, 496; Gf. IV, 932, 938; Rchth. 823), neuter, or masculine *hams*: skin, hide, covering of the body.

**ANA-HAMON**, conjugation II: to put on, ἐπενδύεσθαι: Cor. II, V, 4.

**AND-HAMON**, to put off, ἀπεκδύειν: Col. II, 15.

**AF-HAMON**, to put off, ἐκδύεσθαι: Cor. II, V, 4.

**GA-HAMON**, to put on, change, ἐνδύεσθαι: Rom. XIII, 14; Cor. I, XV, 53; Gal. III, 27; Eph. IV, 24; VI, 11; Col. III, 10, 12; Thess. I, V, 8.

**UFAR-HAMON**, to put on over, ἐπενδύεσθαι: Cor. II, V, 2.

**HANA** (Old Norse *hani*, Anglo-Saxon *hana*, Old French *hona*, Old Saxon and Old High German *hano*, English *hen*, Swedish and Danish *hane*, Dutch *haen*, Modern High German *hahn*; Gr. II, 42; III, 327; Gf. IV, 958; Rchth. 823), masculine: cock, rooster, ἀλέκτωρ: Mth. XXVI, 74, 75; Mc. XIV, 68, 72; Joan. XIII, 38; XVIII, 27.

**HANDUS** (Old Norse *hönd*, Old High German *hant*, Old Saxon, Anglo-Saxon, Old French, English, Dutch, Modern High German *hand*, Swedish *hånd*, Danish *haand*; Gr. II, 35, 458; III, 403; Gf. IV, 965; Rchth. 823), feminine: hand, χείρ: Mth. V, 30; VIII, 3, 15; IX, 18, 25; Mc. I, 31, 41; III, 1, 3, 5; V, 23, 41; VI, 2, 5; VII, 2, 3, 5, 32; VIII, 23, 25; IX, 27, 31, 43; X, 16; XIV, 41, 46; Luc. I, 66, 71, 74; III, 17; IV, 11, 40; V, 13; VI, 1, 6, 8, 10; VIII, 54; IX, 44, 62; XV, 22; XX, 19; Joan. VII, 30; X, 28, 29, 39; XI, 44; Rom. X, 21; Cor. I, XII, 15, 21; XVI, 21; Cor. II, XI, 33; Gal. VI, 11; Eph. IV, 28; Col. IV, 19; Thess. I, IV, 11; Thess. II, III, 17; Tim. I, II, 8; IV, 14; V, 22; Tim. II, I, 6.

**HANDU-VAURHTS**, see under *Vaurkjan*.

**UNHANDU-VAURHTS**, see under *Vaurkjan*.

**LAUS-HANDUS**, adjective: empty, empty-handed, κενός: Mc. XII, 3.

**HANDUGS** (Old Norse *höndugr*), adjective, comparative *handugoza*: skillful, wise, σοφός: Cor. I, I, 20, 25.

**HANDUGEI**, feminine: prudence, wisdom, discernment, σοφία: Mth. XI, 19; Mc. VI, 2; Luc. II, 40; VII, 35; Rom. XI, 33; Cor. I, I, 20, 21, 22, 24; Cor. II, I, 12; Eph. I, 8, 17; III, 10; Col. I, 9, 28; II, 23; III, 16; IV, 5.

**HANSA** (Old and Modern High German *hansa*, English *hans*; Gr. III, 473; Gf. IV, 978), feminine: crowd, multitude, πλῆθος: Luc. VI, 17; cohort, σπεῖρα: Mc. XV, 16; Joan. XVIII, 3.

**HANFS** (Old High German *hamf*; compare Old Saxon *haf*; Gf. IV, 955; Schmell. *Hel. Gloss.*, p. 49), adjective: crippled, having only one hand, κυλλός: Mc. IX, 43.

**HAUBIþ** (*haubid*, Luc. VII, 46; Joan. XIX, 2; Old Norse *höfud*, Old Saxon *hobid, hovid*, Anglo-Saxon *heafod*, Old High German *houbid*, Old French *haved*, English *head*, Swedish *hufvud*, Danish *hovede*, Modern High German *haupt*; Greek κεφαλή, Latin *caput*; Bopp 80; Gr. III, 398, 461, 498; Gf. IV, 755; Rchth. 798), neuter: head, κεφαλή: Mth. V, 36; VI, 17; VIII, 20; X, 30; Mc. VI, 24, 27, 28; XV, 19, 29; Luc. VII, 38, 46; IX, 58; Joan. XIX, 2; Rom. XII, 20; Cor. I, XI, 3, 4, 5, 12, 21; Eph. I, 22; IV, 15; V, 23; Col. I, 18; [Col. 1316] II, 19; *haubiþ afmaitan*, see under *Maïtan*; *haubiþ vaihstins*, “cornerstone,” κεφαλὴ γωνίας: Mc. XII, 10; Luc. XX, 17.

**HAUHS** (Old Norse *há*, Old Saxon *hoh*, Anglo-Saxon *heah*, Old High German *hoh*, Old French *hach, hag*, English *high*, Swedish *hög*, Danish *hoj*, Dutch *hoog*, Modern High German *hoch*; Gr. II, 50; Gf. IV, 772; Rchth. 789), adjective, comparative *hauhiza*, superlative *hauhista*: high, ὑψηλός; highest, ὕψιστος: Mc. V, 7; IX, 2; Luc. I, 32, 35, 76; IV, 5; VI, 35; VIII, 28; XVI, 15.

**HAUHABA**, adverb: highly; *hauhaba hugjan*, “to think highly,” ὑψηλοφρονεῖν: Rom. XI, 20.

**HAUHIS**, comparative adverb: higher, ἀνώτερον: Luc. XIV, 10.

**HAUH-HAIRTS**, see under *Hairto*.

**HAUH-HAIRTEI**, see under *Hairto*.

**HAUHIþA**, feminine:

1) height, the highest point, ὕψος: Luc. I, 78; “high things,” τὰ ὑψηλά: Rom. XII, 16.

2) exaltation, lofty thing, ὕψωμα: Rom. VIII, 39; Cor. II, X, 5.

3) honor, glory, δόξα: Luc. XIV, 10; Joan. VII, 18.

**HAUHEI**, feminine: height, ὕψος: Eph. III, 18.

**HAUHISTI**, neuter: the height, the highest place, τὸ ὕψιστον: Mc. XI, 10; Luc. II, 14; XIX, 38.

**HAUHJAN**, conjugation II:

1) to raise, exalt, ὑψοῦν: Luc. XIV, 11; XVIII, 14; Joan. XII, 32.

2) to magnify, glorify, exalt in praise, δοξάζειν: Mth. V, 16; VI, 2; Luc. XVII, 15; Joan. VII, 39; VIII, 54; XI, 4; XII, 28; XIII, 31, 32; XIV, 13; XV, 8; XVI, 14; XVII, 1, 4, 5, 10; Rom. XV, 6, 9.

**US-HAUHJAN**, to raise, exalt, ὑψοῦν: Mth. XI, 23; Luc. I, 52; X, 15; XIV, 11; XVIII, 14; Joan. VIII, 28; XII, 32, 34; Cor. II, XI, 7; to glorify, ἐνδοξάζειν: Thess. II, I, 10.

**US-HAUHNAN**, conjugation III: to be exalted, glorified, ἐνδοξάζεσθαι: Thess. II, I, 12 (perhaps also verse 10).

**UFAR-HAUHJAN**, to become proud; past participle “having become conceited,” τυφωθείς: Tim. I, III, 6.

**HAUHEINS**, feminine:

1) exaltation;

2) glory, honor, δόξα: Joan. VIII, 50, 54; IX, 24; XI, 4; XII, 43; *lausa hauheïns*, vain glory, κενοδοξία: Phlpp. II, 3.

**HAUIþ**, see on Tim. I, II, 11.

**HAUNS** (Anglo-Saxon *hyuan, henan*, Old French *hena*, Old Saxon *honda*, Old High German *honjan*, Swedish *hån*, Dutch *hoon*, Modern High German *hohn*; Gf. IV, 691; Rchth. 807), adjective: humble, lowly, ταπεινός: Cor. II, X, 1.

**HAUNJAN**, conjugation II: to humble, ταπεινοῦν: Cor. II, XI, 7; Phlpp. IV, 12.

**GA-HAUNJAN**, the same: Cor. II, XII, 21; Phlpp. II, 8.

**HAUNEINS**, feminine: humiliation, lowliness, ταπείνωσις: Phlpp. III, 21; humility, ταπεινοφροσύνη: Eph. IV, 2; Col. II, 18, 23; III, 12; *hauneins gahugdais*, the same: Phlpp. II, 3.

**HAURDS** (Old Norse *hurd*, Anglo-Saxon *hyrdel*, Old High German *hurt*; Gr. II, 62; III, 430; Gf. IV, 1030), feminine: door, θύρα: Mth. VI, 6; Cor. I, XVI, 9; Cor. II, II, 12; Col. IV, 3; Neh. VII, 1.

**HAURI** (compare Old High German *hyr*, Anglo-Saxon *heorð*, Modern High German *heerd*), neuter: coal, ἄνθραξ: Rom. XII, 20; plural *haurja*, coals, ἀνθρακιά: Joan. XVIII, 18.

**HAURN** (Old Norse, Old High German, Anglo-Saxon, Old Saxon, Old French, Swedish, Danish, and Modern High German *horn*; Greek κέρας, Latin *cornu*; Gr. II, 62; III, 409, 461, 498; Gf. IV, 1035; Rchth. 826), neuter:

**þUT-HAURN**, trumpet, bugle, σάλπιγξ: Cor. I, XV, 52; Thess. I, IV, 16.

**HAURNJAN**, conjugation II: to sound a trumpet, σαλπίζειν: Mth. VI, 2; IX, 23.

**þUT-HAURNJAN**, the same: Cor. I, XV, 52.

**HAURNJA**, masculine: trumpeter, σαλπιγκτής: Mth. IX, 23; see this passage.

**HAUSJAN** (*hausjon*, Mc. IV, 33; Luc. V, 15; Joan. VI, 60; Tim. II, II, 14; Old Norse *heyra*, Old Saxon *horian*, Anglo-Saxon *hyran*, Old High German *horran*, Old French *hera, hora*, English *hear*, Swedish *hora*, Danish *höre*, Dutch *hooren*, Modern High German *hören*; Latin *audire*; [Col. 1317] Gf. IV, 1001; Rchth. 808), conjugation II: to hear, ἀκούειν:

a) absolutely, or with following *þatei*, *ei*, infinitive, and also participle: Mth. V, 21, 27, 33; XXVII, 13; Mc. III, 21; IV, 3, 9, 12, 23, 33; VI, 2, 55; VII, 16; XII, 29; XVI, 11; Luc. I, 58; V, 15; VI, 27, 49; VIII, 8, 12, 13, 18; XVIII, 6; Joan. VI, 60; IX, 27, 35; XI, 6, 20, 29; XII, 18, 34; XIV, 28; Rom. X, 18; Gal. I, 23; Eph. IV, 29; Phlpp. II, 26; Col. I, 9; Thess. II, III, 11; Tim. II, II, 14; Neh. VI, 16.

b) with the accusative: Mth. VII, 24, 26; Mc. IV, 16, 18, 20; XIV, 64; Luc. I, 41; IV, 23, 28; V, 1; VI, 47; IX, 9; X, 24; XV, 1; XVI, 2; Joan. VII, 32; VIII, 26, 38, 40, 43, 47; IX, 40; XIV, 24; XV, 15; XVI, 13; XVIII, 20; Cor. II, XII, 4; Eph. III, 2; IV, 21; Phlpp. I, 30; Col. I, 23; Tim. II, I, 13; II, 2.

c) with the dative, to obey: Mc. VI, 11, 20; VII, 14; IX, 7; XII, 37; Luc. II, 46; VI, 17; IX, 35; X, 16; XIX, 48; Joan. IX, 31; X, 3, 8, 20, 27; XII, 47; Rom. X, 14; Tim. I, IV, 16; Skeir. III, b; VI, a.

d) with the genitive, in place of the dative and accusative only: Luc. II, 47; Joan. VI, 60; VII, 40; X, 16; XVIII, 37; XIX, 13.

e) concerning (περί with genitive) someone or something:

aa) *fram* with dative: Mc. III, 21; Luc. XVI, 2.

bb) *bi* with accusative: Luc. IX, 9.

f) from, at the hands of (παρά with genitive and dative) someone or something:

aa) *fram* with dative: Joan. VII, 51; VIII, 38, 40; Skeir. II, b.

bb) *at* with dative: Joan. XV, 15; Tim. II, I, 13; II, 2.

**AND-HAUSJAN**, to hear, obey, with dative, ἀκούειν: Mc. VI, 20; Joan. IX, 31; XI, 41, 42; ἐπακούειν (“to hear favorably”): Cor. II, VI, 2; εἰσακούειν (“to hear, heed”): Mth. VI, 7; Luc. I, 13; Cor. I, XIV, 21; ὑπακούειν (“to obey”): Luc. XVII, 6.

**GA-HAUSJAN**, to hear, ἀκούειν:

a) absolutely, or with a following participle: Mth. VIII, 10; IX, 12; XXVII, 47; Mc. II, 17; III, 8; IV, 9, 15, 23, 24; VI, 14, 16, 29; VII, 16; VIII, 18; X, 41, 47; XI, 15, 18; XII, 28; XIV, 11, 58; XV, 35; Luc. II, 18; VII, 29; VIII, 8, 10, 14, 50; XIV, 35; XVIII, 26, 36; XX, 16, 45; Joan. VI, 60; IX, 32; XI, 4; XII, 12, 29; Cor. II, XII, 6.

b) also emphatically, by contrast with being deaf: Mth. XI, 5; Mc. VII, 37.

c) with the accusative: Mth. X, 27; XI, 2, 4 (15); XXVI, 65; Mc. V, 36; Luc. VII, 9, 22; VIII, 15, 21; IX, 7; X, 24; XIV, 15; XV, 25; XVI, 14; XVIII, 22, 23; XIX, 11; Joan. III, 32; V, 37; XIX, 8; Eph. I, 13, 15; Phlpp. IV, 9; Skeir. VI, d. Luc. II, 20 also belongs here: *ïn allaize þizeei gahausidedun jah gasewun*, “concerning all the things which they had heard and seen”; this is attraction. For *gahausjan*, unlike the simple *hausjan*, does not occur with the genitive.

d) concerning (περί with genitive) someone or something: Mc. V, 27; VII, 25; Luc. VII, 3; Phlpp. I, 27 (for here the Gothic translator read ἀκούσω περὶ ὑμῶν, “I may hear concerning you”).

e) from, at, or out of (παρά with genitive) someone: Joan. VI, 45; Skeir. IV, d.

**UF-HAUSJAN**, to obey, ὑπακούειν: Mth. VIII, 27; Mc. I, 27; IV, 41; Luc. VIII, 25; Rom. X, 16; Col. III, 20, 22; Thess. II, I, 8; III, 14; Skeir. I, c; to submit oneself, ὑποτάσσεσθαι: Luc. II, 51; X, 17, 20; Rom. VIII, 7; X, 3; XIII, 1, 5; Cor. I, XVI, 16; Eph. V, 21, 22, 24; Col. III, 18; to be persuaded, πείθεσθαι: Gal. III, 1; V, 7; to be devoted to, ἀντέχεσθαι: Mth. VI, 24; participle *ufhausjands*, obedient, ὑπήκοος: Cor. II, II, 9; Phlpp. II, 8; “one who is in submission,” ὁ ἐν ὑποταγῇ: Tim. I, III, 4.

**HAUSEINS**, feminine:

1) hearing, ἀκοή: Tim. II, IV, 3, 4.

2) hearing, proclamation, ἀκοή: Joan. XII, 38; Rom. X, 16; Thess. I, II, 13.

**GA-HAUSEINS**, hearing, ἀκοή: Rom. X, 17; Gal. III, 2, 5.

**UF-HAUSEINS**, obedience, ὑπακοή: Cor. II, VII, 15; X, 5, 6; Philem. 21; submission, ὑποταγή: Cor. II, IX, 13; Tim. I, II, 11.

**UFAR-HAUSEINS**, disobedience, παρακοή: Cor. II, X, 6.

**HARDUS** (Old Norse *hardr*, Anglo-Saxon *heard*, Old High German *hart*, Old French *herd*, Old Saxon, English, Dutch *hard*, Swedish *hård*, Danish *haard*, Modern High German *hart*; Gr. II, 62; Gf. IV, 1019; Rchth. 810), adjective, comparative *hardiza*: hard, σκληρός: Joan. VI, 60; harsh, αὐστηρός: Luc. XIX, 21; Skeir. VI, c.

**HARDUBA** (*hardaba*, Cor. II, XIII, 10; see on this passage), [Col. 1318] adverb: harshly, severely, δεινῶς: Mth. VIII, 6; abruptly, sharply, ἀποτόμως: Cor. II, XIII, 10.

**HARDU-HAIRTEI**, see under *Hairto*.

**GA-HARDJAN**, conjugation II: to harden, σκληρύνειν: Rom. IX, 18.

**HARJIS** (Old Norse *hir*, Anglo-Saxon *here*, Old High German and Old Saxon *heri*, Old French *hiri, her*, Dutch and Modern High German *heer*; Gr. II, 459; III, 472, 498; DRA. 292; Gf. IV, 983; Rchth. 815), masculine: army, host, multitude, στρατιά: Luc. II, 13; legion, λεγεών: Luc. VIII, 30.

**HATAN** (*hatjan*, Mth. V, 44; Luc. VI, 27; see on this passage; Old Norse *hata*, Old Saxon *hatan*, Anglo-Saxon *hatian*, Old High German *hazen, hazzon*, Old French *hatia*, English *hate*, Swedish *hata*, Danish *hade*, Dutch *haeten*, Modern High German *hader, hassen*; compare Latin *odi*; Gf. IV, 1069; Rchth. 797), conjugation II: to hate, μισεῖν: Mth. V, 44; Luc. I, 71; VI, 27, in this passage; Rom. VII, 15; participle *hatands*, enemy, foe, ἐχθρός: Luc. VI, 27.

**HATIS**, neuter: wrath, ὀργή: Luc. III, 7; Eph. II, 3, in this passage; V, 6; Col. III, 6, 8; Thess. I, II, 16; V, 9; anger, θυμός: Gal. V, 20; Eph. IV, 31; Skeir. VIII, b.

**HATIZON**, conjugation II: to be angry, χολᾶν: Joan. VII, 23.

**HAVI** (Old Norse *ha, hey*, Old Saxon *houwe*, Anglo-Saxon *heg*, Old High German *hawi*, Old French *ha, hai*, English *hay*, Swedish *hö*, Danish
ho, Dutch *hoy*, Modern High German *heu*; Gr. III, 413; Gf. IV, 708; Rchth. 789), neuter, grass, hay, χόρτος: Matt. VI, 30; John VI, 10; *Skeireins* VII, b.

HAFJAN (Old Norse *hefja*, Old Saxon *hebbian*, Anglo-Saxon *hebban*, Old High German *haban, hefjan*, Old French *heva*, English *heave*, Swedish *häfva*, Danish *haeve*, Dutch *heffen, heven*, Modern High German *heben*; Gr. II, 9; Gf. IV, 814; Rchth. 813), conjugation I, anomalous: *hof, hofun, hafans*, to lift, raise up, αἴρειν: Mark II, 3.

AND-HAFJAN, to answer, ἀποκρίνεσθαι: Matt. VIII, 8; XI, 4, 25; XXV, 40, 45; XXVI, 66; XXVII, 12, 14; Mark III, 33; VII, 6, 28; VIII, 4, 28, 29; IX, 5, 17, 19, 38; X, 3, 5, 20, 24, 29; XI, 22, 29, 30, 33; XII, 17, 24, 28, 29, 34, 35; XIV, 48, 60, 61; XV, 2, 4, 5, 12; Luke I, 19, 60; III, 11, 16; IV, 4, 8, 12; V, 5, 22, 31; VI, 3; VII, 22, 40, 43; IX, 19, 20; X, 28; XV, 29; XVII, 17, 20, 37; XIX, 40; XX, 7, 24, 39; John VI, 7, 26, 29, 43, 68, 70; VII, 16, 20, 21, 46, 47, 52; VIII, 14, 19, 33, 34, 39, 48, 49, 54; IX, 3, 11, 20, 25, 27, 30, 34, 36; X, 25, 32, 33, 34; XI, 9; XII, 30, 34; XIII, 26, 36, 38; XIV, 23; XVI, 31; XVIII, 5, 8, 20, 22, 23, 30, 34, 35, 36, 37; XIX, 7, 12; Col. IV, 6; *Skeireins* VIII, a, b, d; ὑπολαμβάνειν, “to take up [the matter],” Luke X, 30.

AT-HAFJAN, to take down, καθαιρεῖν: Mark XV, 36.

US-HAFJAN, to lift up, raise, αἴρειν: Mark II, 12; Luke V, 24, 25; IX, 17; XVII, 13; John XI, 41; ἐπαίρειν, “to raise,” Luke VI, 20; XVI, 23; XVIII, 13; John VI, 5; XIII, 18; XVII, 1; 2 Cor. X, 5; 1 Tim. II, 8; *ushafjan sik*, to raise oneself, αἴρεσθαι: Mark XI, 23; μεταβαίνειν, “to depart,” Matt. XI, 1; ἐμβατεύειν, “to enter into,” Col. II, 18.

UFAR-HAFJAN, to exalt; *ufarhafjan sik*, to exalt oneself, ὑπεραίρεσθαι: 2 Thess. II, 4.

UFAR-HAFNAN, conjugation III, to be exalted, to be proud, ὑπεραίρεσθαι: 2 Cor. XII, 7.

ANDA-HAFTS, feminine: 1) answer, *Skeireins* VIII, b; 2) judgment, decision, ἀπόκριμα: 2 Cor. I, 9; 3) defence, ἀπολογία: 1 Cor. IX, 3.

HAFTS, I. see under Haban; II. see under Hafjan.

HEþJO (English *hut*, Swedish *hydda*, Modern High German *Hütte*; Gr. III, 428), feminine, inner room, chamber, ταμιεῖον: Matt. VI, 6.

HEITO (Old Norse *heitr*, Old Saxon *het*, Anglo-Saxon *hat, haetu*, Old High German *heiz*, Old French *het*, English *heat, hot*, Swedish *hetta*, Danish *hede*, Modern High German *heiss, Hizze*; Gr. II, 45; Gf. IV, 1074; Rchth. 812), feminine, fever; *ïn heitom*, “being feverish,” πυρέσσων: Matt. VIII, 14.

*HEIV (Old Saxon *hiuua*, “wife,” *hiuuiski*, “household”; Anglo-Saxon *hiwa*, English *hive*; compare Old High German *hiwjan*; Gf. IV, 1063; Schm. II, 132, 259), neuter? house, household.

HEIVA-FRAUJA, see under Frauja.

[Col. 1319]

HELEI, masculine proper name, Ἡλεὶ, Heli: Luke III, 23.

HELEI (Hebrew vocative), Ἠλί, “Eli”: Matt. XXVII, 46.

HELIAS (*Helia*, Matt. XXVII, 49; *Heleias*, Luke IX, 19, 54; *Haileias*, Luke I, 17), masculine proper name, Ἠλίας, Elijah: Matt. XI, 14; XXVII, 47, 49; Mark VIII, 28; IX, 4, 5, 12; XV, 36; Luke I, 17; IV, 25, 26; IX, 19, 33, 54.

HER (Old Norse, Old Saxon, Anglo-Saxon, Danish *her*, English *here*, Modern High German *her, hier*), see under His.

HER, masculine proper name, Ἤρ, Er: Luke III, 28.

HERODES (*Herodis*, Mark VI, 20, 21; Luke IX, 7), masculine proper name, Ἡρῴδης, Herod: Mark VI, 14, 18, 20, 21, 22; VIII, 15; Luke I, 5; III, 1, 19; VIII, 3; IX, 7; *Skeireins* III, a.

HERODIAS (*Hairodias*, Mark VI, 17), feminine proper name, Ἡρῳδιάς, Herodias: Mark VI, 17, 19, 22; Luke III, 19.

HERODIANUS, masculine, Ἡρῳδιανός, Herodian: Mark III, 6; XII, 13.

HIDRE (English *hither*, Danish *hid*), see under His.

HILþAN (Old Norse *halla, hallr, helldr*, Anglo-Saxon *heald, hold, hyld*, Old High German *hald, halt, hold*, Old French … *hald, helde, hulde, hold*, Swedish *helre, huld*, Danish *heller, huld*, Dutch *hulde*, Modern High German *huld, hold*; Gr. III, 590; Gf. IV, 892, 909, 913; Rchth. 790, 804, 823), conjugation I: *halþ, hulþun, hulþans*, to incline oneself; to be gracious, to favour.

HALDIS (Old Saxon *hald*), comparative adverb, willingly, rather: *Skeireins* IV, d.

VILJA-HALþEI, feminine, goodwill, kindness, προσωποληψία, “partiality”: Eph. VI, 9; Col. III, 25; πρόσκλισις, “bias”: 1 Tim. V, 21.

HULþS, adjective, kind, propitious, gracious; *hulþs visan*, “to be propitiated,” ἱλάσθηναι: Luke XVIII, 13.

UN-HULþO (DM. 164, 551, 553; Gf. IV, 915; according to Grimm’s judgment, *DM.* p. 554, the Gothic peoples especially represented demons to themselves as female. This is so true that among the most ancient Goths, even at the very time when the first translation of the New Testament was undertaken, evil spirits—δαιμόνια, δαίμονες—were of feminine gender, and only later, probably under the influence of Greek and Roman myths, were imagined as masculine. This opinion is confirmed by the fact that in the text which, from grammatical arguments, we have shown in the earlier *Prolegomena* to have been composed, only the feminine form occurs; whereas in the verified text of the later recension of Luke, both masculine and feminine forms are found. Hence in the Epistles [translated later] and in the fragments of Matthew’s Gospel copied from the Ambrosian codex [which indeed belong not to the recension of the Codex Argenteus, but to the later recension], *unhulþa* is used for the person of the devil—διάβολος and σατανᾶς. It follows that *unhulþo* in Matt. IX, 33 cannot, with Grimm, *DM.* 553, be changed into *unhulþa*; as to the construction which would support this alteration, we have dealt with it at that passage), feminine, malignant, impure, evil spirit, δαιμόνιον: Matt. VII, 22; IX, 33, 34; XI, 18; Mark I, 34, 39; III, 15, 22; VI, 13; VII, 26, 29, 30; IX, 38; XVI, 9; Luke IV, 33, 41; VII, 33; VIII, 2, 27, 30, 35, 38; IX, 1, 49; X, 17; John VII, 20; VIII, 24, 48, 49, 50, 51, 52; X, 21, 22; 1 Tim. IV, 1; δαίμων: Mark V, 12; *unhulþons haban*, “to be possessed,” δαιμονίζεσθαι: Mark I, 32; John X, 21.

UN-HULþA, masculine: 1) the same, δαιμόνιον: Luke IV, 35; VIII, 33; IX, 42; δαίμων: Luke VIII, 29; 2) devil, διάβολος: Matt. XXV, 41; Eph. IV, 27; VI, 11; 1 Tim. III, 6, 7; VI, 9; 2 Tim. II, 26; σατανᾶς, Satan: 1 Cor. V, 5.

HILMS (Old Norse *hialmr*, Anglo-Saxon, Old Saxon, Old French, Old High German, English, Dutch, Modern High German *helm*, Swedish and Danish *hjelm*; Gr. II, 29, 499; III, 445; Gf. IV, 845; Rchth. 805), masculine, or *hilm*, neuter, helmet, περικεφαλαία: Eph. VI, 17; 1 Thess. V, 8.

HILPAN (Old Norse *hialpa*, Old Saxon and Anglo-Saxon *helpan*, Old French *helfa*, Old High German *helfan*, English *help*, Swedish *hjelpa*, Danish *hjelpe*, Dutch *helpen*, Modern High German *helfen*; Gr. II, 32; Gf. IV, 918; Rchth. 805), conjugation I: *halp, hulpun, hulpans*, governing the genitive, to help, βοηθεῖν: Mark IX, 22, 24; συλλαμβάνεσθαι, “to assist,” Luke V, 7; συνυπουργεῖν, “to cooperate in service,” 2 Cor. I, 11.

GA-HILPAN, to help, βοηθεῖν: 2 Cor. VI, 2.

HIMINS (Old Norse *himin*, Old Saxon and Old High German *himil*, Old French *himul*, Swedish, Danish, and Modern High German *himmel*; Old Saxon *heban*, Anglo-Saxon *heofon*, English *heaven*; Gr. II, 55, 462; III, 393; DM. 398; Gf. IV, 938; Rchth. 814), masculine, heaven, οὐρανός: Matt. V, 16, 18, 19, 45, 48; VI, 1, 9, 10, 20, 26; VIII, 11, 20; XI, 11, 12, 23; Mark I, 10; IV, 32; VII, 34; VIII, 11; X, 21; XI, 25, 30, 31; XII, 25; XIII, 25, 27; XIV, 62; Luke II, 15; III, 21, 22; IV, 25; VI, 20, 23; VIII, 5; IX, 16, 54, 58; X, 15, 18, 20, 21; XV, 7, 18, 21; XVI, 17; XVII, 24, 29; XVIII, 13, 22; XIX, 38; XX, 4; John VI, 31, 32, 33, 38; XII, 28; XVII, 1; Rom. X, 6; 1 Cor. XV, 47; 2 Cor. V, 1, 2; XII, 2; Eph. I, 10, 20; III, 15; IV, 10; VI, 9; Phil. III, 20; Col. I, 16, 20, 23; IV, 1; 1 Thess. IV, 16; 2 Thess. I, 7; *Skeireins* IV, d; VI, c; *sa ufar himinam*, “he who is above heaven,” heavenly, ὁ οὐράνιος: Matt. VI, 26, 32.

HIMINA-KUNDS, see under Kuni.

*HIND (Anglo-Saxon *hindan*, English *behind*, Old High German *hintar*, Modern High German *hinten*; Gr. III, 177, 629; Gf. IV, 702), behind, after.

HINDANA, adverb governing the genitive, beyond, πέραν: Mark III, 8.

HINDAR (Old High German *hintar*; Gf. IV, 702; *Althd. Präpos.* 153 ff.), preposition construed with the dative and accusative; fundamentally it means “after,” and frequently also “across.”

I. With the accusative, in answer to “whither?”: behind, ὀπίσω: Mark VIII, 33; across, εἰς τὸ πέραν: Matt. VIII, 18; Mark V, 21; VIII, 13; ἀπό, “away from”: Matt. VIII, 34; Mark V, 17.

II. With the dative:

1. Locally, behind, across, in answer to “where?”: πέραν: John III, 26; VI, 22, 25 (Mark X, 1?); and after *qiman*, in answer to “whither?”: εἰς τὸ πέραν: Matt. VIII, 28; Mark V, 1; διὰ τοῦ πέραν, “through beyond”: Mark X, 1.

2. Figuratively: Luke IX, 13, *nist hindar uns maizo fimf hlaibam*—“we have no more than five loaves” (οὐκ εἰσὶν ἡμῖν πλεῖον ἢ πέντε ἄρτοι); and Rom. XIV, 5, *stojiþ dag hindar daga*—“he judges one day above another” (κρίνει ἡμέραν παρὰ ἡμέραν).

III. In compounds:

1. With verbs: *hindarleiþan*.

2. With nouns: *hindarveisei*.

3. With adjectives: *hindarveis, unhindarveis*.

HINDUMISTS (Old High German *hintarost*), superlative, farthest back, last, outermost, ἐξώτερος: Matt. VIII, 12.

*HINþAN (Anglo-Saxon *huntian*, English *hunt*, Danish *hente*; Gr. II, 35), conjugation I: *hanþ, hunþun, hunþans*, to take.

US-HINþAN, to take captive, αἰχμαλωτεύειν: Eph. IV, 8; see at that passage.

FRA-HINþAN, the same, αἰχμαλωτίζειν: Rom. VII, 23; 2 Cor. X, 5; preterite participle *frahunþans*, captive, αἰχμάλωτος: Luke IV, 18; *frahunþanana tiuhan*, “to lead away captive,” αἰχμαλωτίζειν: 2 Tim. III, 6.

MIþFRA-HUNþANS, preterite participle, fellow-captive, συναιχμάλωτος: Col. IV, 10; Philem. 23.

HUNþS, feminine (?), captivity, αἰχμαλωσία: Eph. IV, 8.

HIUHMA (*hiuma*, Luke VI, 17; VIII, 4; Gr. II, 50; III, 472), masculine, crowd, multitude, ὄχλος: Matt. VIII, 18; Luke V, 15; VI, 17; VIII, 4; XIV, 25; πλῆθος, “multitude”: Luke I, 10.

HIUFAN (Anglo-Saxon *heofian*, Old Saxon *hiovan*, Old High German *hiufan*; Gr. II, 18; Gf. IV, 837), conjugation I: *hauf, hufun, hufans*, to mourn, θρηνεῖν: Matt. XI, 17; Luke VII, 32; see that passage.

*HIS (Old Norse *hin, hitt, her*; Old Saxon and Anglo-Saxon *he*; Old French *hi, hit*; English *he, his, him, here, hither*; Swedish and Danish *han, hid, her*; Modern High German *heute, hier*, etc.; Latin *hic, huc*; Gr. I, 794; Gf. IV, 693; Rchth. 813), demonstrative pronoun, this, that.

HITA, neuter, this; and *ita nu*, “until that time, until this day”: *Skeireins* IV, b; *und hita*, “until now,” ἕως τοῦ νῦν: Mark XIII, 19; ἕως ἄρτι, “until now”: Matt. XI, 12; John XVI, 24; 1 Cor. XV, 6.

HIMMA, dative: a) masculine, *himma daga*, “to this day, today,” σήμερον: Matt. VI, 11, 30; Luke II, 11; [Col. 1321] IV, 21; V, 26; XIX, 5, 9; b) neuter, *fram himma nu*, “from this day, henceforth,” ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν: Luke I, 48; V, 10; *fram himma*, “from now on,” ἀπ’ ἄρτι: John XIII, 19; XIV, 7.

HINA, accusative: *und hina dag*, “until this day, today,” μέχρι τῆς σήμερον: Matt. XI, 23; ἄχρι τῆς σήμερον: 2 Cor. III, 14; ἕως τῆς σήμερον: Matt. XXVII, 8; ἕως σήμερον: 2 Cor. III, 15.

HIDRE (*hidrei*, Luke IX, 41), adverb, hither, here, ὧδε: Mark XI, 3; Luke IX, 41; XIV, 21.

HIRI, adverbial imperative (Bopp 123), “Come here! Approach!” δεῦρο: Mark X, 21; Luke XVIII, 22; ἔρχου, “come”: John XI, 34; *hiri ut*, “come forth,” δεῦρο ἔξω: John XI, 43.

HIRJATS, dual, “come here, you two!” δεῦτε: Mark I, 17.

HIRJIþ, plural, “come, come here!” δεῦτε: Mark XII, 7.

HER, adverb, here, hither, ὧδε: Matt. VIII, 29; Mark VI, 3; IX, 1, 5; XIII, 21; XVI, 6; Luke IV, 23; VII, 8; IX, 12, 27, 33; XVII, 21, 23; XIX, 27; John VI, 9, 25; XI, 21, 32; Col. IV, 9.

HIVI (Anglo-Saxon *hiv*, English *hew, hue*), neuter, colour, form, appearance, shape, μόρφωσις: 2 Tim. III, 5.

HLAHJAN (Old Norse *hlaea, hlatr*, Old Saxon *hlahan*, Anglo-Saxon *hlihan*, Old High German *hlahhan*, Old French *hlaka*, English *laugh*, Swedish *le*, Danish *lee*, Dutch *lacken*, Modern High German *lachen*; Gr. II, 12; Gf. IV, 1112; Rchth. 818), conjugation I, anomalous: *hloh, hlohun, hlahans*, to laugh, γελᾶν: Luke VI, 25.

BI-HLAHJAN, to mock, ridicule, καταγελᾶν: Matt. IX, 24; Mark V, 40; Luke VIII, 53.

UF-HLOHJAN, conjugation II, to make glad; in the passive, to rejoice, be made glad, laugh, γελᾶν: Luke VI, 21.

*HLAþAN (Old Norse and Old French *hlada*, Old Saxon, Anglo-Saxon, and Old High German *hladan*, English *load*, Swedish *ladda*, Danish *lade*, Modern High German *laden*; Gr. II, 10; Gf. IV, 1113; Rchth. 818), conjugation I: *hloþ, hloþun, hlaþans*; to load.

AF-HLAþAN, to load, heap up, σωρεύειν: 2 Tim. III, 6.

HLAIBA, see under Hlaifs.

HLAINS (Old Saxon *hlinon*, Modern High German *Lehne, lehnen*; compare Greek κλίνειν; Gf. IV, 1094), masculine, hill, βουνός: Luke III, 5.

HLAIV (Old Saxon *hlea, hleo*, Anglo-Saxon *hlaev*, Old High German *hleo*; Latin *clivus*; Gr. II, 462; Gf. IV, 1093; Schm., *Heliand Glossary*, p. 57), neuter, mound, tomb, μνημεῖον: Matt. XXVII, 60; Mark VI, 20; XV, 46; XVI, 2, 3, 5, 8; John XI, 17, 31; XII, 17; τάφος: Matt. XXVII, 61, 64, 66.

HLAIVASNA, feminine, occurring only in the plural *hlaivasnos*, tombs, graves, cemetery; μνημεῖα: Matt. VIII, 28; XXVII, 52, 53; μνήματα: Luke VIII, 27.

HLAIFS (*hlaibs*, Luke IV, 3; Old Norse *hleifr* and *leifr*, Old High German *hlaib*, Anglo-Saxon *hlaf*, English *loaf*, Modern High German *Laib*; Gr. III, 462; Gf. IV, 1111), masculine:

1. Bread, both generically and in individual instances; food, ἄρτος: Matt. VI, 11; Mark II, 26; III, 20; VI, 8; VII, 2, 5, 27; VIII, 4, 5, 6, 14; Luke IV, 3, 4; VI, 4; VII, 33; IX, 3, 13, 16; XIV, 15; XV, 17; John VI, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13, 23, 26, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 41, 48, 50, 51, 58; XIII, 18, 26; 1 Cor. X, 16, 17; XI, 23, 26, 27, 28; 2 Cor. IX, 10; 2 Thess. III, 8, 12; Neh. V, 14, 15, 18; *Skeireins* VII, b, c.

2. Morsel, crumb, ψωμίον: John XIII, 26, 27, 30.

GA-HLAIBA, masculine, companion, fellow-disciple, συμμαθητής: John XI, 16; fellow-soldier, συστρατιώτης: Phil. II, 25; companion, Neapolitan document. [BI-HLAIFS, masculine, the same, Gothic Calendar (?)]

HLAMM (Old Norse *klemma*, Old High German *klemmen*, Old Saxon *clemmian*, Swedish *klämma*, Danish, Modern High German *Klemme*; Gr. II, 33; Gf. IV, 557), neuter, or *hlamma*, feminine, snare, παγίς: 1 Tim. III, 7; VI, 9.

*HLAUPAN (Old Norse *hlaupa*, Old High German *hlaufan, loupen*, Old Saxon *hlopan*, Anglo-Saxon *hleapan*, English *leap*, Old French *hlapa, lapa*, Swedish *löpa*, Danish *lobe*, Dutch *loopen*, Modern High German *laufen*; Gf. IV, 1116; [Col. 1322] Rchth. 818), conjugation I: *hlaihlaup, hlaihlaupun, hlaupans*, to run.

US-HLAUPAN, to leap up, ἀναπηδᾶν: Mark X, 50.

HLAUTS (Old Norse *hlutr*, Old High German *hloz*, Anglo-Saxon, Old Saxon, and Old French *hlot*, English *lot*, Swedish *lott*, Danish and Dutch *lot*, Modern High German *Los*; Gf. IV, 1124; Rchth. 820), masculine, lot, κλῆρος: Mark XV, 24; Col. I, 12; *hlauts gasatiþs visan*, “to be allotted by lot,” κληροῦσθαι: Eph. I, 11; *hlauts ïmma urrann*, “the lot fell to him,” ἔλαχε: Luke I, 9.

HLAS (Old Norse *hlaezt*, “most pleasant”; compare Anglo-Saxon *glæd*, English *glad, glee*, Swedish and Danish *glad*, Modern High German *letzen*; compare Hlahjan), adjective, comparative *hlasoza*; glad, cheerful, ἱλαρός: 2 Cor. IX, 7; free from grief, ἄλυπος: Phil. II, 28.

HLASEI, feminine, cheerfulness, gladness, ἱλαρότης: Rom. XII, 8.

HLEþRA, see Hleiþra.

HLEIBJAN (Old Norse *hlifa*, Old High German *liban*; Gr. II, 39 ff.; Gf. IV, 1109; Schw. 375), to spare; to support, ἀντιλαμβάνεσθαι: Luke I, 54.

HLEIDUMA (English *left*, Modern High German *link*; compare Greek λαιός, Latin *laevus*; Gr. III, 629), adjective, left, ἀριστερός: Matt. VI, 3; 2 Cor. VI, 7; *hleidumei fera*, left side, left hand, τὰ εὐώνυμα: Matt. XXV, 41; also without *fera*: Mark X, 37, 40; XV, 27.

HLEIþRA (*hleþra*, John VII, 2; compare Danish *Lethra*; Old French *hlid, hlidia*, “to cover”; Gf. IV, 104; Rchth. 819), feminine, tent, hut, σκηνή: Luke IX, 33; XVI, 9; σκῆνος: 2 Cor. V, 1, 4.

HLEþRA-STAKEINS, see under Stikan.

UFAR-HLEIþRJAN, conjugation II, to build upon, ἐπισκηνοῦν: 2 Cor. XII, 9.

HLIJA (Old Norse *hlif, hlie*, Anglo-Saxon *hleo*, Old Saxon *hlea*; Gf. IV, 1094; Schm., *Heliand Glossary*, p. 37), masculine, tent, hut, σκηνή: Mark IX, 3.

HLIUþ (Old Norse *hlioþ*, Old Saxon *hlust*, Anglo-Saxon *hlyst*, Old High German *gahlosi*; compare Hliuma; Gf. IV, 1104), neuter, hearing, attention, quietness, ἡσυχία: 1 Tim. II, 11. (Our conjecture at this passage, for *hauïþa*, wrongly devised by Castiglione, is undoubtedly correct, since precisely this is found in *Völuspá* I: *hlióðs bið ek allar helgar kindir*, “I ask silence of all holy kindreds.”)

HLIUMA (Old Norse *hlioma, hlioþ*, Anglo-Saxon *hlyst*, Old Saxon *hlust*; compare Greek κλύειν; Bopp 124; Gf. IV, 1096), masculine, hearing, ἀκοή: Mark VII, 35; Luke VII, 1; 1 Cor. XII, 16.

HLIFAN (Greek κλέπτειν, Latin *clepere*, Modern High German … *klepper*; Bopp 127; DRA. 636), conjugation II, to steal, κλέπτειν: Matt. VI, 19; Mark X, 19; Luke XVIII, 20; Rom. XIII, 9; Eph. IV, 28.

HLIFTUS, masculine, thief, robber, κλέπτης: John X, 1.

HLUTRS (Old Saxon *hluttar*, Anglo-Saxon *hluter*, Old High German *hlutar*, Danish *lutter*, Modern High German *lauter*; Gf. IV, 1105), adjective, pure, clean, ἁγνός: 2 Cor. VII, 11.

HLUTREI, feminine, sincerity, εἰλικρίνεια: 2 Cor. I, 12.

HLUTRIþA, feminine, the same: 2 Cor. II, 17.

HLOHJAN, see under Hlahjan.

HNASQUS (Anglo-Saxon *hnesc*, English *nesh, nice*), adjective, soft, delicate, μαλακός: Matt. XI, 8; Luke VII, 25.

HNAIVS, see under Hneivan.

HNAUPNAN, see under Hnïupan.

HNEIVAN (Old Norse *hniga, hnegia*, Old High German *hnigan, nigan*, Old Saxon and Anglo-Saxon *hnigan*, Old French *hniga*, Danish *neje*, Dutch and Modern High German *neigen*; Gr. II, 17; Gf. IV, 1127; Rchth. 820), conjugation I: *hnaiv, hnivun, hnivans*, to bend; sink, κλίνειν: Luke IX, 12.

ANA-HNEIVAN, to bend oneself, bow down, κύπτειν: Matt. III, 11; Mark I, 7.

HNAIVS, adjective, lowly, ταπεινός: Rom. XII, 16.

HNAIVJAN, conjugation II:

1. To incline.

2. To humble, ταπεινοῦν: Luke XIV, 11; XVIII, 14; preterite participle *hnaiviþs*, lowly, ταπεινός: 2 Cor. VII, 6.

[Col. 1323]

ANA-HNAIVJAN, to recline, κλίνειν: Matt. VIII, 20.

GA-HNAIVJAN, to humble, ταπεινοῦν: Luke III, 5; XIV, 11; XVIII, 14; preterite participle *gahnaiviþs*, lowly, ταπεινός: Luke I, 52.

UF-HNAIVJAN, to subject, submit, ὑποτάσσειν: 1 Cor. XV, 26, 27, 28; Eph. I, 22; Phil. III, 21.

HNAIVEINS, feminine, humility, ταπείνωσις: Luke I, 48.

UF-HNAIVEINS, submission, ὑποταγή: Gal. II, 5.

*HNIUPAN (English *nip*, Swedish *niupa, nypa*, Dutch *knauwen*, Modern High German *kneipen*; Gr. II, 18), conjugation I: *hnaup, hnupun, hnupans*, to break.

DIS-HNIUPAN, to break apart, διαρρήσσειν: Luke VIII, 29.

DIS-HNAUPNAN, conjugation III, to be broken apart, ῥήσσεσθαι: Luke V, 6.

HNUTO (*hnuþo*, see at 2 Cor. XII, 7; that the Goth borrowed this from the Slavic language, see Castiglione, *Glossary on Corinthians*, at this word), feminine, whip, rod, σκώλοψ: 2 Cor. XII, 7.

HUGDS, see under Hugs.

HUGGRJAN (*hugrjan*, 1 Cor. IV, 11; Old Norse *hungr, hungra*, Old Saxon *hungar, hungrian, hingrian*, Old French *hunger, hungera*, Old High German *hungar, hungeren*, Anglo-Saxon, English, Swedish, Danish, and Modern High German *hunger*; Gr. II, 60; Gf. IV, 962; Rchth. 831), conjugation II, to hunger, πεινῆν: 1 Cor. IV, 11; impersonally, *huggreiþ mik*, “I hunger,” πεινῶ: John VI, 35.

HUHRUS, masculine, hunger, famine, λιμός: Luke IV, 25; XV, 14, 17; Rom. VIII, 35.

HUGS (Old Norse *hugr, hyggia*, Old Saxon *hugi, huggian*, Anglo-Saxon *hoga, hogian*, Old French *hei*, Old High German *hugu, hugi*, Swedish *hugher, hog*, Danish *hu*; compare Latin *cogitare*; Gr. II, 462; Gf. IV, 782; Rchth. 803), masculine, mind, understanding, νοῦς: Eph. IV, 17.

HUGJAN, conjugation II, to think, suppose, believe, νομίζειν: Matt. V, 17; Luke II, 44; 1 Tim. VI, 5; δοκεῖν, “to suppose”: John XI, 13; φρονεῖν, “to think”: Gal. V, 10; Phil. II, 2; III, 15; *Skeireins* VII, a; *hugjan hauhaba*, “to be high-minded,” ὑψηλοφρονεῖν: Rom. XI, 20; *vaila hugjan*, “to be well disposed,” εὐνοεῖν: Matt. V, 25.

AND-HUGJAN, see at Phil. III, 15.

AF-HUGJAN, to blind, bewitch, βασκαίνειν: Gal. III, 1.

GA-HUGJAN, to suppose, think, ἡγεῖσθαι: 1 Tim. I, 12.

FAURAGA-HUGJAN, to predetermine, προαιρεῖσθαι: 2 Cor. IX, 7.

UFAR-HUGJAN, to be proud, ὑπεραίρεσθαι: 2 Cor. XII, 7.

GA-HUGDS, feminine, thought, reflection, mind, διάνοια: Mark XII, 30; Luke I, 51; X, 27; Eph. IV, 18; Col. I, 21; νοῦς, “mind”: Rom. VII, 25; συνείδησις, “conscience”: 1 Cor. VIII, 12; X, 27; 1 Tim. III, 9; 2 Tim. I, 3.

HUGS (Anglo-Saxon *haga*, Swedish *hagh, hage*, Danish *have*, Modern High German *Gehege*), neuter, field, landed property: Aretine document.

HUZD (Old Norse *hodd*, Anglo-Saxon *hord, hordan*, Old High German *hort, gahurtjan*, English *hoard*; Gr. II, 463, 500; III, 452; DM. 543; Gf. IV, 1030), neuter, treasure, θησαυρός: Matt. VI, 19, 20, 21; Mark X, 21; Luke VI, 45; XVIII, 22; 2 Cor. IV, 7.

HUZDJAN, conjugation II, to store up treasure, θησαυρίζειν: Matt. VI, 19, 20; 2 Cor. XII, 14, and see at 1 Cor. XVI, 2.

HUHJAN, 1 Cor. XVI, 2, for *huzdjan*; see at that passage.

HUHRUS, see under Huggrjan.

HULþS, see under Hilþan.

HULJAN (Old Norse *hylia*, Anglo-Saxon *helan, heolster*, Old High German *huljan*, English *hele*, Swedish *hölja*, Danish *hylle*, Modern High German *hüllen, helen*; Latin *celare*; Gr. II, 29; Gf. IV, 843), conjugation II, to veil, περικαλύπτειν: Mark XIV, 65; κατακαλύπτειν: 1 Cor. XI, 6.

AND-HULJAN, to reveal, uncover, ἀποκαλύπτειν: Matt. X, 26; Luke II, 35; X, 21, 22; XVII, 30; John XII, 38; Eph. III, 5; Phil. III, 15, at that passage; 2 Thess. II, 3; ἀνακαλύπτειν: 2 Cor. III, 18; ἀποστεγάζειν, “to unroof”: Mark II, 4; preterite participle *andhuliþs*, unveiled, ἀκατακάλυπτος: 1 Cor. XI, 5.

UNAND-HULIþS, preterite participle, unrevealed, μὴ ἀνακαλυπτόμενος: 2 Cor. III, 14.

[Col. 1324]

GA-HULJAN, to veil, hide, conceal, καλύπτειν: Matt. VIII, 24; X, 26; 2 Cor. IV, 3; κατακαλύπτειν: 1 Cor. XI, 6; παρακαλύπτειν: Luke IX, 45; *gahulidamma haubida*, “with the head veiled,” κατὰ κεφαλῆς ἔχων: 1 Cor. XI, 4.

DIS-HULJAN, to hide, cover, καλύπτειν: Luke VIII, 16.

AND-HULEINS, manifestation, revelation, ἀποκάλυψις: Luke II, 32; 1 Cor. XIV, 26; 2 Cor. XII, 1, 7; Gal. II, 2; Eph. I, 17; III, 3; 2 Thess. I, 7.

HULISTR, neuter, veil, covering, κάλυμμα: 2 Cor. III, 13, 14.

*HULS (Old Norse *holr*, Anglo-Saxon *hol, hale, holjan*, Old High German *hol, holi, holjan, holon*, English *hollow*, Old French, Swedish *hol*, Danish *huul*, Modern High German *hohl*; Greek κοῖλος, Latin *caelum, coelare*; Gr. II, 29; Gf. IV, 846; Rchth. 822), adjective, hollow.

US-HULON, conjugation II, to cut out, hew, λατομεῖν: Matt. XXVII, 60.

HULUNDI, feminine, tomb, cave, σπήλαιον: John XI, 38.

…HUN (compare Latin *-cunque*; Gr. III, 32), suffix denoting an indefinite idea, rendered in Latin by the ending *-cunque*; and—

AINS-HUN, see under Ains.  
þIS-HUN, see under þata.  
MANNA-HUN, see under Man.  
WAN-HUN, see under Wan.  
WAS-HUN, see under Was.  
WEILO-HUN, see under Weila.

*HUND (Old Norse *hundraþ*, Anglo-Saxon *hund*, Old Saxon and Old French *hundered*, Old High German *hunt*, English *hundred*, Swedish *hundra*, Danish *hundrede*, Modern High German *hundert*; Greek ἑκατόν, Latin *centum*; Bopp 456; Gr. I, 763; Gf. IV, 975; Rchth. 836), neuter, occurring only in the plural *hunda*, and indeed only in compounds:

þRIJA-HUNDA, see under þreis.  
NIUN-HUNDA, see under Niun.  
TVA-HUNDA, see under Tvai.  
FIMF-HUNDA, see under Fimf.  
HUNDA-FAþS, see under Faþs.

HUNDS (Old Norse *hundr*, Old High German *hunt*, Old Saxon, Anglo-Saxon, and Old French *hund*, English *hound*, Swedish, Danish, and Modern High German *Hund*, Dutch *hond*; Greek κύων, Latin *canis*; Bopp 81; Gr. III, 326; Gf. IV, 976; Rchth. 830), masculine, dog, κύων: Luke XVI, 21; Phil. III, 2; little dog, κυνάριον: Mark VII, 27, 28.

HUNþS, see under Hinþan.

HUNJAN, conjugation II, to desire, endeavour: Mark X, 24. See at that passage.

HUNSL (Old Norse and Swedish *husl*, Anglo-Saxon *husel*; DM. 25), neuter:

1. Offering, sacrifice, θυσία: Matt. IX, 13; Mark IX, 49; Luke II, 24; 1 Cor. X, 18; *Skeireins* I, a; προσφορά, “offering”: Eph. V, 2.

2. Worship, religious service, λατρεία: John XVI, 2.

HUNSLA-STAþS, see under Staþs.

UN-HUNSLAGS, adjective: 1) not making libations; 2) irreconcilable, ἄσπονδος: 2 Tim. III, 3.

HUNSLJAN, conjugation II, to offer a libation, σπένδειν: 2 Tim. IV, 6.

HUPS (Anglo-Saxon *hype*, Old High German *huf*, English *hip*, Swedish *höft*, Danish *hofte*, Dutch *heupe*, Modern High German *Hüfte*; Gr. II, 49; III, 405; Gf. IV, 832), masculine (plural *hupeis*), loins, ὀσφύς: Mark I, 6; Eph. VI, 14.

*HUS (Old Norse, Old High German, Swedish, Old Saxon, Anglo-Saxon, Old French *hus*, English *house*, Danish *huus*, Dutch *huys*, Modern High German *Haus*; Gr. II, 500; III, 426; DM. 39; Gf. IV, 1050; Rchth. 831), neuter, house.

GUD-HUS, house of God, temple, ἱερόν: John XVIII, 20.

HRAINS (Old Norse *hreinn*, Old Saxon *hreni*, Old French *rene*, Old High German *hreini*, Swedish *ren*, Danish *reen*, Dutch *reyn*, Modern High German *rein*; compare English *rinse*; Gr. II, 12; Gf. IV, 1158; Rchth. 992), adjective, pure, clean, καθαρός: Matt. XXVII, 59; John XIII, 11; XV, 3; 1 Tim. I, 5; III, 9; 2 Tim. I, 3; II, 22; Titus I, 15; orderly, respectable, κόσμιος: 1 Tim. II, 9; *Skeireins* III, c; *hrains vairþan*, “to be cleansed,” καθαρίζεσθαι: Matt. VIII, 3; XI, 5; Mark I, 41, 42; Luke V, 13; XVII, 15; see at that passage.

UN-HRAINS:

1. Unclean, impure, ἀκάθαρτος: Mark I, 23, 25, 26, 27; III, 11, 30; V, 2, 8, 13; VI, 7; VII, 25; IX, 25; Luke IV, 33, 36; VI, 18; VIII, 29; IX, 39, 42; 1 Cor. VII, 14; 2 Cor. VI, 17; Eph. V, 5; κοινός, “common”: Rom. XIV, 14; see at that passage.

2. Untrained, unlearned, ἰδιώτης: 2 Cor. XI, 6.

HRAINEI, feminine, purity: *Skeireins* III, b.

UN-HRAINEI, cleanliness, ἀκαθαρσία: Col. III, 5.

UN-HRAINIþA, feminine, the same: 2 Cor. XII, 21; Gal. V, 19; Eph. IV, 19; V, 3; 1 Thess. IV, 7.

HRAINJAN, conjugation II, to purify, καθαρίζειν: 2 Cor. VII, 1.

AF-HRAINJAN, the same: *Skeireins* I, a.

GA-HRAINJAN, the same: Matt. VIII, 2; Mark I, 40; VII, 19; Luke IV, 27; V, 12; VII, 22; XVII, 14, 17; John XV, 2; Eph. V, 26; διακαθαρίζειν, “to cleanse thoroughly”: Luke III, 17; ἐκκαθαίρειν, “to cleanse out”: 2 Tim. II, 21.

US-HRAINJAN, the same, ἐκκαθαίρειν: 1 Cor. V, 7.

HRAINEINS, feminine, purification, καθαρισμός: Luke II, 22; *Skeireins* III, b, d.

GA-HRAINEINS, the same: Mark I, 44; Luke V, 14.

HRAINJA-HAIRTS, see under Hairto.

*HRAIV (Old Saxon *hreu*, Anglo-Saxon *hreav*, Old Norse *hrae*, Old High German *hreo*; Gr. II, 412; III, 398; DM. 659 ff.; Gf. IV, 1131), corpse.

HRAIVA-DUBO, see under Dubo.

HRAMJAN (Old Norse *ram*, Old High German *ramen, ramjan*, Danish *ramme*, Modern High German *rahmen*; Gf. II, 504), conjugation II, to crucify, σταυροῦν: John XIX, 6.

US-HRAMJAN, the same: Matt. XXVI, 2; Mark XV, 13, 14, 15, 20, 25, 27; XVI, 6; John XIX, 6, 10; 1 Cor. I, 13, 23; 2 Cor. XIII, 4; Gal. III, 1; V, 24; VI, 14.

MIþUS-HRAMJAN, to crucify together with, συσταυροῦν: Matt. XXVII, 44; Mark XV, 32; Gal. II, 20.

*HRISJAN (Old Saxon *hrisian*, Anglo-Saxon *hreosan*, Swedish *rista*, compare Modern High German *rütteln*; Gr. II, 46; Gf. IV, 1179), conjugation II, to shake.

AF-HRISJAN, to shake off, cause to tremble, ἀποτινάσσειν: Luke IX, 5; ἀπομάσσεσθαι, “to wipe off”: Luke X, 11.

US-HRISJAN, the same, ἐκτινάσσειν: Mark VI, 11.

HRUGGA (compare Old Norse *hryggr*, Old High German *ruota*; Gf. II, 491), feminine, rod, staff, ῥάβδος: Mark VI, 8.

HRUK (Old Norse *kria, krunka*, Anglo-Saxon *hroc*, Old High German *hruoh*, Modern High German *krähen*; Greek κράζειν, Latin *crocire*; Gf. IV, 1149), neuter (?), crowing, specifically that of a cock; *faur hanins hruk*, “before the cock crows,” πρὶν ἀλέκτορα φωνῆσαι: Matt. XXVI, 75.

HRUKJAN, conjugation II, to crow, said of a cock, φωνεῖν: Matt. XXVI, 74; Mark XIV, 72; John XIII, 38; XVIII, 27.

[Col. 1326]

*HRUSKAN (Swedish *grannska*, Danish *grandske*; compare Modern High German *forschen*?), conjugation II.

AND-HRUSKAN, to examine, ἀνακρίνειν: 1 Cor. X, 25.

*HROþ (Old Norse *hrodr*, Anglo-Saxon *hroðer*, Old High German *hruodi*, Swedish and Danish *ros*; compare English *rout*; Gf. IV, 1153), neuter (?), song, hymn, praise.

HROþEIGS, adjective, victorious, glorious, θριαμβεύων: 2 Cor. II, 14.

HROPJAN (Old Norse *hropa*, Old Saxon *hropan*, Anglo-Saxon *hreopan*, Old French *hropa*, Old High German *hruofan*, Swedish *ropa*, Danish *raabe*, Dutch *roepen*, Modern High German *rufen*; Gf. IV, 1132; Rchth. 829), conjugation II, to cry out, κρᾶζειν: Matt. VIII, 29; IX, 27; XXVII, 50; Mark I, 26; III, 11; V, 5, 7; X, 47; XI, 9; XV, 13, 14, 39; Luke IV, 41; IX, 39; XVIII, 39; XIX, 40; John VII, 28, 37; XIX, 12; Gal. IV, 6; κραυγάζειν, “to shout”: John XI, 43; XVIII, 40; XIX, 6; βοᾶν, “to cry aloud”: Gal. IV, 27.

UF-HROPJAN, to cry aloud, κρᾶζειν: Mark IX, 24; ἀνακράζειν: Mark I, 23; Luke IV, 33; VIII, 28; ἀναβοᾶν: Matt. XXVII, 46; φωνεῖν: Luke XVI, 24.

HROPI, feminine (?), cry, outcry, κραυγή: Eph. IV, 31.

HROPEI, feminine, the same: Eph. IV, 31; see at that passage.

HROT (Anglo-Saxon and Old French *hrof*, Old Saxon *hrost*, Old High German *rost*, English *roof*, Dutch *roef*; Greek ὄροφος; Gf. II, 552; Rchth. 829), neuter, roof, covering, στέγη: Matt. VIII, 8; Mark II, 4; Luke VII, 6; δῶμα, “housetop”: Matt. X, 27; Luke V, 19; XVII, 31.

HYMAINAIUS, masculine proper name, Ὑμέναιος, Hymenaeus: 1 Tim. I, 19.

HYSSOPO (Greek word), feminine, hyssop (ὕσσωπος, according to Num. XIX, 6): *Skeireins* III, c.

HOBAN, see under Haban.

HOHA (compare Latin *occa*; Gr. III, 414, 416; DRA. 535*), masculine, plough, ἄροτρον: Luke IX, 62.

HOLON (Anglo-Saxon *holtihte*, English *hollow*, Old High German *huoljan, holjan*; Gr. II, 41; Gf. IV, 849), conjugation II, to defraud, extort, διασείειν: Luke III, 14.

AF-HOLON, to defraud, extort falsely, συκοφαντεῖν: Luke XIX, 8.

HORS (Old Norse *hor, hora*, Anglo-Saxon *horing*, Old High German and Old French *hor*, English *whore*, Swedish *hora*, Danish *hore*, Dutch *hoere*, Modern High German *Hure*; Greek κόρη; Gr. II, 42; Gf. IV, 1010; Rchth. 826), masculine, adulterer, adulterous man, μοιχός: Luke XVIII, 11; sexually immoral person, πόρνος: 1 Cor. V, 9, 10; Eph. V, 5; 1 Tim. I, 10.

HORINON, conjugation II, to commit adultery, μοιχεύειν: Matt. V, 27; Luke XVI, 18; XVIII, 20; μοιχᾶσθαι, “to commit adultery”: Matt. V, 32; Mark X, 11, 12; present feminine participle *horinondei*, adulteress, μοιχαλίς: Mark VIII, 38; Rom. VII,
3. **GA-HORINON**, the same, *to commit adultery*, μοιχεύειν (‘to commit adultery’): Matthew V.28. **HORINASSUS**, masculine, *adultery, fornication*, μοιχεία (‘adultery’): Galatians V.19; πορνεία (‘fornication’): Mark VII.21; John VIII.41; II Corinthians XII.21; Ephesians V.3; Colossians III.5.
[Col. 1325] þ
[Col. 1325] **þAGKJAN** (þaggkjan Mark VIII, 17; *Skeireins*, VII, a; þankjan Luke XIV, 31; Old Norse *þenkia*, Old Saxon *thenkian, thanc*, Anglo-Saxon *þencan*, Old High German *dankjan, denkjan*, Old Frisian *thanka*, English *think*, Swedish *tänka*, Danish *tænke*, Dutch, Modern High German *denken*; Gr. II, 60; Gf. V, 150; Rchth, 1067), anomalous conjugation; þahta, þahtedun, þahts: to think, reason; λογίζεσθαι, “to reckon, consider”: 2 Cor. III, 5; X, 7, 11 (Mark XI, 31); διαλογίζεσθαι, “to deliberate, reason”: Mark II, 6; VIII, 16, 17; XI, 31; Luke III, 15; V, 21; XX, 14; also þagkjan sis, “to consider within oneself,” Luke I, 29; συλλογίζεσθαι, “to infer, reason”: Luke XX, 5; συμβάλλειν, “to ponder, compare”: Luke II, 19; βουλεύεσθαι, “to deliberate”: Luke XIV, 31; 2 Cor. I, 17; ἀπορεῖσθαι, “to be perplexed”: John XIII, 22; διαπορεῖν, “to be at a loss”: Luke IX, 7.

**AND-þAGKJAN SIK.** 1) To remember, think of, with the genitive: *Skeireins* VII, a, first passage; also without *sik*: *Skeireins* VII, a, second passage. 2) To recognize, γιγνώσκειν, “to know”: Luke XVI, 4.

**BI-þAGKJAN**, to reason, think, διαλογίζεσθαι, “to deliberate”: Luke V, 22.

**ANDA-þAHTS**, adjective: reasonable, λογικός: Rom. [Col. 1326] XII, 1; *Skeireins* II, d; sober-minded, σώφρων: Titus I, 8; temperate, νηφάλιος: 1 Tim. III, 2, 11; see the note on that passage. *andaþahts visan*, “to be temperate,” νήφειν: 2 Tim. IV, 5.

**GA-þAGKI**, neuter: frugality; *us gaþagkja*, sparingly, φειδομένως: 2 Cor. IX, 6.

**þAGKS** (þanks Luke XVII, 9; Old Norse *þakkir*, Old Saxon *thanc*, Anglo-Saxon *þanc*, Old High German *dank*, Old Frisian *thonk*), masculine: thanksgiving, χάρις: Luke XVII, 9.

**þADDAIUS**, masculine proper name: Thaddaeus, Θαδδαῖος: Mark III, 18.

**þADEI**, see under **þata**.

**þAHAN** (Old Norse *þegia, þagga, þagna*, Old High German *dagen*, Old Saxon *thagian, thagon*, Swedish *tiga*, Danish *tie*; Latin *tacere*, “be silent”; Gr. V, 98), second conjugation: to be silent; σιωπᾶν: Mark III, 4; XIV, 61; Luke I, 20; XVIII, 39; σιγᾶν: Luke IX, 36; φιμοῦσθαι, “to be muzzled”: Mark I, 25.

**GA-þAHAN**, the same: σιωπᾶν: Mark X, 48; σιγᾶν: Luke XX, 26.

[Col. 1327] **þAHAINS**, feminine: silence, quietness, ἡσυχία: 1 Tim. II, 12; see the note on that passage.

**þAHTS**, see under **þagkjan**.

**þAHO** (Anglo-Saxon *þo*, Old High German *daha*, Modern High German *thon*; Gr. III, 380; Gf. V, 104; Schm. I, 437), feminine: clay, mud, πηλός: Rom. IX, 21.

**þAþROH**, see under **þata**.

**þAIAUFEILUS**, masculine proper name: Theophilus, Θεόφιλος: Luke I, 3.

**þAIRH** (Old Saxon *thurh*, Anglo-Saxon *þurh*, Old High German *durh*, Old Frisian *thruch*, English *through*, Modern High German *durch*; Gr. II, 63; III, 261; IV, 793; Gf. V, 221; Alth. Praep. 202; Rchth. 1078), a preposition construed with the accusative. It has the same force as Latin *per*, “through,” and corresponds also to Greek διά with the genitive; like the latter, it denotes the means through which, or the person through whom, something takes place. Only very rarely does this particle determine time.

I. As a preposition:

1) In the local sense it always stands for Greek διά with the genitive: after *gaggan*, Mark IX, 30; Luke VI, 1; *þairhgaggan*, Mark II, 23; Luke XVII, 11; *ïnngaggan*, Matt. VII, 13; John X, 1, 2, 9; *galeiþan*, Mark X, 25; 2 Cor. I, 16; *usleiþan*, Matt. VIII, 28; John VIII, 59; *þairhleiþan*, Luke IV, 30; XVIII, 25; *þairhbairan*, Mark XI, 16. So also 2 Cor.
