I, 6, 11, 15, 19; II, 4, 7; III, 16; IV, 3, 6, 10, 14; VI, 4, 10, 12, 15, 16; 2 Tim. I, 3, 6, 11, 13; II, 9, 17; IV, 13, 15; Titus I, 2, 3, 11; Philem. 13; Neh. VI, 14 (17); *Skeireins* IV, d; VII, a, b, c, d; VIII, c; ὃς ἄν, “whoever”: Mark IV, 22; X, 30; ὅσπερ, “the very one who”: Mark XV, 6; ὅστις, “whoever, whoever it may be”: Matt. VII, 24, 26, 27, 55, 62; Mark IV, 20; XII, 18; XV, 7; Luke I, 20; II, 4, 10; VII, 37, 39; VIII, 3, 26, 43; IX, 30; XV, 7; John VIII, 53; Rom. IX, 4; 1 Cor. VII, 13; 2 Cor. IX, 11; Gal. II, 4; IV, 24, 26; V, 19; Eph. I, 23; III, 13; IV, 19; Phil. I, 28; Col. II, 23; III, 5, 14; IV, 11; 2 Thess. I, 9; 1 Tim. I, 4; III, 15; VI, 9; 2 Tim. I, 5; II, 2, 18; Titus I, 11; ὅσος, “as much as, as many as”: Luke XVIII, 12, 22; John X, 41; XVI, 15; XVII, 7; Rom. IX, 7 in this passage; οἷος, “of such a kind as”: Phil. I, 30; sometimes also where the Greek employs a demonstrative (οὗτος, “this”): Matt. XXVII, 46; 2 Cor. XII, 8; Eph. III, 1 in this passage; V, 6 (οὗτος γάρ, “for this”); Titus I, 5; in place of ὁ with a participle: Matt. VI, 4, 6, 18; XI, 14; XXVII, 17; Mark XV, 41; Luke I, 36; VII, 39; VIII, 2; X, 13, 23; XV, 12, 30; XVIII, 9; XIX, 27, 29; XX, 27; John I, 29; V, 37, 45; VI, 22, 33, 44, 50, 58, 64; VII, 28, 49, 50; VIII, 16, 18, 54; XI, 2, 16, 33; XII, 12, 17, 29, 49; XIV, 21; XVIII, 4, 14; Rom. VII, 20; IX, 5; XII, 3; 1 Cor. X, 25, 27; XII, 22; XV, 23 in this passage; 2 Cor. I, 4, 19; II, 2; IV, 6; V, 5; Gal. II, 9; Eph. II, 14; III, 2; V, 4; VI, 24; Phil. III, 19; IV, 7; Col. I, 8, 12, 23, 25, 26, 29; II, 12; IV, 11; 1 Thess. II, 12, 15; IV, 5, 8, 13; V, 10; 2 Thess. II, 16; 1 Tim. V, 9; VI, 2, 5, 16; 2 Tim. I, 9, 14; III, 6, 12; IV, 1, 8; Ps. LIII, 2, compared with 2 Tim. II, 26, *fram þammei gafahanai tiuhanda*, “having been captured by him,” ἐζωγρημένοι ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ; sometimes the participle ὤν, “being,” must also be supplied: Matt. X, 32; Luke V, 7; Rom. VII, 10; 2 Cor. VIII, 23; Col. IV, 7, 9; 1 Tim. I, 11; V, 3, 5; 2 Tim. I, 15; II, 10; Titus I, 1; Neh. V, 15, compared with 2 Cor. VII, 12; IX, 1; and thus the Gothic *ist* (“is”) is also omitted: Eph. IV, 6.

—b) “he who,” referring to a definite but unexpressed object, ὅς: Matt. XI, 10; Mark I, 44; III, 13; IV, 24, 25; IX, 9, 10, 40; XI, 23; XIV, 8; Luke VI, 34, 46; VII, 22, 27, 47; VIII, 18; X, 23, 24; XVII, 10, 27, 29; XIX, 21, 22, 26; John III, 26, 32; V, 21; VII, 25; VIII, 38; X, 29, 36; XI, 3, 45, 46; XIII, 24, 27; XVII, 12; XVIII, 9, 21; Rom. VII, 15, 16, 19, 20; X, 14; 1 Cor. IV, 6; VII, 24; X, 15, 30; XV, 3, 10; 2 Cor. II, 3; XI, 17; Gal. II, 18; Phil. I, 16 in this passage; III, 16; IV, 9; Col. III, 25; 2 Thess. III, 4; 1 Tim. II, 10; 2 Tim. II, 2, 7; Titus I, 11; II, 1; ὅστις: John VIII, 25; Gal. IV, 24; in place of a Greek participle: Mark V, 16, 18, 33; X, 32; Luke I, 2, 35; III, 13; VI, 3; IX, 17; XVII, 9; XX, 2, 35; John VI, 46, 63; VIII, 18, 26, 29, 50; IX, 8, 37; X, 12; XIII, 18; XIV, 30; 1 Cor. IV, 4; X, 33; Gal. I, 23; II, 8; III, 5; Eph. IV, 10; 1 Thess. V, 24; 1 Tim. V, 13; 2 Tim. II, 4; III, 6; also where the participle ὤν (“being”) must be supplied: Col. III, 1, 2. Luke V, 14 also belongs here: *atbair þatei anabaud Moses*, “offer that which Moses commanded,” προσένεγκε καθὼς προσέταξε Μωσῆς.

—c) “whoever,” in general statements: ὃς ἄν, ὃς ἐάν: Matt. V, 19, 21, 22; X, 42; Mark III, 35; VIII, 35, 38; IX, 37, 41; X, 15, 35, 44; Luke III, 11; VIII, 18; IX, 4, 24, 26; X, 5, 8, 10, 22; XVII, 33; XVIII, 17; Rom. IX, 15; 1 Cor. XVI, 3; 2 Cor. XI, 21; Gal. VI, 7; ὅστις: Mark VIII, 34; Luke XIV, 27; Phil. III, 7; ὅστις ἄν: 1 Cor. XVI, 2 (in whose place *þatei wa* is used, John XIV, 13); ὅς: Matt. VI, 8; X, 27, 38; XI, 4; Mark IX, 40; X, 9; Luke IX, 50; XIV, 15; XVII, 31; XX, 18; John XIII, 29; Rom. IX, 18; XIII, 7; 1 Cor. X, 20; 2 Cor. I, 17; II, 10; X, 18; XI, 12; εἴ τις, ἐάν τις, “if anyone”: John III, 3, 5; XV, 6; Eph. IV, 29; compare John VI, 50 in this passage; τίς, “who,” in indirect questions: John VI, 6; Eph. V, 10; in place of a Greek participle: Matt. X, 37, 39; XI, 8, 15; Mark IV, 9; VII, 10; Luke VIII, 8; X, 16; XIV, 10, 11, 35; XVIII, 14; John VI, 47, 54, 56, 57; VII, 18, 38; VIII, 12; X, 1; XI, 25; XII, 25, 35, 44, 45, 48; XIII, 20; XIV, 9, 21, 24; XV, 5, 23; Rom. XIII, 8; XIV, 2, 18; 1 Cor. VII, 22; XI, 29; 2 Cor. IX, 6; X, 18; Gal. VI, 8; Eph. IV, 28; V, 28; 1 Thess. IV, 8; V, 7; 1 Tim. VI, 2, 9; also where ὤν (“being”) must be supplied: Luke XVI, 10; XVII, 31; Rom. XIV, 19; 2 Cor. VIII, 15; Gal. V, 24.

—2) It further occurs in particular constructions and expressions.

a) With an article (demonstrative) immediately preceding: οὗτος ὅς, “this [one] who”: Luke V, 21; John XVI, 17; αὐτὸς ὅστις, “that very one who”: Phil. IV, 3; ὅς: Luke I, 4; John XVII, 9 (compare Luke VII, 43); ὅστις: John XIII, 20; in place of a Greek participle: Mark V, 15; Luke II, 33; VIII, 4; Rom. XI, 22; Gal. IV, 8; Col. III, 10; 1 Thess. IV, 14; 2 Tim. II, 19; *Skeireins* I, a; also where ὤν (“being”) must be supplied in the Greek text: Matt. X, 33; Luke IX, 61; John IX, 13; Rom. VIII, 5; Phil. III, 6, 9, 14; Col. III, 2, 5; IV, 13; 1 Thess. IV, 12; 2 Tim. I, 5.

b) Sometimes, by attraction, it is put in the same case as the preceding demonstrative: Luke II, 20, *hazjandans guþ in allaize þizeei* (instead of *þize þoei*) *gahausidedun*, “praising God for all the things which they had heard”; likewise Mark XV, 12; Luke III, 13; IX, 36; XVII, 27, 29; John VI, 29; VII, 31; XI, 6; 1 Cor. IV, 6; XI, 23; 2 Cor. V, 10; XII, 17; XIII, 10; Gal. V, 1; Col. III, 2; IV, 16; 1 Tim. V, 3; 2 Tim. III, 14; Philem. 21. This applies also where, in relation to the demonstrative, it is not indeed a relative pronoun but merely a relative particle of the same sense that is referred to from what follows: thus *þammei* instead of *þamma ei*, ὅτι (“that”): Mark VII, 18; XVI, 4; Luke I, 22; XV, 6; XVII, 15; John VI, 5; Phil. II, 24 in this passage; 2 Tim. I, 12; *þizei* instead of *þis ei*, ὅτι (“that”): Mark IV, 38; compare Luke VII, 4, *wairþs ist þammei* (instead of *ei þamma*) *fragibis þata*, “he is worthy that you should grant this.”

c) In combination with prepositions, mostly to paraphrase a Greek infinitival or participial construction: *in þizei*, διὰ τό with infinitive (“because of doing”): Mark IV, 5; Luke VIII, 6; [Col. 1343] XVIII, 5; διό, “therefore”: Rom. XV, 7; 2 Cor. IV, 13; XII, 10; Eph. III, 13; IV, 8, 25; 1 Thess. III, 1; διότι, “because”: Phil. II, 26; δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν, “for which reason”: Luke VIII, 47; οὗ χάριν, “for which cause”: Luke VII, 47; οὗ ἕνεκεν, “on whose account”: Luke IV, 18; ἀνθ’ ὧν, “in return for which things”: Luke XIX, 44; *Skeireins* I, d; II, b; III, b; IV, c; VI, a, c; VIII, b; *bi þatei*, διὰ τό with infinitive: Luke XIX, 11; *afar þatei*, μετὰ τό with infinitive (“after doing”): Mark I, 14; *Skeireins* VII, b; *und þatei*, ἄχρις οὗ (“until”): Rom. XI, 25; 1 Cor. XV, 25; ἕως (“until”): Neh. VII, 3; *us þammei*, ἐκ τοῦ with infinitive (“from doing”): 2 Cor. VIII, 11; *du þammei*, πρὸς τό with infinitive (“for doing”): Luke XVIII, 1; *in þammei*, ἐν τῷ with infinitive (“in doing”): Luke IX, 34, 51; Gal. IV, 18; τῷ with infinitive: 2 Cor. II, 12; ὅτι, “that”: Luke X, 20; ἐν ᾧ, “in which”: Rom. VIII, 3; ἐφ’ ᾧ, “on account of which”: Phil. III, 12; *ana þammei*, in place of a Greek genitive absolute: John VI, 23. But *þatei faur ina winnan* for τὸ ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ πάσχειν, “to suffer on his behalf,” Phil. I, 29 in this passage, is certainly erroneous.

d) The expressions *fram þammei*, “from which,” ἀφ’ ἧς: Luke VII, 45; *ana þammei* or *in þammei*, “to the extent that,” ἐφ’ ᾧ: 2 Cor. V, 4; Phil. III, 12; and *þairh þoei*, “therefore”: *Skeireins* VII, a, must also be included here.

e) To paraphrase a substantive: *þatei anafulhun*, “that which was handed down,” παράδοσις, “tradition”: Mark VII, 5, 8; *þatei galiugam saljada*, “that which is sold to idols,” εἰδωλόθυτον, “food sacrificed to idols”: 1 Cor. X, 19; *þatei galeikai*, “that which is pleasing,” ἀρέσκεια, “pleasingness”: Col. I, 10; *þatei winna*, “what I suffer,” τὰ παθήματά μου, “my sufferings”: Col. I, 24; *þatei þeihais þu*, “that by which you prosper,” σοῦ ἡ προκοπή, “your progress”: 1 Tim. IV, 15; *þairh þatei ist brukjaidau*, “through that which is consumed,” τῇ ἀποχρήσει, “by consumption”: Col. II, 22; *þatei ustauhan ist*, “that which has come,” τὸ τέλειον, “the perfect”: 1 Cor. XIII, 10; *þatei goþ sijai*, “that which may be good,” τὸ καλόν, “the good”: 1 Thess. V, 21. *Wah þatei* and *wazuh saei*, see under *Was*. *Þatawah þatei*, see under *Was*. *Þiswah þatei*, see under *Was*.

**þATEI**, conjunction:

a) “that, because,” ὅτι: Matt. V, 20, 21, 22, 23, 27, 28, 31, 32, 33, 38, 43; VI, 5, 16, 29, 32; VII, 23; VIII, 11; IX, 6, 18, 28; X, 34; XI, 4, 24; XXVI, 2, 72; XXVII, 3, 18, 43, 47, 63; Mark I, 15, 37, 40; II, 1, 8, 10, 12, 16; III, 11, 21, 22, 28; V, 23, 28, 29, 35; VI, 4, 14, 13, 18, 23; VII, 6, 20; VIII, 24, 31; IX, 1, 11, 13, 25, 26, 31; X, 33, 42, 47; XI, 3, 17, 24, 32; XII, 6, 7, 12, 14, 19, 26, 28, 29, 32, 34, 35; XIII, 28, 29; XIV, 14, 58, 69, 71, 72; XV, 10, 39; XVI, 11; Luke I, 25, 29, 45, 61; II, 10, 23, 49; III, 8; IV, 4, 10, 12, 21, 24, 25, 36, 41, 43; V, 24, 26, 36; VI, 5; VII, 4, 16, 22, 37, 39; VIII, 20, 47, 49, 53; IX, 7, 8, 19, 22; X, 11, 12, 24; XIV, 24, 30; XV, 2, 7, 27; XVII, 10, 34; XVIII, 8, 29, 37; XIX, 7, 9, 22, 26, 31, 40, 42, 43, 46; XX, 5, 19, 21, 37; John V, 36, 45; VI, 14, 15, 22, 24, 26, 36, 42, 61, 65, 69; VII, 7, 12, 26, 42, 52; VIII, 17, 24, 27, 28, 33, 34, 37, 45, 48, 52, 54; IX, 8, 9, 17, 18, 19, 20, 24, 29, 30, 31, 32, 35, 41; X, 7, 33, 36, 38, 41; XI, 6, 13, 20, 24, 27, 31, 40, 42; XII, 9, 12, 16, 19, 34; XIII, 19, 21, 29; XIV, 10, 11, 19, 20, 31; XV, 5; XVI, 4, 9, 10, 11, 15, 17, 19, 23, 27, 30; XVII, 8, 21, 23, 25; XVIII, 2, 6, 8, 14; XIX, 4, 10; Rom. VII, 1, 14, 16, 18; VIII, 36, 38; IX, 2, 12, 30; X, 2, 5, 9; XIII, 11; XIV, 11, 14; 1 Cor. I, 15; V, 6; IX, 24; X, 1, 19; XI, 3, 23; XII, 15; XIV, 21, 23, 25; XV, 4, 5, 12, 15, 27, 58; XVI, 12, 15; 2 Cor. I, 7, 12; II, 3; III, 3; IV, 14; V, 1, 6, 15; VI, 16; VII, 3, 8; VIII, 2, 9; X, 11; XI, 21, 31; XII, 4, 13; XIII, 2, 5, 6; Gal. I, 23; II, 7, 14, 26; IV, 6, 13, 15, 22; V, 2, 3, 10, 21; Eph. II, 11; IV, 9; V, 5; VI, 9; Phil. I, 17, 19, 25, 27; II, 22; IV, 15; Col. III, 24; IV, 1; 1 Thess. III, 3, 4, 6; IV, 14, 15; V, 2; 1 Tim. I, 8, 9, 15; IV, 1; VI, 7; 2 Tim. I, 5, 15; II, 23; III, 1, 15; *Skeireins* I, b; II, c; III, c; V, a; VI, c; VII, d; VIII, d.

b) “whether, if,” εἰ, in interrogative sentences: 1 Cor. VII, 16.

c) With negation: *ni þatei*, “not that,” οὐχ ὅτι: John VI, 46; VII, 22; 2 Cor. I, 24; III, 5; Phil. III, 12; IV, 11, 17; 2 Thess. III, 9; *Skeireins* IV, b (1 Cor. IX, 9); *niba þatei*, “except that,” εἰ μὴ ὅτι: 2 Cor. XII, 13.

**þEEI**, “that,” only with negation: *ni þeei* or *nih þeei*, “not that,” οὐχ ἵνα: John VI, 38; 2 Cor. II, 4; οὐχ ὅτι: John XII, 6.

**þEI**:

1. Conjunction: “that,” ὅτι, especially after verbs of thinking and saying: Matt. VI, 26; John XIII, 35, 38; XVI, 20, 26; Rom. X, 9; 1 Cor. IV, 9; XI, 2; XV, [Col. 1344] 20; ἵνα, “in order that”: John VI, 7; XIII, 35; XVI, 33; with negation, *þei ni*, ἵνα μή, “so that not”: John VI, 12.

2. Relative particle: “that, when,” ὅτι: John VII, 35; in the expression *und þata weilos þei*, “as long as,” ἐφ’ ὅσον: Matt. IX, 15.

3. (*þe*, 1 Cor. XVI, 6 in this passage.) When added to the demonstrative *was*, *wazuh*, *waduh*, it gives it—as do the other relatives—a generally relative meaning (“whoever,” ὃς ἄν); thus *þiswah þei*, *þatawah þei*, *sawazuh þei*, *þiswaduh þei*: see under *Was*.

**þADEI**, adverb:

1. “Thence, where,” ὅπου and ὅπου ἐάν: Mark VI, 55; XIV, 14; John VI, 62; VIII, 21; XIII, 33, 36; XIV, 4; οὗ, “where”: Luke X, 1.

2. After *þiswaduh*, etc.; see *þei*, 3, under *Was*.

**þAPROH** (*þaþro* in John and Luke IV, 9, 29; Gal. I, 21; II, 1; *Skeireins* VI, d), adverb:

1. Of place: “from there,” ἐντεῦθεν: Luke IV, 9, 29; John VII, 3; XIV, 31; XVIII, 36; ἐκεῖθεν: Luke IX, 4.

2. Of time: “afterward, then,” ἀπὸ τότε: Luke XVI, 16; εἶτα: Mark IV, 17, 28; VIII, 25; Luke VIII, 12; 1 Tim. II, 13; ἔπειτα: 1 Cor. XV, 6; Gal. I, 21; II, 1; *Skeireins* VI, d; καί or δέ: Luke IV, 9; λοιπὸν, “finally”: 2 Tim. IV, 8 in this passage. *þaþroh þan* or *þaþroþ-þan* (*þaþro þan*, 1 Thess. IV, 17; 2 Tim. IV, 8), “then, thereafter,” εἶτα: 1 Cor. XV, 24; ἔπειτα: Mark VII, 5; Luke XVI, 7; John XI, 7; 1 Cor. XV, 7, 23; 1 Thess. IV, 17; οὖν, “therefore”: John III, 25; XVIII, 7; καί, “and”: 2 Cor. VIII, 5; καὶ πάλιν, “and again”: 1 Cor. VII, 5; λοιπόν, “finally”: 2 Tim. IV, 8.

**þAþROEI**, “whence, from which,” ἐξ οὗ: Phil. III, 20.

**þAR**, “there,” ἐκεῖ: Matt. VI, 20; Luke IX, 4.

**þARUH**, adverb and conjunction:

1. “There,” ἐκεῖ: Matt. VI, 21; Mark XVI, 7; John XII, 26; XIV, 3.

2. “Now, indeed, but,” δέ: Mark X, 20, 24; XIV, 64; XVI, 6; Luke III, 12; IV, 43; V, 34; VI, 8, 10; VII, 43; VIII, 31, 46, 52; IX, 42; X, 26; XIV, 16; XV, 27, 29, 31; XVI, 6; John VI, 20; XVIII (5), 15, 18; οὖν, “therefore”: John VI, 5, 10, 14, 19, 21, 24, 28, 53, 66; VII, 6, 35; VIII, 25; XI, 36; XII, 2; XIII, 37; XIV, 5, 9, 22; XVI, 17, 29; XVIII, 5, 6, 11, 12, 16, 17, 18, 25, 27, 29, 31, 37; XIX, 5, 6, 10; καί, “and”: John III, 23; VII, 45; IX, 2.

3. “Behold,” ἰδού: Matt. IX, 18; καὶ (ἰδού), “and behold”: Matt. IX, 3; Luke II, 25; *þaruh sai*, “and behold,” καὶ ἰδού: Luke VII, 12, 37; *þaruh þan*, “now, indeed,” δέ: Luke VIII, 23.

**þAREI**, adverb, “where,” ὅπου: Matt. VI, 19, 20, 21; Mark II, 4, 5, 15; V, 40; IX, 44; XIV, 14; XVI, 6; Luke XVII, 37; John VI, 23; VII, 34, 42; X, 40; XI, 30, 32; XII, 1, 26; XIV, 3; XVII, 24; XVIII, 1, 20; Col. III, 11; οὗ: Luke IV, 16, 17; John XI, 41; Rom. IX, 26; 2 Cor. III, 17; Col. III, 1.

**þE**, see under *þata*.  
**þEI**, see under *þata*.  
**þEIGAINS**, see 1 Tim. II, 12.

**þEIHAN** (Old Saxon *thihan*, Anglo-Saxon *þeon*, Old High German *dihan*, Old French *tigia*, Modern High German *gedeihen*; Gr. II, 18; Gf. V, 105; Rchth. 1085), conjugation I, *þaih, þaihun, þaihans*: “to advance, make progress,” προκόπτειν: Luke II, 52; 2 Tim. III, 9, 13; *Skeireins* IV, b, compared with II, c; *þatei þeiha*, “that I advance,” “my progress,” ἡ προκοπή μου: 1 Tim. IV, 15; συμβιβάζεσθαι, “to be joined together”: Col. II, 19.

**GA-þEIHAN**, the same: ἀναθάλλειν, “to flourish again”: Phil. IV, 10; *Skeireins* IV, b.

**UFAR-þEIHAN**, “to advance, make progress”: *Skeireins* III, d.

**þEIHS** (DM. 457), neuter: “time,” χρόνος: 1 Thess. V, 1; καιρός: Rom. XIII, 11.

**þEIMAUþAIUS**, see under *Teimauþaius*.  
**þEINA**, see under *þu*.  
**þEINS**, see in the same place.  
**þEIWO** (DM. 121), feminine: “thunder,” βροντή: Mark III, 17; John XII, 29.  
**þEVIS**, see under *þivan*.  
**þIZE**, see under *þata*.  
**þIZEI**, see under *þata*.

**\*þINAN** (Old Norse *þenia*, Old Saxon *thenian*, Anglo-Saxon *þenian*, Old High German *danjan*, Modern High German *dehnen, dünn*; Greek τείνειν, “to stretch,” Latin *tendere*; Bopp 118; Gr. II, 56; Gf. V, 143), conjugation I, *þan, þenun, þunans*: “to stretch.”

**UF-þANJAN**, conjugation II: “to lengthen, stretch out,” ἐκτείνειν: [Col. 1345] 2 Cor. X, 14; *sik ufþanjan du—*, “to stretch oneself toward—,” ἐπεκτείνεσθαί τινι: Phil. III, 14.

**\*þINSAN** (Old Saxon *thinsan*, Old High German *dinsan*, Modern High German *(ge)dunsen*; compare *þinan*; Gr. II, 35, 72; Gf. V, 196), conjugation I, *þans, þunsun*: “to draw.”

**AT-þINSAN**, “to draw toward,” ἑλκύειν: John VI, 44; XII, 32.

**þIUBS** (Old Norse *þiofr, þauf*, Old Saxon *thiof*, Anglo-Saxon *þeof*, Old High German *diub*, Old French *thiaf*, English *thief*, Swedish *tyf*, Danish *tyv*, Dutch *dief*, Modern High German *dieb*; Gr. II, 49; DRA. 635; Gf. V, 97; Rchth. 1071), masculine: “thief, robber,” κλέπτης: Matt. VI, 19, 20; John X, 8, 10; XII, 6; 1 Thess. V, 2, 4; λῃστής, “robber”: Luke XIX, 46.

**þIUBI**, neuter: “a den of robbers,” κλοπή, “theft”: Mark VII, 22.

**þIUBJO**, adverb: “secretly, covertly,” λάθρα: John XI, 28; ἐν κρυπτῷ, “in secret”: John XVIII, 20.

**þIUDA** (Old Norse *þiod*, Old Saxon *thiod*, Anglo-Saxon *þeod*, Old High German *diot*, Old French *thiade*; Gr. III, 472; IV, 586; I, 12 [3rd ed.]; DRA. 229; Gf. V, 124; Rchth. 1071), feminine: “nation,” ἔθνος; in the plural it often means “Gentiles, pagans”: Matt. VI, 32; Mark X, 42; XI, 17; Luke II, 32; VII, 5; XVIII, 32; John XVIII, 35; Rom. IX, 24, 30; X, 19; XI, 11, 12, 13, 25; XV, 9, 10, 11; 1 Cor. I, 23; X, 20; 2 Cor. XI, 26; Gal. II, 2, 8, 9, 12, 14; Eph. II, 11; III, 1, 6, 8; IV, 17; Col. I, 27; 1 Thess. II, 16; IV, 5; 1 Tim. II, 7; III, 16; 2 Tim. I, 11; Neh. V, 17; VI, 16; ἐθνικός, “Gentile”: Matt. V, 46; VI, 7; Ἕλλην, “Greek”: John VII, 35; XII, 20; 1 Cor. I, 24; XII, 13.

**GUT-þIUDA**, “the people of God”: Gothic Calendar.

**þIUDISKO**, adverb: “in Gentile fashion, after the manner of the Gentiles,” ἐθνικῶς: Gal. II, 14.

**þIUDANS** (Old Saxon *thiodan*, Anglo-Saxon *þeoden*; Gr. III, 320; DRA. 229), masculine: “king,” βασιλεύς: Matt. V, 35; XI, 8; XXV, 40; XXVII, 11; Mark VI, 14, 22, 25, 26; XV, 2, 9, 12, 18, 26; Luke I, 5; X, 24; XIV, 31; XIX, 38; John VI, 15; XII, 13, 15; XVIII, 33, 37, 39; XIX, 2, 12; 2 Cor. XI, 32; 1 Tim. I, 17; II, 2; VI, 15; Neh. V, 14; Gothic Calendar.

**þIUDAN-GARDI**, see under *Gards*.

**þIUDANON**, conjugation II: “to reign,” βασιλεύειν: Luke I, 33; XIX, 14, 27; 1 Cor. IV, 8; XV, 25; 1 Tim. VI, 15.

**MIþ-þIUDANON**, “to reign jointly,” συμβασιλεύειν: 1 Cor. IV, 8; 2 Tim. II, 12.

**þIUDINASSUS**, masculine: “kingdom,” βασιλεία: Matt. VI, 10; Mark IX, 1; Luke I, 33; IV, 5; VIII, 10; 1 Cor. XV, 24, 50; 2 Tim. IV, 1; ἡγεμονία, “governorship”: Luke III, 1.

**þIUþ** (Gr. III, 602), neuter: “good,” ἀγαθόν: Luke I, 53; VI, 45; Rom. VII, 18; IX, 11; X, 15; XII, 21; XIV, 16; 2 Cor. V, 10; Gal. VI, 10; Eph. IV, 28; VI, 8; 1 Thess. V, 15; Philem. 14; *þiuþ taujan*, “to do good,” τὸ ἀγαθὸν ποιεῖν: Rom. XIII, 3; ἀγαθοποιεῖν: Mark III, 4; Luke VI, 9, 33, 35.

**þIUþ-SPILLON**, see under *Spill*.

**UN-þIUþ**, “evil,” κακόν: Rom. IX, 11; XII, 21; 2 Cor. V, 10; 2 Tim. IV, 14; *unþiuþ taujan*, “to do evil,” κακοποιεῖν: Mark III, 4; Luke VI, 9.

**þIUþEIGS**, adjective:

1. “Good,” ἀγαθός: Matt. VII, 18, first occurrence; Mark X, 17, 18; Luke VI, 45; XVIII, 18, 19; Rom. VII, 12, 13; καλός: Matt. VII, 18, second occurrence.

2. “Blessed,” εὐλογητός: Mark XIV, 61; Luke I, 68; 2 Cor. XI, 31.

**þIUþJAN**, conjugation II, with dative (Luke II, 28) and accusative: “to bless,” εὐλογεῖν: Mark X, 16; XI, 9, 10; Luke I, 28, 29, 42, 64; II, 28, 34; VI, 28; XIX, 38; John XII, 13; Rom. IX, 5; XII, 14; 2 Cor. I, 3; past participle *þiuþiþs*, “blessed,” εὐλογητός: Eph. I, 3.

**GA-þIUþJAN**, the same: Mark VIII, 7; Luke IX, 16; Eph. I, 3; *Skeireins* VII, b.

**UN-þIUþJAN**, “to curse,” καταρᾶσθαι: Rom. XII, 14.

**þIUþEINS**, feminine:

1. “Goodness,” ἀγαθωσύνη: 2 Thess. I, 11.

2. “Blessing,” εὐλογία: 2 Cor. IX, 6; Eph. I, 3.

**þIUþI-QISS**, see under *Qiþan*.  
**þIUS**, see under *þivan*.  
[Col. 1346] **þIS**, see under *þata*.

**\*þIVAN** (Old Norse *þyr, þiona*, Old Saxon *thiu, thionon*, Anglo-Saxon *þeov, þeovian*, Old High German *diu, dionon*, Old French *thianer, thiania*; Gr. II, 336; III, 337; DRA. 302 ff.; Gf. V, 87; Schm. I, 348; Rchth. 1071), conjugation I, *þau, þevun, þivans*: “to minister, serve.”

**ANA-þIVAN**, conjugation II: “to perform service,” δουλαγωγεῖν (“to enslave, bring into subjection”): 1 Cor. IX, 27.

**GA-þIVAN**, the same: δουλοῦν, “to enslave”: 1 Cor. VII, 15; καταδουλοῦν, “to bring into bondage”: 2 Cor. XI, 20; Gal. II, 4; περιπείρειν, “to entangle”: 1 Tim. VI, 10; *mannans gaþivands*, “enslaving men,” ἀνδραποδιστής: 1 Tim. I, 10.

**þIVADU**, neuter: “slavery,” δουλεία: Gal. IV, 24.

**þIUS**, masculine (plural *þivos*): “servant, attendant,” οἰκέτης: Luke XVI, 13; Neh. V, 16.

**þIU-MAGUS**, see under *Magus*.

**þIVI**, feminine: “maidservant,” παιδίσκη: Matt. XXVI, 69; Mark XIV, 66, 69; John XVIII, 17; Gal. IV, 22, 23, 30, 31; δούλη, “female slave”: Luke I, 38, 48.

**þEVIS**, neuter: “slave,” δοῦλος: Col. III, 22; IV, 1.

**þLAQUS** (compare Latin *flaccus*), adjective: “soft, tender,” ἁπαλός: Mark XIII, 28.

**þLAHSJAN** (compare *þliuhan*), conjugation II: “to terrify,” ἐκφοβεῖν: 2 Cor. X, 9; compare Neh. VI, 14.

**GA-þLAHSNAN**, conjugation III: “to be troubled, dismayed,” διαταράττεσθαι: Luke I, 29.

**\*þLAIHAN** (compare Old Saxon *giflehan*, Old High German *flehjan*; Greek θέλγειν (“to charm, enchant”); DM. 20; Gf. III, 755; Schm., *Heliand Glossary*, p. 36), conjugation I, *þaiþlaih, þlaihans*: “to embrace.”

**GA-þLAIHAN**:

1. “To embrace,” ἐναγκαλίζεσθαι: Mark X, 16.

2. “To comfort,” παρακαλεῖν: 2 Cor. II, 7; V, 20; VII, 6; 1 Tim. V, 1; VI, 2; 2 Tim. IV, 2; Titus I, 9; παραμυθεῖσθαι: 1 Thess. II, 11; προνοεῖν, “to provide for”: 1 Tim. V, 8.

**GA-þLAIHTS**, feminine: “comfort, consolation,” παράκλησις: Luke VI, 24; 2 Cor. I, 3, 4, 6, 7; VII, 4, 7; 2 Thess. II, 16; 1 Tim. IV, 13; παραμύθιον: Phil. II, 1.

**þLAUHS**, see under *þliuhan*.  
**þLEIHSL**, see 2 Cor. XII, 10.

**þLIUHAN** (Old Norse *flya*, Old Saxon *fliohan*, Anglo-Saxon *fleon*, Old High German *fliuhan*, Old French *flia*, English *fly, flie*, Swedish *fly*, Danish *flye*, Dutch *vlien*, Modern High German *fliehen*; Bopp 13; Gr. II, 24; Gf. III, 764; Rchth. 746), conjugation I, *þlauh, þlauhun, þlauhans*: “to flee,” φεύγειν: Matt. X, 23; Luke III, 7; John X, 5; 1 Tim. VI, 11; 2 Tim. II, 22.

**AF-þLIUHAN**, the same: John X, 13.

**GA-þLIUHAN**, the same: Matt. VIII, 33; Mark V, 14; XIV, 50, 52; XVI, 8; Luke VIII, 34.

**UNþA-þLIUHAN**, “to escape,” ἐκφεύγειν: 2 Cor. XI, 33; 1 Thess. V, 3.

**þLAUHS**, masculine: “flight,” φυγή: Mark XIII, 18.

**þU** (Old Norse *þu, þinn*, Old Saxon and Old French *thu, thin*, Anglo-Saxon *þu, þin*, Old High German *du, din*, English *thou, thine*, Swedish and Danish *du, din*; Greek σύ (“you”), τύ (“you”), σεός (“your”); Latin *tu, tuus*; Bopp 80, 83, 482; Gr. I, 780; Gf. V, 78; Rchth. 1072, 1079), personal pronoun: “you,” σύ: Matt. VI, 6, 17; XI, 3, 23; XXVI, 73; XXVII, 4, 11; Mark I, 11, 24; III, 11; VIII, 29; XIV, 61, 67, 68; XV, 2; Luke I, 28, 42, 76; III, 22; IV, 7, 41; VII, 19, 20; IX, 20, 60; X, 15; XV, 31; XVI, 7; XVII, 8; XIX, 19, 42; John III, 26; VI, 30, 69; VII, 3, 52; VIII, 13, 25, 33, 48, 52, 53; IX, 17, 28, 34, 35; X, 24, 33; XI, 27, 42; XII, 34; XIII, 38; XIV, 9; XVI, 30; XVII, 5, 8, 21, 23, 25; XVIII, 17, 25, 33, 34, 37; XIX, 9; Rom. IX, 20; XI, 17, 18, 20, 22, 24; XIV, 10; Gal. II, 14; VI, 1; 1 Tim. IV, 15; VI, 11; 2 Tim. I, 18; II, 1, 3; III, 10, 14; IV, 5, 15; Titus II, 1; Philem. 12. **þUEI**, “you who”: Rom. XIV, 4.

**þEINA**, genitive: “of you, your”: Matt. VI, 13; 1 Cor. XII, 21; 2 Cor. VI, 2; Philem. 20.

**þUS**, dative: “to you”: Matt. V, 26, 29, 30, 40, 42; VI, 2, 4, 6, 18, 23; VIII, 13, 29; IX, 2, 5; XI, 10, 21, 24; XXV, 39, 44; XXVII, 19; Mark I, 2, 24; II, 5, 9, 11; V, 7, 19, 41; VI, 18, 22, 23; IX, 5, 17, 25, 43, 45, [Col. 1347] 47; X, 21, 51; XI, 14, 23, 28; Luke I, 3, 13, 14, 19, 28, 30, 35; IV, 6, 34; V, 10, 20, 23, 24; VI, 29; VII, 7, 14, 20, 27, 40, 47, 48; VIII, 28, 39; IX, 33; X, 21; XIV, 10, 12, 14; XV, 29; XVI, 2, 6; XVII, 4; XVIII, 11, 22, 41; XIX, 43, 44; XX, 2; John III, 3, 5, 26; VI, 30; IX, 10, 17, 26, 37; XI, 22, 40, 41; XII, 15; XIII, 38; XVII, 5, 7, 8, 11, 13, 21; XVIII, 30, 34; XIX, 11; Rom. **þUZEI**, “you to whom”: Mark I, 11; Luke III, 22.

**þUK**, accusative: “you”: Matt. V, 23, 25, 29, 30, 39, 41, 42; VI, 3; VIII, 4, 19; IX, 2, 22; XXV, 38, 39, 44; XXVI, 73; XXVII, 13; Mark I, 24, 37, 44; III, 32; IV, 38; V, 7, 19, 31, 34; IX, 43, 45, 47; X, 28, 35, 49, 52; XI, 23; XII, 14, 31; XIV, 60; XV, 4, 30; Luke I, 35; II, 48; IV, 9, 10, 11, 23, 34; V, 8, 14; VI, 29, 30; VII, 6, 50; VIII, 20, 28, 39, 45, 48; IX, 38, 57, 61; X, 27; XIV, 12, 18, 19; XVII, 6, 9, 19; XVIII, 28, 42; XIX, 21, 22, 43, 44; John VII, 4, 20; VIII, 13, 53; X, 33; XI, 8, 28; XIII, 37; XIV, 22; XVI, 30; XVII, 1, 3, 4, 25; XVIII, 26, 35; XIX, 10; Rom. I, 3, 4, 6, 8; II, 1, 15; III, 14, 15; Philem. 13, 19, 23.

**þUKEI**, “you whom”: Mark I, 11; see the note on that passage.

**þEINS**, possessive pronoun: “your,” ὁ σός: Matt. V, 23, 24, 25, 29, 30, 33, 36, 39, 40, 43; VI, 3, 4, 6, 9, 10, 17, 18, 22, 23; IX, 2, 6, 14, 18, 22; XI, 10; XXVI, 73; Mark I, 2; II, 5, 9, 11, 24; III, 5, 32; V, 19, 34, 35; VI, 18; VII, 5, 10, 29; IX, 18, 38, 43, 45, 47; X, 19, 37, 52; XII, 30, 31, 36; XIV, 70; Luke I, 13, 36, 38, 42, 44, 61; II, 29, 30, 32, 35, 48; IV, 7, 8, 11, 12, 23; V, 5, 14, 20, 24; VI, 10, 41, 42; VII, 27, 44, 48, 50; VIII, 20, 39, 48, 49; IX, 40, 41, 49; X, 17, 21, 27; XIV, 12; XV, 18, 19, 21, 27, 29, 30, 32; XVI, 2; XVII, 3, 19; XVIII, 20, 42; XIX, 5, 16, 18, 20, 22, 39, 42, 43, 44; XX, 43; John VII, 3; VIII, 13, 19; XI, 23; XII, 15, 28; XIII, 38; XVII, 1, 6, 11, 12, 14, 17, 26; Rom. X, 6, 8, 9; XII, 20; XIII, 9; XIV, 10, 15; XV, 9; 1 Cor. XV, 55, 56; Gal. V, 14; 1 Tim. IV, 12; V, 23; 2 Tim. I, 4, 5; IV, 5; Philem. 14, 21; σός: Matt. VIII, 11; also *þeins ist* in place of σοὶ ἐστιν, “is yours”: Mark V, 9; Luke VIII, 30; in place of the Greek article: 1 Cor. VII, 16.

**þUGKJAN** (*þuggkjan*, Mark X, 42; John XVI, 2; Old Norse *þenkia*, Old Saxon *thunciun*, Anglo-Saxon *þincan*, Old High German *dunkjan*, Old French *thinka*, English *think*, Modern High German *dünken*; compare *þagkjan*; Gr. II, 60; Gf. V, 172; Rchth. 1074), anomalous conjugation, *þuhta, þuhtedun, þuhts*:

1. “To suppose, think,” δοκεῖν: Mark X, 42; Luke VIII, 18; John XVI, 2; 1 Cor. XII, 22; Gal. II, 6; VI, 3; Phil. III, 4.

2. “To seem,” δοκεῖν: 2 Cor. X, 9; Gal. II, 9; *Skeireins* I, c; IV, c; VI, a (b); φαίνεσθαι: 2 Cor. XIII, 7. Impersonal *þugkeiþ mis*, “it seems to me,” δοκῶ or δοκεῖ μοι: Matt. VI, 7; XXVI, 65; Luke XIX, 11; subscription to 1 Cor.; 2 Cor. XII, 19; Gal. II, 2; φαίνεταί μοι, “it seems to me”: Mark XIV, 64.

**HAUH-þUHTS**, adjective: “puffed up, conceited,” τετυφωμένος: 1 Tim. VI, 6.

**MIKIL-þUHTS**, the same: ὑπερήφανος, “proud”: Luke I, 51.

**þUHTUS**, masculine:

1. “Opinion”: Col. II, 23.

2. “Conscience,” συνείδησις: 1 Cor. X, 28, 29; perhaps also *Skeireins* VI, b.

**þUHTS**, see under *þugkjan*.

**þULAN** (*þuljan*, 2 Tim. III, 11; see the note on that passage; Old Norse *þola*, Old Saxon *tholon*, Anglo-Saxon *þolian*, Old High German *dālen, doljan*, Old French *thielda, tholian*, Danish *taale*, Swedish *tala*, Modern High German and Dutch *dulden*; Greek τλᾶν (“to endure”); Latin *tolerare*; Gf. V, 133; Rchth. 1076), conjugation II: “to endure, bear,” ἀνέχεσθαι: Mark IX, 19; Luke XI, 41; Col. III, 13; στέγειν, “to bear”: 1 Cor. XIII, 7; *þarbos þulan*, see under *þarbs*.

[Col. 1348] **GA-þULAN**, “to suffer,” πάσχειν: Mark V, 26; Luke XVII, 25; ὑπομένειν, “to endure”: 2 Tim. II, 10, 12.

**US-þULAN**, “to endure,” ἀνέχεσθαι: 2 Cor. XI, 1, 4, 19, 20; Eph. IV, 2; 1 Thess. V, 14; 2 Thess. I, 4; 2 Tim. IV, 3; ἐνέχεσθαι, “to be held fast”: Gal. V, 1; ὑπομένειν, “to endure”: Rom. XII, 12; ὑποφέρειν, “to bear”: 2 Tim. III, 11; στέγειν, “to endure”: 1 Thess. III, 1, 5; *Skeireins* VIII, b, d; *gabaurþ anþara usþulan*, “to endure another birth, to be born again”: *Skeireins* II, b; present participle *usþulands*, “patient, forbearing,” ἀνεξίκακος: 2 Tim. II, 24.

**þULAINS**, feminine:

1. “Endurance,” ὑπομονή: Luke VIII, 15; Rom. XV, 4, 5; 2 Cor. XII, 12; 1 Tim. VI, 11; 2 Tim. III, 10.

2. “Suffering,” πάθημα: 2 Cor. I, 5, 6, 7; Phil. III, 10; *Skeireins* II, a.

**US-þULAINS**, “endurance,” ὑπομονή: Col. I, 11; 2 Thess. III, 5.

**þUSUNDI** (Old Norse *þusund*, Old Saxon *thusundig*, Anglo-Saxon *þusend*, Old High German *dusunt*, Old French *thusend*, English *thousand*, Swedish *tusend*, Danish *tusind*, Dutch *tuysend*, Modern High German *tausend*; Gr. I, 764; Gf. V, 230; Rchth. 1081), feminine numeral—although in Ezra II, 15 *þusundja* is also used as a neuter; see the note on that passage—“thousand,” χίλιοι: Mark V, 13; VIII, 9, 19; Luke IX, 14; XIV, 31; John VI, 10; Ezra II, 12, 15, 31, 35, 37, 38, 39; *Skeireins* VII, b; *fimf þusundjos*, “five thousand,” πεντακισχίλιοι: Luke IX, 14.

**þUSUNDI-FAþS**, see under *Faþs*.

**\*þUT** (Old Norse *þiota*, Anglo-Saxon *þeotan*, Old High German *duz, deozan*, English *toot*, Swedish *tiuta*, Dutch *toethorn*, Modern High German *tuten*; Gr. II, 20; Gf. V, 235).

**þUT-HAURN**, see under *Haurn*.

**þRAGJAN** (compare Anglo-Saxon *þrag*; Greek τρέχειν; Bopp 124), conjugation II: “to run,” τρέχειν: Matt. XXVII, 48; Mark XV, 36; Luke XV, 20; 2 Thess. III, 1.

**BI-þRAGJAN**, “to run ahead, precede,” προτρέχειν: Luke XIX, 4.

**þRAIHNS**, see under *þreihan*.

**þRAMSTEI** (Gr. III, 267), feminine: “locust,” ἀκρίς: Mark I, 6.

**\*þRAS** (Old Norse *þras*, Old High German *drāti, drason*; Gr. II, 479; Gf. V, 252, 256), adjective: “headlong, premature.”

**þRASA-BALþEI**, see under *Balþs*.  
**þRASK**, see under *þriskan*.

**þRAFSTJAN** (Old Norse *traust*, Old Saxon *thristi*, Old High German *trost*, English *trust*, Swedish *trösta*, Danish *troste*, Modern High German *trösten*; Gr. II, 43; Gf. V, 474), conjugation II:

1. “To comfort,” παραμυθεῖσθαι: John XI, 31; 1 Thess. V, 14; *þrafstjan sik*, “to take comfort, be encouraged,” θαρσεῖν: Matt. IX, 2; Mark X, 49; Luke VIII, 48; John XVI, 33.

2. “To exhort, comfort,” παρακαλεῖν: Luke III, 18; 1 Thess. IV, 18; V, 11.

3. “To fear,” φοβερίζειν (“to frighten”): Neh. VI, 14; this is unquestionably erroneous; see the note on that passage.

**ANA-þRAFSTJAN**, “to refresh, restore,” ἀναψύχειν: 2 Tim. I, 16; ἀναπαύειν: Philem. 20.

**GA-þRAFSTJAN**:

1. “To comfort,” παραμυθεῖσθαι: John XI, 19.

2. “To refresh, restore,” ἀναπαύειν: 1 Cor. XVI, 18.

3. “To exhort,” παρακαλεῖν: 2 Cor. I, 4, 6; VII, 6, 7, 13; Eph. VI, 22; Col. IV, 8; 1 Thess. III, 7; 2 Thess. II, 17.

**þRAFSTEINS**, feminine: “comfort, consolation,” παράκλησις: Rom. XV, 5.

**GA-þRAFSTEINS**, the same: Rom. XV, 4; 2 Cor. I, 5; VII, 13; Phil. II, 1.

Consolation (παρηγορία): Col. IV, 11; Luke IV, 19 must likewise be understood thus, at least “release” (ἄφις) does not correspond.

þREIHAN (Old Norse þrengia, þryngia; Old Saxon thringan; Anglo-Saxon þringan; Old High German dringan, drangon; English thring, throng; Swedish trenga; Danish trænge; Modern High German drängen; Gr. II, 18; Gf. V, 261), conjugation I, þraih, þraihun, þraihans: to constrict, press, θλίβειν: Matt. VII, 14; Mark III, 9; 2 Cor. I, 6; IV, 8; συνθλίβειν, to press together: Mark V, 24, 31; ἀποθλίβειν, to press upon: Luke VIII, 45; στενοχωρεῖν, to confine: 2 Cor. VI, 12; συμπνίγειν, to choke: Luke VIII, 42.

GA-þREIHAN, the same: θλίβειν, to afflict: 2 Thess. I, 6, 7.

*þRAIHNS, masculine: crowd, multitude.

[Col. 1349]

FAIHU-þRAIHNS (Gr. II, 155): riches, μαμμωνᾶς, Mammon: Luke XVI, 9, 11, 13.

þREIHSL, neuter: distress, στενοχωρία: 2 Cor. XII, 10.

þREIS (Old Norse þrir; Old Saxon thria; Anglo-Saxon þry, þreo; Old High German dri; Old French thre; English three; Swedish and Danish tre; Dutch dry; Modern High German drei; Bopp 80, 82; Gr. I, 761; Gf. V, 239; Rchth. 1076), neuter þrija, numeral: three, τρεῖς: Matt. XXVII, 63; Mark VIII, 2, 31; IX, 5; Luke I, 56; II, 46; IV, 25; IX, 33; 1 Cor. XIV, 27; 2 Cor. XIII, 1; 1 Tim. V, 19.

þREIS-TIGJUS, plural (genitive þrijetigive, accusative þrinstiguns): thirty, τριάκοντα: Matt. XXVII, 3; Luke III, 23.

þRIJA-HUNDA, neuter plural: three hundred, τριακόσιοι: Mark XIV, 5.

þRIDJA, adjective: third, τρίτος: Matt. XXVII, 64; Mark IX, 31; XII, 21; XV, 25; Luke IX, 22; XVIII, 33; XX, 12, 31; 1 Cor. XV, 4; 2 Cor. XII, 2.

þRIDJO, adverb: for the third time, τρίτον: 2 Cor. XII, 14; XIII, 1.

þRIDJA, see under þreis.

*þRIUTAN (Old Norse þriota; Anglo-Saxon þreatjan; Old High German driuzan; Modern High German verdriessen; Gr. II, 20; Gf. V, 247), conjugation I, þraut, þrutun, þrutans: to burden.

US-þRIUTAN: 1) to be harsh, κόπον παρέχειν, “to cause trouble”: Mark XIV, 6; Luke XVIII, 5; 2) to afflict, ἐπηρεάζειν: Mark V, 44.

þRUTS-FILL, see under Fill.

þRISKAN (Old Norse þreskia; Anglo-Saxon þerscan [þrescan]; Old High German drescan; English thresh; Swedish tröska; Danish tærske; Modern High German dreschen; Gr. II, 40; Gf. V, 264), conjugation I, þrask, þruskun, þruskans: to thresh, ἀλοᾶν: 1 Cor. IX, 9; 1 Tim. V, 18.

GA-þRASK, neuter: threshing-floor, ἅλως: Luke III, 17.

þRUTS, see under þriutan.

þROþJAN (Old Norse þrottr, íþrótt; Danish idræt; Swedish idrott), conjugation II: to exercise, γυμνάζειν: 1 Tim. IV, 7.

[Col. 1350]

US-þROþJAN: to initiate, μυεῖν: Phil. IV, 12.

US-þROþEINS, feminine: exercise, γυμνασία: 1 Tim. IV, 8.

þVAHAN (Old Norse þvo; Old Saxon thvahan; Anglo-Saxon þvean, þveal; Old High German thwahan; Swedish tvätta; Danish tvætte; Bavarian zwagen; Gf. V, 267; Schm. IV, 303), conjugation I, þvoh, þvohun, þvahans: to wash, νίπτειν: Matt. VI, 17; John XIII, 14; 1 Tim. V, 10; to wash oneself, νίπτεσθαι: John IX, 7.

AF-þVAHAN: to wash off, νίπτειν: John XIII, 14; to wash oneself, νίπτεσθαι: John IX, 7, 11, 15.

BI-þVAHAN: to wash, νίπτεσθαι: John IX, 11.

US-þVAHAN: to wash, νίπτειν: John XIII, 12, 14; ἀποπλύνειν, to wash off: Luke V, 2.

UN-þVAHANS, past participle: unwashed, ἄνιπτος: Mark VI, 2.

þVAHL, neuter: washing, bath, λουτρόν: Eph. V, 26; Skeir. II. b.

þVAIRHS (Old Norse þver; Anglo-Saxon þveorh; Danish tvær; Gr. II, 39; compare Gf. V, 278; Rchth. 1081), adjective: irascible, ὀργίλος: Titus I, 7; angered, ὀργισθείς: Luke XIV, 21; þvairhs visan, to be angry, ὀργίζεσθαι: Eph. IV, 26.

þVAIRHEI, feminine: 1) anger, ὀργή: Rom. IX, 22; XII, 19; XIII, 4, 5; Eph. IV, 31; 1 Tim. II, 8; παροργισμός, provocation to anger: Eph. IV, 26; θυμός, wrath: Col. III, 8, 21; Skeir. VIII, c; gramjan du þvairhein, see under Gramjan; 2) quarrel, ἔρις: 2 Cor. XII, 20.

*þVAST: safe, firm.

þVASTIþA, feminine: security, τὸ ἀσφαλές, “what is secure”: Phil. III, 1.

GA-þVASTJAN, conjugation II: to confirm, strengthen, βεβαιοῦν: 2 Cor. I, 21; κραταιοῦν, to make strong: 1 Cor. XVI, 13; καρτερίζειν, to make steadfast: Gal. VI, 1; θεμελιοῦν, to establish: Col. I, 23.

þYMIAMA (Greek word), masculine: thymiama, sacrifice, θυμίαμα: Luke I, 10, 11.

þOMAS, proper name: Thomas, Θωμᾶς: Mark III, 18; Luke VI, 15; John XI, 16; XIV, 5.

I
[Col. 1349] **IAEIRUS** (*Jaeirus*, Mark 5:22), masculine proper name, “Jairus,” Ἰάειρος: Mark 5:22; Luke 8:41.

**IAIRAIMIAS**, masculine proper name, “Jeremiah,” Ἱερεμίας: Matthew 27:9.

**IAIRAUPAULIS** (*Jairupula*, see this word), feminine proper name, “Hierapolis,” Ἱεράπολις (a form which the Goth probably borrowed from the nearby Hieropolis in Vindelicia): Colossians 4:13.

**IAIREIKO** (*Iairiko*, Mark 10:46; *eiaireiko*, Ezra 2:34), feminine proper name, “Jericho,” Ἱεριχώ: Mark 10:46; Luke 10:30; 18:35; 19:1; Ezra 2:34.

**IAIRUSALEM**, proper name, “Jerusalem,” Ἱερουσαλήμ: Mark 11:1; 15:41; Luke 2:22, 41, 43; 9:31, 51; 10:30; Nehemiah 7:2, 3; Luke 5:17.

**ÏAIRUSAULYMA** (*Iairausaulyma*, John 12:12), feminine proper name, “Jerusalem,” Ἱεροσόλυμα: Matthew 5:35; Mark 3:22; 10:32, 33; 11:11, 27; Luke 2:38, 42; 5:17; 19:28; John 10:22; 12:12.

**ÏAIRAUSAULYMEIS**, plural only, the same: Mark 3:8; 7:1; John 11:18 (in this passage); “Jerusalemites,” Ἱεροσαλυμῖται: Mark 1:5.

**ÏAIRUSAULYMEITES**, masculine, “Jerusalemite,” Ἱεροσολυμίτης: John 7:25.

**IAISSAIS**, masculine proper name, “Jesse,” Ἰεσσαί: Luke 3:32; Romans 15:12.

**IAKOB**, masculine proper name, “Jacob,” Ἰακώβ: Matthew 8:11; 27:56; Mark 5:37; 6:3; 12:26; Luke 1:33; 3:34; 20:37; Romans 4:13; 11:26.

**ÏAKOBUS** (*Iakubos*, Luke 9:54), masculine proper name, “James,” Ἰάκωβος: Mark 1:19, 29; 3:17, 18; 5:37; 9:2; 10:35, 41; Luke 5:10; 6:16; 9:54; 1 Corinthians 15:7; Galatians 2:9.

[Col. 1350] **IAURDANUS** (*Jaurdanus*, John 3:26), masculine proper name, “Jordan,” Ἰόρδανος: Mark 3:8; 10:1; Luke 3:3; 4:1; John 3:26; 10:40.

**ÏAURDANES**, masculine, “Jordan,” Ἰορδάνης: Mark 1:5, 9.

**IARED**, masculine proper name, “Jared,” Ἰαρέδ: Luke 3:37.

**IAREIM**, masculine proper name, “Harim,” Ξαρίμ: Ezra 2:39.

**IASSON**, masculine proper name, “Jason,” Ἰάσων: Romans 16:21.

**IBAI** (*ïbai*, Luke 17:9; 1 Corinthians 9:8; Galatians 6:1; see the note on that passage; Old Norse *if*, Old Saxon *ef*, Anglo-Saxon *gif*, Old High German *ipu*, English *if*, Swedish *jäf*, Modern High German *ob*; Gr. II, 50; Gf. I, 75).

1. Interrogative particle: “whether? surely not? is it not?” Used in an ironical question, where a negative answer is expected, or where a judgment is also implied; μή: Matthew 9:15; Mark 2:19; Luke 17:9; John 3:4; 6:67; 7:41, 51, 52; 8:53; 9:27, 40; 10:21; 18:17; Romans 9:14, 20; 11:1; 1 Corinthians 1:13; 9:8; 10:22; 2 Corinthians 3:1; 11:7, 16; 12:17, 18. With μήτι, “can it be that?”: Matthew 7:16; Mark 4:21; Luke 6:39.

2. “Lest perhaps,” μή: after *ogan* (“to fear”), 2 Corinthians 12:21; also μήπως, Galatians 4:11; and with *ogands* (“fearing”) understood, Mark 2:21 (εἰ δὲ μή, “otherwise”); 2 Corinthians 12:6; after *bivandjan* (“to avoid”), 2 Corinthians 8:20; *þugkjan* (“to suppose”), Galatians 2:2; *atsaiwan* (“to observe, watch”), Galatians 6:1; *saiwan* (“to see, take heed”), Galatians 5:15; 1 Thessalonians 5:15. Likewise, Galatians 5:13: *þatainei ïbai þana freihals du leva leikis taujaiþ*, “only do not use freedom as an opportunity for the flesh”; μήπως: 1 Corinthians 9:27; 2 Corinthians 9:4; ἵνα μή, “in order that not”: Luke 18:5.

**ÏBAI-AUFTO** (*ïbai ufto*, Matthew 27:64).

1. Interrogative formula, “might it perhaps be?” μήποτε: John 7:26; εἰ μήτι, “unless perhaps,” 2 Corinthians 13:5.

2. “Lest perhaps,” μήτι ἄρα, after *miton* (“to measure, intend”), 2 Corinthians 1:17; μήποτε: Luke 14:12.

3. “Lest perhaps,” μήπως: 2 Corinthians 2:7; 1 Thessalonians 3:5; after *ogan*, 2 Corinthians 11:3; 12:20; μήποτε: Matthew 27:64; ἵνα μή, “in order that not”: 1 Timothy 3:6; ἵνα μήποτε, “in order that perhaps not”: Luke 14:29; εἰ δὲ μή, “otherwise”: Mark 2:22. For *ïbai aufto ni*, see under *ïbai ni*; for *ïbai ei*, see John 7:31.

**Ibai ni**, interrogative: “is it not?” μὴ οὐ: Romans 10:18, 19; 1 Corinthians 9:4, 5; 11:22. Also *ïbai aufto ni*, “lest perhaps not,” μήπως οὐδέ: Romans 11:21. *Ibai wan*, “lest perhaps once,” μήποτε: Matthew 5:25. For *þatainei ïbai*, see under **Ains**.

**IBNS** (Old Norse *jafn*, Old Saxon *efno*, Anglo-Saxon *even*, Old Frisian *ivin*, Old High German *eban*, English *even*, Swedish *jemn*, Danish *jevn*, Modern High German *eben*; Gr. II, 50; IV, 572; Gf. I, 95; Rchth. 856), adjective.

1. In the strong form: “level, plain,” πεδινός: Luke 6:17.

2. In the weak form: “equal, like,” ἴσος: *Skeireins* 1, a; V, d. *ïbna aggilum*, “equal to angels, like angels,” ἰσάγγελος: Luke 20:36.

**GA-ÏBNJAN**, class-II weak verb: “to make level; to raze.” *airþai gaïbnjan*, “to level with the ground, to demolish [a city],” ἐδαφίζειν: Luke 19:44.

**IBNASSUS**, masculine: “equality,” ἰσότης: 2 Corinthians 8:13, 14; Colossians 4:1.

**ÏBNA-LEIKS**, see under **Leiks**.

**ÏBNA-SKAUNS**, see under **Skauns**.

**IBUKS** (belongs to the root **IBAN**, **AF**; Gr. II, 50; compare *Afar*), adjective: “backward, back,” εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω: Luke 17:31; John 6:66; 18:6.

**IGGQIS** (*ïgqis*, Mark 1:17; 10:36; 14:13; *ïnqis*, Luke 19:31), accusative and dative dual of the second-person pronoun (Old Norse *yckr* and *yckar*, Old Saxon *inker* and *ink*, Anglo-Saxon *inc* and *incer*, Old High German *inch* and *inchar*; Bopp 483): “you two.”

1. Dative, “to you two,” ὑμῖν: Matthew 9:29; Mark 10:36; 11:2, 3; 14:13.

2. Accusative, “you two,” ὑμᾶς: Mark 1:17; Luke 19:31.

**ÏGGQARA**, dual genitive: “of you two,” ὑμῶν: 1 Corinthians 12:21.

**ÏGGQAR** (Old Norse *yckar*, Old Saxon *ink*, Anglo-Saxon *incer*, Old High German *incharer*), possessive pronoun: “belonging to you two,” “your [two],” ὁ ὑμῶν: Matthew 9:29.

**ID . . .** (Old Norse *id . . .*, Anglo-Saxon *. . . ed*, Old High German *it . . .*, *ita . . .*; Gr. II, 757; Gf. I, 148), inseparable particle, meaning “back . . . ,” “again/backwards . . . ,” and occurring only in *ïddaljo* and *ïdveit*, together with *ïdveitjan*, derived from the latter.

**IDDJA** (Bopp 123), preterite of **Gaggan**; see that word.

**IDUMAIA**, feminine proper name, “Idumaea,” Ἰδουμαία: Mark 3:8.

**IDR** (Old Norse *idra . . .*, *idraz*; compare Modern High German *Ader*; Gr. III, 407; Schw. under *Ader*): “inner part, inwardness” (?).

**ÏDREIGA**, feminine: “repentance,” μετάνοια: Mark 1:4; Luke 3:3, 8; 5:32; 15:7; 2 Corinthians 7:9, 10; 2 Timothy 2:25; *Skeireins* III, c. *ïnu ïdreiga*, “without repentance; not regretted,” ἀμεταμέλητος: Romans 11:29.

**ÏDREIGON**, class-II weak verb, and *ïdreigon sik* (“to repent oneself”; Luke 17:3; Matthew 11:20 [yet see the note there]; 2 Corinthians 7:8, prefatory matter): “to repent,” μετανοεῖν: Matthew 11:20; Mark 1:15; 6:12; Luke 15:7, 10; 17:3, 4; 2 Corinthians 12:21. “To regret, change one’s mind,” μεταμέλεσθαι: Matthew 27:3; 2 Corinthians 7:8.

**GA-IDREIGON**, the same: “to repent,” μετανοεῖν: Luke 10:13; and it should likewise, more correctly, be read in Matthew 11:21 instead of the simple verb.

**IESUS** (in the manuscripts, when the name is solemnly abbreviated, it is written *is*, *iuis*, *iua* [Note: [Col. 1351] Double-click the ornament icon that follows to see these characters as they appear in Migne.], except when a person other than Christ is meant, as in Colossians 4:11; Ezra 2:36, 40), masculine proper name, “Jesus,” Ἰησοῦς: Matthew 8:29, 34; 9:10; 26:75; 27:17, 54, 58; Mark 1:1, 24; 5:9, 7, 15; 10:47, 50; 12:17, 29, 35; 14:6; Luke 3:21; 4:34; 8:28; 18:38; John 11:41; 12:3, 7, 12; Romans 6:23; 15:6; 1 Corinthians 5:4; 9:1; 15:57; 2 Corinthians 1:1, 2; 11:4, 31; Galatians 2:16; 6:18; Ephesians 1:1, 2; Philippians 3:8, 9; Colossians 3:17; 4:11; 1 Thessalonians 2:18, 19; 3:11, 13; 4:1, 2; 5:9; 2 Thessalonians 3:12; 1 Timothy 1:2; Ezra 2:36, 40.

[Col. 1352] **IZE, IZAI**, see under **Is**.

**IZEI** (*ïze*, Matthew 5:32; Mark 9:1; Luke 8:13, 15; 1 Corinthians 15:27; Galatians 1:1; Ephesians 4:15; 1 Timothy 1:16; compare **Is**), indeclinable relative pronoun: “who, which, that,” ὅς: Luke 8:13; John 8:40; 15:26; 2 Corinthians 1:10; 3:6; Ephesians 1:14; 4:15. With a participle, “the one who,” ὁ with participle: John 12:4; 1 Corinthians 15:57; 2 Corinthians 8:16; Galatians 1:1, 4; Ephesians 1:3. Following immediately after a demonstrative, *sa ïzei*, “this one who,” οὗτος ὁ with participle: John 11:37. “The one who,” ὁ with participle: 1 Corinthians 15:27; 2 Corinthians 5:21; Galatians 6:13; compare Ephesians 2:17. “Whoever,” ὅστις: Matthew 7:15; Mark 9:1; Luke 8:15. “Whoever,” ὃς ἐάν: Matthew 5:32.

**IZVARA** (Old Norse *ydhr*, *ydhar*, Old Saxon *iu*, *iuwer*, *eovih*, *eover*, Old Frisian *iu*, *inwe*, Old High German *iwih*, *iu*, *iwar*, English *your*, Swedish and Danish *eder*, Modern High German *euch*, *euer*; Bopp 484; Gr. I, 780 ff.; Gf. I, 575; Rchth. 1080), plural genitive of the second-person personal pronoun: “of you, your,” ὑμῶν: Matthew 6:27; Mark 10:44; Luke 14:28, 33; 15:4; 17:7; John 6:64, 70; 7:19; 8:46; 11:15; 12:30; 13:21; Romans 11:28; 1 Corinthians 1:13, 14; 4:6; 6:1; 7:5; 11:24; 14:26; 16:2; 2 Corinthians 1:23; 2:3, 10; 4:15; 7:15; 8:9; 9:14; Ephesians 1:16; 3:1; Philippians 1:24; 2:26; 1 Thessalonians 2:11; 3:9; 4:4; 2 Thessalonians 1:3; 3:8.

**ÏZVIZEI**, “you who”: Galatians 3:1.

**ÏZVIS**, accusative: “you,” ὑμᾶς: Matthew 3:11; 5:44, 46; 6:30; 7:23; 10:40; Mark 1:8; 6:11; 7:6; 9:19, 40, 41; 11:29; 16:7; Luke 3:16; 6:9, 22, 26–28, 32; 9:5, 41, 50; 10:3, 8–11; 16:9, 14, 15; 20:3; John 5:45; 6:61, 70; 7:7; 8:26, 32, 36; 12:35; 13:18, 34; 14:3, 18, 26; 15:9, 12, 15–20; 16:2, 13, 22, 26, 27, 33; Romans 10:19; 11:25; 12:1, 2, 10, 14, 19; 15:7, 13; 16:22, 23; 1 Corinthians 5:9; 7:28; 10:1, 20, 27; 11:2, 3, 22; 16:7, 15, 19, 20; 2 Corinthians 1:6, 8, 16; 2:2, 5, 7, 8; 6:1, 17; 7:8, 11, 12; 8:22, 23; 9:4, 8; 10:1, 9, 13, 14, 16; 11:2, 11, 20; 12:13–20; 13:5, 12; Galatians [Col. 1353] 1:6, 7; 2:1, 5; 4:9, 11, 12, 16, 17; 5:4, 7, 8, 10, 12, 15; 6:12, 13; Ephesians 2:1; 3:2, 13; 4:1, 2; 5:6, 18; 6:10, 11; Philippians 1:27; 2:28; 3:17; Colossians 1:7, 9, 12, 13, 21, 22, 24, 25; 2:13, 16, 18; 3:9, 12, 13, 16; 4:2, 8, 10, 12–14; 1 Thessalonians 2:11, 12; 3:2, 5, 6, 9, 12; 4:1, 3, 9, 10, 13; 5:1, 4, 11, 12, 14, 18, 22, 23, 27; 2 Thessalonians 1:3, 5, 11; 2:1–3; 3:3, 6, 14.

**ÏZVAR**, possessive pronoun: “your,” ὁ ὑμῶν: Matthew 5:16, 20, 37, 44, 45, 47, 48; 6:1, 8, 14, 15, 21, 25, 26, 32; 9:4, 11; 10:29, 30; Mark 2:8; 6:11; 7:9, 13; 8:17; 10:5, 43; 11:25, 26; 13:18; Luke 3:14; 4:21; 5:4, 22; 6:22–24, 35, 36, 38; 8:25; 9:5, 44; 10:6, 11, 20; 16:15; John 6:49, 58; 8:21, 24, 38, 41, 42, 44, 56; 9:19, 41; 10:34; 14:1, 27; 15:11, 16; 16:6, 20, 22, 24; 18:31; Romans 12:1, 2; 16:24; 1 Corinthians 5:6; 7:5, 14; 15:17, 58; 16:3, 14, 17, 18; 2 Corinthians 1:14, 24; 2:9; 4:5; 5:11; 6:12; 7:7; 8:14, 24; 9:2, 5, 10, 13; 10:6, 8, 15; 11:3, 8; 12:14, 15, 19; 13:9; Galatians 4:6, 15; 6:18; Ephesians 1:13, 18; 2:1; 3:13, 17; 4:4, 23, 26, 29; 5:19; 6:14, 22; Philippians 1:19, 25, 26; 2:25, 30; 4:5–7; Colossians 1:8; 2:13; 3:3–5, 8, 15, 16, 19, 21; 4:6, 8; 1 Thessalonians 2:17; 3:2, 5–7, 10, 13; 4:3, 11; 5:12, 23; 2 Thessalonians 1:3, 4; 2:17; 3:5; Philemon 22. “Your,” ὁ ὑμέτερος: Luke 6:20; 16:12; John 7:6; 8:17; 15:20; Romans 11:31; 1 Corinthians 15:31; 2 Corinthians 1:6; 8:8; Galatians 6:13. “Concerning you,” ὁ καθ’ ὑμᾶς: Ephesians 1:15. “Of themselves,” ἑαυτῶν: Ephesians 5:25. “One’s own,” ἴδιος: Colossians 3:18 (?); 1 Thessalonians 2:14. *ïzvar misso*, “each of another, one another’s,” ἀλλήλων: Galatians 6:2.

Once it translates τε, “and”: John 6:18; and γε, “indeed”: Luke 18:5.

8. Combined with other particles:
