b. *ïþ nu*, “now, therefore,” οὖν: Matthew 5:19.

**IK** (Old Norse *ek*, Old Saxon and Anglo-Saxon *ic*, Old Frisian and Dutch *ik*, Old High German *ih*, English *I*, Swedish *jag*, Danish *jeg*, Modern High German *ich*; Latin *ego*, Greek ἐγώ, “I”; Bopp 481; Gr. I, 780; Gf. I, 117; Rchth. 848), first-person personal pronoun: “I,” ἐγώ: Matthew 3:11; 5:17, 28, 32, 34, 39, 44; 8:7, 9; 10:32, 33; 11:10; Mark 1:2, 7, 8; 6:19; 9:25; 10:38, 39; 11:29, 33; 12:26, 36; 14:58, 62; Luke 1:18, 19; 2:48; 3:16; 4:43; 6:42; 7:8, 27; 8:46; 9:9; 10:3; 15:17; 16:9; 19:5, 13, 22; 20:3, 8, 43; John 3:30; 5:36, 45; 6:20, 35, 40, 41, 44, 48, 51, 54, 56, 57, 63, 70; 7:7, 8, 17, 29, 34; 8:12, 14–16, 18, 21–24, 26, 28, 29, 38, 42, 45, 49, 50, 54, 55, 58; 9:4, 9, 11, 25, 39; 10:7, 9–11, 14, 15, 17, 25, 27, 28, 30, 34, 38; 11:25, 27, 42; 12:26, 32, 46, 47, 49; 13:15, 18–20, 26, 33, 34, 36; 14:3, 4, 6, 10–12, 14, 16, 19–21, 27, 28, 31; 15:1, 4, 5, 9, 10, 12, 14–16, 19, 20, 26; 16:4, 7, 16, 17, 27, 33; 17:4, 9, 11, 12, 14, 16, 18, 19, 21, 23–26; 18:5, 6, 8, 20, 21, 26, 35, 37, 38; 19:6; Romans 7:9, 10, 14, 17, 20, 24, 25; 9:3; 10:19; 11:1, 13, 19; 12:19; 14:11; 16:22; 1 Corinthians 1:12, 16; 7:8, 10, 12, 28; 9:6, 26; 10:30, 33; 11:1, 23; 15:9–11; 16:6, 10; 2 Corinthians 1:23; 2:2, 10; 6:17; 10:1; 11:16, 18, 21–23, 29; 12:11, 13, 15, 16, 20; Galatians 2:19, 20; 4:12, 18; 5:2, 10, 11; 6:14, 17; Ephesians 1:15; 3:1, 7; 4:1; 6:21; Philippians 2:28; 3:4; 2 Corinthians 12:13; Philippians 4:11; 1 Thessalonians 3:5; 1 Timothy 1:15; 2:7; 2 Timothy 1:11; 4:16; Titus 1:5; Philemon 13, 19, 20; Nehemiah 5:14, 16.

**ÏKEI**, “I who”: 1 Corinthians 15:9; 2 Corinthians 10:1; 1 Timothy 1:13.

**IM** (Old Norse *em*, Anglo-Saxon *eom*, English *am*, Greek εἰμί, “I am”; Old Saxon *biun*, *bium*, Old High German *bim*, Modern High German *bin*, Latin *sum*; Gf. I, 851 ff.), substantive verb: “I am”; see under **Visam**.

**IM, IMMA**, see under **Is**.

**IN** (Old Norse *i*, Old High German *in*, Old Frisian *en, in*, Modern High German *in*; Latin *in*, Greek ἐν, “in”; Gr. III, 252; Gf. I, 287; Alth. *Präpos.* 10 ff.; Rchth. 705, 849), preposition properly denoting motion into something or rest in something, corresponding to the Greek particles εἰς (“into”) and ἐν (“in”). It is constructed with accusative or dative according as it indicates motion or rest. Beyond this fundamental meaning, it expresses direction toward something, and motion or rest upon an object. Moreover, this preposition—distinctively Gothic in this respect—governs the genitive, by which it acquires the causal meaning “because of.”

I. **Preposition**

A. **With the accusative**

1. In local reference: “into, upon, to, toward,” εἰς, especially:

a. After verbs of motion: *galeiþan*, “to go”: Matthew 8:31, *galeiþan ïn þo hairda sveine*, “to go into the herd of swine”; 8:33 (for, according to the Greek text, *ïn baurg*, “into the city,” must be referred to *galeiþandans*, “those going”); 9:7, *galaiþ ïn gard seinana*, “he went into his house”; 25:46, *ïn balvein aiveinon . . . ïn libain aiveinon*, “into eternal punishment . . . into eternal life”; Mark 1:21, *galiþun ïn kafarnaum*, “they went into Capernaum”; 1:45; 2:1, 26; 3:1, 27; 4:1; 5:12, 13, 38; 7:17, 19, 24; 8:10, 13; 9:25, 28, 43, 47; 10:23; 11:11; Luke 1:40; 2:15 (*ïn himin*, genitive, “into heaven”); 4:31, 38; 5:3, 25; 6:6; 7:1; 8:22, 31–33, 37; 9:12; 9:46, *galaiþ mitons ïn ïns*, “a thought entered into them,” ἐν; 9:52; 10:30; 17:27; 18:25; 19:7, 45; John 3:4; 7:8, 10, *ïn dulþ*, “in secret”; 10:40; 13:27; 18:1, 33; 19:9; 2 Corinthians 1:16; 2:13; *Skeireins* II, c.

*ïnngaleiþan*, “to enter”: Matthew 7:21; Luke 18:24; John 3:5. *miþïnngaleiþan*, “to enter with”: John 18:15. *afleiþan*, “to go away”: Luke 15:13. *gaggan*, “to go”: Matthew 6:6; 9:6; 25:41; Mark 6:10, 56; 11:2; 14:13; Luke 1:39; 5:24; 7:11; 8:41; 9:4, 51, 56; 10:8; 17:11; 19:30; John 7:3, 35; 11:7; 18:28. *ïnngaggan*, “to enter”: Mark 5:18; 7:15; 18:11, 2; Luke 4:16; 6:4; 10:5; 17:12. *atgaggan*, “to come to”: Mark 3:20; 11:15; 16:5; Luke 1:9; 7:36, 44; 8:23; John 10:1; 16:28. *ïnnatgaggan*, “to enter”: Matthew 8:5, 23; 27:53. *miþgaggan*, “to go with”: Mark 15:41. *afgaggan*, “to go away”: John 6:15. *usgaggan*, “to go out”: Matthew 26:71; Mark 8:27; 10:17 (*ïn vig*, “into the way”), 33; Luke 6:12 (*ïn fairguni*, “into the mountain”); 7:24; 9:28; 14:21 (*ïn gatvons jah staigos*, “into streets and lanes”); 18:10, 31; 19:28; Galatians 2:1. *faurbigaggan*, “to go before”: Mark 16:7. *gasteigan*, “to go up”: John 6:24; 7:14; Romans 10:7. *ussteigan*, “to go up”: Mark 3:13; John 6:17; Romans 10:6; Ephesians 4:8. *atsteigan*, “to come down”: Matthew 9:1. *rinnan*, “to run”: Luke 8:33. *run gavaurkjan*, “to make a rush”: Matthew 8:32. *urrinnan*, “to run out”: Luke 2:4. *frarinnan*, “to fall among”: Luke 10:30 (*ïn vaidedjans*, “among robbers,” λῃσταῖς περιπίπτειν). *vraton*, “to travel”: Luke 2:41. *faran*, “to journey”: Luke 10:7. *atfarjan*, “to go to”: Luke 8:26. *sliupan*, “to creep”: 2 Timothy 3:6. *þliuhan*, “to flee”: Matthew 10:23. *valtjan*, “to roll”: Mark 4:37. *gavandjan sik*, “to return”: Luke 2:39, 45; 4:14. *ussatjan sik*, “to transplant oneself”: Luke 17:6. *andstandan*, “to withstand”: Galatians 2:11, *ïn andvairþi ïmma andstoþ*, “he withstood him face to face,” κατὰ πρόσωπον. *gadriusan*, “to fall”: Matthew 5:29, 30; Mark 4:7, 8; Luke 6:39; 8:14; John 12:24.

Here also belongs the expression *disskritnan ïn tva*, “to be torn in two”: Matthew 27:51; Mark 15:38. After *qiman*, “to come,” *ïn* with the accusative occurs only at John 6:14, 22; 11:27.

*Visands ïn vitoþ*, “being under the law,” 1 Corinthians 9:22, for ἔννομος, “lawful/under law,” should be *ïn vitoda*.

b. After very many transitive verbs, often metaphorically; thus after *ïnsandjan*, “to send”: Mark 5:12; Luke 1:26; 4:26; 10:1; John 10:36; 17:18; Galatians 4:6; 2 Timothy 4:12. *ussandjan*, “to send out”: Matthew 9:38 (*vaurstvjans ïn asan*, “laborers into the harvest”; compare Luke 10:2). *fravilvan*, “to be caught up”: 2 Corinthians 12:4. *garaihtjan*, “to direct”: Luke 1:79. *tiuhan*, “to lead”: John 18:28. *gatiuhan*, “to lead”: Luke 4:9. *ustiuhan*, “to drive out”: Mark 1:12. *briggan*, “to bring”: Luke 2:22; 1 Corinthians 16:3. *lisan*, “to gather”: Matthew 6:26. *vairpan*, “to cast”: Mark 1:16 (ἐν); 11:23. *atvairpan*, “to cast back”: Matthew 27:5 (ἐν); Mark 9:22. *fravairpan*, “to cast away”: Mark 9:42. *usvairpan*, “to cast out”: Matthew 8:12. *ussatjan*, “to set out”: Luke 10:2. *lagjan*, “to put”: Matthew 27:6; Mark 7:33; Luke 9:44, *ïn ausona þo vaurda*, “put these words into [your] ears”; John 18:11, *hairu ïn fodr*, “the sword into the sheath.” *galagjan*, “to lay”: Matthew 5:25 (*ïn karkara*, “into prison”); 6:30; Luke 3:9 (*ïn fon*, “into fire”); John 15:6. *atlagjan*, “to throw down”: Matthew 7:19. *giutan*, “to pour”: Matthew 9:17; Mark 2:22; Luke 5:37, 38. *saian*, “to sow”: Mark 4:18. *ïntrusgjan*, “to graft in”: Romans 11:17, 24 (ἐν). *speivan*, “to spit”: Mark 8:23. *slahan*, “to strike”: Luke 18:13 (*ïn brusts*, “upon the breast”); 2 Corinthians 11:20 (*ïn andavleizn*, “on the face”). *niman*, “to take”: Mark 6:8 (*ïn vig*, “for the journey”); Luke 9:3; John 6:21. *ganiman*, “to receive”: Luke 2:21 (ἐν). *andniman*, “to receive”: Luke 16:4, 9; Colossians 1:13. *giban*, “to give”: Luke 6:38; 15:22 (*figgragulþ ïn handu*, “a ring on [his] hand”); 2 Corinthians 1:22; 8:16 (ἐν). *atgiban*, “to deliver over”: Mark 9:31; Luke 9:44. *galevjan*, “to betray”: Mark 14:41 (*ïn handuns fravaurhtaize*, “into the hands of sinners”). Likewise *usfulljan*, “to fulfil”: Luke 7:1, *alla þo vaurda ïn hliumans manageins*, “all these words in the hearing of the people.” *gahausjan*, “to hear”: Matthew 10:27 (*ïn auso*, “in the ear”). *merjan*, “to proclaim”: Colossians 1:23 (*aivaggeljon ïn alla gaskaft*, “the gospel in all creation”). *gateihan*, “to report”: Luke 8:34 (*ïn baurg jah ïn veihsa*, “in the city and in the countryside”). *qiþan*, “to say”: Matthew 9:21 (*ïn sik*, “within herself,” ἐν). Matthew 10:28: *fraqistjau saivalai jah leika ïn gaiainnan*, “to destroy soul and body in Gehenna”; a dative can also stand, following Greek ἐν. John 9:7, 11: *gagg þvahan ïn svumsl siloamis*, “go, wash in the pool of Siloam.” Although *ïn* may indeed be referred to *gagg*, “go,” it may nevertheless be explained: “go and wash in this pool.”

2. In temporal reference, it indicates:

a. Duration: “until, unto,” εἰς, in such formulas as *ïn aldins alde* or *aive*, “unto ages of ages/for ever”: Luke 1:50; Ephesians 3:21; 1 Timothy 1:17; *ïn ajukduþ*, “unto eternity”: Luke 1:33; John 6:51, 58; *ïn aivins*, “for ever”: Matthew 6:13.

b. “For, unto,” εἰς: John 12:7, *ïn dag gafilhis meinis gafastaida þata*, “she has kept it for the day of my burial”; 2 Timothy 1:12, *þata anafilh mein fastan ïn jainana dag*, “what I have entrusted [he is] able to keep until that day.”

c. “In, at,” ἐν: Mark 13:24, *ïn jainans dagans sauïl riqizeiþ*, “in those days the sun will be darkened”; Luke 2:1, *varþ ïn dagans jainans urrann gagrefts*, “it came to pass in those days that a decree went out”; Ephesians 6:18, *þairh allos bidos aihtrondans ïn alla mela*, “watching with all prayers at every time.” Hence also John 11:9: *jabai was gaggiþ ïn dag ni gastiggqiþ*, “if anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble,” ἐν ἡμέρᾳ. Thus πρωΐ, “early,” is always translated in Mark by *ïn maurgin*, “in the morning”: 11:20; 15:1; 16:9.

3. In metaphorical reference:

a. “Into,” εἰς, after several of the verbs cited above under 1: *gaggan*, “to go,” Mark 5:34, *ïn gavairþi*, “into peace”; Luke 7:50. *garinnan*, “to attain”: Ephesians 4:13, *ïn ainamundiþa*, “to unity.” *atdriusan*, “to fall into”: 1 Timothy 3:6, *ïn staua*, “into condemnation”; 3:7, *ïn ïdveit*, “into reproach”; *Skeireins* II, b, *ïn tveifl*, “into doubt.” *qiman*, “to come”: 2 Corinthians 2:12, *ïn aivaggeljon*, “to [preach] the gospel”; 12:1, *ïn siunins jah andhuleinins*, “to visions and revelations.” *gavandjan*, “to turn”: Luke 1:17, *ïn frodein*, “to wisdom.” *tiuhan*, “to bring”: 2 Corinthians 10:5, *ïn ufhausein*, “into captivity.” *satjan*, “to appoint”: 1 Thessalonians 5:9, *ïn hatis*, “unto wrath.” *laþon*, “to call”: Luke 5:32, *ïn ïdreiga*, “to repentance.” *allaþon*, “to call”: Ephesians 4:4, *ïn aina ven*, “in one hope,” ἐν. *saggqjan*, “to sink”: 1 Timothy 6:9, *ïn fravardein*, “into destruction.” *atgiban*, “to give up”: 2 Corinthians 4:11, *ïn dauþu*, “to death.” *fairveitjan*, “to look”: 2 Corinthians 3:13, *ïn andi*, “unto the end.”

b. “Because of, on account of, for, toward,” εἰς.

α. After certain verbs and expressions: Luke 15:18, 21, *fravaurkjan ïn himin*, “to sin against heaven”; Romans 12:16, *þata samo ïn ïzvis misso fraþjandans*, “thinking the same thing toward one another”; Ephesians 4:15, *vahsjaima ïn ïna þo alla*, “let us grow in every respect into him”; 2 Corinthians 8:6, *ustiukai ïn ïzvis jah þo anst*, “that he should complete among you also this grace”; 1:5, *ufarassus ïst þulaine xristus ïn uns*, “the sufferings of Christ abound toward us,” where in the translation *nos* (“us,” accusative) must be read instead of *nobis* (“to us,” dative); 9:8, *mahteigs ïst guþ alla anst ufarassjan ïn ïzvis*, “God is able to make every grace abound toward you,” where likewise in the translation *vos* (“you,” accusative) must replace *vobis* (“to you,” dative); Ephesians 1:8, *anst ufarassau ganohida ïn uns*, “grace which he lavished upon us”; 3:2, *ansts gibana ïst mis ïn ïzvis*, “the grace given to me for you”; 3:16, *gasvinþnan ïn ïnnuman mannan*, “to be strengthened as to the inner person”; Romans 10:19, *ïn þvairhein briggan ïn þiuda unfraþjandein*, “to provoke [you] to jealousy through a foolish nation,” ἐπί with accusative; the preceding *ïnuh þiudom* would better be *ïn ni þiudos*, “among no nations.” 1 Thessalonians 4:10, *taujiþ þata ïn allans broþruns*, “you do this toward all the brothers”; Galatians 4:11, *svare arbaidjan ïn wana*, “to labour in vain concerning you.” Elliptically in 2 Corinthians 13:3, 4: *siukeiþ ïn ïzvis . . . libam ïn ïzvis*, “he is weak toward you . . . we live toward you”; in the translation, *vos* must twice be read instead of *vobis*.

β. Frequently after nouns, especially *friaþva*, “love”: 2 Corinthians 8:7 (ἐν); Ephesians 1:15; 1 Thessalonians 3:12; 2 Thessalonians 1:3; *broþralubo*, “brotherly love”: Romans 12:10; *giba*, “gift”: 2 Corinthians 1:11; *andbahti*, “ministry”: 8:4; *ragin*, “dispensation”: Colossians 1:25; *vilja*, “will”: 1 Thessalonians 5:18; *trauains*, “confidence”: 2 Corinthians 8:22; *andahait*, “obedience”: 9:13; *gavaurstva*, “boast”: 8:23; *iimreins*, “edification”: Romans 14:19; *vaurstveig*, “working”: Galatians 2:8.

γ. After certain adjectives: Luke 9:62, *gatils ïn þiudangardja guþs*, “fit for the kingdom of God”; Matthew 5:22, *skula vairþiþ ïn gaiainnan*, “liable to Gehenna,” where *galagjan*, “to lay,” or *vairpan*, “to cast,” may be supplied at will; Romans 10:12, *frauja gabigs ïn allans*, “Lord, rich toward all.”

c. To indicate an outcome: “into, unto,” εἰς: Romans 13:4, *fraveitands ïn þvairhein*, “an avenger for wrath”; 13:14, *ni taujaiþ ïn lustuns*, “make no provision for lusts”; 1 Corinthians 15:54, *ufsaggqiþs varþ dauþus ïn sigis*, “death has been swallowed up in victory”; Ephesians 4:19, *sik atgebun aglaitein ïn vaurstvein unhrainiþos*, “they gave themselves over to licentiousness for the practice of every impurity.” In 1 Corinthians 15:2, τίνι λόγῳ, “by what word,” is unintelligently translated *ïn wo sauþo*.

d. “For,” after verbs of selling: Mark 14:5, *maht vesi þata balsan frahugjan ïn managizo þau þrijahunda skatte*, “this ointment might have been sold for more than three hundred denarii,” ἐπάνω; John 12:5, *duwe þata balsan ni frabauht vas ïn .t.*—that is, *þrijahunda*—*skatte*, “why was this ointment not sold for three hundred denarii?”

*ïn þuk*, “for your sake,” ἕνεκά σου, is so construed once, Romans 8:36; elsewhere *ïn*, when it has this sense, governs the genitive; see below, C.

B. **With the dative**

1. Locally, in a place determined by persons or things:

a. “In,” ἐν.

α. After verbs of rest, such as *visan*, “to be”: Matthew 5:25, *ïs ïn viga*, “he is in the way”; 10:32, *ïn himinam ïst*, “is in the heavens”; 11:8, *ïn gardim þiudane sind*, “are in kings’ houses”; 25:43; Mark 1:13, 23; 2:1; 4:1, 36; 5:5; 6:4; 11:1; 14:66; 15:41; Luke 2:7, 25, 49; 4:33; 5:7, 12; 7:25, 28; 9:12, 61 (εἰς); 17:21 (ἐντός, “within”); 17:31; 18:2, 3; John 7:18; 8:44; 11:6, 10, 30, 31; 12:35; 14:2, 10, 11, 17, 20; 15:4, 7, 11; 17:21, 26; Romans 7:5, 23; 10:8; 1 Corinthians 14:25; 15:10, 28; 2 Corinthians 1:1; 5:4, 6; 7:3; 11:10, 25; 13:5; Galatians 4:25; Ephesians 1:1; 4:18, 21; 5:18; 6:9; Colossians 2:20; 3:15; 4:13; 1 Thessalonians 2:14; 2 Timothy 1:5, 15; 2:28; *Skeireins* IV, c. Compare John 11:17: *juþan fidvor dagans habands ïn hlaiva*, “already having four days in the tomb”; 2 Corinthians 1:12: *usmetum ïn þamma fairwau*, “we conducted ourselves in this world”; hence *Skeireins* I, c: *þai ïn guþa usmetai*, “those who conducted themselves in God.”

*ligan*, “to lie”: Matthew 8:6, *ligiþ ïn garda*, “he lies in the house”; Luke 2:16. *sitan*, “to sit”: Matthew 11:16, *sitandam ïn garunsai*, “sitting in the marketplaces”; Luke 7:32; 10:13, *in sakkum jah azgon sitands gaïdreigon*, “sitting in sackcloth and ashes they would have repented”; therefore in Matthew 11:21 *sitandeins*, “sitting,” may also be understood. *gasitan*, “to sit down”: Mark 4:1. *anakumbjan*, “to recline”: Matthew 8:11; 9:10; Mark 2:15; Luke 7:37; John 13:23; 1 Corinthians 8:10. *standan*, “to stand”: Matthew 6:5; Luke 6:8 (εἰς). *gastandan*, “to remain”: Luke 2:43. *bauan*, “to dwell”: Romans 7:17, 18, 20; Ephesians 3:17; Colossians 3:16; 2 Timothy 1:5, 14. *bauain haban*, “to have a dwelling”: Mark 5:3. *bauains ïst*, “is citizenship/dwelling”: Philippians 3:20. *visan*, in the sense “to remain”: Luke 10:7; 19:5; John 6:56; 7:9; 8:35; 14:10; 15:4, 5; 1 Corinthians 16:8; 2 Corinthians 3:14; Philippians 1:24. *gavisan*, “to stay”: Luke 8:27. *saljan*, “to remain”: 1 Timothy 1:3. *gamotan*, “to find room”: John 8:37; 2 Corinthians 7:2. *liban*, “to live”: Galatians 2:20.

δ. Very often the above-mentioned verbs, particularly *visan* and usually its participle, must be supplied: Matthew 5:15, *allaim þaim ïn þamma razna*, “to all those in the house”; 5:16, *atta ïzvar sa in himinam*, “your Father who is in the heavens”; 5:45, 48; 6:1, 6, 9; 18:23; 7:21; 11:11; 25:39; Mark 11:10, 25; 12:25; Luke 1:15; 2:11, 14; 6:23, 41, 42; 7:28, 37; 8:15; 10:9; 19:38; John 10:38; 17:23; 1 Corinthians 15:10 (εἰς), 23; 2 Corinthians 11:33—*sitting* is to be supplied, and in the translation *corbi* (“basket”) must be read instead of *laqueo* (“noose”); Ephesians 2:12; 3:21; 4:6; Philippians 3:6; Colossians 1:16; 1 Thessalonians 4:16. Similarly: Mark 4:28, *kaurn ïn ahsa*, “grain in the ear”; John 15:2, *tains ïn mis*, “a branch in me”; 2 Corinthians 12:2, *manna ïn xristau*, “a man in Christ”; Ephesians 3:15, *all fadreinis ïn himina*, “every family in heaven.”

β. After verbs which indeed indicate motion, but where the motion is restricted within definite bounds: John 7:1, *warboda ïn galeilaia. ni auk vilda ïn ïudaia gaggan*, “he travelled in Galilee, for he did not wish to travel in Judaea”; Mark 11:27 and John 10:23, *warbon ïn alh*, “they walked in the temple”; Luke 9:57, *gaggan ïn viga*, “to go on the road”; Luke 1:41, 44, *lailaik barn ïn qiþau* or *ïn vambai*, “the child leaped in the womb”; 1 Corinthians 9:24, *ïn spaurd rinnan*, “to run in a racecourse”; Mark 3:3, *urreis ïn midumai*, “rise into the midst,” εἰς.

γ. Regularly after *qiman*, “to come,” “into, to,” εἰς: Matthew 8:14, *qimands ïn garda*, “coming into the house”; 8:28; 9:1, 23, 28; Mark 1:14, 29; 5:1; 6:1; 8:22; 9:33; 10:1, 15, 46; 14:54; Luke 2:27, 51; 4:16; 8:51; 9:34; 15:6, 17; 18:17; John 6:24; 9:39; 11:30; 12:1, 12, 27, 46; 18:37; 2 Corinthians 1:23; 2:12; 7:5; Galatians 2:11; 1 Timothy 1:15; 2 Timothy 1:17. Likewise after *vairþan*, “to become”: Luke 1:44; and *gabaurans vairþan ïn fairwau*, “to be born into the world”: John 16:21.

δ. After transitives: *lagjan*, “to place”: 2 Corinthians 15:19 [as printed]; *galagjan*, “to lay”: Matthew 27:60; Mark 6:29; 15:46; Luke 1:66; 2:7, 12; 19:20; John 3:24; Romans 9:33; *Skeireins* III, a. *gasatjan*, “to set”: Luke 5:19; 1 Corinthians 12:18. *atvairpan*, “to cast”: Matthew 27:5 (ἐν). *gavairpan*, “to cast”: Luke 4:35. *saian*, “to sow”: Mark 4:15. *briggan*, “to bring”: Luke 3:17; 16:22; 1 Timothy 6:7; *Skeireins* II, a. *tiuhan*, “to lead”: Luke 4:1. *nauþjan*, “to press”: Luke 16:16. Also Luke 8:7: *gadraus ïn midumai þaurnive*, “it fell among thorns” [sentence incomplete].

(ἐν μέσῳ), “in the midst”; ε) in very many instances where someone is said to do something, or something to happen, αα) **in**: Matt. V.19 *mikils haitada in thiudangardjai himine*, “he shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven”; VI.2 *swe liutans taujand in gaqumthim*, “as hypocrites do in the synagogues”; 10 *wairthai wilja theins swe in himina*, “thy will be done, as in heaven”; 20 *huzdjaith huzd in himina*, “lay up treasure in heaven”; VIII.24 *wegs warth in marein*, “a storm arose on the sea”; VIII.32 *gadauthnodedun in watnam*, “they perished in the waters”; 33 *gataihun in baurg*, “they reported [it] in the city” (εἰς; like the dative according to Mark v.14, it may also be accusative; see Luke VIII.34); IX.31 *usmerjan in allai airthai*, “to proclaim abroad in all the earth”; 33 *laisjan in gaqumthim*, “to teach in the synagogues”; X.28 *fraqistnan in gaiainnan*, “to destroy in Gehenna” (it may also be accusative); XI.2 *hausjan in karkarai*, “to hear in prison”; 20 *in baurgim waurthun mahteis*, “mighty works were done in the cities”; 21; Mark I.3, 4, 5, 9 (εἰς); XIX.20, 39; IV.17 (*waurtins haban in sis*, “to have root in themselves”); V.13, 14, 20, 21 (*usleithan in skipa*, “to go forth into the boat”); VI.2, 4, 14 (*mahteis waurkjand in imma*, “powers working in him”); XVII.28; VIII.14, 26; IX.33, 50; X.10, 21, 52 (*laistjan in wiga*, “to lead into the way”); XI.15; XII.35; XIII.26 *qiman in milhmam*, “to come among the nations”; XIV.49; Luke I.21, 22, 31, 65, 69; II.3 (*melidai wesun in seinai baurg*, “they were registered in their own city,” deviating from the Greek text, where it depends on ἐπορεύοντο, “they went”); VIII.46, 51; III.2, 17 (*habands windiskauron in handau*, “having a winnowing-shovel in his hand”); 20; IV.15, 21 (*usfullnodedun tho mela in ausam izwaraim*, “this Scripture has been fulfilled in your ears”); 23, 24; IV.20, 28, 44; V.29; VIII.32; X.13, 20; XIV.15; XV.7; XVI.23 to the end; XVIII.22; XIX.30, 44, 45, 47; XX.1; John VI.49, 53 (*habaith libain in izwis*, “you have life in yourselves”); VI.59; VII.28; VIII.20, 26 (εἰς); X.22; XII.25; XIII.31, 32; XIV.13; XVI.33; XVII.13; XVIII.20, 26; Rom. VII.5, 23; VIII.3, 4; [Col. 1358] IX.26; XII.4; 1 Cor. VII.17; X.2; XV.32; 2 Cor. I.8; II.14; III.2, 3, 7; IV.4, 6, 7, 12; V.1, 11; VI.12; VII.8; X.15; XI.10, 32; XIII.3; Gal. III.1, 5; IV.18; Eph. I.20; II.2, 16; III.9, 20; V.5; Phil. III.9; IV.16; Col. I.24, 29; III.3; IV.1; 1 Thess. II.13; III.1; IV.17; 2 Thess. I.4; III.16; 1 Tim. II.8; III.16; 2 Tim. I.18; III.11; Titus I.5; *Skeir.* VII.d.

Especially relevant here are instances such as Mark I.2 *gamelith ist in esaiin*, “it is written in Isaiah”; Luke III.4 *gamelith ist in bokom waurde esaeiins*, “it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah”; Luke II.23 *gamelith ist in witoda*, “it is written in the Law”; X.26; John VIII.17; X.34; XV.25; 1 Cor. IX.9; XIV.21; Luke II.24 *qithan ist in witoda*, “it is said in the Law”; XX.42 *daweid qithith in bokom psalmo*, “David says in the book of Psalms”; Rom. IX.25 *guth in osein qithith*, “God says in Hosea.” Further: Luke XVI.3 *qath insis*, “he said within himself”; XVIII.4; John VI.61 *witands in sis*, “knowing in himself”; XI.38 *inrauhtiths in sis*, “being troubled within himself”; Rom. XI.25; Phil. II.5; Eph. V.19 and Col. III.16 *siggwan in hairtam*, “to sing in [your] hearts”; Rom. X.6 *qithan in hairtam seinaim*, “to say in their hearts”; Matt. V.28 *horinon in hairtin*, “to commit adultery in [his] heart”; IX.4; Mark XI.23; Luke II.19; III.15; V.22; Rom. X.9; 2 Cor. X.12 *in sis silbam sik silbans mitan*, “measuring themselves by themselves.”

ββ) **in**: Mark V.30 *Iesus ufkuntha in sis tho us sis maht usgaggandein*, “Jesus, knowing in himself the power going forth from himself”; John XIV.30 *in mis ni bigitith waiht*, “he finds nothing in me”; XVIII.38; XIX.4, 6; 1 Cor. IV.6; 2 Cor. VIII.24; Phil. I.30; IV.9; 1 Tim. I.16; *Skeir.* VII.c; compare 2 Cor. II.8 *tulgjan in imma friathwa*, “to show love toward him.”

b) **among, in, with**, ἐν: Matt. VIII.10 *ni in Israela swalauda galaubein bigat*, “I have not found such great faith in Israel”; IX.3 *bokarjos qethun in sis*, “the scribes said within themselves”; IX.33 *ni aiw swa uskunth was in Israela*, “never was such a thing seen in Israel”; XI.11 *ni urrais in baurim qinono maiza Iohanne*, “among those born of women none greater than John has arisen”; 21 *mahteis thos waurthanons in izwis*, “the mighty works done among you”; XXVII.56 *in im was Maria*, “among them was Mary”; Mark V.27 *atgaggandei in managein aftana attaitok*, “coming up from behind among the crowd, she touched [him]”; VI.4 *unswers ist in ganithjam*, “a prophet is among his kinsmen”; VIII.38 *saei skamaith sik waurde meinaize in gabaurthai thizai horinondein*, “whoever is ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous generation”; IX.36 *gasatida barn in midjaim im*, “he set a child in their midst”; X.43; XIV.60 (εἰς); XV.40; Luke I.1, 25, 28, 42, 61; II.14, 34, 38, 44, 46; III.8; IV.25, 27; VII.9, 16, 28, 49; IX.48; X.13; XVI.15; John V.38; VII.12, 43; XII.35; XV.24; XVII.26; Rom. XII.3; XV.5; 1 Cor. XI.30; XV.3, 12; 2 Cor. I.19; II.15; VI.16; X.1; XI.26 to the end; XII.12; Gal. II.2; V.14; Eph. I.3, 18, 20; II.3, 6, 10; III.8, 10; V.3; VI.12; Phil. IV.11, 12; Col. I.27; III.7; 1 Thess. V.12, 13; 2 Thess. I.10; III.11; 1 Tim. III.16; *Skeir.* VIII.b.

c) It denotes proximity, “with, at,” but only in the formula *in taihswai* and *in taihswon*, after *sitan*, “sit,” Mark XVI.5; Col. III.1; *wisan*, “be,” Rom. VIII.34; *satjan*, “seat,” Eph. I.20.

2) In a temporal sense:

a) **in, at**, ἐν: Matt. VII.22 *managai qithand mis in jainamma daga*, “many shall say to me on that day”; VIII.16 *gahailnoda thiumagus in jainai weilai*, “he healed the servants at that time”; XI.22 *in daga stauos*, “on the day of judgment”; 24, 25 *in jainamma mela*, “at that time”; Mark I.9 *in jainaim dagam*, “in those days”; II.20; III.4 (*in sabbatim thiu thaujan*, dative, “to do good on the sabbaths”); VI.35; VI.11; VIII.1; XII.23 (*in usstassai*, “in the resurrection”); XIII.17; XV.7 (*in auhjodau maurthr gatawidedun*, “who had committed murder in the insurrection”); Luke I.5 (*in dagam Herodis*, “in the days of Herod”); 25, 26 (*in menoth saihtistin*, “in the sixth month”), 36 (*inkiltho in aldomin seinamma*, “advanced in her old age”), 59 (*in daga ahtudin*, “on the eighth day”); III.1 (*in jera fimftataihundin*, “in the fifteenth year”); IV.2, 5 (*in stika melis*, “in a moment of time”), 16 (*in daga sabbato*, “on the Sabbath day”); IV.25, 31; V.17, 35; VI.1, 2, 6, 7, 12, 23; VII.11, 21; VIII.13 (*in mela fraistubnjos*, “at the time of testing”), 22; IX.34 (*in thammei jainai qemun*, “when they came”); 36, 37; X.12, 14, 21; XIV.14; XVIII.30; XIX.42; XX.1, 10, 19, 33; John VI.40 (*in spedistin daga*, dative, “on the last day”), 44; VII.11 (*sokidedun ina in thizai dulthai*, “they sought him at the feast”), 22, 23, 37, 50 (*in naht*, “by night,” νυκτός); XI.10, 24; XII.20, 48; XIV.20; XVI.23, 26; XVIII.39 (*in pasxa*, “at Passover”); Rom. XIII.13; 1 Cor. V.5; XV.19 (*in thizai libainai*, “in this life”), 52 (*in brawa augins*, “in the twinkling of an eye”); 2 Cor. I.14; VI.2; Eph. I.21 (*in thamma aiwa*, “in that age”); II.7, 12; VI.19 (*in usluka munthis meinis*, “in the opening of my mouth”); 1 Thess. II.19 (*in Xristaus quma*, “at Christ’s coming”); III.13; V.2; 2 Thess. I.7 (*in andhuleinai Xristaus*, “at the revelation of Christ”), 10; 1 Tim. IV.1; VI.15 (dative); 2 Tim. I.18; III.1; Neh. VI.17; *Skeir.* II.a (*in mela thulainais*, “at the time of suffering”); VI.c (*in missaleikaim melam*, “at diverse times”); VIII.c.

b) **in, upon, until**, εἰς: Luke I.20 *waurda meina usfulljanda in mela seinamma*, “my words, which shall be fulfilled in their own time”; John XII.25 *in libainai aiweinon bairgith saiwalai*, “shall keep [his] soul unto eternal life”; Eph. IV.30 *ahmin weihamma gasiglidai sijuth in daga uslauseinais*, “you are sealed with the Holy Spirit for the day of redemption”; 1 Thess. IV.15 *thai bilaibidans in quma fraujins*, “we who remain until the coming of the Lord.”

In a metaphorical sense, most frequently, and also in various closely related senses which are consequently treated interchangeably:

a) **in, into**, ἐν, after all verbs and in all the cases cited above under 1), where *in* refers to the sphere in which something occurs, to abstract objects in relation to which something is done, or to that in which or with whom something occurs. Thus after *wisan*, “be”: Matt. VI.4 *sijai so armahairthitha in fulhsnja*, “thy almsgiving may be in secret”; Luke XVI.23 *in balwein*, “in torment”; John XV.10 *in friathwai*, “in love”; 1 Cor. VII.20; XV.17; 2 Cor. XIII.5; Eph. V.9; Phil. III.19; 1 Thess. V.4 (*in riqiza*, “in darkness”); 1 Tim. I.4; II.2; IV.15. After *wisan* (“remain”): John XV.9 *in friathwai*, “in love”; 2 Tim. III.14 *wisais in thaimai*—that is, *in thaim thoei galaisides*, “remain in the things which thou hast learned”; *thairhwisan*, “continue”: Rom. XI.22 *in selein*, “in kindness”; Col. I.23 *in galaubeinai*, “in faith”; 1 Tim. IV.16 *in thaim*, “in them.” After *standan*, “stand”: 1 Cor. XV.1 *in aiwaggelja*, “in the gospel”; XVI.13 *in galaubeinai*, “in the faith”; *gastandan*, “remain”: John VIII.31 *in waurda meinamma*, “in my word”; 44 *in sunjai*, “in truth”; 1 Cor. VII.24; 1 Thess. III.8; 1 Tim. II.15. After *sitan*, “sit”: Mark X.38 *in wulthau*, “in glory”; Luke I.79; *usmitan*, “be”: Eph. II.3 *in frawaurhtim*, “in transgressions”; *gaggan*, “walk”: Luke I.6 *in anabusnim jah garaihteim fraujins*, “in the commandments and ordinances of the Lord”; John VIII.12 *in riqiza*, “in darkness”; XII.35; 2 Cor. IV.2 *in warein*, “in guile”; Eph. II.2 *in frawaurhtim*, “in transgressions”; V.2 *in friathwai*, “in love”; *qiman*, “come”: Luke VIII.17 *in swekunthamma*, “into manifestation”; 2 Tim. III.7 *in ufkuntja sunjos*, “to the knowledge of truth”; *gaqiman*: Phil. III.11; likewise 1 Tim. II.14 *in missadedai warth*, “was made a transgressor” (where, in the translation, **became** must be read instead of **was**); and Luke I.11 *warth imma in siunai aggilus*, “an angel appeared to him in sight.” After *briggan*, “bring”: Matt. VI.13 *in fraistubnjai*, “into temptation”; VII.13 *in fralustai*, “into destruction”; 14 *in libainai*, “into life”; John XVI.13 *in sunjai*, “into truth”; Rom. X.19 *in aljana*, “to jealousy”; *gasatjan*, “appoint”: 1 Tim. I.12 *in andbahtja*, “to ministry”; *saian*, “sow”: Gal. VI.8 *in leika—in ahmin*, “in the flesh—in the Spirit.”

And after other verbs: Matt. VI.6 *usgibith thus in bairhtein*, “shall reward thee openly”; X.27 *thatei qitha in riqiza, qithaih in liuhada*, “what I tell you in darkness, speak in the light”; Mark IV.2 *qath du im in laiseinai*, “he spoke to them in teaching”; XII.38; Luke I.18 *framaldrozei in dagam seinam*, “advanced in his days”; XVI.10 *triggws wisan in leitilamma—in managamma*, “faithful in little—in much”; 11, 12; XIX.17; John VII.4 *in analaugnein wa taujan*, “to do [anything] in secret”; VIII.21 *in frawaurhtai gadauthnan*, “to die in sin”; 24; Rom. VII.6 *in witoda gahabaiths*, “held in the Law”; X.5 *in witoda liban*, “live by the Law”; XI.23 *gatulgjan sik in ungalaubeinai*, “continue in unbelief”; XIII.9 *anabusns in thamma waurda usfulljada*, “the commandment is fulfilled in this saying”; 1 Cor. I.21 *in handugein Guths ni kunnaida sa fairwus Guth*, “the world did not know God through the wisdom of God”; XIII.12 *saiwam thairh skuggwan in frisahtai*, “we see through a mirror in obscurity”; XV.58 *ufarfulljan in waurstva fraujins*, “abound in the work of the Lord”; 2 Cor. VIII.7 *in allamma managnan*, “in all abundance”; IX.4, 8; X.14; XI.9 (deviating from the Greek text; see the note on this passage); XIII.4; Gal. VI.1; Eph. I.4, 16; II.11; III.4, 18; VI.15; Phil. II.22; IV.3; Col. I.10, 24; II.16; III.15; IV.12; 1 Thess. III.2; IV.15; 1 Tim. I.2; V.10; 2 Tim. II.1, 9; *Skeir.* II.c.

Here also belong the elliptical cases: Matt. VI.6, 18 *atta theins sa in fulhsnja*, “thy Father [who is] in secret”; Luke I.77 *kunthi naseinais in afleta frawaurhte*, “knowledge of salvation in forgiveness of sins”; 1 Cor. XI.25 *sa stikls so niujo triggwa ist in meinamma blotha*, “this cup is the new covenant in my blood”; Eph. I.19 *mikilei maihtais is in uns*, “the greatness of his power in us.”

b) To indicate the manner in which a person acts, appears, or is; or in which something happens, and in which someone is or something works: **in, with, by**, ἐν. Matt. VI.29 *nih Saulaumon in allamma wulthau seinamma gawasida sik swe ains thize*, “not even Solomon in all his glory arrayed himself like one of these”; VII.15 *qimand at izwis in wastjom lambe*, “they come to you in sheep’s clothing”; Luke XX.46; Mark I.23 and V.2 *manna in unhrainjamma ahmin*, “a man with an unclean spirit”; I.30 *in brinnon ligan*, “lying sick with fever”; III.23 *in gajukom qithan*, “to speak in parables”; XII.1; IV.2, 11, 30; Luke VIII.10; John XVI.25; Mark V.25 *in runa blothis wisan*, “to be with an issue of blood”; Luke VIII.43; Mark VIII.38 *qiman in wulthau*, “to come in glory”; Luke IX.26, 31 *thai gasaiwanans in wulthau*, “those who appeared in glory”; 1 Tim. III.16 *andnumans in wulthau*, “received up in glory”; Mark IX.1 *qiman in mahtai*, “come with power”; XII.36 *qithan in ahmin weihamma*, “speak by the Holy Spirit”; Luke I.17; II.27; IV.1, 14; Luke I.75 *skalkinon Gutha in sunjai jah garaihtein*, “to serve God in holiness and righteousness”; 78 *in armahairthein gaweisons*, “by the tender mercy [of God]”; Rom. VII.6 *skalkinon in niujithai ahmins*, “serve in newness of spirit”; XIV.18 *in thaim skalkinoth Xristau*, “in these things serves Christ”; Luke II.29 *fraleitan in gawairthja*, “dismiss in peace”; VIII.48 *gagg in gawairthja*, “go in peace”; 1 Cor. XVI.11; Luke IV.19 *fraletan in gathrafstein*, “to send forth in consolation” (where **consolation** must be read instead of **consolationem**); VI.12 *thairhwakan in bidai*, “continue all night in prayer”; VIII.15 *akran bairan in thulainai*, “bear fruit with patience”; Rom. VIII.3 *Guth seinana sunu sandida in galeikja leikis*, “God sent his own Son in the likeness of flesh”; 37 *in thaim allaim*—that is, “in all these distresses”—*jiukam*, “we conquer”; Rom. IX.22 *usbeidan in managail aggamodein*, “endure with much longsuffering”; 28 *gamaurgjan in garaihtein*, “complete [the matter] in righteousness”; XII.8 *dailjan in allsverein*, “distribute with liberality,” etc.; 1 Cor. I.17 *wailamerjan in snutrein waurdis*, “to preach the gospel in wisdom of speech”; V.8 *dulthjam ni in beista fairnjamma*, “not with old leaven”; XIV.21 *in antharaim razdom jah wairilom antharaim rodja*, “with other tongues and with other lips I shall speak”; XVI.14 *allata in friathwai wairthai*, “let all things be done in love”; 2 Cor. I.12; II.1; VI.4; VII.1; VIII.2; IX.6; X.3; XI.9, 23; XII.9, 12; Gal. VI.1, 6; Eph. I.8; II.4; III.3 (*gameljan in leitilamma*, “to write in brief”); 12; IV.2, 15, 16, 19; V.21, 26; VI.18, 19, 20; Phil. I.27; II.3; Col. I.6, 9, 12, 22, 24, 28; II.11, 23; III.4, 16, 17, 22; IV.2; 1 Thess. II.17; III.13; IV.4, 5, 16; V.13; 2 Thess. I.4; 1 Tim. I.3, 13; II.2, 7, 11; III.9; IV.2; V.2, 5 to the end; 2 Tim. I.3; II.25; IV.2.

Here should also be included cases in which *in* and its complement convey an adverbial or predicative idea: Luke I.44 *lailaik thata barn in swignithai*, “the child leaped in joy”; 2 Cor. VII.14 *in sunjai rodjan*, “to speak truly”; XI.17 and 21 *rodjan in unfrodein*, “to speak foolishly”; Eph. VI.24 *frijon in unriurein*, “love in incorruption”; Col. I.29 *uswaurkjan in mahtai*, “labour with power”; Luke IV.32 *in waldufnja wisan*, “to be with authority”; 2 Cor. VIII.12 *in gagreftai wisan*, “to be according to what one has”; Phil. II.6 *in Guthaskaunein wisands*, “being in the form of God”; 1 Tim. II.12 *wisan in thahainai*, “to be in silence”; with *wisan* understood: Luke I.27 *in fragibtim*, “[a virgin] betrothed”; 2 Cor. III.11 *in wulthau*, “in glory” (where **remaining** must be read instead of **existing**); compare Col. IV.6 *waurd izwar in anstai salta gasuqoth sijai*, “let your speech be always with grace, seasoned with salt”; 2 Cor. III.8 *wairthan in wulthau*, “come in glory”; Phil. II.7 *in galeikja manne wairthans*, “becoming in the likeness of men”; Col. III.21 *wairthan in unlustau*, “be discouraged.”

c) It is also used instrumentally: **in, with, by, through**, ἐν.

α) Where a thing is concerned: Matt. III.11 *daupjan in ahmin*, “baptize with the Spirit”; Luke III.16; Matt. VI.7 *in filuwaurdein audhausjan*, “think that they will be heard for their many words”; Mark I.8 *daupjan in watin—in ahmin*, “baptize with water—with the Spirit”; IV.24 *in mithath mithan*, “measure with the measure”; IX.29 *thata kuni in waihtai ni mag usgaggan niba in bidai jah fastubnja*, “this kind can come out by nothing except prayer and fasting”; Luke IX.43; Mark XI.28, 29 *in hwamma waldufnje thata taujis*, “by what authority doest thou these things?”; Luke XX.2, 8; I.51 *gatawida swinthe in arma*, “he wrought strength with his arm”; VII.25 *in hnasqjaim wastjom gawasiths*, “clothed in soft garments”; John XVII.17 *weihan in sunjai*, “sanctify in truth”; 19; Rom. X.9 *andhaitan in muntha*, “confess with the mouth”; 1 Cor. XVI.20 *goleith izwis in frijonai weihai*, “greet one another with a holy kiss”; 1 Thess. V.26; 2 Cor. VII.6, 7; Eph. I.3, 6; II.3, 7, 13; IV.3, 14; V.18, 19; VI.13, 20; Col. I.11; 2 Thess. I.8, 11; II.16; IV.18; 1 Tim. II.9; III.13 (see the note on this passage); IV.12; *Skeir.* I.c.

β) Where a person is concerned: Matt. IX.34 and Mark III.22 *in fauramatlja unhulthono unhulthons usdreibith*, “by the chief of demons he casts out demons”; 1 Cor. VII.14 *weihada ist qens so ungalaubjandei in abin*, “the unbelieving wife is sanctified by the husband”; XV.22 *in Adama allai gadauthnand—in Xristau allai gaqiunand*, “in Adam all die—in Christ all shall be made alive”; Eph. I.6 *Guth ansteigs was uns in Sunau seinamma*, “God bestowed grace on us in his beloved Son”; X.11; II.13; III.13; Phil. I.26; IV.13; Col. II.15; 2 Tim. II.1.

d) Here also belong many formulas borrowed from Greek and occurring chiefly in the epistles, such as *in fraujin*, “in the Lord”: Rom. XIV.17; XVI.22; 1 Cor. VII.22; XII.13; XV.58; XVI.19; 2 Cor. II.12; Gal. V.10; Eph. I.4; II.21; III.20; IV.1, 17; V.8; VI.21; Phil. I.14; II.29; III.1; IV.1, 4, 10; Col. I.14, 16, 19; III.18, 20; IV.7, 17; 1 Thess. V.12, 16, 27; 2 Thess. III.4; 1 Tim. III.16.

*in Xristau Iesu*, “in Christ Jesus”: Rom. VI.23; VIII.2, 39; XII.5; 1 Cor. XV.18, 22, 31; XVI.24; 2 Cor. I.19, 20; II.14; III.14; V.17, 19; XI.3; XII.2, 19; Gal. I.22; II.4; III.28; V.6; Eph. I.1, 3, 6, 7, 10, 12, 15, 20; II.6, 10, 13, 21; III.6, 11; IV.21, 32; Phil. I.26; II.1; III.3; IV.7; Col. I.28; 1 Thess. II.14; IV.1, 16; V.18; 2 Thess. III.12; 2 Tim. II.1.

*in ahmin*, “in the Spirit”: Eph. II.18, 22; III.5; VI.18; Col. I.8.

Especially *in namin*, “in [the] name”: Matt. X.41, 42; Mark IX.38, 39, 41; XI.9; Luke IX.50; X.17; XIX.38; John X.25; XII.13; XIV.13, 26; XV.16; XVI.23, 24; XVII.11; 1 Cor. I.13, 15; V.4; Eph. V.20; Col. III.17; 2 Thess. III.6.

*in andwairthja*, “in [his] presence”: see **Andwairthi**, under **Wairths**; *in augam*, “in [the] eyes, in [the] sight”: Mark XII.11; Col. III.22; *in wikon*, “in [the] course”: Luke I.8; *in tewai*, “in [the] order”: 1 Cor. XV.23; *in thizai halbai*, “in this half”: 2 Cor. III.10; IX.3; *in thamma*, “in this, in it”: John IX.30; XV.8; 1 Cor. IV.4; XI.22; 2 Cor. VIII.10; *Skeir.* VIII.c; *in thammei*, “because, therefore”: Rom. VIII.3; 2 Cor. II.12; Gal. IV.18; Phil. III.12; “because,” Luke I.78—see the note there; *in allamma*: 2 Cor. II.9 (εἰς); IV.8; VI.4; VII.5, 11; IX.8, 11; XI.6; Eph. V.24; VI.13; Phil. IV.12; Col. I.10; 1 Tim. III.11; *in allaim*: Col. I.18; III.11; 2 Tim. IV.5; *in managaim*: 2 Cor. VIII.22; *in waihtai ni*, “in no respect”: 2 Cor. VI.3; VII.9; Phil. I.20, 25; *Skeir.* VII.c.

e) *In* with the dative is also used where a relation is indicated, in which case elsewhere the accusative or another preposition normally occurs, in the sense “to, in, upon,” ἐν, εἰς. Thus after *galaubjan*, “believe”: Mark I.15; Gal. II.16 (εἰς); *galaubeins*, “faith”: 1 Tim. III.13; *gatrauan*, “trust”: Rom. XIV.14; 2 Cor. II.3 (ἐπί with accusative); VII.16; X.1 (εἰς); Gal. V.10; Phil. II.24; III.3; *trauain haban*, “have confidence”: Phil. III.4; *anananthan*, “boast”: 2 Cor. XI.21; *galeikan*, “be pleasing”: Mark I.11; *waila galeikan*, “be well pleasing”: Luke III.22; *wenjan*, “hope”: 1 Cor. XV.19. So likewise 1 Cor. X.2 *in (εἰς) Mose daupidai wesun*, “they were baptized unto Moses”; Gal. III.27 *in (εἰς) Xristau daupidai wesuth*, “you were baptized into Christ”; 1 Cor. I.13 *in (εἰς) namin Pawlaus daupjau*, “was I baptized in the name of Paul?” Compare 1 Cor. IV.6 *tho thairhgaleikonda iu (εἰς) mis jah Apaullon*, “that ye might learn in us not to go beyond [what is written]”; Luke XVI.8 *thai sunjos this aiwis frodozans sunum liuhadis in (εἰς) kunja seinamma sind*, “the children of this age are wiser toward their own generation than the children of light”; Eph. I.5 *fauragarairoth uns du suniwe gadedai thairh Iesu in (εἰς) imma*, “having predestined us to adoption as sons through Jesus unto himself”; Col. I.20 *thairh ina gafrithon alla in (εἰς) imma*, “through him to reconcile all things unto himself.”

f) *In* sometimes expresses an outcome or result: Rom. XIII.4 *Guths andbahts ist … thus in (εἰς) godamma*, “he is God’s minister … for thy good”; 1 Cor. IV.3 *mis in (εἰς) minnistin ist*, “to me it is a very small matter”; VII.15 *in (ἐν) gawairthja lathoda uns Guth*, “God has called us in peace”; Col. III.15 (where the Greek has εἰς, and **wherein** must be read instead of **whereby** in the translation); 2 Cor. IX.11 *gabignan in (εἰς) allai ainfalthein*, “being enriched unto all liberality”; Eph. I.17 *gibai izwis ahman handugeins in ufkuntja seinamma*, “may [he] give you a spirit of wisdom in the knowledge of him”; Col. I.10 *managan*—which the scribe seems to have omitted—*in (εἰς) ufkuntja Guths*, “abounding unto the knowledge of God” (otherwise this passage belongs under b); 2 Tim. III.16 *talzeins in garaihtein*, “for instruction in righteousness.”

g) Finally, in certain passages it is causal: 2 Cor. IX.13 *mikiljan Guth in ainfalthein*, “glorifying God because of [your] liberality” (above, *ana*); Gal. I.24 *in mis mikilidedun Guth*, “they glorified God because of me”; 2 Cor. VIII.20 *ibai was uns fairinodedi in digrein*, “lest anyone should blame us concerning this abundance”; IX.14 *gairnjandans izwara in (διά with accusative) ufarassau anstais Guths*, “longing for you because of the surpassing grace of God”; Phil. I.17 *in (ἐκ) friathwai*, “from love” (above, *in* with genitive); Eph. III.13 *ni wairthaith usgrudjans in aglom meinaim faur izwis*, “do not lose heart because of my tribulations for you.” Likewise after *gamarzjan*, “be offended”: Matt. XI.6; Mark VI.3; Luke VII.23; *afslauthiths wisan*, “be perplexed”: Gal. IV.20; *afagjan*, “be moved”: 1 Thess. III.3; *wopan*, “boast”: 2 Cor. X.15, 17; XI.12; XII.5, 9; Gal. VI.13; Phil. III.3; 2 Thess. I.4; *woftulja haban*, “have confidence”: Gal. XI.4 [probably an erroneous citation]; compare Phil. I.26; *faginon*, “rejoice”: Luke I.14; X.20; Phil. I.18; *swignjan*, “rejoice”: John V.35.

C. With the genitive it means **for, because of, on account of**, and is used especially:

1) For Greek διά with accusative: Matt. XXVII.18 *in neidis atgebun ina*, “they delivered him up because of envy”; Mark III.9 *skip habaith wisan in manageins*, “that a boat should be ready for him because of the crowd”; IV.17 *qimith wrakja in this waurdis*, “tribulation comes because of the word”; VI.17 *Herodes gaband Iohannen in Hairodiadins*, “Herod had laid hold on John because of Herodias”; 26; XV.10; Luke V.19; John VI.57; VII.13; X.19, 32; XI.42; XII.9, 11, 30; XV.3, 21; Rom. XI.28; XIII.5; 1 Cor. IV.6, 10; VII.5, 26; VIII.11; IX.23; X.25, 28; XV.31; 2 Cor. II.10; III.7; IV.5, 11, 15; VII.12; VIII.9; Gal. II.4; Eph. II.4; IV.18; Phil. I.15, 24; II.30; III.7, 8; Col. IV.3; 1 Thess. V.13; 1 Tim. V.23; 2 Tim. I.6, 12; Titus I.13. Especially after *faginon*, “rejoice”: John XI.15; *sildaleikjan*, “marvel”: Mark VI.6; *gauriths wairthan*, “become sorrowful”: Mark VI.26; Rom. XIV.15.

2) For διά with genitive: 2 Cor. VIII.8 *qitha in thizos antharaize usdaudeins*, “I speak because of the diligence of others”; Gal. V.13 *in friathwos ahmins skalkinoth izwis*, “through love of the Spirit serve one another”; 1 Thess. III.7 *gathrafstidai sijum in izwaraizos galaubeinais*, “we were comforted because of your faith.”

3) For ἐπί with dative: after *gaurs*, “grieved”: Mark III.5; *ganipnands*, “sorrowful”: Mark X.22; *afslauthnan*, “be dismayed”: Mark X.24; *sildaleikjan*, “wonder”: Mark XI.18; Luke V.9; *faginon*, “rejoice”: 1 Cor. XVI.17; 2 Cor. VII.4; Luke XV.7, 10; *awiliud*, “thanksgiving”: 2 Cor. IX.15; *hazjan Guth*, “praise God”: Luke II.20.

4) For ὑπέρ with genitive, after *awiliudon*, “give thanks”: 1 Cor. X.30; Eph. I.16; *hauhjan Guth*, “glorify God”: Rom. XV.9; *wopan*, “boast”: 2 Thess. I.4; and elsewhere as well: John VI.51 *leik mein giba in thizos manasedais libainais*, “I shall give my flesh for the life of the world”; XI.4 *so siukei ist in hauheinais Guths*, “this sickness is for the glory of God”; 1 Cor. I.13; XI.24; 2 Cor. I.6; XII.19; Eph. III.1; 2 Thess. I.5.

5) For περί with genitive: John X.33 *in Guths waurstwis ni stainjam thuk*, “we do not stone thee for a good work”; especially after *hazjan Guth*, “praise God”: Luke XIX.37; *awiliudon*, “give thanks”: 1 Thess. III.9; 2 Thess. I.3; *infeinan*, “have compassion”: Matt. IX.36.

6) For ἕνεκεν: Matt. X.39 *fraqisteith saiwalai seinai in meina*, “whoever loses his life for my sake”; Mark VIII.35; X.29; [Col. 1362] Luke VI.22; IX.24; XVII.33; XVIII.29; Rom. XIV.20; 2 Cor. III.10.

7) For χάριν with genitive: Titus I.11 *laisjan thatei ni skuld ist in faihugairneins*, “teaching things which they ought not, for the sake of base gain”; *Skeir.* II.a; IV.d; VIII.b.

8) Add the formulas: *in this*, “therefore,” τούτου χάριν: Eph. III.14; *Skeir.* IV.d; *inuh this* (*inuth-this*, Rom. XIII.6), “therefore,” διά τοῦτο: Rom. XIII.6; 2 Cor. VII.13; 1 Thess. III.7; 2 Tim. II.10; ἕνεκεν τούτου, Mark X.7; διό: 2 Cor. II.8; IV.16; V.9 (διὸ καί); VI.17; 1 Thess. V.11; *Skeir.* I.a, d; II.a, b; III.d; IV.a, b; VI.c, d; *inuh this nu*, “therefore,” τοιγαροῦν: 1 Thess. IV.8; *in thizei* (*in thize*, Eph. III.13; but *in thize*, Rom. IX.17, is incorrect), “because of which, because,” διό: Rom. XV.7; 2 Cor. IV.13; XII.10 (where **in which** must be read instead of **because of which** in the translation); Eph. III.13; IV.8, 25; 1 Thess. III.1; οὗ χάριν, Luke VII.27; οὗ ἕνεκεν, Luke IV.8; δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν, Luke VIII.47; ἀνθ’ ὧν, Luke XIX.44; διά τό with infinitive: Mark IV.15; Luke VIII.6; XVIII.5; διότι: Phil. II.26; *Skeir.* I.d; III.b; IV.c; VI.a, c; *in thizozei waihtais* (or *fairinos*), “for this reason,” δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν: 2 Tim. I.6, 12; Titus I.13; διά τοῦτο: Eph. III.1; Titus I.5; *in wis*, “why?” διατί: 2 Cor. XI.11; *in thize ei*, “in order that, for which reason,” ἵνα: Titus I.5; Neh. V.18.

II. In composition:

1) With verbs: *inagjan, inaljanon, inbrannjan, indrobnan, inliuhtjan, inmaidjan, inrauhtjan, insaian, insailjan, insaiwan, insakan, insandjan, inswinthjan, intandjan, intundnan, intrusgjan, invagjan, inwidan, invandjan, inwisan, inweitan*; compound forms: *ingaleikon; anainsakan; mithinsandjan.*

2) With nouns: *inahei, ingardja, inkiltho, inmaideins, inniujitha, insahts, invinditha.*

3) With adjectives: *inahs, ingards, inkuns, invinds.*

**ÏNUH**, *in* with enclitic *uh*: see under **uh**.  
**ÏNUH þIS** (*ïnuþ-þis*): see **In**, I.C.8.  
**ÏNN**, adverb: “within,” εἰς …: Matt. IX.25; Mark V.40; VI.22; XV.43; Luke I.28; IV.16; John X.1; XVIII.16. Regularly, when no verb follows, it is combined with one; see *inngaggan, innwairpan; innatbairan, innatgaggan, innattiuhan; inngaleithan; innufsliupan; mithinngaleithan.*  
**ÏNNA**, adverb: “within,” ἔσω: 1 Cor. V.12. Combined with verbs it corresponds to Greek ἐν …; thus *inna gaggan* (ἐμπεριπατεῖν), “to walk among”: 2 Cor. VI.16; *inna gameljan* (ἐγγράφειν), “to write in”: 2 Cor. II.3; *inna uswaurkjan* (ἐνεργεῖσθαι), “to work in”: Col. I.29; likewise *innakunds*. But in *innagahts*, *in* stands in place of *inn*, just as *anda* does for *and*.  
**ÏNNANA**, adverb: 1) “from within,” “within,” ἔσωθεν: 2 Cor. VII.5; 2) “within,” with genitive, ἔσω: Mark XV.16; see the note there.  
**ÏNNAþRO**, adverb: 1) “from within,” ἔσωθεν: Mark I.21, 23; 2) “within,” ἔσωθεν: Matt. VII.15.  
**ÏNNUMA**, comparative adjective: “inner,” ὁ ἔσω: Rom. VII.22 (where *innunin* should be read instead of *inumin*; see Col. I.29); Eph. III.16; ὁ ἔσωθεν: 2 Cor. IV.16.  
**INA**, see under **Is**.  
**INQIS**, see **Igqis**.  
**INILO**, feminine: “cause, pretext,” πρόφασις: John XV.22; Phil. I.18; ἀφορμή: 2 Cor. XI.12.  
**INUH** (*inu* in the Epistles to the Romans and Corinthians, and also 2 Cor. X.15; 1 Tim. V.21; Philem. 14; *Skeir.* I.b; Old Norse *an*; Old Saxon *ano*; Old Frisian *oni, one*; Old High German *ano, anu*; Modern High German *ohne*; Gf. I.283; Rchth. 964), preposition construed with the accusative: “without,” χωρίς: Mark IV.34; Luke VI.49; John XV.5; Rom. VII.8, 9; X.14; XI.29; 1 Cor. IV.8; 2 Cor. XI.28; Eph. II.12; 1 Tim. II.8; V.21; Philem. 14; *Skeir.* I.b; VII.b; ἄνευ: Matt. X.19; ἐκτός: 1 Cor. XV.27; 2 Cor. XII.2; παρεκτός: Matt. V.32; also to render privative α: 2 Cor. X.15 *inu mithath*, “without measure,” ἄμετρος; compare the note on Rom. X.19.  
**INS**, see under **Is**.  
**IUDAIA**, proper name, Greek declension, “Judaea,” Ἰουδαία: Mark I.5; III.7; X.1; Luke I.5; II.4; III.1; V.47; VI.17; [Col. 1363] VII.17; John VII.1, 3; XI.7; 2 Cor. I.6; Neh. V.14; VI.18; *Skeir.* IV.b.  
**ÏUDAIA-LAND**, see under **Land**.  
**ÏUDAIUS** (*Judaius*, John XI.45; 1 Cor. IX.20; XII.13; Gal. III.28), masculine proper name: “Jew,” Ἰουδαῖος: Matt. XXVII.11; Mark VII.13; XV.2; Luke VII.3; John III.25; VI.4, 41, 52; VII.1, 2, 8, 31, 48; IX.22; X.19; XI.45; XII.11; XVIII.35, 36; Rom. IX.24; 1 Cor. IX.20; XII.13; 2 Cor. XI.24; Gal. III.28; 1 Thess. II.14; Neh. V.17; VI.17.  
**ÏUDAIWISKS**, adjective: “Jewish,” Ἰουδαϊκός: Titus I.14; *Skeir.* III.b.  
**ÏUDAIWISKO**, adverb: “in a Jewish manner,” Ἰουδαϊκῶς: Gal. II.14.  
**ÏUDAIWISKON**, second conjugation: “to live in a Jewish manner; to Judaize,” ἰουδαΐζειν: Gal. II.14.  
**IUDAS** (*Judas*, John XII.4; *Iodas*, Luke III.26), masculine proper name: “Judas,” Ἰούδας and Ἰούδα: Matt. XXVII.3; Mark III.19; VI.3; XIV.10; Luke I.39; III.26, 30, 33; VI.16; John VI.71; XII.4; XIII.26, 29; XIV.22; XVIII.2.  
**IUMJO** (Gr. II.47; III.472), feminine: “crowd, multitude,” ὄχλος: Matt. VIII.1.  
**IUP** (Old Norse *upp*; Old Saxon, Anglo-Saxon, English, Swedish *up*; Old Frisian *op*; Old High German *uf*; Danish and Dutch *op*; Modern High German *ob, oben, auf*; Greek ὑπέρ; Latin *super*; Gr. II.49; Gf. I.169), adverb: “up, above,” ἄνω: John XI.41. Combined with verbs it corresponds to Greek ἀνα-; thus *insaiwan iup*, “to look up,” ἀναβλέπειν: Luke XIX.5; *iup ustiuhan*, “to bring up,” ἀνάγειν: Rom. X.7.  
**ÏUPA**, 1) “above,” ἄνω: Gal. IV.26; Col. III.1, 2; 2) “upwards,” ἄνω: Phil. III.14; *Skeir.* II.a.  
**ÏUPANA**, “again, from above,” ἄνωθεν: Gal. IV.9.  
**ÏUPAþRO**, “from above,” ἄνωθεν: Matt. XXVII.51; Mark XV.38; John III.3, 31; XIX.11; “above,” ἄνω: John VIII.23; *Skeir.* II.a; IV.c.  
**IUS**, adjective, comparative *iusiza*: “easy, useful”; *iusiza wisan*, “to be better,” διαφέρειν: Gal. IV.1.  
**ÏUSILA**, feminine: “relief,” ἄνεσις: 2 Cor. VIII.13 (2 Thess. I.7).  
**IUSE**, indeclinable proper name: “Joses,” Ἰωσῆ: Mark VI.3.  
**IS** (Old High German *ir*; Modern High German *er*; Latin *is*; Gr. I.785), feminine *si*, neuter *ita*, third-person personal pronoun: “he, she, it,” ordinarily αὐτός. For example, masculine: singular nominative *is*: Matt. VIII.24; Mark I.8, 45; II.15, 25; III.8, 13; IV.27, 38; V.4; VI.55; VII.36; VIII.29; Luke I.8; II.28; IV.15, 30; V.1, 12, 16, 17; VI.8, 20, 35; VII.5; VIII.1, 22, 37, 42, 54; IX.18, 29, 51; X.1; XV.14; XVI.24; XVII.11; XVIII.35, 39; XIX.37; John VI.15; VII.10; 1 Cor. XV.25, 28; 2 Cor. X.7; Eph. V.23; Col. I.17, 18; 1 Tim. III.7. Genitive *is*: Matt. III.11; V.35; VII.28; VIII.3, 13, 23, 25; IX.10, 11, 19, 20, 21; X.25, 35, 36; XI.20; XXV.41; XXVI.65; XXVII.19, 53, 64, etc. Dative *imma*: Matt. V.25, 39, 40, 41; VIII.1, 3, 4, 5, 7, 15, 16, 19, 20, 21, 22, 23, 27, 28; IX.2, 9, 19, 27, 28, 32; X.32; XI.2, 11; XXVII.11, 13, 14, 19, 42, 44, 54, 55, 64, etc. Accusative *ina*: Matt. VI.8; VII.24; VIII.2, 5, 7, 25, 31, 34; IX.18, 24, 31; X.33; XXVI.71; XVVII.1, 2, 3, 11, 18, 43, 48, 49, etc. Plural nominative *eis*: Matt. IX.32; Luke VI.11; IX.36; XIV.12; XVIII.34; John XVII.8, 19; Rom. XI.31; 2 Cor. VI.16; X.12; Gal. II.9. Genitive *ize*: Matt. VI.14, 15; VII.16, 20; VIII.34; IX.2, 4, 29, 35, 36; X.29; XI.1, etc. Dative *im*: Matt. VI.1, 7; VII.12, 23; VIII.4, 20, 32; IX.12, 15, 18, 24, 28, 30; XI.4; XXV.40, 45; XXVII.17, 48, 65, etc. Accusative *ins*: Matt. VI.26; VII.16, 20, 29; IX.30; X.26; XXVII.10, etc.

Feminine: singular nominative *si*: Luke VII.12. Genitive *izos*: Matt. V.28; VIII.15; IX.25; X.35; Mark I.31; V.29; VII.26; XIV.9; Luke I.5, 41, 58; VII.47; VIII.44, 54, 55, 56; X.10; John XI.1, 5; XVI.21; 1 Cor. X.26, 28; Gal. IV.30; 2 Tim. III.5. Dative *izai*: Matt. V.28, 31; X.39; Mark V.34, 41, 43; VI.23, 26; VII.27, 29; VIII.35; X.15; XIV.6; XVI.11; Luke I.28, 29, 30, 35, 36, 38, 45, 56, 58, 61; II.6; VII.12, 13; VIII.48, 55; [Col. 1364] IX.24; X.9; XVI.16; XVII.33; XVIII.17; XIX.45; John XI.23, 31, 33, 40; XII.25; Rom. IX.12; X.5; 1 Cor. VII.13; Eph. VI.20; Col. IV.2. Accusative *ija*: Matt. VIII.15; IX.18; Mark I.30; V.33; Luke IV.39; John XI.31, 33; XII.7. Plural genitive *izo*: John XI.19; dative *im*: Mark XVI.6; Eph. IV.18; 1 Tim. V.16; accusative *ijos*: Mark XVI.8; John XI.19.

Neuter: singular nominative *ita*: Mark IV.37. Genitive *is*: Matt. VII.27; Mark IV.32; John VIII.44; Col. II.22; 1 Tim. I.8. Dative *imma*: Luke I.66; XIV.35. Accusative *ita*: Matt. V.29; XXVII.59, 60; Mark IV.16; VI.28, 29; IX.36; XI.17; XV.46; Luke VI.48; VIII.16; John XV.2; Rom. VII.20; Eph. V.29; Col. II.14; IV.17. Plural nominative *ija*: Luke II.50; dative *im*: Mark X.13, 16; Luke I.7; II.42, 49, 50, 51; V.2.

In the nominative it is also used for ὁ, ἡ, τό: Matt. VIII.32; IX.31; XXVI.66; XXVII.4, 66; Mark III.4; V.34; VI.24, 28; VII.6, 28; VIII.5, 20, 28, 33; IX.12, 19, 21, 32, 34; X.3, 4, 22, 26, 36, 37, 39, 48, 50; XI.6; XII.3, 14, 16; XIV.11, 46, 52, 61, 64, 68, 70, 71; XV.2, 13, 14, 23; Luke I.20; IV.40, 43; V.33, 34; VI.10; VII.4, 40, 43; VIII.21, 24, 56; IX.13, 19, 21, 45, 59; X.27, 29; XV.27, 29; XVI.7; XVII.37; XVIII.21, 23, 27, 29, 41; XIX.34; XX.5, 11, 12, 17, 25; John IX.15, 17, 38; XVIII.7. For οὗτος: Luke VII.44, 45, 46; Rom. VIII.9; see the note there. For ἐκεῖνος: Mark XVI.11; Luke XIX.4; John VII.29; VIII.42; IX.9; XIV.12; XVI.8; XVIII.17, 25; 1 Cor. IX.25; 2 Cor. VIII.9; 2 Tim. II.12. In the genitive also for αὑτοῦ (otherwise *seins*): Mark VII.26; VIII.3; 2 Thess. I.10 (in these passages, moreover, several manuscripts read αὐτοῦ).

Sometimes the nominative is used as the subject of a sentence where the Greek omits the pronoun: Matt. XI.23 *eis weseina* (ἔμειναν, “they remained”); Mark (VII.36) XV.44; Luke I.63; VII.50; XIV.14; XVIII.38; John VI.21; IX.8, 12, 18; XI.13; XIV.17; XVIII.28, 31, 40; 1 Cor. XVI.12.

**ISAK**, masculine proper name: “Isaac,” Ἰσαάκ: Matt. VIII.11; Mark XII.26; Luke III.34; XX.37; Rom. IX.7, 10; Gal. IV.28.  
**ISKARIOTES** (*Iskarioteis*, Mark XIV.10; *Iscariotes*, John XIV.22), proper name: “Iscariot,” Ἰσκαριώτης: Mark III.19; XIV.10; Luke VI.16; John VI.71; XII.4; XIII.26; XIV.22.  
**ISRAEL**, masculine proper name: “Israel,” Ἰσραήλ: Matt. VIII.10; IX.33; X.23; XXVII.19, 42; Mark XII.29; Luke II.25, 32; IV.25; John XII.13; Rom. IX.27, 31; XI.26; 2 Cor. III.7, 13; Gal. VI.16; Phil. III.5.  
**ÏSRAELEITES** (*Israelites*, Rom. IX.4), proper name: “Israelite,” Ἰσραηλίτης: Rom. IX.4; XI.1; 2 Cor. XI.22.  
**ITAN** (Old Norse and Old Frisian *eta*; Old Saxon and Anglo-Saxon *etan*; Old High German *ezan*; English *eat*; Swedish *äta*; Danish *aede*; Modern High German *essen, ätzen*; Greek ἔδειν; Latin *edere*; Gr. II.25; Gf. I.524; Rchth. 717), first conjugation: infinitive *itan*, plural preterite *etun*, present participle *itans*, “to eat,” ἐσθίειν: Luke XV.16; XVI.21; XVII.27, 28.  
**FRA-ÏTAN** (preterite *frat*, plural *fretun*): “to devour,” κατεσθίειν: 2 Cor. XI.20; καταφαγεῖν: Mark IV.4; Luke VIII.5; XV.30; see the note there.  
**FRA-ATJAN**, second conjugation: “to feed, distribute food,” ψωμίζειν: 1 Cor. XIII.3.  
**AF-ETJA**, masculine: “glutton,” φάγος: Matt. XI.19; Luke VII.34.  
**UZ-ETA**, masculine, or **Uz-eto**, neuter: “manger,” φάτνη: Luke II.7, 12, 16.  
**ITURAIA**, proper name, Greek declension: “Ituraea,” Ἰτουραία: Luke III.1.  
**IFTUMA** (Gr. II.50), adjective: “following, next”; *iftumin daga*, “on the next day,” τῇ ἐπαύριον: Matt. XXVII.62; Mark XI.12; John VI.22; XII.12.  
**IOANAN**, proper name: “Jonan,” Ἰωνάν: Neh. VI.18.  
**IODAS**, the same as **Iudas**.  
**IOHANNA**, feminine proper name: “Joanna,” Ἰωάννα: Luke VIII.3.  
**IOHANNA**, masculine proper name: “Joannan” and “Jonan,” Ἰωαννάν and Ἰωνάν: Luke III.27, 30.  
[Col. 1365]  
**IOHANNES** (*Iohannis*, Mark VI.14), masculine proper name: “John,” Ἰωάννης: Matt. IX.14; XI.2, 4, 7, 11, 12, 13; Mark I.9, 14, 19, 29; III.17; V.37; VI.16, 17; VIII.28; IX.2; X.35, 41; XI.30; Luke III.2, 15; V.10, 33; VI.16; VII.18, 19, 20, 22, 24, 28, 29; VIII.3, 25; IX.9; X.41; XX.4; John III.24, 25; *Skeir.* III.b. [Col. 1366]

IOREIM, masculine proper name, Ἰωρείμ (Joreim): Luke 3:29. IORA, masculine proper name, Ἰωρά (Jora): Ezra 2:18. IOSES, masculine proper name, Ἰωσῆ (Joses): Matthew 27:56; Mark 15:40, 47; Luke 3:29. IOSEF, masculine proper name, Ἰωσήφ (Joseph): Matthew 27:57; Mark 15:43, 45; Luke 2:16, 23, 24, 30, 33; John 6:42; *Skeireins* II, a.

[Col. 1365] K

KABBALARJA, proper noun: Arezzo document.

KAEINAN, masculine proper noun, Καϊνάν: Luke 3:36, 37.

KAIDMEIEL, masculine proper noun, Καδμιήλ: Ezra 2:40.

KAIDRON, proper noun, Κεδρών: John 18:1.

KAISAR (Latin word), masculine, Caesar, Καῖσαρ: Mark 12:14, 16, 17; Luke 2:1; 3:1; 20:23, 24, 25; John 19:12.

KAISARA-GILD, see under *Gildan*.

KAISARIA, proper noun, Καισαρία: Mark 8:27.

KALBO (Old Norse *kalfr*, Old Saxon *calf*, Anglo-Saxon *cealf*, Old High German *kalb*, English *calf*, Swedish and Dutch *kalf*, Danish *kalv*, New High German *Kalb*; Gr. II, 58; Gf. IV, 391), feminine, heifer (δάμαλις, according to Num. 19:2): *Skeireins* III, c.

KALDS (Old Norse *kaldr*, Old Saxon *cald*, Anglo-Saxon *ceald*, Old Frisian *kald*, Old High German *kalt*, English *cold*, Swedish *koll*, Danish *kold*, Dutch *koud*, New High German *kalt*; Gr. II, 9; Gf. IV, 381; Rchth. 856), adjective, cold, ψυχρός: Matthew 10:42; neuter, “the cold thing,” cold, ψῦχος: John 18:18.

KALKJO (*Kalki*?), feminine, adulteress, prostitute, πόρνη: Luke 15:30.

KALKINASSUS, masculine, adultery, sexual immorality, πορνεία: Matthew 5:32; Mark 7:21; Galatians 5:19; 1 Thessalonians 4:3.

KANANEITES, proper noun, Κανανίτης: Mark 3:18.

KANNJAN, see under *Kunnan*.

KAJAFA, masculine proper noun, Καϊάφας: Luke 3:2; John 18:13, 14, 23, 28.

KAULAUSSAUS (or *Kaulaussaius*), proper noun, Κολοσσαεύς, “Colossian”: subscription to Colossians (see the heading of 2 Thessalonians).

KAUPATJAN (compare English *cuff*, Swedish *kuffa*, Danish *kjep*; Greek κόπτειν), anomalous conjugation; preterite *kaupasta*, to strike with the fist, to buffet, κολαφίζειν: Matthew 26:67; Mark 14:65; 1 Corinthians 4:11; 2 Corinthians 11:7.

KAUPON (Old Norse *kaupa*, Old Saxon *capon, capan*, Anglo-Saxon *ceapian*, Old Frisian *kapia*, Old High German *kaufon*, English *cheapen*, Swedish *köpa*, Danish *kjöbe*, Dutch *koopen*, New High German *kaufen*; compare Greek κάπηλος, Latin *caupo*; Gf. IV, 372; Rchth. 859), second conjugation, to trade, transact business, πραγματεύεσθαι: Luke 19:13.

KAURAZEIN, proper noun, Χοραζίν: Matthew 11:21; Luke 10:13.

KAURBAN (Hebrew word), κορβᾶν: Mark 7:11.

KAURBANAUN (Hebrew word), κορβανᾶν: Matthew 27:6.

KAURINþO, feminine proper noun, Κόρινθος, Corinth: subscription to Romans; 2 Corinthians 1:1, 23.

KAURINþIUS (*Kaurinþaius* in the heading and subscription of 2 Corinthians), masculine proper noun, Κορίνθιος, Corinthian: subscription to 1 Corinthians; heading to 2 Corinthians; 2 Corinthians 6:11; subscription.

KAURN (Old Norse, Old Frisian, Old High German, Swedish, Danish, and New High German *korn*; Old Saxon *curni*; Anglo-Saxon and English *corn*; Dutch *koorn*; Gr. II, 61; III, 375; Gf. IV, 494; Rchth. 877), neuter, grain, σῖτος: Mark 4:28; Luke 3:17; 16:7.

KAURNO, neuter, grain, little grain, seed, κόκκος: Mark 4:31; Luke 17:6; John 12:24.

KAURS (Gr. II, 57), adjective, heavy, weighty, βαρύς: 2 Corinthians 10:10.

[Col. 1366] KAURIþA, feminine, burden, βάρος: Galatians 6:2.

KAURJAN, second conjugation, to weigh down, burden, βαρεῖν: Luke 9:32; 2 Corinthians 1:8; 5:4; 1 Timothy 5:16; βαρύνειν, to burden: Nehemiah 5:15; βαρὺν εἶναι, to be burdensome: Nehemiah 5:18; καταβαρεῖν, to weigh down: 2 Corinthians 12:16; ἐπιβαρεῖν, to burden: 2 Thessalonians 3:8; καταναρκᾶν, to be burdensome: 2 Corinthians 11:8; 12:13, 14.

ANA-KAURJAN, the same, ἐπιβαρεῖν, to burden: 2 Corinthians 2:5.

MIþ-KAURJAN, to burden together; *miþ-kauriþs dauþau is*, “burdened together with his death,” συμμορφούμενος τῷ θανάτῳ αὐτοῦ, “being conformed to his death”: Philippians 3:10.

KAUREINS, feminine, burden, βάρος: 2 Corinthians 4:17.

UN-KAUREINS, freedom from burden; *in allaim unkaureinom*, “in every respect unburdensome,” ἐν παντὶ ἀβαρής, 2 Corinthians 11:9; see on this passage.

KAUSJAN, see under *Kiusan*.

KAPILLON (Latin *capillus*), second conjugation, to shear, κείρειν: 2 Corinthians 11:6.

KARA (Old High German *chara*, Anglo-Saxon *caru*, English *care*; Latin *cura*; Gr. II, 57; Gf. IV, 464), feminine, care. *Kar-ist* (i.e. *kara ist*) means “it concerns”; literally, “care holds”; construed with the accusative of the person and the genitive of the matter, μέλει: John 10:13; 12:6. Simple *kara*: Mark 4:38; 12:14. *Wa kara unsis*, “what is that to us?” τί πρὸς ἡμᾶς: Matthew 27:4.

UN-KARJA, adjective, careless, negligent: Mark 4:15, on this passage; *unkarja visan*, to neglect, ἀμελεῖν: 1 Timothy 4:14.

KARON, second conjugation, to be concerned, μέλει: 1 Corinthians 7:21.

GA-KARAN, second conjugation, to take care of, ἐπιμελεῖσθαι: 1 Timothy 3:5.

KAREIAþIAREIM, indeclinable proper noun, Καριαθιαρίμ: Ezra 2:25.

KARKARA (Latin *carcer*), feminine, prison, δεσμωτήριον: Matthew 11:2; φυλακή, prison: Matthew 5:25; 25:39, 44; Luke 3:20; John 3:24; 2 Corinthians 6:5; 11:23.

KARPUS, masculine proper noun, Κάρπος: 2 Timothy 4:13.

KAS (Old Norse *ker*, Old High German *char*, Danish *kar*; Gr. II, 52; III, 456; Gf. IV, 463), neuter, vessel, σκεῦος: Mark 3:27; 11:16; Luke 8:16; 17:31; Romans 9:21; 2 Corinthians 4:7; 1 Thessalonians 4:4; 2 Timothy 2:20, 21; κεράμιον, a water-jar: Mark 14:13; βάτος, a measure: Luke 16:6.

KASJA, masculine, potter, κεραμεύς: Matthew 27:7; Romans 9:21.

KATILS (Old Norse *kati, ketill*, Old High German *kezil*, Anglo-Saxon *cytel*, Old Frisian *ketel*, English *kettle*, Swedish *kettel*, Danish *kjedel*, Dutch *ketel*, New High German *Kessel*; Greek κοτύλη, Latin *catillus*; Gr. III, 457; Gf. IV, 537; Rchth. 867), masculine, cauldron, bronze vessel, χαλκίον: Mark 7:4.

KAVTSJO (Latin word), feminine, security, surety: Neapolitan document.

KAFAIRI, indeclinable proper noun, Χαφιρά: Ezra 2:25; see on this passage.

KAFARNAUM, indeclinable proper noun, Καπερναούμ: Matthew 8:5; 11:23; Mark 1:21; 9:33; Luke 4:31; 7:1; John 6:17, 24.

*KEIAN* (Anglo-Saxon *cennan*, Old Saxon and Old High German *kinan*, New High German *keimen*; Bopp 115 ff.; Gr. I, 854; IV, 26; Gf. IV, 450), first conjugation, *kai, kijun, kijans*, to sprout.

US-KEIAN, to come forth, grow, sprout, φυῆναι: Luke 8:6.

KEINAN, third conjugation, to sprout, βλαστάνειν: Mark 4:27.

[Col. 1367] US-KEINAN, the same, φυῆναι, to sprout: Luke 8:8; ἐκφυῆναι, to put forth: Mark 13:28.

MIþUS-KEINAN, to grow up together, συμφυῆναι: Luke 8:7.

KELIKN (Old Norse *galkn*; Gr. II, 160), neuter: 1. tower, house, πύργος: Mark 12:1; Luke 14:28. 2. upper room, ἀνώγαιον: Mark 14:15.

KEFAS, masculine proper noun, Κηφᾶς: 1 Corinthians 1:12; 9:5; 15:5.

KILEIKIA, feminine proper noun, Κιλικία: Galatians 1:21.

KILþEI (compare Anglo-Saxon *cild*, English *child*), feminine, womb, γαστήρ: Luke 1:31.

ÏN-KILþO, feminine, pregnant, with child, ἡ ἔγκυος: Luke 2:5; συνειληφυῖα, having conceived: Luke 1:36. *Ïnkilþo vairþan*, to conceive, συλλαμβάνειν: Luke 1:24.

KINDINS (compare Anglo-Saxon *cine*, Old Saxon *kunno*; among the Burgundians a king was called *hendinos*, see Ammianus Marcellinus 28.5; Mone, *Geschichte des nordischen Heidenthums*, II, 165; DRA. 229, 231, 756), masculine, governor, ἡγεμών: Matthew 27:2, 11, 14, 15; Luke 20:20. *Visan kindins*, to govern, ἡγεμονεύειν: Luke 2:2.

KINNUS (Old Norse *kinn*, Anglo-Saxon *cyn*, Old Saxon and Old High German *kinni*, Old Frisian *kin*, English *chin*, Danish *kind*, Dutch *kin*, New High German *Kinn*; Greek γένειον, Latin *gena*; Gr. III, 401; Gf. IV, 450; Rchth. 869), feminine, cheek, σιαγών: Matthew 5:39; Luke 6:29.

KINTUS, masculine, quadrans, κοδράντης: Matthew 5:26.

KIUSAN (Old Norse *kiosa, kiora*, Old Saxon *kiosan, coron, coston*, Anglo-Saxon *ceosan, costian*, Old Frisian *kiasa*, Old High German *churi, kiusan*, English *choose*, Swedish *kesa*, Danish *kaare*, Dutch *kiesen*, New High German *kiesen, küren, kosten*; Greek γεύεσθαι, Latin *gustare*; Gr. II, 22; Gf. IV, 507; Rchth. 868), first conjugation, *kaus, kusun, kusans*, to test, prove, δοκιμάζειν: 2 Corinthians 8:8; Galatians 6:4.

GA-KIUSAN, the same: Romans 12:2; 1 Corinthians 11:28; 16:3; Ephesians 5:10; 1 Timothy 3:10. Preterite participle *gakusans*, tested, approved, δόκιμος: Romans 14:18; 2 Corinthians 10:18; 13:7.

UNGA-KUSANS, rejected, reprobate, ἀδόκιμος: 2 Corinthians 13:5, 6, 7; Titus 1:16; see on this passage.

US-KIUSAN: 1. to test, judge, δοκιμάζειν: 1 Thessalonians 5:21. 2. to reject, construed with the dative, ἀποδοκιμάζειν: Mark 8:31; Luke 9:22; 17:25; 20:17; ἀθετεῖν, to set aside: 1 Corinthians 1:19. 3. to cast out, ἐκβάλλειν: Luke 4:29. Preterite participle *uskusans*, rejected, reprobate, ἀδόκιμος: 1 Corinthians 9:27; 2 Timothy 3:8; Titus 1:16.

KUSTUS, masculine, testing, proof, δοκιμή: 2 Corinthians 2:9; 8:2; 12:3.

GA-KUSTS, feminine, the same: 2 Corinthians 9:13.

KAUSJAN, second conjugation: 1. to test, try, with the accusative, δοκιμάζειν: Luke 14:19; 2 Corinthians 13:5. 2. to taste, with genitive and dative, γεύεσθαι: Mark 9:1; Luke 9:27; 14:24; John 8:52; Colossians 2:21.

GA-KAUSJAN, to test, try, δοκιμάζειν: 2 Corinthians 8:22.

*KLAHS* (Old Norse *klekia, klakinn*, Swedish *utkläcka*, Danish *utklaekke*), adjective, born, begotten.

NIU-KLAHS, newly born, little child, infant, νήπιος: Luke 10:21; 1 Corinthians 13:11; Galatians 4:1; Ephesians 4:14.

NIU-KLAHEI, feminine, faint-heartedness: *Skeireins* VII, a.

KLEMAINTUS (*Klaimaintus* at Philippians 4:3, on this passage), masculine proper noun, Κλήμης: Philippians 4:3.

KLISMO, feminine, cymbal, clanging instrument, κύμβαλον: 1 Corinthians 13:1.

KLISMJAN, second conjugation, to clang, ἀλαλάζειν: 1 Corinthians 13:1.

III, 405; Gf. IV, 575; Rchth. 875), neuter, knee, γόνυ: Mark 15:19; Luke 5:8; Romans 14:11; Ephesians 3:14.

KNUSSJAN, second conjugation, to bend the knee, γονυπετεῖν: Mark 10:17. *Knivam knussjan*, the same: Mark 1:40.

[Col. 1368] KNODA (*Knods*?; Anglo-Saxon *cneo*, Old Saxon *cnosles*, Old High German *knot*; Gf. IV, 572), feminine, race, offspring, γένος: Philippians 3:5.

KUBITUS (Latin word), masculine, bed, couch, κλισία: Luke 9:14.

KUKJAN (Old Norse *koss*, Old High German *kussian*, Old Saxon *cus, cussian*, Anglo-Saxon *cyssan*, Old Frisian *kos*, English *kiss*, Swedish *kyssa*, Danish *kysse*, Dutch *kussen*, New High German *küssen*; Gf. IV, 523; Rchth. 878), second conjugation, to kiss, with dative, φιλεῖν: Mark 14:44; καταφιλεῖν, to kiss fervently: Mark 14:45; Luke 7:38; 15:20; φίλημα δοῦναι, “to give a kiss”: Luke 7:45.

BI-KUKJAN, to show affection by kisses, to kiss fervently, καταφιλεῖν: Luke 7:45.

ANA-KUMBJAN, to recline: ἀνακεῖσθαι, Matthew 9:10; Luke 7:37; John 6:11; 12:2; 13:23, 28; κατακεῖσθαι, Mark 2:15; Luke 5:29; 1 Corinthians 8:10; συνανακεῖσθαι, Luke 14:15; ἀνακλίνεσθαι, Matthew 8:11; Luke 7:36; ἀναπίπτειν, Mark 8:6; Luke 14:10; 17:7; John 6:10; 13:12; ἐπιπίπτειν, John 13:25. *Gavaurkjan anakumbjan*, “to cause to recline,” with the dative, κατακλίνειν: Luke 9:14. *Gataujan anakumbjan*, the same, with the accusative, ἀνακλίνειν: Luke 9:15.

MIþANA-KUMBJAN, to recline with, συνανακεῖσθαι: Matthew 9:10; Mark 2:15; 6:22, 26; Luke 7:49; 14:10.

KUMEI, see under *Taleiþa*.

KUNA-VEDA, see under *Vidan*.

KUNDS: 1. see under *Kuni*; 2. see under *Kunnan*.

KUNI (Old Norse *kyn*, Old Saxon *cunni*, Anglo-Saxon *cyn*, Old Frisian *ken, kon*, Old High German *kunni*, English *kin, kind*, Swedish *kön*, Danish *kjön*, Dutch *kunne*; Greek γένος, Latin *genus, gens*; compare *kunnan*; DRA. 468; Gf. IV, 438; Rchth. 862), neuter, race, stock, γένος: 2 Corinthians 11:26; γενεά, generation: Matthew 11:16; Mark 8:12; 9:19; Luke 1:48; 7:31; 11:41, 43; 16:8; 17:25; γέννημα, offspring: Luke 3:7; συγγένεια, kinship: Luke 1:61; φυλή, tribe: Luke 2:36; Philippians 3:5; ἐφημερία, priestly division: Luke 1:8.

ALJA-KUNS (*aljakons*, Ephesians 2:19), adjective, foreigner, ἀλλογενής: Luke 17:18; resident alien, πάροικος: Ephesians 2:19; alien, contrary to nature, παρὰ φύσιν: Romans 11:24.

ÏN-KUNS, of the same people, fellow-tribesman, συμφυλέτης: 1 Thessalonians 2:14.

SAMA-KUNS, kinsman, συγγενής: Romans 9:3.

*KUNDS* (Old Saxon … *cund*), adjective, of a certain kind or manner.

AIRþA-KUNDS, earthly, “from the earth,” ἐκ τῆς γῆς: *Skeireins* IV, c (John 3:31).

GUMA-KUNDS, of the male sex, male, ἄρσην: Luke 2:23; Galatians 3:28.

GODA-KUNDS, of noble birth, εὐγενής: Luke 19:12.

QINA-KUNDS, of the female sex, female, θῆλυς: Galatians 3:28.

HIMINA-KUNDS, heavenly, οὐράνιος: Luke 2:13; ἐπουράνιος, celestial: 1 Corinthians 15:49; Ephesians 1:3; 2:6; 3:10; 6:12; *Skeireins* II, b; IV, c, d.

UFARHIMINA-KUNDS, the same, ἐπουράνιος: 1 Corinthians 15:48.

ÏNNA-KUNDS, domestic, of the household, οἰκιακός: Matthew 10:25, 36.

KUNNAN (Old Norse *kna, kunna, kanna*, Old Saxon *cunnan*, Anglo-Saxon *cnavan, cunnan*, Old Frisian *kanna*, Old High German *kunnan*, English *know, can, ken*, Swedish *känna, kunna*, Danish *kjende, kunne*, Dutch *kennen*, New High German *kennen, können*; Greek γνῶναι; Old Latin *gnoscere* [Caecilius in Diomedes 1, 378]; Bopp 81, 123; Gr. II, 34; Gf. IV, 408; Rchth. 858), anomalous conjugation; present *kann, knnnun* [as printed], preterite *kunþa*, participle *kunþs*: to know, recognize, come to know, γιγνώσκειν: Matthew 7:23; Mark 4:11, 13; 13:28, 29; Luke 1:18, 34; 8:10; 10:22; 16:15; John 6:15, 42; 7:49; 8:43, 55; 10:14, 15, 27; 12:6; 14:7, 17; 15:18, 21; 17:3, 23, 25; Romans 7:1; 1 Corinthians 1:21; 13:19; 2 Corinthians 2:4; 3:2; 5:16, 21; 8:9; Ephesians 3:19; 5:5; 6:22; Philippians 3:10; Colossians 4:8; 2 Timothy 1:18; 2:19; 3:1; ἐπιγινώσκειν, to recognize: 2 Corinthians 13:5.

[Col. 1369] εἰδέναι, to know: Matthew 26:72; 27:65; Mark 1:24, 34; 6:20; 10:19; 12:24; 14:71; Luke 4:34; 18:20; John 6:42; 7:15; 7:28, 29; 8:19, 55; 9:29; 10:4; 14:5; 16:30; Romans 7:7; 1 Corinthians 7:16; 2 Corinthians 5:16; 13:6; Galatians 4:8; 1 Thessalonians 5:12; 2 Thessalonians 1:8; 3:7; 2 Timothy 3:15; ἐπίστασθαι, to know: Mark 14:68; γνωρίζειν, to make known: Philippians 1:22; *Skeireins* I, b; III, a; V, a, d; VII, a.

UN-KUNNANDS, participle, ignorant, ἀγνοῶν: Romans 10:3; *Skeireins* II, b, c; IV, a; VI, b.

ANA-KUNNAN, second conjugation, to read aloud, read, ἀναγινώσκειν: 2 Corinthians 1:13; 3:2.

AT-KUNNAN, to know, experience, παρέχειν, “to furnish”: Colossians 4:1.

GA-KUNNAN: 1. to know, γιγνώσκειν: Luke 8:17; 19:15; Galatians 4:9; ἐπιγινώσκειν, to recognize: Luke 1:4; 2 Corinthians 1:14. 2. to observe, consider, καταμανθάνειν: Matthew 6:28. 3. to read aloud, read, ἀναγινώσκειν: Mark 12:26. 4. to submit oneself, be subordinate, εἴκειν: Galatians 2:5; also *gakunnan sik*, to subject oneself, ὑποτάσσεσθαι: 1 Corinthians 15:28. 5. to acknowledge; participle *gakunnands*, acknowledging, κατὰ συγγνώμην, “by concession”: 1 Corinthians 7:6.

UF-KUNNAN, second conjugation (preterite *kunþa*): 1. to know, γιγνώσκειν: Mark 5:29; Luke 7:39; 8:46; 19:44; John 6:69; 7:17, 26, 51; 8:28, 32, 52; 10:38; 13:35; 14:9, 20, 31; 16:3; 17:7, 25; Romans 7:7; 11:34; 2 Corinthians 2:9; 5:16; Nehemiah 6:16. 2. to recognize, experience, ἐπιγινώσκειν: Matthew 7:16, 20; Mark 2:8; 5:30; 6:54; Luke 5:22; 7:37; 1 Corinthians 13:12; 16:18; 2 Corinthians 1:13; 6:9; 1 Timothy 4:3.

FRA-KUNNAN, anomalous conjugation, to despise, ἐξουδενοῦν: Mark 9:12; ἐξουθενεῖν: Luke 18:9; Romans 14:3, 10; 1 Corinthians 16:11; 2 Corinthians 10:10; Galatians 4:14; 1 Thessalonians 5:20; καταφρονεῖν: Matthew 6:24; Luke 6:13; 1 Corinthians 11:22; 1 Timothy 4:12; 6:2; ἀθετεῖν, to reject: John 12:48; *Skeireins* I, d; VI, d.

KUNþS, participle used adjectivally, known, γνωστός: Luke 2:44; John 18:15. *Kunþs visan*, to become known, γνωρίζεσθαι: Ephesians 3:5; Philippians 4:6; γνωσθῆναι: Philippians 4:5.

UN-KUNþS, unknown, ἀγνοούμενος: 2 Corinthians 6:9; Galatians 1:22.

US-KUNþS, known; *uskunþs visan*, to appear, φανῆναι: Matthew 9:33; φανερωθῆναι, to be manifested: 2 Corinthians 4:10; γιγνώσκεσθαι, to be recognized: Luke 6:44; ἐν παῤῥησίᾳ εἶναι, to be publicly known: John 7:4. *Uskunþs vairþan*, to appear, φανῆναι: Romans 7:13.

SVI-KUNþS (*svekunþs*, Luke 8:17), known, manifest, φανερός: Mark 6:14; Luke 8:17; 1 Corinthians 14:25; 2 Corinthians 3:3; Galatians 5:19; 1 Timothy 4:15; ἐμφανής, evident: Romans 10:20; πρόδηλος, plainly evident: 1 Timothy 5:24, 25; ἔκδηλος, evident: 2 Timothy 3:9. *Svikunþs vairþan*, to be manifested, φανερωθῆναι: Mark 4:22; 2 Corinthians 4:11; Colossians 3:4. *Svikunþs visan*, to have been made manifest, πεφανερῶσθαι: 2 Corinthians 5:11.

UNSVI-KUNþS, comparative *unsvikunþoza*, unknown, forgotten: *Skeireins* VI, a.

SVI-KUNþABA, adverb, openly, publicly, παῤῥησίᾳ: Mark 8:32; John 11:14; ῥητῶς, expressly: 1 Timothy 4:1; *Skeireins* II, a; VIII, b.

GASVI-KUNþJAN, second conjugation, to make manifest, φανεροῦν: [Col. 1370] Colossians 1:26; 2 Timothy 1:10; φανερὸν ποιεῖν, to make manifest: Mark 3:12; συνιστάναι, to commend: 2 Corinthians 10:18; *Skeireins* II, a; VI, c. Passive: to be manifested, appear, ἀναφαίνεσθαι: Luke 19:11.

GA-KUNDS, feminine, persuasion, πεισμονή: Galatians 5:8; see on this passage.

GA-KUNþS, feminine, manifestation; *uf gakunþai*, “from the manifestation,” ἀρχόμενος, “beginning”: Luke 3:23, on this passage.

KUNþI, neuter, knowledge, learning, γνῶσις: Luke 1:77; 1 Corinthians 8:10; 13:2, 8; 2 Corinthians 2:14; 4:6; 6:6; 8:7; 10:5; 11:6; Ephesians 3:19; Philippians 3:8; ἐπίγνωσις, full knowledge: Romans 10:2; Colossians 1:9; *Skeireins* I, d; IV, b; VI, b.

UN-KUNþI, ignorance, ἀγνωσία: 1 Corinthians 15:34.

UF-KUNþI, knowledge, full knowledge, ἐπίγνωσις: Ephesians 1:17; 4:13; Colossians 1:10; 3:10; 1 Timothy 2:4; 2 Timothy 2:25; 3:7; Titus 1:1.

ANA-KUNNAINS, feminine, reading, recitation, ἀνάγνωσις: 2 Corinthians 3:14.

KANNJAN, second conjugation, to make known, inform, γνωρίζειν: John 17:26; 1 Corinthians 15:1; 2 Corinthians 8:1; Ephesians 1:9; *Skeireins* IV, b.

GA-KANNJAN: 1. the same, γνωρίζειν: Luke 2:15; John 15:15; 17:26; Romans 9:23; Ephesians 3:3, 10; 6:19, 21; Colossians 1:27; 4:7, 9; *Skeireins* IV, d; διαγνωρίζειν, to make fully known: Luke 2:17; καταγγέλλειν, to proclaim: 1 Corinthians 11:26; δηλοῦν, to make clear: Colossians 1:8. 2. to commend, συνίστασθαι: 2 Corinthians 12:11.

US-KANNJAN: 1. to make known, inform, γνωρίζειν: Romans 9:22. 2. to commend, συνιστάναι: 2 Corinthians 5:12.

KUNþS, see under *Kunnan*.

KUSA, masculine proper noun, Χουζᾶ: Luke 8:3.

KUSTANTEINUS, masculine proper noun: Gothic calendar.

KUSTUS, see under *Kiusan*.

KREKS, masculine proper noun; plural *krekos*, Greek, Ἕλλην: Romans 10:12; 1 Corinthians 1:22; Galatians 2:3; 3:28; Colossians 3:11.

KRESKUS, masculine proper noun, Κρήσκης: 2 Timothy 4:10.

KRETA, feminine proper noun, Κρήτη: Titus 1:5.

KRETES, plural proper noun, Κρῆτες: Titus 1:12.

KRIUSTAN (compare English *crash*; Gr. II, 22), first conjugation, *kraust, krustun, krustans*, to gnash, τρίζειν: Mark 9:18.

KRUSTS, feminine, gnashing, βρυγμός: Matthew 8:12.

KRISPUS, masculine proper noun, Κρίσπος: 1 Corinthians 1:14; 2 Timothy 4:10.

*KROTON* (Old High German *chrazon*, English *crush*, Swedish *krossa*; Greek κροτεῖν; Gr. II, 43), second conjugation, to break in pieces, crush.

GA-KROTON, the same, συνθλᾶν: Luke 20:18.

KYREINAIUS, masculine proper noun, Κυρηναῖος: Mark 15:21; Luke 2:2.

KONS, the same as *kuns*; see under *Kuni*.

KOSAM, masculine proper noun, Κωσάμ: Luke 3:28.

[Col. 1369] **LAGGS** (Old Norse *langr*, Anglo-Saxon, Old Saxon, Old High German, Danish, Old Frisian, Dutch, Modern High German *lang*, English *long*, Swedish *lång*; Latin *longus*; Gf. II, 225), adjective, long, used only of time: *mela lagga*, for a long time (long since), “for a considerable time,” Luke VIII.27; *laggai weilai*, a long time, “for a time,” Luke XVIII.4; *sva lagga sve*, as long as, “inasmuch as,” Romans XI.13; *sva lagga weila sve*, as long as, “for as long a time as,” Mark II.19; *wan lagg mel*, how long, “how long a time,” Mark IX.21.

**LAGGA-MODEI**, see under *Mods*.

**LAGGEI**, feminine, length, “length,” Ephesians III.18.

**LAGEINS**, see under *Ligan*.

**LAGJAN**, see under *Ligan*.

II, 164; Rchth. 885), second conjugation, to call, summon: Matthew IX.13; Mark II.17; Luke V.32; Romans IX.11, 24; 1 Corinthians VII.15, 20; X.27; Galatians I.6; V.8, 13; Ephesians IV.1; Colossians I.12; III.15; 1 Thessalonians II.12; IV.7; V.24; 1 Timothy VI.12; 2 Timothy I.9.

**LAIAN** (Old Norse *lâ*, Old Saxon and Old High German *lahan*, Anglo-Saxon *lean*; Gf. II, 97 [IV, 687 Grimm rejects the infinitive *laian*, substituting either *lean* or *lehan*; but *laian* is referred to *lailoun* as an infinitive in the same way that *saian* and *vaian* are referred to *saisoun* and *vaivoun*. If, because of Old Saxon and Old High German *lahan*, *lehan* were to be regarded as the infinitive—which again seems by no means necessary—it would have to be said that at John IX.28 *lailoun* is an error for *lailohun*.
