II, 7; *Skeir.* VIII, c. **UN-LIUGANDS**, present participle, not lying, truthful, ἀψευδής: Tit. I, 2. **GA-LIUGS**, adjective, false; **galiug taujan**, to make false, to adulterate, δολοῦν: II Cor. IV, 2. **GA-LIUG**, neuter, idol, εἴδωλον: I Cor. X, 19, 28; II Cor. VI, 16; **galiuge staþs**, idol-temple, εἰδωλεῖον: I Cor. VIII, 10; **galiugam skalkinonds**, idolater, εἰδωλολάτρης: I Cor. V, 10, 11. **GA-LIUGA-APAUSTAULUS**, see under *Apaustaulus*. **GA-LIUGA-BROÞAR**, see under *Broþar*. **GA-LIUGA-PRAUFETUS**, see under *Praufetus*. **GA-LIUGA-XRISTUS**, see under *Xristus*. **LIUGN**, neuter (?), lie, falsehood, ψεῦδος: John VIII, 44; Eph. IV, 25; *Skeir.* I, c. **LIUGNA-VAURDS**, see under *Vaurds*. **LIUGNJA**, masculine, liar, ψεύστης: John VIII, 44, 55; I Tim. I, 10; Tit. I, 12.

**LAUGNJAN**, conjugation II, to lie, ἀρνεῖσθαι, to deny: Matt. XXVI, 70; Mark XIV, 70; Luke VIII, 45. **GA-LAUGNJAN**, 1) to hide, περικρύβειν: Luke I, 24; 2) to be hidden, λανθάνειν: Mark VII, 24; Luke VIII, 47. **ANA-LAUGNS**, adjective, hidden, κρυπτός: Mark IV, 22; Luke VIII, 17; I Cor. IV, 5; XIV, 25; II Cor. IV, 2. **ANA-LAUGNIBA**, adverb, secretly, ἐν κρυπτῷ: John VII, 10. **ANA-LAUGNEI**, feminine, a hidden thing, κρυπτόν: John VII, 4.

**LIUDAN** (Old Danish *liutan*, Old Saxon *liodan*; Gr. II, 21; Gf. II, 198), conjugation I, *lauþ, ludun, ludans*, to become great, grow, μηκύνεσθαι: Mark IV, 27.

* **LAUÞS** (Old Norse *lyd, liod*, Anglo-Saxon *leod*, Old Saxon *liud*, Old High German *liut*, Old Frisian *liode, liude*, English *leod*, Modern High German *Leute*; Gr. III, 472; DRA. 305; Gf. II, 193; Rchth. 902), masculine, man. **JUGGA-LAUÞS**, young man, νεανίσκος: Mark XIV, 51; XVI, 5; Luke VII, 14.

* **LIUHAN** (Old Norse *lysa, lios, lioma*, Anglo-Saxon *leoht, lyhtan, leoma*, Old Saxon *lioht, liomo, logna*, Old Frisian *liaht*, Old High German *lioht*, English *light*, Swedish *ljus, lysna*, Danish *lys*, Modern High German *Lohe, Licht, leuchten*; Bopp 129; Gr. II, 50; III, 391; DM. 121; Gf. II, [Col. 1381] 146; Rchth. 897), conjugation I, *lauh, lauhun, lauhans*, to shine. **LIUHAÞ** (*Liuhad*, Luke VIII, 16; John XI, 10, 12, 46), neuter, light, brightness, φῶς: Matt. V, 16; VI, 23; X, 27; Mark XIV, 54; Luke II, 32; VIII, 16; XVI, 8; John V, 35; VIII, 12; IX, 5; XI, 9, 10; XII, 35, 36, 46; Rom. XIII, 12; II Cor. IV, 6, 6, 14; XI, 14; Eph. V, 8; Col. I, 12; I Thess. V, 5; I Tim. VI, 16; φέγγος, light: Mark XIII, 24. **LIUHADEI**, feminine, light, brightness, illumination, φωτισμός: II Cor. IV, 4, 6. **LIUHADEINS**, adjective, bright, φωτεινός: Matt. VI, 22. **LIUHTJAN** (*Liutjan*, Matt. V, 15), conjugation II, to shine, λάμπειν: Matt. V, 15, 16; II Cor. IV, 6; αὐγάζειν, to shine forth: II Cor. IV, 4; φαίνειν, to shine: John V, 35. **GA-LIUHTJAN**, 1) to illuminate, φωτίζειν: I Cor. IV, 5; II Tim. I, 10; 2) to make evident, make clear, φανεροῦν: I Cor. IV, 5. **IN-LIUHTJAN**, to illuminate, φωτίζειν: Eph. I, 18; III, 9. **LAUHATJAN**, conjugation II, to flash, ἀστράπτειν: Luke XVII, 24. **LAUHMUNI** (*Lauhmoni*, Luke XVII, 24; II Thess. I, 8), feminine, lightning, ἀστραπή: Luke X, 18; XVII, 24; φλόξ, flame: II Thess. I, 8; see on this passage.

**LIUÞON** (Old Norse *lioþ*, Anglo-Saxon *leoð*, Old High German *liod*, English *lay*, Swedish *ljuda, lyda*, Danish *lyde*, Dutch and Modern High German *Lied*; Gf. II, 198), conjugation II, to sing, ψάλλειν: Rom. XV, 9. **LIUÞAREIS**, masculine, singer, ὁ ᾄδων: Ezra II, 41; Neh. VII, 1.

* **LIUSAN** (Old Norse *liosa, laus*, Old Saxon *losian, liosan, los, lari*, Anglo-Saxon *leosan, losian, leas*, Old Frisian *lesa, liasa, las*, Old High German *liusan*, English *leese, loose*, Swedish *förlora, lösa*, Danish *løs*, Modern High German *verlieren, Verlust, los*; Greek λύειν; Gr. II, 22; Gf. II, 262; Rchth. 884, 893, 898), conjugation I, *laus, lusun, lusans*, to lose, destroy. **FRA-LIUSAN**, the same, ἀπολλύναι: Luke XV, 4, 6, 8, 9, 24, 32; XIX, 10; John VI, 27. **FRA-LUSNAN**, conjugation III, to be lost, perish, ἀπόλλυσθαι: I Cor. I, 18; II Cor. II, 15, this passage; IV, 3. **FRA-LUSTS**, feminine, destruction, ἀπώλεια: Matt. VII, 13; John XVII, 12; Rom. IX, 22; Phil. I, 28; III, 19; II Thess. II, 3; I Tim. VI, 9; ὄλεθρος, destruction: I Thess. V, 3; II Thess. I, 9.

**LAUS**, adjective, empty, vain, κενός: Luke I, 53; XX, 10; I Cor. XV, 14, 58; Eph. V, 6; Phil. II, 3; **laus vairþan**, to become empty, vain, κενοῦσθαι: II Cor. IX, 3; **laus visan**, to be made void, καταργηθῆναι: Gal. V, 4; **vitodis laus**, without law, ἄνομος: I Cor. IX, 21. **AKRANA-LAUS**, fruitless, ἄκαρπος: Mark IV, 19. **ANDI-LAUS**, endless, ἀπέραντος: I Tim. I, 4. **GUDA-LAUS**, impious, without God, ἄθεος: Eph. II, 12. **VITODA-LAUS**, without law, ἄνομος: I Cor. IX, 21; I Tim. I, 9. **LAUS-QIÞRS**, see under *Qiþus*. **LAUS-HANDJA**, see under *Handus*. **LAUSA-VAURDS**, see under *Vaurd*.

**LAUSJAN**, conjugation II, 1) to loose, separate, λύειν: I Cor. VII, 15; **sokei lausjan**, “seek a release,” ζήτει λύσιν; 2) to nullify, make void, κενοῦν: I Cor. I, 17; 3) to deliver, ῥύειν: Matt. VI, 13; XXVII, 43; Rom. VII, 24; XI, 26; 4) to exact, πράττειν: Luke III, 13; ἀπαιτεῖν, to demand back: Luke VI, 30. **GA-LAUSJAN**, 1) to break apart, διασπᾶν: Mark V, 4; 2) to free, καταργεῖν: Rom. VII, 2; λύειν: I Cor. VII, 27; 3) to deliver, rescue, ῥύειν: Luke I, 74; II Cor. I, 10; Col. I, 13; II Tim. III, 11; *Skeir.* I, b, c; 4) to preserve, φυλάττειν: II Thess. III, 3; 5) to exact, πράττειν: Luke XIX, 23. **US-LAUSJAN**, 1) to empty, κενοῦν: Phil. II, 7; 2) to deliver, ῥύειν: II Thess. III, 2; ἐξαιρεῖσθαι, to rescue: Gal. I, 4; 3) to uproot; **uslausjan us vaurtim**, to uproot, ἐκριζοῦν: Luke XVII, 6.

[Col. 1382] **US-LAUSEINS**, feminine, redemption, λύτρωσις: Luke I, 68; ἀπολύτρωσις: Eph. IV, 30.

* **LIUTAN** (Anglo-Saxon *lytig, lutan*, Old High German *luzen*; Gf. II, 322), conjugation I, *laut, lutun, lutans*, to flatter, deceive. **LIUTS**, adjective, pretender, γόης, impostor: II Tim. III, 13. **UN-LIUTS**, without deceit, sincere, ἀνυπόκριτος: Rom. XII, 9; II Tim. I, 5. **LIUTA**, masculine, hypocrite, flatterer, ὑποκριτής: Matt. VI, 2, 5, 16; Mark VII, 6; Luke VI, 42. **LIUTEI**, feminine, craftiness, deceit, hypocrisy, ὑπόκρισις: Mark XII, 15; I Tim. IV, 2; κυβεία, trickery: Eph. IV, 14; see on this passage; δόλος, deceit: Mark VII, 22; **us liutein taiknjan sik**, to present oneself deceptively, ὑποκρίνεσθαι ἑαυτόν: Luke XX, 20.

**LUTON**, conjugation II, to deceive. **LUTONDS**, participle used substantively, deceiver, φρεναπάτης: Tit. I, 10. **US-LUTON**, to deceive, ἀπατᾶν: Eph. V, 6; see on this passage; I Tim. II, 14; ἐξαπατᾶν: Rom. VII, 11; II Cor. XI, 3; II Thess. II, 3; φρεναπατᾶν: Gal. VI, 3; *Skeir.* I, b, d.

**LISAN** (Old Norse and Old Frisian *lesa*, Anglo-Saxon, Old Saxon, and Old High German *lesan*, Dutch and Modern High German *lesen*; Greek λέγειν, Latin *legere*; Gr. II, 26; Gf. II, 246; Rchth. 893), conjugation I, *las, lesun, lisans*, to gather, συλλέγειν: Matt. VII, 16; Luke VI, 44; συνάγειν: Matt. VI, 26. **GA-LISAN**, to gather, assemble, συνάγειν: Mark IV, 1; Luke XVII, 37; John VI, 12, 13; XI, 47; XV, 6; Neh. V, 16; ἐπισυνάγειν, to gather together: Mark XIII, 27. **LISTS**, see under *Leisan*. **LITA** (compare *Liutan*; Gf. II, 317), feminine, hypocrisy, ὑπόκρισις: Gal. II, 13. **MIÞ-LITJAN**, conjugation II, to dissemble with, συνυποκρίνεσθαι: Gal. II, 13. **LITEINS** (Greek λιτή), feminine, petition, intercession, ἔντευξις: I Tim. II, 1.

. . . **LIF** (Old Norse . . . *levu*, Anglo-Saxon . . . *lufon*, Old Saxon . . . *liui*, Old Frisian . . . *lif*, . . . *lef*, Old High German . . . *lif*, English . . . *leven*, Swedish . . . *lofva*, Danish . . . *leve*, Modern High German . . . *lf*; Bopp 16; Gf. II, 206), ten, . . . *-teen*. **AIN-LIF**, see under *Ains*. **TVA-LIF**, see under *Tvai*. **LIFNAN**, see under *Leiban*.

* **LUBJA** (Anglo-Saxon *lib*, Old High German *luppi*, Swedish *luf*; Gf. II, 77), feminine (?), poison. **LUBJA-LEISEI**, see under *Leisan*. **LUBS**, see under *Liuban*. **LUDJA** (compare *Liudan*; Gr. III, 401; Gf. II, 201), feminine, face, countenance, πρόσωπον: Matt. VI, 17; compare Gal. IV, 19.

* **LUKAN** (Old Norse *luka, liuka*, Anglo-Saxon and Old Saxon *lucan*, Old Frisian *lukan*, Old High German *luhhan*, English *lock*, Swedish *lycka*, Danish *lukke*, Dutch *luyken*; Gr. II, 22; I, 63 [third edition]; Gf. II, 139; Rchth. 913), conjugation I, *lauk, lukun, lukans*, to shut. **GA-LUKAN**, 1) to shut, κλείειν: Matt. VI, 6; κατακλείειν, to shut up: Luke III, 20; ἀσφαλίζεσθαι, to make secure: Matt. XXVII, 66; 2) to enclose, συγκλείειν: Luke V, 6; Rom. XI, 32. **US-LUKAN**, 1) to open, unclose, ἀνοίγειν: John IX, 14, 17, 21, 26, 30, 32; X, 3, 21; XI, 37; II Cor. II, 12; Col. IV, 3; Neh. VII, 3; διανοίγειν, to open: Luke II, 23; ἀναπτύσσειν, to unroll: Luke IV, 17; 2) to draw out (a sword), σπᾶσθαι: Mark XIV, 47; ἕλκειν, to draw: John XVIII, 10. **GA-LUKNAN**, conjugation III, to be shut, κλείεσθαι: Luke IV, 25. **US-LUKNAN**, to be opened, ἀνοίγεσθαι: Matt. IX, 30; XXVII, 52; Luke I, 64; III, 21; John IX, 10; I Cor. XVI, 9; II Cor. VI, 11; διανοίγεσθαι, to be opened: Mark VII, 34, 35. **US-LUK**, neuter (?), opening, ἄνοιξις: Eph. VI, 19. **US-LUKNS**, adjective, opened, σχιζόμενος: Mark I, 10; this passage. **LUKARN** (Latin *lucerna*; Bopp 129), neuter, lamp, λυχνός: Matt. VI, 22; Mark IV, 21; Luke VIII, 16; XV, 8; John V, 35. **LUKARNA-STAÞA**, see under *Staþs*.

**LUKAS** (*Lokas*; see Prolegomena, col. 476, note 6) [Col. 1383], masculine proper name, Λουκᾶς, Luke: subscription to Luke; Col. IV, 14; II Tim. IV, 11. **LUKIUS**, masculine proper name, Λούκιος, Lucius: Rom. XVI, 21.

**LUSTUS** (Old Norse *lyst, losti*, Old High German, Anglo-Saxon, Old Saxon, Danish *lyst*, Old Frisian, English, Swedish, Dutch, and Modern High German *Lust*; Gr. II, 22; Gf. II, 285; Rchth. 913), masculine, desire, lust, ἐπιθυμία: Mark IV, 19; John VIII, 44; Rom. VII, 7, 8; XIII, 14; Gal. V, 16; Eph. II, 3; IV, 22; Phil. I, 23; Col. III, 5; I Thess. II, 17; IV, 5; I Tim. VI, 9; II Tim. II, 22; III, 6; **us lustum**, willingly, voluntarily, κατὰ ἑκούσιον: Philem. 14. **UN-LUSTUS**, weariness, dejection; **ïn unlustau vairþan**, to become discouraged, ἀθυμεῖν: Col. III, 21. **LUSTUSAMS**, adjective, desired, longed for, ἐπιπόθητος: Phil. IV, 1. **LUSTON**, conjugation II, to desire, ἐπιθυμεῖν: Matt. V, 28.

[Col. 1384] **US-LUSTON**, to deceive, ἀπατᾶν: Eph. V, 6; this passage. **LUTON**, see under *Liutan*. **LUFTUS** (Old Norse *lopt*, Anglo-Saxon *lyft*, Old High German, Old Saxon, Swedish, Danish, and Modern High German *Luft*, Dutch *lucht*; Gr. III, 389; Gf. II, 208), masculine, air, ἀήρ: I Cor. IX, 26; Eph. II, 2; I Thess. IV, 17. **LYDDOMAEIS**, masculine proper name, Λοδαδίδ: Ezra II, 33. **LYSANIUS**, masculine proper name, Λυσάνιος, Lysanias: Luke III, 1. **LYSTRA**, proper name, Λύστρα, Lystra: II Tim. III, 11. **LOD**, masculine proper name, Λώτ, Lot: Luke XVII, 28, 29, 32. **LOS**, feminine, dwelling (?); **los bauan**, to lead a life, βίον διάγειν: I Tim. II, 2; see on this passage. **LOFA** (Gr. III, 404; Gf. II, 205), masculine, a limp hand (French *main morte*); **slahs lofin**, a slap, ῥάπισμα: John XVIII, 22; XIX, 3; **lofam slahan**, to strike with the open hand, ῥαπίζειν: Matt. XXVI, 67; Mark XIV, 65.

M
[Col. 1383] **MAGAN** (Old Norse *mega, mattr*; Anglo-Saxon *magan*; Old Saxon *mag, maht*; Old Frisian *mi, mei*; *macht, mecht*; Old High German *magan, maht*; English *may, might*; Swedish *må*; Danish *maae*; Dutch *meugen*; Modern High German *mögen*; Gr. II, 27; Gf. II, 604; Rchth. 927), anomalous conjugation, *mag, mahta, mahts*, “to be able,” δύνασθαι: Matt. V, 36; VI, 24, 27; VII, 18; VIII, 2; IX, 15, 28; X, 28; Mark I, 40, 45; II, 4, 7, 19; III, 20; IV, 32, 33; V, 3, 4; VI, 5, 19; VII, 15, 24; VIII, 4; IX, 22, 23, 28, 39; X, 26, 38, 39; XIV, 7; Luke I, 20, 22; V, 12, 21, 34; VI, 39, 42; VIII, 19; IX, 40, 50; XIV, 20, 26, 27, 33; XVI, 2, 13; XVIII, 26; XIX, 3; XX, 36; John III, 5; VI, 44, 52, 60, 65; VII, 7, 34; VIII, 21, 43; IX, 33; XI, 37; XII, 39; XIII, 33, 36, 37; XIV, 5, 17; XV, 4, 5; XVI, 12; Rom. VIII, 8; 1 Cor. VII, 21; 2 Cor. I, 4; III, 7; XIII, 8; Eph. III, 4; VI, 11, 13, 16; Phil. III, 21; 1 Thess. III, 9; 1 Tim. VI, 7; 2 Tim. II, 13; *Skeir.* I, a; V, c. “To have strength,” ἰσχύειν: Matt. VIII, 28; Mark IX, 18; Luke VI, 48; VIII, 43; XIV, 29, 30; XVI, 3; XX, 26; Phil. IV, 13. “To have full strength,” ἐξισχύειν: Eph. III, 18. “To know,” εἰδέναι: 1 Tim. III, 5. *mag vairþan*, “it can come to pass,” “it is possible,” δυνατὸν (sc. ἐστί): Rom. XII, 18.

**GA-MAGAN**, “to be able,” ἰσχύειν: Gal. V, 6.

**MAHTS**, adjective, “possible”; *mahts visan*, “to be possible,” δύνασθαι (with an active infinitive for the Greek passive): Mark XIV, 5; John III, 4; X, 35; 1 Tim. V, 25. “To be strong,” ἰσχύειν: Luke VIII, 44; *Skeir.* VI, b.

**MAHTS**, feminine:

1. “Power, strength, capacity,” δύναμις: Matt. VI, 13; Mark V, 30; VI, 14; IX, 1; XII, 24; XIII, 25, 26; XIV, 62; Luke I, 17, 35; IV, 14, 36; V, 17; VI, 19; VIII, 46; IX, 1; X, 19; Rom. VIII, 38; IX, 17; 1 Cor. I, 18, 24; V, 4; XV, 24, 56; 2 Cor. I, 8; IV, 7; VI, 7; VIII, 3; XII, 9; XIII, 4; Eph. I, 19, 21; III, 7, 16, 20; Phil. III, 10; Col. I, 11, 29; 2 Thess. I, 7, 11; 2 Tim. I, 7, 8; III, 5. “Strength,” ἰσχύς: Mark XII, 30, 33; Luke X, 27; 2 Thess. I, 9. “Might,” κράτος: Eph. I, 19; VI, 10; Col. I, 11; *Skeir.* I, b, c; IV, c; V, b; VI, b; VII, a, c; VIII, a.

2. “Mighty act,” δύναμις: Matt. VII, 22; XI, 20; Mark VI, 2, 5; IX, 39; Luke IX, 50; X, 13; XIX, 37; 2 Cor. XII, 12; Gal. III, 5.

**ANA-MAHTS**:

1. “Power”: *Skeir.* I, b.

2. “Injury, violence,” ὕβρις: 2 Cor. XII, 10.

**UN-MAHTS**, “weakness, incapacity,” ἀσθένεια: Matt. VIII, 17; 2 Cor. XII, 5; Gal. IV, 13; see the note on this passage.

**MAHTEIGS**, adjective:

1. “Powerful, strong,” δυνατός: Luke I, 49; XIV, 31, 32; Rom. IX, 22; XI, 23; XIV, 4; 2 Cor. IX, 8; XII, 10; 2 Tim. I, 12; Titus I, 9. “Ruler, potentate,” δυνάστης: Luke I, 52; 1 Tim. VI, 15. “One who is able,” δυνάμενος: Eph. III, 20; 2 Tim. III, 7, 15. *mahteigs visan*, “to be strong, to be able,” δυνατεῖν: 2 Cor. XIII, 3; δύνασθαι: Rom. VIII, 39.

2. “Possible,” δυνατός: Mark IX, 23; X, 27; XIII, 22; Luke XVIII, 27; 2 Cor. X, 4; Gal. IV, 15.

[Col. 1384] **UN-MAHTEIGS**:

1. “Powerless, weak,” ἀσθενής: 1 Cor. IV, 10; IX, 22; Gal. IV, 9. “Weak,” ἀσθενῶν: Rom. XIV, 1, 2; 1 Cor. VIII, 9.

2. “Impossible,” ἀδύνατος: Mark X, 27; Luke XVIII, 27; Rom. VIII, 3. *unmahteigs visan*, “to be impossible,” ἀδυνατεῖν: Luke I, 37.

**ANA-MAHTJAN**, conjugation II, VI, “to employ violence, inflict violence,” βιάζειν: Matt. XI, 12; “to deprive,” ἀποστερεῖν: Mark X, 19; “to extort by false accusation,” συκοφαντεῖν: Luke III, 14; see the note on this passage; “to mistreat outrageously,” ὑβρίζειν: Luke XVIII, 32; “to insult, abuse,” ἐπηρεάζειν: Luke VI, 28; “to wrong,” ἀδικεῖν: 2 Cor. VII, 12.

**MAGDALENE**, proper name, Magdalene, Μαγδαληνή: Matt. XXVII, 56; Mark XVI, 1, 9.

**MAGUS** (Old Norse *mögr, meyda*; Anglo-Saxon *maeg, mago, maegð*; Old Saxon *magu, magath*; Old Frisian *megith, maged*; Old High German *magad*; English *maid*; Modern High German *Magd*; Gr. **MAHAþ**, masculine proper name, Μαάθ: Luke III, 26.

**ÏN-MAIDJAN**, “to change, transform,” μεταμορφοῦν: Mark IX, 2; “to transform,” μετασχηματίζειν: Phil. III, 21; “to change,” ἀλλάττειν: 1 Cor. XV, 51, 52; Gal. IV, 20; *Skeir.* III, b; VI, b.

**MAIHSTUS** (Old Norse *mosk*; Anglo-Saxon *meox*; Old High German, Dutch, and Modern High German *mist*; Gf. II, 882), masculine, “dung,” κοπρία: Luke XIV, 35.

**MAIþMS** (Old Norse *meidm*; Anglo-Saxon *maðm*; Old Saxon *medom*; Gr. II, 16, 508; III, 325, 452; Gf. II, 707), masculine, “gift,” δῶρον: Mark VII, 11.

**MAIL** (Old Norse *melur*; Anglo-Saxon *maal*; Old High German *meil*; English *mole, moil*; Swedish *mål*; Modern High German *Maal*; Latin *macula*; Gr. I, 170 [3rd ed.]; Gf. II, 720), neuter (?), “spot, blemish,” ῥυτίς: Eph. V, 27.

**MAILAIAN**, masculine proper name, Μελεᾶ: Luke III, 31.

**MAILKEIN** (*Mailkeis*, Luke III, 24), masculine proper name, Μελχί: Luke III, 24, 28.

**MAIMBRANA** (Greek word), masculine, “parchment,” μεμβράνα: 2 Tim. IV, 13.

**\*MAINDS**, adjective—

**AF-MAINDS**, “wearied, exhausted,” ἐκλυόμενος: Gal. VI, 9. (Thus Castalio reads; but if he had observed more closely that *mainds* is by no means Gothic, and had been willing or able to compare Old Saxon *mendian* and Old High German *mendjan*, “to rejoice,” he certainly would never have admitted the compound *afmainds*, which could not mean “to rejoice,” since *af* is not a negative preposition, either generally or here in particular, where it is again governed by *ni*. Now, if it had this meaning, it would not fit, since ἐκλυόμενος means “wearied, fatigued [in the service of God].” It is therefore evident that Castalio’s reading is false; ἐκλύειν is rendered *afdaujan* at Matt. IX, 36, and therefore here *afdauïdai* must certainly be written. Moreover, *ni* and *in* are most easily confused in palimpsests, as likewise are *da* and *ma*; compare Rom. VI, 23.)

**\*MAINS** (Old Norse *mein …, minne*; Anglo-Saxon *man, maene, gemaene*; Old Saxon *men*; Old Frisian *mein, mene*; Old High German *gamein*; English *mean*; Swedish *gemen*; Modern High German *gemein, mein …*; DRA. 623, 904; Gf. II, 782; Rchth. 918), adjective, “common.”

**GA-MAINS**:

1. “Common,” κοινός: Titus I, 4; *Skeir.* I, a.

2. “Participant, partner,” συγκοινωνός: Rom. XI, 7; *gamainana briggan*, see under *Briggan*.

3. “Profane, unclean,” κοινός: Mark VII, 2; Rom. XIV, 14.

**GA-MAINJA**, masculine, “participant”; *gamainja visan*, “to share, participate,” κοινωνεῖν: 1 Tim. V, 22.

**GA-MAINJAN**, conjugation II, “to make common”; hence:

1. “To share,” κοινωνεῖν: Rom. XII, 13; Gal. VI, 6; Phil. IV, 15.

2. “To participate,” κοινωνὸν εἶναι: 1 Cor. X, 18; “to share in,” συγκοινωνεῖν: Eph. V, 11.

3. “To defile, render profane,” κοινοῦν: Mark VII, 15, 18, 20.

**GAGA-MAINJAN**, “to defile,” κοινοῦν: Mark VII, 23.

**GA-MAINEI**, feminine, “fellowship, participation,” κοινωνία: 2 Cor. VIII, 4; Gal. II, 9.

**GA-MAINDUþS**, feminine, the same: 1 Cor. X, 16; 2 Cor. VI, 14; IX, 13; Phil. II, 1; III, 10.

**GA-MAINþS**, feminine, “church, assembly,” ἐκκλησία: Neh. V, 13.

**MAIS** (*maizuh*, *Skeir.* VIII, b; Old Norse *meiri*; Anglo-Saxon *mare*; Old Saxon *mer, mest*; Old Frisian *mar, mer, mast*; Old High German *mer*; English *more*; Swedish *mer*; Danish *meer*; Modern High German *mehr*; Greek μείζων; Latin *magis*; Gr. III, 608; Gf. II, 832; Rchth. [Col. 1386] 915 ff.), adverb, “more, rather,” μᾶλλον: Matt. VI, 26, at this passage, 30; X, 25, 28; Mark V, 26; IX, 42, 48; XV, 11; Luke V, 15; VII, 26, 42; XVIII, 39; John XII, 43; XIX, 8; Rom. XI, 12, 24; XIV, 13; 1 Cor. VII, 21; XII, 22; subscription …; 2 Cor. II, 7; III, 8; V, 8; VII, 7; XII, 9; Gal. IV, 9, 27; Eph. IV, 28; V, 4; Phil. I, 23; III, 4; 1 Thess. IV, 1, 10; 1 Tim. I, 4; VI, 2; 2 Tim. III, 4; *Skeir.* I, c; V, c; VII, d; VIII, b. “Much more,” πολλῷ μᾶλλον: Matt. VI, 30. “More,” πλεῖον: Matt. VI, 25; Luke VII, 42. “More abundantly,” περισσσότερον: Luke VII, 26. “Exceedingly,” περισσῶς: Mark XV, 14; Phil. I, 14. “Beyond,” ὑπέρ: 2 Cor. XI, 23. Hence *mais fraþjan*, “to think more highly,” ὑπερφρονεῖν: Rom. XII, 3. *mais þamma* (“more than this”), μᾶλλον περισσσότερον: Mark VII, 36.

**þANA-MAIS**, “still, any more” (in negative or interrogative sentences), ἔτι; and *ni þanamais*, “no longer, not yet,” οὐκέτι, μηκέτι: Mark V, 35; XIV, 63; XV, 5; Luke XVI, 2; see the note on this passage; Rom. XIV, 13; Gal. V, 11. “Henceforth,” τοῦ λοιποῦ: Gal. VI, 17. Also pleonastically *ju þanamais*: Luke XVI, 2; 1 Thess. III, 1; compare Luke XV, 19.

**MAIZA**, comparative adjective, “greater,” μείζων: Matt. XI, 11; Mark XII, 31; Luke VII, 28; John VIII, 53; X, 29; XIII, 16; XIV, 12, 28; XV, 13, 20; XIX, 11; Rom. IX, 12; *Skeir.* III, a. *maizo*, neuter used adverbially, “more,” πλεῖον: Luke IX, 13; “exceedingly beyond,” ὑπὲρ ἐκ περισσοῦ: Eph. III, 20; *Skeir.* VII, c.

**MAISTS**, superlative adjective, “greatest,” μείζων: Mark IV, 32; IX, 34; Luke IX, 46. Substantivally, “the greatest,” μεγιστάς: Mark VI, 21. *maists gudja*, “high priest,” ἀρχιερεύς: John XVIII, 24, 26; XIX, 6.

**MAIST**, adverb, “most, for the most part,” τὸ πλεῖστον: 1 Cor. XIV, 27.

**MAISAULLAM**, masculine proper name, Μεσουλάμ: Neh. VI, 18.

**MAITAN** (Old High German *meizan*; Old Frisian *mete*; Modern High German *Metzger, metzeln, Messer*; Latin *metere*; Gf. II, 911; Rchth. 927), conjugation I, *maimait, maitans*, “to cut,” κόπτειν: Mark XI, 8.

**AF-MAITAN**, “to cut off,” ἀποκόπτειν: Mark IX, 43, 45; John XVIII, 10; “to cut out,” ἐκκόπτειν: Matt. V, 30. *haubiþ afmaitan*, “to behead,” ἀποκεφαλίζειν: Mark VI, 16, 27; Luke IX, 9.

**BI-MAITAN**, “to circumcise,” περιτέμνειν: Luke I, 59; II, 21; John VII, 22; 1 Cor. VII, 18; Gal. II, 3; V, 2, 3; VI, 12, 13.

**UNBI-MAITANS**, passive participle, “uncircumcised,” ἀκροβυστία: Eph. II, 11.

**US-MAITAN**, “to cut down/out,” ἐκκόπτειν: Matt. VII, 19; Luke III, 9; Rom. XI, 22; 2 Cor. XI, 12; “to cut off,” ἀποκόπτειν: Gal. V, 12.

**BI-MAIT**, neuter, “circumcision,” περιτομή: John VII, 22, 23; 1 Cor. VII, 19; Gal. II, 7, 8; V, 6, 11; VI, 15; Eph. II, 11; Phil. III, 3, 5; Col. II, 11; III, 11; IV, 11; Titus I, 10.

**UNBI-MAIT**, “foreskin, uncircumcision,” ἀκροβυστία: Col. II, 13.

**GA-MAITANO**, feminine, “mutilation,” κατατομή: Phil. III, 2.

**MAKEIBIS**, proper name, Μαγεβίς: Ezra II, 30.

**MAKIDONJA** (*Makaidonja*, 2 Cor. II, 13; VII, 5; see the note on this passage; *Makidona*, 2 Cor. VIII, 1; XI, 9; subscription; Phil. IV, 15; 1 Thess. IV, 10; 1 Tim. I, 3; *Makedona*, 1 Tim. I, 3; see the note on this passage), feminine proper name, Macedonia, Μακεδονία: 1 Cor. XVI, 5; 2 Cor. I, 16; II, 13; VII, 5; VIII, 1; XI, 9; subscription (see the note on this passage); Phil. IV, 15; 1 Thess. IV, 10; 1 Tim. I, 3.

**MAKMAS**, proper name, Μαχμάς: Ezra II, 27.

**MALAN** (Old Norse *mala, melja, mylja, miol*; Anglo-Saxon *mylen, melev*; Old Saxon *malan*; Old Frisian *mole*; Old High German *malan, melo, muljan*; English *mill, meal*; Swedish *mala*; Danish *male*; Dutch *molen*; Modern High German *mahlen*; Latin *mola, molere*; Greek μύλη; Gr. II, 9, 54; III, 365; Gf. II, 711; Rchth. 932), conjugation I, *mol, molun, malans*, “to grind,” ἀλήθειν: Luke XVII, 35.

**MALO**, feminine, “moth,” σής (?): Matt. VI, 19, 20.

**MALEILAIEL**, masculine proper name, Μαλελεήλ: Luke III, 37.

**MALKUS**, masculine proper name, Μαλχός: John XVIII, 10.

**MALMA** (Old Norse *malmr*; Anglo-Saxon *mealm*; Old Saxon *melm*; Modern High German *malmem*; compare *Malan*; Gr. III, 379), masculine, “sand,” ἄμμος: Matt. VII, 26; Rom. IX, 27.

**MAN-LEIKA**, see under *Leiks*.

**MANAGS** (Old Norse *mangi*; Anglo-Saxon *manig*; Old Saxon *maneg*; Old Frisian *menie, monich*; Old High German *manag*; English *many*; Swedish *måange*; Danish *mange*; Dutch *menig*; Modern High German *mannig, Menge*; Gr. VII, 28; IX, 8, 23, 25, 33, 36; XI, 7; XXVII, 15; Mark II, 4, 13; III, 9, 20, 32; IV, 1, 36; V, 21, 24, 27, 30, 31; VII, 14, 17; VIII, 1, 2, 6, 34; IX, 14, 15, 17, 25; X, 1, 46; XI, 18; XII, 12, 37; XIV, 43; XV, 8, 11, 15; Luke III, 7, 10; IV, 42; V, 1, 3, 6, 19, 29; VI, 19; VII, 9, 11, 12, 24; VIII, 19, 40, 42, 45; IX, 11, 12, 16, 18, 37, 38; XVIII, 36, 43; XIX, 3, 39; John VI, 1, 22, 24; VII, 12, 15, 20, 31, 32, 40, 42; XII, 9, 12, 17, 29. “People,” λαός: Matt. **MIþ** (*mid ...*, Luke VII, 11; Old Norse *með*, Old Saxon and Anglo-Saxon *mid*, Old French *mith, mit, mei*, Swedish and Danish *med*, Dutch *met*, Old and Modern High German *mit*; Greek *μετά*; Gf. II, 659; Alth. *Präpos.* 110; Rchth. 930), preposition construed with the dative. It almost never indicates a local relation, and never a temporal one; corresponding to Greek *μετά* and *σύν*, it denotes connection and fellowship. It is employed only very rarely for an instrumental relation, that relation being expressed by the bare dative.

I. As a preposition:

1. Local: “through the midst of, in the midst of”: Mark VII, 31, *qam at marein galeilaie miþ tveihnaim markom daikapaulaios*, “he came into the Sea of Galilee through the territory of Decapolis.”

2. It indicates association, companionship, conjunction: “with, among, at”; Greek *σύν* and *μετά*.

   a. Properly:

   α. With verbs of state, such as *visan*, “to be”: Matthew IX, 15, *miþ ïm ïst bruþfaþs*, “the bridegroom is with them”; XXVI, 69, *þu vast miþ ïesua*, “you were with Jesus”; 71; Mark I, 13, *vas miþ diuzam*, “he was with the wild beasts”; II, 19, 26; III, 14; IV, 36; V, 18; VIII, 2; XIV, 67; XVI, 10; Luke V, 34; VI, 3, 4; VIII, 38; XV, 31; John III, 26; VII, 33; IX, 40; XI, 31; XII, 17; XIII, 33; XIV, 9; XV, 27; XVI, 4; XVII, 12, 24; XVIII, 18; Galatians II, 4; Philippians II, 23; II Timothy IV, 11. *Visan* must also be supplied: Matthew XXVII, 54, *hundafaþs jah þai miþ ïmma* (“the centurion and those with him,” sc. “being with him”); Mark I, 36, *simon jah þai miþ ïmma*, “Simon and those with him”; II, 25; V, 40; IX, 8; Luke V, 8; VII, 12; VIII, 1, 45; IX, 32; John XVIII, 26; Galatians I, 2. Further, with *sitan*, “sit,” Mark XIV, 54; *gasitan*, John VI, 3; *standan*, John XVIII, 5; *gastandan*, Luke I, 56; *atstandan*, Luke XX, 1; *anakumbjan*, “recline,” Matthew VIII, 11; Luke V, 29; John XII, 2; *liban*, “live,” Luke II, 36; *bauan*, “dwell,” I Corinthians VII, 12, 13.

   β. With verbs of movement, such as *qiman*, “come,” and its compounds: Mark I, 29; VIII, 38; XIV, 43, 62; John XI, 33; II Corinthians IX, 4; *vairþan*, “come to be,” Luke II, 13; *gaggan*, “go,” and its compounds: Matthew V, 41; Mark X, 46; XI, 11; Luke II, 51; VI, 17; VII, 6; XIV, 31 (Greek *ἐν*); John VI, 66; XVIII, 1, 2; Galatians II, 1; *galeiþan*, “go,” Mark V, 24; VIII, 10; I Corinthians XVI, 4; *miþïnngaleiþan*, John XVIII, 15; *afleiþan*, Mark III, 7; *laistjan*, “follow,” Luke IX, 49; I Thessalonians V, 15; *ïn viga visan*, “be on the way,” Matthew V, 25; *garinnan*, “run together,” Mark XIV, 53.

   b. Metaphorically:

   α. In the sense of furnishing or providing with: Mark XIV, 43, 48, *qiman miþ hairum jah trivam*, “to come with swords and clubs”; John XVIII, 3, *ïddja miþ skeimam jah haizam jah vepnam*, “he went with lanterns, torches, and weapons”; I Corinthians V, 4, *gastauan miþ mahtai fraujins*, “to be gathered with the power of the Lord”; VII, 18, *miþ ... faurafillja galaþoþs varþ was*, “was he called in circumcision?”

   β. Denoting a concomitant state, feeling, action, etc.: Mark III, 3, *ussaiwands ïns miþ moda*, “looking round at them with anger”; IV, 16, *miþ fahedai niman*, “receive with joy”; Luke VIII, 13; Philippians II, 29; Colossians I, 11; Luke X, 17, *miþ fahedai qiþan*, “say with joy”; Mark IX, 24, *miþ tagram qiþan*, “say with tears”; Luke IX, 39, *ahma tahjiþ ïna miþ waþon*, “a spirit seizes him with cries”; Mark X, 30, *andniman miþ vrakom*, “receive with persecutions”; Luke XVII, 20, *ni qimiþ þiudangardi guþs miþ atvitainai*, “the kingdom of God does not come with observation”; II Corinthians VII, 15, *miþ agisa jah reiron andniman*, “receive with fear and trembling”; Ephesians IV, 2, *miþ usbeisnai usþulan*, “bear with longsuffering”; Philippians IV, 6; II Thessalonians III, 12; I Timothy I, 14; II, 15; IV, 3, 4; VI, 6; II Timothy II, 10; *Skeir.* VIII, b.

   γ. To indicate manner and means: Mark I, 27 and Luke IV, 36, *miþ valdufnja anabiudan*, “command with authority” (Greek *κατά* with the accusative and *ἐν*); Mark XIII, 26, *qiman miþ mahtai managai*, “come with great power”; Luke XVII, 15, *miþ stibnai mikilai hauhjan*, “glorify with a loud voice”; II Corinthians VIII, 4, *miþ managai usbloteinai bidjan*, “beg earnestly”; *Skeir.* I, b, *miþ sunjai qiþan*, “speak truthfully”; VIII, c, *miþ baitrein rodjan—miþ balþein ïnsakan*, “speak with bitterness—accuse with boldness.”

   δ. Instrumental: Matthew XXVI, 72, *miþ aiþa svaran*, “swear with an oath”; II Corinthians VIII, 19, *gateviþs miþ anstai*, “chosen by grace”; I Timothy II, 9, *miþ gariudjon jah mahein fetjan sik*, “adorn themselves with proper clothing and modesty.”

3. Being with someone as helper, supporter, provider, or encourager, especially with *visan*, which must sometimes be supplied: Luke I, 28, *frauja miþ þus* (“the Lord [is] with you”); II Thessalonians III, 16; John VIII, 29, *saei sandida mik, miþ mis ïst*, “he who sent me is with me”; XVI, 32, *atta miþ mis ïst*, “the Father is with me”; Philippians IV, 9, *guþ gavairþeis sijai miþ ïzvis*, “the God of peace shall be with you”; John XIV, 16, *parakletus ïst miþ ïzvis*, “the Paraclete is with you”; Luke I, 66, *handus fraujins vas miþ ïmma*, “the hand of the Lord was with him”; Romans XVI, 24, “the grace of the Lord [be] with your spirit”; I Corinthians XVI, 23, “the grace of the Lord [be] with you”; 24; II Corinthians XIII, 13; Galatians VI, 18; Ephesians VI, 23, 24; Colossians IV, 19; I Thessalonians V, 28; II Thessalonians III, 18. With *visan* (“remain”): John XIV, 17, “the Paraclete remains with you”; *vairþan*, II Corinthians XIII, 11, “the God of peace shall be with you.”

4. It denotes association or community, “with.”

   a. With transitives:

   α. Referring to the subject: Matthew IX, 11, *sa laisareis ïzvar miþ motarjam matjiþ*, “your teacher eats with tax collectors”; Mark II, 16; XIV, 14; Luke V, 30; VII, 36; John XIII, 18; Galatians II, 12; Mark IV, 10, *frehun ïna þai bi ïna miþ þaim tvalibim*, “those about him, with the Twelve, asked him”; XV, 7, *þai miþ ïmma drobjandans*, “those who were rioting with him”; XV, 31, *gudjans bilaikandans ïna miþ þaim bokarjam*, “the chief priests, mocking him with the scribes”; Luke XV, 30, *fret þein sves miþ kalkjom*, “he has devoured your property with prostitutes”; I Corinthians XV, 10, *usaivida ansts guþs miþ mis*, “the grace of God with me has not been ineffectual”; XVI, 19, *goleiþ ïzvis priska miþ ïngardjon seinai aikklesjon*, “Prisca, with the church in her house, greets you”; Galatians IV, 30; Ephesians IV, 18; Philippians IV, 3; II Timothy II, 22; *Skeir.* II, a.

   β. Referring to the object: Mark I, 20, *afletandans attan seinana miþ asnjam*, “leaving their father with the hired servants”; VIII, 34, *athaitands þo managein miþ siponjam seinaim*, “having summoned the crowd with his disciples”; XV, 27, *miþ ïesua ushramidedun tvans vaidedjans*, “they crucified two robbers with Jesus”; Luke V, 19, *gasatidedun ïna miþ badja faura ïesua*, “they set him, with the bed, before Jesus”; XIX, 23, *ei miþ vokra galausidedjau þata*, “so that I might have received it with interest”; I Corinthians XVI, 11; II Corinthians I, 21; IV, 14; VIII, 22; Galatians V, 24; Colossians II, 13; III, 9; IV, 9; I Thessalonians III, 13; IV, 14. Compare Mark XV, 23, *gebun ïmma drigkan vein miþ smyrna*, “they gave him wine to drink with myrrh”; II Corinthians I, 1, *pavlus aikklesjon þizai visandein in kaurinþon miþ allaim þaim veiham*, “Paul, to the church which is at Corinth, with all the saints”; II Thessalonians I, 7, *usgildan ïzvis gaþraihanaim ïusila miþ uns*, “to repay you who are afflicted with relief together with us.”

   b. With passives and middles: Mark IX, 4, *ataugiþs varþ ïm helias miþ mose*, “Elijah appeared to them with Moses”; XIV, 7, *vas barabbas miþ þaim drobjandam gabundans*, “Barabbas was bound with the insurgents”; XV, 28, *miþ unsibjam rahniþs vas*, “he was reckoned with transgressors”; Luke II, 5, *urrann ïosef ïn beþlahaim anameljan ... miþ mariïn*, “Joseph went up to Bethlehem to be registered with Mary”; Romans X, 20, *bigitans varþ miþ þaim mik ni gasokjandam*, “I was found by those who did not seek me”; II Corinthians VIII, 19, *gateviþs fram aikklesjon miþ gasinþam uns*, “chosen by the churches as our travelling companion” (*συνέκδημος ἡμῶν*); Ephesians IV, 31, *alla baitrei afvairpaidau af ïzvis miþ allai unselein*, “let all bitterness be put away from you with all malice”; Colossians III, 3, 4; I Thessalonians IV, 17.

   c. With intransitives: John XI, 16, *ei gasviltaima miþ ïmma*, “that we may die with him”; II Corinthians VI, 14, *wo dailo garaihtein miþ ungaraihtein aiþþau wo gamainduþe liuhada miþ riqiza*, “what partnership has righteousness with lawlessness, or what fellowship has light with darkness?” (Greek *καί*, and *πρός* with accusative); II Corinthians XIII, 4 and I Thessalonians V, 10, “live with him”; Galatians IV, 25, *skalkinoþ miþ seinaim barnam*, “she is enslaved with her children.” Likewise with *faginon*, “rejoice,” Luke XV, 6, 9; Romans XII, 15; *sifan*, “mourn,” Romans XV, 10; *bivisan*, “remain,” Luke XV, 29; *gretan*, “greet,” Romans XII, 15.

5. “With, at,” after *haban*, “have”: Mark VIII, 14, *hlaif ni habaidedun miþ sis*, “they had no bread with them”; XIV, 7, *sinteino unledans habaiþ miþ ïzvis*, “you always have the poor with you”; John XII, 8; *niman*, “take,” Galatians II, 1, *ganimands miþ sis teitu*, “taking Titus with him”; *briggan*, “bring,” II Timothy IV, 11, *marku brigg miþ þus*, “bring Mark with you.”

6. Indicating the person toward whom words, fighting, thought, etc. are directed: “about, with, against”: *miton*, Mark IX, 33, *wa miþ ïzvis misso mitodeduþ*, “what were you discussing among yourselves?”; *þagkjan*, Mark VIII, 16; Luke XX, 5, 14; *sik andrinnan*, *Skeir.* III, a; *rodjan*, John IX, 37; Ephesians IV, 25; *birodjan*, John VI, 43; *maþljan*, John XIV, 30; *bilaikan*, Mark XV, 31; *sokjan*, Mark I, 27; IX, 14, 16; John VI, 52; XVI, 19; *sokeins varþ*, John III, 25; *Skeir.* III, b; *garuni gataujan*, Mark III, 16; XV, 1; *staua viljan*, Matthew V, 40; *missaqiss varþ*, John IX, 16; X, 19; *gavairþi haban*, Romans XII, 18; *friaþva haban*, John XIII, 35 (Greek *ἐν*); *gavairþeigs visan*, Mark IX, 50; *sels visan*, Ephesians IV, 32 (Greek *εἰς*).

II. In composition:

1. With verbs: *miþarbaidjan, miþgaggan* (*midïddjedun*, Luke VII, 11), *miþqiþan, miþqiman, miþþiudanon, miþkaurjan, miþlitjan, miþmatjan, miþniman, miþrodjan, miþsokjan, miþsandjan, miþsatjan, miþskalkinon, miþstandan, miþvitan, miþfaginon*; doubly compounded: *miþanakumbjan; miþgaqiujan, miþgadauþnan, miþganavistron, miþgasatjan, miþgasviltan, miþgatimrjan, miþgatiuhan, miþgavisan; miþushramjan, miþuskeinan, miþurreisan, miþurraisjan; miþïnsandjan*; triply compounded: *miþïnngaleiþan*.

2. With participles: *miþfrahunþans; miþgaleikonds*.

3. With substantives: *miþvissei, miþgardavaddjus; miþgaqumþs, miþgasinþa*.

**MIþ-þAN**, see under **þan**.

**MIþ-þANEI**, see under **þan**.

**MIK**, see under **Meina**.

**MIKILS** (Old Norse *mikill*, Anglo-Saxon *mycel*, Old Saxon *mikil*, Old High German *mihil*, Scots *mickle*, English *much*, Swedish *mycken*, Danish *megen*; Greek *μέγας*, Latin *magnus*; Bopp 81; Gr. III, 608; Gf. II, 622), adjective: great, Greek *μέγας*: Matthew V, 19, 35; VII, 27; VIII, 24; XXVII, 46, 50, 60; Mark I, 26; IV, 32, 37, 39; V, 7, 42; X, 42, 43; XIV, 15; XV, 34, 37; XVI, 4; Luke I, 15, 32, 42; II, 9, 10; IV, 25, 38; V, 29; VI, 49; VII, 16; VIII, 28, 37; IX, 48; XIV, 16; XVII, 15; XIX, 37; [Col. 1396] John VI, 18; VII, 37; XI, 43; Romans IX, 2; I Corinthians XVI, 9; II Corinthians XI, 15; I Timothy III, 16; VI, 6; II Timothy II, 20; *Skeir.* VII, a, b. Greek *πολύς* (“much, many”): Matthew VII, 22; Luke V, 29; VI, 17; John VII, 12. *ufarassau mikils*, “exceedingly great,” Greek *ὑπερβάλλων*: Ephesians III, 19. *ufar mikil*, the same, Greek *ὑπερλίαν*: II Corinthians XI, 5.

**MIKIL-þUHTS**, see under **þugkjan**.

**MIKILABA**, adverb: greatly, Greek *μεγάλως*: Philippians IV, 10.

**MIKILDUþS**, feminine: greatness: *Skeir.* IV, b, c.

**MIKILEI**, feminine: magnitude, Greek *μέγεθος*: Ephesians I, 19; majesty, Greek *μεγαλειότης*: Luke IX, 43; mighty deed, Greek *μεγαλεῖον*: Luke I, 49; *Skeir.* IV, d. *mikilein atgiban* (?), “to be marveled at,” Greek *θαυμασθῆναι*: II Thessalonians I, 10; see the note on this passage.

**MIKILJAN**, Class II weak verb: to magnify, celebrate, Greek *μεγαλύνειν*: Luke I, 46; Philippians I, 20. To glorify, Greek *δοξάζειν*: Matthew IX, 8; Mark II, 12; Luke II, 20; IV, 15; V, 25, 26; VII, 16; Romans XI, 13; II Corinthians IX, 13; Galatians I, 24; II Thessalonians III, 1.

**GA-MIKILJAN**, the same, to magnify, Greek *μεγαλύνειν*: Luke I, 58.

**MIKILNAN**, Class III weak verb: to be magnified, Greek *μεγαλυνθῆναι*: II Corinthians X, 15.

**MILDS** (Old Norse *mildr*, Old Saxon *mildi*, Old French *milde*, Old High German *milti*, Anglo-Saxon, English, Swedish, Danish, Dutch, and Modern High German *mild*; compare Greek *μαλακός*, Latin *mollis*; Gf. II, 705; Rchth. 929), adjective: sweet, gentle.

**UN-MILDS**, without natural affection, Greek *ἄστοργος*: II Timothy III, 3.

**FRIAþVA-MILDS**, affectionate, Greek *φιλόστοργος*: Romans XII, 10.

**MILDIþA**, feminine: tenderness, compassion, Greek *σπλάγχνα*: Philippians II, 1.

**MILHMA** (compare Swedish *moln*, Danish *mulm*, Greek *ὀμίχλη*?), masculine: cloud, Greek *νεφέλη*: Mark IX, 7; XIII, 26; XIV, 62; Luke IX, 34; I Corinthians X, 1, 2; I Thessalonians IV, 17.

**MILIþ** (Anglo-Saxon *milisc*, Greek *μέλι*, Latin *mel*; Gr. III, 463), neuter: honey, Greek *μέλι*: Mark I, 6.

**MILITON** (a Latin loanword), Class II weak verb: to serve as a soldier, perform military service, Greek *στρατεύεσθαι*: Luke III, 14.

**MILUKS** (Old Norse *mjǫlk*, Anglo-Saxon *meolc, meoluc*, Old French *melok*, Old High German *miluh*, English *milk*, Swedish *mjölk*, Danish and Dutch *melk*, Modern High German *Milch*; Gr. III, 463; Gf. II, 721; Rchth. 918), anomalous feminine: milk, Greek *γάλα*: I Corinthians IX, 7.

**MIMZ** (compare Castiglione on I Corinthians VIII, 13), neuter: flesh, Greek *κρέας*: I Corinthians VIII, 13.

**MINAN** (Old Norse *minna, muna, mynd*, Anglo-Saxon *mǣnan, manian, munan, mund*, Old French *mena, monia*, Old Saxon *manon, menian, munan*, Old High German *meinjan, mundjan*, English *mean, mind*, Swedish *mena*, Danish *monne, minde*, Dutch *meenen*, Modern High German *meinen, mahnen*; Greek *μέμονα*, Latin *memini, mens*; Bopp 120; Gr. II, 30; Gf. II, 785, 815; Rchth. 918, 934), Class I weak verb: *man, munun, munans*, “to think, suppose.”

**GA-MINþI**, neuter: remembrance, Greek *μνεία*: I Thessalonians III, 6; II Timothy I, 3; Gothic Calendar.

**ANA-MINDS**, feminine: suspicion, Greek *ὑπόνοια*: I Timothy VI, 4.

**MUNAN**, anomalous verb: *man, munda, munds*, “to think, suppose, believe”; Greek *δοκεῖν*: Luke XVII, 9; John XIII, 29; I Corinthians IV, 9; II Corinthians XI, 16. Greek *ἡγεῖσθαι* (“to consider”): II Corinthians IX, 5; Philippians II, 3, 25. Greek *νομίζειν* (“to suppose”): Luke III, 23; I Corinthians VII, 26. Greek *λογίζεσθαι* (“to reckon”): Romans XIV, 14; II Corinthians X, 2; XI, 5; XII, 6; Philippians III, 13. Greek *οἴεσθαι* (“to think”): Philippians I, 16; *Skeir.* II, b.

**GA-MUNAN**, anomalous verb: to remember, call to mind, Greek *μιμνήσκεσθαι*: Matthew V, 23; XXVI, 75; XXVII, 63; Luke I, 54, 72; John XII, 16; I Corinthians XI, 2; II Timothy I, 4. Greek *ἀναμιμνήσκεσθαι* (“to remember”): Mark XI, 21; XIV, 72; II Corinthians VII, 15. Greek *μεμνῆσθαι* (“to remember”): II Timothy I, 4. Greek *μνημονεύειν* (“to remember”): Mark VIII, 18; Luke XVII, 32; John XV, 20; XVI, 4, 21; Galatians II, 10; Ephesians II, 11; Colossians IV, 19; II Timothy II, 8. Greek *κατέχειν* (“hold fast”): I Corinthians XV, 2.

**MUNAN**, Class II weak verb: to plan, intend, Greek *βουλεύεσθαι*: John XII, 10; *Skeir.* III, c. Greek *μέλλειν* (“be about to”): Luke X, 1; XIX, 4; John VI, 15; XIV, 22.

**MUNS**, masculine (plural *muneis*):

1. Thought, Greek *νόημα*: II Corinthians II, 11.

2. Purpose, will, Greek *πρόθεσις*: Romans IX, 11; Ephesians III, 11; II Timothy III, 10. Greek *προθυμία* (“readiness, willingness”): [Col. 1397] II Corinthians VIII, 11. Greek *βουλή* (“purpose, counsel”): Ephesians I, 11.

3. Care, Greek *πρόνοια*: Romans XIII, 14.

**GA-MUNDS**, feminine:

1. Remembrance, thought, Greek *μνημόσυνον*: Mark XIV, 9; Greek *ἀνάμνησις*: I Corinthians XI, 24, 25; Greek *μνεία*: Ephesians I, 16.

2. Conscience, Greek *συνείδησις*: I Timothy I, 5; see the note on this passage.

**UF-MUNNAN**, Class II weak verb: to think of, remember: Philippians II, 28; see the note on this passage.

**UFAR-MUNNON**, Class II weak verb:

1. To forget, Greek *ἐπιλανθάνεσθαι*: Mark VIII, 14; Philippians III, 14.

2. To forget, Greek *παραβουλεύεσθαι*: Philippians II, 30.

**MINS** (*Minz*, II Corinthians XII, 15; compare Old Norse *minni*, Anglo-Saxon *minsian*, Old Saxon and Old French *min*, Old High German *min, miniro*, English *mince*, Swedish and Danish *mindre*, Dutch and Modern High German *minder*; Greek *μείων*, Latin *minus*; Gr. III, 611; Gf. II, 798; Rchth. 929), adverb: less, Greek *ἧττον*: II Corinthians XII, 15; Greek *ἔλαττον*: I Timothy V, 9. *mins haban*, “to have less, be in need,” Greek *ὑστερεῖν*: II Corinthians XII, 11.

**MINNIZA**, comparative adjective: lesser, Greek *μικρότερος*: Matthew XI, 11; Mark XV, 40; Luke VII, 28; *Skeir.* III, d. *minnizo gataujan*, “to lack, be deficient,” Greek *ὑστερεῖν*: II Corinthians XI, 5.

**MINNISTS**, superlative adjective: least, Greek *ἐλάχιστος*: Matthew V, 19; I Corinthians IV, 3. Greek *ἔσχατος* (“last”): Matthew V, 26; see the note on this passage. Greek *μικρός* (“small”): Matthew X, 42. Greek *μικρότερος* (“least”): Mark IV, 31; Luke IX, 48.

**MINZNAN**, Class III weak verb: to become less, decrease, Greek *ἐλαττοῦσθαι*: John III, 30.

**MIS**, see under **Meina**.

**MISS** (Old Norse, Anglo-Saxon, Old French, English, Danish, Dutch *mis*, Old High German *mis, missi*, Swedish and Modern High German *miss*; Gr. II, 470; Gf. II, 862; Rchth. 930), adverb: badly, wrongly.

**MISSA-DEDS**, see under **Deds**.

**MISSA-QISS**, see under **Qiþan**.

**MISSA-LEIKS**, see under **Leiks**.

**MISSA-TAUJANDS**, see under **Taujan**.

**MISSO** (Gr. II, 470), adverb: mutually, one another, Greek *ἀλλήλων*: Romans XIII, 8; Galatians V, 26. Regularly with a personal pronoun, Greek *ἀλλήλων*: Mark I, 27; IV, 41; VIII, 16; IX, 10, 33, 34, 50; X, 26; XI, 31; XII, 6; XV, 31; XVI, 3; Luke II, 15; IV, 36; VI, 11; VII, 32; VIII, 25; XX, 5, 14; John VI, 43, 52; VII, 35; XII, 19; XIII, 14, 22, 34, 35; XV, 12, 17; XVI, 17, 19; Romans XII, 10, 16; XIV, 13, 19; XV, 5, 7; I Corinthians VII, 5; XVI, 20; II Corinthians XIII, 12; Galatians V, 13, 15, 17; Ephesians IV, 2, 32; V, 21; Colossians III, 9, 13; I Thessalonians III, 12; IV, 9, 18; V, 11; II Thessalonians I, 3; *Skeir.* III, a. Greek *ἑαυτούς* (“themselves”): Mark I, 27; IX, 10; X, 26; XI, 31; XVI, 3; John VII, 35. With a possessive pronoun, Greek *ἀλλήλων*: Galatians VI, 2.

**MITAN** (Old Norse *meta, mat*, Anglo-Saxon and Old Saxon *metan*, Old French *meta*, Old High German *mezan*, English *mete*, Swedish *mäta*, Dutch *meten*, Modern High German *messen, Mass*; Greek *μέτρον*, Latin *metiri, meditari*; Gr. II, 25; Gf. II, 891; Rchth. 926), Class I weak verb: *mat, metun* (*meitun*, II Corinthians I, 12; see the note on this passage), “to measure,” Greek *μετρεῖν*: Mark IV, 24; Luke VI, 38; II Corinthians X, 12. Greek *ἀντιμετρεῖν* (“measure in return”): Luke VI, 38.

**GA-MITAN**, the same, Greek *μερίζειν* (? *μετρεῖν*): II Corinthians X, 13.

**US-MITAN**:

1. To conduct oneself, Greek *ἀναστρέφεσθαι*: II Corinthians I, 12; Ephesians II, 3; I Timothy III, 15.

2. To live as a citizen, Greek *πολιτεύεσθαι*: Philippians I, 27. *usviss usmitan*, “to deviate,” Greek *ἀστοχεῖν*: II Timothy II, 18.

**US-MET**, neuter:

1. Conduct, Greek *ἀναστροφή*: Ephesians IV, 22; I Timothy IV, 12; *Skeir.* I, d.

2. Citizenship, Greek *πολιτεία*: Ephesians II, 12.

3. Manner of life, Greek *ἀγωγή*: II Timothy III, 10.

**MITAþS** (*Mitads*, Luke VI, 38), anomalous feminine:

1. Measure, Greek *μέτρον*: Mark IV, 24; Luke VI, 38; Romans XII, 3; II Corinthians X, 13; Ephesians IV, 7, 13, 16.

2. A measure of grain, Greek *κόρος*: Luke XVI, 7.

**MITADJO**, feminine: measure, Greek *μέτρον*: Luke VI, 38.

**MITON**, Class II weak verb: to think, consider, Greek *ἐνθυμεῖσθαι*: Matthew IX, 4; Greek *βουλεύεσθαι*: II Corinthians I, 17; Greek *λογίζεσθαι*: I Corinthians XIII, 5, 11; Philippians IV, 8; Greek *διαλογίζεσθαι*: Mark II, 8; IX, 33; Greek *φρονεῖν*: Romans VIII, 5; Greek *σκοπεῖν*: Philippians II, 4.

**UFAR-MITON**, to cause to forget: *Skeir.* III, c.

[Col. 1398]

**MITONS**, feminine: thought, Greek *ἐνθύμησις*: Matthew IX, 4; Greek *λογισμός*: II Corinthians X, 5; Greek *διαλογισμός*: Mark VII, 21; Luke II, 35; V, 22; VI, 8; IX, 46, 47; Romans XIV, 1.

**GA-MITONS**, the same, Greek *διάνοια*: Ephesians II, 3.

**MUKS** (Old Norse *mjúkr*, English *meek*, Swedish *mjuk*), adjective: meek, gentle.

**MUKA-MODEI**, see under **Mods**.

**NI** (Old Norse *ne, nei*, Anglo-Saxon *ne, na*, Old Saxon *ne, ni*, Old French *ne, ni, na*, Old High German *ni*, English *no, not*, Swedish, Danish *nei*, Modern High German *nein, nicht*; Greek *nē . . .*, Latin *ne*; compare **Ne**; Gf. II, 969; Rchth. 943).

1) The simple particle of negation, “not,” used either positively (*ou*) or hypothetically (*mē*).

a) As regards its construction, it is regularly placed immediately before the word which it governs. Hence:

aa) where the clause is negative, it stands before the verb:

α) with a simple verb:

αα) prohibitively,

[Col. 1402] with the imperative or subjunctive, “do not”: Matt. V, 17 *ni hugjaiþ*, “do not think”; 42 *ni usvandjais*, “do not turn away”; VI, 2 *ni haurnjais*, “do not sound a trumpet”; 3 *ni viti*, “do not let [it] know”; 6 *ni galeikoþ*, “do not be like”; 13, 16, 19, 25, 31; VII, 19; X, 26, 28, 31; Mark V, 7, 36; VI, 9; IX, 39; X, 9, 14, 19; XIII, 21; XVI, 6; Luke I, 13, 30; II, 10; V, 10; VI, 29, 30, 37; VII, 6; VIII, 28, 49, 50, 52; IX, 50; X, 7, 20; XVII, 31; XVIII, 16, 20; John VI, 20, 43; XII, 15; XIV, 1, 27; Rom. X, 6; XI, 18, 20; XII, 2, 14, 21; XIII, 14; XIV, 3, 16; I Cor. V, 9; VII, 13, 18, 21, 23, 27; X, 28; XV, 33, 34; XVI, 11; II Cor. VI, 14, 17; Gal. V, 1, 26; VI, 7, 9; Eph. IV, 30; V, 7, 11; Col. II, 21; III, 8, 9, 19, 21; I Thess. V, 6, 19, 20; II Thess. III, 14; I Tim. IV, 14; V, 1, 19; Neh. VII, 3; with the future, “you shall not”: Matt. V, 21 *ni maurþrjais*, “you shall not murder”; 27, 33; VI, 5; Luke IV, 12; Rom. VII, 7; I Cor. IX, 9.

It is separated from its verb only by words on which emphasis falls, as Rom. XIV, 15 *ni nunu mata þeinamma jainamma fraqistjais*, “do not now destroy that man by your food”; 20 *ni nunu ïn matis gatair vaurstv guþs*, “do not now destroy the work of God for the sake of food.”
