[Col. 1419] **UNTE** (Old Norse *unz*, Old Saxon *unti*, Old High German *unt*; compare *Und*; Gf. I, 363), a particle always placed at the beginning of a clause (except in expressions such as *ni unte*, οὐχ ὅτι, “not that,” 2 Cor. 7:9).

1) Temporal particle:

a) “Until,” ἕως, ἕως ἄν: Matt. 5:18, 26; 10:23; Mark 6:10; 9:1, 12, 36; 14:54; Luke 9:27; 15:4; 17:8; 19:13; 20:43; 1 Cor. 4:5; 1 Tim. 4:13; ἕως ὅτου: Luke 15:8; John 9:18; ἕως οὖ: John 13:38; ἄχρις οὗ: 1 Cor. 11:26; Gal. 4:19; μέχρι: Eph. 4:13.

b) “Until,” ἕως: John 9:4; ἐφ᾽ ὅσον: Matt. 9:15; Luke 5:34 (? ἐν ᾧ).

Causal:

a) “For,” γάρ: Matt. 6:14, 24; 7:25; 9:16, 24; 25:42; Mark 1:22, 38; 4:25; 5:8, 28; 6:20; 7:27; 8:38; 9:31, 40; 10:14; 13:22; Luke 2:10; 6:23; 7:5, 6; 8:18, 29, 52; 9:44, 48, 50, 55; 18:16; John 7:39; 8:42 (10:26); 16:7, 14; Rom. 7:7, 8, 11, 15, 18, 19, 21; 8:2, 3, 5, 7; 9:19; 13:1, 4, 6, 8, 11; 1 Cor. 1:18; 9:2; 11:6, 23; 15:22, 32; 16:10; 2 Cor. 1:8, 12, 13, 19, 24; 2:2, 11, 17; 3:6, 14; 4:17, 18; 5:2, 7, 10, 13, 14, 21; 6:14, 16; 7:8; 8:9, 10; 9:2, 7; 10:4, 12, 14, 18; 11:2, 9, 13, 14, 19; 12:6, 9, 10, 11, 14, 20; Gal. 2:8, 12, 18, 19, 21; 3:28; 4:12, 30; 5:6, 14, 17; 6:9, 14, 17; Eph. 2:8; Phil. 1:19; 3:18; 4:11; Col. 3:3, 20, 24; 1 Thess. 4:9, 14; 5:2, 5, 6; 2 Tim. 1:7, 12; 2:16; 3:9; 4:10, 11; καὶ γάρ, “for indeed”: 2 Cor. 3:10.

b) “Because,” “that,” ὅτι: Matt. 5:8, 34, 35, 36, 45; 6:5, 13; 7:13; 9:36; Mark 1:34; 3:30; 4:29, 41; 5:9; 6:17; 7:19; 8:2, 16, 17, 33; 9:11, 38, 41; 11:18; Luke 1:37, 48, 49, 58, 68; 4:6, 32, 41, 44; 5:8; 6:19, 20, 21, 24, 25, 35; 7:47; 8:31, 37, 41; 9:12, 49, 53; 10:13, 21; 14:11, 14, 17; 15:9, 24, 27, 32; 16:8, 15; 17:9, 10; 18:11, 14; 19:3, 4, 17, 21; John 6:2, 38, 41; 7:1, 7, 8, 23, 29, 30, 39; 8:14, 16, 20, 29, 37, 43, 44, 47; 9:22; 10:4, 5, 13, 17 (26), 36; 11:9, 10, 15, 41; 12:6, 11, 18, 39, 49; 14:12, 17, 28; 15:15, 19, 21, 25, 27; 16:3, 4, 6, 16, 21, 27, 32; 17:8, 9, 14, 24; 18:18; 19:7; Rom. 7:21; 9:17, 28, 32; 11:25, 36; 1 Cor. 1:25; 4:9; 10:17; 15:15; 16:7, 17; 2 Cor. 1:5, 8, 14; 2:15; 3:14; 4:6; 5:19; 7:8, 9, 10, 13, 14, 16; 8:3, 17; 9:2, 12; 10:10; 11:7, 10, 11; Gal. 2:11; 4:20, 27; 6:8; Eph. 2:18; 3:3; 4:25; 5:23; 6:12; Phil. 1:20; 2:30; 4:10, 16; Col. 1:16, 19; 1 Thess. 2:13, 14; 3:8; 4:16; 5:9; 2 Thess. 1:3; 3:8; 1 Tim. 1:12, 13; 4:4, 10; 6:2; 2 Tim. 1:16; 3:6; Neh. 7:2; ἐπεί, “since”: Matt. 27:6; Mark 15:42; John 13:29; 1 Cor. 5:10; 2 Cor. 11:18; 13:3; ἐπειδή, “since”: 1 Cor. 1:21, 22; 15:21; Phil. 2:26 (hence *unte raihtis* for ἐπειδήπερ, “since indeed”: Luke 1:1); διότι, “because”: Luke 2:7; Rom. 8:7; 1 Thess. 4:6; 2 Thess. 2:18; καθότι, “insofar as”: Luke 1:7; 19:9; διὰ τό with infinitive: Mark 4:6; 6:5; τοῦ with infinitive: Phil. 3:21; *Skeir.* III, b; V, d; VI, b, d.

**UR**, see under *Us*.

**US** (also, with *s* assimilated to a following *r*, *ur*, 2 Cor. 4:6; see below under II; with epenthetic *u* and *uh*, *uzu* [Gal. 3:2, 5] and *uzuh* [Mark 11:30; Luke 6:45; 20:4; John 6:66]; Old Norse, Old Saxon, Anglo-Saxon, Old French *ut*, Old High German *uz*, Swedish *ut*, Danish *ud*, English *out*, Dutch *uit*, modern High German *aus*; Greek ἔξ, Latin *ex*; Gf. I, 393; Alth. Präp. 62; Rchth. 1117), properly denotes “out of” (*ex*), distinguishing it from *fram* and *af*, which also mean “out of”; it also means “from” (*ab*), a sense shared by both.

I. Preposition construed with the dative.

1) Locally and habitually: “out of,” “from,” ἐκ, ἀπό.

a) After verbs of motion: *qiman*, Mark 1:11 (*stibna us himina*, “a voice out of heaven”); 7:1 (*us ïairusaulymim*, “from Jerusalem”); 9:7 (*us milhmim*, “out of the cloud”); John 6:23; 7:41, 42; 12:28; Neh. 5:17 (*us þiudom*, “from the nations”); *Skeir.* IV, c; *gaqiman*, Luke 5:17; *vairþan*, Luke 3:22; 9:35; *usgaggan*, Matt. 27:53; Mark 1:10 (*us vatin*, “out of the water”); 1:26 (*ut us þamma mann*, “out of the man”); 1:29; 5:2, 8, 30; 6:54; 7:20, 21 (*mitoneis ubilos us hairtin manne*, “evil thoughts out of a human heart”); 7:29; 9:25; 11:19; Luke 4:22 (*vaurda us munþa ïs*, “words from his mouth”); 4:35; 8:2; 9:5; 17:29; John 8:59; 10:39 (*us handum ïze*, “out of their hands”);

[Col. 1420] 2 Cor. 6:17 (*us midumai ïze*, “from their midst”); Eph. 4:29; Col. 3:8; *utgaggan*, Mark 7:15 (*þata utgaggando us mann*, “that which comes out of a person”); *gagaggan*, Luke 8:4; *atgaggan*, Luke 9:54; *galeiþan*, Mark 7:17 (*ïn gard us þizai managein*, “into the house, away from the crowd”); *usleiþan*, 2 Cor. 5:8 (*us þamma leika*, “from the body”); *rinnan*, Matt. 8:28; John 7:38; *urrinnan*, Luke 2:4; Rom. 11:26; hence Luke 1:78, *urruns us hauhiþai*, “a rising from on high”; *faran*, Luke 10:7; hence 2 Cor. 11:25, *usfarþon us skiþa gataujan*, “to make a journey after being shipwrecked”; *atsteigan*, John 6:33, 38, 41, 50; *driusan*, Luke 10:18; *usdriusan*, Gal. 5:4 (*us anstai*, “from grace”); *usstandan*, Mark 11:22; Luke 4:38; especially *us dauþaim*, “from the dead”: Mark 9:9, 10; 12:25; hence *usstass us dauþaim*, “resurrection from the dead”: Luke 20:35; Phil. 3:11; likewise *libains us dauþaim*, “life from the dead”: Rom. 11:15; *urreisan us dauþaim*, “to rise from the dead”: Matt. 27:64; Mark 6:14, 16; Luke 9:7; Rom. 7:4; 1 Cor. 15:12, 20; *us slepa*, “from sleep”: Rom. 13:11. To this group may be referred *usskavjan*, 2 Tim. 2:26 (*us unhulþins vruggon*, “from the devil’s snare”); *skeinan*, 2 Cor. 4:6 (*liuhaþ ur-riqiza*, “light out of darkness”); *lauhatjan*, Luke 17:24 (*lauhmoni us þamma uf himina*, “lightning out of one part of heaven”); *vahsjan*, Col. 2:19 (*us haubida leik*, “the body from the head”).

b) After transitive verbs: *ïnsandjan*, *Skeir.* VI, c (*sunus fram attin ïnsandiþs vas us himina*, “the Son was sent by the Father out of heaven”); *vopjan*, John 12:17 (*lazaru us hlaiva*, “Lazarus out of the tomb”); *urraisjan*, Luke 3:8 (*us stainam barna*, “children out of stones”); especially *us dauþaim*, “from the dead”: Rom. 10:9; Gal. 1:1; Eph. 1:20; Col. 2:12. Likewise, Col. 1:18 elliptically says *frumabaur … us dauþaim*, “firstborn … from the dead,” i.e. “firstborn [of those raised] from the dead.” *ustiuhan*, Rom. 10:7 (*us dauþaim*, “from the dead”); *usvairpan*, Mark 7:26 (*unhulþon us dauhtr*, “a demon out of [her] daughter”); Luke 6:42 (*anza us augin*, “the splinter out of [the] eye”); John 12:42; *dreiban*, John 16:2; *usdreiban*, Mark 5:10; *uskiusan*, Luke 4:29; *afsatjan*, Luke 16:4 (*us fauragaggja*, “from stewardship”); *gavaljan*, Luke 6:13 (*us ïm tvalib*, “twelve from among them”); John 15:19 (*us fairwau*, “out of the world”); *laþon*, Rom. 9:24 (*us ïudaium—us þiudom*, “from Jews and from Gentiles”); *ustaiknjan*, *Skeir.* VIII, d (*ains reike ustaikniþs us þaim fraqiþanam vas*, “one ruler was appointed from among the condemned”); *lausjan*, Rom. 7:24 (*us þamma leika*, “from this body”); *galausjan*, Luke 1:74 (*us handau fijande*, “from the hand of enemies”); 2 Cor. 1:10 (*us dauþum*, “from deaths”); Col. 1:13 (*us valdufnja riqizis*, “from the power of darkness”); 2 Tim. 3:11 (*us allaim vrakom*, “from all persecutions”); *Skeir.* I, b (*us diabaulaus anamahtai*, “from the devil’s power”); *uslausjan*, Luke 17:6 (*uslausei þuk us vaurtim*, “uproot yourself from the roots”); Gal. 1:4 (*us þamma andvairþin aiva ubilin*, “from the present evil age”); *nasjan*, John 12:27 (*us þizai weilai*, “from this hour”); hence *naseins us fijandam*, “salvation from enemies”: Luke 1:71; *niman*, John 16:14 (*us meinamma*, “from what is mine”); *usniman*, John 17:15 (*us þamma fairwau*, “out of the world”); 1 Cor. 15:13 (*us izvis silbam*, “from among yourselves”); Col. 2:14 (*us midumai*, “from the midst”); *usbairan*, Luke 6:45 (*us þiuþeigamma huzda hairtins*, “out of the good treasure of the heart”); *fravilvan*, John 10:28, 29 (*us handau*, “out of [the] hand”); *lisan*, Luke 6:44 (*smakkans us þaurnum*, “figs from thorns”). Similarly, or elliptically, *us aiwatundjai trudanda veinabasja*, “to gather grapes from thorns”; likewise Mark 11:14, *ni þanaseiþs us þus [bagma] manna akran matjai*, “let no one ever again eat fruit from you [tree].” *Sneiþan*, Gal. 6:8, metaphorically “to reap,” *us þamma leika riurein*, “corruption from the flesh”; *maitan*, Mark 11:8 (*astans us bagmam*, “branches from trees”); Rom. 11:24, *us vistai usmaitans þis vilþeis alevabagmis*, is incorrect for *us þamma vistai usmaitans vilþjin alevabagma*, “cut from the natural wild olive tree”; *gadraban*, Mark 15:46 (*hlaiv us staina*, “a tomb out of stone”); *giban*, John 6:31, 32 (*hlaif us himina*, “bread out of heaven”); 2 Tim. 2:7, *gibiþ þus frauja fraþi us allaim*, “may the Lord give you understanding in all things” (ἐν πᾶσιν; probably *ïn* should be read in place of *us*). Likewise, in 2 Cor. 3:9, *und filu mais ufarïst andbahti garaihteins us vulþau*, “by much more does the ministry of righteousness abound in glory,” where the Greek too has ἐν δόξῃ, “in glory”; *atgiban*, John 17:6 (*mannans us fairwau*, “people out of the world”); *andhuljan*, Luke 2:35 (*mitonins us managaim hairtam*, “thoughts from many hearts”).

c) Origin, source, outcome, or stock from which something proceeds: *Skeir.* II, b, *so leikeina us vambai gabaurþs*, “a body born from a womb”; Luke 10:11, *stubju þana gahaftnandan unsis us þizai baurg ïzvarai afhrisjam ïzvis*, “even the dust of your city that clings to us we wipe off against you”; John 6:13, *gabrukos us fimf hlaibam*, “fragments from the five loaves.” Especially after *visan*, “to be”: John 7:52 (*þu us galeilaia ïs*, “you are from Galilee”); Luke 20:4, 5, 6; Rom. 9:5 (*us þaimei xristus ïst*, “from whom Christ is”); Matt. 5:37 (*þata managizo þaim us þamma ubilin ïst*, “what is more than these is from the evil one”); John 8:44 (*us diabaulau*, “from the devil”); 8:47 (*us guþa*, “from God”); 2 Cor. 3:5; 5:18; Phil. 3:9; Rom. 11:36 (*us fraujin*, “from the Lord”); John 7:22 (*us attam*, “from the fathers”); Eph. 2:8 (*us ïzvis*, “from yourselves”); Gal. 5:8 (*us þamma laþondin*, “from the one who calls”); likewise John 10:32,

[Col. 1421] *goda vaurstva ataugida us attin meinamma*, “I have shown you good works from my Father.” Here belongs the formula *us þamma fairwau visan*, “to be of the world”: John 8:23; 15:19; 17:14, 16; 18:36; and *us þizai airþai visan*, “to be of this earth”: *Skeir.* IV, c. Further, after *vairþan*, “to become”: Gal. 4:4, *ïnsandida guþ sunu seinana vaurþanana us qinon*, “God sent his Son, born of a woman”; 1 Tim. 6:4, *us soknim jah vaurdajiukom vairþand neiþa jah maurþra*, “from disputes and quarrels arise envy and strife.” Compare Gal. 4:22, *abraham tvans aihta sununs, ainana us þiujai jah ainana us frijai*, “Abraham had two sons, one from the slave woman and one from the free woman”; and John 7:22, *xristus us fraiva daveidis qimiþ*, “Christ comes from David’s seed.” It occurs in a special sense in John 3:5, *gabairada us vatin jah ahmin*, “born of water and spirit.”

Accordingly, these words must also be supplied: John 11:1, *lazarus af beþanias us haimai marjins*, “Lazarus of Bethany, from the village of Mary”; Luke 8:27, *sums us baurg*, “a certain man from the city”; Mark 3:7, 8, *filu manageins us galeilaian, us ïudaia*, etc., “a great multitude from Galilee, from Judaea,” etc.; *Skeir.* VI, c, *stibna us himina*, “a voice from heaven”; Mark 8:11; 2 Cor. 5:2; 1 Cor. 15:47, *manna us airþai—us himina*, “a man from the earth—from heaven”; Gal. 4:24, *sa [sunus] us þiujai*, “the [son] from the slave woman”; Ezra 2:36, *sunjus us garda ïesuis*, “sons of the house of Jesus”; Luke 1:27; Ezra 2:40, *sunjus kaidmeielis us sunjum odueiïns*, “sons of Kadmiel, of the sons of Hodaviah”; Phil. 3:5, *us knodai ïsraelis, hebraius us hebraium*, “of the tribe of Israel, a Hebrew of Hebrews”; Luke 1:5, *zakarias us afar abijins*, “Zechariah of the division of Abijah”; 2:36, *anna, dauhtar fanuelis us kunja aseris*, “Anna, daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher”; Rom. 9:4, *þai us ïsrael*, “those of Israel”; 2 Cor. 3:1, *anafilhs us ïzvis*, “a recommendation from you”; 4:7, *mahts us unsis*, “power from us”; 5:1; 8:7; 9:2; 11:26. Also to be included here is 2 Cor. 2:16, *dauns us libainai*, “a fragrance from life” (of one who passes out of life).

d) In a partitive sense, with the preceding usages partly recurring: “to be from among,” “to belong to,” where Greek often uses the genitive alone: John 8:23, *jus us þaim dalaþro sijuþ, ïþ ïk us þaim ïupaþro ïm*, “you are from below, but I am from above”; 1 Cor. 12:12, *liþjus allai us leika þamma ainamma visandans*, “all the members being of the one body”; 12:15, 16; Gal. 2:15; Eph. 4:16; Col. 4:9, 11, 12; 2 Tim. 3:6; Matt. 27:48, *ains us ïm*, “one of them”; Mark 9:17; John 16:5, *ainshun us ïzvis*, “none of you”; 17:12; Luke 9:38, *manna us þizai managein*, “a man from the crowd”; Luke 19:39, *sumai fareisaie us þizai managein*, “some Pharisees from the crowd”; John 12:42; 16:17, *qeþun [sumai] us þaim siponjam*, “some of the disciples said.”

e) Where something is said to exist or occur from someone or something: Mark 11:20, *smakkabagms þaursus us vaurtim*, “the fig tree dried up from its roots”; especially after *laisjan*, Luke 5:3 (*us þamma skipa*, “from the boat”), and *meljan*, subscription to Romans (*du rumonim meliþ ïst us kaurinþon*, “written to the Romans from Corinth”); subscription to 1 Corinthians; subscription to 2 Corinthians. Hence Col. 4:16, *þoei ïst us laudeikaion*, “that which is from Laodicea.” Metaphorically, 2 Cor. 2:4, *us managai aglon jah aggviþai hairtins gamelida ïzvis*, “out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote to you.”

2) To mark time: “from,” “since,” ἐκ: John 6:66, *us þamma mela*, “from that time”; 6:64, *us frumistja*, “from the beginning”; *Skeir.* I, c, *us anastodeinai*, “from the beginning”; John 9:1, *us gabaurþai*, “from birth”; Mark 9:21, *us barniskja*, “from childhood” (παιδιόθεν); 2 Tim. 3:15, ἀπὸ βρέφους, “from infancy”; Mark 10:20, *us jundai*, “from youth”; Luke 18:21.

3) In a purely metaphorical respect:

a) It indicates the source, origin, cause, or basis of something: “from,” “by,” ἐκ. Rom. 9:30, *garaihtei us galaubeinai*, “righteousness from faith”; 10:6; 10:5, *garaihtei us vitoda*, “righteousness from the law”; Phil. 3:9; Rom. 10:17, *garaihtei us gahauseinai*, “righteousness from hearing”; Gal. 3:2, *uzu vaurstvam vitodis ahman nemuþ þau uzu gahauseinai galaubeinais*, “did you receive the Spirit from works of the law or from hearing with faith?”; 3:5; 2 Cor. 13:4, *ushramiþs vas us siukein akei libaiþ us mahtai guþs*, “he was crucified from weakness, yet he lives from the power of God”; Rom. 9:32, *garaihts vairþan us vaurstvam—us galaubeinai*, “to become righteous by works—by faith”; Gal. 2:16; Rom. 9:11, *tavidedeina wa þiuþis aiþþau unþiuþis, ei bi gavaleinai muns guþs visai ni us vaurstvam ak us þamma laþondin*, “whether [it was] of the one who acts or of the one who does not act, so that God’s purpose according to election might remain, not from works but from the one who calls”; Gal. 5:5; Eph. 2:9; Phil. 1:16; *Skeir.* VII, c; 2 Cor. 9:7, *warjizuh svasve fauragahugida ni us trigon aiþþau us nauþai*, “each as he has purposed, not out of reluctance or out of compulsion.” The following examples also belong here: 2 Cor. 8:13, *[þata vairþai] us ïbnassau*, “from equality,” that is, “because of equality”; Luke 19:22, *us munþa þeinamma stoja þuk*, “from your own mouth I judge you”; 6:44, *bagms us svesamma akrana uskunþs ïst*, “a tree is known from its own fruit”; likewise Eph. 3:15, *us þammei all fadreinis ïn himina jah ana airþai namnjada*, “from whom every family in heaven and on earth is named”; *stipulans us gaqissai*, “abstaining by agreement,” 1 Cor. 7:5.

b) It is used modally: John 8:41, *us horinassau gabaurans*, “born from fornication”; Mark 12:30, *frijos fraujan us allamma hairtin, jah us allai saivalai jah us allai gahugdai jah us allai mahtai*, “love the Lord with all [your] heart, with all [your] soul, with all [your] mind, and with all [your] strength”; Luke 20:27. Hence also Col. 3:23, *us saivalai vaurkjan*, “work from the soul, wholeheartedly”; 1 Tim. 1:5, *friaþva us hrainjamma hairtin*, “love from a pure heart”; 2 Tim. 2:22, *anahaitan fraujan us hrainjamma hairtin*, “call upon the Lord from a pure heart”; 2 Cor. 2:7, *us hlutriþai—us guþa rodjan*, “speak from sincerity—as from God” (compare the cases cited above under 1, b with *rodjan*); 9:6, *us gaþagkja saian*, “to sow sparingly”; 8:11, *ustiuhan us þammei habaiþ*, “to complete from what you have.”

[Col. 1422]

c) It forms adverbial expressions: 1 Cor. 13:10, 12, *us dailai*, “in part,” ἐκ μέρους; Philem. 14, *us lustum*, “of free will,” κατὰ ἑκούσίον; Rom. 9:21, *us gabaurþai*, “by nature,” κατὰ φύσιν; Eph. 2:3, in this passage, *us sateinai*, “by nature,” φύσει; Luke 20:20, *sa us liutein*, “one sent as a spy,” ἐγκάθετος.

d) Instrumental: Matt. 27:7, *usbugjam akr us þaim skattam*, “they bought a field with the money.”

Luke 8:3, “they ministered to him from their own possessions”; Luke 16:9, “make friends for yourselves from the unrighteous mammon”; e) to denote the material from which something is made: John 9:6, “he made clay from the spittle”; 19:2, “to weave a crown from thorns”; Romans 9:21, “to make from the lump”; f) after passive verbs: Mark 7:11, “a gift from me”; 2 Corinthians 2:2, “made sorrowful by me”; 7:9, “being grieved by you”; Philippians 1:23, “being constrained by the two”; John 3:25, “there arose a dispute from the disciples”; Romans 12:18, “if it may be from you.” Hence also expressions having a passive sense, such as *galigrja haban*, Romans 9:10 (that is, “to sleep,” where in the interpretation *concubitum* must be read in place of *concubitu*); *haban hazein*, 13:3 (that is, “is rewarded”).

II. In composition:

1. With verbs: *usagjan, usagljan, usaivjan, usanan, usalþan, usbairan, usbaugjan, usbeidan, usbidjan, usbliggvan, usbugjan, usbraidjan, usbruknan, usgaggan, usgeisnan, usgaisjan, usgiban, usgildan, usgutnan, usgraban, usdaudjan, usdreiban, usdriusan, usqiþan, usqiman, usqistjan, ushahan, ushaitan, ushauhjan, ushafjan, ushinþan, ushlaupan, ushulon, ushrainjan, ushramjan, ushrisjan, usþulan, usþriutan, usþroþjan, usþvahan, uskeinan, uskiusan, uskannjan, uslaubjan, usleiþan, usletan, uslagjan, uslausjan, usluton, uslukan, usluknan, usluston, usmaitan, usmanagnan, usmerjan, usmernan, usmitan, usniman, ussaiwan, ussakan, ussokjan, ussaljan, ussandjan, ussiggvan, ussitan, ussatjan, usskavjan, usspillon, usstiggan, usstandan, ussteigan, ustaiknjan, ustiuhan, usvagjan, usvairpan, usvakjan, usvaltjan, usvindan, usvandjan, usfilhan, usfulljan, usfullnan, usfraisan, usfraþvjan*; before *r* it sounds as *ur* in *urredan, urreisan, urraisjan, urrinnan, urrannjan, urrumnan*; double compounds: *(usatbairan); usgasaiwan, miþushramjan, miþuskeinan, miþurreisan, miþurraisjan*.

2. With participles: *usvahsans; unuslaisiþs, unusspilloþs*.

3. With nouns: *usbalþei, usbeisns, usbeisnei, usbloteins, usdaudei, usdrusts, usqiss, usþulains, useta, usþroþeins, usliþa, uslauseins, usluk, usmet, usmets, ussauneins, ussateins, usstass, usstiurei, ustaikneins, ustauhts, ustauhei, usvahsts, usvaurpa, usvalteins, usvaurhts, usvandi, usvissi, usfarþo, usfilh, usfilmei, usfulleins, usfodeins; urrists, urruns*.

4. With adjectives: *usbeisneigs, usgruds, usdauds, ushaists, uskunþs, uslukns, usskavs, usvaurhts, usveihs, usvens, usviss, us fairins, usfilms*.

5. With adverbs: *usdaudo, ussindo, usstiuriba*.

**UT**, adverb: “out,” “outside,” ἔξω: John 11:43; 19:4. It is also used for ἐκ … in compounds, as *utbairan, utgaggan*; ordinarily placed after the verb: *atgaggan ut* (“to go out,” ἐξέρχεσθαι), John 18:29; *galeiþan ut*, 13:30; 18:38. It is most often placed after verbs compounded with *us*: *usgaggan ut*, Matthew 9:32; Luke 15:28; John 18:4, 16; or here also for ἔξω, as *usgaggan ut* (“to go out outside,” ἐξέρχεσθαι ἔξω), Matthew 26:75; John 19:5; *usdreiban ut*, Luke 8:54; *usvairpan ut*, Luke 14:35; John 6:37; 9:34, 35; 12:31; 15:6. With the following preposition *us*, “out of, outside,” ἔξω: Mark 11:19, *usïddja ut us þizai baurg*, “he went out of the city”; 12:18; Luke 4:29; 20:15. For ἐκ: Mark 1:25.

**UTA**, adverb: “outside,” ἔξω: Matthew 26:69; Mark 1:45; 3:31, 32; 4:11; 11:4; Luke 1:10; 8:20; John 18:16; 1 Corinthians 5:12, 13; Colossians 4:5; 1 Thessalonians 4:12. “From outside,” ἔξωθεν: 1 Timothy 3:7.

**UTANA**, adverb: “outside.”

1. With the genitive, ἔξω: Mark 8:23, *ustauh þana blindan utana veihsis*, “he led the blind man outside the village”; *Skeireins* III, c. ἔξωθεν: 2 Corinthians 7:5, *utana vaihjons*, “conflicts from without”; John 9:22, *utana synagogais vairþan*, “to become excluded from the synagogue” (ἀποσυνάγωγος γίνεσθαι).

2. *Sa utana unsar manna*, “our outward man,” ὁ ἔξω ἡμῶν ἄνθρωπος, 2 Corinthians 4:16.

[Col. 1423]

**UTAþRO**, adverb: “from outside,” ἔξωθεν: Mark 7:15, 18.

**UF** (*ubuh*, see under *uh*; Greek ὑπό, Latin *sub*; Gr. IV, 789), a preposition with accusative and dative, indicating a relation of inferiority.

I. Preposition.

A. With the accusative: “under,” ὑπό with accusative.

1. Locally:

a. After verbs of motion: *ïnngaggan*, Matthew 8:8; Luke 7:6; *atdriusan*, *Skeireins* I, a (for here *stauai* must be read in place of *staua*).

b. After transitive verbs: *satjan*, Mark 4:21; *gasatjan*, Luke 8:16 (ὑποκάτω, “underneath”); *galagjan*, 1 Corinthians 15:25; *ufhnaivjan*, 1 Corinthians 15:26; Ephesians 1:22. In 1 Corinthians 15:27 and 28, *ufhnaivjan uf sumana* means ὑποτάσσειν τινί, “to subject someone to someone.”

2. Metaphorically: Romans 7:14, *frabugjan uf fravaurht*, “sold under sin.”

B. With the dative:

1. Locally: “under,” ὑπό with accusative: Mark 12:1, *dal uf mesa*, “a wine-vat beneath the press” (ὑπολήνιον); also after *gabauan*, Mark 4:32, and *visan*, 1 Corinthians 10:1; 1 Timothy 6:1; with *visands* understood, Luke 17:24, *þata uf himina*, “that which is under heaven”; Colossians 1:23.

2. Temporally: “in the time of,” “under,” or with an absolute ablative, ἐπί with genitive: Mark 2:26, *uf abjaþara gudjin*, “in the time of Abiathar the high priest”; Luke 4:27, *uf haileisaiu praufetau*, “in the time of Elisha the prophet”; 1 Timothy 6:13, *uf pauntiau peilatau*, “under Pontius Pilate.” Likewise Luke 3:23, *uf gakunþai*; see on that passage.

3. Metaphorically, after *visan*: Galatians 4:2, *uf raginjam*, “under guardians”; verse 21, *uf vitoda*, “under the law”; 5:18; with *visands* understood, 1 Corinthians 9:20, *þai uf vidota*, “those under the law”; Galatians 4:5; *uf vaira qens*, “a woman under a husband” (ὕπανδρος γυνή); *vaurþans*, Galatians 4:4, *uf vitoda*, “having come under the law”; *gasatiþs*, Luke 7:8, *uf valdufnja*, “placed under authority”; *haban*, Luke 7:8, *uf sis gadrauhtins*, “having soldiers under himself”; Mark 8:9, *uf valdufnja*, “under authority”; *skalkinon*, Galatians 4:3, *uf stabim þis fairwaus*, “to be enslaved under the elementary principles of the world.”

II. In composition:

1. With verbs: *ufbauljan, ufblesan, ufbrikan, ufbrinnan, ufgairdan, ufgraban, ufdaupjan, ufhaban, ufhausjan, ufhlohjan, ufhnaivjan, ufhropjan, ufþanjan, ufkunnan, ufligan, ufmeljan, ufmunnan, ufrakjan, ufsagqjan, ufsliupan, ufsneiþan, ufstraujan, ufsvogjan, ufvopjan*; double compound: *ïnnufsliupan*.

2. With participles: *unufbrikands*.

3. With nouns: *ufhauseins, ufhnaiveins, ufkunþi, ufsvalleins*.

**UFAR** (Old Norse *yfir*, Old Saxon *obar*, Anglo-Saxon *ofer*, Old High German *oba, ubar*, Old Frisian *over, ovir, ur*, Swedish *öfver*, English, Danish, Dutch *over*, Modern High German *über*; Greek ὑπέρ, Latin *super*; compare *Uf*; Bopp 80, 83; Gr. IV, 789; Gf. I, 78; Alth. *Praepos.* 156; Rchth. 1108), a preposition construed with the accusative and dative, denoting a relation of superiority; it stands in the same relation to *uf* as Greek ὑπέρ does to ὑπό.

I. Preposition.

A. With the accusative:

1. Locally: “above,” “over.”

a. Above something, standing over: Luke 4:39, *atstandans ufar ïja*, “standing over her” (ἐπάνω); Ephesians 4:10, *ussteigan ufar allans himinans*, “to ascend above all the heavens” (ὑπάνω).

b. “Over,” “across,” πέραν: John 6:1, *ïesus galaiþ ufar marein*, “Jesus went across the sea”; verses 17; 10:40; 18:1.

2. Metaphorically:

a. “Over”: Ephesians 1:22, *ïna atgaf haubiþ ufar alla aikklesjon*, “he gave him as head over all the churches” (ὑπέρ); 2 Thessalonians 2:4, *ufarhafjands sik ufar all*, “exalting himself above all” (ἐπί with accusative).

b. “Over and above,” “besides,” proceeding further and adding to what precedes, ἐπί with dative: Ephesians 6:16, *ufar all andnimands skildu galaubeinais*, “above all, taking the shield of faith”; Colossians 3:14, *ufar alla gahamoþ ïzvis friaþva*, “above all these things, love.”

c. “Above,” “more than,” with comparative force, ὑπέρ with accusative: Matthew 10:37, *saei frijoþ attan aiþþau aiþein ufar mik*, “he who loves father or mother more than me”; Luke 6:40; 2 Corinthians 12:13; Philemon 16; Nehemiah 7:2; *Skeireins* VII, b; 2 Corinthians 1:8, *ufar maht*, “beyond strength”; 8:3; *Skeireins* VI, b, *attins veitvodei all ufar ïnsaht manniskodaus ïohannes unandsok undredan mag kunþi*, “John, the father of prophets, recognizing the inscrutable power of the divine mystery beyond all human understanding”; *ufar all*, Ephesians 3:20, “beyond all”; *ufar þatei*, Luke 3:13; 1 Corinthians 4:6; 2 Corinthians 12:6, “beyond what”; *ufar mikil et ufar filu*, “exceedingly, exceedingly,” ὑπερλίαν: 2 Corinthians 11:5; 12:11.

B. With the dative:

1. Locally: “above.”

a. Above something, upwards, only in the formula *atta ïzvar sa ufar himinam*, “your Father who is in heaven,” ὁ οὐράνιος, Matthew 6:14, 26, 32; compare *In*.

b. “Over,” “upon,” extending itself over, ἐπί with accusative: Matthew 27:45, *varþ riqis ufar allai airþai*, “there was darkness over all the earth.”

2. Metaphorically: “over,” “upon,” ὑπέρ with accusative: Matthew 10:24, *nist siponeis ufar laisarja*, “a disciple is not above his teacher”; ἐπί with genitive: Romans 9:5, *saei ïst ufar allaim guþ*, “God, who is over all”; Ephesians 4:6; ἐπί with accusative after *þiudanon*, Luke 1:33; 19:14, 27; ἐπάνω after *valdufni haban*, Luke 19:17, and *valdufni giban*, Luke 9:1.

II. In composition:

1. With verbs: *ufargaggan, ufargiutan, ufarhamon, ufarhafjan, ufarhleiþrjan, ufarhugjan, ufarþeihan, ufarleiþan, ufarlagjan, ufarmeljan, ufarmiton, ufarmunnon, ufarskadvjan, ufarsteigan, ufarsvaran, ufartrusnjan, ufarvahsjan, ufarvisan, ufarfulljan*.

2. With nouns: *ufargudja, ufarhauseins, (ufarmaudei), ufarmeleins, ufarmeli, ufarranneins, ufarskafts, ufarsvara, ufarfullei*.

3. With adjectives: *ufarhiminakunds, ufarfulls*.

**UFARO**, adverb: “from above”: John 11:38 (ἐπ’ αὐτῷ); *Skeireins* IV, b. “On,” “above,” “from above,” with the genitive, after *trudan*, Luke 10:19 (ἐπάνω); after *gasatjan*, Ephesians 1:21 (ὑπεράνω); with the dative, after *visan*, Luke 19:19 (ἐπάνω); John 3:31 (ὑπεράνω); after *vitan vahtvom*, Luke 2:8 (ἐπί with accusative).

**UFARASSUS**, masculine: “abundance,” “superfluity,” περισσεία: 2 Corinthians 10:15; περίσσευμα: 2 Corinthians 8:13, 14; ὑπερβολή: 2 Corinthians 3:10; 4:7, 17; τὸ ὑπερέχον, Philippians 3:8; ὑπεροχή, 1 Timothy 2:2. With a following substantive genitive it is used in place of the participle ὑπερβάλλων, “surpassing”; thus 2 Corinthians 9:14, *ufarassus anstais*, “surpassing grace” (ὑπερβάλλουσα χάρις); Ephesians 1:19, *ufarassus mikileins*, “surpassing greatness” (ὑπερβάλλον μέγεθος); 2:7, *ufarassus gabeins*, “surpassing riches” (ὑπερβάλλων πλοῦτος). The dative *ufarassau* is used adverbially: “abundantly,” “exceedingly,” “superabundantly,” “very greatly,” περισσοτέρως: 2 Corinthians 1:12; 2:4; 7:15; 11:23; 1 Thessalonians 2:17; ὑπερπερισσῶς: Mark 7:37; ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ: 1 Thessalonians 3:10; 5:13; ὑπερβαλλόντως: 2 Corinthians 11:23; καθ’ ὑπερβολήν: Romans 8:13; 2 Corinthians 1:8. It also occurs for ὑπέρ in compounds: *ufarassau ufþanjan*, “to stretch out exceedingly,” for ὑπερεκτείνειν, 2 Corinthians 10:14; *ufarassau haban*, “to have abundantly,” “to abound,” with the genitive, περισσεύειν: Luke 15:17; Philippians 4:12; *ufarassau ganohjan*, the same, Ephesians 1:8; *ufarassus ïst*, the same, 2 Corinthians 1:5.

**UFARASSJAN**, second conjugation:

1. “To cause to abound,” “to increase,” περισσεύειν: 2 Corinthians 4:15; 9:8.

2. “To increase,” περισσεύειν: 2 Corinthians 9:12; ὑπερπλεονάζειν: 1 Timothy 1:14.

**UFITAHARI**, proper name, Neapolitan documents (see Massmann on this, p. 22 ff.).

**UFJO** (compare *Ufar*), adverb: “abundantly,” περισσόν: 2 Corinthians 9:1.

**UFTA** (Old Norse *opt*, Old Saxon, Anglo-Saxon, Modern High German *oft*, Old High German *ofto*, English *oft, often*, Swedish *ofta*, Danish *ofte*; Gf. I, 184), adverb: “often,” πολλάκις: Mark 5:4; 9:22; John 18:2; 2 Corinthians 8:22; 11:23, 26, 27; Philippians 3:18; 2 Timothy 1:16. “Frequently,” πυκνά: Mark 7:3; Luke 5:33. *Sa ufta*, “frequently,” “repeatedly,” ὁ πυκνός: 1 Timothy 5:23. *Sva ufta sve*, “as often as,” ὁσάκις: 1 Corinthians 11:25, 26.

**UFTO**, adverb: “perhaps,” “possibly”; however, in Matthew 27:64 it is probably necessary to read *ei*, and in Luke 20:13 certainly *aufto*; see on that passage.

**PEIK** (Gr. III, 377 gives *peika* or *peiko*, calls it cognate with Greek φοῖνιξ, and says that it means “a little palm”; but at I, 68 [third edition] he treats *peika* as shortened from *peinika*, so that it corresponds to Greek φοινικο—. He seems, however, to have come nearer the mark at I, 55, where, comparing our word with Latin *picea* and Greek πεύκη, he explains *peikabagms* as “pine-tree.” In any event, it should properly be compared with Old Saxon and Old French *pik*, Anglo-Saxon *pic*, Old High German *pih*, Modern High German *Pech*, Latin *pix*, Greek πίσσα; Old Norse *bik*, Swedish *beck*, Danish *beek*, and translated “pitch-tree”), neuter: pitch.

VI, 153), conjugation I, *soþ, soþun, saþans*, to satisfy, fill. SAþS (*Sads*, Luke XV, 16), adjective, filled, ἐμπεπλησμένος: Luke VI, 25; satiated, κεκορεσμένος: I Cor. IV, 8; *saþs vairþan*, to be filled or satisfied, χορτάζεσθαι: Mark VII, 27; VIII, 8; Luke VI, 21; IX, 17; John VI, 26; Phil. IV, 12; ἐμπίμπλασθαι: John VI, 12; *saþ itan*, to satisfy oneself, χορτάζεσθαι: Luke XVI, 21; γεμίζειν τὴν κοιλίαν, “to fill the belly”: Luke XV, 16. SOþ, neuter (?), fullness, abundance, πλησμονή: Col. II, 23. GA-SOþJAN, conjugation II, to satisfy, χορτάζειν: Mark VIII, 4; ἐμπιμπλάναι: Luke I, 53.

SAI (compare *Saiwan*; Gr. III, 247; I, 93, 1 [3rd edition]), adverb, behold!, ἰδού: Matt. VIII, 2, 24, 29, 32, 34; IX, 10, 20; X, 28, 33; XI, 8, 10; Mark I, 2; IV, 3; X, 28, 33; XIII, 21, 23; XIV, 41, 42; XV, 4, 35; Luke I, 31, 36, 38, 44, 48; II, 10, 34, 48; V, 12, 18; VI, 23; VII, 12, 25, 27, 34, 37; VIII, 41; IX, 30, 38, 39; X, 3, 19, 25; XV, 29; XVII, 21, 23; XVIII, 28, 31; XIX, 2, 8, 20; John XII, 15; XVI, 31; Rom. IX, 33; I Cor. XV, 51; II Cor. V, 17; VI, 2, 9; Gal. I, 20; ἴδε, “behold!”: Matt. XXVI, 65; Mark II, 24; III, 34; XI, 21; XV, 4; XVI, 6; John I, 29; III, 26; VII, 26; XI, 3, 36; XII, 19; XVI, 29; XVIII, 21; XIX, 4; Rom. XI, 22; Gal. V, 2; ἴδετε, “behold, you all!”: Mark X, 23, at this passage; XVI, 6; Gal. VI, 11; νῦν, “now”: I Thess. III, 8; *sai nu*, ἄρα οὖν, “therefore then”: Eph. II, 19; compare Rom. VII, 25 at this passage; ἔστω, “let it be”: II Cor. XII, 16; see at this passage; *nu sai*, νυνί, “now”: Rom. VII, 6; see at this passage; I Cor. V, 11; II Cor. VIII, 11, 22; Eph. II, 13; νῦν, “now”: Gal. IV, 9; *sai jau, ne*, μή, “not”: John VII, 48.

SAIAN (*Saijan*, Mark IV, 14; Old Norse *sa*, Old Saxon *saian*, Anglo-Saxon *sawan*, Old High German *saan, sawen*, Old French *sea*, English *sow*, Swedish *så*, Danish *saae*, Dutch *saeyen*, Modern High German *säen*; Latin *sero, semen*; Gf. VI, 54; Rchth. 1001), conjugation I, *saiso, saisoun, saians*, to sow, σπείρειν: Matt. VI, 26; Mark IV, 3, 4, 14, 15; Luke VIII, 5; XIX, 21; II Cor. IX, 6, 10; Gal. VI, 7, 8. ÏN-SAIAN, the same: Mark IV, 15.

SAIHS (Old Norse, Old French *sex*, Old High German, Old Saxon *sehs*, Anglo-Saxon, English *six*, Swedish, Danish *sex*, Dutch *ses*, Modern High German *sechs*; Latin *sex*, Greek ἕξ; Gr. I, 762; Gf. VI, 152; Rchth. 1009), indeclinable numeral, six, ἕξ: Mark IX, 2; Luke IV, 25. SAIHS-TIGJUS, masculine plural, sixty, ἑξήκοντα: I Tim. V, 9. SAIHSTA, adjective, sixth, ἕκτος: Matt. XXVII, 45; Mark XV, 33; Luke I, 26, 36. SAIKAINEIAS, masculine proper name, Σεχενίας, “Shecaniah”: Neh. VI, 18.

*SAIL* (Old Norse *seil*, Old Saxon *sel*, Anglo-Saxon *sael*, Old High German *sail, seil*, Old French *sel, sil*, Dutch *zeel*, Modern High German *seil*; Gr. II, 44; Gf. VI, 187; Rchth. 1004), rope. ÏN-SAILJAN, conjugation II, to ensnare, χαλᾶν: Mark II, 4; see at this passage. SAILLAUM, masculine proper name, Σελλούμ, “Shallum”: Ezra II, 42. SAIMAIEIN, masculine proper name, Σεμεί, “Shimei”: Luke III, 26. SAINNAA, masculine proper name, Σεναά, “Senaah”: Ezra II, 35.

SAINJAN (Anglo-Saxon *saene*, Old High German *seino*, Old Saxon *seinn, senian*, Swedish *sen*, Danish *seen*; Latin *segnis*; compare Modern High German *sehnen*), conjugation II, to delay, βραδύνειν: I Tim. III, 15. SAIR (Old Norse *saar*, Anglo-Saxon *sar*, Old Saxon, Old French, Old High German *ser*, English *sore*, Swedish *sår*, Danish *saar*, Dutch *zeer*, Modern High German … *sehren*; Rchth. 1007), neuter, pain, affliction, ὠδίν: I Thess. V, 3; ὀδύνη: I Tim. VI, 10. SAIROK, masculine proper name, Σερούχ, “Serug”: Luke III, 35.

SAIVALA (Old Norse *sal*, Anglo-Saxon *savl*, Old Saxon *seola*, Old High German *sela*, Old French *sele, siele*, English *soul*, Swedish *själ*, Danish *sjel*, Dutch *ziel*, Modern High German *seele*; Gr. III, 390; DM. 477; Gf. VI, 183; Rchth. 1004), feminine, soul, ψυχή: Matt. VI, 25; X, 28, 39; Mark III, 4; VIII, 35, 36, 37; X, 45; XII, 30, 33; Luke I, 46; II, 35; VI, 9; IX, 24, 56; X, 27; XIV, 26; XVII, 33; John X, 11, 15, 17, 24; XII, 25, 27; XIII, 37; XV, 13; Rom. XIII, 1; II Cor. I, 23; XII, 15; Phil. I, 27; II, 30; Col. III, 23; I Thess. V, 23; *Skeir.* II, d; IV, b. SAMA-SAIVALS, adjective, of one soul; united in spirit, σύμψυχος: Phil. II, 2.

SAIVS (Old Norse *saer*, Anglo-Saxon *sae*, Old Saxon, Old High German *seo*, Old French *se*, English *sea*, Swedish *sjö*, Danish *so*, Dutch *zee*, Modern High German *see*; Gr. III, 382; Gf. VI, 56; Rchth. 1001), masculine, sea, lake, λίμνη: Luke V, 1, 2; Neapolitan document. MARI-SAIVS, the same: Luke VIII, 22, 23.

SAIWAN (Old Norse *sia*, Anglo-Saxon *seon*, Old Saxon, Old High German *sehan*, Old French *sia*, English *see*, Swedish *se*, Danish *see*, Dutch *zien*, Modern High German *sehen*; Gr. II, 28; Gf. VI, 110; Rchth. 1010), conjugation I, *saw, sewun, saiwans*: 1) to see, ὁρᾶν: Matt. VIII, 4; IX, 30; XXV, 38; XXVII, 49; Mark V, 6, 14, 22, 32; VIII, 15; IX, 38; XV, 36; Luke II, 15, 26, 30; VII, 25, 26; VIII, 35; X, 24; XIV, 18; XIX, 37; XX, 37; John VII, 52; VIII, 57; XI, 34, 40; XII, 9, 41; XVIII, 26; XIX, 6; I Cor. IX, 1; XVI, 7; II Cor. VII, 11; Col. II, 18; I Thess. V, 15; I Tim. VI, 16; *Skeir.* VI, d; βλέπειν: Matt. V, 28; Mark IV, 12, 24; V, 31; XII, 14; XIII, 23; Luke VIII, 10, 16, 18; IX, 62; X, 23, 24; John IX, 7, 15, 19, 21, 25, 39; XIII, 22; XIV, 7; XVI, 22; I Cor. X, 18; XIII, 12; XVI, 10; II Cor. X, 7; Gal. V, 15; Phil. III, 2; Col. IV, 17; θεᾶσθαι: Matt. VI, 1; XI, 7; Luke VII, 24; John XI, 45; θεωρεῖν: Matt. XXVII, 55; Mark XV, 40, 47; John VI, 40; VII, 3; IX, 8; XII, 19, 45; XIV, 17, 19; XVI, 10, 16; XVII, 24; 2) to look upon, ὁρᾶν: Luke XIV, 18; 3) to see, beware (*faura*), βλέπειν ἀπό—: Mark XII, 38. UN-SAIWANDS, present participle, not seeing, μὴ βλέπων: John IX, 39.

AND-SAIWAN, to look upon, observe, σκοπεῖν: Gal. VI, 1, at this passage; λαμβάνειν: Luke XX, 21. AT-SAIWAN: 1) to attend to, προσέχειν: Matt. VI, 1; with the genitive, I Tim. I, 4; IV, 1; Titus I, 14; with the accusative, σκοπεῖν: Gal. VI, 1; *atsaiwan du*, to give heed to, ἐπέχειν: I Tim. IV, 16; 2) to beware (*faura*), προσέχειν: Matt. VII, 15; Luke XX, 46; also *atsaiwan sis* (*sik*?), with the genitive, βλέπειν ἀπό—: Mark VIII, 15. BI-SAIWAN: 1) to look around, observe, περιβλέπεσθαι: Mark III, 34; X, 23; XI, 11; 2) to notice, κατανοεῖν: Luke XX, 23; 3) to take care, provide, προνοεῖσθαι: Rom. XII, 17.

GA-SAIWAN, to see, look upon, ὁρᾶν: Matt. V, 8, 16; VIII, 14, 18, 34; IX, 2, 8, 9, 23, 36; XXVI, 71; XXVII, 3, 54; Mark I, 10, 16, 19; II, 5, 12, 14, 16; V, 16; VII, 2; VIII, 24, 33; IX, 1, 8, 9, 14, 15, 20, 25; XI, 13, 20; [Col. 1434] XII, 15, 34; XIII, 26, 29; XIV, 62, 67, 69; XV, 32, 39; XVI, 5, 7; Luke I, 12, 22, 29; II, 17, 20, 48; III, 6; V, 2, 12, 20, 26; VII, 13, 22, 39; VIII, 20, 28, 34, 36, 47, 53 (see at this passage); IX, 9, 27, 31, 32, 36, 47, 49, 54; XV, 20; XVI, 23; XVII, 22; XVIII, 15, 24, 43; XIX, 3, 4, 5, 7, 41; XX, 13, 14; John III, 3, 32; V, 37; VI, 2, 14, 24, 36; VIII, 38, 56; IX, 37; XI, 31, 32, 33; XII, 21; XIV, 9, 24; XVI, 16; Rom. VII, 23; I Cor. VIII, 10; XV, 6; Gal. II, 7; Phil. I, 27, 30; II, 28; IV, 9; I Thess. II, 17; III, 6, 10; II Tim. I, 4; *Skeir.* I, a; II, c; IV, d; ἀφορᾶν, to look toward: Phil. II, 23; βλέπειν, to see: Matt. XI, 4; Mark VIII, 18, 23, 24; Luke VII, 44; VIII, 10; X, 24; John IX, 41; XI, 9; Rom. VII, 23; II Cor. IV, 18; VII, 8; XII, 6; ἐμβλέπειν, to look intently: Mark VIII, 25; θεᾶσθαι, to behold: Mark XVI, 11; Luke V, 27; θεωρεῖν, to observe: Mark III, 11; V, 15, 38; Luke X, 18; XIV, 29; John VI, 19, 62; VIII, 51; X, 12; εἰδέναι, to know: Luke VIII, 53; Mark XII, 15, 28; in the passive, to appear, φανῆναι: Matt. VI, 16, 18; past participle *gasaiwans*, seen, visible, ὁρατός: Col. I, 16. UNGA-SAIWANS, past participle, invisible, ἀόρατος: Col. I, 15, 16; I Tim. I, 17; μὴ βλεπόμενος, not seen: II Cor. IV, 4, 18. DUGA-SAIWAN, to see, look upon, ὁρᾶν: Mark X, 14; see at this passage. USGA-SAIWAN, to see, recognize, ὁρᾶν: Gal. II, 14. þAIRH-SAIWAN, to see through, behold as in a mirror, κατοπτρίζεσθαι: II Cor. III, 18.

ÏN-SAIWAN: 1) to look upon (*du*), ἐμβλέπειν: Matt. VI, 26; Mark X, 21, 27; XIV, 67; Luke XX, 17; ἐπιβλέπειν: Luke I, 48; IX, 38; 2) to look up, ἀναβλέπειν: Mark XVI, 4; Luke IX, 16; *iup insaiwan*, the same: Luke XIX, 5; 3) to look around, περιβλέπεσθαι: Mark IX, 8; 4) to look upon, ἐφοράν: Luke I, 25. US-SAIWAN: 1) to look up, ἀναβλέπειν: Mark VII, 34; VIII, 24; 2) to receive sight, ἀναβλέπειν: Matt. XI, 5; Mark VIII, 25; X, 51, 52; Luke VII, 22; XVIII, 41, 42, 43; John IX, 11, 15, 18; 3) to look around, περιβλέπεσθαι: Mark III, 5; Luke VI, 10.

SAKAN (Old Norse *saka, sökja*, Old Saxon *saca, sacan, sokian*, Anglo-Saxon *sacan, secan*, Old Saxon *seka*, Old High German *sachan, sochjan*, English *sake, seek*, Swedish … *saka, söka*, Danish *soge*, Dutch *zoeken*, Modern High German *sache, suchen*; Gr. II, 11, 203; DRA. 855; Gf. VI, 71; Rchth. 1002 ff.), conjugation I, *sok, sokun, sakans*: 1) to rebuke, ἐπιτιμᾶν: Mark X, 13; Luke XIX, 39; 2) to contend, dispute, μάχεσθαι: John VI, 52; II Tim. II, 24. AND-SAKAN, to contradict, ἀντιλέγειν: Luke II, 34. UNAND-SAKANS, past participle, unassailable, invincible: *Skeir.* VI, c. GA-SAKAN: 1) to threaten, rebuke, with the dative, ἐπιτιμᾶν: Matt. VIII, 26; Mark IV, 39; Luke IV, 39, 41; VIII, 24; IX, 55; XVII, 3; 2) to convict, reprove, with the accusative, ἐλέγχειν: Luke III, 19; John VIII, 46; XVI, 8; I Cor. XIV, 24; I Tim. V, 20; II Tim. IV, 2; Titus I, 9, 13; *Skeir.* IV, d; V, b; VII, a; ἐπιστομίζειν, “to silence”: Titus I, 11. ÏN-SAKAN, to set forth, indicate, supply, ὑποτίθεσθαι: I Tim. IV, 6; *Skeir.* IV, c, d; V, a; VIII, c. ANAÏN-SAKAN, to add, submit in addition, προσανατίθεσθαι: Gal. II, 6. US-SAKAN, to lift up, raise, ἀναβάλλεσθαι (ἀνατίθεσθαι): Gal. II, 2. SAKJIS, masculine, fighter; *ni sakjis*, not quarrelsome, ἄμαχος: I Tim. III, 3. SAKJO, feminine, fight, quarrel, μάχη: II Tim. II, 23. GA-SAHTS, feminine, reproof, conviction, ἔλεγχος: II Tim. III, 16; *Skeir.* VIII, b, d. ÏN-SAHTS, account, narrative, διήγησις: Luke I, 1; subscription to I Corinthians; *Skeir.* V, b, c; VI, a, b. FRI-SAHTS: 1) image, εἰκών: I Cor. XV, 49; II Cor. III, 18; IV, 4; Col. I, 15; III, 10; 2) pattern, example, τύπος: Phil. III, 17; II Thess. III, 9; I Tim. IV, 12; ὑποτύπωσις, “outline, model”: I Tim. I, 16; II Tim. I, 13; ὑπόδειγμα, “example”: John XIII, 15; 3) enigma, αἴνιγμα: I Cor. XIII, 12. GAFRI-SAHTJAN, conjugation II, to engrave, imprint, ἐντυποῦν: II Cor. III, 7. [Col. 1435] GAFRI-SAHTNAN, conjugation III, to be conformed; *du laudjai gafrisahtnan*, to be conformed to the likeness: Gal. IV, 19, at this passage. UN-SAHTABA, adverb, incontrovertibly, confessedly, ὁμολογουμένως: I Tim. III, 16; see at this passage. UNAND-SOKS, adjective, unassailable: *Skeir.* VI, c. SOKNS, feminine, question, ζήτησις: I Tim. I, 4; VI, 4; II Tim. II, 23.

SOKJAN, conjugation II: 1) to seek, desire, request, ζητεῖν: Mark I, 37; III, 32; VIII, 11; XI, 18, 24; XII, 12; XIV, 11, 55; XVI, 6; Luke II, 45, 48, 49; IV, 42; V, 18; VI, 19; IX, 9; XV, 8; XVII, 33; XIX, 3; X, 47; XX, 19; John VI, 24, 26; VII, 1, 4, 11, 18, 19, 25, 30, 34; VIII, 21, 37, 50; X, 39; XI, 8; XIII, 33; XVI, 19; XVIII, 4; XIX, 12; Rom. X, 3; I Cor. I, 22; VII, 27; X, 24, 33; II Cor. XII, 14; XIII, 3; Gal. II, 17; Col. III, 1; II Tim. I, 17; Neh. V, 18; ἀναζητεῖν, “search for”: Luke II, 44; ἐπιζητεῖν, “seek after”: Matt. VI, 32; Luke IV, 42; ἐκζητεῖν, “seek out”: Ps. LIII, 2; αἰτεῖν, “ask”: Mark XI, 24; Luke I, 63; 2) to dispute with (*miþ* or *du*), συζητεῖν: Mark I, 27; IX, 10, 14, 16; ζητεῖν: John XVI, 19; *Skeir.* IV, a; also *samana sokjan*, Mark XII, 28. GA-SOKJAN, to seek, ζητεῖν: Rom. X, 20; ἐπιζητεῖν: Phil. IV, 17. MIþ-SOKJAN, to dispute with, συζητεῖν: Mark VIII, 11. US-SOKJAN: 1) to investigate, ἐρευνᾶν: John VII, 52; 2) to examine, judge, ἀνακρίνειν: I Cor. IV, 3; IX, 3; XIV, 24; διακρίνειν: I Cor. IV, 7. SOKEINS, feminine, inquiry, disputation, ζήτησις: John III, 25; *Skeir.* III, b. SOKAREIS, masculine, inquirer, disputant, συζητητής: I Cor. I, 20.

SAKKUS (Old Norse *seckr*, Anglo-Saxon *sacc*, Old High German *sak*; Greek σάκκος, Latin *saccus*; Gr. III, 450; Gf. VI, 70), masculine, sack, σάκκος: Matt. XI, 21; Luke X, 13. SALAþIEL, masculine proper name, Σαλαθιήλ, “Salathiel”: Luke III, 27. SALAM, masculine proper name, Σαλά, “Sala”: Luke III, 35.

SALBON (Anglo-Saxon *sealfian*, Old Saxon *salbon*, Old High German *salb, salbon*, Old French *salva*, English *salve*, Swedish *salfva*, Danish *salve*, Modern High German *salben*; Greek ἀλείφειν; Gf. VI, 191; Rchth. 1000), conjugation II, to anoint, ἀλείφειν: Matt. VI, 17; Luke VII, 46; John XI, 2; μυρίζειν, “to perfume”: Mark XIV, 8; χρίειν, “to anoint”: II Cor. I, 21. GA-SALBON, the same, ἀλείφειν: Mark VI, 13; XVI, 1; Luke VII, 38, 46; John XII, 3; χρίειν: Luke IV, 18. SALBONS, feminine, ointment, perfume, μύρον: John XII, 3. SALDRA (from *sildan, sald?*; compare *Sild*), feminine, jesting, buffoonery, εὐτραπελία: Eph. V, 4. SALMON, masculine proper name, Σαλμών, “Salmon”: Luke III, 32.

SALJAN (Old Norse *selia*, Anglo-Saxon and Old Saxon *sellian*, Old High German *saljan*, Old French *sella*; Gr. II, 54; DRA. 555, 893; Gf. VI, 174; Rchth. 1005), conjugation II, to offer, sacrifice, θύειν: Mark XIV, 12; I Cor. X, 20; θυμιᾶν, “to burn incense”: Luke I, 9; *þatei galiugam saljada*, “that which is offered to idols,” εἰδωλόθυτον: I Cor. X, 19; *hunsla saljan*, to offer an oblation, λατρείαν προσφέρειν: John XVI, 2. GA-SALJAN, to offer, sacrifice, θύειν: I Cor. VIII, 10; *Skeir.* I, a; *galiugam gasaliþ*, sacrificed to idols, εἰδωλόθυτον: I Cor. X, 28.

SALJAN (Old Norse *salr*, Anglo-Saxon, Swedish, Danish *sal*, Old French *sele*, Old Saxon *seli, selda, seliða*, Old High German *sal, salida*; Gr. II, 54; III, 427; Gf. VI, 176; compare Rchth. 1151, see *Windsele*), conjugation II, to remain, stay, μένειν: Mark VI, 10; Luke IX, 4; John X, 40; XI, 6; παραμένειν: I Cor. XVI, 6; ἐπιμένειν: I Cor. XVI, 7; προσμένειν: I Tim. I, 3; καταλύειν: Luke IX, 12; ξενίζεσθαι: I Cor. XVI, 19. US-SALJAN, the same, καταλύειν: Luke XIX, 7. SALIþVOS, feminine plural, dwelling-place, abode, μονή: John XIV, 2, 23; lodging, κατάλυμα: Mark XIV, 14; hospitality, ξενία: Philem. 22.

SALT (Old Norse, Old Saxon, Old French, Swedish, Danish, English *salt*, Anglo-Saxon *sealt*, Modern and Old High German *salz*, Dutch *sout*; Latin *sal*, Greek ἅλς; Gr. III, 381; Gf. VI, 218; Rchth. 1000), neuter, salt, ἅλς: Mark IX, 49, 50; ἅλας: Luke XIV, 34; Col. IV, 6. [Col. 1436] SALTAN, conjugation I, *saisalt, saisaltun, saltans*, to salt, ἁλίζειν: Mark IX, 49. UN-SALTANS, past participle, saltless, tasteless, ἄναλος: Mark IX, 50. SALOME, feminine proper name, Σαλώμη, “Salome”: Mark XV, 40; XVI, 1.

SAMA (Old Norse *samr, saman*, Old Saxon *sama, saman*, Old High German *saman*, Old French *samin, semin*, Anglo-Saxon, English *same*, Swedish *samma*, Danish *samme*, Modern High German *samt, zusammen*; Latin *simul*, Greek ἅμα; Gr. II, 55; III, 4; Gf. VI, 26; Rchth. 1006): 1) pronoun, ordinarily constructed with the article, the same, namely this one, ὁ αὐτός: Matt. V, 46; XXVII, 44; Mark X, 10; Luke II, 8; VI, 33, 38; Rom. IX, 21; XII, 4, 16; XV, 5; I Cor. X, 3; XI, 5; XII, 11; II Cor. I, 6; III, 14, 18; IV, 13; VI, 13; VIII, 16; XII, 18; Eph. VI, 9; Phil. I, 30; II, 2; III, 1; IV, 2; I Thess. II, 14; *Skeir.* V, b, c, d; VII, d; without the article, one, a certain person, εἷς: Mark X, 8; Luke XVII, 34; Eph. II, 14; ὁ: Eph. VI, 9, at this passage; ὁ αὐτός: Rom. X, 12; II Cor. XIII, 11; Phil. III, 16; *Skeir.* VI, a (?); 2) in compounds: *samaqiss, samakuns, samalauds, samaleiks, samasaivals, samafraþjis; samaleiko*. SAMANA, adverb, together, collectively (whence?), ἅμα: Col. IV, 3; I Thess. V, 10; I Tim. V, 13; Ps. LIII, 3; ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, “in one place”: Luke XVII, 35; I Cor. XIV, 23; Gothic calendar: *samana arbaidjan, briggan samana, samana liban, samana sokjan*, see under *Arbaiþs, Briggan, Liban, Sakan*. SAMAþ, adverb, together (whence?), ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό: I Cor. VII, 5; *samaþ gagaggan*, see under *Gaggan*; *samaþ rinnan*, see under *Rinnan*.

SAMARIA, feminine proper name, Σαμαρία, “Samaria”: Luke XVII, 11. SAMAREITES, masculine, Σαμαρείτης, “Samaritan”: Luke IX, 52; XVII, 16; John VIII, 48. SAMJAN (Old Norse *semja*, Old Saxon *somi*, Anglo-Saxon *seman*; Gr. II, 55), conjugation II, to please, ἀρέσκειν: Col. III, 22; *samjan sis*, to make a fair outward show, εὐπροσωπεῖν: Gal. VI, 12. SANDJAN, see under *Sinþan*. SAUDAUMA, proper name, Σόδομα, “Sodom”: Rom. IX, 29. SAUDAUMEIS, masculine, Σόδομος, “Sodom”: Matt. XI, 23, 24; Mark VI, 11; Luke X, 12; XVII, 29. SAUHTS, see under *Siukan*. SAUþA, feminine, reason, foundation, λόγος: I Cor. XV, 2. SAUþS (*Sauds*, Rom. XII, 1; Old Norse *saudr*, compare Anglo-Saxon *seoðan*, Old High German *siudan*, Swedish *sjuda*, Danish *syde*, Dutch *zieden*, Modern High German *sieden*; Gr. II, 21; DM. 25), masculine, sacrifice, θυσία: Rom. XII, 1; Eph. V, 2; whole burnt offering, ὁλοκαύτωμα: Mark XII, 33; *Skeir.* I, a.

SAUIL (Old Norse, Swedish, Danish, Latin *sol*, Greek ἥλιος; Gr. III, 349, 351), neuter, sun, ἥλιος: Mark I, 32; XIII, 24. SAULAUMON, masculine proper name, Σολομών, “Solomon”: Matt. VI, 29; John X, 23.

*SAULJAN* (Old Norse *söla*, Anglo-Saxon *sylian*, Old Saxon *sulian, suiliuuan*, Old High German *salon*, Old French *sülenge*, English *soil*, Swedish *solka*, Danish *solke*, Modern High German *sühlen, sudeln*; Gf. VI, 186; Rchth. 1055), conjugation II, to defile. BI-SAULJAN, the same, μιαίνειν: Titus I, 15. BI-SAULNAN, conjugation III, to be defiled, μιαίνεσθαι: John XVIII, 28. BI-SAULEINS, feminine, defilement, μολυσμός: II Cor. VII, 1. SAULS (Old Norse *sula*, Anglo-Saxon *syl*, Old Saxon *sul*, Old High German *sul, suli*, Old French *sele*, Dutch *zuil*, Modern High German *säule*; Gf. VI, 186; Rchth. 1004), pillar, στύλος: Gal. II, 9; I Tim. III, 15.

SAUN (Old Saxon *gisonian*, Old French *sena, sone*, Modern High German *sühne*; compare *Sunja*; DRA. 622; Rchth. 1006, 1040), neuter (?), ransom, redemption, λύτρον: Mark X, 45; see at this passage. *US-SAUNJAN*, conjugation II, to reconcile. US-SAUNEINS, feminine, reconciliation: *Skeir.* I, a. SAUR, masculine proper name, Σύρος, “Syrian”: Luke II, 2; IV, 27. [Col. 1437] SAURA, feminine, Συρία, “Syria”: Gal. I, 21. SAURINIFYNIKISKA, feminine, Συροφοίνισσα, “Syrophoenician woman”: Mark VII, 26.

SAURGA (Old Norse, Anglo-Saxon, Swedish, Danish *sorg*, Old Saxon *sorga, sorgon*, English *sorrow*, Dutch *zorg*, Old High German *sorge*), feminine, care, anxiety, μέριμνα: Mark IV, 19; Luke VIII, 14; II Cor. XI, 28; grief, λύπη: John XVI, 20; Rom. IX, 2; II Cor. II, 1, 3; VII, 10. SAURGAN, conjugation II, to be anxious, μεριμνᾶν: Matt. VI, 28; to grieve, λυπεῖσθαι: John XVI, 20; II Cor. VI, 10; VII, 9, 11; I Thess. IV, 13. SARAIPTA, proper name, Σάρεπτα, “Zarephath”: Luke IV, 26. SARRA, feminine proper name, Σάρρα, “Sarah”: Rom. IX, 9. SARVA (Anglo-Saxon *searu*, Old High German *saro*; Gr. III, 446), neuter plural, arms, weapons, ὅπλα: Rom. XIII, 12; full armour, πανοπλία: Eph. VI, 11, 13. SATANA (*satanas*, Mark III, 23; IV, 15), masculine proper name, σατανᾶς, “Satan”: Mark I, 13; III, 23, 26; VIII, 33; Luke X, 18; John XIII, 27; II Cor. II, 11; XI, 14; XII, 7; I Thess. II, 18; I Tim. I, 20. SATEINS, see under *Sitan*. SATJAN, see under *Sitan*. SEþ, masculine proper name, Σήθ, “Seth”: Luke III, 38.

*SEþS* and SEDS (*Seiþs*, Luke IX, 13; John XIV, 17, 19; Old Norse, Old Saxon *sad*, Anglo-Saxon *soed*, English *seed*, Modern High German *saat*; Latin *satus*; Bopp 86; Gr. II, 235; DM. 457), feminine, seed, sowing. MANA-SEþS, multitude, people, λαός: Luke IX, 13; world, κόσμος: Mark XIV, 9; Luke IX, 25; John I, 29; VI, 14, 33, 51; VII, 4, 7; VIII, 12; XII, 19, 31, 47; XIV, 17, 22, 27, 30, 31; XV, 18, 19; XVI, 8, 20; XVII, 9, 13, 14, 18, 21, 23, 25; XVIII, 20; I Cor. IV, 9; II Cor. V, 19; Eph. II, 12; *Skeir.* I, a. SEI, feminine of the relative pronoun, see under *þata*. SEIDONA, proper name, Σιδών, “Sidon”: Matt. XI, 21; Mark III, 8; Luke IV, 26. SEIDONEIS, masculine plural, Sidonians: Matt. XI, 22; Mark VII, 24, 31.

SEIþU (Old Norse *sid*, Anglo-Saxon *sið*, Old Saxon *sith*, Old High German *sid*; Gr. III, 89, 258, 590; Gf. VI, 155), adverb, late, evening, ὀψία: Matt. XXVII, 57; John VI, 16. *SEIþS*, comparative, later. þANA-SEIþS, any longer, always construed with the negative *ni* (see this word), no longer, οὐκέτι, μηκέτι: Mark IX, 8, 25; X, 8; XI, 14; XII, 34; Luke XX, 36, 40; John VI, 66; XIV, 19, 30; XV, 15; XVI, 10, 21, 25; XVII, 11; II Cor. I, 23; V, 15; Gal. IV, 7; Eph. IV, 14, 17, 28; Col. II, 20; *Skeir.* I, b; III, b; pleonastically also *ju þanaseiþs ni*, Luke XV, 19, 21, and *nu ni þanaseiþs*, Gal. II, 20.

SEIMON, masculine proper name, Σίμων, “Simon”: Mark I, 16, 29, 30, 36; III, 16, 18; VI, 3; XV, 21; Luke IV, 38; VI, 14, 15; VII, 43, 44; John VI, 68, 71; XII, 4; XIII, 36; XVIII, 10. SEIMONUS, the same: Mark I, 16; Luke V, 4; John VI, 8. SEINA, feminine proper name, Σινᾶ, “Sinai”: Gal. IV, 24, 25.

SEINA (Old Norse, Anglo-Saxon, Old Saxon, Old High German, Old French, Swedish, Danish *sin*, Dutch *zyn*, Modern High German *sein*; Latin *sui, suus*; Gf. VI, 6; Rchth. 1018), genitive of the third-person personal pronoun, of oneself, one’s own, ἴδιος: John XVI, 32; see at this passage; *seina misso*, one another, ἀλλήλων: Luke VII, 32; *seina gairns*, self-loving, φίλαυτος: II Tim. III, 2; see at this passage. SIS, dative, to oneself: Matt. V, 42; VIII, 32; IX, 3; XXVI, 75; Mark I, 27; II, 6, 8, 19, 26; III, 14; IV, 17, 41; V, 4, 30, 37, 40; VI, 20; VIII, 14, 16; IX, 8, 10, 34; X, 26; XII, 6, 7; XV, 31; XVI, 8; Luke II, 15, 20; III, 7; VI, 4, 11; VII, 9, 39, 49; VIII, 25, 37; IX, 12, 25, 47, 52; XV, 17; XVI, 3; XVIII, 4, 7, 9, 11, 40; XIX, 12, 27; XX, 5, 14; John VI, 19, 52, 61; VII, 18, 35; VIII, 22, 31; IX, 22; XI, 38; XII, 19; XIII, 22, 32; XV, 4; XVI, 13, 17; XVII, 13; XIX, 8; Rom. XIII, 2; I Cor. XI, 29; XVI, 2; II Cor. V, 15, 19; X, 7, 12; Gal. V, 17; VI, 4, 12; Eph. II, 15, 16; V, 27; Phil. II, 3; III, 21; Col. II, 15; II Tim. IV, 3; Titus I, 14; *Skeir.* III, a; IV, a.

SIK, accusative, oneself: Matt. VI, 29; VIII, 18; IX, 21, 22; XI, [Col. 1438] 1, 20; XXVII, 5, 53; Mark I, 15; III, 20, 24, 25, 26, 34; IV, 1, 12; V, 5, 21, 30; VII, 1, 6; VIII, 33, 34, 38; IX, 2; X, 1, 35; XII, 33; XIV, 54, 67; XV, 31; Luke I, 24, 56; II, 39, 43, 45; IV, 1; VI, 18, 32; VII, 9, 10, 44; VIII, 37, 40; IX, 8, 10, 23, 26, 33; X, 11, 17, 29; XIV, 11, 12, 25, 31; XV, 1, 15; XVII, 3, 4, 15, 37; XVIII, 14; XIX, 12, 15; XX, 20; John VII, 4, 18; VIII, 59; IX, 21; XI, 33; XII, 4, 36, 48; XIII, 16; XVIII, 18, 25; XIX, 7, 12; Rom. X, 12, 11, 23; XIV, 14; I Cor. VII, 15; IX, 25; XI, 6, 28; XV, 7, 8, 28; XVI, 15; II Cor. V, 15; VIII, 5, 9; X, 7, 12, 18; XI, 13, 14, 15; Gal. I, 4; II, 12, 20; Eph. IV, 19; V, 2, 25, 28; Phil. I, 16; II, 6, 7, 8; Col. II, 15, 18; II Thess. II, 4; III, 14; I Tim. II, 6, 9, 11; V, 13, 25; VI, 10; II Tim. I, 15, 16; II, 4, 13, 21; III, 2, 3, 7; IV, 4; Philem. 15; *Skeir.* I, a; II, a; III, a; IV, c; V, a; VII, a.

SEINS, possessive pronoun, one’s own, standing for ὁ ἑαυτοῦ, αὑτῆς, αὑτῶν: Matt. V, 22, 28, 32, 45; VI, 2, 5, 7, 16, 27, 29; VII, 24, 26; VIII, 22; IX, 37, 38; X, 24, 38, 39, 42; XI, 1, 2, 19; XXVI, 1; XXVII, 60; Mark I, 5, 6, 18, 20; II, 6; III, 7, 9; IV, 2, 3, 34; V, 26; VI, 1, 4, 21, 24; VII, 30, 33; VIII, 6, 10, 12, 27, 33, 34, 35, 36, 37, 38; IX, 18, 31, 41; X, 7, 11, 12, 23, 50; XI, 1, 7, 8, 23; XII, 19, 38; XIII, 16, 24, 27; XIV, 13, 63; XV, 29; Luke I, 7, 15, 18, 23, 36, 48, 51, 54, 56, 58, 66, 68, 70, 72; II, 7, 8, 19, 28, 39, 51; III, 15, 17; IV, 10, 24; V, 15, 25, 29; VI, 13, 20, 45; VII, 1, 16, 19, 35, 38, 44; VIII, 5, 41, 43; IX, 14, 23, 24, 26, 43, 51, 60, 62; X, 1, 2, 7; XIV, 21, 27, 33; XV, 5, 13, 15, 20, 22; XVI, 1, 4, 5, 8, 18, 23; XVII, 33; XVIII, 13, 14; XIX, 13, 29, 35, 36; XX, 45; John III, 4; VI, 3, 12, 22; X, 11; XI, 2, 16, 28; XII, 3, 25; XIII, 18; XV, 22; XVIII, 2; Rom. VIII, 3; I Cor. X, 24; XI, 4, 5 (6); XIII, 5; II Cor. II, 14; XI, 3; Gal. IV, 4, 6, 25; V, 24; VI, 4, 8; Eph. I, 5, 6, 11, 20; II, 7, 15; III, 16; IV, 16, 25; V, 28, 29; Phil. II, 4, 30; Col. I, 13; II, 18; I Thess. II, 12; IV, 4, 6 (II Tim. III, 4); Titus I, 3; *Skeir.* I, d; II, c; III, a; IV, a; VII, c; VIII, b; αὐτοῦ, “his”: Mark V, 17; VI, 17; VII, 12; VIII, 23; X, 46; Luke I, 8, 20, 69, 80; III, 17; IV, 16; VI, 18, 40; VII, 12; XIV, 26; XVII, 24; XVIII, 7; XX, 28; John XIII, 16; XV, 20; I Cor. XVI, 19; Eph. IV, 17, 18; Phil. III, 21; I Thess. III, 13; ἴδιος, “one’s own”: Matt. IX, 1; Luke II, 3; John VII, 18; VIII, 44; Rom. X, 3; XIV, 4; I Cor. VII, 11; XI, 21; XV, 23; Eph. V, 22, 24; I Tim. III, 4, 5, 12; VI, 1; II Tim. I, 9; IV, 3; instead of the Greek article: Matt. VIII, 20; Mark I, 41; VII, 10, 11; Luke VII, 44; X, 21, 23; II Cor. VIII, 4; Col. II, 14; II Thess. I, 11. SEITEINS, the same as *Sinteins*.

SELS (Old Norse *säll*, Old High German *salic*, Anglo-Saxon *sel*, Old Saxon *selich*, Danish *salig*, Modern High German *selig*; Latin *salus*; compare Swedish and Danish *usel*; Gr. II, 54; III, 602; Gf. VI, 179; Rchth. 1005), adjective, good, ἀγαθός: Luke VIII, 15; kind, χρηστός: Eph. IV, 32; *sels visan*, to act kindly, χρηστεύεσθαι: I Cor. XIII, 4. UN-SELS, evil, wicked, πονηρός: Matt. V, 39; VI, 23; Mark VII, 22; Luke VI, 35; XIX, 22; John XVII, 15; Eph. VI, 16; without love of goodness, ἀφιλάγαθος: II Tim. III, 3. SELEI, feminine, goodness, kindness, χρηστότης: Rom. XI, 22; II Cor. VI, 6; Gal. V, 22; Eph. II, 7; Col. III, 12; ἀγαθωσύνη, goodness: Eph. V, 9. UN-SELEI, wickedness, malice, πονηρία: Mark VII, 22; Luke XX, 23; I Cor. V, 8; Eph. VI, 12; κακία, evil: Eph. IV, 31; Col. III, 8; ἀδικία, unrighteousness: II Tim. VI, 19 [probably an erroneous citation]; *Skeir.* I, d; VIII, a, b, d. SEM, masculine proper name, Σήμ, “Shem”: Luke III, 36. SENEIGS, see under *Sins*. SETS, see under *Sitan*.

*SI* … in *sium, sijum, sind, sijau*, etc., see under *Visan*. SI (English *she*, Modern High German *sie*), feminine singular of the third-person personal pronoun, she, see *Is*. SIBAKþANEI (Hebrew vocative), σαβαχθανί, “sabachthani”: Mark XV, 34.

*SIBIS* (Old Norse *sifi*, Anglo-Saxon *sib*, Old Saxon *sibbia*, Old French, Old High German *sibba*, Modern High German [Col. 1439] *sipp*; compare *Sifan*; DRA. 467; Gf. VI, 65; Rchth. 1011), adjective, freeborn, sincere, genuine. UN-SIBIS, lawless, ungodly; ἄνομος: Mark XV, 28; ἀσεβής: I Tim. I, 9. SIBJA, feminine, kinship; *sunive sibja*, adoption, υἱοθεσία: Gal. IV, 5. UN-SIBJA, lawlessness, ἀνομία: Matt. VII, 23; see at this passage. FRASTI-SIBJA, adoption, υἱοθεσία: Rom. IX, 4. GA-SIBJON, conjugation II, to be reconciled, διαλλάττεσθαι: Matt. V, 24.

SIBUN (Old Norse *siö*, Anglo-Saxon *seofon*, Old Saxon and Old High German *sibun*, Old French *soven, saven*, English *seven*, Swedish *siu*, Danish *syv*, Dutch *zeven*, Modern High German *sieben*; Latin *septem*, Greek ἑπτά; Gr. I, 762; Gf. VI, 68; Rchth. 1013), indeclinable numeral, seven, ἑπτά: Mark VIII, 5, 6, 20; XII, 20; XVI, 9; Luke II, 36; VIII, 2; XVII, 4; XX, 9, 33. SIBUNTEHUND, seventy, ἑβδομήκοντα: Luke X, 1, 17.

SIGGQAN (*Sigqan*, Luke IV, 40; V, 7; Old Norse *syqa*, Anglo-Saxon *sigan, sincan*, Old Saxon *sigan, sincan, senkian*, Old High German *sigan, sinchan*, Old French *siga*, English *sink*, Swedish *sjunka, sänka*, Danish *synke, soenke*, Dutch *zinken*, Modern High German *sinken, senken*; Gr. II, 36; Gf. VI, 130; Rchth. 1012), conjugation I, *saggq, suggqun, suggqans*, to sink, be submerged, βαθίζεσθαι: Luke V, 7; to set, δύνειν: Luke IV, 40. GA-SIGGQAN, the same, δύνειν: Mark I, 32; to be swallowed up, καταπίνεσθαι: II Cor. II, 7. DIS-SIGGQAN, the same, ἐπιδύνειν: Eph. IV, 26. SAGGQS, masculine, west; setting sun, δυσμή: Matt. VIII, 11. SAGGQJAN, conjugation II, to sink, drown, βυθίζειν: I Tim. VI, 9. UF-SAGQJAN, to swallow up, καταπίνειν: I Cor. XV—

SIGGVAN (Old Norse *syngia, siunga*, Old High German, Old Saxon, Anglo-Saxon *singan*, Old French *sionga*, English *sing*, Swedish *sjunga*, Danish *synge*, Dutch *zingen*, Modern High German *singen*; Gr. II, 36; Rchth. 1016), conjugation I, *saggv, suggvun, suggvans*: 1) to sing, ᾄδειν: Eph. V, 19; Col. III, 16; 2) to read aloud, ἀναγιγνώσκειν: Luke IV, 16; II Cor. III, 15; Eph. III, 4. US-SIGGVAN, to read aloud, read, ἀναγιγνώσκειν: Mark II, 25; Luke VI, 3; X, 26; Gal. IV, 21, at this passage; Col. IV, 16; I Thess. V, 27. SAGGVS, masculine (plural *saggveis*), song, music, συμφωνία: Luke XV, 25; song, ᾠδή: Eph. V, 19; Col. III, 16; 2) reading, recitation; *saggvs boko*, reading of a book, ἀνάγνωσις: I Tim. IV, 13. SIGIS (Old Norse *sigr*, Old Saxon *sigi*, Old High German
sigu, Anglo-Saxon *sigor*, Old Frisian *si*, Swedish *seger*, Danish *seir*, Dutch *zege*, Modern High German *Sieg*; Gf. VI, 131; Rchth. 1010), neuter, victory, **νῖκος** “victory”: 1 Cor. 15:54, 55, 57.

**SIGIS-LAUN**, see under *Laun*.

**SIGLJAN** (Old Norse *segel*, Anglo-Saxon *sigel*, Old High German *sigiljan*, Old Irish *sigelia*, English *seal*, Swedish *insegel*, Danish *indsegl*, Dutch *zegel*, Modern High German *Siegel*; Latin *sigillum*; Gf. VI, 144; Rchth. 1013), second conjugation, to seal, **σφραγίζεσθαι** “to be sealed”: 2 Cor. 1:22.

**GA-SIGLJAN**, the same, **σφραγίζειν** “to seal”: John 6:27; Eph. 1:13; 4:30.

**FAUR-SIGLJAN**, to mark with a seal, **σφραγίξειν** “to seal”: Matt. 27:66.

**SIGLJO**, neuter, seal, **σφραγίς**: 1 Cor. 9:2; 2 Tim. 2:19.

**SIDUS** (Old Norse *síðr*, Anglo-Saxon and Old Saxon *sidu*, Old High German *situ*, Old Frisian *side*, Swedish *sed*, Danish *saeder*, Dutch *zeden*, Modern High German *Sitte*; Gr. II, 46; Gf. VI, 159; Rchth. 1012), masculine, custom, usage, habit, **ἦθος**: 1 Cor. 15:33; 2 Tim. 3:10, see the note on this passage; *Skeireins* III, b.

**SIDON**, second conjugation, to meditate, **μελετᾶν**: 1 Tim. 4:15.

**+SIHORA** (Old Norse *sira*, Anglo-Saxon *sigora*; Gr. II, 476; DM. 18, 96), masculine, lord. In Augustine, *Epistle* 178 [col. 1440], it is permissible to say that not only barbarians in their own language, but Romans too, say *sihora armen*, which is interpreted “Lord, have mercy.” In place of *armen*, some wish to read *armai*, in order to make Augustine’s translation and the Gothic word agree; others read *arman* (an infinitive for an imperative). Some regard this formula as Vandalic rather than Gothic. For the rest, consult Zahn, *Einleitung*, p. 89 ff., for explanations and the various Western readings.

**SIK**, see under *Seina*.

**SIKLS** (a Hebrew word), masculine, shekel, **δίδραχμον** “didrachm”: Neh. 5:15.

**\*SILAN** (Latin *silere*), second conjugation, to be silent.

**ANA-SILAN**, to become calm, of the wind, **κοπάζειν**: Mark 4:39.

**SILBA** (Old Norse *sialf*, Old High German *selb*, Old Saxon *self*, Anglo-Saxon *sylf*, Old Frisian *self, selva*, English *self*, Swedish *sjelf*, Danish *sjelv*, Dutch *zelf*, Modern High German *selber*; Gr. III, 5; Gf. VI, 193; Rchth. 1004 ff.), pronoun:

a) self, himself, herself, itself, **αὐτός**: Matt. 27:57; Mark 12:36, 37; 15:43; Luke 1:17, 23; 2:35; 3:23; 4:41; 5:1, 37; 6:3, 42; 7:12; 17:13; 20:42; John 6:6; 9:21, 23; 12:24; 16:27; Rom. 7:25; 9:3; 1 Cor. 9:20, 27; 15:28; subscription; 2 Cor. 1:4, 9; 10:1; 11:14; 12:13; Gal. 2:17; 5:14; Eph. 2:20; 4:11; 5:27; Phil. 2:24; 1 Thess. 3:3, 11; 4:9, 16; 5:2, 23; 2 Thess. 1:4; 2:16; 3:7, 16; *Skeireins* I, a; V, d. **αὐτόματος**, “of itself”: Mark 4:28.

b) **ἑαυτοῦ**, “of himself / herself / itself”: Col. 3:13. But it is commonly used to form the reflexives **ἐμαυτοῦ**, “of myself,” **σεαυτοῦ**, “of yourself,” and **ἑαυτοῦ**, “of himself / herself / itself.” In that case the personal pronoun is added, and both are:

aa) ordinarily placed in the same case: Matt. 8:4; 9:3; Mark 1:44; 3:26; 5:30; 8:34; 12:31; 15:30, 31; Luke 4:23; 5:14; 7:7; 8:49; 9:23, 25; 10:27; 14:11; 16:15; 18:4, 14; John 6:53, 61; 7:4; 17:18, 28; 8:13, 14, 18, 22, 28, 42, 53, 54; 10:18; 11:33, 38; 12:49; 14:3, 10, 21, 22; 15:4; 16:13; 17:5, 19; 18:34; 19:7, 12; Rom. 11:25; 12:16, 18, 19; 13:9; 14:14; 1 Cor. 4:3, 4; 5:13; 7:7; 11:28, 29, 31; 16:2; 2 Cor. 1:9; 3:1, 5; 4:2, 5; 5:12, 15; 8:5; 10:7, 12, 18; 11:7, 9; 12:5; 13:5; Gal. 1:4; 2:18, 20; 5:14; 6:1, 3, 4; Eph. 2:15, 16; 4:19; 5:2, 25, 28; Phil. 2:7, 8; 3:13; Col. 3:16; 2 Thess. 3:9; 1 Tim. 2:6; 4:16; 6:10; 2 Tim. 2:13, 15; Philem. 19.

bb) Yet also in different cases: Luke (2:35; 14:26) 18:9; Rom. 13:2; Gal. 6:4; Eph. 5:27, 28.

*is silba*, “he himself,” **αὐτός**: Luke 5:1; 7:12; 1 Cor. 15:28.

*þata silbo*, “this very thing,” **αὐτὸ τοῦτο**: Rom. 13:6; 2 Cor. 7:11; Gal. 2:10; **τοῦτο αὐτό**, “this very thing”: 2 Cor. 2:3; **τοῦτο**, “this”: 2 Cor. 2:1, see the note on this passage.

*seins silbins*, “of his own self,” **ὁ ἑαυτοῦ**: Luke 14:26; Gal. 6:4. The personal pronoun is also absent in 1 Cor. 10:29.

**SILBA-VILJANDS**, see under *Vilja*.

**SILBA-VILEIS**, see under *Vilja*.

**SILBA-SIUNEIS**, see under *Siuns*.

**SILBANUS**, masculine proper name, **Σιλουανός**, “Silvanus”: 2 Cor. 1:19; 2 Thess. 1:1.

**\*SILD** (Old Norse *sialþan*, Anglo-Saxon *seldan*, Old High German *seltan*, Old Frisian *selden, sielden, seldlik*, English *seldom*, Swedish *sellan*, Danish *sjeldan*, Modern High German *selten*; Gf. VI, 216; Rchth. 1004), rare, unusual.

**SILDA-LEIKS**, see under *Leiks*.

**SILUBR** (Old Norse *silfr*, Anglo-Saxon *seolfer*, Old Saxon *silubar*, Old High German *silbar*, Old Frisian *selover, silver*, English *silver*, Swedish *silfver*, Danish *solv*, Dutch *zilver*, Modern High German *Silber*; Gf. VI, 214; Rchth. 1006), neuter, silver, **ἀργύριον**: Matt. 27:5; Luke 19:15, 23; Neh. 5:15.

**SILUBREINS** (*silubrins*, Matt. 27:3), adjective, silver, made of silver, **ἀργυροῦς**: 2 Tim. 2:20. Neuter *silubrein*, used substantivally: a silver coin, **ἀργύριον**: Matt. 27:3, 9.

**SILOAM**, masculine proper name, **Σιλωάμ**, “Siloam”: John 9:7.

**SIMLE** (Anglo-Saxon *symle*, Old Saxon *simbla*, Old High German *simblun, simbler*; Latin *semel*; Gf. VI, 26), adverb, once, ever, **ποτέ**: Rom. 7:9; Gal. 1:23; 2:6; Eph. 2:2, 11, 13; Col. 1:21; 3:7.

**SINAPS** (Anglo-Saxon *senepe*, Swedish *senap*, Danish [lacuna] *sennep*, Modern High German *Senf*; Greek **σίναπι**), masculine, mustard, **σίναπι**: Mark 4:31; Luke 17:6.

**\*SINDO**, see under *Sinþan*.

**\*SINÞAN** (Old Norse *sinn*, Old Saxon *sith, sithon, gisith*, Anglo-Saxon *sið, siðian*, Old High German *sind*, Old Frisian *sith, sid*, Danish *sinde*; Gr. II, 34; Rchth. 1018), first conjugation, *sanþ, sunþun, sunþans*, to go, make a journey.

**SINÞ**, neuter (?), 1) going; 2) occasion, time.

*ainamma sinþa*, “on one occasion,” once, **ἅπαξ**: 2 Cor. 11:25; Phil. 4:16; 1 Thess. 2:18.

*anþaramma sinþa*, “on another occasion,” **ἐκ δευτέρου**, “a second time”: Mark 14:72; John 9:24; **τὸ δεύτερον**, “the second time”: 2 Cor. 13:2.

*tvaim sinþam*, “on two occasions,” twice, **δίς**: Mark 14:72; Luke 18:12; Phil. 4:16; 1 Thess. 2:18.

*þrim sinþam*, “on three occasions,” three times, **τρίς**: Matt. 26:75; Mark 14:72; John 13:38; 2 Cor. 11:25; 12:8.

*fimf sinþam*, “on five occasions,” five times, **πεντάκις**: 2 Cor. 11:24.

*sibun sinþam*, seven times, **ἑπτάκις**: Luke 17:4.

**GA-SINÞA** and **GA-SINÞJA**, masculine, fellow traveller, **συνέκδημος**: 2 Cor. 8:19; plural, companions, travelling party, **συνοδία**: Luke 2:44.

**MIÞGA-SINÞA**, fellow companion, **συνέκδημος**: 2 Cor. 8:19, see the note on this passage.

**\*SINDO**, adverb.

**US-SINDO**, especially, chiefly, **μάλιστα**: Philem. 16.

**SANDJAN** (Old Norse *senda*, Anglo-Saxon *sendan*, Old Saxon *sendian*, Old High German *santan*, Old Frisian *senda*, English *send*, Swedish *sända*, Danish *sende*, Modern High German *senden*; Rchth. 1007), second conjugation, to send, **πέμπειν**: Luke 20:11, 12, 13; John 5:37; 6:38, 40, 44; 7:16, 18, 28, 33; 8:16; 9:4; 12:44, 49; 13:16, 20; 14:24, 26; 15:21; 16:5, 7; 1 Cor. 16:3; Phil. 2:23, 25; Neh. 6:17; **ἀποστέλλειν**, “to send forth”: Matt. 10:40; Mark 9:37; Luke 9:48; 10:16; John 5:36.

**GA-SANDJAN**, to send onward, escort, **προπέμπειν**: 1 Cor. 16:6; 2 Cor. 1:16.

**FAURAGA-SANDJAN**, to send beforehand, **πέμπειν**: 2 Cor. 9:3.

**IN-SANDJAN**, 1) to send, **πέμπειν**: Matt. 11:2; Mark 5:12; Luke 4:26; 7:6, 10, 19; 15:15; John 13:20; 15:26; Rom. 8:3; Eph. 6:22; Phil. 2:28; 4:16; Col. 4:8; 1 Thess. 3:2, 5; *Skeireins* VI, c; **ἀποστέλλειν**, “to send forth”: Matt. 11:10; 27:19; Mark 1:2; 3:14, 31; 4:29; 6:7, 17, 27; 8:26; 11:1, 3; 12:3, 4, 5, 6, 13; 13:27; 14:13; Luke 1:19, 26; 4:18, 43; 7:3, 27; 9:2, 52; 10:1, 3; 14:17, 32; 19:14, 29, 32; 20:10, 20; John 5:38; 6:29, 57; 7:29, 32; 8:42; 10:36; 11:42; 12:3; 17:3, 8, 18, 21, 24; Rom. 10:15; 1 Cor. 1:17; 2 Cor. 12:17; 2 Tim. 4:12; Neh. 6:19; **ἐξαποστέλλειν**, “to send out”: Luke 20:10; Gal. 4:4, 6.

2) To send, **[ἀνα]πέμπειν**: Philem. 11.

3) To send onward, escort, **προπέμπειν**: 1 Cor. 16:11.

**MIÞIN-SANDJAN** (*insandjan miþ*), to send with, **συμπέμπειν**: 2 Cor. 8:22; **συναποστέλλειν**: 2 Cor. 12:18.

**MIÞ-SANDJAN**, the same, **συμπέμπειν**: 2 Cor. 8:18.

**US-SANDJAN**, to cast out, dismiss, **ἐκβάλλειν**: Matt. 9:38; Mark 1:43.

**SINS** (Old High German *sene-skalk*, Swedish *sen*, Danish *seen*; Latin *senex*; Gr. III, 617; DRA. 267, 302; compare *sinistus*, Ammianus Marcellinus 28.5; Mone, *Geschichte des nordischen Heidenthums* II, 165), adjective, old; superlative *sinista*, oldest, eldest, **πρεσβύτερος**: Matt. 27:1, 3; Mark 7:3, 5; 8:31; 11:27; 14:43, 53; 15:1; Luke 7:3; 9:22; 20:1.

**SINEIGS** (*seneigs*, 1 Tim. 5:1, 2), adjective, old man, elder, **πρεσβύτης**: Luke 1:18; **πρεσβύτερος**: 1 Tim. 5:1, 2.

**SINTEINS** (*seiteins*, 2 Cor. 11:28; Gr. I, 68 [3rd edition]; II, 216; compare Old High German *sin*; Gf. VI, 25), adjective, daily, **ὁ καθ’ ἡμέραν**, “the daily [burden]”: 2 Cor. 11:28; **ἐπιούσιος**, “daily”: Matt. 6:11; *Skeireins* III, b.

**SINTEINO**, adverb, always, everywhere, **πάντοτε**: Mark 14:7; Luke 15:31; 18:1; John 7:6; 8:29; 11:42; 12:8; 18:20; 1 Cor. 15:58; 2 Cor. 2:14; 4:10; 5:6; 9:8; Gal. 4:18; Eph. 5:20; 6:18; Phil. 1:20; 4:4; Col. 4:6, 12; 1 Thess. 2:16; 3:6; 5:15, 16; 2 Thess. 1:3, 11; 2 Tim. 3:7; **διὰ παντός**, “continually”: Mark 5:5; 2 Thess. 3:16; **ἀεί**, “always”: Mark 15:8; 2 Cor. 4:11; 6:10; Titus 1:12.

**SIUKAN** (Old Norse *siukr, sott*, Old Saxon *sioc, suht*, Anglo-Saxon *seoc*, Old High German *siuh, siuhjan, suht*, Old Frisian *siek, sechte*, English *sick*, Swedish *sjuk*, Danish *syg*, Dutch *ziek*, Modern High German *siech, Seuche, Sucht*; Latin *saucius*; Gr. II, 50; DM. 670; Gf. VI, 137; Rchth. 1002, 1610), first conjugation, *sauk, sukun, sukans*, to be ill, **ἀσθενεῖν**: 2 Cor. 11:29; 12:10; 13:3, 4, 9; Phil. 2:26; **κακῶς ἔχειν**, “to be unwell”: Luke 7:2; **νοσεῖν**, “to be diseased”: 1 Tim. 6:4.

**SIUKS**, adjective, sick, weak, **ἀσθενής**: Matt. 25:39; Luke 10:9; 1 Cor. 8:10; 11:30; 1 Thess. 5:14; **ἀσθενῶν**, “being sick”: Mark 6:56; Luke 4:40; 7:10; John 6:2; 11:1, 2, 3; 1 Cor. 8:12; **ἄρρωστος**, “ill”: Mark 6:5, 13. *siuks visan*, “to be sick,” **ἀσθενεῖν**: John 11:3, 6; Rom. 8:3; 2 Cor. 11:21; Phil. 2:27.

**SIUKEI**, feminine, illness, weakness, **ἀσθένεια**: John 11:4; 2 Cor. 11:30; 12:9, 10; 13:4; Gal. 4:13.

**SAUHTS**, feminine, the same, illness, weakness, **ἀσθένεια**: Matt. 8:17; Luke 5:15; 8:2; 1 Tim. 5:23; **νόσος**, “disease”: Matt. 9:35; Mark 1:34; 3:15; Luke 4:40; 6:18; 7:21; 9:1.

**SIUNS** (Old Norse *sion, syn*, Anglo-Saxon *siene*, Old Saxon *siun*, Old High German *siuni*, Old Frisian *siune*, Swedish *syn*; compare *Saiwan*; Gr. II, 28; Gf. VI, 127; Rchth. 1018), feminine:

1) sight, faculty of sight, **ἀνάβλεψις**: Luke 4:19; **τὸ βλέπειν**, “the ability to see”: Luke 7:21.

2) sight, appearance, **εἶδος**: 2 Cor. 5:7.

3) passively, vision, **ὀπτασία**: Luke 1:22; 2 Cor. 12:1. *in siunai wairþan*, “to appear,” **ὅρασθαι**: Luke 1:11.

4) sight, form, appearance, **εἶδος**: Luke 3:22; 9:29; John 5:37; *Skeireins* VI, d; **ὄψις**, “appearance”: John 7:24.

**ANA-SIUNS**, adjective, visible: *Skeireins* II, d.

**UNANA-SIUNIBA**, adverb, invisibly: *Skeireins* VIII, a.

**SILBA-SIUNEIS**, masculine, eyewitness, **αὐτόπτης**: Luke 1:2.

**SIUJAN** (Anglo-Saxon *sivian*, Old High German *siwian*, Old Frisian *sia*, English *sew*, Swedish *sy*, Danish *sye*; Latin *suere*; Gf. VI, 61; Rchth. 1010), second conjugation, to sew, **ἐπιρράπτειν**: Mark 2:21.

**SIPONEIS**, masculine, disciple, **μαθητής**: Matt. 8:18, 21, 23; 9:10, 11, 14, 19, 37; 10:24, 25, 42; 11:1, 2; 27:64; Mark 2:15, 18; 3:7; 4:34; 6:1, 29; 7:2; 5:17; 9:14, 28, 31; 10:10, 23, 24; 11:1, 15; 14:12, 13, 14; 16:7; Luke 5:30, 33; 6:1, 13, 17, 20, 40; 7:11, 18, 19; 8:9; 9:14, 40, 43, 54; 14:26, 27, 33; 16:1; 17:22; 18:15; 19:29, 37, 39; 20:45; John 3:25; 6:3, 17; 7:3; 8:31; 9:27, 28; 11:7, 8; 18:15; *Skeireins* IV, a; V, d; VII, d.

**SIPONJAN**, second conjugation, to be a disciple, **μαθητεύειν**: Matt. 27:57.

**SIS**, see under *Seina*.

**SITAN** (Old Norse *sittia, setia*, Anglo-Saxon *sittan, setl*, Old Saxon *sittian, settian*, Old High German *sizzan*, Old Frisian *sitta, setta*, English *sit, set*, Swedish *sitta, sätta*, Danish *sidde, setle*, Dutch *zitten*, Modern High German *sitzen, setzen*; Latin *sedere, sedare*; Greek **ἔζεσθαι, ἵζειν**; Gr. II, 25; III, 433; Rchth. 1008, 1019), first conjugation, *sat, setun, sitans*, to sit, **καθῆσθαι**: Matt. 9:9; 11:16; 26:69; 27:19, 61; Mark 2:6, 14; 3:32, 34; 5:15; 10:46; 12:36; 14:62; 16:5; Luke 1:79; 5:17, 27; 7:32; 8:35; 10:13; 18:35; 20:42; John 9:8; 12:15; Col. 3:1; **συγκαθῆσθαι**, “to sit with”: Mark 14:54; **καθίζεσθαι**, “to sit down”: Luke 2:46; John 11:20; **καθίζειν**, “to cause to sit / sit”: Mark 9:35; 10:37, 40; 11:2; Luke 19:30; 2 Thess. 2:4.

**AND-SITAN**, 1) to set again, examine, **ἀνακρίνειν**: 1 Cor. 10:27; *Skeireins* VIII, b; 2) to remain, receive, **λαμβάνειν**: Gal. 2:6.

**BI-SITAN**, to dwell around, **περιοικεῖν**: Luke 1:65. *bi-sitands*, present participle used substantivally, one dwelling around, neighbour, **περίοικος**: Luke 1:58; **περίχωρος**, “surrounding district”: Mark 1:28; Luke 4:14; 7:17.

**GA-SITAN**, to sit, **καθῆσθαι**: Mark 4:1; John 6:3; **καθίζειν**: Mark 11:7; Luke 4:20; 5:3; 14:28, 31; 16:6; John 12:14.

**DIS-SITAN**, to take, seize, grasp, **λαμβάνειν**: Luke 5:26; 7:16; **ἔχειν**, “to have”: Mark 16:8.

**US-SITAN**, to rise up, sit up, **ἀνακαθίζειν**: Luke 7:15.

**SITLS**, masculine:

1) seat, chair, **καθέδρα**: Mark 11:15; **θρόνος**, “throne”: Col. 1:16.

2) nest, lodging-place, **κατασκήνωσις**: Matt. 8:20; Luke 9:58.

**ANDA-SETS**, adjective, abominable, detestable, execrable, **βδελυκτός**: Titus 1:16.

**ANDASET**, neuter, abomination, **βδέλυγμα**: Luke 16:15.

**SATJAN**, second conjugation, to put, set, **τιθέναι**: Mark 4:21; Rom. 14:13; 1 Thess. 5:9; **ἐπιτιθέναι**, “to place upon”: Mark 4:21; Luke 8:16; to plant, **φυτεύειν**: Luke 17:28; 1 Cor. 9:7. *satiþs visan*, “to be placed,” to lie, **κεῖσθαι**: 1 Thess. 3:3, see the note on this passage; 1 Tim. 1:9. *niuja satiþs*, “newly planted,” neophyte, **νεόφυτος**: 1 Tim. 3:6.

**AND-SATJAN** (?), to resist: *Skeireins* V, c.

**AT-SATJAN**, to set before, present, **παριστάναι**: Luke 2:22; Col. 1:22, 28.

**AF-SATJAN**, to remove, **μεθιστάναι**: Luke 16:4; to dismiss a wife, divorce, **ἀπολύειν**: Matt. 5:32; Mark 10:2.

**BI-SATJAN**, to surround, encircle, **περιτιθέναι**: Mark 12:1.

**GA-SATJAN**, 1) to put, set, **τιθέναι**: Luke 6:48; 8:16; 14:29; 1 Cor. 12:18; 1 Tim. 1:12; 2:7; 2 Tim. 1:11; **ἐπιτιθέναι**, “to put upon”: Luke 8:16; **καθιέναι**, “to let down”: Luke 5:19; **καθίζειν**, “to seat”: Eph. 1:20; **ἱστάναι**, “to set”: Mark 9:36; Luke 4:9; 9:47; Neh. 7:1. *gasatiþs visan*, “to be placed,” **κεῖσθαι**: Phil. 1:17. *aftra gasatjan*, “to set again,” restore, **ἀποκαθιστάναι**: Mark 8:25.

2) To appoint, ordain, **καθιστάναι**: Titus 1:5; *Skeireins* I, d; **τάσσειν**, “to arrange, appoint”: Luke 7:8; Rom. 13:1; 1 Cor. 16:15; compare Eph. 1:11.

3) To give a name, **ἐπιτιθέναι**: Mark 3:16, 17.

**MIÞGA-SATJAN**, to seat together, **συγκαθίζειν**: Eph. 2:6.

**FAURAGA-SATJAN** (*gasatjan faura*), to set before, present, **παριστάναι**: Rom. 14:10; 2 Cor. 4:14.

**MIÞ-SATJAN**, to arrange together, **μεθιστάνειν**: 1 Cor. 13:2.

**US-SATJAN**, 1) to place upon, **ἐπιβιβάζειν**: Luke 19:35.

2) To plant, **φυτεύειν**: Mark 12:1; Luke 17:6; 20:9; **ἐξανιστάναι**: Mark 12:19; **συνιστάναι**: Col. 1:17.

3) To compose: *Skeireins* II, d.

4) To cast out, **ἐκβάλλειν**: Luke 10:2, see the note on this passage.

**SATEINS**, feminine, planting, creation, origin: Eph. 2:3, see the note on this passage.

**AF-SATEINS**, divorce, apostasy, **ἀποστάσιον**: Mark 10:4.

**GA-SATEINS**, establishment, ordination, **καταβολή**: Eph. 1:4.

**US-SATEINS**, origin, beginning: Eph. 2:3, see the note on this passage (?).

**SIFAN** (Anglo-Saxon *sifian*; compare *Sibis*), second conjugation, to rejoice, be glad, **ἀγαλλιᾶσθαι**: John 8:56; **εὐφραίνεσθαι**: Rom. 15:10; Gal. 4:27.

**SION**, indeclinable proper name, **Σιών**, “Zion”: John 12:15; Rom. 9:33; 11:26.

**SKABAN** (Old Norse *skafa*, Anglo-Saxon *scafan*, Old High German *skapan*, English *shave*, Swedish *skafva*, Danish *skave*, Modern High German *schaben*; Gr. II, 9; Gf. VI, 405), first conjugation, *skof, skobun, skabans*, to shear, **κείρειν**: 1 Cor. 11:6.

**BI-SKABAN**, the same, to shave, **ξυρᾶν**: 1 Cor. 11:5.

**SKADUS** (Old Saxon *scado*, Anglo-Saxon *scead, scadu*, Old High German *skato*, English *shade*, Dutch *schaduw*, Modern High German *Schatten*, Old Norse *skuggi*, Swedish *skugge*, Danish *skygge*; Greek **σκιά, σκότος**; Gf. VI, 423), masculine, shadow, **σκιά**: Mark 4:32; Luke 1:79; Col. 2:17.

**UFAR-SKADVJAN**, second conjugation, to overshadow, cast a shadow over, **ἐπισκιάζειν**: Mark 9:7; Luke 1:35; 9:34.

**GA-SKADVEINS**, feminine, overshadowing, covering, **σκέπασμα**: 1 Tim. 6:8.

**SKAÞJAN** (Old Norse *skada, skedia*, Old Saxon *scatho*, Anglo-Saxon *sceðan*, Old High German *skadon*, Old Frisian *skatha, skathia*, English *scath*, Swedish *skada*, Danish *skade*, Dutch and Modern High German *schaden*; Gr. II, 11; Gf. VI, 421; Rchth. 1021), first conjugation, *skoþ, skoþun, skaþans*, to injure, wrong, **ἀδικεῖν**: Col. 3:25.

**GA-SKAÞJAN**, the same: Luke 10:19; 2 Cor. 7:2; Gal. 4:12; Philem. 18; **βλάπτειν**, “to injure”: Luke 4:35.

**SKAÞIS**, neuter, injustice, injury, **ἀδικία**: 2 Cor. 12:13.

**SKAÞULS**, adjective, harmful, **ἀδικῶν**, “doing wrong”: Col. 3:25; **βλαβερός**, “hurtful”: 1 Tim. 6:9.

**SKAIDAN** (Anglo-Saxon *sceadan*, Old Saxon *scethan*, Old High German *skeidan*, Old Frisian *sketha*, Swedish *skeda*, Danish *skede*, Dutch and Modern High German *scheiden*; Latin *scindere, scidi*; Greek **σκεδᾶν, σχίζειν**; Gf. VI, 428; Rchth. 1029), first conjugation, *skaiskaid, skaiskaidun, skaidans*, to divide, separate, part, **διχάζειν**: Matt. 10:35; **χωρίζειν**: Mark 10:9. *skaidan sik*, “to separate oneself,” **χωρίζεσθαι**: 1 Cor. 7:10; also without *sik*: 1 Cor. 7:10, 15.

**AF-SKAIDAN**, the same, **ἀφορίζειν**, “to separate”: Luke 6:22; Gal. 2:12; **χωρίζειν**: Rom. 8:35, 39. *afskaidan sik*, “to separate oneself,” **ἀφορίζεσθαι**: 2 Cor. 6:17; **διαχωρίζεσθαι**: Luke 9:33.

**GA-SKAIDAN**, to separate, withdraw, **στέλλεσθαι**: 2 Thess. 3:6.

**DIS-SKAIDAN**, to separate: *Skeireins* VIII, a.

**GA-SKAIDNAN**, third conjugation, to be separated, **χωρίζεσθαι**: 1 Cor. 7:11.

**GA-SKAIDEI**, feminine, 1) division; 2) distinction, **διαστολή**: Rom. 10:12.

**SKAL**, see under *Skulan*.

**SKALKS** (Old Norse *skalkr*, Old Saxon *scalc*, Anglo-Saxon *scealc*, Old High German and Old Frisian forms, Swedish and Danish *skalk*, Dutch and Modern High German *Schalk*; DRA. 302; Rchth. 1020), masculine, slave, servant, **δοῦλος**: Matt. 8:9; 10:24, 25; Mark 10:44; 12:2; 14:47; Luke 2:29; 7:2, 3, 8, 10; 14:17, 21, 22, 23; 15:22; 17:7, 9, 10; 19:13, 15, 17, 20; 20:10; John 13:16; 15:15, 20; 18:10, 18, 26; 1 Cor. 7:21, 22, 23; 12:13; 2 Cor. 4:5; Gal. 4:1, 7; Phil. 2:7; Col. 3:11; 4:12; 1 Tim. 6:1; 2 Tim. 2:24; Titus 1:1; Philem. 16; **παιδάριον**, “servant-boy”: Neh. 5:15; **οἰκέτης**, “household slave”: Rom. 14:4.

**GA-SKALKI**, neuter, fellow servant, **σύνδουλος**: Col. 1:7; 4:7.

**SKALKINON**, second conjugation, to serve, be enslaved, **δουλεύειν**: Matt. 6:24; Luke 15:29; 16:13; John 8:33; Rom. 7:6, 25; 9:12; 12:11; 14:18; Gal. 4:8, 9, 25; 5:13; 1 Tim. 6:2. Hence *in augam skalkinonds*, “serving for the eye,” **ἐν ὀφθαλμοδουλείᾳ**: Col. 3:22; **δεδουλῶσθαι**, “to be enslaved”: Gal. 4:3; **λατρεύειν**, “to render religious service”: Luke 1:74; Phil. 3:3; 2 Tim. 1:3; **προσκαρτερεῖν**, “to be devoted”: Rom. 13:6. *galiugam skalkinonds*, idolater, **εἰδωλολάτρης**; see under *Liugan*.

**MIÞ-SKALKINON**, to serve with, render service together, **δουλεύειν σύν—**: Phil. 2:22.

**SKALKINASSUS**, masculine, service, servitude, **δουλεία**: Gal. 5:1; **λατρεία**, “religious service”: Rom. 9:4. *galiugagude skalkinassus*, idolatry, **εἰδωλολατρεία**: Gal. 5:20; Eph. 5:5; Col. 3:5.

**SKALJA** (Old Norse *skál, skel*, Anglo-Saxon *sceala*, English *shell*, Swedish and Danish *skal*, Dutch *schaal, schalie*, Modern High German *Schale*; Gr. II, 54), feminine, tile, **κέραμος**: Luke 5:19.
