**SKAMAN** (Old Norse *skam, skammast, skömm*, Old Saxon *scamian*, Anglo-Saxon *sceamian*, Old Frisian *skome*, Old High German *schamen*, English *shame*, Swedish and Danish *skam*, Dutch *schaamen*, Modern High German *schämen*; Gr. II, 30; Rchth. 1032), second conjugation, to be ashamed. *skaman sik*, “to be ashamed,” **αἰσχύνεσθαι**: Luke 16:3; **ἐπαισχύνεσθαι**, “to be ashamed of”: Mark 3:38; Luke 9:26; 2 Tim. 1:8, 12, 16; **ἐξαπορεῖσθαι**, “to be utterly perplexed”: 2 Cor. 1:8, see the note on this passage.

**GA-SKAMAN SIK**, the same, **ἐντρέπεσθαι**, “to be ashamed”: 2 Thess. 3:14.

**SKANDA** (Anglo-Saxon *sceonde*, Old High German *skanta*, Old Frisian *skonde*, Modern High German *Schande*; Greek **σκάνδαλον**; compare *Skaman*; Gr. II, 11; Rchth. 1032), feminine, shame, disgrace, **αἰσχύνη**: Phil. 3:19.

**SKAUDA** (Gr. III, 450)?

**SKAUDA-RAIP**, see under *Raip*.

**SKAUNS** (Anglo-Saxon *sciene*, Old Saxon *sconi*, Old High German *skoni*, Old Frisian *skene, skone*, Swedish *skön*, Danish *skjon*, Dutch *schoon*, Modern High German *schön*; Rchth. 1026), adjective: 1) well formed; 2) beautiful, fair, **ὡραῖος**: Rom. 10:15.

**IBNA-SKAUNS**, conformed, **σύμμορφος**: Phil. 3:21.

**GUÞA-SKAUNEI**, feminine, form of God, **μορφὴ θεοῦ**: Phil. 2:6.

**SKAURPJO** (a Greek word), feminine, scorpion, **σκορπίος**: Luke 10:19.

**SKAURO**, see under *Skiuran*.

**SKAUTS** (Old Norse *skaut*, Anglo-Saxon *sceat*, Old High German *skoza*, Old Frisian *skat*, English *sheet*, Swedish *sköte*, Danish *skod*, Dutch *schoot*, Modern High German *Schoss*; Gr. II, 20; III, 406, 448; Rchth. 1021), masculine (?), hem or fringe of a garment, **κράσπεδον**: Matt. 9:20; Mark 6:56; Luke 8:44.

**\*SKAPJAN** (Old Norse and Swedish *skapa*, Old Saxon *scapan*, Anglo-Saxon *scyppan*, Old High German *skafan*, Old Frisian *skeppa*, English *shape*, Danish *skaffe*, Dutch *scheppen*, Modern High German *schaffen*; Gr. II, 9; Gf. VI, 442; Rchth. 1026), first conjugation, *skop, skopun, skapans*, to create.

**GA-SKAPJAN**, the same, **κτίζειν**: Mark 2:27; 13:19; Eph. 2:10, 15; 3:9; 4:24; Col. 1:16; 3:10; 1 Tim. 4:3.

**GA-SKAFTS**, feminine:

1) creation, created order, **κτίσις**: Mark 10:6; 13:19; Rom. 8:39; 2 Cor. 5:17; Gal. 6:15; Col. 1:15, 23; **καταβολή**, “foundation”: John 17:24.

2) creature, **κτίσμα**: 1 Tim. 4:4.

**UFAR-SKAFTS**, first portion, beginning, **ἀπαρχή**: Rom. 11:16.

**SKAFTJAN**, second conjugation, to create. *skaftjan sik*, to separate oneself, to be about to be, **μέλλειν**: John 12:4.

**SKARIOTES**, see *Iskariotes*.

**\*SKARJAN**, 2 Tim. 2:26, see the note on this passage.

**SKATTS** (Old Norse *skattr*, Old Saxon *scat*, Anglo-Saxon *sceat*, Old High German *skazz*, Old Frisian *sket*, Swedish *skatt*, Danish *skat*, Dutch *schat*, Modern High German *Schatz*; DM. 543; Rchth. 1028), masculine, silver money, **ἀργύριον**: Matt. 27:6; Luke 9:3; 19:16; **δηνάριον**, “denarius”: Mark 12:15; 14:5; Luke 7:41; 20:24; John 6:7; 12:5; mina, **μνᾶ**: Luke 19:16, 18, 20, 24.

**SKATTJA**, masculine, money-changer, **κολλυβιστής**: Mark 11:15. *atlagjan silubr du skattjam* (“to place silver with the money-changers”), **ἐπὶ τράπεζαν**: Luke 19:23.

**\*SKAVJAN** (Old Norse *skoda*, Anglo-Saxon *sceawian*, Old Saxon *scawon*, Old Frisian *skawia*, Old High German *scauuon*, Swedish *skåda*, Danish *skue*, Dutch *schouwen*, Modern High German *schauen*; Rchth. 1021), second conjugation, to look.

**US-SKAVJAN**, passive, or *usskavjan sis*, to recover one’s senses, **ἀνανήφειν**: 2 Tim. 2:26; **ἐκνήφειν**, “to come to one’s senses”: 1 Cor. 15:34.

**US-SKAVS**, adjective, prudent, sober-minded. *usskavs visan*, “to be sober,” **νήφειν**: 1 Thess. 5:8, see the note on this passage.

**UN-SKAVS**, see the note on 1 Thess. 5:8.

**SKAFTS**, see under *Skapjan*.

**SKEIMA** (Old Norse *skima*, Anglo-Saxon *sciman*, Old Saxon *scimo*, Old High German *skimen*, Modern High German *Schimmer*; Gr. II, 45; III, 391), masculine (?), light, brightness, **φανή**: John 18:3.

**SKEINAN** (Old Norse and Old Frisian *skina*, Old Saxon and Anglo-Saxon *scinan*, Old High German *skinan*, English *shine*, Swedish *sken, skyna*, Danish *skinne*, Dutch *schynen*, Modern High German *scheinen*; Gr. II, 12; Rchth. 1031), first conjugation, *skain, skinun, skinans*, to shine, gleam, **λάμπειν**: Luke 17:24; 2 Cor. 4:6; **ἐξαστράπτειν**, “to flash like lightning”: Luke 9:29.

**BI-SKEINAN**, to shine round about, **περιλάμπειν**: Luke 2:9.

**SKEIRS** (Old Norse *skirr, skira*, Old Saxon *scerian*, Anglo-Saxon *scir*, Old Frisian *skiria*, English *sheer*, Swedish *skär*, Danish *skjaer*, Modern High German *schier*; Gr. II, 45; Rchth. 1032), adjective, clear, evident: *Skeireins* IV, b; V, a.

**GA-SKEIRJAN**, to explain, interpret, **ἑρμηνεύειν**: John 9:7; **μεθερμηνεύειν**: Mark 5:41; 15:22, 34; *Skeireins* II, c.

**SKEIREINS** (*Skereins*, 1 Cor. 14:26), feminine, interpretation, **ἑρμηνεία**: 1 Cor. 12:10; 14:26.

**SKEVJAN** (English *shift*?), second conjugation, to make a journey, **ὁδὸν ποιεῖν**: Mark 2:23.

**SKILDUS** (Old Norse *skiöldr*, Anglo-Saxon *scyld*, Old Saxon *scild*, Old High German *skilt*, Old Frisian *skeld*, English *shield*, Swedish *sköld*, Danish *skjold*, Dutch and Modern High German *Schild*; Gr. III, 445; Rchth. 1022), masculine, shield, **θυρεός**: Eph. 6:16.

**SKILLIGGS** (Old Norse *skillingr*, Old Saxon and Anglo-Saxon *scilling*, English *shilling*, Old Frisian, Swedish, Danish *skilling*, Dutch *schelling*, Modern High German *Schilling*; Rchth. 1031), masculine, denarius; *docum* [uncertain]; Neapolitan [form].

**SKILJA** (Old Norse *skilia*, Anglo-Saxon *scylan*, Swedish *skilja*, Danish *skille*; Gr. II, 54), masculine, butcher. *þatei at skiljam (ἐν μακέλλῳ) frabugjada*, “whatever is sold in the meat market”: 1 Cor. 10:25.

**\*SKIUBAN** (Old Norse *skufa*, Anglo-Saxon *scufan*, Old Frisian *skuva*, Old High German *skiuban*, English *shove*, Swedish *skuffa*, Danish *skuffe*, Dutch *schuiven*, Modern High German *schieben*; Gr. II, 18; Gf. VI, 409; Rchth. 1035), first conjugation, *skauf, skubun, skubans*, to send, thrust.

**AF-SKIUBAN**, to remove, with dative, **ἀπωθεῖσθαι**, “to reject”: Rom. 11:1; 1 Tim. 1:19.

**\*SKIURAN** (Old Norse *skiarr, skur*, Anglo-Saxon and Old Saxon *scur*, Old High German *skiura, skur*, Old Frisian *skur, schur*, English *scour, shower*, Swedish *skura, skur*, Danish *skure*, Dutch *schuren, scheure*, Modern High German *Scheuer, Schauer*; Gr. II, 48; III, 388, 417; Rchth. 1034), first conjugation, *skaur, skurun, skurans*, to be violently agitated.

**VINÞI-SKAURO**, feminine, winnowing shovel, **πτύον**: Luke 3:17.

**SKURA**, feminine, roaring, tumult. *skura windis*, whirlwind, **λαῖλαψ**: Mark 4:37; Luke 8:23.

**SKIP** (Old Norse and Old Frisian *skip*, Anglo-Saxon and Old Saxon *scip*, Old High German *skif*, English *ship*, Swedish *skepp*, Danish *skib*, Dutch *schip*, Modern High German *Schiff*; Greek **σκάφη**; Gr. III, 435; Gf. VI, 455; Rchth. 1031), neuter, ship, **πλοῖον**: Matt. 8:23, 24; Mark 1:19, 20; 4:1, 36, 37; 5:2, 18, 21; 6:54; Luke 5:2, 3, 7, 11; 8:37; John 6:17, 19, 21, 24; **πλοιάριον**, “little boat”: Mark 3:9; John 6:22, 23. *usfarþon gataujan us skipa*, “to undergo shipwreck,” **ναυαγεῖν**: 2 Cor. 11:25.

**SKUGGVA** (compare *Skavjan*; compare Old High German *scucar*; Gf. VI, 405, 420), masculine, mirror, **ἔσοπτρον**: 1 Cor. 13:12.

**SKULAN** (Old Norse *skula*, Anglo-Saxon *sculon*, Old Saxon *sculan*, Old High German *skolan*, Old Frisian *skila, skelde, skuld*, English *shall*, Swedish *skola*, Danish *skulle*, Dutch *zullen*, Modern High German *sollen, Schuld*; Gr. II, 28; Gf. VI, 461; Rchth. 1022, 1030), anomalous conjugation; present *skal, skulun*; preterite *skulda*; participle *skulds*:

1) to owe, be a debtor, **ὀφείλειν**: Luke 7:41; 16:5, 7.

2) to be obliged, ought, **ὀφείλειν**: Luke 17:10; John 13:14; 19:7; 1 Cor. 5:10; 15:2; 2 Cor. 12:14; Eph. 5:28; 2 Thess. 1:3; **δεῖν**, “it is necessary”: Mark 8:31; 9:11; Luke 2:49; 4:43; 9:22; 17:25; 18:1; 19:5; John 3:30; 9:4; 10:10; Rom. 12:3; 1 Cor. 15:25; 2 Cor. 2:3; Eph. 6:20; Col. 4:4, 6; 1 Tim. 3:2, 7; 2 Tim. 2:6, 24; Titus 1:11; *Skeireins* I, d; V, c.

3) to be about to be, marking the future: Luke 1:66; **μέλλειν**, “to be about to”: Matt. 11:14; Luke 9:31; John 7:35, 36, 39; 12:33; 2 Tim. 4:1; **ἔχειν**, “to have [to]”: Luke 7:40; John 8:26; 16:12.

**SKULDS**, participle, owed, due. *skulds visan*:

1) to be owed, to be necessary, in a passive sense—that is, with the following verb having passive meaning—**δεῖν**: Luke 15:32; John 12:34; 2 Cor. 5:10; 11:30; 2 Thess. 3:7; 1 Tim. 3:15; 5:13; Titus 1:11; Mark 8:31; **ὀφείλειν**: 2 Cor. 12:11.

2) To be permitted, lawful, **ἐξεῖναι**: Matt. 27:6; Mark 2:24; 3:4; 6:18; 10:2; 12:14; Luke 6:2, 4; 20:22; John 18:31; 2 Cor. 12:4; *Skeireins* VI, d.

3) To be about to be, marking the passive future, **μέλλειν**: Luke 9:44; 19:11.

**SKULDO**, neuter, debt, **ὀφειλή**: Rom. 13:7.

**SKULA**, masculine, debtor, **ὀφειλέτης**: Matt. 6:12; Gal. 5:3; **ἔνοχος**, “liable, guilty”: Matt. 5:22; 26:66; Mark 3:29; 14:64; 1 Cor. 11:27. *skula visan*, “to owe, be a debtor,” with accusative, **ὀφείλειν**: Rom. 13:8; Philem. 18; **προσοφείλειν**, “to owe in addition”: Philem. 19; **δεῖν**, “to be necessary”: 1 Cor. 15:53. *þatei skulans sijaima* (“that of which we are debtors”), **τὰ ὀφειλήματα ἡμῶν**, “our debts”: Matt. 6:12. *dulgis skula*, debtor, **χρεωφειλέτης**: Luke 7:41.

**FAIHU-SKULA**, debtor, **χρεωφειλέτης**: Luke 16:5.

**\*SKULDRS** (compare Gr. II, 332), masculine (?).

**SPAI-SKULDRS**, spittle, **πτύσμα**: John 9:6.

**SKURA**, see under *Skiuran*.

**SKUTTS** (Old High German *skuft*, Modern High German *Schopf*; Gr. III, 408; DRA. 283; Gf. VI, 461), masculine, or *skuft*, neuter, hair, **τρίχες**: Luke 7:38, 44; John 11:2; 12:3.

**\*SKREITAN** (Anglo-Saxon *screadian*, Old Saxon *scritan*, Old Frisian *skreda*, English *shred*, Swedish *skräta*, Danish *skraeder*, Modern High German *schroten*; Rchth. 1033), first conjugation, *skrait, skritun, skritans*, to split, rend.

**DIS-SKREITAN**, the same, **διαρρηγνύναι**: Mark 14:63.

**DIS-SKRITNAN**, third conjugation, to be rent, **σχίζεσθαι**: Matt. 27:51.

**SKYÞUS**, masculine proper name, **Σκύθης**, “Scythian”: Col. 3:11.

**SKOHS** (Old Norse *skor*, Anglo-Saxon *sceo*, Old Saxon *scoh*, Old High German *scuoh*, English *shoe*, Old Frisian, Swedish, Danish *sko*, Dutch *schoe*, Modern High German *Schuh*; Gr. III, 450; Gf. VI, 418; Rchth. 1032), masculine, or *skoh*, neuter, footwear, sandal, **ὑπόδημα**: Matt. 3:11; Mark 1:7; Luke 3:16.

**GA-SKOH**, neuter (?), footwear, sandal, **ὑπόδημα**: Luke 10:4; 15:22.

**GA-SKOHS**, adjective, shod, **ὑποδεδεμένος**: Mark 6:9; Eph. 6:15.

**SKOHSL** (Anglo-Saxon *scucca*, Old High German *sciuhan*, Swedish *sky*, Danish *skye*,
rec. Mod. High German *scheuen*, *Scheusal*; DM. 274, 561; Gf. VI, 417), neuter, evil spirit, demon, δαίμων: Matt. VIII.31; δαιμόνιον, “demon”: Luke VIII.27, at this passage; 1 Cor. X.20, 21.

SLAHAN (Old Norse *slá*, Anglo-Saxon *slean*, Old Saxon and Old High German *slahan*, Old Frisian *sla*, English *slay*, Swedish *slå*, Danish *slaae*, Dutch *slaen*, Modern High German *schlagen*; Gr. II, 12; DRA. 625; Rchth. 1035), conjugation I, *sloh, slohun, slahans*, to strike, beat, τύπτειν: Mark XV.19; Luke XVIII.13; 1 Cor. VIII.12; παίειν, “to strike”: Matt. XXVI.68; Mark XIV.47; John XVIII.10; δέρειν, “to beat”: John XVIII.23; 2 Cor. XI.20; *lofam slahan*, see under *Lofa*.

AF-SLAHAN, 1) to strike, smite, ἀφαιρεῖν: Mark XIV.47; 2) to kill, ἀποκτείνειν: Mark XII.5; Luke XX.14; Eph. II.16.

SLAHS, masculine (plural *slaheis*), 1) blow, stroke, wound, πληγή: 2 Cor. VI.5; XI.23; *slahs lofin*, see under *Lofa*; 2) affliction, disease, μάστιξ: Mark V.29, 34; Luke VII.21.

SLA-HALS, see under *Hals*.

SLAUHTS, feminine, slaughter, σφαγή: Rom. VIII.36.

SLAIHTS (Old Norse *slettr*, Old Frisian *sliucht*, English *slight*, Swedish *slät*, Danish *slet*, Dutch *slecht, slicht*, Modern High German *schlecht, schlicht*; Rchth. 1037), adjective, level, smooth, λεῖος: Luke III.5.

SLAUHTS, see under *Slahan*.

SLAUþJAN, see under *Sliuþan*.

SLAUPJAN, see under *Sliupan*.

SLAVAN (Anglo-Saxon *slavian*), conjugation II, to be quiet, fall silent, σιωπᾶν: Mark IX.34; Luke XIX.40; *slavands*, participle, quiet, ἤρεμος: 1 Tim. II.2.

ANA-SLAVAN, to become quiet, παύεσθαι: Luke VIII.24.

GA-SLAVAN, to be silent, σιωπᾶν: Mark IV.39.

SLEIþA (Old Saxon *slithi*; Schm. *Gloss. Hel.* 99), feminine, loss, penalty, ζημία: Phil. III.7, 8.

SLEIþIS (plural *Sleidjai*), adjective, harmful, dangerous, severe, χαλεπός: Matt. VIII.28; 2 Tim. III.1.

SLEIþEI, feminine, danger, κίνδυνος: Rom. VIII.35.

GA-SLEIþJAN, conjugation II, to injure, ζημιοῦν: Mark VIII.36; Luke IX.25; 2 Cor. VII.9; Phil. III.8.

SLEPAN (Old Saxon and Anglo-Saxon *slapan*, Old Frisian *slepa*, English *sleep*, Dutch *slaepen*, Modern High German *schlafen*; compare Old Norse *sofa*, Swedish *sofva*, Danish *sove*, Old Saxon *suebian*; Latin *sopire, somnium*; Greek ὕπνος, “sleep”; Bopp 84; Rchth. 1037), conjugation I, *saislep* (*saizlep*, John XI.11; [Col. 1448] *saisleip*, Luke VIII.23), *saislepun* (*saizlepun*, 1 Cor. XV.6), *slepans*, to sleep, καθεύδειν: Matt. VIII.24; IX.24; Mark IV.27, 38; V.39; 1 Thess. V.6, 7, 10; κεκοιμῆσθαι, “to have fallen asleep”: John XI.12.

ANA-SLEPAN, to fall asleep, ἀφυπνοῦν: Luke VIII.23; κεκοιμῆσθαι: 1 Thess. IV.13; XIV.15 [as printed].

GA-SLEPAN, the same, κοιμᾶσθαι: John XI.11; 1 Cor. XI.30; XV.6, 18, 20.

SLEPS, masculine, sleep, ὕπνος: Luke IX.32; Rom. XIII.11; κοίμησις τοῦ ὕπνου, “the sleep of slumber”: John XI.13.

SLINDAN (Old High German *slintan*, Dutch *slinden*, Modern High German *schlingen, Schlund*; Gr. II, 35), conjugation I, *sland, slundun, slundans*, to swallow.

FRA-SLINDAN, to swallow up, καταπίνειν: 2 Cor. V.4.

SLIUþAN (Anglo-Saxon *slidan*, English *slide*, Modern High German *schleudern*), conjugation I, *slauþ, sluþun, sluþans*, to be slippery.

AF-SLAUþJAN, conjugation II, to frighten, inspire fear; in the passive, to be frightened, ἐξαπορεῖσθαι: 2 Cor. IV.8; to be utterly alarmed, anxious, ἀπορεῖσθαι: Gal. IV.20.

AF-SLAUþNAN, conjugation III, to be terrified, to be astonished, θαμβεῖσθαι: Mark I.27; X.24; infinitive used substantivally, θάμβος, “astonishment”: Luke IV.36.

SLIUPAN (Old Norse *sleppa*, Anglo-Saxon *slipan*, Old Saxon *slopian*, Old High German *sliofan*, English *slip*, Swedish *slippa*, Danish *slippe*, Modern High German *schlüpfen*; Gr. II, 18), conjugation I, *slaup, slupun, slupans*, to creep in, ἐνδύνειν: 2 Tim. III.6.

UF-SLIUPAN, to withdraw, ὑποστέλλειν ἑαυτόν, “to draw oneself back”: Gal. II.12; present participle *uf-sliupands*, παρείσακτος, “introduced secretly”: Gal. II.4.

ÏNNUF-SLIUPAN, to creep in, παρεισέρχεσθαι: Gal. II.4.

AF-SLAUPJAN, conjugation II, to put off; *afslaupjan sis*, in the middle sense, ἀπεκδύεσθαι, “to strip oneself”: Col. III.9.

SMAIRþR (Old Norse *smiör*, Anglo-Saxon *smere, smyrian*, Old Saxon *smer*, Old High German *smero*, Old Frisian *smere*, English *smear*, Swedish and Danish *smör*, Dutch *smeer*, Modern High German *Schmeer, schmieren*; Gr. II, 57; III, 463; Rchth. 1038), neuter, fatness, richness, πιότης: Rom. XI.17.

SMAKKA (Gr. III, 376), masculine, fig, σῦκον: Matt. VII.16; Mark XI.13; Luke VI.44.

SMAKKA-BAGMS, see under *Bagms*.

SMALS (Old Norse *smár*, Anglo-Saxon *smael*, Old Saxon, Old High German, Swedish, Danish, and Dutch *smal*, English *small*, Modern High German *schmal*; Gr. III, 611), adjective, small; superlative *smalists*, very small, least, ἐλάχιστος: 1 Cor. XV.9.

SMARNA (compare *Smairþr*; Gr. II, 57), feminine, refuse, σκύβαλον: Phil. III.8.

SMEITAN (Old Norse *smita*, Anglo-Saxon *smitan*, Old High German *smeizan*, Old Frisian *smita*, English *smeeth, smut, smutch*, Swedish *smeta*, Danish *smitte*, Dutch *smetten*, Modern High German *schmeissen*; Gr. II, 14; Rchth. 1038), conjugation I, *smait, smitun, smitans*, to anoint.

BI-SMEITAN, to anoint upon, ἐπιχρίειν: John IX.11.

GA-SMEITAN, the same: John IX.6.

SMIþA (Old Norse *smidr*, Old High German *smid*, Anglo-Saxon *smið*, Old Frisian *smeth*, English *smith*, Danish and Swedish *smed*, Dutch *smid*, Modern High German *Schmied*; Gr. II, 46; Rchth. 1037), masculine, smith.

AIZA-SMIþA, a worker in iron, χάλκευς: 2 Tim. IV.14.

GA-SMIþON, conjugation II, to prepare, bring about, κατεργάζεσθαι: 2 Cor. VII.10.

SMYRN (Greek σμύῤῥον), neuter, myrrh; *miþ smyrna*, ἐσμυρισμένος, “mixed with myrrh”: Mark XV.23.

SNAGA (Gr. III, 446), masculine, garment, cloak, ἱμάτιον: Matt. IX.16; Luke V.36.

SNAIVS (Old Norse *snior*, Old Saxon and Old High German *sneo*, Anglo-Saxon *snaw*, English *snow*, Swedish *snö*, Danish *sne*, Dutch *sneeuw*, Modern High German *Schnee*; Greek νίψ; Latin *nix, nivis*; Gr. II, 45; III, 388), masculine, snow, χιών: Mark IX.3.

SNAU, see under *Snivan*.

SNARPJAN (Old High German *snirfan*, Dutch *snerpen*, Modern High German *schnarpen*), conjugation II, to eat at, nibble.

AT-SNARPJAN, the same, θιγγάνειν: Col. II.21.

SNEIþAN (Old Norse *sneida*, Old Saxon, Anglo-Saxon [Col. 1449] *sniþan*, Old High German *snidan*, Old Frisian *snitha, snia*, Swedish *snida*, Danish *snitte*, Dutch *snyden*, Modern High German *schneiden*; Gr. II, 15; Rchth. 1039), conjugation I, *snaiþ, sniþun, sniþans*, 1) to cut; 2) to reap, θερίζειν: Matt. VI.26; Luke XIX.21; 2 Cor. IX.6; Gal. VI.7, 8, 9.

UF-SNEIþAN, to sacrifice, slaughter, θύειν: Luke XV.23, 27, 30; John X.10; 1 Cor. V.7.

SNIUMJAN (compare *Snivan*), conjugation II, to hasten, σπεύδειν: Luke II.16; XIX.5, 6; σπουδάζειν: 1 Thess. II.17; 2 Tim. IV.9.

GA-SNIUMJAN, to press forward, attain, φθάνειν: 2 Cor. X.14.

SNIUMUNDO, adverb, diligently, μετὰ σπουδῆς, “with diligence”: Mark VI.25; Luke I.39; comparative *sniumundos*, more diligently, σπουδαιοτέρως: Phil. II.28.

SNIVAN (Old Norse *snua*, Old Saxon *sniumo*, Anglo-Saxon *snude, sneome*), conjugation I, *snau, snevun* (*snivun*, Mark VI.53), *snivans*, 1) to go, proceed, ὑπάγειν: John XV.16; 1 Cor. IX.25; 2) to attain, φθάνειν: 1 Thess. II.16.

DUAT-SNIVAN, to put in at shore, προσορμίζεσθαι: Mark VI.53.

FAURBI-SNIVAN (*bisnivan faur*), to go before, precede, anticipate, προάγειν: 1 Tim. V.24; φθάνειν: 1 Thess. IV.15.

GA-SNIVAN, to anticipate (in the interpretation, *pervenire* should be altered to *praevenire*), φθάνειν: Rom. IX.31; Phil. III.16.

FAUR-SNIVAN, to go before, anticipate, προλαμβάνειν: Mark XIV.8; 1 Cor. XI.21; *faura faursnivan*, the same, προάγειν: 1 Tim. I.18.

SNUTRS (Old Norse *snotr*, Anglo-Saxon *snoter*; Gr. II, 49), adjective, prudent, wise, σοφός: Luke X.21; 1 Cor. I.19.

SNUTREI, feminine, prudence, wisdom, σοφία: 1 Cor. I.17, 19.

SNORJO (Old Norse *snara*, Old High German *snuor, snaraha*, English *snare*, Swedish *snöre*, Danish *snor*, Modern High German *Schnur*; Gr. II, 42), feminine, 1) cord, rope; 2) noose, basket, σαργάνη: 2 Cor. XI.33.

SUQNS, masculine, stomach, στόμαχος: 1 Tim. V.23, at this passage.

SUQON (compare *Supon*), conjugation II, to season.

GA-SUQON, the same, ἀρτύειν: Col. IV.6.

SUþJAN (*Suþjon*; English *soothe*), conjugation II, to please, flatter, κνήθειν: 2 Tim. IV.3, at this passage.

SULJA (Old High German *sola*, English *sole*, Swedish *sola*, Danish *saale*, Modern High German *Sohle*; Latin *solea*; Gr. III, 405; Gf. VI, 185), feminine, sandal, σανδάλιον: Mark VI.9.

GA-SULJAN, conjugation II, to lay a foundation, found, θεμελιοῦν: Matt. VII.25; Luke VI.48; Eph. III.18.

SUMS (Old Norse *sumr*, Anglo-Saxon, Old High German, Old Saxon, and Old Frisian *sum*, English *some*, Swabian *somliga*, Danish *somme*; Gr. II, 55; III, 4; Gf. VI, 44; Rchth. 1055), adjective, 1) some, a certain one, τις: Matt. IX.3; XXVII.47; Mark II.6; V.25; VII.2; VIII.3; IX.1, 38; XI.5, 8; XII.13; XIV.43, 47, 51, 57, 65; XV.21, 35; Luke VI.2; VII.2, 36, 41; VIII.27, 46, 49; IX.7, 19, 27, 49, 57; X.25; XIV.15, 16; XV.8, 11; XVI.1, 19, 20; XVII.12; XVIII.2, 9, 18, 35; John VI.64; VII.12, 25, 44; IX.16, 40; XI.1, 37; XII.20; Rom. XI.14, 17; 1 Cor. IX.22; XV.6, 12, 34, 35; subscription; 2 Cor. III.1; X.2; Gal. I.7; II.12; 2 Thess. III.11; 1 Tim. I.3, 6, 19; IV.1; V.24; VI.10; 2 Tim. II.18, 20; Titus I.12; *Skeir.* III.a; εἷς, “one”: Mark XIV.43; Luke (IX.8) XV.15, 26; XX.1; *bi sumata*, concerning a certain person, ἀπὸ μέρους, “in part”: Rom. XI.25, at this passage; 2 Cor. I.14; II.5;

2) in distributive sentences (often with the enclitic *uh*, which see):

a) repeated: *sums—sumsuh*, one—the other, ὁ μὲν—ὁ δέ, ὃς μὲν—ὃς δέ: Mark XII.5; Rom. IX.21 (XIV.5); 1 Cor. VII.7; XI.21; 2 Cor. II.16; Phil. I.16, at this passage; 2 Tim. II.20; *Skeir.* VI.d; *sums—sumsuh—sumsuh—sumsuh*, one—another—another—another, ὁ μὲν—ὁ δὲ—ὁ δὲ—ὁ δέ: Eph. IV.11; ἄλλος—ἄλλος, “one—another”: John IX.9 (1 Cor. XII.10); τίς—ἄλλος, “one—another”: John IX.16; *Skeir.* VI.d; τίς—τίς, “one—another”: Phil. I.15; Luke IX.7, 8;

b) with another distributive word: *anþar—sums*, ἄλλος—ἄλλος, “one—another”: Mark VIII.28; Luke IX.19; *sumsuh—anþar*, ὁ μὲν—ἄλλος, “the one—another”: John VII.12; *sum—anþar—sum*, ὃ μὲν—ἄλλο δὲ—ἄλλο, “one—another—another”: Mark IV.4, 5, 7; *sum—anþar—sum—anþar*, ὃ μὲν—ἕτερον—ἕτερον—ἕτερον, “one—another—another—another”: Luke VIII.5, 6, 7; *managai—sumaïh*, πολλοί—ἄλλοι, “many—others”: John X.20, 21; πολλοί—τινές, “many—some”: John XI.46; *managai—sumaih—sumaih*, πολλοί—ἄλλοι—ἄλλοι, “many—others—others”: John VII.40, 41; *sa frumista—anþar—sums*, ὁ πρῶτος—ἕτερος—ἕτερος, “the first—another—another”: Luke XIV.20; ὁ πρῶτος—δεύτερος—ἕτερος, “the first—second—another”: Luke XIX.16, 18, 20;

c) where the distributive word is lacking in the first member of the sentence: —, ἄλλοι, “others”: John XII.29; —, οἱ δέ, “but others”: Matt. XXVI.67; —, οἱ πολλοί, “the many”: 2 Cor. II.17; or in the second: ὃς μὲν—, “the one—”: Rom. IV.2.

SUMAN, adverb, once, formerly, ποτέ: Rom. XI.30; Gal. I.23; Eph. II.3; V.8; *suman—suman* (*sumanuh*), now—now, then—then, ἐκ μέρους—ἐκ μέρους, “in part—in part”: 1 Cor. XIII.9; *suman—suman—suman*: *Skeir.* VI.c.

SUNDRO (Old Norse *sundra*, Anglo-Saxon *syndrian*, Old Saxon *sundar*, Old High German *suntar*, Old Frisian; English *sunder*, Swedish *söndra*, Danish *sonder, sondre*, Dutch *zonder*, Modern High German *sonder, sondern*; Gf. VI, 48; Rchth. 1056), adverb, separately, privately, καταμόνας: Mark IV.10; Luke IX.18; κατ’ ἰδίαν, “privately”: Mark IV.34; VII.33; IX.2, 28; Luke IX.10; X.23; Gal. II.2; ἰδίᾳ, “individually”: 1 Cor. XII.11.

SUNIS (Old Norse *sannr*, Anglo-Saxon *soð*, Old Saxon *soth*, Old Frisian *sone*, Old High German *sunnis, sona*, English *sooth*, Swedish *sann*, Danish *sand*, Modern High German *Sühne, versöhnen*; Gf. VI, 241; Rchth. 1040; compare 1006), adjective, true.

SUNJA, adverb, truly, ἀληθῶς: Luke IX.27; John XVII.3; see at this passage.

SUNJABA, adverb, the same: 1 Thess. II.13.

SUNJA, feminine, truth, ἀλήθεια: Mark V.33; XII.14, 32; Luke IV.25; XX.21; John VIII.32; X.41; XIV.6, 17; XV.26; XVI.7, 13; XVII.17; XVIII.37, 38; Rom. IX.1; XV.8; 1 Cor. V.8; XIII.6; 2 Cor. IV.2; VI.7; VII.14; XI.10; XII.6; XIII.8; Gal. II.5, 14; III.1; V.7; Eph. I.13; IV.21, 24, 25; V.9; VI.14; Phil. I.18; Col. I.6; 1 Tim. II.4, 7; III.15; IV.3; VI.5; 2 Tim. II.15, 18, 25; III.7, 8; IV.4; *Skeir.* I.b, d; VIII.c; ἀληθές, “true”: John VIII.14, 17; X.41; ὁσιότης, “holiness”: Luke I.75; *sunja gateihan*, to speak truth, to be truthful, ἀληθεύειν: Gal. IV.16; *sunja taujan*, the same: Eph. IV.15; *bi sunjai*, in truth, truly, ἀληθῶς: Matt. XXVI.73; XXVII.54; Mark XIV.70; XV.39; John VI.14, 55; VII.26, 40; VIII.31; XVII.8; ἀληθές: 1 Tim. VI.7; ὄντως, “genuinely”: Mark XI.32; 1 Cor. XIV.25; 1 Tim. V.3, 5, 16.

SUNJAI-FRIþAS, see under *friþon*.

SUNJEINS, adjective, true, ἀληθής: Mark XII.14; John VII.18; VIII.13, 16, 26; 2 Cor. VI.8; Phil. IV.8; Titus I.13; Neh. VII.2; ἀληθινός, “genuine”: Luke XVI.11; John VI.32; VII.28; XV.1; *Skeir.* VI.b; ἀγαθός, “good”: John VII.12.

SUNJON, conjugation II, to defend; *sunjon sik*, to defend oneself, justify oneself, ἀπολογεῖσθαι: 2 Cor. XII.19.

GA-SUNJON, to justify, δικαιοῦν: Luke VII.35.

SUNJONS, feminine, defence, justification, ἀπολογία: 2 Cor. VII.11; Phil. I.17; 2 Tim. IV.16.

SUNNA (Old Norse and Old High German *sunna*, Old Saxon *sunna, sunno*, Anglo-Saxon *sunne*, Old Frisian *sunne, sonna*, English *sun*, Dutch *zon*, Modern High German *Sonne*; Gr. III, 349; Gf. VI, 240; Rchth. 1056), masculine, sun, ἥλιος: Mark IV.6; XVI.2.

SUNNO, feminine, the same: Matt. V.45; Luke IV.40; Eph. IV.26; Neh. VII.3.

SUNUS (Old Norse *sonr*, Anglo-Saxon, Old Saxon, Old High German, Old Frisian *sunu*, English, Swedish *son*, Danish *son*, Dutch *zoon*, Modern High German *Sohn*; Gr. III, 320; Gf. VI, 59; Rchth. 1056), masculine, son, υἱός: Matt. V.45; VIII.12, 20, 29; IX.15; X.37; XXVII.9; Mark I.1, 11; II.19, 28; III.11, 17; VI.3; VIII.31; IX.7, 9, 12, 17, 31; X.33, 35, 46; XII.6, 35, 37; XIII.26; XIV.41, 61, 62; Luke I. [Col. 1451] 13, 16, 31, 32, 35, 36, 57; II.7; III.2, 22–38; IV.3, 9, 22, 41; V.10, 24; VI.5, 22, 35; VII.12, 34; VIII.28; IX.20, 22, 26, 35, 38; X.6; XV.11, 13, 24; XVI.8; XVII.22, 24; XVIII.8, 31, 38, 39; XIX.9, 10; XX.13, 34, 36, 41, 44; John V.22, 23; VI.27, 53, 62; VIII.28; IX.39; X.36; XI.4, 27; XII.23, 34; XIII.31; Rom. VIII.3; IX.9, 26, 27; 1 Cor. XV.28; 2 Cor. III.7, 13; VI.18; Gal. II.20; IV.4; VI.22, 30; Eph. I.6; II.2; III.5; IV.13; V.6; Col. I.13; III.6; 1 Thess. V.5; 2 Esdr. II.9–42; Neh. VI.18; *Skeir.* III.c; IV.d; V.a, c; VI.b; *sunive gadeds*, see under *Deds*; *sunive sibja*, see under *Sibis*.

SUNS (Anglo-Saxon *sona*, English *soon*, Modern High German *schon*; Gr. III, 89, 590), adverb, 1) shortly, immediately, εὐθέως: Matt. VIII.3; XXVI.74; XXVII.48; Mark I.10 (12), 18, 20, 21, 29–31, 42, 43; II.2, 8, 12; IV.5, 15–17, 29; V.2, 13, 42; VI.27; Luke V.13, 39; VI.49; VIII.33; XVII.7; John XIII.30; XVIII.27; εὐθύς: Mark I.12, 28; John XIII.32; ἐξαυτῆς, “at once”: Phil. II.23; παραχρῆμα, “immediately”: Luke I.64; VIII.44, 47, 55; XVIII.43; XIX.11; ἀπὸ μιᾶς, “all at once”: Luke XIV.18; ἐν ἀτόμῳ, “in an instant”: 1 Cor. XV.52; ἐφάπαξ, “once for all”: 1 Cor. XV.6; 2) together, ἅμα: 1 Thess. IV.17.

SUNS-EI, conjunction, as soon as, when, ὡς: Luke I.44; XIX.41; John XI.20, 29, 32, 33.

BI-SUNJANE, adverb, near, ἐγγύς: Mark I.38, at this passage; κύκλῳ, “round about”: Mark III.34; VI.6; Luke IX.12; Neh. V.17; VI.16; *þata bisunjane land*, the surrounding region, περίχωρος: Luke IV.37.

SUPON (Old High German *sofon*; Latin *sapere*; compare *Suqon*; Gf. VI, 172), conjugation II, to season, ἀρτύειν: Mark IX.50.

GA-SUPON, the same: Luke XIV.34.

SUSANNA, proper name, feminine, Susanna, Σουσάννα: Luke VIII.3.

SUTIS (Old Norse *saetr*, Anglo-Saxon, Old Frisian *swet*, Old Saxon *suoti*, Old High German *sozi*, English *sweet*, Swedish *söt*, Danish *sød* [OCR uncertain], Dutch *zoet*, Modern High German *süss*; Greek ἡδύς; Gf. VI, 311; Rchth. 1061), adjective; comparative *sutiza*: 1) sweet; 2) mild, patient, ἀνεκτός: Matt. XI.24; Mark VI.11; Luke X.12, 14; ἡσύχιος, “quiet”: 1 Tim. II.2; ἐπιεικής, “gentle”: 1 Tim. III.3.

UN-SUTI, neuter, unrest, disturbance, ἀκαταστασία: 2 Cor. VI.5.

SPAI . . . , see under *Speivan*.

SPAIKULATUR (a Latin word), masculine, executioner, σπεκουλάτωρ: Mark VI.27.

SPAURDS (*Sprauds*, 1 Cor. IX.24; Old High German *spurt, spor*, Old Norse *spor*, Anglo-Saxon *spor, spyrd*, Old Saxon *spuri* [lacuna], *spurnan*, Modern High German *Spur*; Gr. II, 57; III, 396; Gf. VI, 357), anomalous feminine, stadium, στάδιον: John VI.19; XI.18; 1 Cor. IX.24.

SPARVA (Old Norse *spörr*, Old High German *sparo*, Anglo-Saxon *spearva, speara*, English *sparrow*, Swedish *sparv*, Danish *spurve*, Modern High German *Sperling*; Greek ψήρ; Gr. III, 362; Gf. VI, 360), masculine, sparrow, στρουθίον: Matt. X.29, 31.

SPEDS (*speids*, Matt. XXVII.64; *spids*, 1 Tim. IV.1; Old High German *spät*, Swedish *späd*, Danish *spaed*, Dutch *spade*, Modern High German *spät*; Gf. VI, 326), adjective, slow; comparative *spediza*, last, final, ἔσχατος: Matt. XXVII.64; superlative *spedists* (*spedumists*, Mark XII.22), the same: Mark XII.6, 22; John VI.40, 44; VII.37; XI.24; XII.48; 1 Cor. IV.9; XV.8, 52; 2 Tim. III.1; ὕστερος, “later”: Luke XX.32; 1 Tim. IV.1.

SPEIVAN (*Spevan*, Mark VII.33; Old Norse *spya*, Anglo-Saxon *spivan*, Old Saxon *spiuuan*, Old Frisian *spia*, Modern High German *spiwan*, English *spew*, Swedish *spy*, Danish *spye*, Dutch *spuwen*, Modern High German *speien*; Latin *spuere*, Greek ψύττειν; Gf. VI, 364; Rchth. 1041), conjugation I, *spaiv, spivun, spivans*, 1) to spit, πτύειν: Mark VII.33; VIII.23; 2) to spit upon, ἐμπτύειν: Matt. XXVI.67; Mark X.34; XIV.65.

AND-SPEIVAN, to spit out, reject, ἐκπτύειν: Gal. IV.14.

[Col. 1452] BI-SPEIVAN, to spit upon, ἐμπτύειν: Mark XV.19; Luke XVIII.32.

GA-SPEIVAN, to spit, πτύειν: John IX.6.

SPAI-SKULDRS, see under *Skuldrs*.

SPILDA (Old Norse *spialld*; compare *Spill*), feminine, tablet, writing-tablet, πινακίδιον: Luke I.63; πλάξ: 2 Cor. III.3.

SPILL (Old Norse *spell, spilla*, Anglo-Saxon *spell*, Old Saxon and Old High German *spel*, English *spell*; compare Modern High German *spellen, Spiel*; Gf. VI, 333), neuter, saying, fable, μῦθος: 1 Tim. I.4; IV.7; 2 Tim. IV.4; Titus I.14.

SPILLA, masculine, preacher: *Skeir.* I.d.

SPILLON, conjugation II, to proclaim, report, narrate, say, διηγεῖσθαι: Mark V.16; IX.9; ἐκφέρειν, “to report”: Neh. VI.19; εὐαγγελίζεσθαι, “to announce good news”: Luke II.10; Rom. X.15.

GA-SPILLON, to proclaim, διαγγέλλειν: Luke IX.60.

þIUþ-SPILLON, to evangelize, εὐαγγελίζειν: Luke III.18; VIII.1; see at this passage.

US-SPILLON, to announce, κηρύσσειν: Luke VIII.39; διηγεῖσθαι: Luke IX.10.

UNUS-SPILLOþS, past participle, unutterable, ἀνεκδιήγητος: 2 Cor. IX.15; ἀνεξερεύνητος, “unsearchable”: Rom. XI.33.

SPINNAN (Old Norse *spinja*, Anglo-Saxon, Old High German *spinnan*, English *spin*, Swedish *spinna*, Danish *spinde*, Dutch and Modern High German *spinnen*; Gr. II, 34; Gf. VI, 345), conjugation I, *spann, spunnun, spunnans*, to spin, νήθειν: Matt. VI.28.

SPRAUDS, see *Spaurds*.

SPRAUTO (Gr. II, 21), adverb, quickly, suddenly, ταχύ: Matt. V.25; Mark IX.39; John XI.29; ταχέως, “quickly”: Luke XIV.21; XV.22; XVI.6; John XI.31; Gal. I.6; Phil. II.24; 2 Thess. II.2; 1 Tim. V.22; 2 Tim. IV.9; τάχιον, “more quickly”: John XIII.27; 1 Tim. III.14; ἐν τάχει, “speedily”: Luke XVIII.8.

SPYREIDA (a Greek word), masculine, basket, σπυρίς: Mark VIII.8, 20.

STABS (Old Norse *stafr*, Anglo-Saxon *staef*, Old High German *stap*, Old Frisian *stef*, English *staff*, Old Saxon, Swedish, Dutch *staf*, Danish *stav*, Modern High German *Stab*; Gr. II, 51; Rchth. 1046), masculine, elementary principle, στοιχεῖον: Gal. IV.3, 9; Col. II.20.

STAGGAN, see under *Stiggan*.

STAþS (*Stads*, Luke XIV.22; Old Norse *staþr*, Anglo-Saxon *stede*, Old High German *stat*, Old Frisian *sted*, English *stead*, Old Saxon, Swedish, Dutch *stad*, Danish *sted*, Modern High German *Statt*; Latin *statio*; compare *Standan*; Gr. II, 51; Rchth. 1045), masculine (plural *stadeis*), 1) place, station, τόπος: Mark I.35, 45; XV.22; XVI.6; Luke IV.17, 37, 42; VI.17; IX.10, 12; X.1; XIV.9, 10; XIX.5; John X.40; XI.6, 30; XIV.2; XVIII.2; Rom. IX.26; 2 Cor. II.14; 2 Thess. III.16; 1 Tim. II.8; 2) place, τόπος: Luke II.7; XIV.22; *staþ giban*, to give place, τόπον διδόναι: Rom. XII.19; Eph. IV.27; 3) lodging, inn, κατάλυμα: Luke II.7; 4) bank, shore, γῆ: Mark IV.1; Luke V.3; *jainis stadis*, to the farther shore, εἰς τὸ πέραν: Mark IV.35.

HUNSLA-STAþS, gift, offering, altar, θυσιαστήριον: Matt. V.23; Luke I.11; 1 Cor. X.18.

MOTA-STAþS, tax-office, toll-booth, τελώνιον: Luke V.27.

LUKARNA-STAþA, masculine, lampstand, λυχνία: Matt. V.15; Mark IV.21; Luke VIII.16.

ANDA-STAþJIS, masculine, opponent, adversary, ἀντίδικος: Luke XVIII.3; ἀντικείμενος: 1 Cor. XVI.9; Phil. I.28.

STAIGA, see under *Steigan*.

STAINS (Old Norse *steinr*, Anglo-Saxon *stan*, English *stone*, Old Saxon, Old Frisian, Swedish *sten*, Danish, Dutch *steen*, Old High German and Modern High German *Stein*; Gr. III, 378; Rchth. 1047), masculine, rock, stone, λίθος: Matt. XXVII.60; Mark V.5; XII.10; XV.46; XVI.3, 4; Luke III.8; IV.3, 11; XIX.40, 44; XX.17, 18; John VIII.59; X.31; XI.38, 39, 41; Rom. IX.32, 33; 2 Cor. III.7; πέτρα, “rock”: Matt. VII.24, 25; XXVII.51, 60; Mark XV.46; Luke VI.48; VIII.6, 13; hence also used as a proper name for Peter: *Skeir.* VII.a; *stainam vairpan*, to stone, λιθοβολεῖν: Mark [Col. 1453] XII.4; *stainam afvairpan*, the same, λιθάζειν: John XI.8; καταλιθάζειν: Luke XX.6.

VAIHSTA-STAINS, cornerstone, γωνιαῖος (sc. λίθος, “stone”): Eph. II.20.

STAINAHS, adjective, rocky, πετρώδης: Mark IV.5, 16.

STAINEINS, adjective, made of stone, λίθινος: 2 Cor. III.3.

STAINJAN, conjugation II, to stone, λιθάζειν: John X.32, 33; 2 Cor. XI.25.

STAIRNO (Old Norse *stierna*, Anglo-Saxon *steorra*, Old Saxon *sterro*, Old High German *sterno*, Old Frisian *stera*, English *star*, Swedish *stjerna*, Danish *stjerne*, Dutch *ster*, Modern High German *Stern*; Greek ἀστήρ, Latin *stella*; Gr. III, 392; Rchth. 1048), feminine, star, ἀστήρ: Mark XIII.25.

STAIRO (Greek στεῖρος, Latin *sterilis*), feminine, barren, sterile, στεῖρα: Luke I.7, 36; Gal. IV.27.

STAIFANUS, proper name, masculine, Stephanas, Στεφανῆς: 1 Cor. I.16; XVI.15.

STAKS, see under *Stikan*.

STALDAN (Old High German *gastaldis*, Anglo-Saxon *gesteald*), conjugation I, *staistald, staistaldun, staldans*, to possess as one’s own, own.

AND-STALDAN, to bestow, with the thing in the dative and the person in the accusative, ἐπιχορηγεῖν: 2 Cor. IX.10; Gal. III.5; παρέχειν, “to supply”: 1 Tim. I.4.

GA-STALDAN, to gain, make a profit, κερδαίνειν: 1 Cor. IX.20, at this passage; κτᾶσθαι, “to acquire”: Luke XVIII.12; 1 Thess. IV.4; Neh. V.16; ἔχειν, “to have”: 1 Cor. VII.28.

AND-STALD, neuter, help, supply, ἐπιχορηγία: Eph. IV.16; Phil. I.19.

AGLAITGA-STALDS, adjective, pursuing shameful gain, greedy, αἰσχροκερδής: 1 Tim. III.8; Titus I.7.

STAMMS (Old Norse *stamr*, Old High German *stamalon*, Old Saxon *stamm*, Anglo-Saxon *stamer*, English *stammer*, Swedish *stamma*, Danish *stam*, Dutch *stamelen*, Modern High German *stammeln*; Gr. II, 30), adjective, mute, μογιλάλος: Mark VII.32.

STANDAN (Old Norse *standa, styþia*, Anglo-Saxon, Old High German *standan*, Old Saxon *standan, stan*, Old Frisian *stonda, stan*, English *stand*, Swedish *stå*, Danish *staae*, Dutch *staen*, Modern High German *stehn*; Greek στῆναι, Latin *stare*; Gr. II, 11; Rchth. 1051), anomalous conjugation I, *stoþ, stoþun, stoþans* (?), 1) to stand, ἱστάναι, στήκειν, ἑστάναι: Matt. VI.5; XXVI.73; XXVII.11, 47; Mark III.31; IX.1; XI.5, 25; Luke I.11; V.1, 2; VI.8; VII.38; VIII.20; IX.27; XVIII.13; John VI.22; VII.37; XII.29; XVIII.5, 16, 18, 25; Rom. XIV.4; 1 Cor. XV.1; XVI.13; Gal. V.1; Eph. VI.11, 13, 14; Phil. I.27; IV.1; Col. III.12; 1 Thess. III.8; 2 Tim. II.19; σταθῆναι, “to stand”: Luke XVIII.11; XIX.8; ἐφιστάναι, “to stand by”: 2 Tim. IV.2; παρεστάναι, “to be present”: Luke I.19; John XVIII.22; 2) to stand firm, σταθῆναι: Mark III.24, 25.

AND-STANDAN, to oppose, resist, ἀνθιστάναι: Matt. V.39; Rom. IX.19; XIII.2; Gal. II.11; Eph. VI.13; 2 Tim. III.8; IV.15; ἀντικεῖσθαι, “to be opposed”: Gal. V.17; 2 Thess. II.4; 1 Tim. I.10; 2 Tim. II.25; see at this passage; ἀντιλέγειν, “to contradict”: John XIX.12; Rom. X.21; Titus I.9.

AT-STANDAN, to stand beside, παριστάναι: Mark XIV.47, 70; XV.35, 39; ἐφιστάναι: Luke II.38; IV.39; XX.1.

AF-STANDAN, 1) to depart, ἀφιστάναι: Luke IV.13; 2 Cor. XII.8; 2 Tim. II.19; ἀπειπεῖν, “to renounce”: 2 Cor. IV.2; 2) to fall away, ἀφίστασθαι: Luke VIII.13; 1 Tim. IV.1.

BI-STANDAN, to stand round, περιϊστάναι: John XI.42; to surround, περικυκλοῦν: Luke XIX.43.

GA-STANDAN, 1) to remain, stand, ἱστάναι: Mark X.49; Luke VI.8, 17; VII.14; VIII.44; XVII.12; Rom. XI.20; σταθῆναι: Mark III.26; Luke XVIII.40; 2) to remain, stand, ἱστάναι: John VIII.44; 2 Cor. I.24; στήκειν: 1 Thess. III.8; μένειν, “to remain”: Luke I.56; John VIII.31; 1 Cor. VII.24; 1 Tim. II.15; διαμένειν, “to continue”: Gal. II.5; ὑπομένειν, “to remain behind”: Luke II.43; 3) to persist, σταθῆναι: 2 Cor. XIII.1; 4) to restore, ἀποκαθίστασθαι: Luke VI.10; *aftra gastandan*, the same: Mark III.5.

IN-STANDAN, 1) to stand upon, press on, ἐφιστάναι: 2 Tim. IV.2, at this passage; 2) to be imminent, ἐνεστάναι: 2 Thess. II.2, at this passage.

[Col. 1454] MIþ-STANDAN, to stand with, stand together, with the dative, συνιστάναι: Luke IX.32.

US-STANDAN (*ustandan*, Luke VIII.55; X.25), 1) to arise, ἀνιστάναι: Matt. IX.9; Mark I.35; III.26; VII.24; IX.27; X.1; XIV.57, 60; Luke I.39; IV.16, 29, 38, 39; V.25, 28; VIII.55; IX.8, 19; X.25; XV.18, 20; XVII.19; John XI.31; Rom. XV.12; 2) to arise, go out, ἐξέρχεσθαι: Mark VI.1; XI.12; 3) to rise again, ἀνιστάναι: Mark VIII.31; IX.9, 10; X.34; XII.23, 25; XVI.9; Luke IX.8, 19; XVIII.33; John XI.23; 1 Thess. IV.14, 16; ἐγείρεσθαι, “to be raised”: 1 Cor. XV.52.

TVIS-STANDAN, to depart, separate, with the dative, ἀποτάσσεσθαι: 2 Cor. II.13.

FAURA-STANDAN, 1) to stand near, stand beside, παριστάναι: Mark XIV.69; Luke XIX.24; 2) to preside over, be a leader, προΐστασθαι: Rom. XII.8.

AFGA-STOþANS, past participle, having no fixed place, displaced from its own place, ἄτοπος: 2 Thess. III.2, at this passage.

UNGA-STOþANS, unstable; *ungastoþans visan*, ἀστατεῖν, “to be unsettled”: 1 Cor. IV.11.

GA-STOþANAN, conjugation II (?), to persist, stand, ἱστάναι: Rom. XIV.4; see at this passage.

AF-STASS (DRA. 453), feminine, 1) departure, separation; 2) divorce; *afstassais bokos*, certificate of divorce, ἀποστάσιον: Matt. V.31.

US-STASS (*ustass*, Luke XIV.14), resurrection, ἀνάστασις: Mark XII.18, 23; Luke II.34; XIV.14; XX.27, 33, 35, 36; John XI.24, 25; 1 Cor. XV.12, 13, 21; Phil. III.10; 2 Tim. II.18; ἐξανάστασις, “resurrection out from”: Phil. III.11.

TVIS-STASS, dissension, faction, διχοστασία: Gal. V.20.

FAUR-STASSEIS, masculine, leader, overseer, προϊστάμενος: 1 Thess. V.12.

ANA-STODJAN, conjugation II, to begin, commence, ἐνάρχεσθαι: Gal. III.3; inscription to Mark; inscription to Luke; inscription to Ephesians; inscription to 2 Thessalonians; inscription to Titus; *Skeir.* II.a; IV.b.

DU-STODJAN, the same, ἄρχεσθαι: Luke XIV.30; inscription to 2 Corinthians; *faura dustodjan*, to begin beforehand, προενάρχεσθαι: 2 Cor. VIII.6.

ANA-STODEINS, feminine, beginning, ἀρχή: Mark I.1; X.6; XIII.19; John VIII.25, see at this passage; Phil. IV.15; Col. I.18; *Skeir.* I.b, c; ἀπαρχή, “firstfruits”: 1 Cor. XV.20, 23; XVI.15; *fram anastodeinai*, from the beginning, ἄνωθεν: Luke I.3; *fram anastodeinai aivis*, from the beginning of the world, ἀπ’ αἰῶνος: Luke I.70.

AFTRAANA-STODEINS, a second beginning: *Skeir.* I.d.

STAUA (DRA. 748), feminine, 1) judgment, κρίσις: Matt. V.21; XI.22, 24; Mark VI.11; Luke X.14; John V.22; VII.24; VIII.16; XII.31; XVI.8; 2 Thess. I.5; 1 Tim. V.24; *Skeir.* I.a; V.c; κρίμα, “judgment”: John IX.39; Rom. XI.33; 1 Cor. XI.29; 1 Tim. III.6; *du stauai gatiuhan*, to bring to judgment, κατακρίνειν: Matt. XXVII.3; *viljands miþ þus staua*, “wishing to bring a case against you,” θέλων σοι κρίνεσθαι: Matt. V.40; 2) lawsuit, legal case, πρᾶγμα: 1 Cor. VI.1.

STAUA, masculine, judge, κριτής: Matt. V.25; Luke XVIII.2, 6; 2 Tim. IV.8.

ANDA-STAUA, adversary, ἀντίδικος: Matt. V.25.

STAUA-STOLS, see under *Stols*.

STOJAN, conjugation II, preterite *stauïda*, to judge, κρίνειν: Luke VI.37; VII.43;

XIX, 22; John V, 22; VII, 24, 51; VIII, 15, 16, 26, 50; XII, 47, 48; XVIII, 31; Rom. XIV, 3, 4, 5, 10, 13; 1 Cor. IV, 5; V, 3, 12, 13; VI, 1; X, 29; Skeir. V, b; **διακρίνειν**, “to distinguish, judge”: 1 Cor. XI, 31.

**GA-STOJAN**, the same, “to judge,” **κρίνειν**: 1 Cor. V, 3; 2 Cor. II, 1; *gastojans*, participle, “out of place, improper,” **ἄτοπος**: 2 Thess. III, 2; see the note on this passage.

* **STAURKJAN** (Old Norse *storka, storkna*; Anglo-Saxon *stearc*; Swedish *stark*; Danish *staerk*; English *stark, starch*; modern High German *stark*; Gr. II, 62), weak verb II: to dry up (transitive).

**GA-STAURKNAN**, weak verb III: to dry up (intransitive), become dry, **ξηραίνεσθαι**: Mark IX, 18.

* **STAURRAN** (compare modern High German *starr, störrisch*, “stiff, obstinate”; Gr. II, 61), weak verb II: to growl, murmur.

[Col. 1455] **AND-STAURRAN**, the same, “to be indignant,” **ἐμβριμᾶσθαι**: Mark XIV, 5.

**STAUTAN** (Old Norse *steyta*; Old Saxon *stotan*; Old High German *stozan*; Old Frisian *steta*; Danish *stode*; Dutch *stooten*; modern High German *stossen*; Gr. I, 841; Rchth. 1049), weak verb I, *staistaut, stautans*: to strike, beat, **τύπτειν**: Matt. V, 39; “to slap,” **ῥαπίζειν**: Luke VI, 29.

**STASS**, see under **Standan**.

**STEIGAN** (Old Norse and Old Frisian *stiga*; Anglo-Saxon and Old Saxon *stigan*; Old High German *stigi, steigan*; Swedish *stiga*; Danish *stige*; Dutch *stijgen*; modern High German *steigen*; Greek **στείχειν**, “to go”; Gr. II, 17; III, 396; Rchth. 1049), weak verb I, *staig, stigun, stigans*: to go up, ascend, **ἀναβαίνειν**: John VII, 14; X, 1.

**AT-STEIGAN**, to descend; “to embark,” **ἐμβαίνειν**: Matt. IX, 1; “to come down,” **καταβαίνειν**: Matt. XXVII, 42; Mark XV, 30, 32; Luke XIX, 6; John VI, 33, 38, 41, 42, 50, 58; Eph. IV, 9, 10. *atsteigan dalaþ*, see under **Dalaþ**.

**GA-STEIGAN**, to climb, descend; “to embark,” **ἐμβαίνειν**: John VI, 24; “to descend,” **καταβαίνειν**: Rom. X, 7.

**US-STEIGAN**, to ascend, **ἀναβαίνειν**: Mark III, 13; Luke V, 19; XIX, 4; John VI, 62; VII, 14; Rom. X, 6; Eph. IV, 8, 9, 10; *to embark*, **ἐμβαίνειν**: John VI, 17 (where the Gothic undoubtedly read **ἀναβαίνειν**, together with the manuscripts).

**UFAR-STEIGAN**, to ascend, **ἀναβαίνειν**: Mark IV, 7.

**STAIGA**, feminine: path, way, **ὁδός**: Mark I, 3; Luke III, 4; street, **ῥύμη**: Luke XIV, 21.

**STIBNA** (Old Norse *stefna*; Anglo-Saxon *stefen, stemn*; Old Saxon *stemna*; Old Frisian *stemme*; English *steven*; Swedish *stämma*; Danish and Dutch *stemme*; modern High German *Stimme*; DRA. 845; Rchth. 1047), feminine: voice, **φωνή**: Matt. XXVII, 46, 50; Mark I, 3, 11, 26; V, 7; IX, 7; XV, 34, 37; Luke I, 42, 44; III, 4, 22; VIII, 28; IX, 35, 36; XVII, 13, 15; XIX, 37; John V, 37; X, 3, 4, 5, 16, 27; XI, 43; XII, 28, 30; XVIII, 37; Gal. IV, 20; 1 Thess. IV, 16; Skeir. VI, c.

* **STIGGAN** (compare **Stikan**), weak verb I, *stagg, stuggun, stuggans*: to prick.

**US-STIGGAN**, to pluck out (remove), **ἐξαιρεῖν**: Matt. V, 29; see the note on this passage.

**STIGQAN** (*stiggqan*, John XI, 9, 10; Rom. IX, 32; Anglo-Saxon *stingan*; Gr. II, 36), weak verb I, *stagq, stugqun, stugqans*: to engage in battle, **συμβάλλειν**: Luke XIV, 31.

**BI-STIGQAN**, to fall down, rush upon; “to fall upon,” **προσπίπτειν**: Matt. VII, 25, 27; “to dash against,” **προσρηγνύναι**: Luke VI, 48, 49; “to stumble,” **προσκόπτειν**: Rom. IX, 32.

**GA-STIGQAN**, to stumble, **προσκόπτειν**: John XI, 9, 10.

**GA-STAGQJAN**, weak verb II, the same: Luke IV, 11.

**BI-STUGQS** (*bistuggqs*, Rom. IX, 32, 33; 2 Cor. VI, 3), feminine (?): stumbling, offence, **πρόσκομμα**: Rom. IX, 32, 33; XIV, 13; **προσκοπή**, “a stumbling”: 2 Cor. VI, 3; see the note on this passage.

* **STIKAN** (Old Norse *stika*; Old Saxon *stican*; Anglo-Saxon *stician*; Old High German *stehhan*; Old Frisian *steka*; English *stick*; Swedish *sticka*; Danish *stikke*; modern High German *stechen, stecken*; Greek **στίζειν**, “to tattoo, mark”; compare **Stiggan, Stigqan**; Gr. II, 27; Rchth. 1047), weak verb I, *stak, stekun, stukans*: to fasten, pierce.

**STIKS**, masculine: point, moment, **στιγμή**: Luke IV, 5.

**STAKS**, feminine (?): mark, tattoo-mark, **στίγμα**: Gal. VI, 17.

* **STAKJAN**, weak verb II: to prick, fasten.

**HLEþRA-STAKEINS**, feminine: Feast of Tabernacles, **σκηνοπηγία**: John VII, 2.

**STIKLS** (from **Stikan**? compare Old Norse *stikill*; Gr. II, 27; III, 381), masculine: cup, drinking-vessel, **ποτήριον**: Matt. X, 42; Mark VII, 4; IX, 41; X, 38; John XVIII, 11; 1 Cor. X, 16, 17, 21; XI, 25, 26, 27, 28.

**STILAN** (Old Norse; Old Frisian *stela*; Anglo-Saxon and Old Saxon *stelan*; English *steal*; Swedish *stjäla*; Danish *stjoele*; Dutch *stelen*; modern High German *stehlen*; Gr. II, 29; DRA. 635; Rchth. 1047), weak verb I, *stal, stelun, stulans*: to steal, **κλέπτειν**: Matt. VI, 20; John X, 10.

**STIUR** (Anglo-Saxon *steor*; Old Saxon *stier*; Old High German *stior*; English *steer*; modern High German *Stier*; compare Latin *taurus*, “bull,” Greek **ταῦρος**, “bull,” Old Norse *tiur*, Swedish *tjur*, [Col. 1456] Danish *tyr*; Gr. II, 48; III, 325, 330), masculine: calf, young bull, **μόσχος**: Luke XV, 23, 27, 30; Neh. V, 18.

* **STIURS** (Old Norse *styra*; Anglo-Saxon *steore, styran*; Old Saxon *storian*; Old High German *stiura*; Old Frisian *stiora*; English *stear*; Swedish *styra*; Danish *styre*; Dutch *stieren*; modern High German *steuern*; Gr. II, 48; Rchth. 1050), adjective: determined, fixed.

**US-STIURIBA**, adverb: recklessly, dissolutely, **ἀσώτως**: Luke XV, 13.

**US-STIUREI**, feminine: license, dissipation, **ἀσωτία**: Eph. V, 18; Tit. I, 6.

**STIURJAN**, weak verb II:  
1. to establish, **ἱστάναι**: Rom. X, 3;  
2. to affirm, **διαβεβαιοῦσθαι**: 1 Tim. I, 7.

**STIVITI**, neuter: endurance, patience, **ὑπομονή**: 2 Cor. I, 6; VI, 4; 2 Thess. I, 4.

**STUBJUS** (Old High German *stuppi*; Swedish *stoft*; Danish *stov*; Dutch *stof*; modern High German *Staub*; Gr. II, 19; III, 379), masculine: dust, **κονιορτός**: Luke X, 11.

**STUGQS**, see under **Stigqan**.

**STRAUJAN** (Old Norse *stra*; English *streovian*; Old Saxon *strewian*; Old Frisian *strewa*; Anglo-Saxon *straw*; Swedish *strå*; Danish *stroe*; Dutch *strooijen*; modern High German *streuen*; Latin *sternere*, “to spread”; Greek **στρωννύναι**, “to spread”; compare *strava* in Jordanes, *On the Origin and Deeds of the Getae*, p. 132, Lindenbrog: “[After Attila had been mourned with lamentations, they celebrate over his tomb, with a great feast, the *strava*, as they themselves call it]”; *straba* in the scholiast on Statius, *Thebaid* 12, 64: “[For dead kings a pyre was built from the spoils of enemies; barbarians are said even today to preserve this burial rite, which they call *strabas* in their own language]”; Rchth. 1053), weak verb II: to spread, **στρωννύναι**: Mark XI, 8; XIV, 15.

**UF-STRAUJAN**, to spread underneath, **ὑποστρωννύναι**: Luke XIX, 36.

**STRIKS** (Old Norse and Old Frisian *strik*; Old High German *strih*; Anglo-Saxon *strica*; Old Saxon *stric*; English *stroke*; Swedish *strek*; Danish *streg*; Dutch *streke*; modern High German *Strich*; Gr. II, 17, 53; Rchth. 1054), masculine: stroke, line, **κεραία**: Matt. V, 18.

**STODJAN**, see under **Standan**.

**STOþANS**, see under **Standan**.

**STOLS** (Old Norse *stoll*; Anglo-Saxon, Old Saxon, and Old Frisian *stol*; Old High German *stuol*; English *stool*; Swedish and Danish *stol*; Dutch *stoel*; modern High German *Stuhl*; compare Greek **στήλη**, “pillar,” **στύλος**, “column”; Gr. II, 41; III, 433; Rchth. 1051), masculine: step, throne, **θρόνος**: Matt. V, 34; Luke I, 32, 52.

**STAUA-STOLS**, judgment-seat, tribunal, **βῆμα**: Matt. XXVII, 19; Rom. XIV, 10; 2 Cor. V, 10.

**STOMA** (compare modern High German *Stamm*), masculine: assurance, confidence, **ὑπόστασις**: 2 Cor. IX, 4; XI, 17.

**STOJAN**, see under **Staua**.

**SVA** (Old Norse *sva, svo, so*; Anglo-Saxon *sva*; Old Saxon, Old High German, English, and modern High German *so*; Old Frisian *sa, so*; Swedish *så*; Danish *saa*; Dutch *zo*; Greek **ὥς**, “as”; Latin *sic*, “thus”; Bopp 190; Gf. VI, 11; Rchth. 998), adverb: thus, so, **οὕτω**: Matt. V, 16, 19; VI, 9, 30; VII, 12, 17; IX, 33; Mark II, 7, 8, 12; IV, 26, 40; VII, 18; X, 43; XIV, 59; XV, 39; Luke I, 25, 29; II, 48; IX, 15; X, 21; XV, 7, 10; XVII, 10, 24, 26; John V, 21; VIII, 59; XIII, 15, 25; XIV, 31; XV, 4, 5; XVIII, 22; Rom. IX, 20; X, 6; XI, 26, 31; XII, 5; 1 Cor. V, 3; VII, 7, 17, 26; IX, 24, 26; XI, 28; XIV, 21; XV, 11; 2 Cor. I, 5; VII, 14; VIII, 11; X, 7; Gal. I, 6; III, 3; IV, 3; VI, 1; Eph. IV, 20; Phil. III, 17; IV, 1; Col. III, 13; 1 Thess. IV, 14; V, 2; 2 Thess. III, 17; 1 Tim. III, 10; 2 Tim. III, 8; Skeir. I, d; V, c; VI, c; VII, b; “likewise,” **ὡσαύτως**: 1 Tim. III, 8; “and,” **καί**: John XIII, 15; XV, 9; XVII, 18. *sva jah*, “thus also,” **οὕτω καί**: 1 Cor. XII, 12; XVI, 1; 2 Cor. I, 5; VII, 14; VIII, 11; X, 7; “thus,” **οὕτω**: Eph. V, 28. *sva samaleiko*, “likewise,” **ὡσαύτως**: 1 Cor. XI, 25.

**SVAH** (compare *…uh*), ordinarily correlative with *sve* or *svasve*: thus also, **οὕτω καί**: 1 Cor. XV, 22; 2 Cor. VIII, 6; Eph. V, 24; “thus,” **οὕτω**: Luke XIV, 33; “and,” **καί**: John XV, 9; XVII, 8. *svah jah*, “thus,” **οὕτω καί**: Mark [Col. 1457] XIII, 29; Luke XVII, 26; Gal. IV, 29. *svah nih*, “thus not even,” **οὕτως οὐδέ**: John XV, 4.

**SVAU** (compare *…u*), in a question: “Is it so?” **οὕτω**: John XVIII, 22.

**SVAEI** (also written separately *sva-ei*, 2 Cor. VIII, 13; see the note on this passage), conjunction:

1. as, **ὡς**: Luke III, 23;
2. so that, **ὥστε**: Mark I, 27; 2 Cor. III, 7; VII, 2; VIII, 5; Gal. II, 13; 2 Thess. I, 4; II, 4; Skeir. III, d; “for the purpose of,” **εἰς τό**: 2 Cor. VIII, 5; “in order that,” **ἵνα**: 2 Cor. VIII, 13; Gal. II, 9;
3. so that, therefore, **ὥστε**: Mark II, 28; Rom. VII, 6; XIII, 2; 1 Cor. XIV, 22; 2 Cor. II, 7; IV, 12; V, 16, 17; Gal. IV, 7. Pleonastically *svaei nu*, the same: Rom. VII, 4; 1 Cor. XIV, 22; XV, 58; 2 Cor. IV, 12; Phil. IV, 1; 1 Thess. IV, 18.

**SVA-LAUDS**, see under **Lauds**.

**SVA-LEIKS**, see under **Leiks**.

**SVE** (Bopp 189; Gr. III, 43; IV, 707), correlative with *sva*:

1. how, as, **ὡς**: Matt. VI, 10, 12, 29; VII, 29; X, 25; Mark I, 2, 22; IV, 27, 30, 36; VI, 15; VII, 6; VIII, 24; IX, 3; X, 1, 15; XII, 25, 31; XIV, 48, 72; Luke VI, 22, 36, 40; IX, 54; X, 3, 18, 27; XIV, 22; XV, 19; XVII, 6, 28; XVIII, 17; XX, 37; John VII, 10; Rom. VIII, 36; IX, 29; XIII, 9, 13; 1 Cor. IV, 7; V, 3; VII, 25; IX, 20, 22; XIII, 11; 2 Cor. II, 17; III, 1; V, 20; VI, 4, 8, 9, 13; VII, 15; VIII, 7; X, 2, 9; XI, 15, 16, 17; Gal. IV, 12, 14; V, 14, 21; Eph. V, 1, 8, 28; VI, 20; Phil. I, 20; II, 7, 22; Col. II, 20; III, 12, 18; 1 Thess. II, 11; V, 2, 4, 6; 1 Tim. V, 1; 2 Tim. II, 3, 8, 17; Skeir. II, c; VI, d; VII, a, b; “as also,” **ὡς καί**: 1 Cor. VII, 7, 8; IX, 5; “as though,” **ὡς ἄν**: 2 Cor. X, 9; “as if,” **ὡς εἰ** (Matt. IX, 36; Mark I, 10): Matt. IX, 26; Luke III, 22; “just as,” **καθώς**: John XIII, 34; XV, 4; Eph. III, 3; 2 Thess. III, 1; “just as also,” **καθὼς καί**: 1 Thess. IV, 13; “just as,” **καθάπερ**: 1 Cor. XII, 12; “and,” **καί**: 1 Tim. IV, 7 (where the Gothic renders comparatively what the Greek presents conjunctively). *sve raihtis*, “just as,” **ὥσπερ**: 2 Cor. VIII, 7;
2. about, **ὡς**: Mark V, 13; VIII, 9; Luke VIII, 42; John VI, 19; “about,” **ὡσεί**: Luke I, 56; III, 23; IX, 14, 28;
3. thus, when, **ὡς**: Luke I, 41; IV, 25; John VI, 16; XI, 6; XVIII, 6; “when,” **ἡνίκα**: Neh. VI, 16; XVII, 1; in place of the Greek genitive absolute: Luke VIII, 23, *sve faridedun* (“while they were sailing,” **πλεόντων αὐτῶν**);
4. so that, sometimes with the infinitive, **ὥστε**: Luke V, 6, 7; IX, 52;
5. Gal. IV, 16 has *ïþ nu sve* in place of **ὥστε**, which is wholly inexplicable.

*sva lagga sve*, “as long as”; *svaleiks sve*, *sva manags sve*, *sva ufta sve*, *sva filu sve*, see under **Laggs, Leiks, Manags, Ufta, Filu**.

**SVASVE**:

1. as, **οὕτως ὡς**: John VII, 46; 2 Cor. IX, 5; **ὡς**: Matt. VI, 12; VII, 29; VIII, 13; XXVII, 65; Mark I, 22; IV, 26; Luke III, 4; Rom. IX, 25, 27; XII, 3; 1 Cor. VII, 17; XVI, 10; 2 Cor. II, 17; III, 5; VII, 14; X, 14; XI, 3 (23; see the note on this passage); XIII, 2; Eph. II, 3; III, 5; V, 22; 2 Thess. III, 15; 2 Tim. III, 9; Skeir. III, c; “just as,” **ὥσπερ**: Matt. V, 48; VI, 2, 5, 7, 16; Luke XVII, 24; XVIII, 11; John V, 21; Rom. XI, 30 (XII, 4); 1 Cor. IV, 9; XV, 22; XVI, 1; 2 Cor. I, 7; IX, 5; Gal. IV, 29; Eph. V, 24; 1 Thess. XV, 8; “just as,” **καθώς**: Mark IV, 33; IX, 13; XI, 6; XV, 8; XVI, 7; Luke I, 2, 55, 70; II, 20, 23; VI, 10, 31; XVII, 26; XVIII, 11; XIX, 32; John V, 23; VI, 31, 57, 58; VII, 38; VIII, 28; X, 15, 26; XII, 14; XIII, 15, 33; XIV, 27, 31; XV, 9, 10, 12; XVII, 2, 11, 14, 16, 18, 21, 22, 23; Rom. VIII, 36; IX, 12, 29, 32; X, 15; XI, 26; XV, 7, 9; 1 Cor. V, 7; XI, 2; XII, 11, 18; XV, 49; 2 Cor. I, 5; IV, 1; VIII, 5, 6, 15; IX, 3, 7, 9; X, 7; XI, 12; Gal. II, 7; III, 6; Eph. I, 4; IV, 4, 17, 21; V, 2; Phil. III, 17; Col. I, 7; III, 13; 1 Thess. II, 13, 14; III, 4; IV, 1, 6, 11 (*svasve jah*); V, 11; 2 Thess. I, 3; 1 Tim. I, 3; “just as also,” **καθὼς καί**: 1 Cor. X, 33; XI, 1; 2 Cor. I, 14; “as,” **καθά**: Matt. XXVII, 10; “just as,” **καθάπερ**: Rom. XII, 4; 2 Cor. I, 14; III, 13, 18; VIII, 11; 1 Thess. II, 11; III, 6, 12; IV, 5. Luke II, 24: *svasve qiþan ïst*, “as it has been said,” **κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον**;
2. according to whatever, **καθὸ ἐάν**: 2 Cor. VIII, 12;
3. about, approximately, **ὡς**: John VI, 19; XI, 18; “about,” **ὡσεί**: John VI, 10;
4. so that, also with the infinitive, **ὥστε**: Matt. VIII, 24, 28; XXVII, 14; Mark I, 45; II, 2, [Col. 1458] 12; III, 10, 20; IV, 1, 32, 37; IX, 26; X, 8; XV, 5; 1 Cor. XIII, 2; 2 Cor. I, 8.

**SVAGGVJAN**, see under **Sviggvan**.

**SVAIHRA** (Old Norse *svara*; Anglo-Saxon *sveor, sveger*; Old Saxon *suiri*; Old High German *suehor*; Swedish *svär*; Danish *svoger*; Dutch *swager*; modern High German *Schwager, Schwieger*; Latin *socer*, “father-in-law”; Greek **ἑκυρός**, “father-in-law”; Bopp 81; Gr. II, 53; III, 335), masculine: father-in-law, **πενθερός**: John XVIII, 13.

**SVAIHRO**, feminine: mother-in-law, **πενθερά**: Matt. VIII, 14; X, 35; Mark I, 30; Luke IV, 38.

* **SVAIRBAN** (Old Norse *sverfa*; Old Saxon *suerban*; Latin *sorbere*, “to swallow up”; Gr. II, 38), weak verb I, *svarf, svaurbun, svaurbans*: to erase.

**AF-SVAIRBAN**, to wipe out, blot out, **ἐξαλείφειν**: Col. II, 14.

**BI-SVAIRBAN**, the same, “to wipe away,” **ἐκμάσσειν**: Luke VII, 38, 44; John XI, 2; XII, 3.

**SVALLEINS**, see under **Svillan**.

**SVAMMS** (*svams*, Mark XV, 36; Old Norse *svampr*; Anglo-Saxon *svam*; Old High German *swam*; Swedish and Danish *svamp*; Dutch *swamme*; modern High German *Schwamm*; compare **Svimman**; Gr. II, 33; III, 372), masculine: sponge, **σπόγγος**: Matt. XXVII, 48; Mark XV, 36.

**SVARAN** (Old Norse *svara, sveria*; Anglo-Saxon *sverian*; Old Saxon *suerian*; Old High German *swerjan*; Old Frisian *swera*; English *swear*; Swedish *svärja*; Danish *svaerge*; Dutch *sweeren*; modern High German *schwören*; Gr. II, 9; DRA. 892; Rchth. 1058), weak verb I, *svor, svorun, svarans*: to swear, **ὀμνύειν, ὀμνύναι**: Matt. V, 34, 36; XXVI, 74; Mark VI, 23; XIV, 71; Luke I, 73.

**BI-SVARAN**, to adjure, **ὁρκίζειν**: Mark V, 7; 1 Thess. V, 27.

**UFAR-SVARAN**, to swear falsely, commit perjury, **ἐπιορκεῖν**: Matt. V, 33.

**UFAR-SVARA** (*ufar-svars*?), masculine: perjurer, **ἐπίορκος**: 1 Tim. I, 10.

**SVARE** (*svarei*, 2 Cor. VI, 1; compare modern High German *schwer*), adverb: in vain, gratuitously:

1. without reason, **εἰκῇ**: Matt. V, 22; Rom. XIII, 4; 1 Cor. XV, 2; Gal. III, 4; IV, 11; Col. II, 18; Skeir. IV, b;
2. in vain, **μάτην**: Mark VII, 7; **μάταιος**, “vain”: 1 Cor. XV, 17; “into emptiness,” **εἰς κενόν**: 2 Cor. VI, 1; Gal. II, 2; 1 Thess. III, 5; **κενός**, “empty”: 1 Cor. XV, 14 (where the adverb is used as an adjective); “freely, without cause,” **δωρεάν**: Gal. II, 21.

**SVARTS** (Old Norse *svartr*; Anglo-Saxon *sveart*; Old Saxon *suart*; Old Frisian *swart*; English, Swedish, and Dutch *svart*; Danish *sort*; modern High German *schwarz*; Rchth. 1057), adjective: black, **μέλας**: Matt. V, 36.

**SVARTIZL**, neuter: blackness, ink, **μέλαν**: 2 Cor. III, 3.

**SVARTIZLA**, feminine: the same: 2 Cor. III, 3, this passage.

**SVE**, see under **Sva**.

**SVEGNJAN** (*svignjan*, John V, 35; Col. III, 15; compare Anglo-Saxon *svegian*, Old Saxon *suogan*), weak verb II: to rejoice, exult, **ἀγαλλιάζειν**: Luke I, 47; X, 21; John V, 35; “to rule,” **βραβεύειν**: Col. III, 15.

**SVEGNIþA** (*svigniþa*, Luke I, 44), feminine: joy, gladness, exultation, **ἀγαλλίασις**: Luke I, 14, 44.

**SVEIBAN** (Old Norse *svefia*), weak verb I, *svaif, svibun, svibans*: to cease, leave off, **διαλείπειν**: Luke VII, 45.

**UN-SVEIBANDS**, present participle: unceasing, unremitting, “not ceasing,” **οὐ παυόμενος**: Eph. I, 16; “unceasing,” **ἀδιάλειπτος**: 1 Thess. II, 13; V, 17; 2 Tim. I, 3.

**SVEIN** (Old Norse, Anglo-Saxon, and Swedish *svin*; Old High German *suu, swin*; Old Saxon and Old Frisian *suin, swin*; English *swine*; Danish *sviin*; Dutch *zwijn*; modern High German *Schwein*; Latin *sus*, “pig”; Greek **ὗς**, “swine”; Gr. III, 329; Gf. VI, 63; Rchth. 1062), neuter: pig, swine, **χοῖρος**: Matt. VIII, 30; Mark V, 11, 12, 13, 14, 16; Luke VIII, 32, 33; XV, 15, 16.

* **SVEIPAN** (Old Norse *svipa, sopa*; Anglo-Saxon *svapan*; English *sweep*; modern High German *schweppern*; Gr. II, 13; DM. 472), weak verb II: to flood.

**MIDJA-SVEIPAINS**, feminine: flood, deluge, **κατακλυσμός**: Luke XII, 27.

**SVERAN** (Anglo-Saxon *syrvan*), weak verb I, *saisvor, sverans*: to plot against, lie in wait for, **ἐνέχειν**: Mark VI, 19; see the note on this passage.

**SVERS** (Anglo-Saxon *svaer*; modern High German *schwer*), [Col. 1459] adjective: honoured, held in honour, **ἔντιμος**: Luke VII, 2; Phil. II, 29.

**UN-SVERS**, dishonoured, without honour, **ἄτιμος**: Mark VI, 4; 1 Cor. IV, 10.

**SVERIþA**, feminine: honour, **τιμή**: Col. II, 23; 1 Thess. IV, 4; 1 Tim. I, 17; VI, 1; 2 Tim. II, 21; Skeir. V, a, c, d.

**UN-SVERIþA**, dishonour, ignominy, **ἀτιμία**: 2 Cor. XI, 21.

**ALL-SVEREI**, feminine: uprightness, simplicity, **ἁπλότης**: Rom. XII, 8.

**UN-SVEREI**, dishonour, **ἀτιμία**: 2 Cor. VI, 8.

**SVERAN**, weak verb II:

1. to honour, **τιμᾶν**: Mark VII, 6, 10; X, 19; Luke XVIII, 20; John V, 23; VIII, 49; XII, 23, 26; 1 Tim. V, 3; “to regard,” **ἡγεῖσθαι**: 1 Thess. V, 13;
2. to glorify, **δοξάζειν**: John XII, 23.

**GA-SVERAN**, to glorify, **δοξάζειν**: John XII, 16; XIII, 31.

**UN-SVERAN**, to dishonour, **ἀτιμάζειν**: Luke XX, 11; John VIII, 49.

**SVERAINS**, feminine: honour, **τιμή**: 2 Tim. II, 20.

**UN-SVERAINS**, dishonour, disgrace, **ἀτιμία**: 2 Tim. II, 20.

**SVES** (Anglo-Saxon *svaes*; Old Saxon and Old High German *suas*; Old Frisian *swes*; Gr. II, 52; DRA. 491; Rchth. 1060), neuter: property, possessions, **οὐσία**: Luke XV, 13; livelihood, **βίος**: Luke XII, 12, 30.

**SVES**, adjective: one’s own, belonging to, **ἴδιος**: Mark XV, 20; Luke VI, 44; John X, 3, 12; XV, 19; Rom. XI, 24; 1 Cor. VII, 7; IX, 7; 2 Cor. V, 10 (see the note on this passage); Gal. VI, 5, 9; Eph. IV, 28; 1 Thess. II, 15; IV, 11; 1 Tim. II, 6; IV, 2; V, 4, 8; VI, 15; Tit. I, 3, 12; Skeir. I, c; V, b; “belonging to the household,” **οἰκεῖος**: Gal. VI, 10.

* **SVI**, inseparable preposition.

**SVI-KUNþS**, see under **Kunnan**.

**SVIBLS** (Anglo-Saxon *svefel*; Old High German *sueful*; Swedish *svafvel*; Danish *svovel*; modern High German *Schwefel*; Gr. III, 381), masculine: sulphur, brimstone, **θεῖον**: Luke XVII, 29.

* **SVIGGVAN** (Old Norse *svigna*; Anglo-Saxon *svengan*; Old Saxon *suingan*; Old Frisian *swinga*; English *swing*; Swedish *svinga*; Danish *svinge*; modern High German *schwingen*; Gr. II, 37; Rchth. 1062), weak verb I, *svaggv, svuggvun, svuggvans*: to sway, fluctuate.

* **SVAGGVJAN**, weak verb II: to shake.
