**TIUHAN** (Old Norse *toga*, Anglo-Saxon *teon*, Old Saxon *tiohan*, Old Frisian *tia, toga*, Old High German *ziuhan*, English *tug*, Modern High German *ziehen*; Latin *ducere*; Gr. II, 24; Gf. V, 600; Rchth. 1082, 1090), class I verb, *tauh, tauhun, tauhans*, to draw, lead, ἄγειν: Luke IV, 1; XVIII, 40; John XVIII, 28; II Cor. X, 5; Gal. V, 18; I Thess. IV, 14; II Tim. III, 6; ἀπάγειν, “to lead away”: Mark XIV, 44; ὁδηγεῖν, “to guide”: Luke VI, 39; Skeir. IV, b; *frahunþanana tiuhan*, see under *Hinþan*; *gafahanana tiuhan*, see under *Fahan*.

**AT-TIUHAN**, to draw or bring to, προςάγειν: Luke IX, 41; εἰσάγειν, “to bring in”: Luke XIV, 21; John XVIII, 16; ἄγειν: Mark XI, 2; XV, 22; Luke XIX, 30, 35; John VII, 45; XIX, 4; Skeir. VIII, b; *dalaþ attiuhan*, see under *Dal*.

**ÏNNAT-TIUHAN**, to bring in, εἰσάγειν: Luke II, 27.

**AF-TIUHAN**, to bring back, ἐπανάγειν: Luke V, 3; to take aside, προςλαμβάνεσθαι: Mark VIII, 32.

**BI-TIUHAN**:

1. To lead about, περιάγειν: I Cor. IX, 5.
2. To go about seeking, with the accusative, περιάγειν: Matt. IX, 35; Mark VI, 6.

**GA-TIUHAN**, to lead, lead away, ἄγειν: Luke IV, 9; John IX, 13; ἀπάγειν: Matt. XXVII, 2; Mark XIV, 53; XV, 16; John XVIII, 13; κατάγειν, “to bring down”: Luke V, 11; *du stauai gatiuhan*, see under *Staua*.

**MIþGA-TIUHAN**, to carry away together, συναπάγειν: Gal. II, 13.

**US-TIUHAN**:

1. To lead out, cast out, ἐξάγειν: Mark VIII, 23; XV, 20; John X, 3; ἐκβάλλειν: Mark I, 12; John X, 4; ἀνάγειν, “to lead up”: Luke IV, 5; ἀναφέρειν, “to bring up”: Mark IX, 2; *ïup ustiuhan*, to lead upward, ἀνάγειν: Rom. X, 7.
2. To complete, finish, bring to an end, τελεῖν: Matt. X, 23; XXVI, 1; Luke II, 39; XVIII, 31; II Cor. XII, 9; Gal. V, 6, 16; II Tim. IV, 7; Neh. VI, 15; τελειοῦν, “to make complete”: Luke II, 43; John XVII, 4, 23; ἐκτελεῖν, “to carry through”: Luke XIV, 29, 30; συντελεῖν, “to complete”: Matt. VII, 28; Luke IV, 2, 13; Rom. IX, 28; ἐπιτελεῖν, “to bring to completion”: II Cor. VII, 1; VIII, 6, 11; Gal. III, 3; καταρτίζειν, “to equip, restore”: Luke VI, 40, in this passage; II Cor. XIII, 11; I Thess. III, 10; παριστάναι, “to present”: Eph. V, 27; κατεργάζεσθαι, “to produce”: II Cor. VII, 10; *du ustiuhan*, “for completion,” πρὸς ἀπαρτισμόν: Luke XIV, 28; hence passive participle *ustauhans*, completed, perfect, τέλειος: Rom. XII, 2; I Cor. XIII, 10; ἄρτιος, “complete, equipped”: II Tim. III, 17; Skeir. I, a.
3. Intransitively, to finish, only in the subscriptions of the Epistles to Romans, I and II Corinthians, Galatians, Ephesians, Colossians, and II Thessalonians.
4. To pay, τελεῖν: Rom. XIII, 6.

**US-TAUHTS**, feminine, completion, perfection, τελειότης: [Col. 1465] Col. III, 14; τελείωσις: Luke I, 45; τέλος: Rom. X, 4; κατάρτισις: II Cor. XIII, 9.

**US-TAUHEI**, feminine, the same, καταρτισμός: Eph. IV, 12.

**TIVAN** (Old Norse *tivaskr*, Old High German *zawian, gizawa*, Anglo-Saxon *tavian*, English *taw*, Dutch *touwen*; Gf. V, 713; Schm. IV, 209), class I verb, *tau, tevun, tivans*, to be prepared.

**TAUJAN**, class II verb:

1. To do, make, ποιεῖν: Matt. V, 46; VIII, 9; IX, 28; Mark II, 24; III, 8; V, 32; VII, 8, 13; X, 17; XI, 3, 5, 28, 33; XII, 9; Luke III, 10, 11, 12, 14; IV, 23; V, 6; VI, 2, 46, 49; VII, 8; X, 25, 28; XVI, 3, 4; XVIII, 18; XX, 2, 13; John VI, 6, 28, 39; VII, 4, 51; VIII, 28, 38, 40; IX, 33; XIII, 15, 17, 27; XIV, 13, 14, 31; XV, 5, 14, 15; XVI, 3; Rom. VII, 15, 16, 20; XII, 20; I Cor. IX, 23; X, 31; XVI, 1; II Cor. VIII, 10, 11; XI, 12; XIII, 7; Gal. II, 10; V, 17; VI, 9; Eph. III, 20; VI, 8; Col. III, 13, 17, 23; I Thess. V, 11; II Thess. III, 4; I Tim. IV, 16; V, 21; Philem. 14; πράττειν, “to do, practise”: Rom. VII, 15, 19; IX, 11; XIII, 4; Gal. V, 21; Eph. VI, 21; Phil. IV, 9; I Thess. IV, 11; τελειοῦν, “to finish”: John V, 36. It is also used in very many expressions in which Greek likewise uses ποιεῖν, as: *viljan taujan*, “to do [the] will”: John VI, 38; VII, 17; IX, 31; Eph. II, 3; *lustuns taujan*, “to do desires”: John VIII, 44; *fravaurht taujan*, “to commit transgression”: II Cor. XI, 7; *vaurstv taujan*, “to do works”: John V, 36; VII, 3; VIII, 39, 41; X, 37, 38; XIV, 10, 12; *taikn taujan*, “to perform a sign”: John VI, 30; VII, 31; IX, 16; *anabusn taujan*, “to make a commandment”: Matt. V, 19; *þo anabudanona taujan*, “to do what has been commanded”: Luke XVII, 10; *vitoþ taujan*, “to do the law”: John VII, 19; Gal. V, 3; *vaurd taujan*, “to do the word”: Matt. VII, 24, 26; Luke VI, 47; VIII, 21; *armahairtiþa taujan*, “to show mercy”: Luke I, 72; *garaihtein taujan*, “to perform righteousness”: Rom. X, 5; *sunja taujan*, “to do truth”: Eph. IV, 15; *gavairþi taujan*, see under *Vairþan*; *usvahst taujan*, “to cause growth”: Eph. IV, 16; *akran taujan*, “to bear fruit”: Luke VI, 43; VIII, 8; *staua taujan*, Skeir. V, c; *garuni taujan*, “to take counsel”: Mark XV, 1; *bidos taujan*, “to make prayers”: Luke V, 33; I Tim. II, 1; *armaion taujan*, “to give alms”: Matt. VI, 1, 2, 3; and with similar nouns understood: I Cor. XVI, 2, *warjizuh ïzvara fram sis silbin taujai* (τιθέτω), “let each of you put aside for himself”; *freihals taujan* (ἐλευθερίαν διδόναι?), “to grant freedom”: Gal. V, 13; *vaila taujan*, to do good, εὖ ποιεῖν: Mark XIV, 7; καλῶς ποιεῖν: Matt. V, 44; Luke VI, 27; καλοποιεῖν: II Thess. III, 13; *harduba taujan*, to act harshly, ἀποτόμως χρῆσθαι: II Cor. XIII, 10; *vairaleiko taujan*, see under *Leiks*; *þiuþ taujan*, see under *þiuþ*; *galiug taujan*, see under *Liugan*. Besides the accusative of the thing done, or the adverb indicating how it is done, there is also a dative denoting the person for whom something is done, or with whom something is done, etc.; hence Matt. VII, 12 (*sva jah taujaiþ ïm*), XXV, 40, 45; Mark VII, 12; X, 35, 36, 51; XV, 8, 12; Luke VI, 11, 23, 26, 31; XVIII, 41; XX, 15; John XV, 21; also with *bi* governing the accusative: Luke II, 27; *viþra*: Eph. VI, 9; *ïn* governing the accusative: I Thess. IV, 10.
2. To make:
   a. With a double accusative: *wana þuk silban taujis?*, “what do you make yourself?” (τίνα σεαυτὸν ποιεῖς?): John XV, 8; XIX, 12; Luke XVI, 9, where the accusative of the object is understood; Rom. IX, 28. The predicate is also expressed with *du*: *taujis þuk silban du guþa*, “you make yourself God” (ποιεῖς σεαυτὸν θεόν): John X, 33; VI, 15; Rom. IX, 21; Gal. V, 13.
   b. With a following accusative and infinitive: *taujiþ þo horinon*, “he makes her commit adultery” (ποιεῖ αὐτὴν μοιχᾶσθαι): Matt. V, 32; likewise *liban taujan*, see under *Liban*.
   c. With a following *ei*: *taujaiþ ei* (ἵνα), “that [they may] also be read in the Laodicean church”: Col. IV, 16.

**GA-TAUJAN**:

1. To do, make, ποιεῖν: Mark II, 25; V, 19; VI, 20, 30; IX, 13; XIV, 8, 9; XV, 14; Luke VI, 3; IX, 10, 15, 43; XVII, 9, 10; XIX, 48; John XI, 43, 46; XVIII, 35; I Tim. I, 13; Skeir. VII, c; πράττειν: II Cor. V, 10; XII, 21; κατεργάζεσθαι, “to accomplish”: I Cor. V, 3; II Cor. VII, 11; XII, 12. In very many expressions corresponding to Greek ποιεῖν, as: *saliþva gataujan*, “to make a dwelling”: John XIV, 23; *vaurstv gataujan*, “to do works”: John VII, 21; XV, 24; *maht gataujan*, “to perform mighty works”: Matt. VII, 22; Mark VI, 5; *taikn gataujan*, “to perform signs”: John VI, 2, 14; X, 41; XII, 18, 37; *mun gataujan*, “to make purpose”: Eph. III, 11; *mikilein gataujan*, “to do great things”: Luke I, 49; *svinþein gataujan*, “to show strength”: Luke I, 51; *garuni gataujan*, “to take counsel”: Mark III, 6; *maurþr gataujan*, “to commit murder”: Mark XV, 7; *akrana gataujan*, “to bear fruit”: Matt. VII, 17; *sinapi gataujiþ astans mikilans*, “it makes branches great”: Mark IV, 32; *þaurft sis gataujan*, see under *þaurban*; *vaurstveig gataujan*, see [Col. 1466] under *Vaurstv*; *minnizo gataujan*, see under *Mins*; *vaila gataujan*, “to do well”: Mark VII, 37; Phil. IV, 14; *froduba gataujan*, “to act wisely,” φρονίμως ποιεῖν: Luke XVI, 8. As after *taujan* (see above), so here too the dative is used: Mark V, 19 (*wan filu þus frauja gatavida*, “how much the Lord did for you”), 20; IX, 13; Luke I, 25, 49; II, 48; VIII, 39; John IX, 26; XII, 16; XIII, 12, 15; *taikn gataujan bi siukamma*, “to perform signs concerning the sick man”: John VI, 2.
2. To make, ποιεῖν:
   a. With a double accusative: Matt. V, 36; Mark X, 6, where the accusative of the object is understood; John VII, 23; XIX, 7; Rom. IX, 20, where *sva* occurs in place of *svaleik*; hence *dvalana gataujan*, see under *Dvals*; *vanana gataujan*, see under *Vans*. The predicate is also rendered with *du*: Luke XIX, 46, *gard meinana gatavideduþ du filegrja þiube*, “you have made my house a den of thieves”; Eph. II, 14; or periphrastically with *sve*: Luke XV, 19, *gatavei mik sve ainana asnje*, “make me as one of [your] hired servants.”
   b. With a following accusative and infinitive: Mark I, 17; VII, 37; VIII, 25; Luke V, 34; IX, 15; Skeir. VII, c; thus *ganohnan gataujan*, see under *Nahan*; *vahsjan gataujan*, see under *Vahsjan*; *anakumbjan gataujan*, see under *Kumbjan*; *liban gataujan*, see under *Liban*.
   c. With a following *ei*: John XI, 37.

**MISSA-TAUJANDS**, participle, evildoer, one who does wrong, παραβάτης: Gal. II, 18.

**TAUÏ**, neuter, genitive *tojis*, work, deed, ἔργον: John VIII, 41; πρᾶξις: Rom. XII, 4; Col. III, 9; πρᾶγμα: II Cor. VII, 11; ποίημα: Eph. II, 10; ἐνέργεια: Eph. III, 7.

**UBIL-TOJIS**, adjective, evildoer, κακοποιός: John XVIII, 30; criminal, κακοῦργος: II Tim. II, 9.

**FULLA-TOJIS**, perfect, τέλειος: Matt. V, 48.

**TEVA**, feminine, order, sequence, τάγμα: I Cor. XV, 23.

**TEVI**, neuter, company, band: I Cor. XV, 6, in this passage.

**GA-TEVJAN**, class II verb, to appoint, ordain, χειροτονεῖν: II Cor. VIII, 19.

**UNGA-TEVIþS**, unordered; *ungateviþs visan*, to behave disorderly, ἀτακτεῖν: II Thess. III, 8.

**TUGGL** (Old Norse *tungl*, Anglo-Saxon *tungel*, Old Saxon *tungal*, Old High German *zungal*, Swedish *tungel*; Gr. II, 61; III, 392; DM. 399; Gf. V, 683), neuter (?), star: Gal. IV, 3, in this passage.

**TUGGO** (Old Norse *tunga*, Anglo-Saxon *tunge*, Old Saxon *tunga*, Old Frisian *tunge, tonge*, Old High German *zunka*, English *tongue*, Swedish *tunga*, Danish *tunge*, Dutch *tonge*, Modern High German *Zunge*; Latin *lingua*; Bopp 165; Gr. II, 61; III, 400; Gf. V, 681; Rchth. 1094), feminine, tongue, γλῶσσα: Mark VII, 33, 35; Luke I, 64.

**TUZ**, see under *Tvai*.

**TUKEIKUS**, the same as *Tykeikus*.

**TULGUS** (Anglo-Saxon *tulgo*, English *tall*; Gr. II, 58), adjective, steadfast, ἑδραῖος: I Cor. XV, 58; firm, στερεός: II Tim. II, 19.

**TULGJAN**, class II verb, to establish, confirm, κυροῦν: II Cor. II, 8; στηρίζειν: I Thess. III, 13.

**GA-TULGJAN**, the same, στηρίζειν: Luke IX, 51; I Thess. III, 2; II Thess. II, 17; III, 3; βεβαιοῦν, “to confirm”: Rom. XV, 8; *gatulgjan sik*, to establish oneself, persevere, ἐπιμένειν: Rom. XI, 23; *gatulgids*, passive participle, established, confirmed, ἑδραῖος: Col. I, 23; βέβαιος: II Cor. I, 6; ἀμεταμέλητος, “not to be regretted”: II Cor. VII, 10.

**TULGIþA**, feminine, stronghold, ὀχύρωμα: II Cor. X, 4; security, ἀσφάλεια: I Thess. V, 3; foundation, ἑδραίωμα: I Tim. III, 15.

**TUNDNAN**, see under *Tindan*.

**TUNþUS** (Old Norse *tönn*, Anglo-Saxon *toð*, Old High German *zand, zan*, Old Frisian *tond, toth*, English *tooth*, Old Saxon, Swedish, Danish, Dutch *tand*, Modern High German *Zahn*; Latin *dens*, Greek ὀδούς; Bopp 80; Gr. II, 60; III, 400; Gf. V, 683; Rchth. 1092), masculine, tooth, ὀδούς: Matt. V, 38; VIII, 12; Mark IX, 18.

**TRAKAUNEITIDUS**, masculine proper name, Τραχωνῖτις, Trachonitis: Luke III, 1.

**TRAUADA**, feminine proper name, Τρωάς, Troas: II Cor. II, 12; II Tim. IV, 13.

**TRAUAN** (Old Norse *trua*, Anglo-Saxon *treovian*, Old Saxon *truon*, Old Frisian *triuwe, trouwa*, Modern High German *trauen, treu*, English *true, trust*, Swedish *tro*, Danish *troe*, Dutch *trouw*; [Col. 1467] Bopp 65; Gf. V, 464; Rchth. 1094), class II verb, to trust, have confidence, πεποιθέναι, with *du* or *ïn*: Matt. XXVII, 43; Luke XVIII, 9; II Cor. I, 9; Phil. III, 4; πεπεῖσθαι, “to be persuaded”: II Tim. I, 5.

**GA-TRAUAN**:

1. The same, with the dative or *ïn*, πεποιθέναι: II Cor. II, 3; X, 7; Gal. V, 10; Phil. I, 14; II, 24; III, 3; II Thess. III, 4; Philem. 21; πεπεῖσθαι: Rom. VIII, 38; XIV, 14; II Tim. I, 12; θαῤῥεῖν, “to be confident”: II Cor. V, 6, 8; VII, 16; X, 1.
2. To believe, πιστεύειν: Gal. II, 7; I Tim. I, 11; Titus I, 3; πιστοῦν, “to entrust”: II Tim. III, 14.

**TRAUAINS**, feminine, confidence, πεποίθησις: II Cor. I, 15; III, 4; VIII, 22; X, 2; Eph. III, 12; Phil. III, 4; boldness, παῤῥησία: II Cor. VII, 4; Phil. I, 20.

**TRAUSTI**, neuter, testament, covenant, διαθήκη: Eph. II, 12.

**TRIGGVS** (compare *Trauan*?), adjective, faithful, πιστός: Luke XVI, 10, 11, 12; XIX, 17; I Cor. IV, 2; VII, 25; II Cor. I, 18; Eph. I, 1; VI, 21; Phil. I, 20; Col. I, 7; IV, 7, 9; II Thess. III, 3; I Tim. I, 15; III, 1, 11; IV, 9; II Tim. II, 2, 11, 13; Titus I, 9.

**UN-TRIGGVS**, unfaithful, unjust, ἄδικος: Luke XVI, 10.

**TRIGGVABA**, adverb, faithfully, confidently; *triggvaba vitan*, to know with confidence, πεποιθὼς εἰδέναι: Phil. I, 25; *triggvaba galaubjan*, to be firmly persuaded, πεπεῖσθαι: Luke XX, 6.

**TRIGGVA**, feminine, covenant, testament, διαθήκη: Luke I, 72; Rom. IX, 4; XI, 27; I Cor. XI, 25; II Cor. III, 6, 14; Gal. IV, 24.

**TRIGO** (Old Norse *tregi, tregr*, Old High German *tragi*, Old Saxon *tregan*, Old Swedish *träga*, Modern High German *träg*; Gr. II, 53; Gf. V, 502), feminine, grief, λύπη: II Cor. IX, 7.

**TRIMPAN** (Old Norse *trampa, trappa*, English *trip, trample*, Swedish *trippa*, Danish *trampe*, Dutch *trampen*, Modern High German *trampeln, trippeln*; compare Greek τρέω, Latin *tremere*; Gr. II, 33), class I verb, *tramp, trumpun, trumpans*, to go, rush.

**ANA-TRIMPAN**, to rush upon, press upon, ἐπικεῖσθαι: Luke V, 1.

**TRIU** (Old Norse, Old Frisian *tre*, Anglo-Saxon *treov*, Old Saxon *treo*, English *tree*, Swedish *trä*, Danish *trae*, Dutch *tere*; Greek δρῦς; Gr. III, 368; Rchth. 1093), neuter, genitive *trivis*, wood, tree, ξύλον: Mark XIV, 43, 48.

**VEINA-TRIU**, vine, ἄμπελος: John XV, 1, 4; plural, vineyard, ἀμπελών: I Cor. IX, 7.

**TRIVEINS**, adjective, wooden, ξύλινος: II Tim. II, 20.

**TRISGAN** (Gr. I, 43 [3rd edition]), class I verb, *trasg, trusgun, trusgans*, to sow.

**ÏN-TRISGAN**, to graft in, ἐγκεντρίζειν: Rom. XI, 24.

**TRUSGJAN**, class II verb, to sow.

**ÏN-TRUSGJAN**, to graft in, ἐγκεντρίζειν: Rom. XI, 17, 19, 23.

**TRUDAN** (Old Norse *troda, tradka*, Anglo-Saxon, Old Saxon *tredan*, Old Frisian *treda*, Old High German *tretan*, English *tread*, Swedish *träda*, Danish *traede*, Dutch *treden*, [Col. 1468] Modern High German *treten*; Latin *trudere*; Gr. II, 25; Gf. V, 520; Rchth. 1093), class II verb (?), to tread, πατεῖν: Luke X, 19; to gather grapes, τρυγᾶν: Luke VI, 44.

**GA-TRUDON**, class II verb, to tread down, καταπατεῖν: Luke VIII, 5; see this passage.

**TRUSNJAN** (compare Old Norse *trosna*?), class II verb.

**UFAR-TRUSNJAN**, to leap over: Skeir. III, c.

**TVAI** (Old Norse *tvo*, Anglo-Saxon *tva*, Old Saxon *tüe, tua*, Old Frisian *twa*, Old High German *zuei*, English *two*, Swedish *två*, Danish *to*, Dutch *twee*, Modern High German *zwei*; Latin *duo*, Greek δύω; Gr. I, 761; Gf. V, 715; Rchth. 1095), numeral; feminine *tvos*, neuter *tva*, genitive *tvaddje*, two, δύω: Matt. VI, 24; XXVII, 51; Mark V, 13; VI, 9; Luke VII, 19, 41; IX, 13, 16, 30, 32; X, 1; XV, 11; XVI, 13; XVII, 34; XVIII, 10; XIX, 29; John VIII, 17; I Cor. XIV, 27; II Cor. XIII, 1; Gal. IV, 22, 24; Eph. II, 15; Phil. I, 23; I Tim. V, 19; Skeir. II, d; III, d; V, c.

**TVEIHNAI**, distributive, two by two, ἀνὰ δύο: Luke IX, 3; compare Mark VII, 31, *miþ tveihnaim markom*, “through the midst of the borders,” ἀνὰ μέσον τῶν ὁρίων.

**TVALIF** (*tvalib*, Luke II, 42; VIII, 1; Old Norse, Swedish *tolf*, Anglo-Saxon *tvelf*, Old Saxon *twelif*, Old High German *zwelif*, English *twelve*, Danish *tolv*, Dutch *twaalf*, Modern High German *zwölf*; Gr. I, 763; Gf. V, 720; Rchth. 1097), twelve, δώδεκα: Matt. X, 1; XI, 1; Mark III, 14; IV, 10; V, 42; VI, 7; VIII, 19; IX, 35; XIV, 10, 43; Luke II, 42; VIII, 1, 42, 43; IX, 1, 12, 17; John VI, 67, 71.

**TVAI-TIGJUS**, masculine plural, twenty, εἴκοσι: Luke XIV, 31.

**TVA-HUNDA**, neuter plural, two hundred, διακόσια: John VI, 7.

**TVIS**, adverb, only in *tvis-standan*, see *Standan*.

**TUZ** (Old Norse *tor*, Old High German *zur*; Gf. V, 698), adverb, only in *tuz-verjan*, see under *Verjan*.

**TVEIFLS** (Old Norse *tuifli, tuiflian*, Old Frisian *twifil*, Old High German *zwifal*, Modern High German *Zweifel*; compare *Tvai*; Gf. V, 724; Rchth. 1096), masculine, doubt: Skeir. II, c.

**TVEIFLJAN**, class II verb, to raise doubt, doubt: Skeir. VI, b.

**TVEIFLEINS**, feminine, doubt, distinction, διάκρισις: Rom. XIV, 1; reasoning, dispute, διαλογισμός: I Tim. II, 8.

**TYKEIKUS** (*Tykekus*, Col. IV, 7; *Tukeikus*, Eph. VI, 21), masculine proper name, Τυχικός, Tychicus: Eph. VI, 21; Col. IV, 7, see the note on this passage; II Tim. IV, 12.

**TYRA**, feminine proper name, Τύρος, Tyre: Mark III, 8; Luke X, 14.

**TYRUS**, masculine proper name, Tyre: Matt. XI, 21, 22; Mark VII, 24, 31.

**TOBEIAS**, masculine proper name, Τωβίας, Tobiah: Neh. VI, 17.

**TOJIS**, see under *Tivan*.

[Col. 1467] V
[Col. 1467] **VAGGARI** (Anglo-Saxon *vangere*; compare Old Norse *vangi*, Old Saxon, Old High German *wanga*, Modern High German *Wange*; Gr. III, 401; Gf. I, 894), neuter, pillow, προσκεφάλαιον: Mark IV.38.

**VAGGS** (Old Norse *vangr*, Old Saxon *wang*, Anglo-Saxon *vang*, English *wang*, Danish *vaenge*; Gr. III, 395; DM. 475; Gf. I, 894), masculine (?), paradise, παράδεισος: 2 Cor. XII.4.

**VAGJAN**, see under *Vigan*.

* **VADDJUS** (Anglo-Saxon *vag*, Swedish *vägg*, Danish *vaeg*; Gr. III, 429), feminine, wall.

**BAURGS-VADDJUS**, city walls, rampart, τεῖχος: 2 Cor. XI.33; Neh. V.16; VI.15; VII.1.

**MIþGARDA-VADDJUS**, middle wall, partition-wall, μεσότοιχον: Eph. II.14.

**GRUNDU-VADDJUS**, foundation, θεμέλιον: Luke VI.48, 49; XIV.29; Eph. II.20; θεμέλιος: 2 Tim. II.19.

[Col. 1468] **VADI**, see under *Vidan*.

* **VAHS** (Old Norse *veikr*, Old Saxon *wah*, Anglo-Saxon *vac*, English *weak*, Danish *vaeg*, Swedish *vek*, Dutch *week*, Modern High German *weich*; compare *schwach*), adjective, weak, needy.

**UN-VAHS**, blameless, ἄμεμπτος: Luke I.6.

**VAHSJAN** (Old Norse *vaxa*, Old Saxon *wahsan*, Anglo-Saxon *veaxan*, Old High German *wahsan*, Old Frisian *vaxa*, English *wax*, Swedish *vexa*, Danish *voxe*, Dutch *wassen*, Modern High German *wachsen*; Bopp 116; Gr. II, 12; Gf. I, 682; Rchth. 1028), conjugation I, *vohs, vohsun, vahsans*, to grow, αὐξάνειν: Matt. VI.28; Luke I.80; II.40; John III.30; 2 Cor. X.15; Eph. II.21; IV.15; Col. II.19. *vahsjan gataujan*, to cause to grow, to multiply, αὐξάνειν: 2 Cor. IX.10.

**US-VAHSJAN**, to come to maturity; *usvahsans visan*, to be adult, ἡλικίαν ἔχειν, John IX.21.

[Col. 1469] **UFAR-VAHSJAN**, to increase exceedingly, ὑπεραυξάνειν: 2 Thess. I.3.

**US-VAHSTS**, feminine, increase, αὔξησις: Eph. IV.16.

**VAHSTUS**, masculine: 1. increase, αὔξησις: Col. II.19; 2. stature, age, ἡλικία: Matt. VI.27; Luke II.52; XIX.3; Eph. IV.13.

**VAHTVO**, see under *Vakan*.

**VAI** (Old Saxon *we*, Anglo-Saxon *vea*, Old High German *we*, Old Frisian *wach*, English *woe*, Swedish *ve*, Danish *vae*, Dutch *wee*, Modern High German *wehe*; Latin *vae*, Greek οὐαί; Gr. III, 292, 607; Gf. I, 632; Rchth. 1121), interjection, woe, οὐαί: Matt. XI.21; Mark XIII.17; Luke VI.24, 26; X.13.

**VAI-DEDJA**, see under *Deds*.

**VAI-FAIRWJAN**, see under *Fairwus*.

**VAJA-MERJAN**, see under *Merjan*.

**VAIAN** (Old High German *waian*, Old Frisian *waia*, Danish *vaee*, Modern High German *wehen*; Greek ἄημι; Gf. I, 621; Rchth. 1122), conjugation I, *vaivo, vaivoun, vaians*, to blow, πνεῖν: Matt. VII.25, 27; John VI.18.

**VAIBJAN**, see under *Veiban*.

**VAIHJO**, see under *Veihan*.

**VAIHSTA** (Gr. III, 429), masculine, corner, γωνία: Matt. VI.5; Mark XII.10; Luke XX.17.

**VAIHSTA-STAINS**, see under *Stains*.

**VAIHTS** (Old Norse *vaett*, Anglo-Saxon *viht, vuht*, Old Saxon, Old High German *wiht*, English *wight, ought*, Modern High German *Wicht, nicht, etwas*; DRA. 491; DM. 246; Gf. I, 730), feminine (also nominative neuter *vaïht*, Matt. X.26; XXVII.19; Tit. I.15; in the plural, as an anomalous form, Skeir. II.d), thing, matter, πράγμα: Luke I.1; appearance, kind, εἶδος: 1 Thess. V.22; Skeir. II.d; VII.b, c. *ïn þizozei vaihtais*, on this account, τούτου χάριν: Eph. III.1; Tit. I.5; δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν, “for which reason”: 2 Tim. I.6. Regularly with negation, *ni vaiht* or *vaïht ni*, “not at all,” “nothing,” οὐδέν, μηδέν: Matt. X.26; XXVII.12, 19; Mark I.43; V.26; VI.8; VII.12, 15; IX.29; XI.13; XIV.60, 61; XV.4; Luke III.13; IV.2, 35; IX.3, 36; X.19; XVIII.34; XX.40; John VI.63; VIII.28, 54; XIV.30; XVI.23; XVIII.20; Rom. VIII.1; XIII.8; XIV.14; 1 Cor. IV.4; VII.19; X.20, 25, 27; XIII.2, 3; 2 Cor. VI.3, 10; VII.5, 9; XI.5; XII.11; XIII.7; Gal. II.6; IV.1, 12; V.10; VI.3, 14; Eph. III.1; Phil. I.20, 28; II.3; IV.6; 2 Thess. III.11; 1 Tim. IV.4; V.21; VI.4, 7; Tit. I.15; Philem. 14; μή τι, “anything at all”: John VI.12; Gal. V.6; VI.15; οὐ, “not”: Rom. IX.1; 2 Cor. XII.5.

**VAILA** (Old Norse and Anglo-Saxon *vel*, Old Saxon *wala, wel*, Old High German *wela, wola*, Old Frisian *wel*, English *well*, Swedish *väl*, Danish *vel*, Dutch *wel*, Modern High German *wohl*; Gr. III, 603; Gf. I, 831; Rchth. 1132), adverb, well, καλῶς: Mark I.11; VII.6, 9, 37; XII.28, 32; Luke VI.26, 27; XV.23; XVI.19; XX.39; John VIII.48; XIII.13; XVIII.23; Rom. XI.20; 2 Cor. XI.4; Gal. IV.17; V.7; 1 Tim. III.4, 12, 13; εὖ: Luke XIX.17; Skeir. VI.a; βέλτιον, “better”: 2 Tim. I.18, in this passage; πάντως, “in every way”: 1 Cor. IX.22, in this passage. *vaila þau*, “even if,” κἄν: 2 Cor. XI.16; see the note on this passage. *vaila qiþan*, see under *Qiþan*; *vaila hugjan*, under *Hugs*; *vaila galeikaiþs*, under *Leikan*; *vaila andanems*, under *Niman*; *vaila taujan*, under *Tivan*; *vaila visan*, under *Visan*; *vaila fraþjan*, under *Fraþjan*.

**VAILA-MERJAN**, see under *Merjan*.

**VAILA-QISS**, see under *Qiþan*.

**VAILA-VIZNS**, see under *Vizan*.

**VAINAHS** (Old High German *wenag*; Gf. I, 889), adjective, unhappy, wretched, ταλαίπωρος: Rom. VII.24; see the note on this passage.

**VAINEI**, adverb, would that, ὄφελον: 1 Cor. IV.8; 2 Cor. XI.1; Gal. V.12.

**VAIPS**, see under *Veipan*.

**VAIR** (Old Norse and Anglo-Saxon *ver*, Old Saxon *wer*, Old High German *wir, wer*, Old Frisian *wer*; Latin *vir*; Gr. II, 56; III, 319; DRA. 418; Gf. I, 931; Rchth. 1136), masculine, man, husband, ἀνήρ: Matt. VII.24; Mark VI.20; Luke VII.20; VIII.27, 38, 41; IX.30, 32; John VI.10; Rom. VII.3; 1 Cor. XIII.11; 2 Cor. XI.2; Eph. IV.13; V.[Col. 1470]23, 25, 28; Col. III.18, 19; 1 Tim. II.8, 12; 2 Esdr. II.25, 26, 27, 28; Neh. VII.2. *uf vaira qens*, “a woman under a husband,” ὕπανδρος γυνή: Rom. VII.2.

**VAIRA-LEIKO**, see under *Leiks*.

**VAIRDUS** (Old High German *wirt*, Old Frisian *werda*, Swedish *värd*, Danish *vaerd*, Modern High German *Wirt*; Gf. I, 932; Rchth. 1137), masculine, host, stranger, ξένος: Rom. XVI.23.

**VAIRþAN** (Old Norse *verda*, Anglo-Saxon *veorðan*, Old Saxon *werthan*, Old High German *werdan*, Old Frisian *wertha*, Swedish *varda*, Danish *vorde*, Dutch and Modern High German *werden*; compare Greek ἕρδειν; Gr. II, 39; Gf. I, 982; Rchth. 1143), conjugation I, *varþ, vaurþun, vaurþans*, to become, to be, γίγνεσθαι, ἔσεσθαι.

1. As an independent verb: to come to be, be born, be accomplished, be manifested, appear, happen, occur: Matt. V.18; VI.10 (*vilja*, “will”); VIII.12 (*grets jah krusts tunþive*, “weeping and gnashing of teeth”), 16 (*andanahti*, “evening”); XI.20 (*mahts*, “mighty works”), 21, 23; XXVI.2 (*paska*, “Passover”); XXVII.1 (*maurgins*, “morning”), 45 (*riqis*, “darkness”), 57 (*seiþu*, “late”); Mark IV.11, 35; V.14, 33; VI.2 (*sabbato*, “Sabbath”); IX.7 (*milhma*, “cloud”), 21; XI.19, 23, 24; XII.11 (*fram fraujin varþ sa*, “this came from the Lord”), 23 (*qens ïmma*, “his wife”); XIII.18 (*þlauhs*, “tribulation”), 19 (*aglo*, “anguish”), 29; XIV.4; XV.33 (*weila saihsto*, “the sixth hour”), 42; Luke I.14 (*faheds*, “joy”), 20, 33 (*andeis*, “end”), 44 (*stibna ïn ausam*, “a sound in the ears”), 45 (*ustauhts*, “fulfilment”), 65 (*agis ana allaim*, “fear upon all”); II.10, 13 (*miþ ïmma managei harjis*, “with him a multitude of the host”), 15, 42 (*tvalib vintruns*, “twelve years old”); III.2 (*vaurd guþs at ïohannen*, “the word of God came to John”), 22 (*stibna us himina*, “a voice from heaven”), 23, 25 (*huhrus and alla airþa*, “a famine over all the land”); IV.42 (*dags*, “day”); VI.13, 48 (*garunjo*, “completion”); VIII.34; IX.7; XV.7, 10, 14, 17, 24, 34 (*tvai ana ligra samin*, “two together in one bed”); John VI.21 (*skip ana airþai*, “the ship at land”); VII.43 (*missaqiss ïn managein*, “division in the crowd”); VIII.58; X.19, 22 (*ïnniujiþa*, “the feast of dedication”); X.35 (*vaurd guþs du ïm*, “the word of God to them”); XII.29 (*þeiwo*, “thunder”), 30; XIV.22; XV.7; Rom. VII.3, 4; IX.9 (*sunus ïzai*, “a son to her”); XI.11 (*ganists*, “salvation”), 25 (*daubei ïmma*, “blindness to him”); XV.22 (*vaurts*, “guilt”); 1 Cor. IV.5; XV.54; XVI.2 (*gabaur*, “a burden”); 2 Cor. XI.15; XIII.11; Gal. IV.4 (*us qinon*, “from a woman”); 1 Tim. VI.4 (*us vaurdajiukom neiþa*, “from word-struggles, envy”); 2 Tim. II.18 (*usstass*, “resurrection”); Skeir. II.a; III.c (*sokeins*, “investigation”); VI.c; VII.c (*vaninassus*, “want”).

Impersonally, especially in the formula *varþ*, “it came to pass,” followed by an accusative with infinitive or by *jah* (“and”), or also by a subordinate clause attached without a conjunction: Matt. VII.28; IX.10, 29 (*bi galaubeinai ïggqarai*, “according to your faith”); Mark I.9; II.15; IV.4; V.16 (*waiva varþ bi ïna*, “what had happened to her”); Luke I.8, 23, 38 (*bi vaurda þeinamma*, “according to your word”), 41, 59; II.1, 6, 15, 46; III.21; IV.36; V.1, 12, 17; VI.1, 6, 12; VII.11; XIV.22 (*varþ sve anabaust*, “it happened as he had commanded”); XVII.11, 26, 28, 30; John XIII.19; XIV.29; Rom. IX.26; 1 Thess. III.4; Neh. VII.1. To this group also belong 2 Cor. VII.7, *svaei mis mais faginon varþ*, “so that I rejoiced the more,” and Luke VIII.5, provided that the reading of the text is sound.

2. As a copulative verb:

a. With a substantive as predicate: Matt. V.22, 45; Mark I.17; Luke IV.3; VI.35; John IX.27; X.16; XII.36; Rom. VII.13; XV.8; 1 Cor. IV.9; VII.23; IX.23; XI.27; XIII.11; XV.20; 2 Cor. VI.16; Eph. III.7; V.7; Phil. III.17, 19; Col. I.23, 25; 1 Tim. IV.6; 2 Tim. II.21; Skeir. I.d; III.c. Likewise in periphrastic renderings of Greek verbs, e.g. *arbja vairþan*, “become an heir”; *vairþan usgrudja*, “become uprooted”; *alaþarba vairþan*, “become needy”; *ïnkilþo vairþan*, “become guilty”; *galaista vairþan*, “become a debtor”; *usvena vairþan*, “become accustomed”; *usfilma vairþan*, “be fulfilled,” etc.

b. With an adjective: Matt. V.21; VI.16; IX.16; XI.22; Mark II.21; IV.19, 22, 32; VI.14, 21, 26; X.31, 43, 44; XIII.28; Luke I.15, 32; II.2; VI.35, 49; IX.48; XIV.14; XVI.11, 12; John VIII.33; IX.39; Rom. XI.17 (end); XII.16; 1 Cor. VII.21; XIV.25; XV.10; Eph. IV.32; V.17; 2 Tim. III.2; Skeir. I.c. And frequently in periphrastic renderings of verbs: *airzis vairþan*, “become astray”; *bairhts vairþan*, “become manifest”; *bauþs vairþan*, “become commanded”; *unbruks vairþan*, “become useful”; *gabigs vairþan*, “become rich”; *gredags vairþan*, “become hungry”; *hails vairþan*, “become whole”; *hrains vairþan*, “become clean”; *svikunþs vairþan*, “become evident”; *galeiks vairþan*, “become like”; *laus vairþan*, “become free”; *managizo vairþan*, “become more numerous”; *modags vairþan*, “become courageous”; *naqaþs vairþan*, “become naked”; *garaihts vairþan*, “become righteous”; *riurs vairþan*, “become empty”; *saþs vairþan*, “become full”; *faurhts vairþan*, “become afraid”; *fulls vairþan*, “become filled,” etc.

c. With a possessive pronoun: Mark XII.7; Luke IV.7.

d. With a participle: Mark IX.3, 50; XIII.25; Luke VI.16, 36 (VIII.5); XIV.12; XVII.35; John VI.45; Gal. IV.16; V.26; Eph. V.1; Phil. II.8; Col. III.15; 1 Thess. II.14; 2 Tim. III.2. In periphrastic verbs, e.g. *drugkans vairþan*, see under *Drigkan*; *anatiþs vairþan*, see under *Lats*.

e. With an adverb: Mark IV.10; 2 Cor. I.19; Eph. II.13.

f. With a preposition, especially *du*: Mark XII.10; Luke III.5; 1 Cor. I.26; 2 Cor. VI.18; *ïn*: Phil. II.7. Likewise in periphrastic Greek expressions: *ïn unlustau vairþan*, see under *Lustus*; *ïn siunai vairþan*, see under *Siuns*.

g. With relative (*sve*, “as”) or interrogative (*wa*, “what”) periphrases: Mark IX.26; Luke I.66; VI.40; Gal. IV.12.

3. As an auxiliary verb:

a. In the present for the future, e.g. John XVI.20, *saurgandans vairþiþ*, “you will be sorrowful” (λυπηθήσεσθε); Phil. I.20, *gaaiviskoþs vairþa*, “I shall be put to shame” (αἰσχυνθήσομαι); Skeir. I.a, *ustauhana habaida vairþan*, “will have been raised.”

b. In the past, regularly for the passive aorist: Matt. VIII.3, 24; IX.25, 33; XXVII.3, 8; Mark I.14, 22; II.27; VI.3; VII.27; IX.4, 12; XVI.11; Luke VI.18; VII.35; VIII.5, 20; IX.22, 36; XV.24; XVI.1; XVII.14, 17, 18; John IX.2, 3, 19, 20, 34; XII.38; XIII.18, 31; XVI.21; XVII.12; Rom. VII.4, 6, 10, 13; X.20; XI.17, 24; XV.4; 1 Cor. I.13; VII.18; XV.54; 2 Cor. IV.1; VII.14; XII.4, 12; Eph. I.13; III.8; Phil. III.12; Col. I.16, 26; III.4; 2 Thess. II.3; 1 Tim. I.16; II.13, 14; III.16; IV.14; VI.10; Tit. I.13; Neh. VI.15; VII.1; Skeir. VIII.b. For the perfect: Mark III.26; John XVI.11; 2 Cor. VII.13; Gal. II.20.

**FRA-VAIRþAN**, to corrupt, be corrupted, καταφθείρεσθαι: 2 Tim. III.8.

**GA-VAIRþI** (Old High German *giwurt*; Gf. I, 993), neuter, peace, tranquillity, εἰρήνη: Matt. X.34; Mark V.34; Luke I.79; II.14, 29; VII.50; VIII.48; X.5, 6; XIV.32; XIX.38, 42; John XIV.27; XVI.33; Rom. VIII.6; X.15; XIV.17, 19; 1 Cor. VII.16; XVI.11; 2 Cor. I.2; XIII.11; Gal. I.3; V.22; VI.16; Eph. I.2; II.14, 15, 17; IV.3; VI.15, 22; Phil. IV.7, 9; Col. III.15; 1 Thess. V.3, 23; 2 Thess. I.2; III.16; 1 Tim. I.2; 2 Tim. I.2; II.22; Tit. I.4. *gavairþi haban*, to have peace, εἰρηνεύειν: Rom. XII.18; 1 Thess. V.13. *gavairþi taujan*, to maintain peace, εἰρηνοποιεῖν: Col. I.20. *gavairþi taujands visan*, to be at peace, εἰρηνεύειν: Col. II, XIII.11.

**GA-VAIRþEIGS**, adjective, peaceable; *gavairþeigs visan*, to be at peace, εἰρηνεύειν: Mark IX.50.

**GAGA-VAIRþJAN**, conjugation II, to reconcile, καταλλάττειν: 1 Cor. VII.11.

**GAGA-VAIRþNAN**, conjugation III, to be reconciled, καταλλάττεσθαι: 2 Cor. V.20.

* **VAIRþS** (Old Saxon *ward*, Anglo-Saxon *veard*, Old High German *wart, wert*, Old Frisian *ward*, English *wards*, Dutch *waarts*, Modern High German *wärts*; Latin *vertere, versus*; Gr. II, 39; Gf. I, 998; Rchth. 1155), adjective, turned, directed.

**ANA-VAIRþS**, future, coming, ἐρχόμενος: Mark X.30; John XVI.13; μέλλων, “about to be”: Luke III.7; Rom. VIII.38; Eph. I.21; Col. II.17; 1 Tim. I.16; IV.8; Skeir. II.c; V.a. *anavairþ ïst mis*, “I am about to,” μέλλω: 1 Thess. III.4.

**AND-VAIRþS**, present, παρών: 1 Cor. V.3; 2 Cor. X.2, 11; XIII.2, 10; ἐνεστώς, “present”: Rom. VIII.38; 1 Cor. VII.26; Gal. I.4, see the note on this passage; ὁ παραυτίκα, “the momentary”: 2 Cor. IV.17. *andvairþs visan*, to be present, παρεῖναι: Gal. IV.18.

**AND-VAIRþIS**, adverb, opposite, with the dative, ἀπέναντι: Matt. XXVII.61.

**JAIND-VAIRþS**, adverb, there, ἐκεῖ: John XVIII.3.

**VIþRA VAIRþS**, adjective, opposite, ὁ κατέναντι: Mark XI.2; Luke XIX.30; ἀντιπέραν, “on the opposite side”: Luke VIII.26. *þata viþravairþo*, on the contrary, τοὐναντίον: Gal. II.7.

**FRAM-VAIRþIS**, adverb, far, further, beyond; *framvairþis visan*, to continue, remain further, μένειν: 2 Tim. III.14.

**SVULTA-VAIRþJA**, adjective, tending toward death, on the point of dying, μέλλων τελευτᾶν: Luke VII.2; see also the note on this passage.

**AND-VAIRþI**, neuter:

1. Presence; in the expression *ïn andvairþja*, in the sight of, before, ἔμπροσθεν: Matt. V.16, 24; VI.1; X.32, 33; Mark IX.2; Luke X.21; John XII.37; 1 Thess. II.19; Neh. VI.19; ἐνώπιον: Luke I.6, 15, 17, 19, 75; IV.7; V.18, 25; VIII.47; XV.10, 18, 21; XVI.15; Rom. XII.17; 2 Cor. IV.12; VII.12; VIII.21; Gal. I.20; 1 Tim. II.3; V.4, 20, [Col. 1472]21; VI.12, 13; 2 Tim. II.14; IV.1; κατενώπιον: 2 Cor. II.17; XII.19 (? κατέναντι, “opposite”): Eph. I.4; ἐν προσώπῳ, “in the presence of”: 2 Cor. II.10; IV.6; V.12; εἰς πρόσωπον, “face to face”: 2 Cor. VIII.24; κατὰ πρόσωπον, “before the face”: Luke II.31; ἐξ ἐναντίας, “opposite”: Mark XV.39; ἔναντι, “before”: Luke I.8; ἐναντίον, “in the presence of”: Luke XX.26. *ïn managamma andvairþja*, before many persons, ἐκ πολλῶν προσώπων: 2 Cor. I.11. *faura andvairþja*, before, ἐναντίον: Mark II.12; ἀπὸ προσώπου, “from before”: Neh. V.15; πρὸ προσώπου, “before”: Luke VII.27; X.1.

2. Face, πρόσωπον: Matt. VI.16; Mark XII.14; XIV.65; Luke I.76; V.12; VII.27; IX.29, 51, 53; X.1; XX.21; 1 Cor. XIII.12; 2 Cor. III.18; V.12; X.7; Gal. II.6, 11; 1 Thess. II.17; III.10.

3. Person: Skeir. V.a, c.

**VAIRþS** (Old Norse *verd*, Anglo-Saxon *veorð*, Old Saxon *werth*, Old High German *werd*, Old Frisian *werth*, English *worth*, Swedish *värd*, Danish *voerd*, Dutch *weerd*, Modern High German *werth, Würde*; Gr. II, 39; Gf. I, 1011; Rchth. 1143), masculine, price; Neapolitan document. *vairþs galaubs*, a great price, τιμή: 1 Cor. VII.23.

**VAIRþS**, adjective, worthy, sufficient, ἱκανός: Matt. III.11; VIII.8; Mark I.7; Luke III.16; VII.6; 1 Cor. XV.9; 2 Cor. II.16; III.5; 2 Tim. II.2; ἄξιος: Matt. X.37, 38; Luke III.8; VII.4; X.7; XV.19, 21; 1 Cor. XVI.4; 2 Thess. I.3; 1 Tim. I.15; IV.9; V.18; VI.1. *vairþs visan*, to be counted worthy, καταξιωθῆναι: Luke XX.35. *vairþana briggan*, to make worthy, sufficient, ἱκανοῦν: 2 Cor. III.6; ἀξιοῦν: 2 Thess. I.11; καταξιοῦν: 2 Thess. I.5. *vairþana rahnjan*, see under *Rahnjan*.

**VAIRþABA**, adverb, worthily, ἀξίως: Eph. IV.1; Phil. I.27; Col. I.10; 1 Thess. II.12.

**UN-VAIRþABA**, unworthily, ἀναξίως: 1 Cor. XI.27, 29.

**VAIRþIDA**, feminine, worthiness, sufficiency, ἱκανότης: 2 Cor. III.5; Skeir. V.d; VII.a.

**AND-VAIRþI**, neuter, price, τιμή: Matt. XXVII.6, 9.

**VAIRþON**, conjugation II, to value, τιμᾶν: Matt. XXVII.9.

**VAIRILO** (Old Norse *vör*, Anglo-Saxon *veler*, Old Frisian *were*; Gr. II, 56; III, 400; Rchth. 1138), feminine, lip, χεῖλος: Mark VII.6; 1 Cor. XIV.21.

**VAIRPAN** (Old Norse *verpa*, Old Saxon *werpan*, Anglo-Saxon *veorpan*, Old High German *werfan*, Old Frisian *werpa*, Dutch *werpen*, Modern High German *werfen*, Greek ῥίπτειν; Gr. II, 37; Gf. I, 1026; Rchth. 1142), conjugation I, *varp, vaurpun, vaurpans*:

1. To throw, βἀλλειν: Matt. V.29; Mark I.16; IV.26; VII.27; XI.23; XV.24; Luke IV.9; John VIII.59; Skeir. III.c; to let down, χαλᾶν: Luke V.5.

2. To throw stones, stone, λιθάζειν: John X.31. *stainam vairpan*, to stone, λιθοβολεῖν: Mark XII.4.

**AT-VAIRPAN**, to cast, βαλλειν: Mark IX.22, 47; ῥίπτειν: Matt. XXVII.5. Past participle *atvaurpans*, cast down, lying, βεβλημένος: Luke XVI.20.

**AF-VAIRPAN**, to cast away, ἀποβάλλειν: Mark X.50; to remove, αἴρειν: Eph. IV.31. *stainam afvairpan*, to stone, καταλιθάζειν: Luke XX.6; λιθάζειν: John XI.8.

**GA-VAIRPAN**, to cast, βἀλλειν: Mark IX.45; ῥίπτειν: Luke IV.35; to dash, ῥήσσειν: Mark IX.18.

**ÏNN-VAIRPAN**, to throw in, βαλλειν: John XII.6.

**US-VAIRPAN**:

1. To cast out, expel, ἐκβάλλειν: Matt. VIII.12, 16; Mark V.40; XI.15; XII.8; Luke XIX.45; XX.12, 15; John VI.37; IX.34, 35; XII.31; Gal. IV.30; to cast, βαλλειν: Luke XIV.35; John XV.6. *us synagogein usvaurpans*, expelled from the synagogues, ἀποσυνάγωγος: John XII.42.

2. To reject, ἐκβάλλειν: Luke VI.22; ἀποδοκιμάζειν: Mark XII.10.

3. To cast out unclean spirits, ἐκβάλλειν: Matt. VII.22; VIII.16, 31; Mark I.34, 39; III.15, 22, 23; VII.26; XVI.9.

4. To go out, ἐκβάλλειν: Mark IX.47; Luke VI.42.

5. To put away, ἀποτιθέναι: Rom. XIII.12.

6. To throw upon, ἐπιρρίπτειν: Luke XIX.35.

**FRA-VAIRPAN**: 1. to cast away, βαλλειν: Mark IX.42; 2. to scatter, ῥίπτειν: Matt. IX.36.

**US-IVAURPA**, feminine: 1. rejection, ἀποβολή: Rom. XI.15; 2. abjection, untimely birth, ἔκτρωμα: 1 Cor. XV.8; rejected thing, ἀπόβλητον: 1 Tim. IV.4.

**VAIRS** (Old Norse *verr*, Anglo-Saxon *vyrs*, Old Saxon, Old High German *wirs*, Old Frisian *werra*, English *worse*, Swedish *värr*, Danish *vaerre*, Modern High German *wïrsch*; Gr. [Col. 1473]III, 589; Gf. I, 1046; Rchth. 723), comparative adverb, worse, χεῖρον: Mark V.26.

**VAIRSIZA**, comparative adjective, worse, χείρων: Matt. IX.16; XXVII.64; 1 Tim. V.8; 2 Tim. III.13.

**VAITEI**, see under *Veitan*.

**VAKAN** (Old Norse *vaka, vekia*, Anglo-Saxon *vacian, veccan*, Old Saxon *wacon*, Old High German *wachen, wekjan*, Old Frisian *waka*, English *wake*, Swedish *vaken, väkka*, Danish *vaage, vaekke*, Dutch *waken, wäcken*, Modern High German *wachen, wecken*; Gr. II, 11; Gf. I, 672; Rchth. 1122), conjugation I, *vok, vokun, vakans*, to watch, γρηγορεῖν: 1 Cor. XVI.13; Col. IV.2; 1 Thess. V.6, 10; ἀγρυπνεῖν, “keep awake”: Eph. VI.18.

**DU-VAKAN**, the same, ἀγρυπνεῖν: Eph. VI.18, in this passage.

**þAIRH-VAKAN**, to keep watch through the night, ἀγραυλεῖν: Luke II.8. *naht þairhvakan*, to spend the night awake, διανυκτερεύειν: Luke VI.12.

* **VAKJAN**, conjugation II, “to cause to wake.”

**US-VAKJAN**, to wake, rouse from sleep, ἐξυπνίζειν: John XI.11.

**GA-VAKNAN**, conjugation III, to wake up, διαγρηγορεῖν: Luke IX.32.

**VAHTVO**, feminine, watch, φυλακή: Luke II.8.

**VOKAINS**, feminine, watchfulness, φυλακή: 2 Cor. VI.5; ἀγρυπνία: 2 Cor. XI.27.

**VALDAN** (Old Norse *valld*, Anglo-Saxon *vealdan*, Old Saxon *waldan*, Old High German *waltan*, Old Frisian *wald, walda*, Swedish *våld*, Danish *vold*, Dutch *welden*, Modern High German *walten, Gewalt*; Latin *valere*; Gr. II, 58; Gf. I, 805; Rchth. 1122), conjugation II (?):

1. To govern. *garda valdan*, to rule, manage a household, οἰκοδεσποτεῖν: 1 Tim. V.14. *garda valdands*, participle used substantivally, master of a household, householder, οἰκοδεσπότης: Matt. X.25; Luke XIV.21.

2. To exercise authority, ἀρχεῖσθαι: Luke III.14; see the note on this passage and Prolegomena, compare p. 485.

**ALL-VALDANDS**, participle used substantivally, Almighty, παντοκράτωρ: 2 Cor. VI.18.

**GA-VALDAN**, to exercise lordship, κατεξουσιάζειν: Mark X.42.

**VALDUFNI**, neuter, power, dominion, authority, ἐξουσία: Matt. IX.4; XV.24; 2 Cor. X.8; XIII.10; Eph. I.21; II.2; III.10; VI.12; Col. I.13, 16; II.15; 2 Thess. III.9; Skeir. I.b, c; V.c; VII.a.

**GA-VALIS**, chosen, elect, ἐκλεκτός: Col. III.12.

**US-VALTJAN**, to overturn, turn over, subvert, καταστρέφειν: Mark XI.15; ἀνατρέπειν: 2 Tim. II.18; Tit. I.11.

**US-VALTEINS**, feminine, overthrow, subversion, καταστροφή: 2 Tim. II.14; rupture, ῥῆγμα: Luke VI.49.

**VALVJAN** (Anglo-Saxon *vealvian*, Old High German [Col. 1474]*wellan*, English *wallow*, Dutch *wallen, wellen*, Modern High German *wallen, Welle*; Latin *volvere*; Gf. I, 789), conjugation II, to roll.

**AF-VALVJAN**, to roll away, ἀποκυλίνδειν: Mark XVI.3, 4.

**VALVISON** (this reading of the Codex Argenteus is to be preferred to our conjecture *valvnoda*, from *valvnan*, which has been adopted in the text; for the ending *-ison, -izon* not only actually occurs in Gothic in *hatizon*, and *agison, riqizon,* and *sigison* may have existed, but was also very frequently used in Old High German; compare Gr. II, 271), conjugation II, to roll, κυλίεσθαι: Mark IX.20. See this passage.

**VAMMS**, see under *Vimman*.

**VANDJAN**, see under *Vindan*.

**VANDUS** (Old Norse *vöndr*, English *wand*, Danish *vaand*), masculine, rod; *vandum usbliggvan*, to beat with rods, ῥαβδίζειν: 2 Cor. XI.25.

**VANS** (Old Norse *van, vanr*, Anglo-Saxon *vana*, Old Saxon and Old High German *wan*, Old Frisian *wania*, English *want, wane*, Swedish and Danish *van* …, Modern High German *Wahn* …; Latin *vanus*; Gr. II, 55; Gf. I, 854; Rchth. 1158), adjective, lacking, deficient, λείπων: Tit. I.5. *van visan*, with the genitive: a. to lack, λείπειν: Luke XVIII.22; ὑστερεῖν: Mark X.21; b. to be deficient in, ἡττᾶσθαι: 2 Cor. XII.13. *vanana gataujan*, to invalidate, set aside, ἀθετεῖν: 1 Tim. V.12. *fidvortigjus ainamma vanai*, forty less one, τεσσαράκοντα παρὰ μίαν: 2 Cor. XI.24.

**VANINASSUS**, masculine, want, deficiency, ὑστέρημα: 1 Cor. XVI.17; 1 Thess. III.10; Skeir. VII.c.

* **VANAN**, conjugation II, to lack.

**VANAINS**, feminine, deficiency, loss, ἥττημα: Rom. XI.12.

**GA-VAURKI**, neuter: 1. work, business, πραγματεία: 2 Tim. II.4; 2. gain, κέρδος: Phil. I.21; III.7; gain, profit, πορισμός: 1 Tim. VI.6. *du gavaurkja haban*, to gain, κερδαίνειν: Phil. III.8.

**FAIHUGA-VAURKI**, gain, profit, πορισμός: 1 Tim. VI.5.

10; IV, 12; V, 11; Phil. I, 22; II, 30; III, 21; Col. I, 10, 21; III, 17; 1 Thess. V, 13; 2 Thess. I, 11; II, 17; 1 Tim. II, 10; III, 1; V, 10, 25; 2 Tim. I, 9; II, 21; III, 17; IV, 5, 14; Neh. V, 16; VI, 14; Skeir. VI, b; **ἐνέργεια**, activity, operation: Eph. I, 19; IV, 16; Col. I, 29; II, 12.

**VAILA-VIZNS**, feminine, wages, sustenance: Skeir. VII, b.

**GA-VIZNEIGS**, adjective, glad; **gavizneigs visan**, to rejoice together, συνήδεσθαι: Rom. VII, 22.

**VIþRA** (Anglo-Saxon *vider*, Old High German *widar*, Old Saxon *withar*, Old Frisian *with*, Modern High German *wider*; Gr. III, 260; Gf. I, 635; Alth. Präp. 192; Rchth. 1154).

I. A preposition governing the accusative, primarily expressing opposition.

1. Local: it means “before,” “in the sight of,” “before,” πρός with accusative: 1 Cor. XIII, 12, **andvairþi viþra andvairþi**, “face to face”; Mark IV, 1, **managei viþra marein ana staþa vas**, “a crowd was on land before the sea”; 15 **þai viþra vig**, “those by the way”; Luke VIII, 12; I, 73, **guþ aiþ svor viþra abrahama**, “God swore an oath before Abraham”; 2 Cor. V, 12, **viþra ainana wopan**, “to boast before another”; VII, 12, **gabairhtjan usdaudein viþra ïzvis**, “to make our diligence manifest before you” (where, in our translation, “before you” should be read in place of “toward you”); XII, 19, **sunjon sik viþra ïzvis**, “they defend themselves before you” (ὑμῖν, “to you”). Thus Matt. VIII, 34, **usïddja viþra ïesu**, is translated: “he went out to meet Jesus” (ἐξῆλθεν εἰς συνάντησιν τῷ Ἰησοῦ).

2. It is used metaphorically:

a. In a favorable sense: “for, toward,” πρός with accusative: 1 Thess. V, 14, **usbeisneigs visan viþra allans**, “to be patient toward all”; 2 Tim. II, 24, **qairrus visan viþra allans**, “to be gentle toward all”; Gal. VI, 10, **vaurkjan þiuþ viþra allans**, “to do good toward all”; Eph. VI, 9, **þiuþ taujaiþ viþra ïns**, “do the same toward them”; 1 Thess. V, 5, **þiuþ laistjaiþ viþra allans**, “pursue what is good toward all.”

b. In an unfavorable sense: “against,” “in opposition to,” πρός with accusative: Col. III, 19, **baitrs visan viþra ainana**, “to be bitter against one another”; 1 Cor. VI, 1, **viþra anþarana staua haban**, “to have a case against another”; Col. III, 13, **haban fairina**, “to have a complaint”; Eph. VI, 11, **standan**, “to stand”; Luke XIV, 31, **stigqan viþra anþarana**, “to advance against another” (συμβάλλειν ἑτέρῳ); Eph. VI, 12, **brakja viþra bloþ**, “to struggle against flesh [and blood]”; Mark X, 5, **viþra harduhairtein gameljan anabusn**, “because of hardness of heart he wrote [this] commandment.”

It represents κατά with the genitive: **viþra ïzvis ïst**, “is against you”: Luke IX, 50; 2 Cor. X, 5, **ushafjan sik**, “exalting itself [against]”; XIII, 8, **magan wa**, “to be able [against]”; Mark XI, 25, **wa haban**, “to have something against [someone]”; Matt. X, 35, **skaidan mannan viþra attan**, “to divide a man against his father”; Gal. V, 17, **leik gairneiþ viþra ahman**, “the flesh desires against the Spirit”; [V,] 23, **viþra þo svaleika nist vitoþ**, “against such things there is no law.”

It represents ἐπί with the accusative: Mark III, 24, 25, **þiudangardi viþra sik gadailjada**, “a kingdom divided against itself.”

It represents εἰς: 1 Cor. VIII, 12, **fravaurkjan viþra broþruns**, “to sin against brothers.”

It represents παρά with the accusative: Skeir. I, c, **þata ïst viþra þata gadob**, “this is contrary to that which is fitting.”

Hence also **andhafjan viþra**, to deny or oppose, so that another’s statement is contested, or at least declared false; πρός with accusative: Luke IV, 4, **andhof ïesus viþra ïns**, “Jesus answered them”; VI, 3; Skeir. VIII, b; Matt. XXVII, 14, **andhof vïþra ni ainhun vaurde**, “he answered him not a single word.” Hence 1 Cor. IX, 3: **meina andahafts viþva þans mik ussokjandans þat-ïst**, “this is my defense before those who examine me.”

II. In composition it occurs only in **viþragaggan**, **viþragamotjan**, and **viþravairþs**.

**VIþRUS** (Old Norse *vedr*, Old Saxon *withar*, Anglo-Saxon *veðer*, Old High German *widar*, English *wether*, Modern High German *Widder*; Gr. III, 326; Gf. I, 779), masculine, lamb, ἀμνός: John I, 29.

**VIþON** (compare English *waddle*, Modern High German *wedeln*), class-II verb, to move, κινεῖν: Mark XV, 29.

**VIKO** (Old Norse *vika*, Anglo-Saxon *vica, veoc*, Old Saxon *wïca*, Old High German *wecha*, Old Frisian *wice*, English and Dutch *week*, Swedish *vecka*, Danish *uge*, Modern High German *Woche*; Gf. I, 701; Rchth. 1149), feminine, week.

[Col. 1483] Luke I, 8 (the Goth translates the Greek ἐν τῇ τάξει τῆς ἐφημερίας αὐτοῦ, “in the order of his division,” by **hebdomade ejus classis**, “in the week of his division”; that is, when the division of priests to which he belonged was performing its ministry; compare de Wette on Luke I, 5. Hence “in a week” or “during a week” should be read in the translation in place of “in turn,” and *viko* in Gr. II, 16 must be distinguished from our root).

**VILþEIS** (Old Norse *villr*, Anglo-Saxon, Swedish, Danish *vild*, Old High German *wildi*, Old Frisian *wilde*, Dutch and Modern High German *wild*; Gr. II, 58; Gf. I, 803; Rchth. 1149), adjective, wild, ἄγριος: Mark I, 6, at this passage; **vilþeis alevabagms**, wild olive tree, ἀγριέλαιος: Rom. XI, 17, 24.

**VILJAN** (Old Norse *vilia*, Anglo-Saxon *villa, vilnian*, Old High German *wellan*, Old Saxon *willian*, Old Frisian *wella, willa*, English *will*, Swedish *vilja*, Danish *ville*, Modern High German *Wille, wollen*; Greek βούλεσθαι, Latin *velle*, “to will”; Gr. II, 28; Gf. I, 815; Rchth. 1150), irregular verb, present subjunctive *viljau*, preterite *vilda*, to will, θέλειν: Matt. V, 40, 42; VIII, 2, 3; IX, 13; XI, 14; XXVII, 15, 17, 43; Mark I, 40; III, 14; VI, 19, 22, 25, 26; VII, 24; VIII, 34; IX, 30, 35; X, 35, 36, 43, 44, 51; XIV, 7; XV, 9; Luke I, 62; IV, 6; V, 12, 39; VI, 31; IX, 23, 24; XIV, 28; XV, 28; XVIII, 4, 13, 41; XIX, 14, 27; XX, 46; John V, 21, 35; VI, 11, 21, 67; VII, 1, 17, 44; VIII, 44; IX, 27; XII, 21; XV, 7; Rom. IX, 22; 2 Cor. XI, 12; XII, 20; Gal. I, 7; Col. I, 27; II, 18; 1 Thess. II, 18; 2 Thess. III, 10; 1 Tim. I, 7; II, 4; to wish, βούλεσθαι: Mark XV, 15; Luke X, 22; John XVIII, 39; 1 Cor. XII, 11; 2 Cor. I, 15; 1 Tim. II, 8; V, 14; to be well pleased, εὐδοκεῖν: Mark I, 11, at this passage; to prosper, εὐοδοῦσθαι: 1 Cor. XVI, 2; **silba viljands**, voluntarily, of one’s own accord, αὐθαίρετος: 2 Cor. VIII, 17.

**VILJA**, masculine: 1) will, θέλημα: Matt. VI, 10; VII, 21; X, 29; Mark III, 35; John VI, 38, 40; VII, 17; IX, 31; Rom. XII, 2; 1 Cor. XVI, 12; 2 Cor. I, 1; VIII, 5; Gal. I, 4; Eph. I, 1, 5, 11; II, 3; V, 17; Col. I, 9; IV, 12; 1 Thess. IV, 3; V, 18; Skeir. I, c; V, b, c; purpose, βούλημα: Rom. IX, 19; purpose, πρόθεσις: Eph. I, 11; readiness, προθυμία: 2 Cor. VIII, 12; **frijondans viljan seinana mais þau guþ**, “lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God,” φιλήδονοι μᾶλλον ἢ φιλόθεοι: 2 Tim. III, 4; 2) good pleasure, εὐδοκία: Rom. X, 1; Eph. I, 9; **gods vilja**, the same: Luke II, 14; Phil. I, 15.

**VILJA-HALþEI**, see under **Hilþan**.

**GA-VILEIS**, adjective: 1) willing; **gavileis visan**, to agree, consent with, συνευδοκεῖν: 1 Cor. VII, 12, 13; 2) unanimous, ὁμοθυμαδόν: Rom. XV, 6.

**SILBA-VILEIS**, willing of one’s own accord, αὐθαίρετος: 2 Cor. VIII, 3.

**ANA-VILJEI**, feminine, gentleness, moderation, τὸ ἐπιεικές: Phil. IV, 5; see on this passage; dignity, σεμνότης: 1 Tim. III, 4; see on this passage.

**VILJARIþ**, masculine proper name, Neapolitan document.

**VILVAN** (compare **Vulfs**; Gf. I, 848), class-I verb, preterite *valv*, plural *vulvun*, participle *vulvans*, to seize, snatch, ἁρπάζειν: John VI, 15; to plunder, διαρπάζειν: Mark III, 27; present participle **vilvands**, rapacious, robber, ἅρπαξ: Matt. VII, 15.

**DIS-VILVAN**, to plunder, seize, διαρπάζειν: Mark III, 27.

**FRA-VILVAN**: 1) to snatch away, ἁρπάζειν: Matt. XI, 12; John X, 12, 28; 2 Cor. XII, 2, 4; 1 Thess. IV, 17; 2) to seize, συναρπάζειν: Luke VIII, 29.

**VILVS**, adjective, rapacious, ἅρπαξ: Luke XVIII, 11; 1 Cor. V, 10, 11.

**VULVA**, feminine, robbery, seizure, ἁρπαγμός: Phil. II, 6.

**VIMMAN** (Old Norse *vömm, vaema*, Old Saxon *wam*, Anglo-Saxon *vom, vemman*, Old High German *wamm, wemmian*, Old Frisian *wam*, Swedish *vämjas*, Danish *vaemmes*; Gf. I, 851; Rchth. 1024), class-I verb, preterite *vamm*, plural *vummun*, participle *vummans*, to stain, make impure.

**VAMM**, neuter (?), stain, spot, σπῖλος: Eph. V, 27.

**GA-VAMMS**, adjective, unclean, base, common, κοινός: Rom. XIV, 14.

**UN-VAMMS**, unstained, blameless, ἄμωμος: Eph. I, 4; V, 27; Col. I, 22; spotless, ἄσπιλος: 1 Tim. VI, 14.

**UN-VAMMEI**, feminine, sincerity, εἰλικρίνεια: 1 Cor. V, 8.

**ANA-VAMMJAN**, class-II verb, to find fault with, blame, μωμᾶν: 2 Cor. VI, 3.

**VINDAN** (Old Norse *vinda*, Anglo-Saxon *vindan, invidd*, Old Saxon *windan, wendian*, Old High German *wintan, inwit*, Old Frisian *winda*, English *wind*, Swedish *vinda, vaenda*, Danish *vinde, vende*, Dutch *winden*, Modern [Col. 1484] High German *winden, wenden*; Gr. II, 35; Gf. I, 746, 769; Rchth. 1151), class-I verb, preterite *vand*, plural *vundun*, participle *vundans*, to wind, roll.

**BI-VINDAN**: 1) to wrap round, clothe, περιβάλλειν: Mark XIV, 51; XVI, 5; to wrap up, ἐντυλίττειν: Matt. XXVII, 59; to wind around, ἐνειλεῖν: Mark.

XV, 46; 2) to wrap, to swaddle, Greek *sparganoûn* (“to swaddle”): Luke II.7, 12. DUGA-VINDAN, to entangle, Greek *emplekein* (“to entwine”): II Timothy II.4. US-VINDAN, to plait, Greek *plékein* (“to braid”): Mark XV.17; John XIX.2. ÏN-VINDS, adjective: 1) perverse, Greek *diestramménos* (“twisted, perverted”): Luke IX.41; 2) unjust, Greek *ádikos* (“unjust”): Matthew V.45; Luke XVI.11; XVIII.11; I Corinthians VI.1. ÏN-VINDIþA, feminine, iniquity, injustice, Greek *adikía* (“injustice”): Luke XVI.8, 9; XVIII.6; John VII.18; Romans IX.14; I Corinthians XIII.6. VANDJAN, conjugation II, to turn, turn about, Greek *stréphein* (“to turn”): Matthew V.39; *vandjan sik*, to turn oneself, Greek *stréphesthai*: Luke VII.9. AT-VANDJAN, to turn; *atvandjan sik aftra*, to return, Greek *epanérchesthai*: Luke XIX.15. AF-VANDJAN, to turn, return, Greek *apotréphein* (“to turn away”): Romans XI.26; II Timothy I.15; IV.4; Titus I.14; Greek *apotrépein* (“to turn away”): II Timothy III.5; Greek *metatithénai* (“to transfer, desert”): Galatians I.6; *Skeireins* II.a. BI-VANDJAN, to avoid, Greek *stéllesthai* (“to keep oneself from”): II Corinthians VIII.20; Greek *paraitesthai* (“to decline, avoid”): I Timothy IV.7; V.11; II Timothy II.23; Greek *periístasthai* (“to avoid”): II Timothy II.16.

GA-VANDJAN: 1) to turn, return, Greek *epistréphein* (“to turn back”): Luke VIII.55; 2) to bring back, Greek *apostréphein* (“to turn back”): Matthew XXVII.3; 3) to return, Greek *epistréphein*: Luke I.16, 17; *Skeireins* I.c; * to gain, Greek *kerdaínein*: I Corinthians IX.21, in this passage. *gavandjan sik* (*sis*, Luke II.20): a) to turn back, Greek *stréphesthai*: Luke VII.44; XIV.25; Greek *epistréphesthai* (“to turn round”): Matthew IX.22; Mark V.30; VIII.33; Luke XVII.31; Greek *ektrépesthai* (“to turn aside”): II Timothy IV.4; also without *sik*, Greek *stréphesthai*: Luke IX.55; X.21, 23; * to come together, Greek *synérchesthai*: I Corinthians VII.5; see this passage. b) to turn oneself back, Greek *hypostréphein* (“to return”): Luke I.56; II.20, 39, 43, 45; IV.1, 14; VII.10; VIII.37; IX.10; X.17; XVII.15; also without *sik*: Luke XVII.18; Greek *anakámptein* (“to return”): Luke X.6. c) to return, Greek *epistréphein*: Mark IV.12; Luke XVII.4; Galatians IV.9; also without *sik*: II Corinthians III.16; Greek *epistréphesthai*: John XII.40; *Skeireins* III.c. ÏN-VANDJAN, to pervert, corrupt, Greek *metastréphein* (“to change, pervert”): Galatians I.7. US-VANDJAN, to turn away, Greek *apostréphesthai*: Matthew V.42; Greek *ektrépesthai*: I Timothy I.6; Greek *ekklínein* (“to turn aside”): Psalm LIII.3. GA-VANDEINS, feminine, return: *Skeireins* I.d. US-VANDI, feminine, meditation, conduct, Greek *methodeía* (“craft, stratagem”): Ephesians IV.14; see this passage.

VINDS (Old Norse *vindr*, Old Frisian, Old Saxon *wind*, Old High German *wint*, Anglo-Saxon, Swedish, Danish *vind*, English, Dutch, Modern High German *Wind*; Latin *ventus*, “wind”; Gr. III.390; Gf. I.623; Rchth. 1151), masculine, wind, Greek *ánemos*: Matthew VII.25, 27; VIII.26, 27; XI.7; Mark IV.37, 39, 41; XIII.27; Luke VII.24; VIII.23, 24, 25; John VI.18.

*VINþJAN* (Anglo-Saxon *vindvian*, English *winnow*; compare Latin *vannus*, “winnowing-fan”), conjugation II, to shake. DIS-VINþJAN, to shake to pieces, Greek *likmân* (“to crush”): Luke XX.18. VINþI-SKAURO, see under *Skiuran*.

VINNAN (Old Norse *vinna*, Anglo-Saxon *winnan*, Old Saxon, Old High German *winnan*, Old Frisian *winna*; Gr. II.34; Gf. I.875; Rchth. 1151), conjugation I, *vann, vunnun, vunnans*, to suffer, Greek *páschein*: Mark VIII.31; IX.12; Luke IX.22; II Corinthians I.6; Philippians I.29; Colossians I.24; I Thessalonians II.14; II Thessalonians I.5; II Timothy I.12; to be distressed, Greek *odynâsthai*: Luke II.48; *vinnands arbaidai*, “labouring in toil,” Greek *en kópōi kai móchthōi* (“in labour and hardship”): II Thessalonians III.8; *vraka vinnan*, to suffer persecution, Greek *diókesthai*: Galatians VI.12; *agliþos vinnan*, to suffer affliction, Greek *thlíbesthai*: I Thessalonians III.4; *aglons vinnan*, the same: I Timothy V.10. GA-VINNAN, to suffer, Greek *páschein*: Galatians III.4. VINNO, feminine, suffering, pain, Greek *páthema* (“suffering”): Romans VII.5; Galatians V.24; Greek *páthos* (“passion, suffering”): Colossians III.5. VINNA, feminine, the same, Greek *páthos*: Colossians III.5, in this passage. VUNNS, feminine, the same, Greek *páthema*: II Timothy III.11.

VINJA (Old High German *winjan*; Gr. II.55; DRA. 521; Gf. I.882), feminine, pasture, Greek *nomḗ*: John X.9.

VINTRUS (Old Norse *vetr*, Old Saxon, Old High German *wintar*, Old Frisian *winter*, Anglo-Saxon, Swedish, Danish *vinter*, English, Dutch, Modern High German *Winter*; Gf. I.630; Rohth. 1152), masculine: 1) winter, Greek *cheimṓn*: Mark XIII.18; John X.22; 2) year, in reckonings of time, Greek *étos*: Matthew IX.20; Luke II.42; VIII.42; *vintru visan*, see under *Visan*. VIPJA, see under *Veipan*.

VIS (Gr. II.26), neuter, calm of the sea, Greek *galḗnē*: Matthew VIII.26; Mark IV.39; Luke VIII.24.

*VIS* (Old Saxon and Old Frisian *wiss*; compare *Veitan*; Gf. I.1106), adjective, certain. UN-VIS, uncertain, Greek *ádēlos*: I Corinthians IX.26.

VISAN (Old Norse *vera*, Anglo-Saxon *vesan*, Old Saxon, Old High German *wesan*, Old Frisian *wesa*, English *was*, Swedish *vära*, Danish *være*, Dutch, Modern High German *wesen*; compare Latin *esse*, “to be”; Gr. II.26; Gf. I.1053; Rchth. 1143), anomalous conjugation; present *ïm, ïs, ïst, sijum, sijuþ, sind*; preterite *vas*, plural *vesum* (in the third-person singular present it contracts with negation *ni* into *nist*: Matthew X.24, 37; Mark VI.4; IX.40; X.40; XII.27, 31, 32; XVI.6; Luke I.37; VI.40; VII.28; IX.13, 50; XIV.32; XX.38; John VI.24; VII.16, 18; VIII.13, 44; IX.16; X.12; XI.4, 10; XIII.16; XIV.24; XV.20; XVIII.36; Romans XIII.1; XIV.17; I Corinthians VII.15; XII.14, 15, 16; XV.12, 13, 58; II Corinthians I.18; XI.14, 15; Galatians I.7; III.28; V.2, 23; Ephesians VI.9, 12; Colossians III.11, 25; I Timothy I.9; II Timothy II.9 [but Romans VIII.9 has *ni ïst*, and Luke VI.43; VIII.17, *ni auk ïst*]; with *þata* in *þat-ïst*, see under *þata*; with *kara* in *kar-ïst*, see under *Kara*).

1. To be, as an independent verb.

a. To be, exist, Greek *eînai*: Matthew VI.30, *þata havi haiþjos himma daga visando*, “the grass of the field that exists today”; Mark VIII.1, *at filu managai managein visandein*, “when there was a very great crowd”; XII.18; Luke XX.27, 29; John VIII.58; XI.9; XVII.5; Romans X.12; XIII.1. To come to be, Greek *gígnesthai*: Luke I.5. To be present, Greek *pareînai*: John VII.6.

b. To mean, to be called, Greek *eînai*: Mark VI.2, *gamainjaim handum, þat-ïst unþvahanaim matjan*, “with common hands, that is, to eat unwashed”; XI.34; Romans VII.18; IX.10; X.6, 7.

c. *vaiht visan*, to have force or validity, Greek *ti ischýein* (“to be of any account”): Galatians VI.15.

d. To become, Greek *gígnesthai*, in *ni sijai* (*nis-sijai*), “may it not be”: Luke XX.16; Romans VII.7, 13; IX.15; XI.1, 11; Galatians II.17; VI.14.

e. In a local sense, although often metaphorical.

α. With adverbs: *her*, here: Mark VI.3, *niu sind svistrjus ïs her at unsis?*, “Are not his sisters here with us?”; XVI.6; John VI.9; XI.21; Colossians IV.9. *jainar*, there: Matthew XXVII.55, *vesun-uh þan jainar qinons managos*, “and many women were there”; 61; Mark III.2; V.11; Luke II.6; VI.6; VIII.32; X.6; John VI.22, 24; XI.15; XII.9. *þaruh*, there: Matthew VI.21, *þarei auk ïst huzd ïzvar, þaruh ïst jah hairto ïzvar*, “for where your treasure is, there your heart also is”; John XII.26; XIV.3; II Corinthians III.17. *þaþro*, thither: John XVIII.36, *þiudangardi meina nist þaþro*, “my kingdom is not from there.” *þarei*, where: Mark II.4, *andhulidedun hrot, þarei vas Iesus*, “they uncovered the roof where Jesus was”; Matthew VI.21; John VII.34, 36, 42; XI.32, 41; XII.1, 26; XIV.3; XVII.24; XVIII.1; Colossians III.1, 11. *þadei*, where: John VI.62, *gasaiwiþ sunu mans ussteigan, þadei vas faurþis*, “you see the Son of Man ascending where he was before”; Mark VI.55. *war*, where: Mark XIV.14, *war sind saliþvos, þarei paska matjau?*, “Where is the guest-chamber where I may eat the Passover?”; Luke VIII.25; John VII.11; VIII.19; IX.12; I Corinthians XV.55. *waþro*, whence: John VII.27, *ni manna vait, waþro ïst*, “no one knows whence he is”; 28; IX.29, 30; XIX.9. *newa*, near: Mark XIII.28, *kunnuþ þatei newa ïst asans*, “you know that summer is near”; 29; Luke XIX.11; John VI.4; VII.2; XI.18; Romans X.8; Philippians IV.5; otherwise see under *New*. *newis*, nearer: Romans XIII.11, *newis ïst naseins unsara þau þan galaubidedum*, “our salvation is nearer now than when we believed.” *fairra*, far: Matthew VIII.30, *vas-uh þan fairra ïm hairda sweine*, “there was a herd of swine at some distance from them”; Mark XII.34; Luke XIV.32; Ephesians II.13; otherwise see under *Fairra*. *faura*, before: Philippians III.14, *du þaim, þoei faura sind, mik ufþanjands*, “stretching forward to the things that are before.” *ïupa*, above: Colossians III.1, *þoei ïupa sind, sokeiþ*, “seek the things above”; 2. *uta*, outside: I Thessalonians IV.12, *gaggaiþ gafehaba du þaim þaiei uta sind*, “walk honourably toward those who are outside”; Mark I.45. *utaþro*, from outside: Mark VII.15, *ni vaihts ïst utaþro mans inngaggando in ina*, “nothing entering a person from outside is [able to defile] him.” *ufaro*, above: *Skeireins* IV.b, *ni þatei ufaro visandan svare kannidedi*, “nor did he recognize clearly that which exists above.” *aljar visan*, see under *Alis*.

β. With prepositions: with *ïn*, “in”: Matthew V.25, *und þatei ïs ïn viga miþ ïmma*, “while you are on the way with him”; VI.4; X.32, 33; XI.8; XXVII.56; Mark I.23; II.1; V.5, 25; XV.41; Luke I.61; II.8, 25, 44, 49; IV.25, 27, 32, 33; V.7, 12; VII.25 (Greek *hypárchein*, “to be”); VIII.43; IX.12, 61; XVI.23 (Greek *hypárchein*); XVII.21; XVIII.2, 3; John VII.12, 18; VIII.44; IX.5, 30; XI.6, 10, 30; XII.35; XIV.2, 10, 17; XVII.11, 26; Romans VII.5, 23; VIII.8, 9, 34; XII.3; I Corinthians IV.3; XIV.25; XV.17; II Corinthians I.1; V.4; VII.3; XI.10, 25, *naht jah dag ïn diupiþai vas mareins*, “I spent a night and a day in the deep,” Greek *nychthḗmeron en tōi bythōi pepoíēka*; XIII.5; Galatians IV.25; Ephesians I.1; II.11; IV.18, 21; V.9, 18; Philippians III.6; IV.3; Colossians IV.13; I Thessalonians II.14; V.4; I Timothy I.4; II.2, 12; IV.15; II Timothy I.5, 6, 15; II.10, 20; *ïn fragiftim visan*, see under *Giban*; *ïn gagreftai visan*, see under *Grefts*.

With *ana*, “on”: Mark I.45, *ana auþjaim stadim vas*, “he was in desert places”; IV.1; X.32; Luke I.80; II.25, 40; XV.25; XVII.31; John VI.10; VII.39; Colossians III.2, 5. With *at*, “at, with”: Mark IX.19, *und wa at ïzvis sijau*, “how long shall I be with you?”; XIV.49; Luke IX.41; John XVII.7; II Corinthians I.17; XI.8 (Greek *pareînai*, “to be present”); Ephesians VI.9; Colossians III.25; I Thessalonians III.4; II Thessalonians III.10. With *ufar*, “above”: Matthew X.24, *nist siponeis ufar laisarja*, “a disciple is not above the teacher”; Luke VI.40; II Corinthians XI.5; *ufar filu visan*, see under *Filu*. With *ufaro*, “over”: Luke XIX.19, *þu sijais ufaro fimf baurgim*, “be over five cities,” Greek *gínou* (“become”); John III.31. With *uf*, “under/on”: I Corinthians X.1, *attans unsarai allai uf milhmin vesun*, “our fathers were all under the cloud”; Galatians IV.2, 21; V.18; I Timothy VI.1. With *faura*, “before”: Mark V.21, *vas faura marein*, “he was by the sea”; Colossians I.17; Nehemiah V.15. With *faur*, “for”: Mark IX.40, *saei nist wiþra ïzvis, faur ïzvis ïst*, “who is not against you is for you”; Luke IX.50. With *wiþra*, “against”: see the preceding passage and Galatians V.23; *Skeireins* I.c. With *miþ*, “with”: Matthew IX.15, *und þata weilos, þei miþ ïm ïst bruþfaþs*, “as long as the bridegroom is with them”; XXVI.69, 71; Mark I.13; II.19, 26; III.14; IV.36; XIV.67; Luke I.66; V.34; VI.3, 4; VIII.38; XV.31; John III.26; VII.33; VIII.29; IX.40; XI.31; XII.17; XIII.33; XIV.9; XV.27; XVI.4, 32; XVII.12, 24; Philippians I.23; IV.9; II Timothy IV.11. With *fram*, “from”: John VI.46, *saei ïst fram attin, sa saw attan*, “he who is from the Father has seen the Father”; VII.17, 22, 29; IX.16, 33. With *us*, “out of”: Mark XI.30, *daupeins Iohannis uzuh himina vas þau uzuh mannam?*, “Was John’s baptism from heaven or from men?”; Luke II.4; XX.4; John VII.52; VIII.23, 41, 47; XV.19; XVII.14, 16; XVIII.36; II Corinthians III.5; Galatians V.8; Philippians III.9; Colossians IV.9, 11, 17; *Skeireins* IV.c. With *afar*, “after”: Matthew XXVII.62, *ïftumin daga, saei ïst afar paraskaivein*, “on the next day, which is after the Preparation.”

f. To remain, Greek *ménein*: John XII.34; XIV.10, 16; XV.4, 7, 10, 11, 16; I Corinthians VII.8, 20; XV.6.

g. With the dative, to have, Greek *eînai*: Luke I.7, *ni vas ïm barne*, “they did not have children” [literally, “there were no children to them”]; 36; II.7; VI.32, 33, 34; VIII.42; IX.38; XIV.10; John XII.31; XVIII.39; Romans IX.2; XIII.11; I Corinthians XV.12, 13; Ephesians VI.9, 12; II Thessalonians III.2.

2. To be, as the substantive verb joining predicate and subject, Greek *eînai* (sometimes also where Greek omits it).

a. Before a noun or adjective as predicate: Matthew III.11, *sa afar mis gaggida swinþoza mis ïst*, “he who comes after me is mightier than I”; V.34, *stols ïst guþs*, “it is God’s throne”; 35, 48; VI.22, 23; V.9, 13, 14, 34; VI.3, 4, 11, 15, 16; VII.4, 15, 26, 27; VIII.9, 27, 29; IX.5, 6, 10, 34, 35, 42, 43, 45, 47; X.8, 24, 25, 43, 44, 47; XI.13, 32; XII.7, 11, 14, 26, 27, 28, 29, 31, 32, 33, 35, 37; XIII.19, 22; VII.6, 7, 12, 18, 26, 28, 36, 40, 41, 50; VIII.12, 13, 14, 16, 17, 25, 26, 31, 33, 34, 36, 37, 39, 42, 44, 45, 48, 53, 54, 55; IX.4, 5, 8, 9, 13, 14, 17, 18, 19, 24, 25, 28, 31, 40, 41; X.1, 2, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 13, 14, 22, 24, 29, 30, 33, 34, 36, 41; XI.1, 25, 27, 38, 39; XII.2, 6, 34; XIII.16, 30, 35; XIV.6, 28; XV.1, 3, 5, 12, 20; XVI.17, 18, 32; XVII.3, 11, 17, 19, 21, 22; XVIII.13, 15, 16, 18, 28, 30, 33, 35, 37, 38, 40; XIX.12; Romans VII.3, 8, 14;
