XII.6, 10, 11; XIII.9; Galatians I.7, 22; II.3, 6, 9; III.3, 28, 29; IV.1, 3, 6, 7, 8, 15, 18, 24, 26, 28, 31; V.3, 10, 19, 22; VI.3; Ephesians I.4, 14, 18, 23; II.1, 3, 4, 5, 8, 10, 14, 19, 20; III.6, 13, 18; IV.9, 14, 15, 18, 25, 29; V.3, 5, 8, 10, 17, 23, 27; VI.17; Philippians I.21, 22, 23, 28; II.6, 28; III.3, 6, 7, 8, 15, 19; IV.8, 11; Colossians I.7, 15, 18, 24, 27; II.13, 14, 17; III.5, 14; IV.11; I Thessalonians II.15, 19, 20; IV.3; V.5, 18, 21; II Thessalonians I.3, 6; III.17; I Timothy I.5, 7, 8, 15; II.3, 10; III.12, 15, 16; IV.8, 10, 15; V.3, 4, 5, 8, 24, 25; VI.2, 6, 10; II Timothy I.12; II.2, 24; IV.11; Titus I.9, 10, 13, 16; II.1; Philemon 12; Nehemiah V.14; VI.18; VII.2; *Skeireins* I.a; II.c; IV.b, c, d; V.b, d; VI.b; VII.b, d; VIII.d.

Greek *gígnesthai*, “to become”: Luke I.2; XIX.17; Romans XI.34; I Corinthians XIV.20; Philippians III.6; Colossians IV.11; I Timothy IV.12; V.9. Greek *hypárchein*, “to exist”: Luke IX.48; XVI.14; I Corinthians VII.26; XII.22; II Corinthians VIII.17; XII.16; Galatians II.14; Philippians II.6; III.20. The following expressions also belong here: *sa ïst sa manna*, “Behold the man,” Greek *íde ho ánthrōpos*: John XIX.5; *iudaieis visandans*, “being Jews by nature,” Greek *phýsei Ioudaîoi*: Galatians II.15; further, *fauragaggja visan*, “to be a forerunner”; *kara visan*, “to be burdened”; *galaista visan*, “to be instructed”; *fraþjamarzeins visan*, “to be prudent”; *ufarassus visan*, “to be superior”; *skula visan*, “to be indebted”; *galiugaveitvods visan*, “to be a false witness”; *airzis visan*, “to be in error”; *ansteigs visan*, “to be acceptable”; *baitrs visan*, “to be bitter”; *barnisks visan*, “to be childish”; *batiza visan*, “to be better”; *usbeisneigs visan*, “to be exemplary”; *biuhts visan*, “to be useful”; *bruks visan*, “to be profitable”; *gredags visan*, “to be hungry”; *dauþs visan*, “to be dead”; *hails visan*, “to be whole”; *afhaims visan*, “to be away from home”; *anahaims visan*, “to be at home”; *hulþs visan*, “to be gracious”; *andaþahts visan*, “to be acceptable”; *þvairhs visan*, “to be angry”; *ïusiza visan*, “to be more … [uncertain]”; *unkarja visan*, “to be strange”; *aljakuns visan*, “to be of another kind”; *uskunþs visan*, “to be unknown”; *svikunþs visan*, “to be manifest”; *galeiks visan*, “to be like”; *laus visan*, “to be free”; *mahteigs visan*, “to be powerful”; *unmahteigs visan*, “to be powerless”; *gamainja visan*, “to be common”; *ganohs visan*, “to be sufficient”; *binauhts visan*, “to be content”; *uhteigs visan*, “to be early”; *uhtiugs visan*, “to be late”; *garaids visan*, “to be ready”; *bireks visan*, “to be poor”; *sels visan*, “to be good”; *siuks visan*, “to be sick”; *usskavs visan*, “to be wise”; *vairþs visan*, “to be worthy”; *andvairþs visan*, “to be present”; *anavairþs visan*, “to be absent”; *gavairþeigs visan*, “to be peaceable”; *vans visan*, “to be lacking”; *vars visan*, “to be wary”; *gavileis visan*, “to be glad”; *unweis visan*, “to be ignorant”; *unvits visan*, “to be foolish”; *vulþags visan*, “to be glorious”; *vulþriza visan*, “to be more valuable”; *vods visan*, “to be mad, demon-possessed”; *gafulgins visan*, “to be fulfilled”; *fuls visan*, “to be full”; etc.

b. With a possessive pronoun: Matthew VI.13; Mark X.40; Luke VI.20; XV.31; John VII.16; XIV.24; XVI.15; XVII.6, 9, 10.

c. With a participle. α. With a present participle: Matthew VII.29, *vas auk laisjands ïns swe waldufni habands*, “for he was teaching them as having authority”; Mark I.39; II.18; IV.38; V.40; IX.4; X.22; XIV.54; XV.40, 43; Luke I.10, 20, 21, 22; II.33, 51; IV.20, 31, 44; V.1, 16, 17, 20; VI.12; VIII.40; IX.18, 53; XV.1; XIX.17, 47; John X.40; XIII.23; XVIII.18, 25; I Corinthians X.19; XI.2; XV.19; II Corinthians I.9; II.9, 11; V.19; IX.12; XIII.11; Galatians I.23; IV.3; Philippians II.26; Colossians I.21; II.23; I Thessalonians IV.6; I Timothy I.13; III.2; Titus I.6; *Skeireins* II.b; III.b, d. Greek *gígnesthai*, “to become”: Mark I.4; I Corinthians X.32; XVI.10; Colossians I.18.

β. With a present participle. αα. In a passive sense, Greek *eînai*: Matthew X.26, *ni waiht auk ïst gahuliþ*, “for nothing is covered,” Greek *oudèn gár estin kekalymménon*; 30; Mark I.6; XV.7, 22, 26, 34, 46; Luke II.26; IV.16, 17, 38; VIII.2; IX.32, 45; John III.24; VI.31, 45, 65; X.34; XII.14, 16; XVI.24; XVII.23; XIX.11; Romans XIII.1; I Corinthians V.11; X.28; XIII.10; II Corinthians IV.3; X.18; XIII.5, 6; Galatians II.11; Ephesians II.5, 8; Colossians III.20; I Thessalonians III.9; I Timothy III.10; V.7; II Timothy III.17; Titus I.7; Nehemiah V.18.

ββ. In an active sense: Mark I.33, *so baurgs alla garunnana was at daura*, “the whole city was gathered at the door”; Luke V.17, *þaiei wesun gaqumanai us allamma haimo*, “who had come from every village.” Here belong expressions such as *druggkans visan*, “to be drinking”; *habaiþs visan*, “to be possessed”; *þaursiþs visan*, “to be thirsty”; *asþaursiþs visan*, “to be very thirsty”; *þaurfts visan*, “to be needy”; *kunþs visan*, “to be known”; *mahts visan*, “to be able”; *hlauts gasatiþs visan*, “to be allotted and appointed”; *skulds visan*, “to be indebted”; *ungatewiþs visan*, “to be unprepared”; *uswahsans visan*, “to be grown up”; etc.; where the verb is merely auxiliary, see under 3.

d. With predicate expressed by an adverb: Matthew VI.25, *niu saiws mais ïst fodeinai?*, “Is not life more than food?”; I Corinthians XV.17, *swari so galaubeins ïzwar ïst*, “then your faith is vain”; I Thessalonians II.10, *waiwa weihaba ïzweis þaim galaubjandam wesum*, “how holily we behaved toward you who believe,” Greek *egenḗthēmen*, “we became”; Luke I.34; Mark IV.36, *andnemun ina, swe was, in skipa*, “they took him, as he was, in the boat”; II Corinthians II.17; II Timothy III.9, *unwiti ize swikunþ wairþiþ allaim, swaswe jah jainaize was*, “their folly will become evident to all, as that of those also became,” Greek *egéneto*; I Thessalonians II.13; Mark IV.26, *swa ist þiudangardi guþs*, “thus is the kingdom of God”; X.43; I Corinthians VII.26.

e. With a preposition as predicate. α. With *bi*: Romans VIII.5, *þai bi leika wisandans*, “those who are according to the flesh”; Ephesians VI.21, 22; Philippians II.23, 28; Colossians IV.7, 8; I Timothy I.11; Titus I.1; Philemon 14. β. With *du*: John XI.4, *so siukei nist du dauþau*, “this sickness is not unto death”; Romans VII.10; I Corinthians XIV.22, *razdos du bandwai sind*, “tongues are for a sign”; II Corinthians VII.15; Ephesians I.12; Colossians II.22; *du botai visan*, see under *Batan*; compare Luke V.17, *mahts fraujins was du hailjan ins*, “the Lord’s power was present to heal them.” γ. With *ïnu*: Romans XI.29, *ïnu idreiga sind auk gibos jah laþons guþs*, “for the gifts and calling of God are without repentance”; Ephesians II.12.

f. With predicate expressed by a complete or elliptical clause, either α. in direct speech: Matthew V.37, *sijaiþ-þan waurd ïzwar: ja ja, ne ne*, “but let your word be: Yes, yes; no, no”; IX.13, *ganimiþ wa sijai, armahairtiþa wiljau jah ni hunsl*, “go and learn what this is: ‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice’”; XXVII.46; II Corinthians I.18; or β. joined to what precedes by a relative: αα. by a relative pronoun: Matthew XI.10, *sa ist auk, bi þanei gameliþ ist*, “this is he concerning whom it is written”; Mark IV.16, 22; VII.15; IX.1, 39; Luke VII.27; XVI.15; XVIII.29; XX.2; John V.45; VI.63, 64; VII.25; VIII.18, 30, 54; IX.8; X.6; XI.2; XIII.24, 26; XIV.21; XVIII.14, 26; I Corinthians XV.10; II Corinthians II.2; XII.13; Ephesians IV.10; II Timothy III.6; Nehemiah VI.17. ββ. by a relative particle: *þatei*: Mark II.16, *wa ist, þatei miþ motarjam jah fravaurhtaim matjiþ jah driggkiþ?*, “Why does he eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”; *ei*: Mark IX.21, *wan lagg mel ist, ei þata warþ imma?*, “How long has it been since this happened to him?”; I Corinthians XVI.12; *þarei*: Mark IV.15, *þai wiþra wig sind, þarei saiada þata waurd*, “these are those by the way, where the word is sown”; *swe*: Mark XII.25, *sind swe aggiljus þai in himinam*, “they are like the angels in heaven”; *swaswe*: Matthew VI.5, *ni sijaiþ swaswe þai liutans*, “do not be like the hypocrites”; Luke XVIII.11; Romans IX.27.

g. With a genitive joined to the predicate, expressing α. to whom something belongs: Mark X.14, *þize ist þiudangardi guþs*, “of such is the kingdom of God”; XII.16, *hwis ist sa manleika?*, “Whose image is this?”; IX.41; Luke V.3; IX.55; XVIII.16; John X.12, 21; Romans VIII.9; IX.4; I Corinthians I.12; X.26; II Corinthians II.3; IV.7; X.7; Galatians V.24; II Timothy II.19. β. to what something belongs: Matthew XXVI.73, *bi sunjai jah þu þize is*, “surely you too are one of them”; Mark XIV.69, 70; John X.16, 26; XII.20; XV.19; XVIII.17, 25; I Corinthians XII.15, 16; I Timothy I.19; II Timothy I.15; II.17. γ. a particular quality: John XVIII.37, *wazuh saei ist sunjos*, “everyone who is of the truth”; Romans VIII.5, *þo þoei leikis sind miton*, “those who are of the flesh think [on fleshly things]”; XIV.19, *þoei gawaiþjis sind, laistjaima jah þoei timraineis sind in uns misso*, “let us pursue the things of peace and the things of mutual edification.” Expressions such as *dagis visan*, “to be of the day,” I Thessalonians V.8, and *visan jere twalibe*, “to be twelve years [old],” Mark V.42, also belong here.

h. The predicate must be supplied: Mark XIV.44, *sa ist*, “this is this”; 62, *ik im*, “I am this”; John VI.20; VIII.24, 28; IX.9, 36, 37; XIII.19, 25; XVIII.5, 6, 8, 17, 25; I Corinthians XIV.26.

3. As an auxiliary verb for periphrastic passive forms.

a. In the present and preterite in place of an aorist: Matthew V.21, *qiþan ist*, “it was said,” Greek *errhḗthē*; 27, 31, 33, 38, 43; VIII.3; IX.33; Mark I.9; III.21; XV.15, 28; Luke I.13, 19, 26; II.11, 17, 20, 21; IV.17, 26, 27; VII.12; X.20, 22; XVII.9; John VII.39; IX.32; XII.5, 16; XIII.31, 32; XV.8; XVI.21; XVIII.36; Romans IX.11, 12; XII.3; I Corinthians I.13, at the end; V.7; VII.20, 21, 22, 23, 24; X.2; XII.13; XV.4, 5, 6; subscription; II Corinthians I.8; IV.10; VII.7, 9; XI.25, 33; XII.7; XIII.4; subscription; Galatians II.3, 17; III.1, 27; V.13; Ephesians I.11; III.2, 3, 5, 10; IV.1, 4, 7, 21, 30; Philippians I.29; III.8; Colossians I.23, 25, 26; III.15; I Thessalonians III.1, 7; II Thessalonians I.10; I Timothy I.11, 13; II.7; VI.12; II Timothy I.9, 11; III.14; Titus I.3; Nehemiah V.17, 18; *Skeireins* I.b; III.b; IV.d; VI.c; VII.c.

b. In the present in place of a perfect: Matthew XI.8; Mark I.2, *gameliþ ist*, “it is written,” Greek *gégraptai*; IV.11; V.4; VII.6; IX.12, 13, 42; X.40; XI.17; XV.4 (for the Gothic reads Greek *tétheitai*, “has been laid down”); XVI.4; Luke II.23, 24; III.4; IV.4, 6, 8, 10, 12; VIII.10; X.26; XIX.46; John VI.65; VII.8, 47; VIII.17, 41; XVII.10; XVIII.37; Romans VII.2; VIII.36; IX.13, 33; X.15; XI.26; XII.19; XIII.1; XIV.11; XV.9; I Corinthians I.13, 19; IV.4, 6; VII.14, 15, 27; XIV.21; XV.27; II Corinthians VII.4, 13; VIII.15; IX.2, 3, 9; Galatians II.7; IV.22, 23, 27; V.11; VI.14; Philippians I.17; III.12; IV.12; Colossians I.16, 17; III.3; IV.3, 6; I Thessalonians III.3; I Timothy I.9; VI.5; II Timothy II.9; IV.8; Titus I.15.

c. In the preterite in place of a pluperfect: Matthew VII.25, *gasuliþ was*, “had been founded,” Greek *tethemelíōto*; Luke IV.29; VI.48; VIII.2; XVI.20; John IX.22; XI.38, 44.

d. In the preterite in place of an imperfect: Mark I.5, *daupidai wesun*, “they were being baptized,” Greek *ebaptízonto*; Luke I.65; III.23; IV.1; VII.12; VIII.27, 29; XVI.19; XVII.27; John III.23; VI.18; XVIII.10; Romans VII.6; XI.23; compare Matthew XXVII.12; Luke II.3, 33. Hence also e. in the present in place of a present: I Corinthians XVI.13, *gaþwastidai sijaiþ*, “be strengthened,” Greek *krataiousthe*; II Corinthians I.4; XIII.11; Galatians IV.20; VI.13; Ephesians II.22; compare I Timothy VI.8.

AT-VISAN, to be present, Greek *paristánai*: Mark IV.29; Greek *ephistánai*: II Timothy IV.6; Greek *parakeîsthai*, “to lie at hand”: Romans VII.21. ÏN-VISAN, to be imminent, Greek *diágígnesthai*: Mark XVI.1. MIþ-VISAN, to be present with, Greek *symparagígnesthai*: II Timothy IV.16. UFAR-VISAN, to remain over: 1) to surpass, excel, Greek *hyperéchein*: Philippians IV.7; Greek *perisseúein*, “to abound”: II Corinthians III.9; 2) to be superior, Greek *hyperéchein*: Romans XIII.1. FAURA-VISAN, to be at hand: II Corinthians VIII.11; *Skeireins* VIII.b. VISTS, feminine, being, nature, Greek *phýsis*: Romans XI.24; Galatians IV.8; Ephesians II.3; *Skeireins* II.c, d.

VISAN, conjugation I, *vas, wesun* (*wisans*), to remain, stay, Greek *ménein*: Luke X.7; XIX.5; John V.38; VI.27, 56; VII.9; VIII.35; XII.46; XIV.17, 25; XV.4, 5, 6, 9, 10; Romans IX.11; I Corinthians VII.11; XV.6; II Corinthians III.11, 14; IX.9; II Timothy II.13; III.14; Greek *prosménein*, “to remain with”: Mark VIII.2; Greek *diaménein*, “to continue”: Luke I.22; Greek *epiménein*, “to persist”: I Corinthians XVI.8; Philippians I.24; Greek *endēmeîn*, “to be at home”: II Corinthians V.6; *wintru visan*, to winter, Greek *paracheimázein*: I Corinthians XVI.6; *waila visan*, to fare well, rejoice, Greek *euphraíthesthai*: Luke XV.23 (24), 32; XVI.19. BI-VISAN, to fare well, rejoice, Greek *euphraíthesthai*: Luke XV.29. GA-VISAN, to remain, Greek *ménein*: Luke VIII.27. MIþGA-VISAN, to be carried away together, Greek *synapágesthai*: Romans XII.16. þAIRH-VISAN, to remain, Greek *ménein*: John IX.41; to continue, Greek *epiménein*: Romans XI.22; Colossians I.33; I Timothy IV.16; to continue steadfastly, Greek *diaménein*: Galatians II.5, in this passage; to remain, Greek *paraménein*: Philippians I.25; to persist, Greek *prosménein*: I Timothy V.5.

VISS, see under *Vidan*. VISSEI, see under *Veitan*. VIT (Old Norse *vid*, Old Saxon *wit*, Anglo-Saxon *vit*; compare *Veis*), nominative dual of the first-person personal pronoun, “we two,” Greek *hēmeîs*: John XVII.11, 22. VITAN, see under *Veitan*. VITS, see under *Veitan*. VITOþ, see under *Veitan*. VLAITON, see under *Vleitan*.

*VLEITAN* (Old Norse *lita*, Anglo-Saxon *vlitan, vlite*, Old Saxon *wliti*, Old Frisian *wlite*; Gr. II.14; III.401; Gf. I.1130; II.322; Rchth. 1157), conjugation I, *vlait, vlitun, vlitans*, to look upon. ANDA-VLEIZNS (Old High German *antluzi*, Anglo-Saxon *andvlite*, Modern High German *Antlitz*), masculine, countenance, face, Greek *prósōpon*: Matthew XXVI.67; Luke XVII.16; I Corinthians XIV.25; II Corinthians III.13; XI.20. VLAITON, conjugation II, to look around, Greek *periblépesthai*: Mark V.32. VLITS, masculine: 1) countenance, face, Greek *prósōpon*: Mark XIV.65; II Corinthians III.7; Galatians I.22; appearance, Greek *ópsis*: John XI.44; 2) appearance, sight, form, Greek *morphḗ*: Philippians II.7. VLIZJAN, conjugation II, to chastise, buffet, Greek *hypōpiázein*: I Corinthians IX.27. YMAINAIUS, masculine proper name, Hymenaeus, Greek *Hyménaios*: II Timothy II.17.

VULAN (Old High German, Old Saxon *wallan*, Anglo-Saxon *weallan*, Old Frisian *walla*, Modern High German *wallen*; Latin *bullire*, “to boil”; Gf. I.797; Rchth. 1024), conjugation I, *waul, wulun, wulans* (?), to boil, be fervent, Greek *zeîn*: Romans XII.11; to spread, literally “to have increase,” Greek *nomḕn échein*: II Timothy II.17; see this passage.

VULþUS (Anglo-Saxon *wuldor*; compare *Valdan*; Gr. II.58; Gf. I.848, 899), masculine, glory, honour, Greek *dóxa*: Matthew VI.13, 29; Mark VIII.38; X.37; XIII.26; Luke II.9, 14, 32; IV.6; IX.26, 31, 32; XVII.18; XIX.38; John XI.40; XII.41; XVII.5, 22, 24; Romans IX.4, 23; XI.36; XV.7; I Corinthians X.31; II Corinthians I.20; III.7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 18; IV.6, 15; VI.7; VIII.19, 23; Galatians I.5; Ephesians I.6, 7, 12, 14, 17, 18; III.13, 16, 21; Philippians III.19, 21; Colossians I.11, 27; III.4; I Thessalonians II.12, 20; II Thessalonians I.9; I Timothy I.11, 17; III.16; II Timothy II.20; *Skeireins* IV.b. VULþAGS, adjective: 1) noble, honoured, Greek *éndoxos*: Luke VII.25; I Corinthians IV.10; II Corinthians III.7, see these passages; Ephesians V.27; glorified, Greek *dedoxasménos*: II Corinthians III.10; *vulþags visan*, to have been glorified, Greek *dedoxásthai*: II Corinthians III.10; 2) remarkable, extraordinary, Greek *parádoxos*: Luke V.26. VULþRS, feminine, value; *ni waiht vulþrais ist*, “it is of no value or importance,” Greek *oudèn diaphérei*: Galatians II.6, in this passage. VULþRS, comparative adjective *vulþriza*, superior, more valuable; *vulþriza visan*, to be superior, Greek *diaphérein*: Matthew VI.26; see this passage. VULþRIS, comparative adverb, rather, more valuably; *vulþris visan*, Greek *diaphérein*: Galatians II.6.

VULLA (Old Norse *ull*, Anglo-Saxon *wull*, Old High German *wolla*, Old Frisian *wolle*, English *wool*, Swedish *ull*, Danish *uld*, Modern High German *Wolle*; Gr. III.410; Gf. I.794; Rchth. 1158), feminine, wool (Greek *érion*, “wool,” according to Numbers XIX.5): *Skeireins* III.c. VULLAREIS, masculine, fuller, Greek *grapheús* (“scribe”): Mark IX.3. VULVA, see under *Vilvan*. VULFS (Old Norse *ulfr*, Old Saxon *wulf*, Anglo-Saxon *wulf*, Old High German, Old Frisian, English, Dutch, Modern High German *wolf*, Swedish and Danish *ulf*; Latin *vulpes* [*lupus*], “fox [wolf]”; Greek *alṓpēx*, “fox”; Gf. I.848; Rchth. 1158), masculine, wolf, Greek *lýkos*: Matthew VII.15; Luke X.3; John X.12.

*VUNAN* (compare Anglo-Saxon *wyn*, Old Saxon *wun …*, *wunnia*, Old High German *wunna*, Modern High German *Wonne*; Gr. II.55; Gf. I.882), conjugation II, to rejoice. UN-VUNANDS, present participle, distressed, afflicted, Greek *adēmonôn*: Philippians II.26. VUND …, see under *Vindan*. VUNDS (Old Norse *und*, Old Saxon *wund*, Anglo-Saxon *wund*, Old High German *wunta*, Old Frisian *wunde, unde*, English *wound*, Modern High German *Wunde*; Gf. I.896; Rchth. 1162), adjective, wounded, injured; *haubiþ wundan briggan*, to behead, Greek *kephalaioûn*: Mark XII.4. *VUNDON*, conjugation II, to wound. GA-VUNDON (*ga-vondon*), the same, Greek *traumatízein*: Luke XX.12. VUNDUFNI, feminine, stripe, scourge, Greek *mástix*: Mark III.10. VUNNS, see under *Vinnan*.

VRAIQS (Anglo-Saxon *wrenc*, English *wry*, Scots *wrink*; compare Swedish *vriden*, Danish *vride*), adjective, crooked, Greek *skoliós*: Luke III.5. VRAK, see under *Vrikan*. VRATON (Old Norse *rata*; Gr. II.51), conjugation II, to go, travel, Greek *poreúesthai*: Luke II.41; I Corinthians XVI.6; to travel through, Greek *diodeúein*: Luke VIII.1. VRATODUS, masculine, journey, Greek *hodoiporía*: II Corinthians XI.26.

VREKEI, see under *Vrikan*. *VRIGGAN* (Anglo-Saxon *wringan*, English *wring*), conjugation I, *wragg, wruggun, wruggans*, to twist. VRUGGO, feminine, snare, Greek *pagís*: II Timothy II.26. VRIþUS (Anglo-Saxon *wræþ*, Swedish *vråd*, Danish *vraad*; Gr. III.475), feminine, herd, flock, Greek *agélē*: Luke VIII.33.

VRIKAN (Old Norse *recka*, Anglo-Saxon *wrecan*, Old Saxon *wrak, wrekan*, Old Frisian *wreka*, Old High German *wreh, rehhan*, English *wreak, wrong*, Modern High German *rächen*; compare *Vrohjan*; Gr. II.27; Gf. I.1130, 1131; Rchth. 1160), conjugation I, *wrak, wrekun, wrikans*, to persecute, Greek *diókein*: Matthew V.44; see this passage; John XV.20; Romans XII.14; I Corinthians XV.9; II Corinthians IV.9; Galatians I.23; IV.29; V.11. GA-VRIKAN: 1) to avenge, Greek *ekdikeîn*: Romans XII.19; 2) to take vengeance, Greek *ekdíkēsin poieîn*: Luke XVIII.7, 8. FRA-VRIKAN, to persecute, Greek *ekdiṓkein*: I Thessalonians II.15. VRAKS, masculine, persecutor, Greek *diṓktēs*: I Timothy I.13. VRAKA, feminine, persecution, Greek *diōgmós*: Mark X.30; Galatians VI.12, in this passage; II Timothy III.11, 12. VRAKJA, feminine, the same: Mark IV.17; Romans VIII.35; II Thessalonians I.4; II Timothy III.11; *wrakja winnan*, to suffer persecution, Greek *diókesthai*: Galatians VI.12. VRAKJAN, conjugation II, to persecute, Greek *diókein*: Philippians III.6. VREKEI, feminine, persecution, Greek *diōgmós*: II Corinthians XII.10.

*VRISQAN*, conjugation II (?), to bear fruit. GA-VRISQAN, the same, Greek *telesphoreîn* (“to bring fruit to maturity”): Luke VIII.14. VRITS (Old Norse *rita*, Anglo-Saxon *writan*, Old Saxon *writan*, Old High German *rizan, reiz*, English *write*, Modern High German *reissen*; Gr. II.14; Gf. I.1130; II.557), masculine, point, needle, Greek *keraía*: Luke XVI.17. VRUGGO, see under *Vriggan*.

VROHJAN (Old Norse *rægja, rogr*, Old Saxon *wrogian*, Anglo-Saxon *wregan, wroht*, Old Frisian *wrogian, ruogia, rueka*, Old High German *rogjan*, Dutch *wrok*, Modern High German *wroge, rügen*; compare *Vrikan*; DRA. 855; Gf. I.1130; II.432; Rchth. 1161), conjugation II, to accuse, Greek *katēgoreîn*: Matthew XXVII.12; Mark III.2; XV.3; Luke VI.7; John V.45. FRA-VROHJAN, to slander, Greek *diabállein*: Luke XVI.1. VROHS, feminine, accusation, Greek *katēgoría*: John XVIII.29; I Timothy V.19.

VODS (Old Norse *óðr*, Anglo-Saxon *wōd, wēdan*, Old High German *wuot*, English *wood*, Dutch *woed*, Modern High German *Wuth*; Gr. II.10; Gf. I.766), adjective, mad, demon-possessed, Greek *daimonizómenos*: Mark V.15, 16; *wods wisan*, to be demon-possessed, Greek *daimonízesthai*: Mark V.18.

*VODS* (compare Anglo-Saxon *wudu-wita*; or is *weitwods* formed from a verb *weitwjan*, “to indicate, show, signify,” which would be related to *weitan*? Gr. II.10; DRA. 857), masculine, anomalous; plural *wods*. VEIT-VODS, witness, martyr, Greek *mártys*: Matthew XXVI.65; Mark XIV.63;

Cor. II, I, 23; XIII, 1; Tim. I, V, 19; VI, 12. **GALIUGAVEIT-VODS**, false witness, ψευδομάρτυρ: Cor. I, XV, 15; *galiugaveitvods visan*, to bear false witness, ψευδομαρτυρεῖν: Mc. X, 19; Luc. XVIII, 20. **VEIT-VODJAN**, conjugation II, to testify, μαρτυρεῖν: Luc. IV, 22; Joan. III, 26, 32; V, 36, 37; VII, 7; VIII, 13; X, 25; XII, 17; XIII, 21; XV, 26, 27; XVIII, 23; Rom. X, 2; Cor. I, XV, 15; Cor. II, VIII, 3; Gal. IV, 15; Col. IV, 13; Thess. I, II, 12; Tim. I, VI, 13; Skeir. IV, c; VI, b; καταμαρτυρεῖν, to testify against: Mth. XXVII, 13; Mc. XIV, 60; [Col. 1492] XV, 4; μαρτύρεσθαι, to call to witness / testify: Gal. V, 3; Eph. IV, 17; διαμαρτύρεσθαι, to solemnly testify: Thess. I, IV, 6; Tim. I, V, 21; Tim. II, II, 14; IV, 1; *galiug veitvodjan*, to testify falsely, ψευδομαρτυρεῖν: Mc. XIV, 56, 57. **MIþVEIT-VODJAN**, to testify together with, συμμαρτυρεῖν: Rom. IX, 1. **VEITVODIþA** (*veitvodida*, Joan. III, 32), feminine, testimony, μαρτύριον: Mth. XXVII, 13; Mc. I, 44; VI, 11; Luc. V, 14; IX, 5; Tim. II, I, 8; μαρτυρία, testimony: Mc. XIV, 55, 56, 59; Joan. III, 32; V, 36; VIII, 13, 17; Tim. I, III, 7; *veitvodiþa haban*, to be testified of, μαρτυρεῖσθαι: Tim. I, V, 10. **VEIT-VODEINS**, feminine, the same, Skeir. VI, c. **VEIT-VODEI**, feminine, the same, μαρτύριον, testimony: Cor. II, I, 12; Thess. II, I, 10; Tim. I, II, 6; μαρτυρία, testimony: Tit. I, 13; Skeir. VI, b. **VEIT-VODI**, neuter, the same, Tim. II, II, 2; see at that passage. **VOþS** (Old Saxon *wothi*; Gr. III, 786), adjective, good, acceptable; *dauns voþi*, a good fragrance, εὐωδία: Cor. II, II, 15; ὀσμὴ εὐωδίας, “a fragrant aroma,” Eph. V, 2. **VOK**, see under **Vakan**. **VOKRS** (Anglo-Saxon *vocor*, Old High German *wuochar*, Old Frisian *woker*, Swedish *ocker*, Danish *aager*, modern High German *Wucher*; Gr. II, 11; Gf. I, 680; Rchth. 1157), masculine, interest, τóκος: Luc. XIX, 23. **VONDON**, see **Vundon**. **VOPJAN** (Anglo-Saxon *vop, vepan*, Old Saxon *wopan*, Old High German *wuofan*, Old Frisian *wepan*, English *whoop, weep*; compare Latin *vocare*; Gf. I, 780; Rchth. 1135), conjugation II: 1) to cry out, φωνεῖν: Mth. XXVII, 47; Mc. X, 49; XIV, 68, 72; XV, 35; Luc. VIII, 54; XIX, 15; Joan. XI, 28; XII, 17; XIII, 13; XVIII, 33; βοᾶν, to cry aloud: Mc. I, 3; XV, 34; Luc. III, 4; XVIII, 7; 2) to call out to, summon, προσφωνεῖν: (Mth. XI, 16) Luc. VII, 32. **AT-VOPJAN**, to call to, φωνεῖν: Mc. IX, 35; X, 49; Luc. XVI, 2; Joan. IX, 18, 24; προσφωνεῖν: Luc. VI, 13. **UF-VOPJAN** (*ubuh-vopida*, Luc. XVIII, 38), to cry out, ἀναφωνεῖν: Luc. I, 42; φωνεῖν: Luc. VIII, 8; XVI, 2; ἀναβοᾷν, to cry aloud: Luc. IX, 38; βοᾷν, to cry aloud: Luc. XVIII, 38.

F
[Col. 1491] **FAGINON**, see under *Faihan*. **FAGRS**, see under *Faihan*. **FADAR** (Old Norse *fadir*, Anglo-Saxon *fader*, Old High German *fatar*, Old Frisian *feder, fader, feider*, English *father*, Old Saxon, Swedish, Danish *fader*, Dutch *vader*, Modern High German *vater*; Greek *patēr*, Latin *pater*; Bopp 80, 83; Gr. II, 43; III, 320; Gf. III, 374; Rchth. 729), anomalous masculine: father, Greek *patēr*: Gal. IV, 6.

**FADREIN**, indeclinable masculine plural: parents, Greek *goneis*: Luc. VIII, 56; XVIII, 29; Joan. IX, 2, 3, 18, 20, 22.

**FADREIN**, neuter: 1) fatherhood, Greek *patria*: Eph. III, 15; 2) plural, parents, Greek *goneis*: Cor. II, XII, 14; Col. III, 20; Tim. II, III, 2; ancestors, Greek *progonoi*: Tim. I, V, 4; Tim. II, I, 3.

**FADREINS**, feminine: family, lineage, Greek *patria*: Luc. II, 4.

**FAHAN** (Old Norse *fá*, Anglo-Saxon *fon*, Old Saxon and Old High German *fahan*, Old Frisian *fa*, English *fang*, Swedish *fånga, få*, Danish *fange, faae*, Dutch *vangen*, Modern High German *fahen, fangen*; Gr. II, 28; Gf. III, 386; Rchth. 723), conjugation I, *faifah, faifahun, fahans*: to seize, Greek *piazein*: Joan. VII, 44; VIII, 20.

**GA-FAHAN**, the same: to seize, Greek *piazein*: Joan. VII, 30, 32; X, 39; Cor. II, XI, 32; to apprehend, Greek *katalambanein*: Mc. IX, 18; Joan. XII, 35; Rom. IX, 30; Eph. III, 18; Phlpp. III, 12; Thess. I, V, 4; to lay hold of, Greek *epilambanesthai*: Luc. XX, 20, 26; to overtake, Greek *prolambanein*: Gal. VI, 1; *gafahanana tiuhan*, to capture, Greek *zōgrein*: Tim. II, II, 26; *gafahanana haban*, the same: Tim. II, II, 26, at this passage.

**GA-FAH**, neuter (?): a catch, Greek *agra*: Luc. V, 9.

**FAHEþS**, see under *Faihan*. **FAHJAN**, see under *Faihan*.

[Col. 1492] **FAþA** (cf. Old High German *fadam*, Anglo-Saxon *faeðem*, Old Frisian *fethm*, English *fathom*, Modern High German *faden*; Gf. III, 374, 450; Rchth. 736), feminine: hedge, Greek *phragmos*: Mc. XII, 1; Luc. XIV, 23; Eph. II, 14.

**FAþS** (*fads* Luc. VII, 6; cf. Anglo-Saxon *fadan*; Bopp 83; Gr. I, XLII [1st ed.]; III, 319; DM. 689; DRA. 754; Gf. III, 374; cf. Aschbach, *Geschichte der Westgothen*, p. 264), masculine (plural *fadeis*): lord, chief.

**BRUþ-FAþS**: bridegroom, Greek *nymphios*: Mc. II, 19, 20; Luc. V, 34, 35; bridal chamber, Greek *nymphōn*: Mth. IX, 15; Mc. II, 19; Luc. V, 34.

**HUNDA-FAþS**: centurion, Greek *hekatontarchos*: Mth. VIII, 5, 13; Luc. VII, 2, 6; Greek *kentouriōn*: Mc. XV, 39, 44, 45.

**þUSUNDI-FAþS**: commander, chiliarch, Greek *chiliarchos*: Mc. VI, 21; Joan. XVIII, 12.

**SYNAGOGA-FAþS**: ruler of the synagogue, Greek *archisynagōgos*: Mc. V, 22, 35, 36, 38.

**FAIAN**, see under *Feian*.

**FAIHAN** (Old Norse *feigenn, fagna*, Anglo-Saxon *fea, faegnian*, Old Saxon *fagan, faganon*, Old High German *gafehan, gafag, fagon*, English *fain*, Swedish *fägna*; Gr. II, 28, 44; Gf. III, 417), conjugation I, *fah, fehun, faihans*: to be fitting, to suit.

**BI-FAIHON**, conjugation II: to defraud, Greek *pleonektein*: Cor. II, VII, 2; XII, 17, 18; Thess. I, IV, 6.

**GA-FAIHON**, the same: Cor. II, II, 11, at this passage.

**BI-FAIHONS**, feminine: fraud, covetousness, Greek *pleonexia*: Cor. II, IX, 5.

**BI-FAIH**, neuter: the same: Cor. II, XII, 20, at this passage.

**FAHJAN** (DM. 24; Gf. III, 419), conjugation II: to adapt, fit.

[Col. 1493] **FULLA-FAHJAN**: 1) to satisfy, “to make sufficient,” Greek *hikanon poiein*: Mc. XV, 15; Skeir. VII, d; 2) to serve, Greek *latreuein*: Luc. IV, 8.

**FAHEþS** and **FAHEDS** (*faheids* Luc. II, 10; VIII, 13), feminine: joy, Greek *chara*: Mc. IV, 16; Luc. I, 14; II, 10; VIII, 13; X, 17; XV, 7, 10; Joan. III, 29; XV, 11; XVI, 21, 22, 24; XVII, 13; Rom. XIV, 17; XV, 13; Cor. II, II, 3; VII, 4, 13; VIII, 2; Gal. V, 22; Phlpp. I, 25; II, 2, 29; IV, 1; Col. I, 11; Thess. I, II, 19, 20; III, 9; Tim. II, I, 4.

**FAGINON**, conjugation II: to rejoice, with the dative, also with *fram, ana,* or *ïn*, Greek *chairein*: Mc. XIV, 11; Luc. I, 14; VI, 23; X, 20; XV, 5, 32; XIX, 6, 37; Joan. VIII, 56; XI, 15; XIV, 28; XVI, 20, 22; Rom. XII, 12, 15; Cor. I, XIII, 6; XVI, 17; Cor. II, II, 3; VI, 10; VII, 7, 9, 13, 16; XIII, 9, 11; Phlpp. I, 18; II, 28; III, 1; IV, 4, 10; Col. I, 24; Thess. I, III, 9; V, 16. *Fagino*, imperative: hail, Greek *chaire*: Luc. I, 28.

**MIþ-FAGINON** (or *faginon miþ*): to rejoice with, Greek *synchairein*: Luc. I, 58; XV, 6, 9; Cor. I, XIII, 6.

**FAGRS** (Old Norse *fagr*, Anglo-Saxon *faegr*, Old High German *fagar*, English *fair*, Swedish *fager*, Danish *favr*; Gf. III, 420), adjective: suitable, useful, good, Greek *euthetos*: Luc. XIV, 35.

**UN-FAGRS**: useless, ungrateful, Greek *acharistos*: Luc. VI, 35.

**GA-FAHRJAN**, conjugation II: to prepare, Greek *kataskeuazein*: Luc. I, 17.

**GA-FEHS** (Old Saxon *feh*), adjective: fitting, suitable.

**GA-FEHABA**, adverb: suitably, decently, Greek *euschēmonōs*: Thess. I, IV, 12.

**FAIHU** (*faiho* Mc. X, 33; Old Norse *fe*, Old High German *fihu*, Anglo-Saxon *feoh*, Old Saxon *fehu, fe*, Old Frisian *fia*, English *fee*, Swedish *fä*, Danish *fae*, Modern High German *vieh*; Greek *pōu* [uncertain], Latin *pecus, pecunia*; cf. *Faihan*; Bopp 81, 83; Gr. II, 28; Gf. III, 425, 428), neuter: possessions, wealth, Greek *chrēmata*: Mc. X, 23, 24; property, Greek *ktēmata*: Mc. X, 22; money, silver, Greek *argyrion*: Mc. XIV, 11.

**FILU-FAIHUS**, adjective: manifold, very various, Greek *polypoikilos*: Eph. III, 10, at this passage.

**FAIHU-GAIRNEI**, see under *Geiran*. **FAIHU-GEIRO**, see under *Geiran*. **FAIHU-þRAIHNS**, see under *þreihan*. **FAIHU-SKULA**, see under *Skulan*. **FAIHU-GAVAURKI**, see under *Vaurkjan*. **FAIHU-FRIKS**, see under *Friks*. **FAIHON**, see under *Faihan*.

**FAIR** (Old Norse, Anglo-Saxon *for-*, Old Saxon *far-*, Old High German *far-, fir-*, Swedish *för-*, Danish *for-*, Dutch and Modern High German *ver-*; Gf. III, 604, 605), inseparable preposition, corresponding to Germanic *ver-*, *ent-*, and occurring only in the following words: 1) with verbs: *fairainan, fairgreipan, fairhaitan, fairrinnan, fairvaurkjan, fairveitjan*; 2) with a participle: *unfairlaistiþs*; 3) with a noun: *fairveitl*.

**FAIRAN** (Old Norse *far, firin*, Anglo-Saxon *firen*, Old Saxon and Old High German *firina, fara*, Old Frisian *firne, ferne*, Modern High German *gefährde*; Gr. II, 56; DRA. 624; Gf. III, 575, 679; Schm. I, 550; Rchth. 743), conjugation I, *far, ferun, faurans*: to accuse.

**FAIRINS**, adjective: guilty, culpable.

**UN-FAIRINS**: blameless, Greek *amemptos*: Thess. I, III, 13; V, 23; unreprovable, Greek *anegklētos*: Col. I, 22.

**US-FAIRINS**, the same: blameless, Greek *amemptos*: Phlpp. III, 6.

**FAIRINA**, feminine: 1) reproach, Greek *momphē*: Col. III, 13; 2) accusation, Greek *aitia*: Mc. XV, 26; Joan. XVIII, 38; XIX, 6; 3) cause, reason, Greek *logos*: Mth. V, 32; accusation, Greek *aitia*: Tim. II, I, 12; Tit. I, 13.

**FAIRINON** (*Fairrinon* Gal. V, 15), conjugation II: to blame, Greek *mōmasthai*: Cor. II, VIII, 20; Gal. V, 15. *Fairinonds*, present participle: slandering, a slanderer, Greek *diabolos*: Tim. II, III, 3.

**UNGA-FAIRINONDS**, present participle: irreproachable, Greek *anegklētos*: Tit. I, 6; above reproach, Greek *anepilēptos*: Tim. I, III, 2.

**UNGA-FAIRINOþS**, past participle: the same, irreproachable, Greek *anegklētos*: Tim. I, III, 10; Tit. I, 7; above reproach, Greek *anepilēptos*: Tim. I, V, 7; VI, 14.

**UN-FAIRINODABA**, adverb: blamelessly, Greek *amemptōs*: Thess. I, II, 10.

**FERJA**, masculine: spy, Greek *enkatheto*: Luc. XX, 20.

**GA-FAURDS**, feminine: council, sanhedrin, Greek *synedrion*: Mc. XIV, 55; XV, 1.

**FAIRGUNI** (Old Norse *fiörgyn*, Anglo-Saxon *firgen*; Gr. II, 175; DM. 116), neuter: mountain, Greek *oros*: Mth. VIII, 1; Mc. III, 13; V, 5, 11; IX, 2; XI, 1, 23; Luc. III, 5, 19, 29, 37; IV, 5, 29; VI, 12; VIII, 32; IX, 28, 37; Joan. VI, 3, 15; Cor. I, XIII, 2; Gal. IV, 24.

**FAUR** and **FAURA** (Old Norse *fyri, for*, Anglo-Saxon *fore, for*, Old Saxon *far, for, fora, furi*, Old Frisian *fara, fore, fori, for*, Old High German *fora, furi*, English *before*, Swedish *för*, Danish *for*, Modern High German *fur, vor*; Greek *pro*, Latin *pro, prae*; Gr. II, 726; Gf. III, 612; Alth., *Präpositionen*, 130 ff.; Rchth. 728, 751), prepositions. The former indicates a local relation, “before”; a temporal relation, “before”; and a moral relation, “for.” The latter indicates only a local and a moral relation.

**I. Faur.**

A. A preposition governing the accusative, meaning:

a) Locally, “at,” “beside,” where one object precedes another, Greek *para* with accusative: Mc. I, 16, *warbonds faur marein*, “casting beside the sea”; likewise after *galeiþan*, Mc. II, 13; *gadriusan*, IV, 4; Luc. VIII, 5; *sitan*, Mc. X, 46; Luc. XVIII, 35. Hence *sa faur marein*, “one by the sea,” for Greek *paralios*, “coastal”: Luc. VI, 17. Also Mc. VIII, 6, *atlagidedun faur þo managein*, “they set [them] before the crowd,” Greek *parethēkan tō ochlō*. Once it occurs in Mc. XIV, 68, *galaiþ faur gard*, “he went out before the courtyard,” Greek *exēlthen eis to proaulion*.

b) Temporally, “before,” Greek *pro*: *faur mel*, Mth. VIII, 29; Cor. I, IV, 5; Skeir. VIII, a; *faur mela aiveina*, “before eternal times,” Tim. II, I, 9; Tit. I, 2; *faur jera fidvortaihun*, “fourteen years before,” Cor. II, XII, 2; *faur gaskaft fairwaus*, “before the creation of the world,” Joan. XVII, 24; *faur gasatein fairwaus*, “before the foundation of the world,” Eph. I, 4; *faur hanins hruk*, “before the cock crowed,” Mth. XXVI, 75; *faur þata*, Skeir. III, a. Thus Thess. I, IV, 15, *ni bisnivam faur þans anaslepandans*, “we shall not precede those who have fallen asleep,” Greek *ou mē phthasōmen tous koimēthentas*.

c) Metaphorically, after verbs and expressions of every kind that indicate that an action, suffering, speech, and so forth is done for someone, whether to denote purpose, cause, or substitution: “for,” Greek *hyper* with genitive: Mc. IX, 40 (*saei nist viþra ïzvis, faur ïzvis ïst*, “he who is not against you is for you”); X, 45 (*giban saivala faur managans saun*, “to give his life as a ransom for many”); Luc. IX, 50; Joan. X, 11, 15; XIII, 37, 38; XV, 13; XVIII, 14; Rom. VIII, 15; IX, 3; XIV, 15; Cor. I, IV, 6; V, 7; XV, 3, 29; Cor. II, I, 6, 11; V, 15, 20, 21; VII, 7, 8, 12; VIII, 16, 24; IX, 14; XII, 5, 10, 15; XIII, 8; Gal. I, 4; II, 20; Eph. III, 10; V, 2, 25; VI, 20; Phlpp. I, 29; IV, 10; Col. I, 7, 9, 24; Thess. I, V, 10; Tim. I, II, 6; Philem. 13; Skeir. I, a; II, a; VIII, c, d.

B. Adverb: Mc. VIII, 6, *atlagjan faur*, “to set before,” Greek *paratithenai*; Luc. XIX, 4, *biþragjan faur*, “to run ahead,” Greek *protrechein*.

C. In compounds: a) with verbs: *faurbiudan, faurgaggan, faurdammjan, faurqiþan, faurlagjan, faurmuljan, faurrinnan, faursigljan, faursnivan, faurvalvjan, faurvaipjan*; double compounds: *faurbigaggan, faurbiþragjan, faurbisnivan*; b) with nouns: *faurbauhts, faurhah, faurlageins, faurstasseis*; c) with an adjective: *unfaurveis*.

**II. Faura.**

A. A preposition governing the dative, meaning:

a) Locally, “before,” Greek *emprosthen*: Mth. VI, 2 (*ni haurnjais faura þus*, “do not sound a trumpet before yourself”); XI, 10 (*aggilus gamanveiþ vig þeinana faura þus*, “my messenger shall prepare your way before you”); XXVI, 70; XXVII, 11; Mc. I, 2; Luc. V, 29; XIX, 27; Joan. X, 4; Cor. II, V, 10; Gal. II, 14; Thess. I, III, 9, 13; Neh. V, 15; “before, in the presence of,” Greek *enōpion*: Luc. XIV, 10; “in the sight of,” Greek *katenōpion*: Col. I, 22; “before [the] face,” Greek *pro prosōpou*: Mth. XI, 10; Mc. I, 2; Luc. IX, 52. This expression is also rendered by *faura andvairþja*: Luc. I, 76; VII, 27; X, 1; Neh. V, 15; and it is also used for Greek *enantion*, “opposite, before”: Mc. II, 12. Moreover *faura* is used for Greek *kata* with accusative: Gal. III, 1; Greek *para* with accusative: Mc. V, 21; Luc. VII, 38; VIII, 4, 37; XVII, 16; and Greek *para* with dative: Luc. IX, 47. Hence Luc. II, 22, *atsatjan faura fraujin*, “to present before the Lord,” Greek *paristanai tō kyriō*; Rom. XIV, 10, *gasatjan faura stauastola*, “to stand before the judgment seat,” Greek *paristanai tō bēmati*. Compare Cor. I, XV, 28, *gakunnan sik faura ainamma*, “to subject oneself to someone,” Greek *hypotassesthai tini*; Tim. I, II, 12, *fraujinon faura vaira*, “to exercise authority before a man,” Greek *authentein andros*. This may also be translated, instead of “before, in the presence of a man,” as “over, more than a man,” so that at least Col. I, 17, *ïs ïst faura allaim*, “he is before all things,” Greek *pro*, is to be explained.

b) Metaphorically, “before,” “away from,” after verbs of administering, fleeing, hiding, preserving, and the like, Greek *apo*: Mth. VII, 15, *atsaiwiþ faura liugnapraufetum*, “beware of false prophets”; Mc. XII, 38; XIV, 52; Luc. III, 7; IX, 45; X, 21; XIX, 42; XX, 46; Joan. X, 5; XII, 36; Greek *ek*, “from”: Joan. XVII, 15; “because of, on account of,” Greek *apo*: Luc. XIX, 5, *ni mahta ïesu gasaiwan faura managein*, “he could not see Jesus because of the crowd”; Greek *dia* with accusative: Joan. XII, 42, *faura fareisaium ni andhaihaitun*, “because of the Pharisees they did not confess.” For “before” indicating superiority, see above, A(a).

B. Adverb: 1) “before,” Greek *emprosthen*: Phlpp. III, 14; 2) “previously,” Greek *proteron*: Tim. I, I, 13; Skeir. I, c; 3) for Greek *pro-* in compounds, as *faura dustodjan*, “to begin beforehand,” Greek *proenarchesthai*: Cor. II, VIII, 6; *faura fravaurkjan*, “to sin beforehand,” Greek *prohamartanein*: XII, 21; 4) to indicate the perfect, as *faura haitans*, “called,” Greek *keklēmenos*: Luc. XIV, 24; also redundantly, as Tim. I, I, 18, *faura faursnivan*.

C. In compounds: a) with verbs: *fauragaggan, fauraqiþan, fauraqiman, fauramanvjan, faurameljan, faurarahnjan, faurastandan, fauravenjan, fauravisan*; double compounds: *fauragahaitan, fauragahugjan, fauragaleikan, fauragamanvjan, fauragameljan, fauragasandjan, fauragasatjan, fauragateihan* (*fauradustodjan*); b) with nouns: *fauragaggi, fauragaggja, fauragagga, fauradauri, faurahah, fauramaþleis, fauramaþli, fauratani, faurafilli*.

**FAURþIS** (cf. Gr. II, 730 and Gf. III, 620), adverb: first, Greek *prōton*: Mth. V, 24; Mc. III, 27; VII, 27; IX, 11, 12; Luc. VI, 42; IX, 59, 61; XIV, 31; XVII, 25; Eph. IV, 9; Thess. I, IV, 16; Tim. I, V, 4; Tim. II, I, 5; previously, Greek *proteron*: Joan. VI, 62; VII, 51; IX, 8; Cor. II, I, 15; Skeir. I, d; V, b; formerly, Greek *pote*: Joan. IX, 7.

**FULGINS**, adjective: hidden, Greek *kryptos*: Mth. X, 26; Mc. IV, 22; Luc. VIII, 17.

**FILL** (Old Norse *fell, felldr*, Old High German *fel*, Anglo-Saxon, English, Old High German *fell*, Dutch *vell*; Latin *pellis*; Gr. II, 57; III, 408; Gf. III, 469), neuter: skin, hide.

**FILM** (cf. Anglo-Saxon *film*, Old Frisian *filmene*): skin.

**US-FILMS**, adjective, always occurring in the weak form *usfilma*: properly, shaggy-haired; terrified, astonished. *Usfilma vairþan*, to be alarmed, struck with astonishment, Greek *plēttesthai*: Mc. I, 22; to be afraid, Greek *phobeisthai*: Luc. IX, 43.

[Col. 1499] **US-FILMEI**, feminine: fear, terror, Greek *ekstasis*: Mc. XVI, 8; Luc. V, 26.

**FILU** (Old Norse *fiöl*, Anglo-Saxon *fela*, Old Saxon and Old High German *filu*, Old Frisian *fel*, Dutch *veel*, Modern High German *viel*; Greek *polys*; Gr. III, 613; Gf. III, 471; Rchth. 731), adverb: 1) used adjectivally, much, many, very great, Greek *polys*: Mth. IX, 14; Mc. III, 7, 8, 12; V, 10, 21, 23, 24, 43; IX, 14; Luc. V, 6; VII, 11, 47; IX, 37; Joan. XII, 9, 12; XIV, 30; Cor. I, XVI, 12, 19; Cor. II, VIII, 15; Tim. I, III, 8; 2) exceedingly, Greek *lian*: Mth. VIII, 28; XXVII, 14; Mc. XVI, 2; Tim. II, IV, 15; very, Greek *sphodra*: Luc. XVIII, 23; further, Greek *epi pleion*: Tim. II, II, 16; 3) much, with a comparative, Greek *pollō*: Mc. X, 49; Cor. I, XII, 22; Skeir. VII, d; 4) in the expressions *filu gabaurjaba*, “most gladly,” Greek *hēdista*: Cor. II, XII, 9; *filu manags*, very numerous, Greek *pampolys*: Mc. VIII, 1; *ufar filu*, especially, exceedingly, Greek *hyperlian*: Cor. II, XII, 11; *ufar filu visan*, to abound exceedingly, Greek *perisseuein*: Cor. II, I, 5; *und filu*, much, with a comparative, Greek *pollō*: Luc. XVIII, 39; Cor. II, III, 9; Phlpp. I, 23; *sva filu*, so much, Greek *tosouto*: Luc. XV, 19; Joan. XII, 37; Gal. III, 4; *sva filu sve*, as much as, how much, Greek *hosos*: Mc. IX, 13; X, 21; Luc. VIII, 39; IX, 10; Joan. VI, 11; XVI, 13; Rom. XV, 4; Skeir. VII, c; *wan filu*, how much? Greek *posos*: Mth. VI, 23; XXVII, 13; Mc. XV, 4; Luc. XV, 17; XVI, 5; Greek *hosos*: Mc. III, 8; V, 19, 20; VII, 36; Luc. IV, 23; VIII, 39; with a comparative, Greek *posō*: Rom. XI, 24; *wan filu mais*, Greek *hosos*: Tim. II, I, 18; see at this passage; *und wan filu*, how much, with a comparative, Greek *posō*: Mth. X, 25.

**FILAUS**, adverb: much, with a comparative, Greek *poly*: Cor. II, VIII, 22; more abundantly, Greek *perissoterōs*: Cor. II, VII, 13; Skeir. III, d; V, c; VII, c.

**FILU-DEISEI**, see under *Deis*. **FILU-GALAUBS**, see under *Liuban*. **FILU-VAURDEI**, see under *Vaurd*. **FILU-FAIHUS**, see under *Faihu*.

**FILUSNA**, feminine: multitude, crowd, Greek *plēthos*: Neh. V, 18; Skeir. VII, b (Joan. VI, 10, at this passage), c; excess, Greek *hyperbolē*: Cor. II, XII, 7. *Du filusnai*, further, Greek *epi pleion*: Tim. II, III, 9.

**FIM**, the same as *Fimf*.

**FIMF** (*fif* Cor. I, XV, 6; *fim* Luc. XVI, 6; Old Norse *fimm*, Anglo-Saxon, Old Saxon, Old Frisian *fif*, Old High German *finf*, English *five*, Swedish and Danish *fem*, Dutch *vyf*, Modern High German *fünf*; Greek *peempe*, Latin *quinque*; Bopp 80, 83; Gr. **FIMF-TIGJUS** (*fimtigjus* Luc. XVI, 6), masculine plural: fifty, Greek *pentēkonta*: Luc. VII, 41; IX, 14; XVI, 6; Joan. VIII, 57.

**FIMF-HUNDA**, see under *Hund*. **FIMF-TAIHUN**, see under *Taihun*.

**FINþAN** (Old Norse and Swedish *finna*, Anglo-Saxon, Old Saxon, Old High German *findan*, Old Frisian *finda*, English *find*, Danish *finde*, Dutch *vinden*, Modern High German *finden*; Greek *pynthanesthai*; Gr. II, 35; Gf. III, 529; Rchth. 740), conjugation I, *fanþ, funþun, funþans*: to know, learn, recognize, Greek *gignōskein*: Mc. V, 43; XV, 45; Luc. IX, 11; Joan. XII, 9; Rom. X, 19.

Greek *ichthys*; Gr. III, 363; Gf. III, 708; Rchth. 743), masculine: fish, Greek *ichthys*: Luc. V, 6, 9; IX, 13, 16; Skeir. VII, b, c; small fish, Greek *ichthydion*:

**FITAN** (compare Old Norse *fitna*; Latin *fetare* and *futere*; [Col. 1500] Gr. II, 45; Gf. III, 374, 738), class-I verb (?), *fat, fetun, fitans*, to beget, to travail, **ὠδίνειν**: Gal. IV, 19, 27.

**FIF**, the same as **FIMF**.

\* **FLAIHTAN** (Old High German *flehtan*, Modern High German *flechten*; Greek **πλέκειν**, “to plait,” Latin *plectere*; Gf. III, 769), class-I verb, *flaht, flauhtun, flauhtans*, to twist.

**FLAHTA** or **FLAHTO**, feminine, a braid, plait, **πλέγμα**: 1 Tim. II, 9.

**FLAUTAN** (compare Old English *flitan*, English *flite*, *flout*), class-I verb (?), *faiflaut, faiflautun, flautans*, to boast, **περπερεύεσθαι**: 1 Cor. XIII, 4; present participle *flautands*, boasting, vainglorious, **κενόδοξος**: Gal. V, 26.

**FLEKAN** (compare Greek **πεπληγέναι**, Latin *plangere*; Gr. III, 755, 758), class-I verb, *faiflok, faiflokun, flekans*, to mourn, beat the breast, **κόπτεσθαι**: Luke VIII, 52.

**FLODUS** (Old Norse *fliot*, Old English *fleod*, Old Frisian *flod, flet*, Old Saxon, Swedish, Danish *flod*, Old High German *flot*, English *flood*, Dutch *vloed*, Modern High German *Fluth*; Latin *fluere*, *fluctus*; Gr. II, 235; III, 383; Gf. III, 740; Rchth. 746), feminine, stream, river, **ποταμός**: Luke VI, 49.

**FUGLS** (Old Norse *fugl*, Old English and Old Frisian *fugel*, Old Saxon *fugal*, Old High German *fogal*, English *fowl*, Swedish *fogel*, Danish *fugl*, Dutch and Modern High German *Vogel*; compare Latin *volare*; Gr. **FULA** (Old Norse *foli*, Old English *fole*, Old High German *folo*, Old Frisian *folla*, English *foal*, Swedish and Danish *fole*, Dutch *veulen*, Modern High German *Füllen*; Greek **πῶλος**, Latin *pullus*; Gr. III, 325; Gf. III, 476; Rchth. 749), masculine, colt, **πῶλος**: Mark XI, 2, 4, 5, 7; Luke XIX, 30, 33, 35; John XII, 15.

**FULHSNI**, see under **Filhan**.

**FULLS** (Old Norse *fullr*, Old Saxon *ful*, Old Frisian *ful, fol*, Old English and English, Swedish *full*, Danish *fuld*, Old High German *fol*, Dutch *vol*, Modern High German *voll*; Greek **πλέος**, Latin *plenus*; Bopp 80, 83; Gr. II, 57; Gf. III, 477; Rchth. 769), adjective:

1. full, **πλήρης**: Mark VIII, 19; Luke IV, 1; V, 12; *Skeir.* VII, c; *spyreidans fullai gabruko*, “baskets full of fragments,” **σπυρίδων πληρώματα κλασμάτων**: Mark VIII, 20; *banjo fulls*, see under **Banja**; *fulls vairþan*, “to become full,” **πίμπλασθαι**: Luke IV, 28; V, 26; VI, 11; **πληροῦσθαι**, “to be filled”: John XII, 3.
2. perfect, **τέλειος**: Eph. IV, 13.
3. universal, catholic: *Calendarium Gothicum*.

**UFAR-FULLS**, superabundant, filled beyond measure, **πεπλησμένος**: Luke VI, 38.

**FULLJAN**, class-II verb, to fill up, fill, **πιμπλάναι**: Matt. XXVII, 48; **πληροῦν**, “to fill”: Rom. XV, 13; 2 Thess. I, 11.

**GA-FULLJAN**, the same, **πιμπλάναι**: Luke I, 15; V, 7; **γεμίζειν**, “to fill”: Mark XV, 36; John VI, 13.

**US-FULLJAN**:

1. to fill up, fulfil, **πληροῦν**: Luke III, 5; 2 Cor. VII, 4.
2. to fill, **πληροῦν**: Matt. V, 17; Luke I, 20; John VII, 8; XVII, 12, 13; Rom. VIII, 4; XIII, 8; Gal. V, 14; Col. I, 25; IV, 17; **ἀναπληροῦν**, “to supply, complete”: Gal. VI, 2; **πληροφορεῖν**, “to accomplish fully”: 2 Tim. IV, 5; **ἀνακεφαλαιοῦν**, “to sum up”: Rom. XIII, 9; likewise *aftra usfulljan*, the same: Eph. I, 10.
3. to complete, **πληροῦν**: John XV, 11; XVI, 24; 2 Cor. X, 6; Phil. II, 2; **ἀναπληροῦν**: 1 Thess. II, 16.
4. to fulfil, **πληροῦν**: Luke I, 23; VII, 1; IX, 31; Eph. I, 23; **τελεῖν**, “to finish”: Matt. XI, 1; **τελειοῦν**, “to bring to completion”: Neh. VI, 16.
5. to supply, **ἀναπληροῦν**: 1 Cor. XVI, 17; Phil. II, 30; Col. I, 24; **προσαναπληροῦν**, “to supply in addition”: 2 Cor. IX, 12; XI, 9.

**UFAR-FULLJAN**:

1. to fill beyond measure, **ὑπερπερισσεύειν**: 2 Cor. VII, 4.
2. to abound exceedingly, **περισσεύειν**: 1 Cor. XV, 58.

**FULLNAN** (*fulnan*, Luke II, 21), class-III verb, to be filled, **πληροῦσθαι**: Luke II, 40; Eph. III, 19; V, 18; Col. I, 9.

**GA-FULLNAN**, the same, **πίμπλασθαι**: Luke I, 41, 67; **συμπληροῦσθαι**, “to be fulfilled together”: Luke VIII, 23; **γεμίζεσθαι**, “to be filled”: Mark IV, 37.

**US-FULLNAN**, the same, **πληροῦσθαι**: Matt. VIII, 17; XXVII, 9; Mark I, 15; XIV, 49; XV, 28; Luke IV, 21; John III, 29; XII, 38; XV, 25; XVIII, 8, 32; 2 Tim. I, 4; [Col. 1501] **συμπληροῦσθαι**: Luke IX, 51; **πίμπλασθαι**: Luke I, 23, 57; II, 6, 21, 22; **γεμίζεσθαι**: Luke XIV, 23.

**US-FULLEINS**, feminine, fullness, fulfilment, **πλήρωμα**: Rom. XIII, 10; Gal. IV, 4; Eph. I, 10.

**UFAR-FULLEI**, feminine, abundance, surplus, **περίσσευμα**: Luke VI, 45.

**FULLIþ**, neuter (?), full moon: Col. II, 16; see the note on that passage.

**FULLEIþS**, feminine, abundance, fullness; *fulleiþs kaurnis*, “an abundance of grain,” **πλήρης σῖτος**: Mark IV, 28.

**FULLO**, feminine, fullness, fulfilment, completion, **πλήρωμα**: Matt. IX, 16; Mark II, 21; Rom. XI, 12, 25; 1 Cor. X, 26, 28; Eph. I, 23; III, 19; Col. I, 19.

**FULLA-TOJIS**, see under **Taujan**.

**FULLA-VEISJAN**, see under **Veis**.  
**FULLA-FAHJAN**, see under **Fahjan**.

**FULS** (Old Norse *full*, Old English, Old High German, Old Frisian, Swedish *ful*, English *foul*, Modern High German *faul*; Greek **φαῦλος**; Gf. III, 494; Rchth. 770), adjective, corrupt, putrid; *fuls visan*, “to stink,” **ὄζειν**: John XI, 39.

**FUNISKS**, see under **Fon**.

**FRA** (Old Saxon, Swedish, Danish, Old High German *fra*, Old English *frae*, Modern High German *ver...*; compare **Fair**; Bopp 82; Gr. III, 731; Gf. III, 604), inseparable preposition, corresponding to Modern High German *ver-*; it occurs in compounds:

1. with verbs: *frabugjan, fragiban, fragildan, fradailjan, fraqiþan, fraqiman, fragistjan, fraqistnan, frahinþan, fraïtan, fraatjan, frakunnan, fraletan, fraliusan, fralusnan, franiman, frarinnan, fraslindan, fravairþan, fravairpan, fravaurkjan, fravilvan, fravisan, fraveitan, fravrikan, fravrohjan*; and in the double compound *miþfrahinþan*.
2. with nouns: *fragifts, fraqisteins, fralet, fralusts, fravaurhts, fravardeins, fraveit*.
3. with adjectives: *fralets, fravaurhts*.

**FRAGAN**, see under 2 Cor. XIII, 5.

**FRAþJAN** (Old Norse *fräda, frodr*, Old English, Old Saxon, Old Frisian *frod*, Old High German *frot*, Dutch *vroed*; Greek **φράζεσθαι**; Gr. II, 10; Gf. III, 819; IV, 695; Rchth. 767), class-I verb, *froþ, froþun, froþans*:

1. to think, **φρονεῖν**: Mark VIII, 33; Rom. XII, 3, 16; XV, 5; 1 Cor. IV, 6; XIII, 11; 2 Cor. XIII, 11; Phil. II, 5; III, 19; IV, 2, 10; Col. III, 2; *Skeir.* VIII, c. *Mais fraþjan*, “to think more highly,” **ὑπερφρονεῖν**: Rom. XII, 3. *Vaila fraþjan*, “to think soberly,” **σωφρονεῖν**: Rom. XII, 3.
2. to understand, **συνιέναι**: Mark IV, 12; VII, 14; VIII, 21; Luke II, 50; VIII, 10; XVIII, 34; 2 Cor. X, 12; Eph. V, 17; Ps. LIII, 2; *Skeir.* II, b; **γιγνώσκειν**, “to know”: Mark VIII, 17; XII, 12; Luke XX, 19; John VIII, 27; X, 6; Rom. VII, 15; **ἐπιγιγνώσκειν**, “to recognize”: Luke I, 22; **νοεῖν**, “to perceive”: Mark VII, 18; VIII, 17; John XII, 40; Eph. III, 4, 20; 1 Tim. I, 7; 2 Tim. II, 7; **αἰσθάνεσθαι**, “to perceive”: Luke IX, 45. *Ni fraþjan*, “not to understand, to be ignorant,” **ἀγνοεῖν**: Mark IX, 32; Luke IX, 45.
3. to be of sound mind, **σωφρονεῖν**: Mark V, 15; Luke VIII, 35.

**UN-FRAþJANDS**, present participle, unintelligent, imprudent, **ἀσύνετος**: Rom. X, 19.

**FULLA-FRAþJAN**, to be of sound mind, **σωφρονεῖν**: 2 Cor. V, 13.

**FRAþI**, neuter, understanding, intelligence, **νόημα**: 2 Cor. III, 14; IV, 4; X, 5; XI, 3; **νοῦς**, “mind”: Rom. XI, 34; XII, 2; Eph. IV, 23; Col. II, 18; **σύνεσις**, “understanding”: Mark XII, 33; 2 Tim. II, 7; **φρόνημα**, “mindset”: Rom. VIII, 6, 7; **φρήν**, “mind”: 1 Cor. XIV, 20.

**GRINDA-FRAþJIS**, adjective, faint-hearted, **ὀλιγόψυχος**: 1 Thess. V, 14.

**SAMA-FRAþJIS**, of one mind, “thinking the one [same thing],” **τὸ ἓν (αὐτὸ) φρονῶν**: Phil. II, 2.

**GA-FRAþJEI**, feminine, wisdom, sobriety, **σωφροσύνη**: 1 Tim. II, 15.

**US-FRAþVJAN** (*usfratvjan*), class-II verb, to act wisely, **σοφίζειν**: 2 Tim. III, 15; see the note on that passage.

**FROþS**, adjective; comparative *frodoza*, prudent, **φρόνιμος**: Matt. VII, 24; Luke XVI, 8; Rom. XI, 25; [Col. 1502] 1 Cor. IV, 10; 2 Cor. XI, 19; **συνετός**, “understanding”: Luke X, 21; 1 Cor. I, 19; **σοφός**, “wise”: 1 Tim. I, 17; **σώφρων**, “self-controlled”: 1 Tim. III, 2.

**FRODABA**, adverb, prudently, **φρονίμως**: Luke XVI, 8; **νουνεχῶς**, “sensibly”: Mark XII, 3.

**UNFROþS**, imprudent, foolish, **ἄφρων**: 2 Cor. XI, 16; Eph. V, 17; **ἀνόητος**: Gal. III, 1, 3.

**FRODEI**, feminine, prudence, understanding, **φρόνησις**: Luke I, 17; Eph. I, 8; **σύνεσις**: Luke II, 47; 1 Cor. I, 19; Eph. III, 4; Col. I, 9 (III, 16); **σοφία**, “wisdom”: Luke II, 52; *Skeir.* I, d.

**UN-FRODEI**, folly, imprudence, **ἀφροσύνη**: 2 Cor. XI, 1, 17, 21; **ἄνοια**: Luke VI, 11.

**FRAIHNAN** (Old Norse *fregna*, Old English *fregnan*, Old Saxon *fragon*, Old High German *fragen*, Old Frisian *fregia*, Swedish *fråga*, Dutch *vragen*, Modern High German *fragen*; Gr. II, 28; Gf. III, 811; Rchth. 759), anomalous verb, *frah, frehun, fraihans*, to ask, **ἐπερωτᾶν**: Matt. XXVII, 11; Mark V, 9; VII, 5, 17; VIII, 5, 23, 27; IX, 11, 16, 21, 28, 32, 33; X, 2, 10; XI, 29; XII, 18, 28, 34; XIV, 61; XV, 2, 4, 44; Luke II, 46; III, 10, 14; VI, 9; VIII, 9, 30; IX, 18; XVII, 20; XVIII, 18, 40; XX, 21, 27, 40; John XVIII, 7, 19, 21; **ἐρωτᾶν**: Mark IV, 10; Luke IX, 45; XIX, 31; XX, 3; John IX, 2, 15, 19, 21, 23; XVI, 5, 19, 23, 30; **πυνθάνεσθαι**, “to inquire”: Luke XV, 26; XVIII, 36; John XIII, 24.

**GA-FRAIHNAN**:

1. to ask, **ἐπερωτᾶν**: Rom. X, 20.
2. to inquire, hear, **ἀκούειν**: Mark II, 1.

**FRAISAN** (Old Norse *freista*, Old English *frasian*, Old High German *fresa*, Old Saxon *fresa, freson*, Old Frisian *frasa, fres*, Swedish *fresta*, Danish *friste*; Greek **πειράζειν**; Gf. III, 830; Rchth. 758), class-I verb, *faifrais, faifraisun, fraisans*, to test, tempt, **πειράζειν**: Mark I, 13; VIII, 11; X, 2; XII, 15; Luke IV, 2; XX, 23; John VI, 6; 1 Cor. VII, 5; 2 Cor. XIII, 5; Gal. VI, 1; 1 Thess. III, 5; **ἐκπειράζειν**, “to put to the test”: Luke IV, 12; X, 25.

**US-FRAISAN**, the same, **πειράζειν**: 1 Thess. III, 5.

**FRAISTUBNI** (*fraistobni*, Luke IV, 13), feminine, temptation, testing, **πειρασμός**: Matt. VI, 13; Luke IV, 13; VIII, 13; Gal. IV, 14; 1 Tim. VI, 9.

**FRAIV** (Old Norse *frio, friof*, Swedish *frö*, Danish *fro*; Gr. III, 413; Gf. III, 819), neuter, seed, offspring, **σπέρμα**: Mark IV, 3, 31; XII, 20; Luke I, 55; VIII, 5, 11; XX, 28; John VII, 42; VIII, 33, 37; Rom. IX, 7, 29; 2 Cor. IX, 10; XI, 22; Gal. III, 29; 2 Tim. II, 7; **σπόρος**, “seed sown”: Mark IV, 26, 27.

**FRAM** (Old Norse *fra*, Old English *fram, from*, Old Saxon and Old High German *fram*, English *from*, Swedish *fram, från*, Danish *frem, fra*; Greek **παρά**; Gr. II, 55; Gf. III, 638; Alth. *Präp.* 241), preposition governing the dative. It is used locally to mean “from, away from” (in opposition to *ad*, “to”), temporally “from, since,” and metaphorically to indicate the departure, origin, root, and so forth, of something from someone.

I. **Preposition with the dative** (for Luke VIII, 49, where a genitive seems to be used, must be understood elliptically; see below).

1. Locally, “from,” **ἀπό**:

   a. Mark XIII, 27, *fram andjam airþos und andi himinis*, “from the ends of the earth to the end of heaven”; John XII, 21, *filippus sa fram beþsaeida*, “Philip, the one from Bethsaida.”

   b. Especially after verbs of motion, such as *qiman*, “to come”: Matt. VIII, 11; Mark I, 9; V, 35; XIV, 43 (**παρά** with the genitive); Gal. II, 12; 1 Thess. III, 6; *laistjan*, “to follow”: Matt. XXVII, 55; *gavandjan sik*, “to return”: Luke IV, 1; **παρά** with the genitive: *urrinnan*, “to go forth,” John VIII, 42 (**ἐκ**, “out of”); XV, 26 (**ἀπό**); XVI, 27, 30 (**ἀπό**); XVII, 8; *usgaggan*, “to go out”: John XVI, 28. Here also belongs the elliptical expression Luke VIII, 49: *gaggiþ sums manne fram þis fauramaþleis synagogeis*, “someone has come from the ruler of the synagogue.” Also:

   c. after transitive verbs, such as *ïnsandjan*, “to send”: John XV, 26; *tiuhan*, “to lead”: John XVIII, 28 (**ἀπό**).

2. Temporally, “from, since,” **ἀπό**: Matt. IX, 22, *fram þizai weilai*, “from that hour”; Col. I, 9, *fram þamma daga*, “from that day”; Neh. V, 14; Matt. XI, 12, *fram þaim dagam*, “from those days”; Neh. V, 14, *fram jera .k.*, “from the year 20”; 2 Cor. IX, 2, *fram fairnin jera*, “since last year”; John IX, 32, *fram aiva*, “from eternity”; Eph. III, 9, “from the ages”; Col. I, 26; John XIX, 12, *fram þamma*, “from then” (**ἐκ**); Luke VII, 45, *fram þammei*, “since”; John XIII, 19, *fram himma*, “from now” (**ἀπ’ ἄρτι**); XIV, 7; 2 Cor. V, 16, *fram þamma nu*, “from now on”; Luke I, 48, *fram himma nu*, “from now on”; V, 10; John XV, 27, *fram fruma*, “from the beginning”; XVI, 4 (**ἐκ**); John VIII, 44, *fram* [Col. 1503] *frumistja*, “from the first beginning”; Luke I, 2, *fram frumistin*, “from the beginning”; Mark XIII, 19, *fram anastodeinai*, “from the creation”; Luke I, 3, **ἄνωθεν**, “from above/from the beginning” (this passage should be added under *anastodeins*); *Skeir.* I, b; Luke I, 70, *fram anastodeinai aivis*, “from the beginning of the age”; Luke II, 36, *fram magaþein*, “from her virginity.”

3. In a metaphorical sense:

   a. Where the noun has subjective force:

   aa. “from,” **ἀπό**: Rom. XIII, 1, *nist valdufni alja fram guþa*, “there is no authority except from God.” In the same way, 2 Tim. I, 3, *guþa skalkino fram fadreinam*, “God, whom I serve from [my] forefathers,” should be explained. John VIII, 42, *fram sis silbin*, “from himself, by his own impulse,” *qiman*, “to come”; likewise John VII, 17 and 18, *rodjan fram sis silbin*, “to speak from oneself.” 2 Cor. VI, 5, *afhaims visan fram guþa*, “to be from God”; Gal. III, 2, *viljan vitan*, “I wish to know”; 1 Tim. III, 7, *veitvodiþa haban*, “to have testimony”; 1 Cor. IV, 5, *hazeins vairþiþ*, “praise shall come.” Likewise in the formula *ansts ïzvis jah gavairþi fram guþa*, “grace to you and peace from God”: 2 Cor. I, 2; Gal. I, 3; Eph. I, 2; VI, 23; 2 Thess. I, 2; 2 Tim. I, 2; Tit. I, 4. After passives: Matt. XI, 19, *usvaurhta gadomida varþ handugei fram barnam seinaim*, “wisdom was justified by her children”; Mark VIII, 31; Luke VII, 35; IX, 22; XVII, 25; 2 Cor. VII, 13; compare the end of Phil. I, 28.

   bb. In this latter use, formally for Greek **ὑπό**, “by”: Matt. VI, 2; VIII, 24; XI, 7; Mark I, 5, 9, 13; II, 3; XVI, 11; Luke I, 26; II, 18, 21, 26; III, 7, 19; IV, 2, 15; V, 15; VI, 18; VII, 24, 30; VIII, 29, 43; IX, 7; X, 22; XVI, 22; XVII, 20; Rom. XIII, 1, second occurrence; 1 Cor. IV, 3; VII, 25; XIV, 24; 2 Cor. I, 4; II, 11; III, 2, 3; V, 4, 8, 19, 20; XII, 11; Gal. IV, 9; Eph. II, 11; Phil. I, 28; III, 12; Col. II, 18; *Skeir.* I, b; IV, d; VI, c. Matt. XXVII, 9, *þatei garahnidedun fram sunum ïsraelis*, “that which they reckoned from the sons of Israel,” should also be explained in the passive sense. 2 Cor. II, 6, *andabeit þata fram managizam*, “this punishment by the many,” namely, imposed by them. A passive sense likewise appears in 2 Cor. I, 16, *gasandjan sik*, “to be conducted”; XI, 24, *slahins niman*, “to be beaten”; Mark V, 26, *gaþulan*, “to suffer”; 1 Thess. II, 14, *vinnan*, “to suffer.”

   cc. **ἐκ**, “from, out of”: John VII, 17, *laiseins ïst fram guþa*, “the teaching is from God”; 22, *bimait ïst fram mose*, “circumcision is from Moses”; 1 Cor. VII, 7, *giba haban*, “to have a gift”; John VI, 65, *atgiban visan*, “to be granted.”

   dd. **παρά** with the genitive: after *visan*, “to be,” John VI, 46; VII, 29; IX, 16, 33; in Rom. XI, 27, *so fram mis triggva*, “this covenant from me,” or something similar, must be supplied; *vairþan*, “to happen”: Mark XII, 11; Luke II, 1, *urrann gagrefts fram kaisara*, “a decree went out from Caesar”; further, after *hausjan*, “to hear”: John VII, 51; VIII, 40; *Skeir.* II, b; *andniman*, “to receive”: Luke VI, 34; passively, Neh. VI, 16, *varþ usfulliþ þata vaurstv*, “the work was completed”; Luke I, 45, *vairþiþ ustauhts fram fraujin*, “there shall be fulfilment from the Lord.”

   ee. **παρά** with the dative (where *at* ought properly to have been used): Matt. VI, 1, *laun haban*, “to have reward”; Mark X, 27, *unmahteig visan*, “to be impossible”; Luke I, 30, *bigitan anst*, “to find favour”; John VIII, 38, *hausjan*, “to hear”; Rom. IX, 14, *ïnvindiþa fram guþa*, “unrighteousness with God”; 1 Cor. XVI, 2, *fram sis silbin taujai*. The Gothic translator has interpreted this wrongly, since the Greek says: each person should set aside something with himself—that is, in his own house.

   ff. **ἐπί** with the genitive: 1 Cor. VI, 1, *stojan fram ïnvindaim*, “to go to law before the unrighteous,” where the Gothic translator treated **κρίνεσθαι** as a passive, “to be judged by,” whereas it means “to bring a case before.”

   b. Where the noun has objective force: concerning, on account of, for.

   aa. **περί** with the genitive: Luke IV, 37, *usïddja meriþa*, “a report went out concerning [him]”; Luke XVI, 2, *hausjan*, “to hear concerning”; Mark III, 21 is also to be explained in this way; see the note on that passage. Rom. XIV, 12, *raþjon usgiban*, “to give an account”; Luke II, 24, *hunsl giban*, “to offer a sacrifice”; Mark I, 44, *atbairan*—namely, a sacrifice; Luke V, 14.

   bb. **ὑπέρ** with the genitive: 2 Cor. VII, 14, *wopan*, “to boast concerning”; IX, 2; V, 12, *woftuli*, “boasting”; IX, 3; John XVII, 19, *sik veihan*, “to sanctify oneself for”; Rom. XV, 8, *andbahts vairþan*, “to become a servant for”; Luke VI, 28, *bidjan*, “to pray for”; Eph. VI, 18, 19, *bida*, “prayer”; Eph. V, 20, *aviliudon*, “to give thanks”; 1 Tim. II, 1, 2, *taujan aviliuda*, “to make thanksgivings.”

   cc. **ἀπό**: 2 Cor. II, 3, *faginon*, “to rejoice because of.”

   dd. **ἐπί** with the dative: 1 Thess. III, 7, *gaþrafstiþs visan*, “to be comforted concerning.”

II. **Adverb**, “forward, before,” **ἔμπροσθεν**: Luke XIX, 28, *ïddja fram*, “he went ahead”; compare **Framis**.

III. In composition it occurs only in the noun *framgahts*, in the adjective *framaldrs*, and in the adverbs *framvairþis* and *framvigis*; compare **Fra**.

**FRAMIS**, comparative adverb, before, in advance of; it corresponds to Greek **προ-** in compounds: Mark I, 19, *ïnngaggan framis*, “to go farther on,” **προβαίνειν**; Rom. XIII, 12, *framis galeiþan*, “to advance,” **προκόπτειν**.

**FRAMAþEIS** (Old Norse *framandi*, Old English *fraemd, fremd*, Old Saxon *fremithi*, Old High German *framadi*, Old Frisian *framd, fremed*, Swedish *främmande*, Danish *fremmed*, Dutch *vremd*, Modern High German *fremd*; DRA. 396; Gf. III, 642; Rchth. 756), adjective, alien, belonging to another, foreign, [Col. 1504] **ἀλλότριος**: Luke XVI, 12; John XX, 5; Rom. XIV, 4; 1 Tim. V, 22; **ἀπηλλοτριωμένος**, “alienated”: Eph. II, 12; IV, 18.

**FRAMAþJAN**, class-II verb, to alienate, **ἀπαλλοτριοῦν**: Col. I, 21.

**FRAUJA** (in manuscripts generally written in abbreviated form *fa, fins*, etc., except when it is not used of God or Christ, as Matt. VI, 24; XXVII, 63; Luke XVI, 13; XIX, 33; John XIII, 16; XV, 15; Old Norse *fru*, Old English *frea*, Old Saxon *fro, froho, froio*, Old High German *fro*, Modern High German *Frau*; Gr. III, 320; DM. 15, 135; Gf. III, 804), masculine, lord, **κύριος**: Matt. V, 33; VI, 24; VII, 21, 22; VIII, 2, 21; IX, 38; X, 24; XXVII, 63; Mark I, 3; II, 28; V, 19; VII, 28; XI, 3, 9; XII, 8, 11, 29, 30, 36, 37; XIII, 20; Luke I, 6, 9, 11, 15, 16, 25, 28, 32, 38, 43, 45, 46, 58, 66, 68, 76; II, 9, 11, 15, 22, 23, 24, 26, 37, 38, 39; IV, 8, 12, 18, 19; V, 8, 12, 17; VI, 5, 13, 46; VII, 6, 13; IX, 54; X, 1, 27; XIV, 21, 23; XVI, 3, 5, 8, 13; XVII, 5, 6, 37; XVIII, 6, 41; XIX, 16, 31, 33, 38; XX, 13, 37, 42, 44; John VI, 23; XI, 2; XIII, 16; XV, 15; Rom. VI, 23; VIII, 39; IX, 28; X, 12, 13; XI, 33; XII, 11; XIII, 14; 1 Cor. IV, 4; V, 4; VII, 22; IX, 1; X, 26; XIV, 21; 2 Cor. I, 2, 3; III, 18; IV, 14; V, 6, 11; VI, 17; VIII, 5, 9, 19; XI, 17; XII, 2, 8; XIII, 10, 13; Gal. V, 10; Eph. I, 2; IV, 1; VI, 9, 24; Phil. I, 14; II, 24; III, 8, 20; Col. I, 10; III, 16; 1 Thess. II, 15, 19; III, 8; 2 Thess. I, 1; 1 Tim. VI, 15; 2 Tim. II, 19, 22, 24; *Skeir.* I, b, c; II, b, c; IV, b, d; VII, a; VIII, b, d; **δεσπότης**, “master”: 1 Tim. VI, 1, 2; 2 Tim. II, 21; **θεός**, “God”: Neh. VII, 2.

**HEIVA-FRAUJA**, master of the house, householder, **οἰκοδεσπότης**: Mark XIV, 14.

**FRAUJINON**, class-II verb, to rule, lord it over, **κυριεύειν**: Rom. VII, 1; XIV, 9; 2 Cor. I, 24; 1 Tim. VI, 15; Neh. V, 15; **αὐθεντεῖν**, “to exercise authority”: 1 Tim. II, 12. *Frauginonds frauja*, ruler, master, **δεσπότης**: Luke II, 29. *Svasve fraujinonds*, “as one ruling,” **κατ’ ἐπιταγήν**, “by way of command”: 2 Cor. VIII, 8.

**GA-FRAUJINON**, to exercise lordship, **κατακυριεύειν**: Mark X, 42.

**FRAUJINASSUS**, masculine, dominion, lordship, **κυριότης**: Eph. I, 21; Col. I, 16.

**FRASTS** (compare Modern High German *Fratz*; Schm. I, 622), masculine; plural *frasteis*, child, **τέκνον**: 2 Cor. VI, 13.

**FRASTI-SIBJA**, see under **Sibis**.  
**FRATVJAN**, see under **Fraþjan**.

**FREIDJAN** (compare **Friþon**), class-II verb, to spare, **φείδεσθαι**: Rom. XI, 21; 1 Cor. VII, 28; 2 Cor. I, 23; XII, 6; XIII, 2.

**GA-FREIDEINS**, feminine, preservation, acquisition, **περιποίησις**: Eph. I, 14; 1 Thess. V, 9.

**UN-FREIDEINS**, lack of restraint, unsparingness, **ἀφειδία**: Col. II, 23.

**FREIS** (Old Norse, Old High German, Old Frisian *fri*, Old English *freo, freols*, English *free*, Swedish and Danish *fri*, Dutch *vrij*, Modern High German *frei*; Gf. III, 11. *Briggan frijana*, see under **Briggan**.

**FREI-HALS** (*freij-hals*), see under **Hals**.

**FRIJEI**, feminine, freedom, **ἐλευθερία**: 1 Cor. X, 29.

**FRI**, a prefixed syllable occurring only in *frisahts* and thence in the derivative *gafrisahtjan*.

\* **FRIþON** (Old Norse *fridr, frida*, Old English *frið*, Old Saxon *frithon, frithu*, Old High German *fridu*, Old Frisian *frethia, frithia*, Swedish and Danish *fred*, Dutch *vrede*, Modern High German *Friede*; Gf. III, 788; Rchth. 759), class-II verb, to reconcile.

**GA-FRIþON**, to reconcile, **καταλλάττειν**: 2 Cor. V, 18, 19; **ἀποκαταλλάττειν**, “to reconcile completely”: Eph. II, 16; Col. I, 20, 21.

**GA-FRIþONS**, feminine, reconciliation, **καταλλαγή**: 2 Cor. V, 18, 19.

**SUNJAI-FRIþAS**, proper name, Neapolitan document.  
**FRIþA-REIKS**, proper name, see under **Reiks**.

[Col. 1505] **FRIKS** (Old Norse *frek*, Old English *fraec*, Old High German *freh*, English *freak*, Dutch *vreck*, Modern High German *frech*; Gf. III, 793), adjective, greedy.

**FAIHU-FRIKS**, greedy, covetous, avaricious, **φιλάργυρος**: Luke XVI, 14; **πλεονέκτης**, “greedy, covetous”: 1 Cor. V, 10, 11; Eph. V, 5; \* **δίλογος**, “double-tongued”: 1 Tim. III, 8. *Ni faihufriks*, “not greedy for money,” **ἀφιλάργυρος**: 1 Tim. III, 3.

**FAIHU-FRIKEI**, feminine, greed, covetousness, **πλεονεξία**: Mark VII, 22; Eph. IV, 19; V, 3.

**FRIJEI**, see under **Freis**.

**FRIJON** (*frion*, John XI, 36; XIV, 24; 2 Tim. III, 2; Old Norse *freia*, Old English *freond*, Old Saxon *friund*, Old High German *friunt*, Old Frisian *friond*, English *friend*, Danish *fraende*, Dutch *vriend*, Modern High German *Freund, freien*; Bopp 82, 123; Gf. III, 783; Rchth. 766), class-II verb:

1. to love, be fond of, **φιλεῖν**: Matt. VI, 5; X, 37; John XI, 3, 36; XII, 25; 1 Cor. XVI, 22; **ἀγαπᾶν**, “to love”: Matt. V, 43, 44, 46; VI, 24; Mark XII, 30, 31, 33; Luke VI, 27, 32, 35; VII, 5, 42, 47; X, 27; XVI, 13; John VIII, 42; X, 17; XI, 5; XII, 43; XIII, 23, 34; XIV, 15, 23, 24, 28, 31; XV, 9, 17, 19; XVI, 27; XVII, 23, 24; Rom. VIII, 37; IX, 13; XIII, 8; 2 Cor. IX, 7; XI, 11; XII, 15; Gal. II, 20; IV, 14; Eph. II, 4; V, 2, 25, 28; VI, 24; Col. III, 19; 1 Thess. IV, 9; 2 Thess. II, 16; 2 Tim. IV, 8, 10; *Skeir.* V, a. *Sik frijonds*, “loving oneself,” **φίλαυτος**: 2 Tim. III, 2. *Frijonds viljan seinana*, “loving one’s own pleasure,” **φιλήδονος**: 2 Tim. III, 4. *Frijonds guþ*, “loving God,” **φιλόθεος**: 2 Tim. III, 4.
2. to kiss affectionately, **ἀγαπᾶν**: Mark X, 21.

**FRIJONDS**, participle used substantively, friend, **φίλος**: Matt. V, 47; XI, 19; Luke VII, 6, 34; XIV, 10, 12; XV, 6, 29; XVI, 9; John XI, 11; XV, 13, 14, 15; XIX, 12.

**FRIJONDJA**, feminine, female friend, **φίλη**: Luke XV, 9.

**FRIJONS**, feminine, kiss, **φίλημα**: 1 Cor. XVI, 20; 2 Cor. XIII, 12.

**GA-FRIJONS**, the same: 1 Thess. V, 26.

II, 4, 8; V, 14; VI, 6; VIII, 7, 8, 24; XIII, 11, 13; Gal. V, 6, 13, 22; Eph. I, 4, 15; II, 4; III, 18, 19; IV, 2, 15, 16; V, 2; VI, 23; Phil. I, 17; II, 1, 2; Col. I, 8, 13; III, 14; 1 Thess. III, 6, 12; V, 8; 2 Thess. I, 3; III, 5; 1 Tim. I, 5, 14; II, 15; IV, 12; VI, 11; 2 Tim. I, 7, 13; II, 22; III, 10; *Skeir.* V, d.

**FRIAþVA-MILDS**, see under **Milds**.

**FRIUS** (Old Norse *frys, friosa*, Old English *frysan*, Old Saxon *frost*, Old High German *friusan*, Old Frisian *frost, forst*, English *freeze*, Swedish *fryza*, Danish *fryse*, Dutch *vriezen*, Modern High German *frieren, Frost*; Gr. II, 22; Gf. III, 828; Rchth. 768), neuter, cold, **ψῦχος**: 2 Cor. XI, 27.

**FRUMS** (Old Norse, Old English, Modern High German *frum*, Old Saxon *fruma*, Old Frisian *forma*; compare English *first*, Swedish *först*, Danish *forst*, Modern High German *Fürst*; Greek **πρῶτος**, Latin *primus*; Gr. II, 55; Gf. III, 645; Rchth. 751), masculine, beginning, origin, **ἀρχή**: John XV, 27; XVI, 4.

[Col. 1506] **FRUMA**, adjective, first, **πρῶτος**: Matt. XXVII, 64; Mark X, 31; XVI, 9; John XV, 18; 1 Cor. XV, 47; subscriptions; 2 Thess. subscription; 1 Tim. inscription; II, 13; *Calendarium Gothicum*; **πρότερος**, “former”: Gal. IV, 13; Eph. IV, 22. *Anþar fruma*, “second-first,” **δευτερόπρωτος**: Luke VI, 1. *Fruma sabbato*, “the first [day] before the Sabbath,” **προσάββατον**: Mark XV, 42. *Fruma giban*, see under **Giban**.

**FRUMISTS**, superlative, first, **πρῶτος**: Mark VI, 21; IX, 35; X, 44; XII, 20, 28, 30; XIV, 12; Luke II, 2; XIV, 17; XV, 22; XVI, 5; XIX, 16, 47; XX, 29; 1 Tim. I, 15, 16; 2 Tim. VIII, 5; 1 Tim. II, 1; III, 10; 2 Tim. II, 6; *Skeir.* II, b.

**FRUMISTO**, neuter, beginning, origin, **ἀρχή**: Luke I, 2.

**FRUMISTI**, neuter, the same: John VI, 64; VIII, 44. *Ïn frumistjam*, “above all, principally,” **ἐν πρώτοις**: 1 Cor. XV, 3.

**FRUMADEI**, feminine, preeminence; *frumadein haban*, “to hold first place,” **πρωτεύειν**: Col. I, 18.

**FRUMA-BAUR**, see under **Bairan**.  
**FRODEI**, see under **Fraþjan**.  
**FROþS**, see under **Fraþjan**.

**FYGAILUS**, masculine proper name, Phygelus, **Φύγελος**: 2 Tim. I, 15.

**FYNIKISKA**, see **Saur**.

**FODJAN** (Old Norse *fodra*, Old English *fedan, foda*, Old Saxon *fodian*, Old High German *fotjan*, Old Saxon *feda, foda*, English *feed, food*, Swedish *föda*, Danish *fode*, Dutch *voeden*, Modern High German *füttern*; Gr. II, 43; Gf. III, 374; Rchth. 729), class-II verb, to nourish, bring up, **τρέφειν**: Matt. VI, 26; Luke IV, 16; **ἐκτρέφειν**, “to nurture”: Eph. V, 29; *Skeir.* VII, d. *Barna fodjan*, “to bring up children,” **τεκνοτροφεῖν**: 1 Tim. V, 10.

**FODEINS**, feminine, food, nourishment, **τροφή**: Matt. VI, 25; Luke VII, 25; see the note on that passage.

**US-FODEINS**, the same, **διατροφή**: 1 Tim. VI, 8.

**FODR** (Danish *foder*, Dutch *voedering*, Modern High German *Futteral*), neuter, sheath, **θήκη**: John XVIII, 11.

**FON** (Old Norse *funi*; compare Modern High German *Funke*; Greek **φῶς**; Bopp 124; Gr. III, 352; Gf. III, 527), anomalous neuter; genitive *funins*, fire, **πῦρ**: Matt. V, 22; VII, 19; XXV, 41; Mark IX, 22, 43, 44, 45, 46, 47, 48, 49; Luke III, 9, 16, 17; IX, 54; XVII, 29; John XV, 6; Rom. XII, 20; 2 Thess. I, 8.

**FUNISKS**, adjective, fiery, kindled, **πεπυρωμένος**: Eph. VI, 16.

**FOTUS** (Old Norse *fotr*, Old Saxon, Old English, Old Frisian *fot*, Old High German *foz*, English *foot*, Swedish *fot*, Danish *fod*, Dutch *voet*, Modern High German *Fuss*; Greek **πούς**, Latin *pes*; Bopp 80, 83; Gr. II, 43; III, 403; Gf. III, 733; Rchth. 755), masculine, foot, **πούς**: Matt. V, 35; Mark V, 22; VI, 11; VII, 25; IX, 45; XII, 36; Luke I, 79; IV, 11; VII, 38, 44, 45; VIII, 35, 41; IX, 5; X, 11; XV, 22; XVII, 6; XX, 43; John XI, 2, 32; XIII, 12, 14, 15; Rom. X, 15; 1 Cor. XII, 15, 21; XV, 25, 26; Eph. I, 22; VI, 15; 1 Tim. V, 10.

## W

[Col. 1505] **WA**, see under *Was*. **WAd**, see under *Was*. **WAþAR**, see under *Was*.

**WAþJAN**, conjugation II, to foam, froth (*ἀφρίζειν*): Mc. IX, 18, 20.

[Col. 1506] **WAþO**, feminine, foam, froth (*ἀφρός*): Luc. IX, 39.

**WAIRBAN** (Old Norse *hverfa*; Anglo-Saxon *hveorfan, hvyrft*; Old High German *hwerban*; Old Saxon *huarab*; Old Frisian *hwerva*; English *warp*; Modern High German *Wirbel*; compared with Greek *ῥίπτειν*, Latin *vortex*; Gr. II, 38; Gf. IV, 1229; [Col. 1507] Rchth. 836), conjugation I, *warb, waurbun, waurbans*, to walk (*περιπατεῖν*): Thess. II, III, 6, 11.
