**GA-WAIRBS**, adjective, joinable, capable of being united: *Skeir.* VI, d.

**UNGA-WAIRBS**, not joinable, disobedient, insubordinate (*ἀνυπότακτος*): Tit. I, 6, 10; disobedient (*ἀπειθής*): Tim. II, III, 2.

**WEILA-WAIRBS**, temporary, momentary (*πρόσκαιρος*): Mc. IV, 17; Cor. II, IV, 17.

**WARBON**, conjugation II, to go, walk (*περιπατεῖν*): Mc. XI, 27; Joan. VII, 1; X, 23; to pass by (*παράγειν*): Mth. IX, 27; Mc. I, 16; II, 14; Joan. VIII, 59.

**WAIRNEI** (compared with Anglo-Saxon *braegen*, English *brain*, Swedish *hjerna*, Danish *hjerne*, Modern High German *Hirn*; Greek *κρανίον*, Latin *cranium*), feminine, skull, cranium (*κρανίον*): Mc. XV, 22.

**WAITEIS** (Old Norse *hveiti*; Anglo-Saxon *hvaete*; Old Saxon *hueti*; Old High German *hwaizi*; English *wheat*; Swedish *hvete*; Danish *hvede*; Dutch *weyt*; Modern High German *Weizen*; Gr. III, 370; Gf. IV, 1244), masculine, or **waiti**, neuter, wheat (*σῖτος*): Joan. XII, 24.

**WAIVA** (Anglo-Saxon *hwu*; English *how*; Swedish *huru*; Danish *hvor*; Modern High German *wie*; compare *Was*), interrogative adverb, “how,” in direct and indirect questions (*πῶς*): Mth. VI, 28, 30; Mc. II, 26; III, 23; IV, 13, 40; V, 16; VIII, 21; IX, 12; X, 23; XI, 18; XII, 35; XIV, 11; Luc. I, 34; V, 19; VI, 42; VIII, 18, 36, 47; X, 26; XVIII, 24; XX, 41, 44; Joan. III, 4; V, 47; VI, 42, 52; VII, 15; VIII, 33; IX, 10, 15, 16, 19; XXI, 26; XI, 36; XII, 34; XIV, 5, 9; Rom. X, 14, 15; Cor. I, XV, 12, 35; Cor. II, III, 8; Gal. IV, 9; II, 14; Col. IV, 6; Thess. I, II, 10; IV, 1; Thess. II, III, 7; Tim. I, III, 5, 15; *Skeir.* V, b.

“As” (*ὡς*): Mc. XII, 26; Luc. VI, 4; VIII, 47; Rom. XI, 33; Thess. I, II, 10.

“What?” (*τί*): Luc. I, 62.

*sokidedun waiva ïna ïnnatbereina*, “they sought how to bring him in” (*ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν εἰσενεγκεῖν*), Luc. V, 18.

*waiva manags*, “how great, how much” (*ὅσος*): Cor. II, I, 20.

*ei waiva*, “if somehow, perhaps” (*εἴπως*): Rom. XI, 14; “that by all means” (*ἵνα πάντως*): Cor. I, IX, 22.

**WAN** (Anglo-Saxon *hvaenne*; Old Saxon *huan*; English *when*; Modern High German *wann*; compare *Was*), adverb:

1. In a question, “when?” (*πότε*): Mth. XXV, 38, 39, 44; Luc. XVII, 20; Joan. VI, 25.
2. “When” (*ποτέ*): Phlpp. IV, 10.
3. Before adjectives, “how, what?” (*τί*): *wan aggvus*, “how narrow” (*τί στενός*), Mth. VII, 14; *wan laggs*, see under *Laggs*; *wan filu*, see under *Filu*.
4. Before comparatives, “by how much” (*πόσῳ*): Rom. XI, 12.
5. After other interrogative particles, “when? perhaps”: *ïbai wan*, “lest perhaps, lest at any time” (*μήποτε*), Mth. V, 25; *nibai wan*, “unless perhaps” (*μήποτε*), Mc. IV, 12; *ei wan ni*, “lest at any time” (*μήποτε*), Luc. IV, 11.

**WAN-HUN**, ever, always with a negation: *ni wanhun*, “not ever, never” (*οὐδέποτε*): Mth. VII, 23; Luc. XV, 29; “never yet” (*οὐ πώποτε*): Joan. V, 37; VI, 35; “not ever” (*οὐ-ποτέ*): Eph. V, 29.

**WAPJAN**, conjugation II, to extinguish, suffocate.

**AF-WAPJAN**, the same: to choke (*συμπνίγειν*), Mc. IV, 7, 19; to choke off (*ἀποπνίγειν*), Luc. VIII, 7; to quench (*σβεννύναι*), Eph. VI, 16; Thess. I, V, 19.

**AF-WAPNAN**, conjugation III, to be suffocated: to be choked (*πνίγεσθαι*), Mc. V, 13; to be choked together (*συμπνίγεσθαι*), Luc. VIII, 14; to be choked off (*ἀποπνίγεσθαι*), Luc. VIII, 33; to be quenched (*σβέννυσθαι*), Mc. IX, 44, 46, 48.

**UN-WAPNANDS**, participle, unquenchable (*ἄσβεστος*): Mc. IX, 43, 45; Luc. III, 17.

**WAR**, see under *Was*. **WARBON**, see under *Wairban*. **WARJIS**, see under *Was*.

**WAS** (Old Norse *hver*; Anglo-Saxon *hva*; Old High German *hwer*; Old Saxon *hwe*; Old Frisian *hwa*; English *who*; Swedish *ho*; Danish *hvo*; Modern High German *wer, was*; Greek *ὅς*; Latin *quis*; Gf. IV, 1182; Rchth. 833), feminine **wo**, neuter **wa**, pronoun:

1. Interrogative: “who? what?”

   a. In direct questions, “who? what?” (*τίς*): Mth. VI, 27, 28, 31, 46, 47; VIII, 26, 29; XI, 7, 8, 9, 16; XXVI, 65, 68; XXVII, 4, 17; Mc. I, 24, 27; II, 7, 16, 24; III, 33; IV, 30, 41; V, 7, 9, 30, 31, 35, 39; VI, 2, 24; VIII, 12, 17, 27, 29, 36, 37; IX, 10, 16, 33, 50; X, 3, 17, 18, 26, 36, 51; XI, 5, 28; XII, 9, 15, 16; XIV, 63, 64; [Col. 1508] XV, 12, 14; XVI, 3; Luc. I, 18, 21; II, 48, 49; III, 7, 10, 12, 14; IV, 34, 36; V, 21, 22; VI, 2, 32, 41, 46; VII, 24, 25, 26, 31, 49; VIII, 28, 30, 45; IX, 9, 18, 20, 25; X, 25, 26, 29; XIV, 28, 31, 34; XV, 4; XVI, 3, 11, 12; XVII, 7; XVIII, 18, 19, 26, 41; XX, 13, 15, 17, 23, 24; Joan. VI, 9, 28, 30, 60, 68; VII, 19, 20; VIII, 25, 46, 53; IX, 2, 17, 26, 27, 36; X, 20; XII, 27, 34, 38; XIII, 25; XIV, 22; XVI, 17, 18; XVIII, 4, 7, 21, 29, 35, 38; Rom. VII, 7, 24; VIII, 35; IX, 14, 19, 20, 30; X, 6, 7, 8, 16; XI, 15, 34, 35; XIV, 4, 10; Cor. I, IV, 7; V, 12; VII, 16; IX, 7; X, 19; XI, 22; XIV, 26; XV, 29, 32; Cor. II, II, 2, 16; VI, 14; XV, 16; XI, 11, 29; XII, 13; Gal. III, 1; IV, 30; V, 7; Eph. IV, 9; Phlpp. I, 18; Col. II, 20; Thess. I, II, 19; III, 9.

   “Who then?” (*τίς ἄρα*): Luc. I, 66; VIII, 25. “Of what sort?” (*ποῖος*): Mc. XI, 28; Luc. VI, 32, 33, 34; XX, 2. *wa þau*, “what?” (*τί*): Phlpp. I, 22. *und wa*, “how long? until when?” (*ἕως πότε*): Mc. IX, 19; Luc. IX, 41; Joan. X, 24.

   b. In indirect questions, “who? what?” (*τίς*): Mth. IX, 13; XXVI, 70; Mc. II, 25; IV, 24; V, 14; VIII, 1, 2, 23; IX, 6; X, 38; XIV, 60, 68; XV, 24; Luc. IV, 34; VI, 9, 11, 47; VII, 39; VIII, 9; IX, 55 (33); X, 22; XV, 26; XVI, 4; XVII, 8; XVIII, 6, 36; XIX, 3, 15, 48; XX, 2; Joan. VI, 64; VII, 36, 51; IX, 21; X, 6; XIII, 12, 24; XV, 15; XVI, 18; XVIII, 21; Rom. XII, 2; Cor. I, XV, 2 (?); Eph. I, 18, 19; III, 18; V, 17; VI, 21, 22; Phlpp. I, 22; Thess. I, IV, 2; Tim. I, I, 7; Tim. II, III, 14.

   “Of what sort?” (*ποῖος*): Mc. XI, 29, 33; Luc. XX, 2, 8. “Of what kind?” (*οἷος*): Luc. IX, 55. “Which?” (*ὅς*): Luc. IX, 33 (where the Gothic, together with the manuscripts, does not read *τι*); Tim. II, I, 12.

   Also in the expression *wa bi mik (ïzvis etc.) ïst*, “what concerns me (you, etc.),” *τὰ περὶ ἐμέ* (*ὑμῶν*): Phlpp. II, 23 (28); Col. IV, 8; Eph. VI, 22; *τὰ κατ’ ἐμέ*, Eph. VI, 21.

   *þatei wa*, “whatever” (*ὅ τι ἄν*): Joan. XIV, 13.

   Used to paraphrase the Greek infinitive construction: Luc. I, 21, *sildaleikidedun wa latidedi ïna*, “they wondered at his delaying,” *ἐθαύμαζον ἐν τῷ χρονίζειν αὐτόν*.

2. Indefinite: “someone, anyone, a certain person,” always in an affirmative sense, even where the sentence is negative (*τις*): Mc. VIII, 4; Luc. VII, 40; Rom. IX, 11; XIV, 14; Cor. I, VI, 1; VII, 18; X, 19, 31; XIV, 27; XVI, 7; Cor. II, II, 10; III, 5; XI, 1, 16, 21; XII, 6; Gal. II, 6; Eph. V, 27.

   In a negative sentence: Mc. IV, 22; Joan. VII, 4; Rom. IX, 11; Cor. II, XII, 6; XIII, 8; Col. II, 23; Thess. II, III, 8; Tim. I, VI, 7.

   Especially in subordinate clauses, after *þatei*: Mth. V, 23; Joan. VI, 46; IX, 32; Cor. I, X, 19; *ei*: Mc. IX, 30; XI, 13; Joan. XIII, 29; XV, 13; XVI, 30; Cor. I, IV, 2; *ei ni*: Cor. I, I, 15; Eph. II, 9 (Thess. I, IV, 6); *waþro*: Mc. VIII, 4; *ïbai*: Cor. II, VIII, 20; XI, 16; XII, 6, 17, 18; Thess. I, V, 15; *jabai*: Mth. V, 39 (*ὅστις*), 41; Mc. IV, 23 (*εἴ τις*); VII, 16; IX, 35; XI, 3, 25; XII, 19; XIII, 21; Luc. IX, 23; XIV, 26; XIX, 8, 31; XX, 28; Joan. VI, 51; VII, 17, 37; VIII, 51, 52; IX, 22, 31; X, 9; XI, 9, 10; XII, 26, 47; XIV, 14, 23; Rom. VIII, 9; XIII, 9; Cor. I, V, 11; VII, 12; VIII, 10; X, 27, 28; XIV, 24; XVI, 22; Cor. II, II, 5, 10; V, 17; VII, 14; X, 7, 8; XI, 20; Gal. VI, 1, 3; Phlpp. II, 1; III, 4, 15; IV, 8; Col. III, 13; Thess. II, III, 10, 14; Tim. I, I, 8, 10; III, 1, 5; V, 4, 8; VI, 3; Tim. I, I, 10; Tim. II, II, 5, 21; Tit. I, 6; Philem. 18.

   *wo weilo*, “for a certain time” (*πρὸς καιρόν*), Cor. I, VII, 5; “for some time” (*χρόνον τινά*), Cor. I, XVI, 7.

**WE**, dative (properly instrumental; Bopp 189; Gr. I, 798; IV, 707), used adverbially: perhaps (*ἄν*): Cor. II, XI, 21; see the note on that passage.

**WE-LAUDS**, see under *Lauds*. **WE-LEIKS** (*wileiks*), see under *Leiks*.

**DU-WE**, adverb, “why?” (*διατί*): Mth. IX, 11, 14; Mc. II, 18; VII, 5; IX, 28; XI, 31; Luc. V, 30, 33 (IX, 43); XIX, 23, 31; XX, 5; Joan. VII, 45; VIII, 43, 46; XII, 5; XIII, 37; Rom. IX, 32; “for what purpose?” (*εἰς τί*), Mc. XV, 34; “for what?” (*πρὸς τί*), Joan. XIII, 28; “why?” (*ἵνα τί*), Mth. XXVII, 46; Cor. I, X, 29; “because?” (*ὅτι*), Mc. IX, 28; “what?” (*τί*), Mc. II, 8; IV, 40; ZI, 3 [uncertain citation as printed]; XIV, 6; Luc. XVI, 2; XIX, 33; Joan. XVIII, 23; Cor. I, X, 30; XV, 29, 30; Gal. V, 11.

**WAS-HUN**, any, always with a negation: *ni washun*, “none, no one” (*οὐδείς, μηδείς*): Mth. IX, 16; Mc. X, 18, 29; Luc. X, 22; Joan. X, 18, 28; Col. II, 18. “Not anyone” (*οὐ-τίς*): [Col. 1509] Joan. X, 28; Cor. I, XVI, 11. Castillion’s reading in Thess. II, II, 3 is false.

**WAZUH**, pronoun, feminine **woh**, neuter **wah**:

1. Whoever, every, all (*πᾶς* and *πᾶς ὁ*): Mc. IX, 49; Luc. II, 23; VI, 30, 47; XVI, 16; Cor. I, XI, 5; XV, 30; Gal. V, 3; Eph. IV, 14; “one” (*εἷς*): Neh. V, 18.

   *jera wammeh*, “year by year” (*κατ’ ἔτος*), Luc. II, 41; *daga wammeh*, “day by day” (*καθ’ ἡμέραν*), Mc. XIV, 49; Luc. XVI, 19; XIX, 47; Cor. I, XV, 31; *dag wanoh*, the same, Luc. IX, 23.

   Ordinarily with a following relative (*wazuh saei*): “everyone who, whoever” (*πᾶς ὅστις*), Mth. VII, 24; “everyone who” (*πᾶς ὅς ἄν*), Rom. X, 13; “whoever” (*ὃς ἄν*), Mth. V, 31, 32; XI, 6; Cor. I, XI, 27; “everyone who” (*πᾶς ὁ*), Mth. V, 28; VII, 21, 26; Luc. XIV, 11; XVI, 18; XX, 18; Joan. VI, 40; VIII, 34; XI, 26; XII, 46; XVIII, 37; Cor. I, IX, 25; Tim. II, II, 19.

   Also with a participle: Luc. VI, 47, *wazuh sa gaggands*, “everyone who comes” (*πᾶς ὁ ἐρχόμενος*); Joan. VI, 45; Rom. X, 11. Or with an adjective in place of the Greek participle: Mth. V, 22, *wazuh modags*, “everyone who is angry” (*πᾶς ὁ ὀργιζόμενος*).

2. With numerals, distributives are formed: *tvans wanzuh*, “two by two” (*δύο δύο*), Mc. VI, 7; “two at a time” (*ἀνὰ δύο*), Luc. X, 1.

**SA-WAZUH**, every; *sawazuh saei*, “everyone who, whoever” (*πᾶς ὅστις*), Mth. X, 32; “everyone who” (*πᾶς ὁ*), Luc. XVIII, 14; “whoever” (*ὅστις ἄν*), Gal. V, 10; “whoever” (*ὃς ἐάν*), Mc. IX, 37, 42; X, 11, 43; Luc. VII, 23; IX, 48. With following *ïzei*, the same (*πᾶς ὁ*): Joan. XVI, 2; XIX, 12. *þatawah þei*, “whoever” (*ὁ ἐάν*): Joan. XV, 7.

**þIS-WAZUH**, the same. *þiswazuh saei*, “whoever” (*ὅστις ἄν*): Mth. X, 33; Col. III, 17, 23; “whoever” (*ὃς ἄν*): Mc. IV, 25; VII, 11; Gal. V, 17; “as many as” (*ὅσος*): Phlpp. IV, 8. *þiswazuh ei*, “whoever” (*ὃς ἄν*): Mc. XI, 23. *þiswazuh þei*, “whoever” (*ὅστις ἄν*): Joan. XV, 16; “whoever” (*ὃς ἐάν*): Mc. VI, 22, 23; XI, 23; Luc. IV, 6; Joan. XV, 7; “as many things as” (*ὅσος ἄν*): Mc. XI, 24; Joan. XI, 22; XVI, 23.

**WEH**, adverb, only, merely (*μόνον*): Gal. VI, 12; *weh þatainei*, the same: Phlpp. I, 27.

**WAþAR**, interrogative pronoun, “which?” “which of two?” (*τίς*): Mth. IX, 5; Mc. II, 9; Luc. V, 23; VII, 42; *Skeir.* III, a.

**WAþARUH**, pronoun, which of two: *Skeir.* V, d (where either *waþarammeh* or also *waþaramme* must be read in place of *waþaramma*).

**AIN-WAþARUH**, the same: *Skeir.* III, a.

**WARJIS**, interrogative pronoun, “which?” among several (*τίς*): Mc. IX, 34; XII, 23; Luc. IX, 46; XX, 33; Joan. VI, 64; X, 32; XIII, 22; “of what kind?” (*ποῖος*): Mc. XII, 28; Joan. X, 32; “who” (*ὅς*): Joan. XIII, 18.

**WARJIZUH**, pronoun, each, every one (*ἕκαστος*): Mth. XXVII, 14; Luc. II, 3; VI, 44; IX, 14; Joan. VI, 7; XVI, 32; Rom. XII, 3; XIV, 12; Cor. I, IV, 5; VII, 7, 17, 20; X, 24; XII, 11; XIV, 26; XV, 23; XVI, 2; Cor. II, V, 10; IX, 7; Gal. VI, 4, 5; Eph. IV, 16, 25; Phlpp. II, 4; Thess. I, IV, 4; *Skeir.* IV, b; VI, b.

“All” (*πᾶς*): Luc. VI, 40; XIV, 33; XIX, 23, 26.

*warjizuh wa*, “each what?” (*τίς, τί*), Mc. XV, 24; see the note on that passage.

*and dulþ warjanoh* (*warjoh*), “at each feast,” “at every feast” (*κατὰ ἑορτήν*): Mth. XXVII, 15; Mc. XV, 6.

**AIN-WARJIZUH**, each one (*εἷς ἕκαστος*): Luc. IV, 40; XVI, 5; Cor. I, XII, 18; Eph. IV, 7; Col. IV, 6; Thess. I, II, 11; Thess. II, I, 3; “each” (*ἕκαστος*): Cor. I, VII, 17; “one” (*εἷς*): Rom. XII, 5; *Skeir.* VII, c (where *ainwarjammeh* must be read in place of *ainwarjamma*).

*ainwarjizuh anþar anþarana*, “each one [the] other” (*εἷς τὸν ἕνα*), Thess. I, V, 11.

**WAþ** (*wad*, Joan. XIII, 36), adverb, “where? whither?” (*ποῦ*): Joan. VIII, 14; XII, 35; XIII, 36; XIV, 5; XVI, 5.

**þIS-WADUH**; *þiswaduh þadei*, “wherever” (*ὅπου ἄν*): Mth. VIII, 19; Mc. VI, 56; Luc. IX, 57; *þiswaduh þei* (*þe*), the same: Mc. VI, 10; “wherever” (*οὗ ἐάν*): Cor. I, XVI, 6.

**WADRE**, adverb, “whither?” (*ποῦ*): Joan. VII, 35.

**WAþRO**, adverb, “whence?” (*πόθεν*): Mc. VI, 2; VIII, 4; [Col. 1510] XII, 37; Luc. I, 43; XX, 7; Joan. VI, 5; VII, 27, 28; VIII, 14; IX, 29, 30; XIX, 9.

*ni habandam waþro usgebeina*, “when they had no means from which they could pay,” *μὴ ἐχόντων αὐτῶν ἀποδοῦναι*, Luc. VII, 42.

**WAR**, adverb, “where?” (*ποῦ*): Mth. VIII, 20; Mc. XIV, 12, 14; Luc. VIII, 25; IX, 58; XVII, 17, 37; Joan. VII, 11; VIII, 19; IX, 12; XI, 34; Cor. I, I, 20; XII, 17, 19; XV, 55.

**þIS-WARUH**; *þiswaruh þei*, “wherever” (*ὅπου ἄν*): Mc. IX, 18; XIV, 9.

**WASS** (Old Norse *hvatr, hvass*; Old High German *hwassi*; Anglo-Saxon *hvat*; Swedish *hvass*; Gr. II, 43; Gf. IV, 1239), adjective, severe, vehement.

**WASSABA**, adverb, severely, vehemently (*ἀποτόμως*): Tit. I, 13.

**WASSEI**, feminine, severity, vehemence: Rom. XI, 22.

**WE** and **WEH**, see under *Was*.

**WEIHTS**, adjective, light (*ἐλαφρός*): Cor. II, IV, 17.

**WEILA** (Old Norse and Swedish *hvila*; Anglo-Saxon *hvil*; Old Saxon *huila*; Old High German *hwila*; Old Frisian *hwile*; English *while*; Danish *hvile*; Dutch *wijl*; Modern High German *Weile*; DM. 457; Gf. IV, 1224; Rchth. 836), feminine, time, occasion, hour (*ὥρα*): Mth. VIII, 13; IX, 22; XXVII, 45, 46; Mc. XV, 25, 33, 34; Luc. I, 10; II, 38; VII, 21; X, 21; XIV, 17; XVIII, 3; XX, 19; Joan. VII, 30; VIII, 20; XI, 9; XII, 23, 27; XVI, 2, 4, 21; Cor. I, IV, 11; XV, 30; Cor. II, VII, 8; Thess. I, II, 17; Philem. 15; *Skeir.* VI, a.

“Time” (*χρόνος*): Luc. XVIII, 4; Joan. VII, 33; Rom. VII, 1; Cor. I, XVI, 7.

“Season, appointed time” (*καιρός*): Cor. I, VII, 5.

*und þata ueilos þei*, “during this time that; for as long as” (*ἐφ’ ὅσος*): Mth. IX, 15.

**WEILAN**, conjugation II, to cease (*παύεσθαι*): Col. I, 9.

**ANA-WEILAN**, to rest, refresh (*ἀναπαύειν*): Cor. II, VII, 13.

**GA-WEILAN**, to cease (*παύεσθαι*): Cor. I, XIII, 8; *gaweilan sik*, to remain, stay (*ἐπαναπαύεσθαι*): Luc. X, 6.

**GA-WEILAINS**, feminine, rest, tranquillity (*ἄνεσις*): Cor. II, II, 13; VII, 5.

**UN-WEILS**, adjective, unceasing, continual (*ἀδιάλειπτος*): Rom. IX, 2.

**WEILO-HUN**, adverb, for a time (*πρὸς ὥραν*): Gal. II, 5.

**WEILA-WAIRBS**, see under *Wairban*.

**WEITS** (Old Norse *hvitr*; Anglo-Saxon *hwit*; Old Saxon *huit*; Old High German *hwiz*; Old Frisian *hwit*; English *white*; Swedish *hvit*; Danish *hviid*; Dutch *wit*; Modern High German *weiss*; Gf. IV, 1242; Rchth. 836), adjective, white (*λευκός*): Mth. V, 36; Mc. IX, 3; XVI, 5; Luc. IX, 29 (XX, 46).

**WI . . .**, see under *Was*.

**WILFTRI** (Gr. II, 58, 133), feminine, bier (*σορός*): Luc. VII, 14.

**WO** and **WOH**, see under *Was*.

**WOPAN**, conjugation I, *waiwop, waiwopun, wopans*, to boast (*καυχᾶσθαι*): Rom. XI, 18; Cor. I, IV, 7; XIII, 3, at this passage; Cor. II, V, 12; VII, 14; IX, 2; X, 8, 15, 16, 17; XI, 12, 16, 18, 19, 30; XII, 1, 5, 9, 11; Gal. VI, 13, 14; Eph. II, 9; Phlpp. III, 3; Thess. II, I, 4.

**WOFTULI**, feminine, ground for boasting, boast (*καύχημα*): Cor. I, V, 6; Cor. II, I, 14; V, 12; IX, 3; Gal. VI, 4; Phlpp. I, 26; boasting (*καύχησις*): Cor. I, XV, 31; Cor. II, I, 12; VII, 4, 14; VIII, 24; IX, 4; XI, 10, 17; Thess. I, II, 19.

**WOTA** (Gr. II, 43), feminine, threat (*ἀπειλή*): Eph. VI, 9; *Skeir.* II, a.

**WOTJAN**, conjugation II, to rebuke, reprove, threaten (*ἐπιτιμᾶν*): Mc. X, 48; Luc. IV, 35.

**GA-WOTJAN**, the same: Mc. IX, 25; Luc. IX, 41, 42; Tim. II, IV, 2; to rebuke sternly (*ἐμβριμᾶσθαι*): Mc. I, 43; *Skeir.* I, c.

**WOFTULI**, see under *Wopan*.

## O

[Col. 1509] **O**, interjection:

1. “O” (*ὦ*): Mc. IX, 19; Gal. III, 1.
2. “Woe!” (*οὐαί*): Mc. XV, 29.

**OBEID**, proper masculine noun, Obed (*Ὠβήδ*): Luc. III, 32.

**OGAN**, see under *Agan*.

**ODUEIA**, proper masculine noun, Oduias (*Ὠδουίας*): Esdr. 2, 40.

[Col. 1510] **OHTEIGO**, the same as *Uhteigo*; see under *Uht*.

**OSANNA** (Hebrew vocative), Hosanna (*ὡσαννά*): Mc. XI, 9; Joan. XII, 13.

**OSEA**, proper masculine noun, Hosea (*Ὠσηέ*): Rom. IX, 25.

## B. GREEK–GOTHIC GLOSSARY

[Col. 1511]

barms: **breast, chest; bosom**. στήκειν: **see ἱστάναι, “to stand.”** στηρίζειν, tulgjan, gatulgjan: **to establish, strengthen**. στίγμα, staks: **mark, brand**. στιγμή, stiks: **a moment, point**. στίλβειν, glitmunjan: **to shine, gleam**. στοά, ubizva: **portico**. στοιβάς, asts: **leafy branches, bedding**. στοιχεῖν, gaggan, galaista visan: **to walk, follow in line with**. στοιχεῖον, stabs: **element, letter**. στολή, vasti: **robe, garment**. στόμα, munþs, munþ: **mouth**. στόμαχος, qiþus, suqns: **stomach, belly**. στρατεία, drauhtinassus, drauhtivitoþ: **military service, warfare**. στρατεύειν, driugan: **to serve as a soldier**; στρατεύεσθαι, drauhtinon, militon: **to wage war, serve as a soldier**. στρατιά, harjis: **army, host**. στρατιώτης, gadrauhts: **soldier**. στρατολογῶν, sa þammei drauhtino: **one who enlists soldiers**. στρέφειν, vandjan: **to turn**; στρέφεσθαι, vandjan sik, gavandjan sik, gavandjan: **to turn oneself, turn back**. στρουθίον, sparva: **sparrow**. στρωννύναι, straujan: **to spread, strew**. στυγνάζειν, ganipnan: **to become gloomy, be downcast**. στύλος, sauls: **pillar, column**. σύ, þu: **you**; ὁ σοῦ, þeins: **what is yours, your [own]**. συγγένεια, kuni: **kinship, kindred**. συγγενής, samakuns, niþjis, ganiþjis, niþjo: **kinsman, relative, of the same people**. συγγνώμη; κατὰ συγγνώμην, gakunnands: **concession; by way of concession**. συγκαθίζειν, miþgasatjan: **to seat together**; συγκαθῆσθαι, sitan: **to sit together**. συγκακοπαθεῖν, miþarbaidjan: **to suffer hardship together**. συγκαλεῖν, gahaitan, galaþon: **to call together**. συγκατάθισις, samaqiss: **sitting together**. συγκλείειν, galukan: **to shut up, enclose**. συγκληρονόμος, gaarbja: **fellow-heir**. συγκοινωνεῖν, gamainjan, briggan gamainana: **to share, participate with**. συγκοινωνός, gamains, gadaila: **partner, participant**. συγκρίνειν, gadomjan: **to compare, interpret**. συγχαίρειν, miþfaginon: **to rejoice with**. συζευγνύναι, gavidan: **to join together, yoke**. συζῆν, miþliban, samana liban: **to live together**. συζητεῖν, miþsokjan, sokjan miþ, samana sokjn, sokajan du: **to discuss, dispute together**. συζητητής, sokareis: **disputer, debater**. σύζυγος, gajuko: **yokefellow, companion**. συζωοποιεῖν, miþgaqiujan: **to make alive together**. συκάμινος, bainabagms: **mulberry tree**. συκῆ, smakkabagms: **fig tree**. συκομορέα, smakkabagms: **sycamore fig tree**. σῦκον, smakka: **fig**. συκοφαντεῖν, anamahtjan, afholon: **to extort, accuse falsely**. συλᾶν, biraubon: **to rob, despoil**. συλλαλεῖν, miþrodjan, rodjan miþ: **to speak with**. συλλαμβάνειν, greipan, undgreipan, ganiman: **to seize, take together**; ganiutan, ïnkilþo vairþan: **to conceive, become pregnant**; hence συνειληφυῖα, ïnkilþo: **having conceived, pregnant**. συλλαμβάνεσθαι, niþan; hilpan: **to help, assist**. συλλέγειν, lisan: **to gather**. συλλογίζεσθαι, þagkjan sis: **to reason, deliberate**. συλλυπεῖσθαι; συλλυπούμενος, gaurs: **to grieve with; grieving together**. συμβαίνειν, gadaban: **to happen, occur**. συμβάλλειν, stigqan; þagkjan sis: **to bring together; consider, deliberate**. συμβασιλεύειν, miþþiudanon: **to reign together**. συμβιβάζειν, gagahaftjan, þeihan: **to unite, instruct, bring together**.

[Col. 1542] συμβουλεύειν, garaginon: **to counsel**. συμβούλιον, runa, garuni: **counsel, deliberation**. σύμβουλος, ragineis: **counsellor**. συμμαθητής, gahlaiba: **fellow disciple**. συμμαρτυρεῖν, miþveitvodjan: **to bear witness with**. συμμέτοχος, gadaila: **fellow participant**. συμμιμητής, miþgaleikonds: **fellow imitator**. σύμμορφος, ïbnaskauns: **conformed, having the same form**. συμμορφοῦν, miþkaurjan: **to conform**. συμπαραγίγνεσθαι, miþvisan: **to be present with**. συμπαραλαμβάνειν, ganiman miþ: **to take along with**. συμπαραμένειν: **the same as παραμένειν, “to remain.”** συμπέμπειν, miþsandjan, miþïnsandjan: **to send with**. συμπληροῦσθαι, gafullnan, usfullnan: **to be fulfilled together, be filled up**. συμπνίγειν, þreihan, afwapjan: **to choke, press together**; συμπνίγεσθαι, afwapnan: **to be choked**. συμπολίτης, gabaurgja: **fellow citizen**. συμπορεύεσθαι, miþgaggan, gaqiman sik: **to go together**. συμφάναι, gaqiss visan: **to agree**. συμφέρειν, batiza visan, bruks visan, dugan: **to be advantageous, profitable, useful**. συμφύεσθαι, miþuskeinan: **to grow together**. συμφυλέτης, ïnkuns: **fellow tribesman, compatriot**. συμφωνεῖν, gatiman: **to agree, be in harmony**. συμφώνησις, samaqiss: **agreement**. συμφωνία, saggvs: **harmony, agreement**. σύμφωνον, gaqiss: **harmonious, agreed**. συμφώνως, gatemiba: **in agreement, harmoniously**. σύμψυχος, samasaivals: **like-minded, united in soul**. σύν, miþ: **with**. συνάγειν, briggan, lisan, galisan; galaþon: **to bring together, gather; summon**; συνάγεσθαι, gagaggan, samaþ gagaggan, gaqiman, gaqiman sik: **to assemble, come together**. συναγωγή, gaqumþs, synagoge: **assembly, synagogue**. συναθλεῖν, miþarbaidjan, samana arbaidjan: **to strive or labour together**. συναιχμάλωτος, miþfrahunþans: **fellow captive**. συνακολουθεῖν, afargaggan miþ: **to follow with**. συναναβαίνειν, miþgaggan: **to go up with**. συνανακεῖσθαι, miþanakumbjan, anakumbjan: **to recline at table together**. συναναμίγνυσθαι, blandan: **to mingle with**. συναντᾶν, gamotjan: **to meet**. συνάντησις; ἐξέρχεσθαι εἰς συνάντησίν τινι, usgaggan viþra ainana, viþragamotjan ainamma: **meeting; to go out to meet someone, to meet someone face to face**. συναπάγειν, miþgatiuhan: **to lead away with**; συναπάγεσθαι, miþgavisan: **to be carried away with**. συναποθνήσκειν, miþgadauþnan, miþgasviltan: **to die together with**. συναποστέλλειν, miþïnsandjan: **to send with**. συναρμολογεῖν, gagatilon: **to fit together, join together**. σύνδεσμος, gabinda, gabindi, gabundi: **bond, fastening**. σύνδουλος, gaskalki: **fellow servant**. συνεγείρειν, miþurraisjan: **to raise together**; συνεγείρεσθαι, miþurreisan: **to rise together**. συνέδριον, gaqumþs, gafaurds: **council, assembly**. συνειδέναι, miþvitan: **to know with, be conscious of**. συνείδησις, miþvissei, gahugds, þuhtus, gamunds: **conscience, awareness, thought**. συνεῖναι, gamotjan (?): **to be with, meet (?)**. συνειςέρχεσθαι, miþïnngaleiþan, miþqiman: **to enter with**. συνέκδημος, gasinþa, gasinþja, miþgasinþa: **fellow traveller**. συνεργεῖν; συνεργῶν, gavaurstva: **to work together; working together**. συνεργός, gavaurstva: **fellow worker**. συνέρχεσθαι, gagaggan, gaqiman, garinnan miþ, samaþ garinnan, gavandjan sik: **to come together, assemble**. συνεσθίειν, miþmatjan: **to eat with**.

[Col. 1543] σύνεσις, fraþi, froþei: **understanding, insight**. συνετός, froþs: **intelligent, discerning**. συνευδοκεῖν, gavileis visan: **to approve with, consent**. συνέχειν, anahaban; dishaban; biwairban: **to hold together; restrain; surround, press upon**. συνήδεσθαι, gavizneigs visan: **to delight together, rejoice with**. συνήθεια, biuhti: **custom, habit**. συνθάπτειν, miþganavistron: **to bury together**. συνθλᾶν, gakroton: **to crush together**. συνθλίβειν, þreihan: **to press hard, crush**. συνιέναι, gaqiman; fraþjan, vitan: **to understand, comprehend**. συνιστάναι and συνιστᾶν, miþstandan, ussatjan; ustaiknjan, uskannjan, gasvikunþjan; anafilhan: **to stand with, set before; demonstrate, make known, commend**; συνίστασθαι, gakannjan: **to be established, consist**. συνοδία, gasinþa (plural): **company of travellers**. συνοικοδομεῖν, miþgatimrjan: **to build together**. συνοχή, aggviþa: **distress, anguish**. συντάττειν, anabiudan: **to command, prescribe**. συντελεῖν, ustiuhan: **to complete, bring to an end**. συντέμνειν, gamaurgjan: **to shorten, cut short**. συντηρεῖν, gafastan; vitan: **to keep, preserve; watch**. συντίθεσθαι, gaqiþan sis: **to agree, make an arrangement**. συντρίβειν, gabrikan, malvjan: **to break, crush**. συντυγχάνειν, andqiþan: **to meet, happen upon**. συνυποκρίνεσθαι, miþlitjan: **to play the hypocrite with**. συνυπουργεῖν, hilpan: **to assist, cooperate in service**. συσπαράττειν, tahjan: **to tear violently**. σύσσημον, bandvo: **a common sign, signal**. σύσσωμος, galeika: **of the same body, fellow-member**. συστασιάστης, drobjands miþ: **a fellow rebel, participant in sedition**. συστατικός; συστατικαὶ ἐπιστολαί, anafilhis bokos: **commendatory; letters of recommendation**. συσταυροῦν, miþushramjan: **to crucify together with**. συστοιχεῖν; συστοιχοῦσα, gamarko: **to correspond; corresponding**. συστρατιώτης, gahlaiba: **fellow soldier**. συσχηματίζεσθαι, galeikon sik: **to conform oneself**. σφαγή, slauhts: **slaughter**. σφόδρα, abraba, filu: **very, exceedingly**. σφραγίζειν, gasigljan, faurasigljan: **to seal, seal beforehand**; σφραγίζεσθαι, sigljan: **to be sealed**. σφραγίς, sigljo: **seal**. σχῆμα, manauli: **form, appearance**. σχίζειν, aftaurnan: **to split**; σχίζεσθαι, disskritnan: **to be divided**; σχιζόμενος, uslukns: **rent open**. σχίσμα, gataura; missaqiss: **division, schism; discord**. σχολάζειν, uhteigs visan: **to be at leisure, be free**. σώζειν, nasjan, ganasjan: **to save, heal**; σώζεσθαι, ganisan, hails visan: **to be saved, be healed**. σῶμα, leik: **body**. σωματικός, leikeins: **bodily**; σωματικὸν εἶδος, leikis siun: **bodily form**. σωρεύειν, afhlaþan: **to heap up**. σωτήρ, ganasjands: **saviour, deliverer**. σωτηρία, ganists, naseins: **salvation, deliverance**. σωτήριον, naseins: **salvation, deliverance**. σωφρονεῖν, vaila fraþjan, fullafraþjan, fraþjan: **to think soundly, be self-controlled**. σωφρονισμός, ïnahei: **discipline, sound-mindedness**. σωφροσύνη, gafraþjei, *mahei (read ïnahei): **sound-mindedness, self-control**. σώφρων, froþs, andaþahts: **sensible, self-controlled**. τάγμα, teva: **order, rank**. ταλαίπωρος, vainahs: **wretched, miserable**. ταμιεῖον, heþjo: **inner room, store-room**. τάξις, *viko: **order, arrangement**. ταπεινός, hauns, hnaivs, hnaiviþs, gahnaiviþs: **lowly, humble**. ταπεινοῦν, haunjan, gahaunjan, hnaivjan, gahnaivjan: **to humble, abase**. ταπεινοφροσύνη, hauneins gahugdais, hauneins: **humility, lowliness of mind**. ταπείνωσις, hauneins, hnaiveins: **humiliation, lowliness**. ταράττειν, drobjan, ïnvagjan: **to trouble, disturb**; ταράττεσθαι, gadrobnan, ïndrobnan: **to be troubled, disturbed**.

[Col. 1543] τάττειν, gasatjan: **to appoint, arrange**. ταφή, usfilh: **burial**. τάφος, hlaiv: **tomb, grave**. τάχα, aufto: **perhaps, quickly**. ταχέως, sprauto: **quickly**. τάχος; ἐν τάχει, sprauto: **speed; quickly, with haste**. ταχύ, sprauto: **quickly**; τάχιον, sprauto: **more quickly**. τε, ïþ, sveþauh: **and, also, even**. τεῖχος, baurgsvaddjus: **wall [of a city]**. τεκνίον, barnilo: **little child**. τεκνογονεῖν, barna bairan: **to bear children**. τεκνογονία, barne gabaurþs: **childbearing**. τέκνον, barn, barnilo, magus, frasts: **child, little child, offspring**. τεκνοτροφεῖν, barna fodjan: **to nourish children**. τέκτων, timrja: **craftsman, carpenter**. τελεῖν, ustiuhan, usfulljan: **to complete, fulfil**. τέλειος, fullatauhans, fullatojis, fulls; fullavits, fullaveis: **complete, perfect, mature; fully knowing, assured**. τελειότης, ustauhts: **perfection, completeness**. τελειοῦν, usfulljan, ustiuhan, taujan: **to make complete, fulfil, accomplish**. τελείωσις, ustauhts: **completion, perfection**. τελεσφορεῖν, gavrisqan: **to bear fruit to maturity**. τελευτᾶν, gasviltan, gadauþnan, afdauþjan (passive): **to die, come to an end**; μέλλων τελευτᾶν, svultavairþja: **about to die**. τέλος, andeis; ustauhts; mota: **end; completion; tax, toll**. τελώνης, motareis: **tax collector**. τελώνιον, mota, motastaþs: **toll, customs station**. τέρας, fauratani: **wonder, portent**. τεσσαράκοντα, fidvortigjus: **forty**. τέσσαρα, fidvor: **four**. τεταρταῖος, fidurdogs: **on the fourth day**. τετραπλοῦς, fidurfalþs: **fourfold**. τετράρχης, taitrarkes: **tetrarch**. τετραρχῶν, fidurragineis: **ruling as tetrarch**. τηλαυγῶς, bairhtaba: **clearly, brightly**. τηλικοῦτος, svaleiks: **so great, of such an age or size**. τηρεῖν, bairgan; fastan, gafastan; vitan: **to keep, guard; preserve; observe**. τήρησις, fastubni, fastubnja: **keeping, observance**. τίειν; δίκην τίειν, fraveit (??) usgiban: **to pay; to pay the penalty**.

> **Note:** [Col. 1543] See 2 Thessalonians 1:9.

τιθέναι, satjan, gasatjan; lagjan, galagjan, aflagjan; taujan: **to put, place, set; lay down, put away; make**. τίκτειν, bairan, gabairan: **to bear, give birth**; οὐ τίκτουσα, unbairandei: **not bearing, barren**. τίλλειν, raupjan: **to pluck**. τιμᾶν, sveran; vairþon; garahnjan: **to honour, value, reckon worthy**. τιμή, sveriþa, sverains; and vairþi, vairþs galaubs: **honour, value, price, worth**; εἰς τιμήν, galaubs: **for honour, honourable use**. τίς, *(quis)* was, warjis; *(uter)* waþar; wileiks, saei: **who? which [of two]? what kind? whoever**; τίς ἄρα, was: **who then?**; τί, wa þau; du we: **what? why?** τὶς, sums, was: **someone, anyone**; οὐ-τίς, ni washun: **no one**; μή τις, ni mannahun: **lest anyone, no one**; μή τι, ni vaiht: **lest anything, nothing**; τὶ, wan: **at some time**. τό, þata: **the, that, it**. τοιγαροῦν, ïnuh þis nu: **therefore, consequently**. τοίνυν, nu, aþþan nu: **therefore, then**. τοιοῦτος, svaleiks: **such, of such a kind**. τόκος, vokrs: **interest, usury**. τολμᾶν, gadaursan, anananþjan: **to dare, venture**. τόπος, staþs, rums: **place, space**. τοσοῦτος, svalauds, sva manags, sva filu: **so great, so many, so much**. τότε, þan, þanuh, þanuh þan, bi þe: **then, at that time**; τότε οὖν and τότε καί, þanuh þan: **then therefore; then also**. τοὐναντίον: **see ἐναντίον, “opposite, contrary.”** τοὔνομα: **see ὄνομα, “name.”** τράπεζα, mes, biuds; skattjans: **table; money-changers’ table**. τραυματίζειν, gavundon: **to wound**.

[Col. 1544] τράχηλος, hals, halsagga: **neck**. τραχύς; τραχεῖα, usdrusts: **rough; rugged [places]**. τρεῖς, þreis: **three**. τρέμειν, reiran: **to tremble**. τρέφειν, fodjan: **to nourish**. τρέχειν, þragjan, rinnan: **to run**. τριάκοντα, þreistigjus: **thirty**. τριακόσια, þrijahunda: **three hundred**. τρίβολος, vigadeina: **thorn-bush, brier**. τρίζειν, kriustan: **to gnash, creak**. τρίς, þrim sinþam: **three times**. τρίτον, þridjo: **thirdly, for the third time**. τρίτος, þridja: **third**. τρίχες: **see θρίξ, “hair.”** τρόμος, reiro: **trembling**. τρόπος, haidus: **manner, way**. τροφή, fodeins: **food, nourishment**. τρυγᾶν, trudan: **to gather grapes, tread**. τρυγών, hraivadubo: **turtledove**. τρυμαλιά, þairko: **eye of a needle**. τρώγειν, matjan: **to eat**. τυγχάνειν, niutan, gatilon: **to obtain, happen upon**. τύπος, frisahts: **pattern, form, example**. τύπτειν, slahan, stautan: **to strike, beat**. τυφλός, blinds: **blind**. τυφλοῦν, gablindjan: **to blind**. τυφοῦν, ufbauljan: **to puff up, make conceited**; τυφωθείς, ufarhauhiþs: **having become puffed up**; τετυφωμένος, hauhþuhts: **conceited**. τυχόν, vaitei: **perhaps, by chance**. ὑβρίζειν, anamahtjan: **to insult, mistreat violently**. ὕβρις, anamahts: **insolence, violence**. ὑβριστὴς, ufbrikands: **violent person, insolent man**. ὑγιαίνειν, hails visan: **to be well, healthy**; ὑγιαίνων, hails: **healthy**. ὑγιής, hails: **sound, healthy**. ὑδροποτεῖν, vato drigkan: **to drink water**. ὕδωρ, vato: **water**. υἱοθεσία, sunive gadeds, sunive sibja; frastisibja: **adoption as sons, sonship; filial relationship**. υἱός, sunus: **son**. ὑμεῖς, jus: **you [plural]**; ὁ ὑμῶν, ïzvar (plural), ïggqar (dual): **yours**; τὰ ὑμῶν, ïzvaros aihtins: **your possessions**. ὑμέτερος, ïzvar: **your [plural]**. ὕμνος, hazeins: **hymn**. ὑπάγειν, gaggan, galeiþan, garinnan, snivan: **to go away, depart**. ὑπακοή, ufhauseins: **obedience**. ὑπακούειν, ufhausjan, andhausjan: **to obey, heed**. ὕπανδρος, uf vaira: **under a husband, married**. ὑπαντᾶν, gamotjan, gaggan gamotjan, viþragamotjan, viþragaggan: **to meet, go to meet**. ὑπάντησις: **the same as συνάντησις, “meeting.”**

ὑπάνω, ufar: **above**. ὑπάρχειν, visan: **to be, exist**; τὰ ὑπάρχοντα, aigin, aihts: **possessions, property**. ὑπεναντίος, andaneiþs: **opposed, contrary**. ὑπέρ with genitive, bi (accusative), du, ïn (genitive), faur, fram; mais: **for, on behalf of, concerning, beyond, more than**; with accusative, ufar: **over, above**. ὑπεραίρεσθαι, ufarhafjan sik, ufarhugjan: **to exalt oneself, be conceited**. ὑπεράνω, ufaro: **far above**. ὑπεραυξάνειν, ufarvahsjan: **to increase exceedingly**. ὑπερβαίνειν, ufargaggan: **to transgress, go beyond**. ὑπερβάλλειν; ὑπερβάλλων, ufarassau mikils: **to surpass; surpassing, exceedingly great**. ὑπερβαλλόντως, ufarassau: **exceedingly**. ὑπερβολή, ufarassus, filusna: **excess, surpassing measure**. ὑπερέκεινα; εἰς τὸ ὑπερέκεινα, ufarjaina: **beyond; unto the regions beyond**. ὑπερεκπερισσοῦ, ufarassau: **beyond all measure, exceedingly abundantly**. ὑπερεκτείνειν, ufarassau ufþanjan: **to stretch out beyond measure**. ὑπερεκχύνειν, ufargiutan: **to pour out excessively**.

[Col. 1545] ὑπερέχειν, ufarvisan: **to be above, surpass**; ὑπερέχων, auhuma: **superior, ruler**; τὸ ὑπερέχον, ufarassus: **that which is preeminent, superiority**. ὑπερηφάνης, mikilþuhts: **proud, arrogant**. ὑπερηφανία, hauhhairtei: **pride, arrogance**. ὑπερήφανος, hauhhairts: **proud, arrogant**. ὑπερλίαν, ufar mikil, ufar filu: **exceedingly, very greatly**. ὑπερνικᾶν, jiukan: **to conquer overwhelmingly, be more than victorious**. ὑπεροχή, ufarassus: **eminence, superiority**. ὑπερπερισσεύειν, ufarfulljan: **to abound exceedingly**. ὑπερπερισσῶς, ufarassau: **exceedingly abundantly**. ὑπερπλεονάζειν, ufarassjan: **to increase beyond measure, abound exceedingly**. ὑπερφρονεῖν, mais fraþjan: **to think more highly**.
ὑπήκοος, obedient: *ufhausjands*. ὑπηρέτης, attendant, minister: *andbahts*. ὕπνος, sleep: *sleps*. ὑπό, with the genitive, “from”: *fram*; with the accusative, “under”: *undar*, *uf*. ὑπογράφειν, to write beneath: *ufmeljan*. ὑπόδειγμα, example, pattern: *frisahts*. ὑποδεικνύναι, to point out: *ataugjan*, *gataiknjan*. ὑποδεῖν, to bind underneath; ὑποδεδεμένος, shod: *gaskohs*. ὑποδέχεσθαι, to receive: *andniman*. ὑπόδημα, shoe, sandal: *skohs*, *gaskoh*. ὑποκάτω, below: *undaro*, *uf*. ὑποκρίνεσθαι ἑαυτόν, to feign oneself: *us liutein taiknjan sik*. ὑπόκρισις, hypocrisy: *liutei*, *lita*. ὑποκριτής, hypocrite: *liuta*. ὑπολαμβάνειν, to take up; ## ADDITIONS TO THE GRAMMAR

Col. 960, last line, after *sporta*, add: *lukarnastaþa*, lampstand; *staua*, judge; *stoma*, cloth; *svaihra*, father-in-law.

Col. 967, line 24, after *luscus*, add: *hails*, sound, healthy.

Col. 968, line 7, after *hordeaceus*, add: *gumeins*, human.

Same column, line 11, after *seiteins ea*, add: *sinteins*.

Col. 1008, line 40, after *bairhts)*, add: *baitrei* (from *baitrs*).

Col. 1029, line 35, after δουλεύειν, “to serve as a slave,” add: λατρεύειν, “to perform religious service.”

Col. 1059, line 24, after Gal. II.4, add: *vilvands*: ἄρπαξ, “rapacious,” Matt. VII.15; *horinandei*: μοιχαλίς, “adulteress,” Mark III.38; *unagands*: ἄφοβος, “fearless,” 1 Cor. XVI.10; *silba*.

Col. 1068, line 30, after *siuns*, add: Luke VII.21.

Col. 1117, line 51, after *virgo* (“virgin”), add: Luke I.6, *vesun garaihta ba* (“they were both righteous”; Greek ἀμφότεροι, namely Zacharias and Elizabeth); 7, *vas aileisabaiþ stairo jah ba framaldra daga seinaize vesun* (“Elizabeth was barren, and both were advanced in their days”); Mark X.8, *sijaina þoba* (“the two shall be”; οἱ δύο, namely the man and the virgin).

Col. 1125, line 8, after *ungahabands*, add: ἄγαμος, “unmarried”: *unliugaiþs* and *unqeniþs* (“unwived,” unmarried); ἄζυμος, “unleavened”: *unbeistjoþs*; ἄναλος, “unsalted”: *unsaltans*.

Same column, line 9, after *jands*, add: ἄσβεστος, “unquenchable,” *unwapnands*; ἄφθαρτος, “incorruptible,” *undivans*; ἄνεπτος, “unwashed,” *unþvahans*; “not born,” *unbaurans*.

[Col. 1548]

Col. 1131, line 45, after “in God,” add: Luke VI.12, *bida guþs*, “the prayer of God,” that is, prayer to God.

Col. 1152, add the following note:

From Old High German *wuofan, wuofjan*, “to weep, lament, mourn,” etc. (Gf. I, 780 ff.), it must be concluded that this is the genuine meaning of Gothic *vopjan*. From this same passage in Luke it is also possible both to restore the fragmentary passage of Matthew XI.16 and to correct our own annotation: in the manuscript stands *anþarauþ* [lacuna], and Ulfilas wrote *anþar anþaris*, with a genitive after *vopjan*, as in Luke VII.32. But this *anþar anþaris* serves in place of the reflexive *seina* omitted; see § 200, 2. Now the reflexive in that passage of Matthew, where the manuscripts read ἑταίροις, “companions,” or ἑτέροις, “others,” has been borrowed from the parallel passage in Luke; at least the Latin versions (Vercellensis, Veronensis, Colbertinus) have *ad invicem*, “to one another.”

Col. 1216, line 12, after *þeins sve*, add: *ïn himina, jah ana airþai*, “in heaven and on earth”; Mark I.22, *vas laisjands ïns sve valdufni habands jah ni svasve* (“he was teaching them as having authority, and not as …”).

Col. 1228, line 46, after *uzetin*, add: “—and they found the child lying (κείμενον, ‘lying’) in a manger”: *jah bigetun þata barn liganda ïn uzetin*.

Same column, line 56, after κρυπθῷ, “in secret,” add: *wa taujiþ*—*galaiþ ïn þo alh analaugniba* (“what he does—he goes into the temple secretly,” ἐν κρυπτῷ).

Same column, last line, after ἕως ἄν, “until,” add: *usleiþiþ himins jah airþa, jota ains aiþþau ains striks ni nsleiþiþ af vitoda, unte* (“until heaven and earth pass away, not one iota or one stroke shall pass from the law, until …”).

[Col. 1547]

## ORDER OF SUBJECTS CONTAINED IN THE GRAMMAR
## INTRODUCTION

**Introduction.** On the Gothic language, §§ 1 ff.; its dialects, § 4; its foreign element, § 5; its literature, § 6; the peoples for whom it was a native language, § 7; its characteristics, § 8; its grammar, § 9.

**CHAPTER I. ON WRITING AND PRONUNCIATION.**

A. On writing. On the letters, § 10; the invention of the script, § 11; their shape and form, § 12; diacritical marks, § 12; their numerical value, § 14; their order, § 15; their names, § 16; reading signs, § 17; Gothic words relating to writing, § 18.

B. On pronunciation, § 19.

I. On vowels, § 20; short and long vowels, § 21; *a*, § 22; *i*, § 23; *u*, § 24; *e*, § 25; *o*, § 26; *y*, § 27; *ai*, § 28; *au*, § 29; *ei*, § 30; *iu*, § 31; lengthening, shortening, vowel change, weakening, breaking, apocope, syncope, hiatus, contraction, § 22.

II. On consonants, § 33:

1. Semivowels: *j*, § 34; *v*, § 35.
2. Liquids: *l*, § 36; *m*, § 37; *n*, § 38; *r*, § 39.
3. Mutes:
   - a) gutturals: *g*, § 40; *h*, § 41; *k*, § 42; *x*, § 43; *q*, § 44; *w*, § 45;
   - b) labials: *b*, § 46; *f*, § 47; *p*, § 48;
   - c) linguals: *d*, § 49; *þ*, § 50; *t*, § 51.
4. Sibilants: *s*, § 52; *z*, § 53.

On the combination of consonants, § 54; gemination, § 55; transition, § 56; paragogē, epenthesis, metathesis, and elision, § 57.

**CHAPTER II. ON THE INFLECTION OF WORDS.**

On the parts of speech, § 58.

A. On declension.

I. On the substantive: gender, § 59; number, § 60; cases, § 61; stem, § 62; declension divided into vocalic and consonantal, § 63.

A. On vocalic declension, § 64 ff.

1. Where the root-vowel is *a*, § 66 ff.  
[Col. 1558]  
2. Where it is *i*, § 75 ff.  
3. Where it is *u*, § 78 ff.  
4. Where it is *r*, §§ 83–84; on irregularities of vocalic declension, § 85 ff.

B. On consonantal declension, § 88:

a) on the masculine, § 89;  
b) on the neuter, § 90;  
c) on the feminine, §§ 91–92;  
on irregularities, § 93.

On the declension of proper and foreign names, § 94 ff.

II. On the adjective, § 97.

A. On vocalic declension, § 98 ff.  
B. On consonantal declension, § 101.

On the degrees of comparison, § 102. On participles.

III. On numerals:

a) cardinals, § 104;  
b) ordinals;  
c) distributives;  
d) multiplicatives;  
e) iteratives, § 105.

IV. On pronouns:

a) personal, § 106;  
b) possessive;  
c) demonstrative, § 108;  
d) relative, § 109;  
e) interrogative, §§ 110–111;  
f) indefinite, § 111;  
g) correlative, § 112.

B. On conjugation, § 113. On the three classes of conjugation, §§ 114–115. A general paradigm is presented in § 116.

I. On the active voice. On the first conjugation:

a) ablauting, § 117 ff.;  
b) reduplicating, § 124 ff.

On the second conjugation, § 127 ff. On the third conjugation, § 131.

II. On the passive voice, § 132.  
III. On the middle voice, § 133.  
On irregular verbs, § 134.

C. On indeclinable words, § 135.

**CHAPTER III. ON WORD-FORMATION.**

On roots, §§ 136–137. On transformation, § 138. On lost strong verbs, § 139. On the base or stem, §§ 140–141.

A. On the formation of nouns.

I. On the substantive, § 142:

1. [Col. 1559] derivation without a formative element, § 143;
2. derivation with a formative element, § 144 ff.

II. On the adjective, §§ 149–150. On comparison, § 151.

B. On the formation of pronouns, § 152.

C. On the formation of verbs.

I. On the first conjugation, § 153.  
II. On the second conjugation, § 154 ff.  
III. On the third conjugation, §§ 160–161.

D. On the formation of adverbs.

I. On adverbs of manner, § 163.  
II. On adverbs of place, § 164.  
III. On adverbs of time, § 165.

E. On formation by composition.

I. On the composition of nouns:

1. substantives, § 167;
2. adjectives, § 168;
3. numerals, § 169.

II. On the composition of pronouns, § 170.  
III. On the composition of particles, §§ 171–172.

On the limits of word-formation, § 173.

**CHAPTER IV. ON THE CONNECTION OF WORDS, OR SYNTAX.**

A. On the parts of speech considered in relation to syntax.

A. On the common noun:

1. gender, § 191;
2. number, § 192;

interchange of the substantive with the infinitive and participle, § 193.

B. On the proper noun, § 194. On the article, § 195.

3. On the numeral, § 198.

B. possessive, § 201;  
C. demonstrative, § 202;  
D. relative, § 203;  
E. interrogative, § 204;  
F. indefinite, § 205.

B. On the simple sentence.

I. On the subject, attribute, and copula, § 206:

2. on the attribute, § 209;
3. on the copula, § 210.

On attributive verbs, § 211. On the vocative, § 212. On negation, § 213. On interrogation, § 214.

II. On the attributive relation:

1. on the noun as attribute, § 215;
2. on the genitive as attribute, § 216;
3. on apposition, § 217.

III. On the objective relation, § 218:

1. On the nominal object:

D. causal [case], § 239.  
E. instrumental [case], § 240.

2. On the verbal object: the infinitive, § 252. On the accusative with infinitive, § 253. On the infinitive with *du*, considered as supine and gerund, § 254. On ellipses of the object, § 255.

C. On complex sentences, § 256.

I. On coordinated sentences, § 257:

1. on the copulative sentence, § 258;
2. on the adversative sentence, §§ 259–260;
